For the purposes of this Act, a “certification trade mark” means a mark defining certified products or services conforming to a particular standard and authorized by the proprietor of the certification trade mark under a scheme suitable to ensure that the goods or services so certified conform to the said standard; such standard shall be established and maintained by a body independent of the producers of the goods or providers of the services. The use of a certification trade mark shall be restricted to those products or services which satisfy the requirements as specified in the certification scheme, and any alteration to that scheme requires prior notification to the Registrar.

An application for the registration of a certification trade mark shall be deemed to be made in accordance with this Act if it contains a statement specifying the characteristics or qualities which the goods or services certified under the trade mark must possess, and the manner in which those characteristics are verified. The Registrar may require the applicant to furnish evidence demonstrating that adequate measures exist for precluding abuse of the certification trade mark, including provisions for inspection and redressal of grievances by certificate holders. Such measures shall be deemed insufficient if they do not provide for a system of periodic review of conformity with established standards. An interested party may object to the registration on grounds that the proposed specifications are vague or lack enforceability as provided herein.

Any person seeking to use a certification trade mark shall apply to the Registrar in the form specified herein, providing evidence of their eligibility and continued adherence to the standards underlying the certification. The Registrar may, after due consideration of the application and any objections received under this Act, grant registration if satisfied that the proposed mark is distinctive and conforms to prescribed regulations regarding certification marks. Upon successful registration, the proprietor of a certification trade mark shall be entitled to enforce its rights against all infringers, seeking remedies including injunctions and damages as provided herein. Any false or misleading representation concerning goods certified under this Act will constitute an offence, punishable with imprisonment and fines. The Registrar may revoke registration if it is established that the standards have ceased to operate or are not maintained consistently.

Any person seeking to use a certification trade mark relating to goods other than those produced by members of a defined organization shall make an application to the Controller, setting forth the particulars of the organization and its constitution, including details regarding the process for membership assessment and revocation. The application must also specify the standards of quality or characteristics which the certified goods are required to meet, and demonstrate that these standards are objectively verifiable through regular audits conducted by independent bodies approved by the Controller. Such approval shall be granted only after a thorough examination of the audit methodology and reporting procedures. The Registrar may require further information concerning the organization's financial stability and governance structure before proceeding with registration. Any alteration to the defined organization’s membership criteria or certification standards requires prior notification and consent from the Controller, failing which the certification trade mark shall be deemed liable for cancellation.

A person shall be entitled to register a certification trade mark if the sign distinguishes goods of a particular geographical origin or manufactured by a specific production method, provided that the applicant demonstrates control over the conditions under which those goods are produced and certified. The Registrar may require evidence establishing adherence to defined standards relating to quality, characteristics, or other relevant attributes of the certified goods. Such standards shall be documented and made publicly available, ensuring transparency in the certification process. Further, the applicant must demonstrate that the certification trade mark is used honestly and without misleading consumers regarding the origin or nature of the goods. Any alteration to the registered sign affecting its distinctive character will require prior approval from the Registrar.

Any person seeking to use a certification trade mark as provided herein shall apply to the Controller for registration, furnishing evidence of their eligibility to certify goods conforming to a defined standard, specification or characteristic. The Controller may reject such an application if satisfied that the proposed certification trade mark is likely to deceive or cause confusion in relation to any goods or services. Any proprietor of a registered certification trade mark who makes use of it in a manner contrary to the regulations governing its use shall be liable for damages and subject to penalties as determined by the Controller, including suspension or revocation of registration. False or misleading representations concerning certified goods are strictly prohibited and will incur substantial fines.

Any proprietor seeking to license the use of a certification trade mark under this Act shall execute an agreement specifying the terms and conditions governing such licensing, including but not limited to the scope of permitted activities, quality control measures, and royalty payments. Such agreements may be assigned or sub-licensed subject to prior written approval from the Registrar, provided that the assignee undertakes to abide by all obligations imposed upon the original proprietor as stipulated herein. The Registrar shall have the power to reject any proposed assignment or sub-licence if it deems such transfer detrimental to the integrity of the certification trade mark or likely to mislead consumers regarding the origin or quality of goods or services bearing the mark. Further, any alteration to a licensing agreement requires notification and approval from the Registrar before its effective date.

The Registrar may, upon application by any association seeking to register a certification trade mark, direct the publication of particulars relating thereto in the Trade Marks Journal, provided that such association demonstrates adherence to prescribed standards and procedures for ensuring conformity with the certified characteristics. Any party aggrieved by a direction under this Act concerning registration or refusal thereof, or by any condition imposed upon registration, may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order. The Board shall hear appeals regarding disputes over eligibility criteria for certification trade mark usage and determine whether the association maintains impartiality in its assessment processes, subject to principles of natural justice as provided herein.

Any person seeking to register a certification trade mark shall furnish evidence demonstrating adherence to prescribed quality standards and operational procedures as determined by the relevant regulatory authority. Failure to maintain such standards or demonstrate compliance may result in suspension of registration and imposition of penalties not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees. The Registrar, upon receiving a rectification register notice alleging misrepresentation or deceptive practices associated with a certification trade mark, shall issue a hearing notice to the proprietor. Any party aggrieved by a decision regarding rectification may appeal under this Act within sixty days; wilful violation of conditions relating to a certification trade mark constitutes an offence punishable with imprisonment and fines as provided herein.

The right to use a certification trade mark, as provided herein, may be granted to any producer association engaged in inspecting and certifying goods in accordance with established standards. Such grant shall not preclude the assignment or licensing of that right subject to the approval of the Controller. Any producer seeking to license the certification trade mark must submit a detailed proposal outlining the scope of permitted use, quality control measures maintained by the licensee, and royalty structure payable to the association. The Controller may impose conditions on such licenses, including limitations on geographical area or product categories covered. Further, any assignment shall be recorded with the Registrar within three months of execution; failure to do so renders the assignment void. The producer association retains ultimate responsibility for ensuring continued compliance with certification standards by all licensees and assignees.

The use of a certification trade mark relating to goods originating from a geographical indication registered under this Act shall be permitted only by persons who produce such goods within the defined geographical area and conform to the standards as may be prescribed; provided that any person claiming entitlement to use such certification trade mark, but who does not meet these requirements, may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. The Registrar shall, upon receiving a complaint from an aggrieved party alleging misuse or dilution of said certification trade mark, initiate inquiries and may, after affording the alleged infringer an opportunity of being heard, direct cessation of its use if it is found that the standards are not being adhered to or that the geographical boundaries have been improperly extended.

For the purposes of this Act, a certification trade mark is defined as a mark used to distinguish goods certified by a person or body having control over the standards and characteristics of those goods, and not necessarily connected with the trade name of any manufacturer or trader; such certification shall relate only to particular qualities or features of the goods. The applicant for registration of a certification trade mark must demonstrate that it meets prescribed criteria regarding impartiality and adherence to established quality benchmarks. Any alteration to these standards requires notification to the Registrar under this Act, ensuring continued validity of the trade mark registration.

For the purposes of this Act, a “form petition particulars” shall mean the specific details required in an application seeking registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design. These particulars include, but are not limited to, the name and address of the applicant, a description of the layout-design, its intended use, and the date of first commercial exploitation, if any. The form petition particulars shall also encompass declarations regarding ownership and originality as provided herein. Any application failing to contain all requisite form petition particulars shall be deemed incomplete and may be rejected under this Act. Further details relating to the prescribed format are available in the First Schedule.

An application for registration of a layout-design relating to an integrated circuit shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the drawings, plans or other representations depicting the said layout-design. The Registrar may require the applicant to furnish such further particulars as are necessary for the proper examination of the application under this Act. Such particulars shall include a detailed description of the functionality and intended use of the integrated circuit. Where an application is deemed deficient in its form petition particulars, the Registrar shall issue a notice requiring the applicant to rectify the deficiencies within a prescribed period. Failure to comply with such notice may result in the rejection of the application as provided herein.

Where a registered layout design proprietor alleges infringement, the aggrieved party shall file a Form Petition with the Controller within three years from the date of first commercial exploitation of the infringing layout design. The particulars contained in such a Form Petition must specify, with reasonable precision, the layout design allegedly infringed, detailing its salient features and demonstrating substantial similarity to the registered layout design. Failure to provide these requisite particulars may result in the rejection of the petition under this Act.

The Controller may require further clarification or supplementary information regarding any aspect of the form petition particulars if deemed necessary for a proper assessment of the claim. Any order passed by the Controller concerning the admissibility of a Form Petition shall be subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. The proprietor is entitled to seek interim relief, including an injunction, pending determination of the infringement proceedings.

Applications for registration of a layout-design shall be made in such form as may be prescribed, and accompanied by particulars detailing the salient features of the integrated circuit. The Registrar shall prescribe a standard form for all applications under this Act, ensuring uniformity in presentation and facilitating efficient processing. Every application must specify the name and address of the applicant, along with details regarding ownership or right to apply. Further, the petition particulars shall include a clear representation of the layout-design, either as drawings or photographic reproductions, demonstrating its originality and distinctiveness. The Registrar may require additional information or clarification concerning any aspect of the application, provided that such requests are reasonable and do not unduly delay the proceedings. Failure to provide complete and accurate form petition particulars may result in rejection of the application under this Act.

An application for registration of a layout-design relating to an integrated circuit shall be accompanied by a detailed statement specifying the salient features of the design, including its intended functionality and any relevant manufacturing processes employed. The applicant must furnish complete form petition particulars delineating the precise boundaries of the claimed layout-design, supported by technical drawings conforming to standards prescribed under this Act. Such particulars shall include a comprehensive description of all elements comprising the integrated circuit’s architecture and their interrelationships. Provided that, if the application relates to a design incorporating pre-existing works, the applicant shall declare such incorporation and provide evidence of authorization where required as provided herein. Failure to submit accurate form petition particulars may render the application liable for rejection.

Any person aggrieved by an action taken under this Act may file a petition before the designated Intellectual Property Enforcement Tribunal. Such petition shall specify, with particularity, the nature of the grievance, the actions complained of, and the relief sought. The petition particulars must clearly demonstrate that the respondent has engaged in activities infringing upon registered layout-design rights as defined herein. Failure to provide complete and accurate form petition particulars will render the petition liable for rejection without further notice. Any order passed by the Tribunal may include a direction for damages, injunctive relief, and account of profits derived from the infringing activity. The Tribunal shall impose penalties for wilful disobedience of its orders, subject to provisions regarding appeals as provided herein.

Where a layout design owner desires to grant a license or assign rights in respect of a registered integrated circuit layout design, such license or assignment shall be documented through a formal instrument specifying the full particulars of the transaction. These particulars include, but are not limited to, the identity of the licensor and licensee or assignee, a precise description of the licensed or assigned elements of the layout design, the geographical scope of the grant, and the duration thereof. Any subsequent modification to the terms of such license or assignment must also be recorded in writing, adhering to similar form petition particulars as initially prescribed. Provided that, where the license is non-exclusive, the owner may grant further licenses without requiring consent from prior licensees; however, any royalty rates shall be disclosed under this Act.

Where a person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act believes that the order was manifestly unjust or based on an erroneous interpretation of the law, such person may prefer an appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. The appeal shall be accompanied by a detailed statement of grounds specifying the errors apparent on the face of the record and demonstrating prejudice suffered as a direct consequence thereof. Failure to provide this comprehensive justification within the prescribed time limit shall render the appeal inadmissible. Regarding the *form petition particulars* required for such appeals, these must strictly adhere to Schedule B annexed hereto; any deviation may be deemed a procedural deficiency warranting dismissal. The Tribunal may, at its discretion, require further clarification or supplementary documentation from the appellant.

Where a layout design owner seeks to grant a license or assign rights in respect of a registered integrated circuit layout design, the application shall specify, with particularity, the scope of such license or assignment. The form petition particulars accompanying the application must clearly delineate the geographical territory covered by the proposed arrangement and any restrictions on use as may be agreed between the owner and licensee or assignee. Further, where an alleged offence arises from a breach of conditions stipulated in a licensed agreement, the Registrar may require submission of supplementary documentation detailing the contractual terms relevant to the dispute. The layout design owner shall provide evidence demonstrating due diligence in monitoring compliance with the license or assignment, subject to regulations prescribed under this Act concerning confidentiality and trade secrets.

An applicant seeking to register a layout design shall submit a duly completed Application Form A, along with requisite fees as determined by the Controller. The form petition particulars must include a precise description of the integrated circuit layout, its intended function, and details regarding the creator’s rights. Furthermore, the application shall specify any modifications or adaptations made to existing designs, accompanied by documentation demonstrating originality. Failure to provide complete and accurate information within the prescribed format will render the application liable for rejection under this Act. The Controller may require additional clarification or supporting documents deemed necessary for a thorough assessment of the layout's eligibility to register said layout.

For the purposes of this Act, a “zm form petition” shall mean a formal application submitted to the Controller seeking registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout design, presented in a prescribed format as detailed in Schedule B. Such a petition must contain specific particulars relating to the applicant, including their address for service and details of ownership or right to apply. The petition shall also include a clear representation of the layout design itself, accompanied by requisite documentation establishing its originality and compliance with the provisions herein. Failure to adhere strictly to the prescribed format of a zm form petition may render the application liable for rejection under this Act.

An applicant seeking registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall submit a zm form petition in the prescribed format, along with requisite fees as determined by the Controller. The petition must contain a detailed description of the layout-design, including its functionality and intended use, and specify the name and address of the owner claiming protection under this Act. Supporting documentation, such as technical drawings and circuit diagrams, may be appended to substantiate the claim. Provided that an applicant demonstrates due diligence in ensuring the accuracy and completeness of information furnished within the zm form petition, any inadvertent clerical errors shall not constitute grounds for rejection. The Controller may request further clarification or additional details from the applicant at any stage during processing.

Where a registered proprietor alleges infringement of their layout-design rights, they shall institute proceedings before the relevant jurisdictional authority as provided herein. The proprietor may seek injunctive relief to restrain further acts of manufacture, import, sale, offer for sale, or use which constitute an infringement. Compensation for loss suffered by the proprietor due to the infringing activity shall be determined based on demonstrable damages, including lost profits and reasonable royalties. A crucial element in initiating such proceedings is the proper filing of a zm form petition, detailing the layout-design registered, the alleged infringing acts, and supporting evidence substantiating the claim. Failure to adhere strictly to the prescribed format within the zm form petition may result in its rejection. The authority shall provide an opportunity for both parties to present their case; however, frivolous or vexatious petitions are subject to penalties as determined by regulations framed under this Act.

An applicant seeking registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall file a zm form petition with the Registrar, in such format as may be prescribed by regulations framed under this Act. The petition must contain a detailed description of the layout-design, including its functionality and intended use, accompanied by requisite drawings and specifications conforming to standards specified by the Controller General. Any alteration or addition to the information provided within the zm form petition after its initial submission shall require prior written approval from the Registrar, subject to payment of a prescribed fee. Failure to adhere to the stipulated format or providing incomplete or misleading information may render the petition liable for rejection. The Registrar may request further clarification or documentation as deemed necessary during examination. All petitions are considered public documents upon registration and availability for inspection under this Act.

An applicant seeking registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall, in addition to fulfilling requirements as provided herein regarding novelty and originality, submit with their application a duly executed zm form petition. This petition must contain a comprehensive description of the layout-design, including its intended function and any associated documentation deemed relevant by the Registrar. The applicant shall also declare under oath that they are the rightful owner of the layout-design or have been authorized to apply for registration. Failure to accurately complete the zm form petition, or providing false information therein, renders the application liable for rejection subject to an opportunity being afforded to rectify deficiencies. Any alteration made after submission requires prior written consent from the Registrar.

Any person alleging infringement of layout-design rights under this Act may institute proceedings before the designated Intellectual Property Enforcement Tribunal. Such a complaint shall specify, with particularity, the alleged infringing acts and the corresponding layout-design in respect of which the infringement is claimed. Failure to adequately detail these elements within the petition will render it liable for dismissal without further notice. The Tribunal may, subject to just considerations, impose penalties including monetary damages proportionate to the loss suffered by the registered proprietor. Repeated or wilful infringements shall attract enhanced penalties as determined by the Tribunal, and orders for account of profits derived from such acts may be issued. A correctly filed zm form petition is a prerequisite for initiating these proceedings.

The registered owner of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design may, subject to this Act, grant licenses or assign their rights pertaining to the design. Any such license agreement shall clearly specify the scope of permitted use, including but not limited to reproduction, adaptation, and commercial exploitation. Where an assignment is made, the assignee shall be deemed the new registered owner for all purposes under this Act, and a formal notification thereof must be filed with the Controller within thirty days. A zm form petition detailing the terms of any license or assignment, along with supporting documentation establishing ownership and consent from relevant parties, shall accompany such filings. Provided that, where the layout-design incorporates elements protected by copyright under another law, the licensing agreement must not contravene those rights; furthermore, royalties may be payable as stipulated in separate agreements.

Where any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act, including but not limited to orders relating to infringement or validity of layout designs, desires to challenge such order, he shall be required to file a petition within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. The form of petition shall adhere strictly to Form ZM as prescribed in Schedule B and must include detailed particulars of the impugned decision and grounds for challenging it. Provided that, where the petitioner demonstrates exceptional circumstances preventing timely filing, the Appellate Authority may entertain a petition filed after the stipulated period, subject to imposition of such costs as deemed appropriate. Any appeal against an order passed under this Act concerning a zm form petition shall be made to the High Court within ninety days from the date of the order appealed from.

Where a registered proprietor alleges infringement of their layout-design rights, they may institute proceedings before the relevant jurisdictional authority. Such proceedings shall commence with the filing of a zm form petition detailing the alleged infringing acts and providing particulars of the registered layout-design in question. The petitioner must demonstrate reasonable grounds for believing that an act restricted under this Act has occurred within India; however, actions occurring outside produced limits india do not automatically preclude jurisdiction, subject to considerations of substantial connection as determined by the authority. Any respondent may challenge the admissibility of the petition on grounds of technical deficiency or lack of standing. The authority shall afford both parties opportunity for argument and evidence before rendering a decision, which is appealable to the appellate forum established under this Act.

Where an interested party seeks review of a determination made by the Controller relating to the validity of a registered layout-design, such party shall file a petition with the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. The petition shall be in the prescribed zm form petition, obtainable from the Registry’s website or any designated facilitation centre. It must clearly state the grounds upon which the review is sought, supported by all relevant documents and evidence demonstrating material error apparent on the face of the record. Failure to adhere to the prescribed format may result in rejection of the petition. The Controller shall provide a reasoned order within sixty days of receipt of the petition. Where the layout-design incorporates a denomination variety shall be considered as part of the overall design for purposes of assessing originality, and any challenge relating thereto must be explicitly addressed within the petition.

For the purposes of this Act, "petition particulars contained" shall mean all information explicitly stated within a petition filed before the Controller under this Act seeking remedies relating to infringement or violation of layout-design rights. These particulars include, but are not limited to, the name and address of the petitioner, a detailed description of the integrated circuit layout design in question, the nature of the alleged infringement, and the relief sought as provided herein. The Controller may require further clarification or documentation subject to principles of natural justice. Failure to provide complete petition particulars contained shall render the petition liable for rejection without prejudice to any other action under this Act.

An application for registration of a layout-design relating to an integrated circuit shall contain, as petition particulars contained therein, a detailed description of the layout-design, including its intended function and any relevant manufacturing processes employed. Such particulars must specify the name and address of the applicant claiming ownership of the design, along with proof of such claim, subject to verification by the Controller. The application shall also include copies of the layout-design in a format prescribed as rules made under this Act. Provided that where the integrated circuit incorporates elements previously registered or claimed elsewhere, these prior registrations must be explicitly disclosed within the petition particulars contained. Failure to provide complete and accurate information may result in rejection of the application.

Where a registered layout design proprietor seeks redress for infringement, the petitioner shall file a Petition of Complaint with the designated Intellectual Property Enforcement Tribunal. Such Petition must specify, with particularity, the acts constituting alleged infringement, including but not limited to the reproduction, modification, or commercial exploitation of the protected layout design. The petition particulars contained therein shall detail the registration number of the layout design, the date of first registration, and a clear description of the infringing product or process. Failure to adequately specify these details may result in the Petition being deemed deficient and subject to rejection. Further, the petitioner must provide evidence demonstrating reasonable grounds for believing that infringement has occurred, provided that such evidence need not be conclusive at the time of filing. The Tribunal may, upon application, grant interim relief pending final determination.

Where a registered proprietor seeks rectification of an integrated circuit layout design registration, the petition particulars contained within the application shall specify with precision the grounds upon which such rectification is claimed. The Registrar may require further clarification or supporting documentation to adequately assess the merits of the petition. Any alteration to the original registration sought through rectification must be clearly delineated in the petition particulars and justified by demonstrable error or misrepresentation. Failure to provide complete and accurate petition particulars shall render the application liable for rejection, subject to an opportunity being afforded to the petitioner to remedy the deficiencies within a period not exceeding thirty days from notification of such deficiency. The registered proprietor shall bear the burden of proving the grounds for rectification as provided herein.

Where a person aggrieved by any order passed under this Act desires to present a petition for revision, such petition shall be filed within ninety days from the date of communication of that order. The petition particulars contained therein must specify with particularity the grounds upon which the revision is sought, detailing each error apparent on the face of the record. Provided that the Board may entertain a petition filed after the stipulated period if satisfactory cause for delay is demonstrated, subject to conditions as provided herein. Any document or evidence relied upon in support of the petition shall be clearly indexed and appended thereto. Failure to comply with these requirements regarding the petition particulars contained therein may result in the rejection of the petition without further hearing.

Where any person alleges that another has contravened a provision relating to layout-design rights, such person may file a complaint with the designated Intellectual Property Enforcement Authority. The complaint shall be accompanied by detailed particulars as prescribed under this Act, including but not limited to, evidence demonstrating unauthorized reproduction or importation of the allegedly infringing integrated circuit layout design. Failure to provide complete and accurate petition particulars contained within the complaint will render it liable for dismissal without further notice. The Authority may, subject to due process, impose penalties commensurate with the severity of the infringement, including monetary damages and injunctive relief. Any appeal against an order issued by the Intellectual Property Enforcement Authority shall be made within sixty days.

Where a petitioner seeks redressal for alleged infringement of layout-design rights under this Act, the particulars contained within the petition shall adhere strictly to Form A as prescribed in the First Schedule. Failure to comply with these formal requirements may result in rejection of the petition. However, where deficiencies are discovered after filing, the respondent may, within thirty days of service of the petition, file an objection citing the inadequacy of the petition particulars contained therein. The petitioner shall then have fifteen days to rectify such deficiencies. Any subsequent objection relating to the same matter shall be deemed frivolous and subject to appropriate costs as determined by the Controller.

For the purposes of this Act, "petition particulars contained" shall mean the specific details relating to a registered layout-design, as delineated in Schedule B annexed hereto. These particulars include, but are not limited to, the date of first fixation, the geographic location where the layout-design was initially made available, and a comprehensive description of the circuit elements comprising the integrated circuit. Failure to accurately reflect these petition particulars contained during registration proceedings may render subsequent claims of infringement registered less defensible under this Act. The Registrar shall maintain a publicly accessible record of all such particulars as provided herein.

An application for rectification of a registered layout-design, or for any other purpose as provided herein, shall be in Form D annexed to these regulations. The petitioner shall furnish with such application detailed particulars contained within a schedule specifying the alleged errors or omissions requiring correction, along with supporting documentation demonstrating their impact on the validity or enforceability of the design registration. Where the rectification sought involves an indication certification trade mark appearing on the layout-design, the applicant must provide evidence of prior use and established reputation associated with that mark. The Registrar may require further information or clarification regarding the petition particulars contained therein, and shall afford the respondent a reasonable opportunity to file a counter-statement. Failure to comply with these procedural requirements may result in rejection of the application under this Act.

For the purposes of this Act, "petition particulars" shall mean a detailed statement annexed to any petition filed before an Adjudicating Officer or other authority established under this Act. These particulars must specify with clarity the layout-design in respect of which relief is sought, including its functional elements and essential features as discernible from technical documentation submitted therewith. The petition particulars shall also delineate the alleged acts of infringement, providing dates, locations, and identities of persons involved where ascertainable. Provided that, any deficiency in the specificity of these petition particulars may be remedied by order of the Adjudicating Officer, subject to due notice being given to the petitioner.

An application for registration of a layout-design relating to an integrated circuit shall be accompanied by detailed petition particulars, specifying the name and address of the applicant, whether individual or corporate body, and the date of first commercial exploitation, if any. The petition particulars must also include a clear representation of the layout-design, either in the form of photolithographic masks or digital representations thereof, as deemed appropriate by the Registrar. Provided that, where an application relates to a layout-design incorporating elements previously registered under this Act, the petition particulars shall explicitly identify those prior registrations and detail the nature of incorporation. The applicant may also submit supporting documentation demonstrating ownership rights, subject to verification by the Controller. Failure to provide complete and accurate petition particulars will render the application liable for rejection.

Where a registered proprietor seeks redress for infringement under this Act, the petitioner shall file a Petition of Particulars with the relevant jurisdictional authority. Such petition must specify, with particularity, the layout design allegedly infringed, detailing its salient features and identifying any unauthorized copies or substantially similar integrated circuits. The petition shall further state the facts giving rise to the cause of action, including dates, locations, and names of individuals involved in the infringing activity. Failure to provide these particulars as required herein may result in the rejection of the petition. Provided that, a petitioner seeking interim relief under this Act must demonstrate an imminent threat of irreparable harm resulting from the continued infringement. The authority may require further documentation or clarification regarding the petition particulars at any stage of the proceedings.

An application for rectification of a registered layout-design shall be accompanied by an affidavit verifying the truthfulness of the statements made therein, and such application may be presented to the Controller in the prescribed form. The petition particulars required under this Act must specify with particularity the grounds upon which the rectification is sought, detailing any errors or omissions appearing on the register relating to the layout-design. Further, the applicant shall provide evidence supporting the claims made within the petition particulars, including but not limited to copies of relevant documents and expert opinions where applicable. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish additional information or clarification regarding the petition particulars if deemed necessary for a proper assessment of the application. Failure to comply with these requirements as provided herein will render the application liable to be rejected without further notice.

An aggrieved party seeking redressal under this Act relating to infringement of layout-design rights shall file a Petition with the designated Intellectual Property Enforcement Tribunal. Such Petition must adhere strictly to the prescribed format as notified by the Controller General, failing which it may be rejected without further consideration. The petition particulars shall include, but are not limited to, detailed identification of the allegedly infringing integrated circuit layout design, precise description of the acts constituting infringement, and a clear statement outlining the relief sought from the Tribunal. Provided that, if the aggrieved party is unable to fully comply with these requirements due to demonstrable hardship, they may submit an affidavit explaining the deficiencies, subject to approval by the Tribunal.

Where any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act, or by a direction issued thereunder, desires to challenge such order or direction, he shall file a petition with the designated Intellectual Property Enforcement Tribunal. Such petition must specify clearly the order or direction impugned, the grounds upon which it is challenged, and the relief sought. The petition particulars shall include precise details of the alleged infringement, including dates, locations, and quantities involved, as well as supporting documentation demonstrating reasonable efforts to mitigate damages. Failure to provide complete and accurate petition particulars may result in the rejection of the petition or imposition of costs. Any deliberate misrepresentation within the petition particulars will render the petitioner liable for penalties under this Act.

Where a registered layout design owner desires to grant a license or assign their rights relating to a protected integrated circuit layout design, the particulars of such proposed license or assignment shall be detailed in a formal petition submitted to the Controller. This petition must clearly specify the scope of the licensed right or assigned ownership, including any restrictions on use, reproduction, or adaptation as agreed between the parties. The petition particulars shall also identify all parties involved, their addresses for service, and the duration of any granted license. Further, where an assignment includes a confidentiality undertaking, this obligation’s terms must be explicitly stated within the petition. Subject to compliance with these requirements, the Controller may grant approval or impose conditions as deemed necessary under this Act to ensure fair practice and prevent undue exploitation of intellectual property rights.

Where a party seeks redressal against an order passed by the Controller relating to the validity of a registered layout-design, such appeal shall be made within sixty days from the date of communication of the said order. The appellant is required to file with the Appellate Board a detailed statement setting forth the grounds of appeal and demonstrating how the original decision was manifestly unjust or beyond the scope of the Controller's jurisdiction under this Act. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in the dismissal of the appeal. Furthermore, the petition particulars filed by the appellant must precisely identify the specific findings challenged and provide supporting documentation as evidence. The Board may require further clarification regarding the petition particulars if deemed necessary for a just determination.

An application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be accompanied by detailed petition particulars, specifying the name and address of the applicant, the title of the layout-design, and the date of first commercial exploitation, if any. The petition must also include a complete list of all persons who have contributed to the creation of the layout-design, along with their respective roles. Failure to provide accurate or complete petition particulars may result in rejection of the application under this Act. Where the applicant demonstrates compelling circumstances and satisfies the relevant authority, a compulsory licence may be granted permitting use of the registered layout-design for purposes of research and development, subject to conditions as provided herein.

Where a person desires to challenge any order passed by the Registrar relating to the registration of a layout-design, or the rectification thereof, such person shall file a Petition before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. The said Petition shall be accompanied by certified copies of the relevant orders sought to be challenged and all supporting documentation as deemed necessary by the Board. Particulars of the petition must include the name and address of the petitioner, details of the layout-design in question, and a concise statement of grounds upon which the challenge is based. The Registrar may, subject to regulations framed under this Act, require further information or clarification regarding the particulars presented. Any mark uses registered on the layout-design shall be clearly identified within these particulars. Failure to provide complete and accurate petition particulars may result in the rejection of the Petition by the Board.

Where a registered layout design alleges infringement, any party aggrieved may file a Petition before the designated Intellectual Property Enforcement Authority. Such Petition shall contain, as essential petition particulars, a detailed description identifying the design registered layout claimed to be infringed, specifying the nature and extent of the alleged infringing activity, and providing evidence demonstrating reasonable grounds for believing that an act of infringement has occurred. The Petition must further state the relief sought, which may include injunctions, damages, or any other remedy available under this Act. Provided that the petition particulars are complete and accurate, the Authority shall proceed to consider the matter in accordance with procedures as provided herein. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in rejection of the Petition.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act may prefer a petition to the Controller seeking redressal, provided that such petition shall be accompanied by certified copies of all relevant documents including the original layout-design registration certificate, if applicable. The petition particulars must specify the grounds upon which the challenge is based and clearly identify the order being challenged. Failure to comply with these requirements will render the petition liable for rejection without further notice. Upon receipt of a petition, the Controller shall maintain an inspection register detailing its filing date, assigned case number, and subsequent procedural steps. The Controller may direct any party to produce documents referenced in the petition particulars for verification purposes.

A form petition, as provided herein, shall prescribe the particulars required for initiating proceedings relating to the determination of validity of a registered layout-design. Such particulars include, but are not limited to, the name and address of the petitioner, details regarding the challenged layout-design registration number and date, and a concise statement outlining the grounds upon which the challenge is based. The form petition shall also require the petitioner to specify any evidence supporting their claim under this Act. Further, it must contain an affirmation by the petitioner verifying the truthfulness of the statements made therein, subject to penalties for false verification.

An applicant seeking registration of a layout-design relating to an integrated circuit shall submit a duly completed form petition in the prescribed format, available on the Controller General’s website. The form petition must contain a detailed description of the layout-design, including its intended function and any relevant technical specifications as determined by the Controller. Particulars regarding the applicant's entitlement to registration, such as evidence of original creation or prior disclosure, shall also be clearly stated within the form petition. Any subsequent alterations or additions to the information provided in the initial form petition may require a supplementary submission, subject to approval from the Controller. The prescribed fee for processing the form petition is payable at the time of submission and is non-refundable under any circumstances.

Where a person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act believes that such order is manifestly unjust or erroneous in fact or law, they may present a form petition to the Controller seeking review. The form petition shall be accompanied by a statement of grounds for reconsideration, supported by relevant documentation demonstrating material errors impacting the original determination. Any party who previously had opportunity to make representations during the initial proceedings under this Act shall be notified of the presentation of the form petition and afforded a further opportunity to submit observations within thirty days. The Controller may, after considering the submissions and any counter-submissions received, confirm, vary or annul the order subject to just considerations. This process does not grant an automatic right to re-hearing; it is discretionary with the Controller.

Applications for registration of a layout-design shall be made in the prescribed form, obtainable from the office of the Controller. Every such form petition must contain a clear and concise description of the layout-design sought to be registered, including its intended function and any relevant technical specifications. The petitioner shall furnish with the form petition a representation of the layout-design in the manner specified by the Controller; this may include photographic or graphical depictions deemed sufficient for assessment. Provided that where the layout-design incorporates elements previously disclosed, the petitioner must explicitly identify such prior disclosures and provide supporting documentation as required under this Act. The Controller may require further information or clarification regarding any aspect of the form petition before proceeding with examination. Failure to comply with these procedural requirements may result in rejection of the application.

An applicant seeking registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall submit a duly completed form petition in the prescribed format, obtainable from the designated office or its website. The form petition must clearly specify the title of the layout-design, the name and address of the claimant, and details pertaining to the first marketing date outside India, if any. Provided that, where the applicant is an entity incorporated outside India, they shall furnish a certified copy of their incorporation certificate as supporting documentation. Any alteration or erasure made on the form petition after its submission renders it invalid, requiring resubmission. The Registrar may reject a form petition deemed incomplete or containing false particulars under this Act.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act may prefer a form petition seeking review, subject to payment of such fee as may be prescribed. The petition shall specify with particularity the grounds upon which the challenge is based, including demonstrable errors of fact or law apparent on the face of the record. Failure to adhere to the prescribed format and content requirements within the form petition will render it liable for rejection without further notice. Where a petitioner has failed to demonstrate reasonable diligence in pursuing remedies available under this Act prior to filing a review petition, such petition may be summarily dismissed. The Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal shall have power to impose costs on any party found to have filed frivolous or vexatious petitions.

Where a layout design owner desires to grant a license or assign ownership rights in a semiconductor integrated circuit layout design, such transfer shall be documented through a duly executed form petition submitted to the Controller. The form petition must clearly delineate the scope of the licensed right, specifying whether it is exclusive or non-exclusive and detailing any restrictions on use, manufacture, or importation as provided herein. Assignment petitions require explicit consent from the original designer, if different from the layout design owner. Any subsequent transfer of rights derived from a license granted under this Act shall also be recorded via form petition, maintaining transparency regarding ownership lineage. The Controller may request supplementary documentation to ascertain the validity and completeness of the information presented in the form petition. Failure to accurately complete the required fields within the form petition renders the submission invalid and subject to rejection.

Where a person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act believes that such order is manifestly unjust or perverse, they may prefer a form petition seeking review before the Controller. The form petition shall clearly state the grounds upon which the challenge is based, supported by affidavits verifying the facts alleged therein. Subject to regulations prescribed by the Central Government, any party who was not given adequate notice of the original proceeding, or whose representation was demonstrably prejudiced due to procedural irregularities, may also file a form petition. The Controller may, after affording an opportunity for hearing to all concerned parties, dismiss the form petition or modify the order challenged, provided that such modification does not substantially alter the rights of any party involved.

Where a person aggrieved by any order passed under this Act believes that such order is manifestly unjust or erroneous in law, they may present a form petition to the Controller seeking review. The form petition shall be accompanied by an affidavit verifying the grounds for reconsideration and specifying the errors alleged to have been committed. Subject to payment of the prescribed fee, the Controller may entertain any such form petition if it demonstrates a clear departure from established legal principles or procedural fairness relating to the examination of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design. Provided that frivolous or vexatious petitions shall be summarily dismissed without opportunity for hearing. The Controller shall provide notice to all parties involved in the original proceeding and afford them an opportunity to respond to the petition before rendering any decision.

An applicant seeking registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall submit a duly completed form petition in the prescribed format, obtainable from the designated government website or through authorized facilitation centres. The form petition must contain precise details regarding the layout-design, including its title, date of creation, and the name and address of the creator. Failure to accurately disclose any material information within the form petition constitutes a violation under this Act. Any individual found guilty of submitting a false or misleading form petition may be subject to innocently punishable imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, alongside a monetary penalty as determined by the relevant adjudicating officer. The Registrar may reject an application if the submitted form petition is incomplete or non-compliant with these requirements, provided that the applicant receives written notification of such rejection and an opportunity to rectify any deficiencies.

Any person aggrieved by an act or omission contravening the provisions of this Act relating to the infringement of layout-design rights may file a form petition with the Commercial Court having jurisdiction over the place where the cause of action arose. Such petition shall specify, inter alia, the particulars of the alleged infringing integrated circuit layout design and the details of the patented article in relation to which the infringement occurred. Failure to adhere strictly to the prescribed format within the form petition shall render it liable for rejection without further notice. The Court may, upon finding an infringement, order remedies including damages, injunctions, and account of profits derived from the infringing activity, subject to limitations as provided herein regarding wilful or negligent acts.

Where a patentee desires to grant a license or assign rights in relation to a registered layout-design, such transfer shall be effected by way of a formal petition submitted to the Controller. The petition must clearly identify the layout-design concerned, the proposed licensee or assignee, and the scope of the rights being transferred, including any restrictions or conditions attached thereto. Any consideration paid for the license or assignment is to be disclosed within the form petition, along with details of the parties involved in the transaction. Further, a declaration affirming the patentee’s exclusive ownership and right to assign such layout-design must accompany the submission. The Controller may require additional documentation as deemed necessary to verify the authenticity of the transfer and protect the interests of any third parties claiming rights under this Act.

An application for registration of a layout-design shall be deemed invalid if, following the grant of registration, it is demonstrated that the design incorporates elements substantially derived from an earlier, unregistered layout-design. Any person aggrieved by such registration may file a form petition with the Registrar challenging its validity, setting forth particulars of the prior art and demonstrating clear evidence of copying. The Registrar shall provide the registrant with an opportunity to respond to the allegations contained within the petition before rendering a decision. Further, the registrant may appeal any order cancelling registration under this Act to the relevant appellate authority, subject to prescribed timelines and procedures as provided herein.

Where any party aggrieved by a decision of the Registrar relating to the registration of a layout-design or any other matter arising under this Act, may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board. Such appeal shall be filed within sixty days from the date of communication of the order sought to be appealed against. The appeal shall specify the decisions registrar clause upon which the appeal is based and state the grounds on which it is founded. The Registrar shall furnish to the Appellant a certified copy of the record of the proceedings relevant to the decision appealed from, subject to application and payment of prescribed fees. Provided that the Appellate Board may, at its discretion, require further evidence or afford an opportunity for cross-examination. The appeal shall be disposed of as expeditiously as possible, and the order of the Appellate Board shall be final.

Where any party aggrieved by a decision of the Registrar concerning the registration of a layout-design or related matters, including but not limited to objections raised during examination, may appeal to the Appellate Board. Such appeals shall be filed within ninety days from the date of communication of the decision. The Appellant shall deposit with the Appeal fees as prescribed; failure to do so will render the appeal inadmissible. The Registrar shall furnish all relevant records pertaining to the original application and the contested decision to the Appellate Board promptly upon request, subject to maintaining confidentiality where necessary. Any party may present evidence or arguments before the Appellate Board. Decisions of the Appellate Board concerning these decisions registrar clauses are final and binding.

For the purposes of this Act, “layout-design element” means any distinctive feature or combination of features of an integrated circuit, including but not limited to its topology, masking techniques, lead frame configurations, and interconnections. Such elements shall be assessed in relation to their overall impression on the informed user, irrespective of minor variations or adaptations. The determination of originality under this Act shall consider whether the layout-design element was created by a process using his own skill and judgment. Where an integrated circuit incorporates pre-existing layout-design elements, as provided herein, the question of infringement under section 53 zn shall be decided based on substantial similarity to the original work.

Where any person, being aggrieved by an order made under this Act relating to a claim for damages or other remedies available as provided herein, considers that such order is unlawful or has been passed without due regard to the principles of natural justice, he may appeal to the Commercial Court having jurisdiction over the matter. Such appeal shall be filed within ninety days from the date of communication of the order and shall state specifically the grounds on which the order is challenged. The appellate court may, after affording an opportunity for hearing to all parties concerned, confirm, modify, or reverse the original order, or remand the case to the original adjudicating authority for further consideration. This right of appeal shall not preclude any party from seeking appropriate remedies under section 53 zn concerning infringement of layout-design rights.

Where a layout design is substantially similar to an earlier layout design, subject to compliance with the provisions regarding reverse engineering as provided herein, any person claiming to be the first to have made that layout design shall furnish evidence demonstrating due diligence in ascertaining the originality of their work. Such evidence must include documented records pertaining to the design process and verification procedures undertaken prior to commercial exploitation. Furthermore, where a claim is asserted under section 53 zn relating to a mask work derived from an integrated circuit layout design, it shall be established that the claimant possesses lawful right or license to utilize the original layout design for such derivation. Failure to provide satisfactory evidence may result in rejection of the application and potential liability for damages incurred by any aggrieved party.

Any person who, knowing or having reason to believe that any act, omission, or publication constitutes an infringement of layout-design rights as provided herein, facilitates such infringement, shall be deemed guilty of contributory infringement. Such facilitation includes the manufacture, importation, distribution, sale, or offer for sale of semiconductor integrated circuits incorporating the infringing layout design. The penalty for contributory infringement shall be a fine not less than fifty thousand rupees and may extend to two hundred thousand rupees, and imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years. Further, any person found guilty under this Act may be subject to an order restraining them from further acts of facilitation, as determined by the relevant adjudicating officer. This applies particularly where such infringement relates to matters governed by section 53 zn.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any registered layout-design owner may grant a license or assign their rights in respect of the design to another person, either wholly or partially, for specific purposes including but not limited to manufacture, import, sale, hire, or use. Such licenses shall be documented in writing and may specify territorial limitations, duration, and royalty payments as agreed upon between the parties. Where a license is granted, the licensee shall be bound by any restrictions imposed on the layout-design owner under this Act. Assignment of rights shall vest complete ownership with the assignee, who thereafter possesses all privileges afforded to the original registrant. The transferor remains liable for any infringement committed prior to the assignment’s effective date, as provided herein. Further, a license or assignment is deemed invalid if it contravenes section 53 zn concerning reverse engineering prohibitions.

An applicant patent shall be deemed to include any legal entity claiming inventorship through assignment or otherwise, and for the purposes of this Act, the term “applicant” refers exclusively to the individual or body named as such in the formal application filed before the Patent Office. An applicant patent may amend the claims of a pending application only if such amendments do not extend beyond what is described in the original specification; provided that any alteration introducing new matter shall be considered invalid and subject to objection under this Act. The Controller General may, at his discretion, require further clarification from an applicant patent regarding the scope or basis of their claim.

An applicant patent seeking registration under this Act shall furnish a statement regarding any priority claim asserted in relation to the invention. This statement must include particulars of the earlier application relied upon for claiming priority, specifying the country where it was filed and its filing date. The Controller General may require further documentation substantiating the priority claim, including certified copies of relevant records from foreign patent offices. Failure to provide a complete and accurate statement regarding priority shall render the applicant liable to objections during examination. An application may be rejected if the claimed priority is demonstrably invalid or obtained through fraudulent means, as determined by the Controller. The applicant remains responsible for ensuring the veracity of all information submitted concerning the applicant patent and its related claims.

Where a notice of opposition is served upon an applicant patent under this Act, the Controller may, subject to any terms specified in the notice, grant leave to the applicant to file a counter-statement within such time as the Controller deems appropriate. The counter-statement shall address each ground of objection raised in the notice and may include evidence supporting the validity of the application. Failure by the applicant patent to comply with this requirement or to file a timely counter-statement shall be deemed an abandonment of the proceedings, and the opposition shall proceed ex parte. Any party aggrieved by such decision of the Controller relating to leave to file a counter-statement may appeal under this Act. The appellate authority may allow the application for leave or direct the applicant patent to file a counter-statement within a specified timeframe.

An applicant patent seeking examination of an application under this Act shall furnish a certified copy of any corresponding application made in a convention country not later than six months from the date of making the Indian application. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish such further information or documents as are necessary for facilitating the determination of novelty and inventive step, provided that the request is made within eighteen months of the filing date of the patent application. Failure to comply with a direction issued under this Act shall render the application liable to be refused. Any person aggrieved by an order passed by the Controller relating to the acceptance or rejection of an applicant patent may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order. The Board’s decision is final, subject to further appeals as provided herein.

An applicant patent seeking grant under this Act shall furnish a complete specification including a claim defining the scope of protection sought. The specification must disclose the invention in a manner as to enable any person skilled in the art to make and use it; provided that such disclosure does not compromise trade secrets essential for implementation, subject to conditions prescribed herein regarding non-obviousness. Where an applicant has previously published details concerning the invention prior to filing the patent application, they must provide full particulars of such publication along with a reasoned justification demonstrating why this prior disclosure should not preclude examination. The Controller may require further clarification or experimental data to ascertain compliance with these requirements and assess novelty as provided herein.

Where any applicant patent fails to disclose information reasonably ascertainable which would have been obvious to a person skilled in the art at the time of filing, and this omission materially affects the validity of the granted patent, the Controller may initiate revocation proceedings. Such proceedings shall be conducted expeditiously, affording the applicant an opportunity for hearing as provided herein. Any party aggrieved by a decision revoking an applicant patent may appeal to the Appellate Intellectual Property Tribunal within sixty days from the date of such decision. The Tribunal’s order shall be final, subject to further appeal to the Supreme Court on a point of law. Penalties for wilful non-compliance with this provision include fines not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees and imprisonment up to three years.

An applicant patent may grant a non-exclusive license under this Act relating to the patented invention to any person, subject to conditions as deemed fit by the Controller. Such license shall specify the field of exploitation and duration thereof, provided that the terms are reasonable and do not unduly prejudice the interests of the inventor. Further, an applicant patent is empowered to assign the entire interest in the application or granted patent to another party, whether located within India or abroad, through a registered agreement. This assignment may include all rights pertaining to the invention, including the right to grant licenses as described above. Any subsequent license granted by the assignee shall be subject to similar conditions and review under this Act, ensuring continued protection of public interest and equitable access to patented technologies.

Where an applicant patent seeks revocation of a patent granted under this Act on the ground that the invention was not novel or obvious at the date of filing, the Controller may require such applicant to furnish evidence demonstrating the prior publication or use of the invention. This requirement shall apply irrespective of whether the alleged prior art originates within India or abroad. The Controller shall afford the patentee an opportunity to be heard and present counter-evidence refuting the claims made by the applicant patent. Any party aggrieved by a decision under this provision may appeal to the Appellate Board, provided that such appeal is filed within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. The Appellate Board’s decision shall be final, subject to further review under principles of natural justice as provided herein.

An applicant patent may grant a non-exclusive license under the granted patent to any person, subject to conditions specified in the licensing agreement and recorded in the office register of patents. Such an agreement shall clearly delineate the scope of the licensed rights, including but not limited to field of use, duration, and royalty payments. The Controller General may require further details regarding the consideration provided for such a license, ensuring fairness and transparency as provided herein. Assignment of an applicant patent or any part thereof is permissible with prior written consent from the Controller, and shall be recorded in the office register patents, creating a public record of ownership transfer. Any subsequent licensee deriving title through assignment must also notify the Controller General within thirty days for registration purposes.

Where an applicant patent seeks to amend the specifications or drawings contained within a patent application already published under this Act, such amendment shall be permissible only if it does not substantially alter the scope of protection initially sought. The Controller General may require the applicant to furnish a reasoned explanation for the proposed alteration and its consistency with the original disclosure. Further, any amendment so submitted is subject to objection by any interested party within sixty days from the date of publication of notice thereof in the Patent Journal. Such objections shall be considered by a member appointed bench constituted under this Act, which may allow or reject the amendment after affording the applicant an opportunity for hearing. The Controller’s decision on amendments is final, provided that it does not contravene any provision as provided herein relating to novelty and inventive step.

For the purposes of this Act, “invention” means a new and useful art, process, manufacture or composition of matter; provided that an invention which is obvious from prior publications or knowledge does not constitute an invention. An application for a patent shall disclose the manner in which the invention may be made or used. The term "patent" includes patents of addition, relating to matters disclosed in the original patent application. A person shall be entitled to apply for a patent only if they are the true and first inventor of the subject matter claimed in the patent. Subject to any conditions specified under this Act, a patent shall confer upon the patentee exclusive right to make, use or sell the patented invention within India.

An application for registration of a patent shall include particulars specifying the invention, its claims, and details relating to priority, if any. The applicant shall furnish a declaration stating that they are the true and first inventor of the claimed subject matter. Where an assignment of rights in the invention has occurred prior to the filing of the patent application, documentation substantiating such assignment must be submitted alongside the registration request. Failure to provide complete and accurate information regarding the invention or its ownership may result in rejection under this Act. The Controller General shall maintain a register of all patents granted, accessible for public inspection as provided herein.

An application for a patent shall include particulars specifying the invention claimed to be novel and inventive, together with details of priority if applicable. The Controller General may require an applicant to furnish further information or clarification regarding the subject matter of the invention under this Act, and such requirements shall be complied with within the time specified by the Controller General. Where an application relates to a method or process capable of being applied in any industry, the description shall disclose how the said method or process may be performed. The determination of patentability is subject to examination as provided herein, including assessment of prior art publications and existing patents. Any person aggrieved by an order passed by the Controller under this Act may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within a period of sixty days from the date of receipt of such order.

An application for a patent shall disclose the matter which the invention relates to, clearly and completely. The claimed invention must satisfy the criteria of novelty and inventive step; otherwise, it is not eligible for grant under this Act. Where an applicant has failed to comply with prescribed formalities during prosecution, including timely submission of requisite forms or payment of fees, the patent shall be deemed abandoned. Any person aggrieved by a decision relating to the acceptance or rejection of a patent application may appeal to the Controller. The Controller may allow such an appeal if satisfied that there was material error or omission in the original decision. Subject to this, patents for products manufactured outside India are not grantable.

For the purposes of this Act, “Technical Member” means a person who possesses specialized knowledge or experience in matters relating to technology, engineering, science, or any other relevant technical field and shall be appointed by the Central Government under such conditions as may be prescribed. A Technical Member is deemed to possess such expertise if he holds a degree in an appropriate branch of engineering or natural sciences from a recognized institution or possesses equivalent professional qualifications as determined by the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. The decision of a Technical Member, when dealing with technical aspects of a case, shall carry significant weight and may be binding on other members of the tribunal, subject to reasoned dissent.

An application for registration of a trademark shall be deemed deficient if the proposed mark contains exclusively geographical indications as defined under this Act, unless it is established that such indication has become generally descriptive of the goods or services with which it is associated. The Registrar may require the applicant to submit evidence demonstrating acquired distinctiveness where a refusal is based on descriptivity. Further, an appeal against an order refusing registration due to lack of distinctiveness shall be heard by a Technical Member, who shall consider expert testimony and consumer surveys submitted by both the appellant and the respondent. The decision of the Technical Member shall be final, subject to further appeal under the provisions herein relating to appellate jurisdiction.

Where any proprietor institutes proceedings under this Act seeking relief for the infringement of a registered trademark, the Intellectual Property Appellate Board may, upon application by the defendant, direct that the matter be referred to a Technical Member for determination of technical aspects relating to the goods or services in relation to which the trade mark is used. Such referral shall not preclude the Appellate Board from considering other issues arising in the proceedings. The proprietor of the trademark shall be entitled to counter-claim against the defendant seeking damages for acts of unfair competition, provided that such claims are directly related to the alleged infringement. Any order made by the Technical Member shall be binding on both parties and form part of the record of the Appellate Board. Further, costs associated with the referral may be awarded as deemed appropriate by the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

The Appellate Board shall be constituted by a Chairperson who is or has been a Judge of a High Court, and one Technical Member. The Technical Member shall possess specialized knowledge or experience in matters relating to trademarks, industrial designs, geographical indications, or related fields, as determined by the Central Government. Applications for appointment as Technical Member shall be invited through public advertisement, specifying essential qualifications and desirable attributes. Upon receiving such applications, a Selection Committee comprising representatives of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trademarks, and an eminent intellectual property professional will evaluate candidates. The Chairperson may require any applicant to appear before the Board for further assessment. Decisions regarding appointment shall be made by the Central Government, subject to the recommendations of the Selection Committee. Any appeal arising from a decision of the Appellate Board concerning technical aspects shall be heard by a bench including the Technical Member.
