Where an appeal lies under this Act before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board, the Board shall consist of a Chairperson who is a Judge of a High Court or has held judicial office and at least two Technical Members. A person shall be appointed as a Technical Member only if he possesses specialized knowledge and experience in trade marks law, patents, designs, copyrights or geographical indications. The Chairperson may require any authority or officer to furnish such information as the Board deems necessary for the proper disposal of an appeal; provided that the presiding officer of the Board shall ensure confidentiality regarding sensitive commercial information submitted during proceedings. Technical Members shall exercise their powers and discharge their functions in accordance with principles of natural justice, subject to applicable rules of procedure.

Where any proprietor institutes proceedings under this Act seeking relief for the infringement of a registered trade mark, the Intellectual Property Appellate Board shall, upon receiving such proceedings, constitute a Bench comprising at least one Technical Member possessing expert knowledge in matters relating to trademarks and branding. The Board may, subject to appeal to the High Court, order an injunction restraining the defendant from using any marks which are identical or confusingly similar to the registered trade mark of the complainant. Furthermore, damages shall be awarded to the proprietor for all losses sustained due to the infringement, calculated as provided herein, and may include punitive damages where the infringing activity was undertaken with malicious intent. The Board shall also order the destruction of infringing materials.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any proprietor of a registered trademark shall be permitted to grant a license conferring the right to apply for, register, and utilize said trademark within a specified territory. Such licenses may be exclusive or non-exclusive, as determined by the grantor, provided that the terms thereof are clearly defined in a written agreement executed prior to commencement of use under the licensed rights. Assignment of trademarks, including partial assignments relating to specific goods or services, shall require registration with the Trade Marks Registry and notification to all interested parties. The Technical Member, while adjudicating disputes concerning such licenses and assignments, may consider factors including but not limited to the duration of the license, royalty rates stipulated, and any restrictions placed upon sub-licensing activities. Further, a licensee may assign their rights under this Act with consent from the proprietor.

Where an appeal lies under this Act before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board, the Board shall have power to entertain appeals from any order passed by the Registrar relating to the rectification of a trademark, including but not limited to disputes concerning dilution and passing off. The Board may, at its discretion, require the appearance of both the appellant and respondent, affording each party an opportunity to present evidence and arguments. Further provided that in cases where technical expertise is deemed necessary for proper adjudication, the Board shall have the power to constitute a bench including a Technical Member possessing relevant qualifications in fields such as chemistry or engineering. Decisions made by the Board are subject to judicial review under law.

For the purposes of this Act, “Technical Member” means a person who possesses specialized knowledge or experience in matters relating to technology, engineering, science, or any other relevant technical field and shall be appointed by the Intellectual Property Appellate Board under such procedure as may be prescribed. A Technical Member is deemed to possess expertise sufficient to understand complex technological arguments presented during hearings concerning validity of registered trademarks or infringement proceedings. The Intellectual Property Appellate Board may require a Technical Member to participate in a prescribed proceeding appellate relating to matters involving technical evaluation, subject to the provisions regarding quorum and decision-making as provided herein.

An application for registration of a trademark shall be deemed refused if the examining officer finds that the proposed mark is descriptive of the goods or services for which it is sought, subject to the provisions sub section relating to acquired distinctiveness. The Registrar may, however, accept such an application if the applicant demonstrates, through evidence duly admitted under this Act, that the mark has in fact, by reason of its use, become distinctive and capable of distinguishing their goods or services from those of others. A Technical Member of the Appellate Board shall be specially convened to hear appeals concerning decisions regarding acquired distinctiveness, ensuring a thorough assessment of the submitted documentary proof. The Registrar’s decision is final provided that it does not contravene any established principles of trademark law as interpreted by the courts.

Where an application for registration of a design is opposed under this Act, the Appellate Board shall, upon receiving notice of opposition, afford both the applicant and the opponent a reasonable opportunity of being heard. The Board may require production of evidence, including expert testimony, relevant to the novelty and originality of the claimed design. Subject to compliance with prescribed procedural requirements, the Technical Member of the Appellate Board shall be empowered to determine questions relating to technical aspects of the design’s aesthetic merit or functionality. Provided that any party aggrieved by an order made by the Technical Member may seek further review before a bench comprising other members of the Appellate Board. The decision of the Appellate Board shall be final, subject to appeal under the provisions herein.

An application for registration of a proposed trade mark shall not be accepted if it is deemed identical or confusingly similar to an earlier registered trade mark relating to identical goods or services. The Registrar may require the applicant to furnish evidence demonstrating distinctiveness acquired through use, provided that such use has occurred prior to the date of the aforementioned application and satisfies conditions as provided herein regarding duration and geographical extent. Further, a registered trade mark shall cease to be protected if the proprietor fails to file renewal forms within the prescribed time limit or pays the requisite fees. Any alteration to a registered trade marks representation requires consent from the Registrar, subject to compliance with regulations concerning clarity and accuracy of depiction.

Any person who, without due cause or justification, applies for registration of a mark identical or deceptively similar to a previously registered trade marks shall be liable to pay a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees. Such application shall be deemed an infringement under this Act, irrespective of any claim of fair use or descriptive necessity. Further, the Trade Marks Registry may, upon receiving complaint from the proprietor of the existing registered trade marks, refuse registration and issue directions for withdrawal of the offending application. Any subsequent attempt to register a mark infringing on another’s rights shall attract enhanced penalties, potentially including imprisonment for a term not less than six months and up to three years. The Registrar is empowered to order seizure of goods bearing such infringing marks as provided herein.

The proprietor of a registered trade mark may grant a license to use the mark for specific goods or services, subject to terms and conditions agreed upon in writing between the parties. Such licenses shall be assignable along with the underlying registered trade mark, provided that notice of assignment is filed with the Trade Marks Registry within three months of the transfer. Any subsequent proprietor acquiring rights under an assignment shall be bound by any existing license agreements pertaining to the registered trade marks. Further, a license granted under this Act may contain provisions restricting the licensed user’s activities, including geographical limitations and quality control standards as determined by the grantor. The Registrar may require evidence demonstrating compliance with these conditions before registering an endorsement of assignment involving licenses for registered trade marks.

A registered trade mark shall confer on the proprietor thereof the exclusive right to use the trade mark in relation to the goods or services for which it is registered, subject to any condition entered on the register. The proprietor may institute proceedings for infringement under this Act where there exists a likelihood of confusion arising from the adoption of an identical or similar marks relating to identical or similar goods or services. Any alteration to a registered trade mark shall be permissible only with prior approval obtained from the Trade Marks Registry, provided that such alteration does not affect the distinctive character of the marks. The Registrar may require evidence demonstrating continued use of the registered trade marks within five years of renewal before further registration is granted. It is stipulated that marks means trade names, service indicators and other similar indications.

The proprietor of a registered trade mark may grant a license to use the mark subject to terms and conditions specified in the license agreement, provided that such agreement does not extend beyond the scope of goods or services for which the trade mark is registered under this Act. Any assignment of the said registered trade marks shall be recorded at the Trade Marks Registry within three months from the date of the assignment, failing which it shall be deemed invalid. The International Bureau may request further information regarding any such assignment to verify compliance with international obligations as provided herein. A licensee may subsequently assign their rights under a license agreement subject to approval by the proprietor and recording at the registry. Further, sub-licensing is permissible only with explicit written consent from the original proprietor of the registered trade mark.

An unregistered trade mark shall be deemed to include any mark used to distinguish the goods or services of one undertaking from those of others, irrespective of whether such use constitutes registration under this Act. For the purposes of determining infringement, an unregistered trade mark is considered valid if its reputation has been established through substantial and continuous use in India prior to the infringing activity. The rights conferred by way of protection for an unregistered trade mark shall be subject to the provisions relating to fair dealing and permissible uses as provided herein. Any person claiming damages due to the misuse of an unregistered trade mark must demonstrate demonstrable prejudice resulting from such unauthorized application.

An application for registration of a trade mark shall be refused if the marks applied for includes any identifier that is identical or confusingly similar to an existing unregistered trade mark used by another person in relation to goods or services. Such refusal may be overridden where the applicant can demonstrate continuous use of the potentially infringing sign for a period exceeding five years prior to the date of application, and that such use has established amongst the relevant consuming public a clear association between the sign and the applicant’s goods or services. The Registrar shall consider evidence presented by both parties in determining whether confusion is likely, taking into account all surrounding circumstances as provided herein.

An unregistered trade mark shall be deemed to confer upon the proprietor thereof no right to institute proceedings to prevent, or for the removal of, any infringement thereof; provided that such proprietor may, subject to the provisions herein relating to remedies, bring an action founded in law other than under this Act against a person who, without consent, uses a sign which is identical or confusingly similar to the unregistered trade mark. The remedy available shall be limited to damages proven to have been suffered by the proprietor as a direct result of the infringing use, and no injunction restraining such use may be granted unless it is demonstrated that the infringement has caused, or is likely to cause, substantial damage to the reputation or goodwill associated with the unregistered trade mark. This right shall not extend to prevent use arising from honest descriptive application relating to the goods or services.

An action may be instituted in the High Court against any person who, having knowledge of an unregistered trade mark used by another person to distinguish their goods or services, makes use of an identical or deceptively similar mark for such goods or services, with intent to pass off his own goods or services as those of the former. The plaint shall specify the particulars of the unregistered trade mark, the goods or services in relation to which it is used, and the date from which its use commenced. Upon perusal of the plaint and after hearing the plaintiff and defendant, the High Court may grant such relief as it deems just and equitable, including an injunction restraining the defendant from further infringing upon the unregistered trade mark. The court shall also be entitled to award damages to compensate for losses suffered by the proprietor of the unregistered trade mark due to the infringement.

Where any sign is employed in relation to goods or services without being registered under this Act, it shall be deemed an unregistered trade mark for the purposes of this provision. An action may be brought against a person using such an unregistered trade mark if that use creates a likelihood of confusion amongst consumers regarding the origin of the goods or services. Provided that, where the honest and contemporaneous user of a sign has acquired through its continuous usage substantial recognition of reputation in relation to specific goods or services, subsequent use by another party shall not be actionable as infringement unless it is clearly established that such subsequent use takes unfair advantage of, or is detrimental to, the distinctiveness of the prior user’s unregistered trade mark. Subject to compliance with prescribed procedures, remedies for such detriment may include an injunction and damages.

No person shall institute any suit for the recovery of damages for infringement of an unregistered trade mark unless it is shown that special damage has been caused thereby to the plaintiff. Such special damage may include, but is not limited to, loss of profits, diminished sales, and harm to reputation. Where a finding of infringement of an unregistered trade mark is made, the Court may grant such relief as it deems just and equitable, subject to the provisions regarding costs under this Act. Any party aggrieved by an order passed under this Act relating to an unregistered trade mark may appeal to the Appellate Intellectual Property Tribunal within sixty days from the date of such order; provided that the Tribunal shall have power to award damages in lieu of or in addition to any remedy granted by the Court.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any person who, prior to the registration of a trademark, has used such mark in India for bona fide purposes may apply to the Registrar for an assignment or license of that unregistered trade mark. Such application shall specify the territory within India where the use occurred and provide evidence thereof satisfactory to the Registrar. The Registrar may grant the application if satisfied that the applicant’s use was continuous and not merely sporadic, and that no other person has a superior right to the mark. Any assignment or license granted under this Act shall be recorded in the Register of Trade Marks and shall confer upon the assignee or licensee the rights as if it were a registered trademark for the duration specified within the agreement, provided that such use does not infringe upon any existing registered trade marks.

Where any person alleges that another has used an unregistered trade mark in relation to goods or services without his consent, and such use constitutes an infringement under this Act, he may institute proceedings before the relevant intellectual property tribunal. The tribunal shall hear all parties and consider evidence pertaining to the distinctiveness of the alleged unregistered trade mark, the nature of the goods or services involved, and any evidence of actual confusion among consumers. It is provided that a defendant asserting prior honest usage of the mark may present arguments demonstrating lack of consumer deception. Any party aggrieved by an order made under this Act may appeal to the appellate forum as prescribed herein, subject to fulfilling procedural requirements for filing such appeals.

The term "Chairperson" with reference to this Act shall mean the individual appointed by the Central Government to preside over the Intellectual Property Disputes Tribunal established under this Act. The Chairperson shall be a person who is or has been a Judge of a High Court or possesses substantial experience in intellectual property law, technological matters and administrative practice. Subject to the provisions herein, the Chairperson may delegate any of their functions to other members of the Tribunal. Provided that such delegation shall not extend to the power to impose penalties under this Act. The Central Government may prescribe the terms and conditions of service for the Chairperson as provided herein.

The Register shall, upon receipt of an application for registration of a layout-design, forward it to the Chairperson for examination. The Chairperson may, after affording the applicant an opportunity for being heard, direct the Register to proceed with the registration if satisfied that the layout-design is original and not contrary to this Act or any rules made thereunder. Any person aggrieved by an order of the Chairperson under this section may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within a period of sixty days from the date of such order. The application for registration shall include particulars relating to the creator, owner, and any modifications undertaken to the layout-design. Further, the Register shall maintain a record of all communications pertaining to applications processed by the Chairperson.

Where any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act concerning infringement of layout-design rights may appeal to the Intellectual Property Tribunal, such appeal shall be filed within ninety days from the date of communication of the order. The Intellectual Property Tribunal may, after giving notice to all concerned parties and affording them a reasonable opportunity for being heard, confirm, modify, or reverse the order appealed against. Any party dissatisfied with the decision of the Intellectual Property Tribunal may further appeal to the Supreme Court on a point of law. The Chairperson of the Intellectual Property Tribunal shall be appointed by notification in the Official Gazette, subject to such qualifications as are prescribed under this Act. Compensation for infringement shall include damages sustained or losses incurred by the registered proprietor, provided that punitive damages may also be awarded where the infringing activity was undertaken with knowledge of the layout-design right and malicious intent.

The functions of the Chairperson shall include the superintendence and direction of all proceedings relating to inquiries under this Act. The Chairperson may, at any time, require any officer subordinate to him or her to furnish such reports or information as he or she deems necessary for the discharge of his or her duties. Decisions regarding the appointment of expert witnesses in matters before the relevant adjudicating authority shall be subject to review by the Chairperson upon application by an interested party, provided that such application is made within thirty days of the order under consideration. The Chairperson may issue directions to any adjudicating officer concerning the procedure to be followed during inquiries and hearings. Any question arising as to whether a matter falls within the jurisdiction of a particular adjudicating authority shall be determined by the Chairperson whose decision shall be final. The Chairperson shall submit an annual report to the Central Government detailing the performance of all adjudicating authorities under this Act.

The Chairperson shall exercise such powers as are conferred upon them under this Act and may, subject to any rules made in this behalf, determine the procedure for conducting inquiries and hearings. The Chairperson is responsible for ensuring compliance with timelines prescribed for disposal of applications and appeals relating to layout-design registrations and infringement proceedings. Provided that, where a matter before the Chairperson involves technical aspects pertaining to semiconductor technology, they shall be assisted by an expert panel constituted in accordance with regulations framed by the Central Government. Any decision made by the Chairperson is subject to judicial review under established principles. The Chairperson may issue directions for rectification of errors appearing on the register and shall report annually to the Central Government regarding the performance of their duties as provided herein.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act may appeal to the Intellectual Property Tribunal. The Tribunal shall consider such appeals expeditiously and may, while hearing any appeal, require the Chairperson of the relevant authority to appear and produce records pertaining to the original decision. Failure to comply with such a requirement shall render the erring officer liable for a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees, recoverable from their salary. Further, where an appeal is filed alleging improper influence exerted upon the original adjudicating officer, the Tribunal may initiate inquiries into administrative misconduct, subject to applicable service rules and disciplinary proceedings. The Chairperson’s testimony before the Tribunal shall be deemed admissible as evidence.

The Chairperson may, upon application by a registered proprietor of a layout-design, grant a non-exclusive license to utilize the design for research purposes, provided that such application demonstrates a clear public benefit arising from the proposed research. Any assignment of rights under this Act relating to a layout-design shall be deemed valid only if executed in duplicate and duly notarized, with copies registered within three months as provided herein. Further, any licensee granted permission by the Chairperson is obligated to report annually on the progress and outcomes of their research, detailing any commercial applications derived from the licensed design. Failure to comply with this reporting requirement may result in revocation of the license and potential penalties under this Act. The Chairperson retains discretion regarding the terms and duration of such licenses, ensuring equitable consideration for both the proprietor and the public interest.

The functions conferred upon the Chairperson under this Act shall be exercised subject to the oversight and direction of the Governing Body, notwithstanding any challenge brought before the Intellectual Property Tribunal alleging undue influence from said body. Any decision made by the Chairperson concerning the registration of a layout-design, or relating to an interim injunction against infringement, may be appealed to the Tribunal within sixty days of communication thereof. The appeal shall not operate as a stay of the original order unless the Tribunal is satisfied that irreparable harm would result pending disposal of the appeal; provided that the applicant for such stay must demonstrate demonstrable prejudice. Further, any determination by the Chairperson regarding costs incurred in proceedings before them is open to review on grounds of manifest arbitrariness.

The Chairperson shall exercise such powers and perform such duties as may be prescribed under this Act and as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify. The Chairperson is responsible for ensuring the efficient conduct of proceedings before the Controller and for coordinating activities relating to the registration of layout-designs and related disputes. Business India situate outside of the territory of India may nominate a representative who shall act on behalf of such business in matters pertaining to applications or investigations under this Act, subject to the approval of the Chairperson. The Central Government shall consult with the Chairperson when formulating rules and regulations concerning the administration of this Act. Decisions regarding procedural irregularities shall be determined by the Chairperson after due consideration of representations from all affected parties. The Chairperson may issue directions to officers subordinate to him for the proper implementation of these provisions, provided that such directions are consistent with the objectives of this legislation.

The Chairperson shall exercise such powers and perform such duties as may be delegated by the Central Government under this Act. The Chairperson is responsible for ensuring compliance with all procedural requirements relating to applications filed by proprietors registered users seeking extensions of layout-design protection. Any application submitted failing to demonstrate continued commercial viability, as evidenced by audited financial statements presented annually, shall be rejected without further notice. Further, the Chairperson may direct a hearing if any objection is raised regarding the validity of such an extension, provided that the proprietor registered user is given reasonable opportunity to present their case and rebut evidence. Decisions made by the Chairperson concerning extensions are subject to review under established appellate procedures as provided herein.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act may appeal to the Intellectual Property Tribunal within sixty days from the date of such order. The Tribunal shall consider any violation concerning a layout design relation and determine whether the actions constitute infringement as defined herein. Failure to comply with a cease-and-desist order issued by the Tribunal shall be deemed a contempt of court, punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with a fine, or both, subject to judicial discretion. The Chairperson of the Intellectual Property Tribunal shall have the power to issue warrants and summon witnesses as provided under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. Penalties imposed are recoverable by way of suit in a civil court.

The Chairperson may, upon application by a registered proprietor seeking to assign or license rights in a layout-design, authorize the transfer of such rights subject to conditions deemed necessary to safeguard public interest and ensure equitable access. Such authorization shall be granted only if the applicant demonstrates that the proposed assignee or licensee possesses the requisite technical expertise and financial stability to adequately exploit the layout-design. Further, any assignment or license granted under this Act shall specify the geographical territory and field of use permitted. An appeal section shall exist wherein aggrieved parties may challenge decisions made by the Chairperson concerning the validity of such assignments or licenses, provided that the appeal is filed within sixty days from the date of notification of the order. The Chairperson’s decision on any appeal shall be final.

For the purposes of this Act, a “registered proprietor layout” means a layout-design which has been entered in the Register and in respect of which a certificate of registration has been granted under this Act; provided that such registration shall not confer upon the registered proprietor any right to prevent any person from using or importing any layout-design unless such use or import constitutes a reproduction of the registered layout-design. The term “registered proprietor layout” includes, subject to any conditions specified in the certificate of registration, the exclusive right to exploit commercially the layout-design as provided herein and shall be deemed to vest in the registrant until the expiration of the period for which registration is granted.

An application for registration of a layout-design shall include particulars verifying ownership and demonstrating that the applicant is the rightful registered proprietor layout of the design sought to be protected under this Act. Where an application discloses that the layout-design incorporates elements previously disclosed in another published work, the applicant must provide detailed documentation establishing their right to register the layout-design independently, subject to a determination by the Controller regarding originality and inventive step. The Registrar may require further evidence substantiating the claim of registered proprietor layout if doubts arise concerning the veracity of information presented within the application or relating to prior publication. Any alteration made to the layout-design after the date of application shall be disclosed and assessed for impact on novelty as provided herein.

Where any act is done without leave of the court in contravention of an order under this Act restraining any person from doing anything which would infringe the rights of the registered proprietor layout, such person shall be liable to pay damages to the registered proprietor layout. The amount of damages shall be determined having regard to the loss suffered by the registered proprietor layout and the need for deterring similar infringements. Provided that, in determining the quantum of damages, the court may take into account any benefit accruing to the infringing party directly or indirectly from the infringement. Further, a registered proprietor layout may institute appropriate proceedings against any person who reproduces, sells, offers to sell, hires or displays an integrated circuit layout-design which is substantially similar to their registered layout design.

Upon registration of a layout-design under this Act, the applicant shall become the registered proprietor layout and shall be entitled to exercise all rights pertaining thereto as provided herein. The Controller General may, upon application by any person claiming an interest in a layout-design already registered, entertain proceedings for rectification of the register if it appears that the registration was obtained through fraud or misrepresentation, or that there has been a material alteration of the registered layout-design without notice to and consent from the registered proprietor layout. Such applications shall be accompanied by a statement specifying the grounds upon which the application is based and supported by all relevant documents. The Controller General may require the registered proprietor layout to submit counter-statements and evidence in response to the rectification application. Decisions regarding rectification shall be made after affording both parties an opportunity of being heard, subject to any procedural safeguards as prescribed under this Act.

Where an application for registration of a layout-design is granted and a certificate of registration issued, the applicant shall become the registered proprietor layout in respect of that design. The registered proprietor layout shall have the exclusive right to exploit the layout-design commercially, subject to any conditions specified in the certificate of registration or imposed under this Act. Any person desiring to exploit a registered layout-design must obtain prior authorization from the registered proprietor layout, provided that such authorization may be granted on terms and conditions as determined by the Controller. Failure to comply with the prescribed procedures for obtaining authorization constitutes an infringement actionable under this Act. The registered proprietor layout shall maintain records of all licenses granted and make them available for inspection upon request by the Controller.

Any infringement of the rights of a registered proprietor layout shall render the infringing party liable for damages, including compensation for loss of profits and reasonable royalties, as determined by the High Court. Where an infringement has occurred, the registered proprietor layout may apply to restrain further acts of infringement through an injunction, subject to demonstrating actual harm or potential irreparable injury. Furthermore, any person found guilty of knowingly dealing with a counterfeit integrated circuit layout-design shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and with a fine not less than fifty thousand rupees; provided that repeat offenders are liable to double the penalty. The Central Government may issue guidelines regarding assessment of damages in cases involving infringement under this Act.

Where an application for registration is rejected under this Act, the applicant shall have the right to appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order of rejection; provided that the Appellant shall demonstrate reasonable grounds for challenging the findings of the Registrar concerning originality or lack of sufficient distinction. The Tribunal may, after affording an opportunity of being heard to both the appellant and the Registrar, confirm, vary, or reverse the order appealed against. Any party aggrieved by an order of the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal relating to the determination of rights of a registered proprietor layout may further appeal to the Supreme Court within sixty days, subject to satisfaction of the conditions prescribed under the relevant appellate provisions.

Where an application for registration of a layout-design is refused under this Act, the applicant shall have the right to appeal to the Appellate Board constituted under subsection (1) of section 48. Such appeal shall be made within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order of refusal and shall comply with the requirements as provided herein regarding form and content. The Appellate Board may, after affording an opportunity for a hearing to both the applicant and the Controller General, allow or dismiss the appeal, subject to such modifications as it deems fit. Further, any decision made by the International Bureau concerning the examination of an application for registration shall be taken into consideration by the Appellate Board in its deliberations regarding the merits of the appeal filed by a registered proprietor layout.

Any person who knowingly and wilfully reproduces an integrated circuit layout design in contravention of the rights of the registered proprietor layout shall be liable to pay damages equivalent to a sum not exceeding five per centum of the plaintiff’s aggregate turnover for any period of three years preceding the date of the institution of the suit, or ten lakh rupees, whichever is greater. Further, where a certificate purporting to be a copy of a registration certificate is presented as evidence in any proceeding under this Act, and it is subsequently proven that such certificate is false or fraudulently obtained, the person presenting said certificate shall be guilty of an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, and also liable to a fine. The Central Government may, by notification, prescribe guidelines regarding assessment of damages as provided herein.

Where an application for registration of a layout-design is opposed under this Act, and the Board finds that the opponent has established a case of prior use or other ground for opposition sufficient to warrant interim relief, it may grant an ex parte injunction restraining the applicant from exploiting the layout-design pending determination of the merits of the opposition. Such injunction shall be subject to such terms as the Board deems just, including requiring the opponent to furnish security for costs and damages. The registered proprietor layout shall retain all rights conferred under this Act notwithstanding any interlocutory order made by the Board; provided that a finding of prior use against the applicant does not prejudice their ultimate entitlement to compensation if infringement is subsequently established.

For the purposes of this Act, “notice” with respect to any action required or permitted thereunder shall mean a written communication directed to the relevant party and delivered in such form and manner as may be prescribed. The manner issuing notice shall include service by registered post with acknowledgement due, personal delivery, or publication in a widely circulated newspaper where the address of the intended recipient is unknown or cannot be ascertained with reasonable diligence. Provided that, any notice required to be given under this Act shall be deemed conclusively served on the date of dispatch when sent by registered post.

Where the Registrar deems it necessary to seek clarification or additional information from an applicant regarding a layout-design registration, the Registrar shall issue notice to the applicant. The manner issuing notice shall be in writing and delivered by registered post with acknowledgement due to the address specified by the applicant in their application form, or at such other address as may subsequently be notified under this Act. Provided that, if the applicant fails to acknowledge receipt of the notice within thirty days, a further notice may be served through publication in a widely circulated national newspaper. The Registrar shall record the details of each notice issued and any responses received, forming part of the registration file.

Where a registered proprietor alleges infringement of their layout-design, they shall serve notice on the alleged infringer specifying the particulars of the infringing integrated circuit and demanding cessation of the infringing activity. The manner issuing notice shall be in writing and delivered by registered post or electronic means with delivery acknowledgement, as prescribed by regulations framed under this Act. Failure to adhere to the prescribed manner may render the notice invalid. Provided that, where the alleged infringer is located outside India, service shall be effected through diplomatic channels or other internationally recognised methods. The proprietor shall also provide reasonable particulars of the layout-design and the basis for alleging infringement. A copy of such notice shall be filed with the relevant adjudicating officer within thirty days of dispatch.

Where the Registrar deems it necessary to bring any matter relating to a registered layout-design or application thereof to the attention of the interested parties, the Registrar shall issue notice in such manner as may be prescribed. Such notice shall ordinarily be served by registered post with acknowledgement due to the address specified in the register maintained under this Act. Provided that, where the registered proprietor has failed to acknowledge receipt of a previous communication within thirty days, subsequent notices relating to the same matter may be affixed on a conspicuous part of the premises for which the layout-design was registered. The Registrar shall record the date and manner of such affixation in the register. Any party aggrieved by the manner issuing notice may file an application before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board seeking redressal, subject to any fees prescribed under this Act.

Where the Registrar deems it necessary to communicate with any person concerning a matter arising under this Act, the manner issuing notice shall be as follows: such notice may be served by registered post acknowledgement due or through electronic means utilizing a secure and authenticated digital signature. Provided that, where service by registered post is chosen, the Registrar shall record the date of dispatch and receipt in the official register maintained for that purpose. Further, if the address of the intended recipient is unknown, the Registrar may publish the notice in a widely circulated national newspaper, specifying the subject matter and providing a period of thirty days for response. Any person failing to respond within this stipulated timeframe shall be deemed to have waived their right to contest the matter as provided herein.

Where any person intends to initiate proceedings alleging infringement of a registered layout-design, they shall provide written notice to the alleged infringer at their principal place of business or such other address as may be specified in the Register. The notice must clearly state the particulars of the alleged infringement and specify the remedies sought under this Act. Failure to comply with the prescribed manner issuing notice, including providing insufficient detail regarding the infringing activity, shall render the subsequent proceedings vulnerable to challenge and dismissal by the relevant court. Any party demonstrating prejudice due to non-compliance with these requirements may apply for a stay of proceedings or other appropriate relief as provided herein. Repeated failure to adhere to this process will be deemed contemptuous conduct subject to penalties.

Where a registered layout design owner desires to grant a license or assign their rights pertaining to a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design, they shall provide written notification to the Controller. This notice must detail the proposed licensee or assignee, the scope and duration of the license or assignment, and any royalties or other considerations involved. The Controller shall, upon receiving such notice, issue a public notice inviting objections within sixty days from the date of publication. Any interested party may submit representations concerning the propriety of the grant or assignment. Following this period, the Controller may proceed with registration of the license or assignment, subject to ensuring that it does not unduly prejudice the interests of other registered layout designs. The manner issuing notice shall adhere strictly to the prescribed forms and procedures detailed in the Regulations framed under this Act.

Where an interested party seeks to challenge a determination made by the Controller regarding infringement of a registered layout-design, such party shall provide written notice to the Controller and the respondent within thirty days of the publication of the determination. The manner issuing notice shall adhere strictly to Form LDN-7 as prescribed in the First Schedule, including particulars of the challenged determination and grounds for objection. Provided that, failure to comply with the requirements of Form LDN-7 will render the notice invalid, subject to a petition filed before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board demonstrating excusable delay and prejudice arising from circumstances beyond the petitioner’s control. The Controller may, at his discretion, entertain such petitions but shall not be bound to do so if the delay is deemed excessive or unwarranted.

Where an objection is raised against the registration of a layout-design, or any part thereof, based on similarity to a previously registered design internationally, the Registrar shall proceed to issue notice to both the objector and the applicant. The manner issuing notice in such circumstances shall conform strictly to the prescribed form detailed in Schedule B, ensuring clarity regarding the grounds for objection and timelines for response. Failure to adhere to this specified format will render the notice invalid and subject to challenge before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. Provided that, if the international registration was obtained through the International Bureau under the Hague Convention concerning the Deposit of Industrial Designs, the Registrar may accept evidence submitted electronically in lieu of physical documentation, as deemed appropriate.

For the purposes of this Act, “notice” with reference to any communication required or permitted to be given by or to any party shall mean a written document delivered personally or sent by registered post or recorded delivery. The manner issuing notice shall conform to the forms prescribed by the Trade Marks Registry and published in the Official Gazette. Such notice is deemed received on the date of personal delivery, or, where dispatched by post, seven days from the date of posting. Provided that any notice required under this Act may be served electronically, subject to verification protocols as determined by the Central Government.

Where an application for registration of a layout-design is deemed to be deficient, the Registrar shall issue notice to the applicant specifying the deficiencies and requiring them to rectify such deficiencies within a period not exceeding sixty days from the date of the notice. The manner issuing notice shall conform to Form D as prescribed in the First Schedule. Failure to comply with the requirements of the notice within the stipulated time may result in the application being deemed withdrawn, subject to an opportunity for reconsideration if the applicant can demonstrate that the delay was caused by circumstances beyond their reasonable control and establishes a clear priority date for the layout-design. Any such demonstration shall be accompanied by supporting documentation as determined by the Registrar.

Where a registered proprietor alleges infringement of their layout-design rights, they shall institute proceedings before the relevant jurisdictional authority. The proprietor may serve notice on the alleged infringer detailing the particulars of the suspected violation and demanding cessation of the infringing activity within sixty days. Failure to comply with such notice constitutes an aggravating factor in determining damages recoverable under this Act. The manner issuing notice shall adhere strictly to the prescribed form, available on the Controller General’s website, ensuring clarity regarding the layout-design allegedly infringed and the nature of the infringement. India filed months ago a clarification regarding procedural timelines for these notices, which are now incorporated into the updated guidelines. Provided that, if the alleged infringer disputes the validity of the registered layout-design, they may file a counter-notice within thirty days, triggering an investigation as provided herein.

Where a person aggrieved by any order passed under this Act, including an order relating to rectification or invalidation of a registered layout-design, believes that such order is manifestly unjust or perverse, he may prefer an application for review before the Controller. Such application shall be made within ninety days from the date of communication of the order and shall specify the grounds on which the applicant seeks review. The Controller may, after affording opportunity to all parties concerned, pass such orders as he deems fit, confirming, modifying, or reversing the original order. An application under section 26 procedure is subject to a fee prescribed by regulations framed by the Central Government. Any party dissatisfied with an order passed by the Controller in review may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days of that order’s communication.

Where an interested party seeks to challenge a determination made by the Controller relating to the validity of a registered layout-design, such party shall file an application before the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. The application must be accompanied by a certified copy of the order sought to be challenged and a statement specifying the grounds upon which the challenge is based. Under this Act, the applicant shall pay such fees as may be prescribed for the institution of proceedings. Provided that any person aggrieved by an interim order passed by the Controller relating to a layout-design may appeal against such order under section 26 procedure directly to the Tribunal. The Tribunal shall admit the application if it is satisfied that it is made within the time limit specified and that the applicant has locus standi. Notice of the proceedings shall be served upon all parties as provided herein.

An application for rectification of a registered layout-design, as provided herein, shall be made to the Controller in Form D and accompanied by the requisite fee. The applicant must demonstrate that the error or omission relates directly to particulars recorded during registration, and not to any subsequent use or alleged infringement. Subject to compliance with these requirements, the application may proceed under section 26 procedure. Any person aggrieved by a registered layout-design may also apply for rectification, provided that such grievance is substantiated by documentary evidence establishing clear error in the original record. The Controller shall provide an opportunity of being heard to both the applicant and the registered proprietor before issuing any order concerning rectification.

Where any party aggrieved by an order passed under this Act, including but not limited to orders relating to rectification or invalidation of a registered layout-design, desires to appeal, such party shall file an application for appeal with the Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of service of the order. The application shall specify the grounds of appeal and state the relief sought. Provided that where the aggrieved party was unable to apply for leave to appeal within the stipulated period due to circumstances beyond their control, they may apply to the Tribunal for condonation of delay accompanied by a supporting affidavit explaining the reasons for such failure. The Tribunal may entertain such application subject to satisfaction regarding the reasonableness of the delay and its cause; however, this does not preclude the possibility of further appeals under section 26 procedure to the High Court.

For the purpose of this Act, “layout design” shall include any three dimensional representation of a semiconductor integrated circuit or those relating to it. The term "appellate authority" means the body established under this Act for hearing appeals arising from orders passed by the Registrar and exercising such other powers as are conferred upon it by or under this Act. The manner applying appellate jurisdiction, including the form of petitions, timelines for filing submissions, and procedures for oral hearings, shall be prescribed by regulations framed by the Central Government. Provided that any regulation so framed shall not contradict provisions relating to natural justice.

An application for registration of a layout-design shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the relevant documentation establishing prior publication, if any, and such documentation must clearly indicate the date and place of first disclosure. The Registrar may require further clarification regarding the manner applying appellate procedures in cases where the applicant claims priority based on an earlier foreign application. Provided that the applicant demonstrates diligent pursuit of the foreign right, the registration shall be deemed to have been filed on the priority date. Any appeal against a decision refusing registration, or imposing conditions thereof, must be made within sixty days from the date of communication of the order and shall follow the manner applying appellate jurisdiction as prescribed under this Act.

Where a registered layout design is infringed, the owner shall be entitled to seek remedies as provided herein. The appropriate remedy shall include an injunction restraining the infringer from further infringing acts, and damages proportionate to the loss suffered by the owner, subject to a minimum amount determined by the Intellectual Property Tribunal. Further, any articles manufactured or imported in violation of this Act may be seized and destroyed at the owner’s expense. An appeal against an order made by the Intellectual Property Tribunal concerning the assessment of damages or the manner applying appellate jurisdiction shall lie to the High Court within whose territorial jurisdiction the cause of action arose. The aggrieved party may also seek interim relief pending determination of the matter, provided that security is furnished as deemed fit by the court.

Appeals arising from orders passed by the Controller relating to revocation of registration or any other matter determined under this Act shall be made to the Appellate Tribunal. The appeal shall be filed within sixty days from the date of communication of the order, and shall specify the grounds on which the order is sought to be challenged. Subject to provisions regarding limitation, an extension not exceeding thirty days may be granted by the Appellate Tribunal upon a showing of sufficient cause. The manner applying appellate jurisdiction requires that all relevant documents and arguments supporting the appeal must accompany the initial filing. Provided that where such documents are voluminous, they may be filed sequentially within fourteen days thereafter. The Controller shall furnish to the Appellate Tribunal a copy of the order appealed against and all related records. Any party aggrieved by an interim order passed by the Appellate Tribunal may seek redress through further appeal as provided herein.

An appeal against any order passed by the Registrar relating to the grant or refusal of registration, or concerning revocation of registration under this Act, shall be made within sixty days from the date of communication of such order. The appellant shall deposit with the Appellate Body a sum equivalent to twenty-five percent of the prescribed fee for the appeal; provided that any party demonstrating financial hardship may apply for a waiver or reduction of said fee, subject to review by the Board. Further, the manner applying appellate proceedings shall adhere strictly to the forms and procedures as notified by the Central Government from time to time. The Appellate Body may, after affording an opportunity of being heard to all concerned parties, confirm, vary, or reverse the order appealed against.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed by the Controller under this Act may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Tribunal. Such appeal shall be filed within sixty days from the date of communication of the order, and a memorandum of grounds of appeal shall accompany the application. Failure to file the appeal within the stipulated time shall ordinarily preclude consideration thereof, provided that the Tribunal may entertain appeals delayed due to force majeure or other exceptional circumstances, subject to such conditions as it deems fit. The manner applying appellate jurisdiction is governed by regulations framed by the Central Government and published in the Official Gazette. Penalties for non-compliance with these regulations include fines not exceeding ten thousand rupees and potential dismissal of the appeal.

Where the registered owner of a layout-design grants a license conferring rights to utilize, reproduce, or commercially exploit the design, such license shall be assignable subject to the terms and conditions stipulated therein. Any assignment undertaken without prior written consent from the licensee shall be deemed void. The assignee shall step into the shoes of the original licensor with respect to the assigned rights, possessing all privileges and obligations as if they were the initial grantor. Further, an appeal against any decision concerning the validity or enforceability of a license agreement or its assignment may be made to the Appellate Tribunal established under this Act within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. The manner applying appellate remedies shall adhere strictly to the procedural guidelines prescribed herein and as amended from time to time.

Where any party aggrieved by an order passed by the Controller under this Act is dissatisfied, such party may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Tribunal. The appeal shall lie within sixty days from the date of communication of the order and shall be in respect of any question of fact or law arising out of the decision or determination made by the Controller. Provided that the Appellate Tribunal may entertain appeals filed after the expiry of the said period if satisfactory reasons for the delay are tendered, subject to its discretion. The manner applying appellate proceedings before the Tribunal shall be as provided herein and shall not preclude the Tribunal from directing any party to furnish further information or evidence deemed necessary for a just resolution of the dispute.

Where a registered layout design is alleged to have been infringed, any interested person may institute an action for relief in a civil court having jurisdiction. Subject to appeal under this Act, such court shall determine whether the respondent has reproduced or done any act amounting to reproduction of the said layout design without authorization. The claimant shall be entitled to equitable remedies including injunctions restraining further acts of infringement and damages proportionate to the loss suffered. In assessing damages, the court may undertake a cc inquiry into the respondent’s profits derived from the infringing activity. Provided that where the infringement is deemed willful, enhanced damages may be awarded. The manner applying appellate review shall adhere strictly to procedural guidelines established by the High Court.

An appeal against any order passed by the Registrar relating to the registration of a layout-design or concerning any matter arising under this Act shall be made to the Appellate Tribunal. The application for appeal shall be in the prescribed form and shall specify the order appealed from, the grounds on which it is sought to be set aside, and the relief claimed. Such an application must be filed within sixty days from the date of communication of the order to the appellant. The Registrar may, before entertaining any such appeal, require the applicant to satisfy himself as to the maintainability of the appeal and may direct him to file additional documents or information as deemed necessary. The manner applying appellate jurisdiction is governed by regulations framed under this Act. Further, a registrar application prescribed for submission of evidence shall be accompanied by an affidavit verifying its authenticity.

For the purposes of this Act, “prescribed form” means a form specified in the First Schedule or as may be prescribed by the Central Government and includes any alterations or additions thereto directed by the Controller; the term shall also encompass any digital format approved under regulations framed by the government. The manner issuing certificates relating to layout-design registration, including but not limited to those pertaining to extensions of time for filing documents or rectification of errors, shall be as prescribed in the Second Schedule and subject to such conditions as may be deemed necessary by the Controller. Any deviation from the prescribed form or manner issuing is void.

An application for registration of a layout design shall be accompanied by such particulars as may be prescribed, including a representation of the integrated circuit in a form suitable for reproduction and verification. The Registrar may require the applicant to furnish further information or clarification regarding the layout design, provided that any such request must specify the deficiencies perceived. The manner issuing certificates of registration shall conform strictly to the format detailed in Schedule A, appended hereto. Any alteration to this prescribed manner requires prior notification published in the Official Gazette. Furthermore, an appeal against a refusal of registration may be made within sixty days from the date of communication of the order, detailing the grounds for challenge and submitting supporting documentation as stipulated under this Act.

Where a registered layout design is infringed, the owner shall be entitled to seek an injunction restraining the infringing party from continuing such infringement and for damages sustained by reason thereof. The measure of damages shall be determined in accordance with principles of fairness and equity, taking into consideration the loss of profits suffered by the owner and any damage caused to their reputation as a result of the unauthorized use of the layout design. Further, the Court may order the delivery up or destruction of infringing layouts, tools, equipment, and materials used in the manufacture thereof. The Registrar shall prescribe the manner issuing notices relating to infringement proceedings under this Act, ensuring due process for all parties involved. Provided that any application seeking remedies must be filed within three years from the date of first proven infringement.

Applications for registration of a layout-design shall be submitted to the Controller in the prescribed form, accompanied by requisite fees and such documentation as may be specified. The Controller shall issue a public notice inviting objections within two months from the date of receipt of the application. Any person aggrieved by the proposed registration may file an objection, setting forth the grounds thereof, in the manner determined by the Controller. Upon consideration of any objections received, the Controller may proceed with or reject the application. Where the Controller deems it necessary to seek further clarification from the applicant, a written request shall be issued, allowing fifteen days for response. The manner issuing registration certificates and subsequent amendments thereto is governed by regulations framed under this Act. Any appeal against an order of the Controller shall lie before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

An application for registration of a layout-design shall be accompanied by such particulars and documents as may be prescribed, including detailed schematics conforming to the standards specified in Schedule A. The Registrar shall issue directions regarding the format and content of these submissions; any deviation from said directions will render the application liable for rejection. Subject to compliance with regulations concerning confidentiality, applicants may request preliminary advice on their layout-design’s registrability. The manner issuing certificates of registration shall be as provided herein, including stipulations relating to affixation of seals and signatures by authorized officers. Provided that, any alteration to a registered layout-design requires prior notification and approval from the Registrar, following a prescribed procedure.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order. The Board shall, while hearing appeals, follow the manner issuing notices to all concerned parties and afford them a reasonable opportunity for being heard. Failure to comply with the prescribed procedures relating to the filing of appeals or the presentation of evidence shall render the appeal liable to dismissal. Any attempt to obstruct the proceedings before the Appellate Board, or to influence its decision through fraudulent means, shall be deemed a cognizable offence punishable with imprisonment and a fine as determined by the competent court. The Registrar may, subject to regulations framed under this Act, prescribe the manner of serving documents related to appeals.

Where a layout design owner grants a license conferring the right to manufacture integrated circuits incorporating their protected layout, such license shall specify the precise scope of permitted acts, including but not limited to, geographical territory and duration. The licensee may further assign or transfer this license subject to prior written consent from the original layout design owner, provided that any assignee assumes all obligations and liabilities arising under the original licensing agreement. Failure to obtain such consent renders the assignment void. The manner issuing subsequent licenses by an assignee shall be consistent with the terms of the initial grant unless expressly modified in writing and agreed upon by both the original owner and the assignee. Any alteration to the permitted uses or geographical scope requires a formal amendment, duly recorded with the Controller General.

Where an application for registration is rejected, the Registrar shall provide a reasoned order specifying the grounds for rejection. Any party aggrieved by such an order may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. The manner issuing notices pertaining to appeals under this Act shall be as prescribed in the First Schedule; however, any deviation from these prescriptions must be demonstrably justified due to circumstances specific to the appellant’s location or disability. Provided that, if the Registrar considers the rejection manifestly without merit, he may issue a corrigendum and proceed with registration, but such action is subject to challenge by any interested party within thirty days thereafter.

The Central Government shall, by notification in the Official Gazette, prescribe the manner issuing certificates of registration relating to layout designs and integrated circuits. Such prescriptions may specify forms for application, declarations required from applicants, and procedures for verification of claims made therein. The chairperson shall ensure that all notifications issued under this Act are consistent with established principles of intellectual property law and international best practices. Provided that, where the Central Government deems it necessary to amend or clarify the manner issuing such certificates, a draft notification shall be published for public feedback prior to finalization. This process is subject to review by an advisory committee constituted as provided herein.

Where a registered patent agent, acting on behalf of an applicant for registration of a layout-design, fails to comply with any procedural requirement as provided herein, including but not limited to the timely filing of prescribed forms or the payment of requisite fees, the Registrar may issue a notice specifying the deficiency and granting a period not exceeding thirty days for rectification. Failure to rectify the deficiency within that period shall result in the application being deemed abandoned, without prejudice to any penalties under this Act. The manner issuing notices concerning deficiencies shall be determined by regulations framed by the Central Government. Any party aggrieved by an action taken by the Registrar relating to abandonment may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within a period of sixty days from the date of communication of such action.

An application for registration of a layout-design shall be accompanied by such particulars and documents as the Registrar may prescribe, provided that any applicant demonstrating compliance with established industry standards relating to digital representation of integrated circuits may submit documentation in a format deemed acceptable by the Registrar. The Registrar shall issue certificates of registration in the manner prescribed under this Act, indicating the date of application and the layout-design’s unique identification number as assigned upon acceptance for examination. Any registered layout-design is subject to periodic review; failure to maintain accurate records pertaining to commercial exploitation may result in revocation proceedings initiated by the Registrar. The manner issuing certificates shall adhere strictly to guidelines published by the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trademarks.

For the purpose of this Act, “procedure” with respect to any application, notice, or other document required or permitted to be filed under this Act shall mean the specific steps and formalities prescribed by regulations framed by the Central Government. Such procedure may include, but is not limited to, requirements regarding form, language, verification, fees, and modes of delivery. Any deviation from the prescribed procedure shall render the application or notice void, subject to any exemptions granted by the Controller based on demonstrable hardship. The Central Government may amend these procedures as deemed necessary for efficient administration, provided that such amendments are published in the Official Gazette at least thirty days prior to their effective date.

An application for registration of a layout-design shall be accompanied by such particulars as may be prescribed, including a representation of the integrated circuit in a form acceptable to the Registrar. The applicant shall furnish an execution report verifying the authenticity of the layout-design and detailing the process followed during its creation. Upon receipt of an application, the Registrar may direct the applicant to rectify any deficiencies or provide further clarification regarding the design's technical specifications. Any objection raised by a third party against the registration procedure must be submitted within sixty days from the date of publication of the application under this Act. The Registrar shall afford both the applicant and the objector an opportunity for hearing, as provided herein, before making any determination on the validity of the layout-design.

Where a registered layout design is infringed, the owner shall be entitled to seek remedies as provided herein. The injured party may institute civil proceedings for damages, which shall include compensation for loss of profits and any measure of the damage suffered by the owner attributable to the infringement. Further, subject to demonstrating reasonable efforts to mitigate losses, exemplary damages may be awarded at the discretion of the court. A request for an injunction restraining further acts of infringement is also permissible under this Act. The procedure for determining the extent of damages shall follow principles of fairness and proportionality, considering factors such as the duration of the infringing activity and the willful nature thereof. Any party aggrieved by a decision regarding remedies may appeal to the relevant appellate forum as prescribed.

An application for registration of a layout-design shall be filed with the Registrar in such form and containing such particulars as may be prescribed. The applicant shall furnish along with the application, a copy of the layout-design in electronic format, conforming to standards specified by the Controller General. Upon receipt of an application, the Registrar shall issue an acknowledgment under this Act. Any person aggrieved by any order passed by the Registrar relating to registration or refusal thereof may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order. The procedure for filing and disposal of appeals shall be as provided herein, subject to such conditions regarding fees and time limits as are prescribed in the Regulations framed under this Act. The Registrar may require further information or clarification from the applicant at any stage of the registration process.

An application for registration of a layout-design shall be accompanied by such particulars as may be prescribed, including a detailed description of the fabrication process employed and a statement affirming compliance with all applicable standards relating to design security. The Registrar shall, upon receipt of an application, verify that it conforms to the requirements outlined herein and that the requisite fee has been duly paid. Failure to provide complete or accurate information will result in rejection of the application under this Act. Any applicant aggrieved by such a decision may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days of receiving notification of the Registrar’s order, following the prescribed procedure for appeals as provided herein.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act may, subject to the provisions herein, prefer an appeal from such order to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. The appeal shall be filed within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order and shall specify the grounds on which the appeal is based. Failure to file the appeal within the stipulated time shall render the appellant liable for a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees, recoverable as arrears of land revenue. Where an appeal has been admitted by the Tribunal, the procedure for hearing the appeal shall be as determined by the Tribunal, provided that the respondent may submit written arguments within thirty days of the date of admission.

Where a layout design owner grants a license conferring rights to utilize, reproduce, or commercially exploit a registered integrated circuit layout design, such license shall be documented in writing and specify the scope of permitted acts, including but not limited to manufacturing, importing, selling, or hiring. The procedure for assignment of licenses is governed by this Act; any assignment must clearly identify both the assignor and assignee, along with a precise description of the rights being transferred. Provided that the license agreement explicitly outlines royalty payments, if applicable, and duration, it shall be deemed valid under this Act. Furthermore, where an assignment involves partial transfer of layout design rights, the remaining ownership shall vest in the original owner unless otherwise stipulated within the assignment document. Any modification to a licensed arrangement requires written consent from all parties involved, following the established procedure for amendments as provided herein.

Where any party aggrieved by an order passed under this Act, relating to the determination of infringement or validity of a registered layout-design, desires to appeal, such party shall, within sixty days from the date of communication of the order, file an application for leave to appeal with the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. The Tribunal may, after hearing all parties involved and subject to satisfaction that the order in question is erroneous in law or on the facts, grant leave to appeal. Provided that if the aggrieved party fails to apply for leave within the stipulated period, such omission shall be considered a waiver of the right to appeal, and no further proceedings relating to the matter shall be entertained unless the Tribunal deems it fit to condone the delay on sufficient cause shown. The procedure for appeals before the Tribunal shall be as provided herein.

An applicant seeking registration of a layout-design shall, as part of the prescribed procedure, submit with the application a detailed technical description outlining the functionality and intended use of the integrated circuit. The Registrar may require further clarification or supplementary documentation to ascertain compliance with the requirements under this Act relating to novelty and originality. Upon receipt of an application, the Registrar shall issue a public notice inviting objections from any interested party within a period specified herein. Any objection received shall be promptly communicated to the applicant, who is then afforded an opportunity to submit a written response addressing the concerns raised. The registration process continues with examination by the Registrar, and may include inspection of working models where deemed necessary for verification purposes; successful completion leads to grant of register patents.

Where a layout design owner, being a person or body corporate engaged in the manufacture of semiconductors integrated circuits, grants a license to another party for the exploitation of their registered layout design, such license shall specify the precise scope of permitted activities, including but not limited to reproduction, modification, and commercial use. The procedure for assignment of licenses is governed by regulations framed under this Act; any assignee shall notify the Registrar within thirty days of the transfer, providing details as prescribed. Further, where a layout design incorporates elements that also constitute a well-known trade mark, the license agreement must explicitly address rights pertaining to such marks and ensure no infringement occurs during exploitation. The licensor may impose reasonable conditions restricting the use of the layout design beyond the agreed scope, provided that these conditions are clearly stated in the written license document.

An application for registration of a layout design shall be accompanied by such particulars as may be prescribed, including detailed schematics illustrating the topological representation of the integrated circuit. The Registrar may require applicants to furnish additional information or clarifications regarding the layout design’s functionality and intended use, provided that such requests are limited to ensuring compliance with the provisions under this Act. Regarding the manner applications clause, all submissions must adhere strictly to the prescribed forms available on the designated online portal; deviations from these formats will render the application liable for rejection without further notice. The applicant shall also declare ownership of the layout design and affirm its originality, subject to verification by the Registrar.

Where a person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act relating to the revocation or modification of registration, or concerning any right conferred thereby, seeks redressal, such person shall be entitled to file an appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. The appeal shall be filed within ninety days from the date of communication of the order. Provided that the Tribunal may entertain appeals filed after the said period if it is satisfied that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from filing the appeal within the stipulated time, and such delay did not substantially prejudice the respondent. Applications under this Act concerning rectification proceedings shall adhere strictly to the manner applications clause prescribed in Schedule II, ensuring all requisite forms and declarations are duly completed. Failure to comply with these procedural requirements may result in rejection of the application.

An application for registration of a layout design shall be accompanied by such particulars as may be prescribed, including but not limited to, a detailed description of the fabrication process employed and a list of all materials utilized in its creation.
