Such proceedings may include claims for injunction restraining any act of manufacture, sale, hire, use, or importation infringing upon the said geographical indication. Provided that, where an infringer has acted in good faith and without knowledge of the registered plaintiff right, the court may, subject to considerations of public interest, grant a reasonable period within which such infringement shall cease. Further, damages recoverable under this Act shall be determined based on the loss suffered by the proprietor or authorized user, taking into account any profits made by the infringer.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any registered proprietor of a plaintiff right geographical indication shall be entitled to grant licenses conferring specific rights relating to the use of such indication on goods or services. Such licenses may be exclusive or non-exclusive, and may specify territory, time period, and permitted uses as determined by the grantor. Assignment of a plaintiff right geographical indication, including all associated licensing agreements, requires prior approval from the Geographical Indications Registry, provided that the assignee demonstrates sufficient capacity to uphold the standards of quality and authenticity linked to the indication. Any transfer or assignment undertaken without such approval shall be deemed null and void. Further, any licensee may sub-license rights granted under this Act with the express written consent of the registered proprietor, as provided herein.

The Registrar shall, upon receiving an application for registration of a geographical indication, provide notice thereof to any persons or parties claiming through prior usage or other rights under this Act. Any such claimant may, within sixty days from the date of publication of the notice, file objections with the Registrar detailing the grounds on which the registration should be refused. Provided that, where an objection is based upon a plaintiff right geographical indication already recognized in another jurisdiction, the claimant shall submit evidence substantiating said recognition and its impact on Indian trade. The Registrar shall consider all such objections and may afford the applicant and objector opportunities for hearing. Any order passed by the Registrar concerning registration or refusal of registration may be appealed to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within a period of three months from the date of receipt of the order.

An application for registration of a geographical indication shall be deemed to include an assertion of plaintiff right geographical over the goods specified therein. The Registrar may, upon receiving such an application, issue a public notice inviting objections from any interested party, provided that any objection must specify the grounds on which it is based and demonstrate a substantial interest in maintaining the distinctiveness of similar goods. Where an objection is received, the Registrar shall provide the applicant with an opportunity to file a reply addressing the concerns raised. The relationship proposed registered between the geographical indication and the goods shall be scrutinized by the Registrar for conformity with the standards prescribed under this Act. Any party aggrieved by a decision of the Registrar may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such decision, as provided herein.

An application for registration of a geographical indication shall include particulars specifying the name of the agricultural product, foodstuff, or other goods for which the indication is sought, along with a map of the defined geographic area. The Registrar may require the applicant to furnish further details concerning the qualities, reputation, or characteristics directly attributable to the origin of the goods and linking them uniquely to that place. Where an objection is raised against registration on grounds of likelihood of confusion with any prior trademark or other similar indication, the applicant shall be afforded a reasonable opportunity for rebuttal under this Act. The geographical indication complained of must demonstrate a continuous link between the product and its specified origin; otherwise, registration may be refused.

Any proprietor seeking remedies under this Act relating to a registered geographical indication shall be entitled to apply to the relevant jurisdictional authority for an injunction restraining any person from making, using, or applying for registration of a sign that is identical or deceptively similar to the registered geographical indication complained. Such application may include claims for damages sustained by the proprietor as a direct result of the infringing activity, subject to proof of actual financial loss and reasonable mitigation efforts undertaken. The authority shall consider evidence presented regarding consumer confusion arising from the use of the impugned sign, and may order the infringer to account for profits derived from the deceptive practice. Provided that, where the infringement was demonstrably unintentional and without malicious intent, the authority may impose a lesser penalty or require corrective measures instead of monetary damages.

An application for registration of a geographical indication shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the relevant documents establishing, subject to any directions issued by the Geographical Indications Registry, the conditions necessary to demonstrate origin. The Registrar may require the applicant to furnish further particulars or evidence concerning the characteristics and qualities of the goods, as well as the methods of production applicable to the geographical indication complained of. Where an objection is raised against the registration on grounds that the proposed name misdescribes the goods or is contrary to law or morality, the Registrar shall give notice thereof to the applicant and any other interested party. Any interested party may file their response within a period specified by the Registrar. The Registrar shall consider such objections and responses before proceeding with the application, and may require a hearing to be held for the determination of the matter.

An application for registration as a Geographical Indication shall be deemed invalid if, prior to the date of such application, the name or sign proposed for registration has been used extensively by any person other than an authorized user, provided that such use did not constitute commercial exploitation of the product’s qualities and reputation. The Registrar may require the applicant to submit documentary evidence demonstrating adherence to established production practices and quality control measures specific to the geographical territory claimed, as defined in the application. Further, a Geographical Indication complained of shall not be registrable if it is deemed deceptive or misleading regarding the origin or nature of the goods; this determination shall consider prevailing consumer perceptions within India.

Any person aggrieved by the registration of a geographical indication may institute an action in the High Court, subject to payment of prescribed fees, alleging inter alia that the said indication is deceptively similar to another mark already registered under the Trade Marks Act. The court shall have power to grant such relief as it deems just, including but not limited to the cancellation of registration and an injunction restraining further use of the geographical indication complained of. Provided that any order made by the High Court may be appealed to the Supreme Court within a period of ninety days from the date of the order. Failure to comply with an injunction shall render the defaulting party liable to a penalty, as determined by the court, and may also attract imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months.

The registered proprietor of a geographical indication shall be entitled to grant non-exclusive licenses conferring the right to make, sell, offer for sale, or import goods identified by the said indication. Such licenses may be granted on such terms and conditions as are agreed upon between the proprietor and the licensee, provided that any license agreement explicitly states the scope of permitted use and geographical area covered. Assignment of a registered geographical indication is permissible subject to prior approval from the Geographical Indications Registry, ensuring continued adherence to quality standards associated with the indication. Further, where an assignment includes rights relating to pending applications for similar indications, the assignee shall undertake to maintain the distinctiveness of the geographical indication complained of and prevent any dilution thereof through misleading practices or unauthorized use. The Registrar may require undertakings as a condition of approval.

Where an application for registration of a geographical indication is opposed, the Appellate Board may, upon receiving written submissions from both the applicant and the opponent, direct the Registrar to conduct a hearing. Such hearing shall be deemed a quasi-judicial proceeding under this Act. The opponent alleging misuse of the geographical indication complained of must demonstrate, with credible evidence, that the use in question causes or is likely to cause dilution of the distinctive character or reputation associated with the registered indication. Provided that, the applicant may present counter-evidence refuting such claims and demonstrating lack of consumer confusion. The Board’s decision shall be final, subject to appeal before the High Court within a period of ninety days from the date of the order.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, an application for registration as a Geographical Indication shall include a detailed description of the goods or products for which the indication is sought, accompanied by verifiable data substantiating their unique qualities attributable solely to the geographical origin. Such data may incorporate visual recordings demonstrating traditional production methods and distinctive characteristics, provided that these recordings are authenticated by recognized experts in the relevant field and submitted as supporting evidence. The Registrar may reject an application if the proposed Geographical Indication complained of is deemed descriptive of the goods or services, or if its use would mislead consumers regarding the origin of those goods or services. Further, any prior usage or registration affecting the distinctiveness of the indication shall be considered during assessment.

Any person aggrieved by the registration or non-registration of a geographical indication may institute proceedings before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board, subject to appeal to the High Court. Where it is demonstrated that the continued use of a geographical indication complained of constitutes an unfair trade practice or misrepresentation likely to deceive or cause confusion, the Board shall order its cessation and impose a penalty not exceeding five lakhs rupees for each instance of infringement. Further penalties may be levied where the violation is repeated, potentially doubling the initial fine. The registration variety of a geographical indication shall not protect trivial or minor deviations from the registered form, provided that such variations do not mislead consumers regarding origin.

The owner of a registered Geographical Indication shall be entitled to grant exclusive licenses conferring specific rights relating to the use of such indication on goods, provided that any such license agreement specifies the scope of permitted use, including but not limited to product categories and geographical territories. Such licenses may be assigned to third parties with the prior written consent of the Registrar, who may require payment of a transfer fee equivalent to twenty-five percent of the current registry fee for the Geographical Indication. Where an exclusive license is granted, the licensee shall be bound by any conditions imposed on the owner under this Act and shall remain liable for compliance therewith. Further, the owner’s consent for assignment or licensing may be withheld if deemed detrimental to the continued protection of the Geographical Indication complained of, particularly where it involves a substantial alteration in production methods or quality standards.

Where an application for registration of a geographical indication is opposed, the Registrar may, upon receiving evidence from either party demonstrating ambiguity or lack of clarity in the originally filed claim specification, direct the applicant to undertake a claim specification amendment. Such direction shall not prejudice the rights of the opponent unless the amended specification substantially alters the essential characteristics of the goods or products for which registration is sought. An appeal lies to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board against any order directing such an amendment, and the Board may allow the appeal or dismiss it, subject to just terms and conditions. The burden shall be on the appellant to demonstrate that the Registrar’s decision was manifestly unjust or beyond its powers under this Act concerning a geographical indication complained of.

For the purposes of this Act, “essentially derived variety” means a variety that is not clearly distinguishable from the original variety according to the characteristics indicated in its documentation and which, subject to section 29, has been obtained through any conventional techniques like cross-pollination or genetic engineering. A variety shall be deemed essentially derived if it is visibly, functionally, or genotypically identical to the original variety for all traits that are assessed under this Act; however, minor variations arising from stress conditions or geographical location shall not disqualify a variety as non-essentially derived. The india department agriculture shall maintain records pertaining to varietal characteristics and assessment protocols.

An application for registration of a Plant Variety shall be made to the Plant Varieties Registration and Farmers’ Rights Authority in such form and manner as may be prescribed. Such application shall include particulars relating to the genetic composition of the variety, its expression potential, and stability over successive generations. The applicant shall furnish documentation demonstrating that the variety is distinct, uniform, and stable, conforming to established criteria under this Act. Where the Plant Variety has been developed through utilization of germplasm obtained from india department agriculture sources, acknowledgement of such source shall be explicitly stated in the application. Further, any technical data pertaining to the novelty assessment must be submitted for verification by the Authority.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act relating to the revocation of a Plant Variety Protection, or concerning the imposition of any penalty for infringement of Farmers’ Rights, may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of such order. The Appellate Board shall consider all materials placed before it and may affirm, modify, or reverse the original order. Where an infringement of Farmers' Rights has occurred, the aggrieved farmer shall be entitled to compensation commensurate with the loss suffered, determined by the Board based on prevailing market rates and agricultural practices. Further, the india department agriculture shall provide assistance in assessing damages and facilitating mediation between parties. The Appellate Board’s decision is final, subject to challenge only under writ jurisdiction before a High Court.

Applications for registration of a Plant Variety shall be filed with the Registrar, specifying particulars including but not limited to the variety denomination, geographical area from which seeds or other propagating material are available, and details of its expression. The application shall be accompanied by documentation demonstrating genetic uniformity and stability as determined through established testing procedures approved by the india department agriculture. Any person claiming rights in a Plant Variety may oppose registration within a period prescribed herein, submitting reasons supported by evidence to the Registrar who shall provide an opportunity for hearing both the applicant and the opponent. Decisions of the Registrar regarding objections are subject to appeal to the Appellate Board. The Authority may issue guidelines concerning appropriate testing methodologies and data analysis relevant to assessing distinctness, uniformity, and stability.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, any person seeking authorization for conducting a Research Activity involving the utilization of Plant Genetic Resources originating in India shall submit an application to the india department agriculture detailing the proposed methodology, anticipated outcomes, and measures undertaken to safeguard Farmers' Rights. Such applications must include a comprehensive assessment demonstrating adherence to bio-safety protocols as prescribed by the competent regulatory authority. The Authority may require additional information or modifications to the Research Activity proposal to ensure equitable benefit sharing with local communities and compliance with extant intellectual property regulations. Failure to comply with these conditions shall render the authorization liable for revocation, following due process and opportunity for hearing.

Any person who knowingly makes any false statement or suppresses material facts in an application for registration of a plant variety, or in any documentation submitted under this Act, shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees, and may also be subject to proceedings for revocation of registration. Furthermore, officers of the india department agriculture, upon reasonable suspicion, are empowered to conduct inspections of farms and research facilities involved in plant breeding activities; failure to comply with such inspection requests constitutes an offense punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year. The Central Government may issue directions regarding compliance with bio-containment protocols during genetic modification experiments related to registered varieties, and non-compliance shall attract penalties as provided herein.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and any rules made thereunder, a person holding an entitlement under this Act relating to a plant variety may grant a license conferring specific rights in respect of the commercial use of such variety. Such licenses may be granted for a term not exceeding five years, renewable by mutual agreement between the grantor and licensee. The terms of any such license shall specify the geographical area within which the licensee is authorized to conduct activities related to the plant variety, as well as the specific rights being assigned, including but not limited to seed production, distribution, or cultivation. Further, a license granted under this Act may be assigned by the licensee with the prior written consent of the grantor, provided that such assignment does not alter the fundamental terms and conditions established in the original agreement. The india department agriculture shall maintain a record of all licenses and assignments relating to plant varieties registered under this Act.

Where a Plant Variety Protection Appeal Tribunal determines, upon review of evidence presented under this Act, that the Registrar’s decision regarding eligibility for protection has been manifestly arbitrary or based on an erroneous interpretation of prevailing agricultural practices, it may remit the matter to the Registrar for reconsideration. Such remittal shall specify the grounds for the determination and direct the Registrar to provide a reasoned order within sixty days. Any party aggrieved by the Tribunal's order may further appeal to the High Court within ninety days, subject to demonstrating substantial cause for delay. The india department agriculture shall be deemed a necessary party in any proceedings concerning disputes over farmers’ rights relating to saved seed.

For the purposes of this Act, "Farmers' Rights" includes the right of farmers to save, reuse, exchange, share or sell farm saved seed, subject to conditions as may be specified under this Act; and such rights shall not extend to commercial exploitation of plant varieties without prior authorization from the Authority. The term “farm saved seed” means a seed obtained by a farmer from his own yield during any previous harvest. A farmer engaging in traditional breeding methods, or a performer contributing to the genetic improvement of a variety through indigenous knowledge, shall be deemed to have exercised Farmers' Rights as provided herein, and such activities are not considered infringement under this Act. The india department agriculture will provide guidance on best practices for seed management.

Applications for registration of a Plant Variety shall include particulars relating to its denomination, geographical area where it is cultivated, and any relevant index names registered under this Act. The application must specify the method of propagation employed and provide detailed information regarding the expression of essential characteristics which differentiate the variety from other known varieties. Further, applicants shall furnish documentation substantiating their claim of novelty and distinctiveness, including data derived from field trials conducted in accordance with guidelines issued by the india department agriculture. Any prior disclosure of the Plant Variety before the date of application shall be disclosed to the Authority, subject to provisions regarding grace periods as provided herein.

For the purposes of this Act, “crop sciences indian” means the application of scientific principles and techniques relating to plant breeding, genetics, physiology, agronomy, soil science, and related disciplines, specifically adapted for agricultural practices within the territory of India; it includes, but is not limited to, methods employed in the isolation, identification, characterization, and utilization of genetic resources. An expression of crop sciences indian shall be deemed to include any modification or improvement made through conventional breeding techniques or innovative biotechnological approaches, subject to compliance with all applicable regulations under this Act concerning biosafety and intellectual property rights.

An application for registration of a novel plant variety shall include a detailed description conforming to internationally recognized descriptors and incorporating data derived from established crop sciences indian methodologies. Such description must accurately reflect the expression of traits in successive generations, demonstrating stability and uniformity across diverse agro-climatic conditions. The applicant shall furnish documentation substantiating the distinctiveness of the variety, including comparative performance data against extant varieties commonly cultivated within India. Further, a proposal for gene banking material preservation is required, ensuring long-term conservation of the registered plant variety’s genetic resources. Provided that any prior disclosure of the variety before application filing will be considered under this Act and may impact registration eligibility.

Where a Plant Breeder’s Authorization is revoked under this Act, any person who has lawfully acquired propagating material of the variety prior to the date of revocation shall retain the right to use such propagating material for personal cultivation and seed production for their own consumption or distribution amongst members of their cooperative society, subject to conditions as may be prescribed. This provision does not grant a commercial right to sell propagating material derived from the revoked authorization. Any infringement of plant breeder’s rights relating to crop sciences indian varieties shall render the infringing party liable to pay damages commensurate with the loss suffered by the Plant Breeder, determined by the Authority. Further, the Authority may order the seizure and destruction of any propagating material produced or marketed in violation of these provisions, provided that due process is followed.

Applications for registration of a Plant Variety shall include a detailed description conforming to the format prescribed by the Register, encompassing morphological characteristics, physiological traits, and data pertaining to its expression across diverse agro-climatic zones. The application must specify the duration of vegetative propagation, if applicable, and provide evidence demonstrating genetic uniformity within the variety. Any prior disclosure of the Plant Variety, whether through publication or commercialization, shall be disclosed in the application; failure to do so may render the application liable for rejection under this Act. Assessments by Examining Authorities will incorporate principles of crop sciences indian methodology, including but not limited to field trials conducted according to established protocols and statistical analysis of relevant data. The Register may require supplementary information as deemed necessary to ascertain distinctiveness and stability.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, any person seeking grant of a Plant Variety Protection for a novel variety developed through crop sciences indian techniques or conventional breeding methods shall submit an application detailing the genetic composition, lineage, and distinctiveness of the variety. The application must include data demonstrating stability of the characteristics across successive generations and in comparison to commonly cultivated varieties. Furthermore, evidence confirming that the variety possesses at least one desirable trait, such as enhanced yield, disease resistance, or improved nutritional content, is required for consideration. Any modification to the submitted data after initial assessment may render the application liable for rejection, provided that the modifications materially affect the claimed distinctiveness.

Any person who, having knowledge of the registration of a Plant Variety, commercially exploits such variety without authorization from the Registrar, or in contravention of the terms and conditions stipulated during registration, shall be liable to pay compensation determined by the Central Government. Such compensation may include damages sustained by the registered plant breeder, reasonable costs incurred in pursuing legal remedies, and an additional penalty not exceeding five times the value of the infringing exploitation. Further, any entity found guilty of repeated violations under this Act relating to crop sciences indian practices shall face suspension of their registration for a period as determined by the Registrar. The Central Government may issue directives regarding enforcement actions against those engaging in unauthorized propagation or marketing of protected plant varieties.

The right to commercialize a Plant Variety conferred under this Act may be assigned or licensed subject to conditions stipulated herein. Any license granted for propagation material derived from a registered variety shall clearly define the geographical area and duration of such authorization. The Assignor or Licensor, being the original registrant, retains the power to audit records pertaining to royalty collection and utilization by the Licensee, ensuring adherence to agreed-upon terms. Further provision is made that any sub-licensing activity requires prior written consent from the Assignor, failing which it shall be deemed a breach of contract. The application of crop sciences Indian principles in developing new varieties necessitates careful consideration of farmer’s rights; therefore, licenses granted to corporations must include provisions for equitable benefit sharing with farming communities involved in initial breeding trials or conservation efforts related to the protected variety.

Where a Plant Variety Protection Appellate Tribunal determines, upon review of evidence presented under this Act, that an allegation of infringement has arisen from legitimate crop sciences indian research activities undertaken for the purpose of breeding new varieties, it shall issue an order directing the complainant to engage in mediation with the accused. Such mediation shall be facilitated by a mediator appointed by the Central Government and conducted within a period not exceeding ninety days. Failure to reach a mutually agreeable resolution through mediation may result in the Tribunal referring the matter to arbitration as provided herein. Any party aggrieved by an arbitral award may, subject to limitations on appeal concerning matters of law only, file an application for revision before the Appellate Tribunal.

For the purposes of this Act, "crop sciences indian" means the scientific discipline concerned with the cultivation, improvement, and genetic manipulation of plants, including but not limited to agronomy, plant breeding, physiology, pathology, and biotechnology relating to agricultural species. An allegation that a person has engaged in activities contrary to the provisions regarding farmers’ rights shall be investigated by the appropriate authority; such investigation may include examination of records pertaining to seed sales, planting material distribution, and harvesting practices. Evidence obtained during an investigation of a commission alleged offence is admissible under this Act subject to rules of evidence applicable in Indian courts.

An application for registration of a novel plant variety under this Act shall include particulars relating to the denomination of the variety, its origin and history, including details of breeding methods employed and any relevant crop sciences indian research undertaken. The applicant, being a business india applicant, must provide comprehensive data demonstrating distinctness, uniformity, and stability, as per guidelines issued by the Authority. Such data shall be accompanied by detailed morphological descriptions and performance trial results obtained from at least three generations or harvests. Further, the application shall disclose any indications of resistance to pests or diseases, along with information regarding its reaction to biotic and abiotic stresses. The Registrar may require additional documentation deemed necessary for assessing the novelty and compliance as provided herein.

Applications for inclusion in the Register relating to crop sciences indian varieties shall be submitted to the Registrar in the prescribed form accompanied by such documents and information as may be required under this Act. The application must specify the name of the variety, its botanical designation, a detailed description including essential characteristics relevant for identification, and the geographical region where it is predominantly cultivated. An applicant seeking inclusion based on an included register geographical indication shall provide evidence demonstrating a clear link between the variety’s unique properties and that specified area. The Registrar may require further clarification or additional data to ascertain compliance with the provisions herein. Objections to any application may be filed by any person within three months from the date of publication of the advertisement under this Act, stating reasons for the objection.

An application for registration of a novel plant variety shall include detailed particulars relating to its botanical designation, lineage, and expression of essential characteristics, accompanied by documentation verifying compliance with established guidelines. The applicant shall furnish evidence demonstrating that the variety has been cultivated in India for a period not less than six years prior to the date of application, or imported into India under license from an authorized body. Upon receipt of such an application, the Agriculture Commissioner government may initiate an examination process involving field trials and expert assessment. Provided that any objection raised by third parties regarding the novelty or distinctiveness of the variety must be addressed comprehensively within a stipulated timeframe as provided herein.

Applications for registration of a Plant Variety shall include detailed particulars regarding its genetic composition, lineage, and method of propagation, as determined acceptable by the agriculture commissioner government. Such applications must demonstrate compliance with established guidelines concerning documentation of field trials conducted over at least three successive agricultural seasons; failure to provide verifiable data relating to yield stability across diverse agro-climatic zones will render the application ineligible for further processing. The agriculture commissioner government may require applicants to submit additional information or conduct supplementary assessments to ascertain conformity with provisions pertaining to farmers’ rights and access to propagating material, provided that such requests are made within a period not exceeding ninety days from the date of initial submission.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and any rules made thereunder, a Plant Variety Protection Licensee may grant licenses for the commercial use of protected plant varieties, including rights relating to seed production, sale, distribution, and import. Such licenses shall be documented in writing and specify the scope of permitted activities, duration, geographical area, and royalty payments payable to the original breeder or their assignee. The Agriculture Commissioner government may, upon application by an interested party demonstrating a public interest concern regarding access to protected varieties for research or conservation purposes, authorize non-exclusive licenses under conditions it deems appropriate. Any assignment of rights in a plant variety protection license requires prior notification to and registration with the Agriculture Commissioner government, accompanied by details of the assignee’s qualifications and intended use of the assigned rights. Failure to register an assignment shall render such assignment voidable.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act relating to the revocation of protection granted to a plant variety, or concerning the imposition of penalties for infringement of farmers’ rights, may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order. The Appellate Board shall consider all relevant evidence and arguments presented by the appellant and the Agriculture Commissioner Government, and may affirm, modify, or reverse the original order. Provided that, in cases involving alleged unauthorized transmissible use layout of a protected plant variety for commercial purposes, the burden of proving consent lies upon the accused party. Failure to comply with an order of the Appellate Board shall render the defaulting party liable to further penalties as determined by the Board and subject to judicial review under established principles.

An application for registration of a plant variety under this Act shall include a detailed report prepared by an authorized breeder, specifying the distinctiveness and stability of the variety, along with evidence demonstrating its genetic uniformity. The Agriculture Commissioner government may require submission of additional data pertaining to field trials conducted in at least two agro-climatic zones representative of conditions prevalent within India; such trials must adhere to guidelines prescribed by notification. Provided that, if the applicant is from an application convention country and has already obtained breeder’s rights for the variety in that country, the Agriculture Commissioner may waive requirements concerning certain aspects of field trial data, subject to a review of equivalent protections afforded therein. The Registrar shall verify compliance with these stipulations prior to proceeding with examination.

For the purposes of this Act, the term “agriculture commissioner” means an officer designated by the State Government, possessing qualifications and experience in agricultural practices or plant protection, who is responsible for receiving applications relating to Plant Variety Registration and Farmers’ Rights. The agriculture commissioner shall verify information submitted regarding the denomination of a variety, ensuring it conforms to prescribed guidelines and does not conflict with existing denominations under this Act. Further, the agriculture commissioner may conduct field inspections to ascertain the distinctiveness and stability of a plant variety as claimed by the applicant, subject to procedures outlined herein.

An application for registration of a novel plant variety shall include particulars regarding its designation, lineage where known, and expression of distinctive characteristics conforming to guidelines issued by the agriculture commissioner. The applicant shall furnish documentation substantiating the stability of these traits across successive generations, alongside evidence demonstrating freedom from prior public use or cultivation under any nomenclature. Where an application relates to a variety derived from another, the parentage must be clearly stated, along with details concerning the derivation process. The agriculture commissioner may require further information or clarification at any stage during examination and processing of the registration request. Any alteration to the submitted data necessitates notification to the Commissioner prior to publication for public comment as provided herein.

Where a Plant Variety is found to infringe upon the rights of another person under this Act, any aggrieved party may file a complaint with the Agriculture Commissioner. Upon receiving such a complaint, the Agriculture Commissioner shall serve notice on both the complainant and the alleged infringer, affording each an opportunity for hearing and presentation of evidence. The Agriculture Commissioner may order the cessation of infringing activities, including but not limited to the unauthorized sale, cultivation, or distribution of the infringing Plant Variety. Further, where damages are proven, the Agriculture Commissioner may award compensation to the affected party, taking into account the extent of the infringement and the profits derived therefrom. Any party aggrieved by an order made under this Act may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order, as provided herein.

Applications for registration of a Plant Variety shall be submitted to the agriculture commissioner in triplicate, accompanied by such documentation as may be prescribed, detailing the variety's designation, lineage, and method of reproduction. The agriculture commissioner shall within thirty days of receipt of an application, acknowledge its receipt and assign it a serial number. Any interested party may, subject to conditions specified herein, file objections to the registration of a Plant Variety with the agriculture commissioner within two months from the date of publication of the advertisement under this Act. Objections must be supported by affidavits verifying their factual basis. The agriculture commissioner shall provide an opportunity for both the applicant and the objector to present their case in writing and orally. Decisions regarding objections, as well as requests for clarification or further information, are binding on all parties involved until formally reviewed through appeal.

The application for registration of a novel plant variety submitted under this Act shall include a detailed report prepared by an accredited Plant Breeding Institute, verifying compliance with the essential derivation criteria. Such report must explicitly state whether the applicant has adhered to all relevant guidelines pertaining to genetic modification and marker assisted selection techniques, as applicable. The Agriculture Commissioner may, upon receiving such application and associated documentation, conduct on-site inspections of the breeding program to ascertain adherence to good agricultural practices and record keeping protocols. Any deviation from prescribed procedures identified during inspection shall be reported to the applicant for rectification within a stipulated timeframe. Failure to rectify deficiencies may result in rejection of the registration application as provided herein.

Any person who obstructs an officer authorized under this Act in the exercise of his powers, or disobeys any direction given by such officer, shall be deemed guilty of an offence and liable to a penalty of five thousand rupees for the first instance, and ten thousand rupees for subsequent instances. Failure to comply with a notice issued by the Agriculture Commissioner requiring submission of records pertaining to plant breeding activities will attract a daily penalty of one thousand rupees until compliance is achieved. Further, any entity found to be engaging in unauthorized commercialization of a registered variety without proper authorization from the Registrar shall face suspension of their registration and a fine not exceeding twenty-five thousand rupees, as provided herein. The Agriculture Commissioner may also initiate prosecution for wilful default.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and any rules made thereunder, a Plant Variety Protection Agreement, whether entered into prior to or subsequent to the registration of a plant variety, may stipulate conditions relating to the licensing and assignment of farmers’ rights pertaining to propagated material. Such agreements shall clearly define the scope of permitted uses, including but not limited to cultivation for self-consumption, sale, and exchange. The Agriculture Commissioner may, upon receiving a complaint regarding unfair or restrictive clauses within such an agreement, initiate inquiries and issue directives to rectify imbalances affecting farmer interests. Assignment of farmers’ rights under this Act requires prior written consent from the concerned farmer and registration with the appropriate authority. Any transfer shall be deemed invalid if it contravenes the principles of equity and fairness as determined by the Agriculture Commissioner.

Where any person aggrieved by an order passed by the Agriculture Commissioner under this Act relating to the grant, revocation, or modification of Plant Variety Registration, or concerning infringement proceedings, desires to appeal, such person may, within sixty days from the date of communication of the said order, file an appeal with the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. The appeal shall be accompanied by a statement of grounds and reasons for challenging the order. Provided that the Board may, if it considers necessary, require the appellant to furnish security deposit as deemed fit. Any party against whom such an order is passed may also appeal under similar conditions and procedures as provided herein.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed by the Agriculture Commissioner under this Act may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. The Appellate Board shall hear appeals arising out of orders relating to revocation of registration or opposition proceedings, and any other matter as provided herein concerning plant variety rights. Subject to just cause shown, failure to file an appeal within the stipulated time shall be deemed a waiver of the right to seek redressal. Furthermore, where infringement of registered plant breeder’s rights is established, the Board may order remedies including damages proportionate to the loss suffered by the claimant and account of profits made by the infringer. The layout design registered in connection with the protected variety shall also be afforded protection against unauthorized use.

Applications for registration of a Plant Variety shall include detailed particulars regarding its expression and genetic purity, including data from at least three generations demonstrating stability across diverse agro-climatic zones. The Agriculture Commissioner may require submission of additional documentation pertaining to propagation methods employed and any modifications introduced during cultivation. Provided that, if the application incorporates a provisions act mark indicating a novel breeding technique, the applicant shall furnish a comprehensive report detailing the methodology utilized and its potential impact on subsequent generations. Failure to comply with these requirements, or providing information deemed insufficient by the Agriculture Commissioner, will result in rejection of the application, subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

Applications for registration of a Plant Variety shall include particulars relating to its designation, denomination if any, repository details where propagating material is available, and the name and address of the applicant. Where an application relates to a variety developed by or for a farmer, the application may be filed jointly by such farmer and any other person seeking commercial advantage from the variety. The Central Government may require submission of additional data concerning distinctness, uniformity, stability, and resistance to pests and diseases as deemed necessary for evaluation under this Act. All applications shall be processed in accordance with procedures established by the indian council agricultural, which will assess conformity with registration criteria.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act relating to the revocation of registration of a plant variety, or concerning any action taken affecting their breeder’s rights, may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of such order. The Appellate Board shall consider all relevant evidence and arguments presented by both the appellant and the respondent, including submissions regarding alleged infringement of farmers' rights or unfair trade practices impacting access to plant varieties. Further, any complaint alleging that the indian council agricultural has failed in its duty to promote equitable access to protected plant varieties for smallholder farmers may be investigated by a committee appointed by the Central Government. Remedies available under this Act include injunctions, damages, and orders compelling compliance with obligations as provided herein.

The indian council agricultural established under this Act shall function under the superintendence and control of the Board. The Council’s primary responsibility is to advise the Board on matters concerning plant breeder's rights, farmers’ rights, and the conservation of plant genetic resources as provided herein. Applications for registration of germplasm patents may be referred to the indian council agricultural for technical evaluation prior to consideration by the Board; such referrals shall include all relevant documentation submitted with the application. The Council shall submit its recommendations within ninety days of referral, detailing any concerns regarding novelty or distinctiveness. Failure to provide a recommendation within this timeframe will not impede the Board’s decision-making process. Members of the council shall be appointed by the Board from amongst individuals possessing expertise in agronomy, botany, and intellectual property law.

The indian council agricultural shall maintain a register of registered plant varieties and associated farmers’ rights, accessible for public inspection subject to reasonable restrictions as may be prescribed. Any person aggrieved by an entry in the register relating to registration or farmers' rights may appeal to the Authority within sixty days from the date of such entry. The Authority shall consider appeals based on compliance with established protocols concerning novelty, distinctiveness and stability; provided that evidence demonstrating traditional knowledge contributions shall be given due consideration during assessment. Further, any application for registration requiring data generated through field trials must demonstrate adherence to Good Agricultural Practices guidelines as stipulated under this Act. Failure to comply with these conditions renders the application liable for rejection.

Any person who contravenes any provision of this Act relating to the registration of a plant variety, including making false statements in an application or failing to disclose material information, shall be liable for a penalty not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees and may also face imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years. Furthermore, where a registered plant variety is reproduced for sale by any person without authorization from the Registrar, that person shall be subject to damages assessed by the civil court, taking into account lost profits and reasonable expenses incurred. The indian council agricultural shall have the power to initiate investigations into suspected violations and report findings to the Central Government for appropriate action, including prosecution under this Act.

The Indian Council Agricultural shall maintain a register of complaints arising from alleged infringements of farmers’ rights relating to plant varieties, and any person aggrieved by a decision of the Council concerning such a complaint may appeal to the Appellate Board. The Board shall consider appeals on grounds that the original decision was manifestly unjust or based on an error of law apparent on the face of the record. Provided that, the appellant must demonstrate prejudice resulting from the alleged error. Further, any party dissatisfied with the order of the Appellate Board may petition the Supreme Court under Article 136 of the Constitution, subject to fulfilling requirements regarding locus standi and demonstrating special circumstances warranting intervention.

For the purposes of this Act, “breeder” means a person who has either developed new plant varieties or discovered and scientifically evaluated existing varieties, and shall include any natural person, legal entity or community of persons. The term "variety" signifies a plant grouping exhibiting a consistent combination of inherited traits distinguishable from other plant groupings; provided that such distinction is stable and heritable. Protection granted breeder under this Act confers the right to produce, sell, import, export and distribute propagating material of the variety for commercial purposes, subject to any conditions specified in the grant of protection. Any person claiming rights as a breeder may apply to the Authority demonstrating compliance with prescribed criteria.

An application for protection granted breeder rights shall be made to the Plant Varieties Registration Board in the prescribed form and accompanied by a detailed description of the variety, including its essential characteristics, distinctiveness, stability, and uniformity. The application must also specify the origin of the variety and, where applicable, the name and address of the initial developer. Evidence demonstrating that the variety is new and possesses one or more traits substantially differentiating it from existing varieties shall be submitted with the application. Any person claiming to have a right over the variety may file an objection under this Act within the period specified, stating reasons for opposing registration. The Board may require further information or clarification from the applicant during processing of the application.

An application for protection granted breeder may be made to the Plant Variety Protection Appellate Tribunal in the form specified under this Act and accompanied by such documentation as demonstrates distinctness, uniformity, and stability of the variety. The application shall include a detailed description of the plant genetic resources utilized in the development of the variety, including any germplasm donors or ancestral lines. Where the applicant is not the original breeder, they must provide evidence of authorization or assignment from the original breeder, duly executed as per prescribed procedures. The Tribunal may require further information or clarification from the applicant to ascertain compliance with these requirements and to ensure transparency regarding the origin and development process. Any person aggrieved by an order of the Plant Variety Protection Appellate Tribunal may appeal to the High Court within a period of sixty days from the date of such order, subject to fulfilling all procedural requisites as provided herein.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, a protection granted breeder shall be entitled to exercise rights including the right to produce, sell, market, distribute and import seeds or planting material of the variety, provided that such exercise is compliant with prescribed quality standards as determined by the Central Government. The authority may, upon receiving a complaint duly verified under this Act, investigate whether the activities of any person infringe upon the breeder’s rights, particularly concerning unauthorized commercialization or genetic modification without prior consent. Further, any infringement shall be subject to penalties including but not limited to monetary fines and injunction orders as provided herein; however, farmers' rights relating to seed saving and exchange are expressly protected notwithstanding such restrictions.

Any person aggrieved by an order made under this Act relating to the revocation or modification of protection granted breeder may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of such order. Failure to comply with prescribed procedures during any infringement proceedings shall render the complainant ineligible for recovery of costs incurred in pursuing said action. Where a farmer utilizes propagating material obtained in violation of restrictions imposed under this Act, and subsequently engages in commercial exploitation thereof, they shall be liable to pay damages equivalent to three times the value of the infringing material sold or distributed. The Authority may impose a penalty not exceeding five lakh rupees for any contravention of provisions relating to benefit-sharing agreements as provided herein.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, a protection granted breeder may enter into agreements for the licensing or assignment of rights pertaining to their registered plant variety. Such agreements shall clearly delineate the scope of permitted activities, including but not limited to seed production, distribution, and research use. The terms of any license agreement concerning propagation material derived from the protected variety must specify royalty rates payable to the breeder, which may be adjusted based on prevailing market conditions as determined by the Controller General. Assignment of rights shall require prior notification to the Authority and approval in accordance with prescribed procedures. Provided that, any such assignment cannot restrict farmers’ rights under this Act to save, reuse, exchange or share farm saved seed of such variety.

Subject to the provisions contained herein, protection granted breeder of a plant variety may be challenged before the Appellate Board if it is alleged that the criteria for eligibility under this Act were not duly satisfied at the time of grant. Such challenge shall be initiated within six months from the date of publication of the notification relating to registration in the Official Gazette. The Authority may, upon receiving such an appeal, direct a re-examination of the evidence presented during the original application process and any subsequent material submitted by either the breeder or the appellant. It is provided that the burden of demonstrating non-compliance with the Act’s requirements shall rest upon the appellant; failing which, the appeal shall be dismissed with costs.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, an application for advertisement registration relating to a plant variety shall be accompanied by a detailed statement specifying the manner in which the plant variety’s characteristics are portrayed and the claims made regarding its novelty, stability, and uniformity. Such applications must demonstrate compliance with guidelines issued by the Plant Varieties Authority concerning truthful representation of traits and avoidance of misleading comparisons with other varieties. The protection granted breeder for a registered plant variety shall not extend to the use of any advertisement that falsely implies the protected variety possesses characteristics it does not demonstrably exhibit, as determined by the Authority. Any person aggrieved may file an objection under this Act against such advertisement application registration within sixty days.

Subject to the provisions contained herein, a protection granted breeder of a plant variety may assign or license their rights under this Act to any other person, including companies engaged in agricultural research and development, provided that such assignment or license is recorded with the Registrar within three months of its execution. Any subsequent transfer of such assigned right shall also be similarly recorded. The terms of any license granted shall specify the scope of use permitted, including but not limited to propagation, sale, import, and export, and may include royalty payments as determined by a mutually agreed contract between the licensor and licensee. Such contracts are subject to review for fairness under principles analogous to those governing patent licenses. Failure to register an assignment or license shall render it void against third parties claiming through that unregistered transfer.

Subject to the provisions contained herein, protection granted breeder of a plant variety may be challenged before the Appellate Board if it is alleged that the claimed novelty was derived from an existing variety or species through the use of a computer programme employed in genetic modification techniques. Such challenge shall be initiated within six months from the date of publication of the grant notice under this Act and must specify with particularity the prior art upon which the claim of non-novelty is based, including detailed algorithmic descriptions where applicable. The Board may, after affording the breeder an opportunity to present a rebuttal and expert testimony, determine whether the protection granted was improperly conferred, provided that the burden of proof regarding lack of novelty shall rest entirely with the petitioner.

For the purposes of this Act, a “breeder” shall mean an individual or entity who has developed a new plant variety and is responsible for its initial selection, improvement, and reproduction. A "breeder breeder complied" designation may be applied to a breeder who demonstrates adherence to established protocols concerning documentation of lineage, maintenance of genetic purity, and provision of samples for verification purposes as provided herein. Such compliance shall not, however, confer any additional rights beyond those already granted under this Act. Any person claiming the status of “breeder” must satisfy the Authority that they possess demonstrable expertise in plant breeding techniques and have fulfilled all relevant obligations pertaining to notification and reporting requirements.

An application for compulsory licensing under this Act relating to a plant variety shall not be entertained unless it is demonstrated to the Authority that the breeder has failed to satisfy the reasonable requirements of local farmers regarding seed availability or price, and such failure persists despite repeated representations made by affected farmer groups. The Authority may require the applicant to provide evidence demonstrating the extent of non-compliance and its impact on agricultural productivity. Where a plant variety has been developed through breeding methods involving genetic modification, the application shall further specify whether the breeder breeder complied with all applicable regulations pertaining to biosafety assessment and containment procedures as provided herein.

Any farmer who, without authorization from the registered breeder, conducts acts infringing upon the plant variety protection conferred under this Act shall be liable to pay damages as determined by the Authority. Such damages shall account for lost profits reasonably attributable to the unauthorized use of propagating material and any unjust enrichment derived therefrom. Where a farmer has demonstrably engaged in activities constituting *breeder breeder complied* practices, including self-saving or exchange of seed without permission, they may be subject to an order restricting future propagation rights. The Authority may also impose penalties proportionate to the scale of infringement, considering factors such as the number of farmers involved and the extent of distribution. Further, any entity found facilitating unauthorized breeding activities shall face administrative sanctions, including suspension of registration privileges.

Where a plant variety is deemed to possess essentially derived characteristics from an existing variety, and a claim of *breeder breeder complied* status is asserted by the claimant seeking protection, the Examining Authority shall issue a notice to both the original breeder and the alleged essentially derived variety applicant. Such notice shall detail the grounds for assessment concerning whether the subsequent variety satisfies the conditions as provided herein regarding novelty and distinctiveness, taking into consideration any technical data submitted demonstrating derivation. The original breeder may submit objections within sixty days of receipt of the notice, outlining reasons why the claimed status is not justified. Further, the Authority may request additional information or conduct hearings to ascertain the veracity of claims relating to the breeding process and contribution of each party. Decisions regarding *breeder breeder complied* determinations shall be recorded in writing and made publicly available on the designated online portal.

A plant variety shall be deemed eligible for protection under this Act if the breeder demonstrates compliance with established guidelines regarding distinctiveness, uniformity and stability. The Authority may require submission of detailed records pertaining to lineage tracing, demonstrating adherence to breeding protocols and ensuring traceability back to original parent material. Where a plant variety has been developed through genetic modification techniques, the applicant shall provide comprehensive documentation outlining the nature and extent of such modifications, subject to review by the appropriate regulatory body. Further, if a breeder breeder complied with prior obligations regarding benefit sharing agreements relating to germplasm resources utilized in the development process, this compliance shall be considered favorably during assessment.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, a breeder may, through an assignment or license agreement, grant rights to utilize propagating material derived from a protected plant variety. Such agreements shall clearly delineate the scope of permitted activities, including but not limited to seed production, distribution, and cultivation for commercial purposes. Where a licensee engages in breeding activities involving the protected variety, any resulting novel variety exhibiting substantially similar characteristics shall be deemed a *breeder breeder complied* derivative, requiring prior written consent from the original breeder. The license agreement may stipulate royalty payments or other considerations payable to the breeder, as mutually agreed upon. Failure to adhere to the terms of such agreements constitutes infringement under this Act and renders the infringing party liable for damages. Further, any assignment shall be registered with the Plant Varieties Registry within thirty days of execution.

Where a plant variety is deemed to infringe upon the rights of an existing breeder, and such infringement is predicated upon demonstrable evidence of unauthorized breeding or propagation, the aggrieved breeder may file an appeal with the Appellate Board. The appellant shall bear the burden of proving, by clear and convincing evidence, that the respondent breeder breeder complied with all stipulated conditions regarding germplasm access and subsequent derivation. Provided that, a finding of substantial similarity alone shall not constitute conclusive proof of infringement; genetic fingerprinting analysis as prescribed under this Act must be presented to establish direct lineage. The Board may, after affording both parties an opportunity for hearing, dismiss the appeal or grant such relief as it deems just and equitable, including but not limited to injunctive orders and compensatory damages.

The Authority shall establish and maintain a Plant Biodiversity Fund for the conservation and sustainable use of plant genetic resources. Contributions to the Plant Biodiversity Fund shall include royalties received from licensees utilizing protected varieties where such utilization demonstrably impacts indigenous farming practices or traditional knowledge associated with the variety. Further, any benefit sharing arrangement under this Act relating to the commercialization of germplasm derived from accessions held in public gene banks shall be remitted directly into the Plant Biodiversity Fund. The Authority may prescribe guidelines for the disbursement of funds towards research and development activities concerning crop improvement and farmer welfare. A portion of all registration fees paid under this Act shall also *gene fund shall* be credited to the Plant Biodiversity Fund.

An application for registration of a plant variety shall include detailed particulars regarding the source germplasm and any genetic modifications undertaken during its development. Where the applicant is unable to ascertain the precise origin of the initial material used, or where such origin involves contributions from multiple sources, they may elect to contribute to the gene fund as provided herein. The amount contributed shall be determined by a committee established under this Act, taking into consideration factors including the extent of genetic modification and potential commercial benefit derived from the variety. Any breeder who utilizes protected varieties in their breeding program shall also be subject to reporting requirements concerning resultant progeny. Contributions made to the gene fund shall be utilized exclusively for supporting research related to crop improvement and conservation efforts as deemed appropriate by the Central Government.

The Authority shall maintain a comprehensive register detailing all contributions made towards the gene fund. Contributions shall include, but are not limited to, benefit-sharing amounts received from commercialized plant varieties and fees levied on propagating material derived therefrom. The Register shall be accessible for public inspection subject to reasonable restrictions as determined by the Authority to protect confidential information pertaining to registered breeders. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Authority regarding the assessment or collection of contributions may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such decision. The gene fund shall be utilized exclusively for supporting research and development activities related to plant genetic resources, including in-situ conservation efforts and the establishment of germplasm banks. Further, funds may be allocated towards providing financial assistance to farmers engaged in traditional farming practices that contribute to biodiversity preservation as provided herein.

The Authority shall establish and maintain a Plant Variety Gene Fund for the purpose of supporting research relating to plant genetic resources and providing financial assistance to farmers engaged in the conservation and sustainable utilization of traditional crop varieties. Contributions to the gene fund shall include, but are not limited to, levies collected from entities importing propagating material derived from registered plant varieties, subject to exemptions determined by notification issued by the Central Government. Any expenditure incurred from the gene fund shall be strictly in accordance with guidelines approved by the Protection of Plant Varieties Council and require prior sanction from a designated Finance Committee constituted under this Act. Further, any distribution of funds must prioritize programs demonstrating demonstrable benefit to smallholder farmers cultivating indigenous varieties.

Any person who contravenes any provision of this Act relating to the unauthorized propagation or sale of plant varieties shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding five thousand rupees for each instance. Repeated offences may attract penalties escalating up to ten thousand rupees per instance, as determined by an adjudicating officer appointed under this Act. Furthermore, any entity found guilty of misleadingly representing a variety's characteristics or origin in commercial transactions will face additional fines and potential prohibition from propagating material for a period not less than one year. The Central Government shall establish a mechanism to ensure that funds recovered through penalties are deposited into the gene fund shall be utilized exclusively for supporting research and development activities related to plant breeding, particularly benefiting smallholder farmers and public institutions.

Any person holding rights relating to a plant variety shall be entitled to grant licenses in respect thereof, subject to the conditions prescribed herein. Such license agreements may include provisions for sub-licensing, provided that the original holder retains ultimate control over the scope and duration of any such assignment. Further, where a licensee fails to adhere to the terms stipulated within the agreement concerning benefit sharing with farmers, the rights granted under the license shall be liable to revocation by the Controller. The Central Government may, at its discretion, require licensees to provide detailed reports on cultivation practices and yield data obtained through licensed propagation material. Any sums received as royalties or fees relating to a plant variety shall, after deduction of reasonable expenses, contribute towards the gene fund shall be deposited with the National Gene Fund within three months of receipt.

Where any dispute arises concerning the eligibility of a farmer for benefit sharing from the gene fund shall, notwithstanding anything contained elsewhere under this Act, be first referred to a Grievance Redressal Committee constituted by the State Government. The decision of said committee shall be final, subject to appeal before the Appellate Authority within sixty days of such determination. Provided that an appeal may only be entertained if the appellant demonstrates demonstrable prejudice resulting from the initial finding and deposits with the Authority an amount equivalent to twenty-five percent of the disputed benefit. Further, any challenge to the methodology employed in calculating contributions to the gene fund shall be addressed through a writ petition before the High Court.

Where any person aggrieved by an order passed by the Plant Variety Protection Appellate Board concerning the revocation of registration or the imposition of conditions affecting rights respect registration, or relating to benefit sharing arrangements, appeals such order before the High Court within ninety days from the date of communication of the said order. The appeal shall be on grounds specified in the memorandum of appeal and may challenge the findings of fact or law made by the Appellate Board. Provided that the Central Government shall, upon receiving evidence suggesting misappropriation of funds derived from benefit sharing obligations, deposit such sums into the gene fund shall to ensure equitable distribution amongst registered farmers contributing to varietal improvement. Any dispute regarding the calculation of contributions to the gene fund shall be subject to review under this Act.

The Authority shall maintain a comprehensive register detailing all applications for registration of plant varieties, including particulars relating to the breeder, the geographical location where the variety was initially developed, and any relevant documentation pertaining to genetic modification or traditional breeding techniques employed. Upon successful examination and verification under this Act, the applicant shall be notified in writing by the Registrar, affording them a period of thirty days within which to submit the prescribed registration fee. Failure to remit said fee within that timeframe will result in automatic rejection of the application. Further, any design registered on propagating material derived from a protected variety shall remain subject to the provisions relating to infringement as provided herein. The gene fund shall be utilized exclusively for supporting research into indigenous plant varieties and providing financial assistance to farmers engaged in sustainable agricultural practices.

Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Plant Variety Protection Appellate Board relating to the infringement of plant variety rights under this Act may appeal to the High Court within sixty days from the date of such decision. The appellate court shall have the same jurisdiction as it would have in respect of original suits under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. Claims purposes section concerning revocation of a granted Plant Variety Protection shall be subject to judicial review on grounds of procedural irregularity or demonstrable error of law. Further, remedies for infringement, including injunctions and damages, are available as provided herein; however, wilful infringement shall attract enhanced penalties determined at the discretion of the court. The burden of proving prior use lies upon the claimant seeking revocation.

Applications for grant of Plant Variety Rights shall be accompanied by a detailed statement specifying the denomination proposed for the variety and a justification demonstrating its distinctiveness relative to existing varieties. The Examining Authority may require further clarification or experimental data regarding claimed characteristics, provided that such requests are made within sixty days from the date of receipt of the application. Objections relating to novelty or distinctiveness must be filed by any interested party within ninety days from the publication of an advertisement under this Act inviting objections. Claims purposes section 18(2) dictates that all objections shall state the grounds upon which they are based and provide supporting evidence, failing which they shall be deemed inadmissible. The Authority shall afford both the applicant and the objector a reasonable opportunity to present their case during hearings. Decisions regarding the acceptance or rejection of claims shall be recorded in writing and communicated to all parties involved.

Any person found to have made a false representation in support of an application for registration under this Act shall be liable to pay a pecuniary penalty not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees. The Authority may, upon receiving credible information regarding such misrepresentation, initiate inquiries and issue notices requiring the applicant or claimant to submit evidence refuting the allegations. Failure to adequately respond to such notice, or determination that the representation was indeed false, will result in the rejection of the application or revocation of registration, as deemed appropriate by the Authority. Claims purposes section dictates that all supporting documentation must be verifiable; willful falsification constitutes a criminal offence punishable under the Indian Penal Code.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, a Plant Breeder’s Authority shall grant licenses relating to rights granted under this Act upon application. Such applications shall clearly specify the scope of the licensed right, including geographical limitations and duration, and may include conditions restricting exploitation of the variety for specific purposes. Assignment of such licenses is permissible, provided that the assignee adheres to all terms and conditions initially stipulated in the license agreement. The Plant Breeder’s Authority may, upon receiving a complaint or observing non-compliance, revoke any license granted if it determines that the licensee has acted contrary to the claims purposes section of this Act or engaged in unfair trade practices impacting farmers' rights. Further, sub-licensing is permitted with prior written consent from the original licensor and notification to the Authority.

An application for registration of a plant variety shall specify the denomination proposed by the applicant and include a detailed description conforming to the guidelines issued by the Authority. The Registrar may require amendment of the denomination if it is deemed confusingly similar to an existing registered variety or contravenes any provision under this Act. Claims purposes section 34(2) dictates that the statement of originality must accurately reflect the distinctiveness observed during evaluation, and failure to do so shall render the registration liable for cancellation. An authorised user who has derived a new plant variety through genetic modification is obligated to disclose such derivation in their application, subject to confidentiality provisions as provided herein.

Applications for recognition as a plant variety shall be accompanied by a detailed description conforming to the format prescribed by the Registrar and including particulars relating to its essential characteristics, distinctiveness, stability and uniformity. The applicant shall also furnish evidence demonstrating freedom from any existing rights or encumbrances pertaining to the variety. Upon receipt of an application, the Authority may direct the submission of additional information or clarification deemed necessary for assessment. Claims purposes section 3(4) provides that where a proposed plant variety incorporates elements derived from varieties already registered under this Act, the applicant must explicitly identify those sources and demonstrate compliance with existing rights. A marks registry established by the Controller General shall be consulted to ascertain any potential conflicts arising from proposed denomination usage. The Registrar may reject an application if it fails to meet these requirements or is deemed frivolous.
