Further, a suit for damages or injunction relating to infringement by an exclusive licensee may be brought against either the patentee or the licensee, as appropriate, provided that the aggrieved party furnishes security satisfactory to the court regarding any ultimate award made. The provisions herein shall apply irrespective of whether the license was granted prior to or subsequent to the grant of the patent itself; and it is clarified that an exclusive licensee shall have standing to pursue remedies for infringement.

Where a patentee grants an exclusive licence under this Act, such license shall be deemed to create a contractual relationship governed by principles of contract law, and any dispute arising from the terms or conditions of said license may be adjudicated according to established legal precedent. The patentee shall provide written notification to the Controller within thirty days of granting an exclusive licence, detailing the scope of rights transferred and the territory covered thereby. Further, an exclusive licensee shall be entitled to exercise all rights pertaining to the patented invention as if they were the patentee, subject to compliance with all applicable provisions regarding working conditions and compulsory licensing procedures as provided herein. Any assignment or further sub-licensing by the exclusive licensee requires prior written consent from the original patentee.

Where a patentee grants an exclusive licence under this Act, such licence shall define the territory and field of exploitation to which the exclusivity pertains, and may specify royalties payable by the licensee to the patentee. The patentee shall provide written notice to the Controller of Patents within thirty days of granting any such exclusive licence, detailing the identity of the licensee and the scope of their rights. Subject to compliance with this requirement, an exclusive licensee shall be entitled to enforce against third parties all rights pertaining to the invention as if they were the patentee themselves. Provided that, where the terms of the exclusive licence are not clearly defined or contain ambiguities, the Controller may intervene to clarify such terms and ensure fairness between the patentee and the licensee. Any assignment of a patent shall be deemed to include any existing exclusive licences relating thereto, unless explicitly excluded in writing.

Where a patentee grants an exclusive licence under this Act, the exclusive licensee shall be entitled to institute proceedings for infringement of the patent relating to the invention as specified in the license agreement. The Controller may, upon receiving a complaint from any person alleging that an exclusive licensee has failed to exercise the rights granted to him or her, issue notice requiring the licensee to show cause why such failure should not be deemed to constitute abandonment of the exclusive licence. Such proceedings shall be conducted in accordance with the prescribed procedure and subject to the provisions regarding limitation periods as provided herein. A farmer cultivating a patented plant variety under an exclusive license shall be considered for any remedial action arising from non-exercise of rights, proportionate to their investment in seeds obtained through the licensee. The patentee may revoke the exclusive licence if it is established that the licensee has materially prejudiced the interests of the invention.

Where a patentee grants an exclusive licence under this Act, the exclusive licensee shall possess all rights pertaining to the patented invention as if they were the original patentee, subject to the terms and conditions stipulated within the licensing agreement. However, any challenge to the validity of the patent arising prior to the grant of such exclusivity may be pursued by the aggrieved party notwithstanding the existence of the exclusive licence. It is provided that a company claiming to be an exclusive licensee must demonstrate, through documented evidence submitted before the Controller, its unequivocal right to exercise these privileges. Disputes concerning the scope or interpretation of this exclusivity shall be subject to appeal as per established procedures under this Act.

For the purposes of this Act, “assignment” means a voluntary transfer of the exclusive right to the patent, or any interest therein, subject to such terms and conditions as may be stipulated; provided that an assignment shall only confer upon the assignee the rights which the assignor was legally entitled to at the time of the assignment. "means licence patentee" includes any person who is for the time being the registered proprietor of a patent and to whom right to exploit the patented invention has been assigned under this Act, or who holds an exclusive license; further, such term shall not include a licensee unless he is also the assignor.

The Register of Patents shall maintain a separate register for recording assignments and licences relating to registered patents, and every assignment or licence granted under this Act shall be recorded in such manner as may be prescribed. Where an agreement purports to create a means licence patentee, the Registrar may require evidence demonstrating the full extent and duration of the rights transferred. Such evidence shall include copies of all relevant contractual documents and declarations from both parties confirming their consent to the registration. Failure to provide satisfactory documentation will result in refusal to register the assignment or licence. The Register shall be open for public inspection during normal business hours, subject to any restrictions imposed by the Controller to protect confidential information as provided herein.

Where a patentee grants a licence, and such licence contains terms restricting the exploitation of the patented invention by any person other than the licensee or those duly authorised by them, then for the purposes of this Act, that licence shall be deemed a means licence patentee. Any infringement of the rights granted under a means licence patentee shall be actionable as if it were an infringement directly against the original patentee, and the remedies available to the means licence patentee under this Act shall include injunctions, damages, and delivery up or destruction of infringing goods. Provided that, where the terms of the licence agreement limit the scope of rights granted, such limitation shall not preclude a claim for relief based on an infringement occurring outside the scope of those limitations. The patentee may also pursue actions against any person who induces, causes, or knowingly participates in an act of infringement relating to the patented invention under this means licence patentee.

Where a patentee grants a licence to any person, such grant shall be deemed to create an interest in property and subject to the provisions of this Act, may be assigned, mortgaged, or alienated in manner similar to other forms of movable property. The term "means licence patentee" signifies that for the purposes of revocation proceedings under this Act, a party holding a license granted by the original patentee shall possess standing to petition where such license explicitly confers upon them the right to enforce the patent against infringement. Further, any alteration or modification to the terms of a licence agreement affecting the scope of the patented invention requires prior notification to the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trademarks. This requirement applies irrespective of whether the alteration is undertaken by the patentee or the licensee. The Controller may issue directions regarding such alterations if deemed necessary to protect public interest.

Where a patentee grants a licence under this Act, and such licence stipulates conditions relating to manufacture within India or the importation of the patented article for the purposes of that manufacture, compliance with those stipulated conditions shall be deemed a material term of the agreement. Failure to adhere to these conditions, as determined by the Controller based on evidence presented, may render the licence liable for revocation under this Act. For the purpose of determining whether such failure constitutes a breach, the burden of proving adherence to the prescribed conditions rests upon the licensee. The expression "means licence patentee" shall apply where the grant includes provisions concerning compulsory licensing or government use as provided herein.

Any person who imports or manufactures any patented article without authorization from the patentee, or their means licence patentee, shall be liable to pay damages equivalent to a sum equal to ten times the profits made by such importation or manufacture. The Controller may, upon receiving a complaint regarding infringement, issue an injunction restraining further acts of infringement, subject to due process and affording the alleged infringer an opportunity for hearing. Failure to comply with an order issued under this Act concerning patent enforcement shall render the defaulting party liable to a penalty not exceeding one hundred thousand rupees for each day of non-compliance. The right to seek rectification of errors appearing in the register relating to patents is provided that such application must be made within six months from the date on which the error appears.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and any rules made thereunder, a patentee may grant licences relating to the patented invention, whether solely or jointly with other inventions, and such licence shall be deemed to be an assignment unless explicitly stated otherwise within the terms of the agreement. Where a licence is granted under this Act, the patentee retains the right to assign the underlying patent, provided that any subsequent assignee becomes bound by the conditions precedent established in the original licensing arrangement. A “means licence patentee” shall include any entity acting on behalf of or as representative for the patentee in negotiating and executing such licences. Further, where a license is granted which includes the right to manufacture the patented invention, the licensee shall be entitled to use the patent for that purpose, subject to adherence to all quality control standards prescribed under this Act.

The term “registered trade mark licence” means a permission granted by the owner of a registered trade mark to another party for use of that trade mark, subject to conditions specified therein and recorded with the Trade Marks Registry. Where such registered trade mark licence is also a means licence patentee, the provisions relating to compulsory licences under this Act shall apply as if the registered trade mark were part of the patented invention. Any assignment or transfer of rights pertaining to a registered trade mark licence, whether exclusive or non-exclusive, must be executed in the prescribed form and duly notified to the Controller for registration. Failure to register such assignments may render them unenforceable against third parties. The Controller may require further documentation as provided herein to verify authenticity and prevent fraudulent claims relating to these licences.

For the purposes of this Act, “biotechnological process” includes any technique utilizing living organisms or biological systems for the production or modification of products or processes, and shall be interpreted broadly to encompass advancements within genetic engineering, cell culture methodologies, and enzyme-based reactions. A biotechnological process shall be deemed patentable only if it results in a product or substance means new, exhibiting characteristics not previously known or predictable based on existing biological knowledge. Provided that the novelty of such a product is established through rigorous experimental data demonstrating its unique properties and utility, subject to the provisions regarding obviousness under this Act.

For the purposes of registration under this Act, a “biotechnological innovation” shall be deemed eligible if it demonstrates novelty and an inventive step as provided herein. The Controller General may require submission of detailed genomic sequencing data to ascertain the origin and composition of any biological material incorporated within the claimed innovation. An application for registration shall explicitly state whether the biotechnological innovation constitutes a new variety of plant, a genetically modified organism, or another form of biological entity. It is established that a substance means new; therefore, prior public disclosure, even in academic literature, will preclude registration unless such disclosure is demonstrably incidental to the invention itself and does not compromise its inventive character.

Where an aggrieved party alleges that a patent has been granted in contravention of this Act, such party may institute civil proceedings seeking remedies as provided herein. The court shall determine whether the invention claimed in the patent possesses substance means new, considering prior art publications and existing knowledge at the time of the application’s filing date. If it is found that the patented invention lacks novelty or involves a trivial variation of an already known process or article, the aggrieved party shall be entitled to seek revocation of the patent. Further, where infringement of another's intellectual property rights is demonstrated as a consequence of the invalid patent, damages may be awarded including compensation for loss of profits and reasonable royalties. The court may also issue injunctions restraining further acts of infringement subject to considerations of public interest.

An application for a patent shall be deemed to lack novelty if the invention disclosed is not new and does not involve an inventive step. For the purposes of this Act, “substance means new” signifies that the claimed matter must not have been previously described or made available to the public anywhere in the world by any means before the date of filing of the patent application. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish further particulars relating to the invention and its claims, including details regarding prior publications or use. An objection under this provision shall be communicated to the applicant within six months from the date of receipt of the request for examination. The applicant shall then have a period of three months to respond to such objections, subject to extensions granted by the Controller upon demonstration of sufficient cause.

For the purposes of determining patentability under this Act, an invention shall be considered to possess substance only if it demonstrates novelty and involves an inventive step. An application for a patent may be filed disclosing the matter referred to in section 10, provided that such disclosure adequately describes the manner in which the invention can be performed. The Controller General shall have power to require amendment of any claim where it is found not to clearly define the scope of protection sought. Where an applicant has previously published particulars of the invention, a period of twelve months from the date of first publication shall apply for claiming priority under this Act. An invention which consists essentially of a substance means new and lacks inventive step shall be deemed unpatentable as provided herein.

Where an application for patent is refused under this Act on the ground that the claimed invention lacks novelty or involves an obvious step, the applicant shall be afforded an opportunity of presenting arguments and evidence demonstrating the inventive merit of the subject matter. It shall be conclusively established that the invention, as claimed in the patent specification, possesses substance means new, considering prior publications or knowledge available to a person skilled in the art at the date of filing. Failure to adequately demonstrate this novelty will result in immediate rejection. Any party aggrieved by such a decision may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days; however, any penalty for non-compliance with procedural requirements shall be strictly enforced as provided herein.

Where an invention relating to a pharmaceutical substance is assigned under this Act, the assignee shall be entitled to grant non-exclusive licenses pertaining to the use of said substance for research purposes only. Such licenses may be granted subject to conditions as prescribed herein, including but not limited to limitations on commercial exploitation and requirements for reporting findings back to the assignor. The assignor retains the right to terminate any such license if the licensee fails to diligently pursue research or acts in a manner detrimental to the interests of the patent holder. For the purposes of this Act, a pharmaceutical substance means new and involves an inventive step over existing knowledge; it shall not be deemed obvious to a person skilled in the art. Any assignment document must clearly delineate the scope of permitted licenses and associated royalties.

For the purposes of determining novelty under this Act, “substance means new” shall be interpreted strictly and applied with due regard to the principles of inventive step. An invention shall not be considered novel if it is disclosed, or demonstrated as publicly available, in a manner that would have rendered it obvious to a person skilled in the art at the date of filing the patent application. However, this determination shall be subject to consideration of any conflicting evidence presented by the applicant demonstrating unforeseen results or unexpected advantages arising from the combination of prior art elements. The Controller may, upon review and after affording an opportunity for argument, determine whether the claimed invention possesses a degree of ingenuity sufficient to overcome the presumption of lack of novelty as provided herein.

An application for a patent shall be deemed to lack novelty if it discloses subject matter which is not new, and further, that such substance means new with respect to prior publications or use anywhere in the world. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish evidence demonstrating the inventive step involved in the claimed invention, including detailed experimental data and comparative analysis against existing technologies. Failure to provide satisfactory documentation within the prescribed time shall render the application liable for rejection. Where an invention relates to a process by which a substance is produced, the patent shall only be granted if the process itself is new. The applicant shall pay the prescribed registry fee at the time of filing the application and subsequent fees as stipulated under this Act; non-payment will result in abandonment of the application.

Where an application for patent is rejected under this Act on the ground that the claimed invention lacks novelty or involves an obvious step, the applicant shall be afforded an opportunity to present counter-arguments and evidence demonstrating the inventive character of the subject matter. It shall be conclusively established that the substance means new, and any prior public knowledge rendering a claim non-patentable will be rigorously assessed against the totality of the application’s disclosure. Failure to adequately address objections regarding lack of novelty may result in immediate abandonment of the patent process. Any party aggrieved by a decision relating to the inventive step shall have recourse to appeal as provided herein, subject to penalties for frivolous or vexatious proceedings.

Where any patent has been granted in respect of an invention, and it is subsequently determined under this Act that the invention was not novel or obvious at the date of filing of the patent application, or that the invention does not fall within the definition of “invention” as provided herein, the Controller may order for the revocation of such patent. Any person aggrieved by a decision relating to the validity of a patent may appeal against such decision to the Appellate Board. Subject to this, any party seeking to challenge the subsistence of a patent shall be required to demonstrate that they have suffered material loss or damage as a direct consequence of the continued operation of the patent. The Controller shall provide an opportunity for all interested parties to present their case before making any order concerning the revocation of a register patents referred to in section sixty-seven.

Any party aggrieved by a decision relating to the revocation of a patent shall have the right to appeal under this Act to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of such decision. Failure to comply with prescribed procedures during the examination or grant of a patent may render the patent liable for rectification, subject to judicial review. Where infringement proceedings are instituted, any claim construction undertaken by the court shall be binding on all parties involved and shall not prejudice the validity of the patent in question. The Controller may, upon receiving evidence demonstrating wilful infringement, direct the imposition of enhanced penalties as provided herein, proportionate to the benefit derived from the infringing activity. Any false representation made during the application process for a register patents referred can result in criminal prosecution under relevant penal codes.

An international application patent is an application for a patent which originates from an initial application filed in a country designated as a “receiving State” under the Patent Cooperation Treaty and subsequently designates India as one of the countries where protection is sought. Such applications may be processed initially by the International Bureau, facilitating examination procedures across multiple jurisdictions. For the purposes of this Act, an international application patent shall be treated as if it were an original application filed directly before the Controller, subject to any requirements relating to translation and priority claims as provided herein. The applicant shall comply with all applicable timelines under this Act pertaining to prosecution and grant.

An applicant seeking entry of an international application patent into the Register shall furnish along with the request, a certified copy of the international search report and the written opinion received from the International Searching Authority. The Controller may require the applicant to submit translations of these documents into English or Hindi, as deemed necessary for proper examination. Where an international preliminary examination is conducted, a certified copy of the resulting report shall also be submitted within the time prescribed under this Act. Failure to provide these documents promptly may result in the application being held pending until compliance is demonstrated. The applicant shall pay such fees as are determined by notification issued from time to time.

Where an applicant elects to pursue an international application patent, and subsequently files a corresponding application in India, the priority date of the Indian application shall be determined by reference to the filing date of the earlier international application, subject to compliance with all applicable provisions regarding novelty and inventive step under this Act. Any person aggrieved by a decision relating to the examination or grant of an international application patent may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of such decision. The Controller shall have power to impose a penalty for failure to comply with any procedural requirement in relation to an international application, and such penalty shall be recoverable as if it were a decree of a civil court. Further, wilful misrepresentation made during the prosecution of an international application patent may render the applicant liable to damages.

An international application patent, when filed with designation of India, shall be processed according to the procedures outlined herein, subject to any specific provisions relating to such applications. The applicant shall furnish a certified copy of the international search report and written opinion within thirty days from the date of its communication under this Act. Failure to comply with this requirement may result in the application being deemed withdrawn. Where an amended claim is introduced following examination, the Controller shall provide opportunity for objection by any interested party as provided herein. The request for accelerated examination of an international application patent may be entertained only if all prescribed fees have been duly paid and supporting documentation submitted. Any decision regarding grant or refusal shall be communicated to both the applicant and the International Bureau.

An international application patent, where the designated State is India, shall be processed according to the procedures outlined herein, subject to compliance with all applicable provisions regarding novelty and inventive step. The applicant shall furnish a certified copy of the priority document, if any, within six months from the date of filing the international application; failure to do so may result in the application being deemed withdrawn. Where an examination is requested under this Act for an invention claimed in an international application patent, the Controller shall consider the search report and written opinion submitted by the International Searching Authority. The applicant shall be afforded an opportunity to respond to any objections raised during examination, provided that such response is filed within the prescribed time limit.

An international application patent, once examined and granted, shall confer upon the patentee exclusive rights subject only to limitations prescribed herein regarding compulsory licenses for public use. Any person aggrieved by a decision relating to an international application patent may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days of such decision; failure to comply with this timeframe shall render the appeal inadmissible. The Controller may, acting independently and without regard to any prior examination under the Patent Cooperation Treaty, revoke an international application patent if it is found that the invention was not novel or obvious at the date of filing. Such revocation proceedings are subject to a penalty of one thousand rupees for each day the infringement continues after notice.

An international application patent, once granted, shall remain subject to assignment and licensing agreements executed prior to or subsequent to its registration, provided that any such agreement explicitly addresses the scope of rights transferred and royalties payable. The Controller may, upon receiving a formal request accompanied by requisite documentation demonstrating due diligence in identifying all assignees and licensees, issue certificates confirming the validity of these assignments and licenses for evidentiary purposes in legal proceedings. Furthermore, where an international application patent incorporates subject matter derived from pre-existing intellectual property held by third parties, the applicant shall ensure that appropriate license agreements are secured to facilitate commercial exploitation, failing which, remedies available under this Act pertaining to infringement may be invoked against the licensee. Any transfer of rights relating to an international application patent requires notification to the Controller within thirty days.

An international application patent, once examined and granted according to procedures established herein, shall remain subject to challenge regarding its novelty or inventive step as though it were initially filed directly under this Act. Any party aggrieved by a decision relating to an international application patent may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days of such decision, provided that the appellant demonstrates substantial grounds for believing the original determination was erroneous based on misinterpretation of prior art or failure to adequately consider evidence presented during examination. The Controller shall provide reasons in writing for any rejection or modification of claims arising from an international application; these reasons are subject to judicial review if challenged within the prescribed appeal period.

An international application patent, where designation of India is included within its scope, shall be processed according to the procedures outlined herein, subject to any specific provisions relating to priority claims. The applicant shall provide a certified copy of the international search report and written opinion as soon as it becomes available. Where an international application designates India, the application date shall be taken as the filing date for the purposes of novelty assessment under this Act; however, the Controller may require further documentation demonstrating compliance with Indian patentability criteria. Any request for examination of such an international application must be filed within the prescribed timeframe following the publication of the international search report. The applicant is responsible for translating all relevant documents into English if they are initially submitted in another language.

Any person found to have made or caused to be made any false representation concerning an international application patent, whether in respect of priority, novelty, or inventive step, shall be liable for damages as determined by the High Court. Such damages may include compensation to any party demonstrably prejudiced by the misrepresentation and a sum not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees. Further, where a registered trade mark is falsely associated with an invention claimed in such an international application patent through deceptive advertising, the Controller may issue an injunction restraining further use of the misleading association. Any appeal from an order made under this provision shall lie to the High Court within ninety days.

An international application patent, upon examination and grant, shall be subject to challenge by any person aggrieved, within six months of such grant, on grounds including but not limited to lack of novelty or inventive step as determined under this Act. The Controller may, after affording the patentee an opportunity for a hearing, dismiss the patent if satisfied that it was obtained in error; however, the patentee shall have recourse to appeal such dismissal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. Furthermore, any party claiming rights in a certification trade mark identical or confusingly similar to a feature of the patented invention may petition the Controller seeking clarification regarding scope and enforceability, which determination shall be binding pending judicial review.

An international application patent, within the meaning of this Act, is one arising from an application filed under the Patent Cooperation Treaty and designating India as a member state. Such designation shall constitute a request for examination under this Act. The applicant proposing to register such an international application patent must demonstrate that all prescribed fees have been duly paid to the International Bureau. Further, where a relationship proposed registered between the international application and a prior Indian application exists, the date of filing of the earlier application shall be taken into account in determining novelty and inventive step as provided herein.

For the purposes of this Act, “invention” means a new and useful art, process, manufacture or composition of matter; provided that it is patentable subject matter as defined herein. An invention shall be deemed to include any improvement of an existing invention which, at the time of application, would not have been obvious to a person skilled in the art. To “apply patent” means to file a formal request with the Controller seeking examination and grant of exclusive rights under this Act relating to the claimed invention; such application must contain a full description of the invention enabling persons skilled in the art to practice it, along with claims defining the scope of protection sought.

An applicant desiring to apply patent shall furnish with the prescribed fee a statement of particulars relating to the invention, including its title and a concise description thereof. The statement must further detail the class or classes to which the invention relates, as determined by the controller. Where an application incorporates by reference matter which has previously been made available to the public, whether in India or elsewhere, the applicant shall provide a written explanation of the circumstances under which such matter became available and demonstrate that the claimed invention is not obvious to a person skilled in the art. The Controller may require further clarification regarding the novelty assessment if deemed necessary for proper examination.

Where any person considers that another person has infringed his patent, he may institute proceedings for relief against such infringement subject to the provisions of this Act. The remedies available to the patentee include injunction restraining the infringing party from further acts of infringement and damages sustained by the patentee as a consequence of the infringement. In determining the amount of damages, due consideration shall be given to the extent of the use made of the patented invention by the infringer and any profits which he has derived therefrom. The Controller may, upon application by the defendant in an action for infringement, order discovery of information relating to the patent or the alleged infringing act. A party seeking to apply patent must demonstrate reasonable grounds for believing that the claimed invention is novel and non-obvious.

An applicant seeking to apply patent shall furnish with the application a statement setting forth the inventor or inventors of the invention and their addresses. Where there are two or more applicants jointly applying for a patent, they shall be deemed to have made common assignment or agreement for the benefit of all such applicants. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish further particulars relating to any matter specified in the application, provided that such requirement is reasonable and does not impose an undue burden on the applicant. Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board within a period of sixty days from the date of receipt of the order. The Controller shall consider all relevant information submitted during the examination process before issuing any communication regarding patentability, subject to the provisions concerning confidentiality as provided herein.

An applicant seeking to apply patent shall furnish a complete specification describing the invention and its mode of operation, accompanied by claims clearly defining the scope of protection sought. The description must disclose the best method known to the applicant for carrying out the invention at the date of filing. Provided that, where the invention relates to a process for producing a substance, the specification shall also describe an enabling method for using that substance. Furthermore, the application must include particulars relating to priority, if any, claimed under this Act and be verified by the applicant or their authorized representative. The Controller may require further information or clarification regarding any aspect of the invention described in the patent application, which shall be submitted within a prescribed timeframe.

Any person who, having applied for a patent, makes or causes to be made any representation concerning the invention which is false and calculated to deceive, shall be guilty of an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. The Controller may, subject to appeal under this Act, issue an order restraining such person from further making such representations. Where a patent has been granted, the right to apply patent shall vest in the patentee and his successors in title; any infringement of that right is actionable as a civil wrong. Further, where damages are claimed for infringement, the Court may award compensation reflecting the reasonable royalty which the infringer would have paid had he lawfully sought to apply patent.

Where the controller is satisfied that any patented invention is necessary to prevent further undue exploitation of an earlier invention, or where such patented invention relates to a process for producing a substance already commercially available, the controller may permit another party to apply patent for the said invention subject to conditions as he deems fit. Such conditions shall include provisions regarding royalty payments and other financial considerations payable to the original patent holder. The agreement governing this permission to apply patent must be registered with the Controller within three months of its execution, detailing the scope of permitted use and duration. Failure to register such an agreement may render it unenforceable under this Act. Further, any assignment or license granted in relation to a permitted invention shall also require registration as provided herein.

An applicant seeking to apply patent protection shall furnish with the application a statement setting forth the claimed invention and its technical field; however, where such statement is demonstrably deficient in clarity or fails adequately to disclose the underlying inventive concept, the Controller may issue a notice requiring amendment within a prescribed period. Failure to comply with this notice shall render the application liable for rejection, though an appeal against such rejection lies before the Appellate Board. The Board’s determination on any question of fact relating to the adequacy of disclosure is final and binding, subject to challenge only upon demonstrable proof of material error apparent on the face of the record.

An applicant seeking to apply patent protection shall furnish with the application a statement detailing the extent to which the invention is novel and non-obvious, subject to examination by the Controller. The use patented processes or compositions described within an accepted patent requires prior authorization from the patent holder, unless such use falls under exceptions as provided herein relating to research activities undertaken for non-commercial purposes. Any party intending to commercially exploit a patented process must demonstrate compliance with stipulated licensing terms and conditions, including payment of royalties where applicable. Failure to adhere to these stipulations may result in legal action initiated by the patentee, potentially leading to injunctions restricting further use or manufacture. The Controller shall maintain records pertaining to all authorizations granted under this Act.

Where the proprietor of a patent seeks to apply patent rights relating to a process used in the manufacture of a substance applied for or obtained by means of fermentation, he may grant a license conferring the right to use such process, subject to conditions as provided herein. Such licenses shall be assignable and transmissible, whether jointly with the patent or separately, and any assignment or transmission shall be recorded in the prescribed manner. Further, where an invention incorporates elements protected by an unregistered trade mark used prominently in connection with a product manufactured using the patented process, the license agreement may stipulate restrictions on use of such trade mark to safeguard the goodwill associated with both the patented technology and the brand identity. The Controller may require disclosure of any such trade mark usage within the license terms before registration is complete.

Where any person alleges that another party has unlawfully sought to apply patent protection to an invention incorporating elements identifiable as constituting an authorised use mark previously registered by the claimant, such allegation may be brought before the relevant Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. The tribunal shall consider whether the application for the patent infringes upon the exclusive rights afforded under the Marks Act and any associated regulations pertaining to the said mark. It is provided that the applicant for the patent bears the onus of demonstrating a lack of substantial similarity between the patented invention and the registered authorised use mark, or that the claimed invention constitutes an inventive step independent of the mark’s distinctive character. Decisions of the tribunal are subject to appeal under this Act.

An application to apply patent shall include particulars of the invention, specifying the technical field to which it relates and stating the prior art knowledge known to the applicant as of the date of filing. The term "invention" for the purposes of this Act means a new technical solution to a problem in any field, subject to exclusions provided herein relating to discoveries, scientific theories, mathematical methods, schemes or methods for performing mental acts, playing games or doing business, and programs for computers. A patent shall not be granted for an invention that is contrary to public morality and order, human life or animal life, or inventions the use or commercialization of which are prohibited under any law.

An applicant intending to apply patent shall furnish with the prescribed fee a statement of priority claiming benefit from any earlier filing, provided that such earlier filing was made by the applicant or a legal representative. The particulars of the practitioner, being a practise patent agent, who assists in the preparation and filing of the application shall be clearly indicated on the form. Failure to disclose this information may result in delays in processing. Any modification to the statement of priority after the initial filing requires prior written consent from the Controller. Further, any subsequent assignment or alteration of ownership relating to the invention must also be registered with the patent office and accompanied by a duly executed instrument as provided herein.

For the purposes of this Act, “apply patent invention” means the utilization of a patented process or product in any manufacturing activity or commercial enterprise, whether directly by the patentee or through a licensee authorized under this Act. Such application shall encompass not only the direct exploitation of the invention but also activities ancillary thereto, provided that such activities are integral to the overall process and contribute substantially to the realization of the invention’s intended purpose. Nothing in this definition shall be construed as requiring the use of the patented invention for research or experimental purposes undertaken without commercial intent, subject to conditions prescribed herein.

An applicant seeking registration of a utility model invention shall furnish particulars relating to the field of use and intended purpose of the invention, along with a detailed description sufficient to enable a person skilled in the art to apply patent invention without undue experimentation. The prescribed fee for such furnishing shall be remitted at the time of application. Where an objection is raised by the Registrar regarding the clarity or completeness of these particulars, the applicant may submit further information within the period specified under this Act. Failure to comply with such a notice shall render the utility model application liable for rejection. Any alteration to the initially submitted particulars after the grant of registration will be subject to approval from the Controller and may incur additional fees as determined by regulations framed in accordance with this Act.

Where any person aggrieved by an order of the Controller relating to the refusal of a patent or the revocation thereof, or by any other decision taken under this Act affecting his rights, appeals to the Appellate Board, the Board shall give notice to all parties concerned and hear them before passing any order. The appeal may be made on grounds that the invention does not satisfy the criteria for patentability as provided herein, including novelty and inventive step; or that the Controller erred in interpreting the scope of a claim. It is further provided that an applicant seeking to *apply patent invention* shall demonstrate, during appellate proceedings, clear evidence substantiating the arguments presented against the original decision, failing which the appeal shall be dismissed summarily.

An applicant seeking to apply patent invention relating to a process or composition for producing a substance shall furnish with the request a detailed description of the method of manufacture and particulars concerning any apparatus used therefor. The Controller may require the applicant, prior to acceptance, to submit further information regarding the working of the invention, including details pertaining to scale-up procedures and anticipated yields. Any discrepancies arising between the claimed scope of protection and the registered particulars shall be subject to rectification register proceedings initiated by either the patent holder or a third party with a demonstrable interest. Such applications for rectification must specify the errors sought to be corrected and provide supporting documentation as provided herein.

Where any person considers that another party has infringed his right to apply patent invention, he may institute proceedings for relief in the manner prescribed herein. Such proceedings shall involve demonstrating prima facie evidence of the patented invention and establishing that the defendant’s actions fall within the scope of claims as defined in the granted patent. The remedies available under this Act include an injunction restraining further acts of infringement, damages proportionate to the loss suffered by the plaintiff, and costs of litigation. Provided that, where the infringing act relates to a drug intended for use as medicine, the Court may also order the destruction of the infringing goods. Further, any party aggrieved may appeal against any decision under this Act to the appellate forum as provided herein.

An applicant seeking protection through an application patent cooperation procedure shall file particulars including the title of the invention, inventor’s name and address, priority details where applicable, and a concise description of the invention as provided herein. The prescribed form shall include claims defining the scope of protection sought; these claims must be clear, precise, and supported by the disclosure. An international application designating India under the Patent Cooperation Treaty constitutes an application for patent rights in India only if a subsequent national phase application is filed within the time limit specified under this Act. Failure to do so will render the initial international application deemed abandoned.

An applicant seeking registration of a design shall furnish particulars relating to the true and complete nature of the proposed design, including any relevant technical data or schematics demonstrating its novelty and industrial applicability. The Registrar may require submission of additional documentation substantiating claims of originality where ambiguity exists concerning prior art. Where an invention is claimed through an application patent cooperation procedure, the applicant shall provide certified copies of all documents filed with the International Bureau, translated into English if originally in another language, as evidence of priority date and international stage proceedings. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in rejection of the design registration or postponement of examination until such time as the deficiencies are rectified.

Where any person discovers that his invention is being commercially exploited without his authorization, he may institute civil proceedings seeking injunctive relief and damages. Such remedies are available irrespective of whether a patent has already been granted for the invention or remains pending as an application. Where an applicant elects to utilize the application patent cooperation system under the Patent Cooperation Treaty, the Controller shall have the power to require submission of translations of claims and drawings into English, provided that such requirement does not unduly delay the processing of the international application. Failure to comply with a direction issued by the Controller concerning translation may result in the rejection of the corresponding Indian application. The applicant shall be liable to pay costs incurred by the Controller in connection with obtaining said translations.

An applicant seeking protection of an invention through an application patent cooperation procedure shall furnish with the request a statement indicating whether the claim is for priority right or not; failure to do so may render the application liable for rejection under this Act. The Controller, upon receipt of an international application designating India, shall notify the International Bureau and undertake such actions as are prescribed by the Patent Cooperation Treaty. Where an applicant elects to enter regional phase in India, the request for further examination shall be processed according to established guidelines. Any fees payable relating to the processing of the application shall be remitted within the stipulated timeframe; otherwise, the application may be deemed abandoned. The Controller is empowered to require additional information or clarification from the applicant at any stage of the proceedings, provided that such requests are reasonable and relevant to assessing patentability.

An applicant seeking protection through an application patent cooperation procedure shall ensure that the request for international search and examination is received by the designated receiving office within thirty months of the earliest priority date claimed in the application. The prescribed fees, as determined under this Act, must be remitted to the receiving office at the time of filing the international application; failure to do so will render the application deemed withdrawn. Where an applicant elects to proceed with examination after transmittal to the International Bureau, the Controller may require submission of additional information or clarification regarding the invention’s novelty and non-obviousness as compared to prior art disclosed. Any such request shall be complied with within six months, subject to extension granted by the Controller upon demonstration of good cause.

Any person who, knowing that any information relating to the invention has been obtained in pursuance of this Act, communicates such information to any other person without authorization shall be liable for damages as determined by the High Court. An applicant seeking patent protection under this Act may elect to file an application patent cooperation request, provided that such election is made within the time limits prescribed herein and subject to compliance with all applicable international regulations. Failure to adhere to these timelines will render the cooperative request void ab initio. The Controller shall have power to impose a penalty of not less than fifty thousand rupees but not exceeding two hundred thousand rupees on any party found in violation of this provision, without prejudice to other remedies available under this Act.

Where the applicant for a patent is a body corporate or a partnership, any license granted or assignment made of the patent, or of any right or interest therein, shall require prior registration with the Patents Office and shall be deemed invalid unless so registered within three months of its execution. The Controller may, subject to fulfilling prescribed conditions regarding public interest and national security, permit a licensee under such a registered license to sub-license rights pertaining to the patented invention, provided that the original patent holder retains ultimate control over the exploitation of the intellectual property. Further, any application patent cooperation agreement involving an Indian resident shall be treated as if it were a domestic application for all purposes under this Act and may be subject to additional scrutiny regarding benefit sharing with local inventors.

An applicant seeking protection through an application patent cooperation procedure shall furnish a certified copy of the international preliminary examination report, including any amendments or observations made by the International Searching Authority, within six months from the date on which that report is communicated to the applicant under this Act. Failure to comply with this requirement may result in the application being deemed abandoned, subject to appeal before an appellate tribunal. The Controller shall provide written reasons for such a determination and the applicant shall have thirty days to submit counter-arguments demonstrating due diligence or excusable delay. Any challenge to the validity of the patent granted based on non-disclosure under this Act must be brought within five years from the grant date, provided that the aggrieved party demonstrates prejudice arising directly from the omission.

An application patent cooperation process initiated outside of India relating to an invention shall be considered a valid application under this Act provided that within six months from the date of publication of the international search report, a request for substantive examination is duly filed with the Indian Patent Office. The applicant shall indicate whether the invention relates to agriculture, horticulture, or any other form of cultivation and may provide details concerning the geographical indication registered in connection with the agricultural product derived from said invention. Failure to comply with this provision will render the application liable for abandonment as provided herein.

An applicant seeking registration of an invention under this Act relating to a process involving micro-organisms shall furnish with the application detailed particulars regarding the method of cultivating, preserving and maintaining such cultures. The Controller may require the deposition of such microbial cultures with an internationally recognized depository authority, subject to conditions prescribed by regulations framed under this Act. Such deposited cultures shall be deemed part of the patent application for the purposes of novelty assessment. Any right granted through a patent obtained via application patent cooperation is wholly transmissible and assignable in accordance with the provisions herein. The applicant shall provide proof of such transmission upon request, as may be required by the Controller.

An applicant seeking protection through an application patent cooperation procedure shall furnish a declaration attesting to the best of their knowledge that the invention disclosed is novel and involves inventive step, failing which rectification proceedings may be initiated under this Act. Where an international search report indicates a lack of novelty or inventive character, the Controller may require the applicant to submit arguments rebutting such findings within a prescribed period; failure to do so shall render the application liable for rejection. Any person aggrieved by a decision relating to the grant or revocation of a patent arising from an application patent cooperation procedure may appeal to the Appellate Board. The burden of proving prior use or publication negating novelty lies upon the appellant, subject to procedural safeguards as provided herein regarding evidence and hearings.

For the purposes of this Act, a form filed patent is defined as a patent granted subsequent to an application initially submitted in a prescribed format, wherein at least one claim was originally drafted utilizing terminology or structural elements deemed by the Controller to be substantially similar to those previously employed within published patent applications. Such similarity shall not, however, preclude grant provided that the invention itself possesses subject matter novelty and inventive step as required under this Act. The determination of substantial similarity for the purposes of a form filed patent shall consider prevailing industry practices and prior art disclosures.

An applicant seeking registration of a form filed patent shall furnish with the application a declaration specifying the source and circumstances under which the design was derived, provided that such declaration is not required where the design originates from independent creation by the applicant or their employees. The Controller may require further documentation substantiating the claimed originality if reasonable doubt arises regarding the veracity of the declaration. Any alteration to the form filed patent after its initial registration shall be subject to approval by the Controller and will constitute a new filing, requiring fresh examination as provided herein. Failure to disclose material information pertaining to prior use or publication of the design may render the registered form filed patent liable for revocation under this Act.

Where a form filed patent is granted based on information contained within the formal request and accompanying documentation, any person aggrieved by such grant may institute proceedings before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board seeking revocation of the patent. Such proceedings shall be predicated upon grounds demonstrating that the invention was not novel or involved an inventive step at the date of filing of the application for the form filed patent. The Board may, after affording the patentee and the petitioner a reasonable opportunity to be heard, determine whether the grant was improperly made. If the Board finds in favour of the petitioner, it shall order that the patent be revoked with effect from such date as the Board deems just and equitable. Costs of the proceedings shall be determined by the Board under this Act.

An applicant seeking entry of a form filed patent into the Register shall submit with the request a certified copy of the document constituting the form filing, duly authenticated by the appropriate authority as prescribed herein. The Controller may require such further documentation or clarification regarding the authenticity and completeness of the form filing as is deemed necessary for verification purposes. Where the form filing contains discrepancies or omissions that materially affect the clarity or scope of the invention claimed, the Controller shall notify the applicant and provide an opportunity to rectify the deficiencies within a period not exceeding ninety days from the date of notification. Failure to adequately address these concerns within the stipulated timeframe will result in rejection of the request for entry into the Register. The decision regarding acceptance or rejection of a form filed patent is subject to appeal under this Act.

An applicant seeking grant of a patent shall file a form filed patent accompanied by the prescribed particulars relating to priority, if any, claimed under this Act. The information disclosed within the form filed patent must accurately reflect the invention as described and claimed; failure to do so may render the patent liable for revocation proceedings. Where an amendment is proposed to the claims of a form filed patent during examination, such amendment shall not be allowed unless it meets the requirements regarding support for the amended claim in the original specification. The Controller may require further clarification or documentation from the applicant concerning any aspect detailed within the form filed patent before proceeding with its assessment.

Any person who knowingly makes, uses, or imports any process, article, or substance embodying an invention claimed in a form filed patent without the authorization of the patentee shall be liable to pay damages equivalent to the greater of five per centum of the sales realized from such acts or fifty thousand rupees. The Controller may, upon receiving a complaint regarding infringement, issue interim injunctions restraining any person from continuing such infringing activities pending final determination of the matter. Failure to comply with an order for disclosure of information relating to the form filed patent, as directed by the Controller, shall constitute contempt and render the defaulter liable to imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months. Further, costs associated with enforcement proceedings shall be borne by the infringing party.

Where the controller is satisfied that a form filed patent relates to an invention which comprises improvements upon an existing technology, and where such improvement incorporates elements derived from intellectual property rights held by another person or entity, the controller may direct the applicant to provide for a license granting royalty-free access to said incorporated elements. Such direction shall be accompanied by a written explanation detailing the basis of the finding regarding derivation. The applicant shall then have a period of ninety days to comply with this directive, either by negotiating and executing a suitable licensing agreement or submitting a reasoned objection under this Act. Failure to do so may result in rejection of the patent application. Any assignment of a form filed patent shall be deemed to include all rights pertaining to any license granted pursuant to these provisions.

Where any person aggrieved by an order of the Controller relating to the acceptance or rejection of a form filed patent, or concerning the determination of priority between two or more applications for such patents, may appeal to the Appellate Board. The Appellate Board shall admit appeals only if it is satisfied that a substantial question of law has arisen and that the decision of the Controller was manifestly erroneous. Provided that an appeal under this Act does not operate as a stay of any order made by the Controller unless the Appellate Board otherwise directs. Any party seeking to challenge the validity of a form filed patent granted shall do so within six months from the date of publication of said grant, subject to the provisions regarding pre-grant opposition.

An application for a patent that is presented in the prescribed form and contains information required under this Act, but which does not fully comply with all formal requirements as provided herein, shall constitute a form filed patent. Where deficiencies are identified following examination, the Controller may issue an error amendment notice to the applicant specifying the particulars of such deficiencies. The applicant shall be afforded a reasonable opportunity to rectify these errors and file amended documents. Failure to address the concerns raised in the error amendment notice within the stipulated time period may result in rejection of the application under this Act.

An applicant seeking examination of a patent shall file a form filed patent accompanied by the prescribed fee and particulars relating to priority, if any, claimed in respect thereof. The statement of inventiveness required under this Act shall clearly delineate the novelty and non-obviousness of the invention over prior art. Where an application incorporates by reference designs or layouts, the applicant must provide evidence demonstrating ownership or a valid license pertaining to those incorporated elements. Layout design vested rights are not affected by the filing of a patent incorporating such designs unless expressly authorized in writing by the registered proprietor of the layout design. The Controller may require further clarification regarding any aspect of the form filed patent and shall afford the applicant an opportunity to respond within the timeframe prescribed. Failure to comply with this requirement may result in rejection of the application.

An applicant seeking registration of a utility model shall furnish with the application a declaration stating whether the invention is already known or described and, if so, providing particulars thereof. Where an international application for a patent designating India is received under the Patent Cooperation Treaty, the Controller may require the applicant to submit translations of the description, claims, and any drawings into English or Hindi, as deemed necessary by the Controller. The prescribed fees for filing such applications shall be remitted electronically, subject to exceptions granted by the Controller in cases of demonstrable financial hardship. Any request for extension of time under this Act relating to a patent filed designating India must be accompanied by an affidavit explaining the reasons for delay and supporting documentation.

Where any person considers that another person has infringed a patent granted under this Act, such person may institute proceedings for relief against the infringement in the manner provided herein. Subject to appeal to the Appellate Board, an injunction restraining the infringing party from further acts of infringement shall be granted if it is established that the patented invention was being used without authorization. The Controller may, upon receiving a complaint regarding unauthorized use or manufacture of a patented article, direct any person aggrieved by such action to submit evidence substantiating the claim. Any patent filed designating India and subsequently found invalid due to prior publication or use shall be liable for damages payable to those prejudiced by the grant. The amount of compensation shall be determined based on the extent of commercial detriment suffered.

Where any person institutes proceedings for infringement of a patent, it shall be incumbent upon that party to demonstrate, beyond reasonable doubt, that the patented invention was indeed being manufactured, used or sold without license from the patentee. Failure to provide such conclusive evidence may result in dismissal of the claim and imposition of costs reflective of the frivolous nature of the litigation. Further, any entity found to have knowingly misrepresented facts pertaining to a patent filed designating India during opposition proceedings shall be liable for damages equivalent to three times the lost profits suffered by the patent holder, as provided herein. The Controller may, subject to appeal, order seizure and destruction of infringing goods discovered through such investigations.

Where the proprietor of a patent desires to grant a license or assign his rights relating to the invention claimed in the patent filed designating India, he shall execute an instrument in writing specifying the terms and conditions thereof, including but not limited to the scope of exclusivity granted, royalty rates payable, and duration of the license. Such instrument may be registered with the Controller upon payment of the prescribed fee, and such registration shall confer on the licensee or assignee the benefit of priority as provided herein. The proprietor shall provide notice of any assignment or license to the Controller within thirty days of execution; failure to do so will render the assignment or license voidable at the option of a subsequent bona fide purchaser. Any modification to a registered license agreement requires further registration, subject to the same procedural requirements applicable to initial registration.

A complete specification, when amended subsequent to the initial filing date but prior to the sealing of the patent, shall be treated as a substitute for the original specification for all purposes under this Act. The amendment itself must clearly indicate the changes made to the originally filed description, claims, and drawings. Such amendments are permissible only if they do not alter the inventive concept disclosed in the complete specification as initially presented. Any addition or alteration that introduces new matter is prohibited. A patent examiner may require further clarification regarding the scope and effect of a complete specification amended in this manner, provided that such requirement does not unduly delay the processing of the application.

Where an application for a patent has been laid open for public inspection under this Act, and subsequently a complete specification amended is filed by the applicant, such amendment shall only be entertained with the written consent of the Controller. The Controller may require the applicant to submit a declaration affirming that the proposed amendments do not substantially alter the scope or nature of the invention as originally claimed. Further, any person aggrieved by the acceptance of an amended specification may within sixty days from the date of publication thereof file a notice of opposition under this Act. Such opposition shall be deemed to relate specifically to the matters introduced by the amendment and shall proceed according to the established procedures provided herein.

Where an applicant for a patent has submitted a complete specification, and subsequently seeks to amend said specification under this Act, such amendment shall only be permissible if it clarifies the subject matter disclosed in the original application. Any party aggrieved by a decision relating to the acceptance or rejection of an amended specification may appeal to the Controller within sixty days from the date of communication of that decision. The Controller may, after giving all parties concerned an opportunity of being heard, confirm, vary, or reverse such decision. Further, any person claiming damages arising from the grant of a patent based on a complete specification amended without proper clarity shall be entitled to seek redressal through appropriate legal proceedings, subject to limitations as provided herein regarding contributory infringement.

Where an application for a patent has been laid open for public inspection under this Act, and subsequently a complete specification amended pursuant to a direction issued by the Controller or with the applicant’s consent, the amended specification shall take effect as if it had been originally filed. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish such further information or particulars relating to the invention as are necessary for the purposes of examination. Any person may, within one month from the date on which the amended complete specification is laid open, file with the Controller any representation against the grant of patent based upon the amended specification. Such representations shall be dealt with in accordance with the procedure prescribed herein. The applicant shall be afforded an opportunity to respond to such representations and submit counter-arguments as provided herein.

Where an application for a patent has been laid open for public inspection under this Act, and subsequently a complete specification amended pursuant to a direction issued by the Controller or with the applicant’s consent, such amendment shall not affect the rights of any person who has taken notice of the original specification. The amended specification must clearly indicate the changes made relative to the originally filed document; failure to do so shall render the patent liable to revocation under this Act. Provided that if the amendments relate solely to claims and do not introduce any new matter, the Controller may permit the amendment without requiring further examination, subject to compliance with prescribed procedural requirements. The applicant shall furnish an undertaking confirming adherence to these stipulations.

Where an application for a patent has been granted and subsequently subject to amendment resulting in a complete specification amended after the initial publication under this Act, any person aggrieved by such amendment may institute proceedings before the Controller seeking revocation of the patent. The Controller shall, upon receiving notice of such challenge, issue summons requiring the patentee to appear and defend the validity of the patent as modified by the amended specification. Failure to comply with the summons or a finding that the complete specification amended does not meet the requirements for patentability under this Act will render the patent liable for forfeiture and subject the patentee to penalties prescribed herein, including compensatory damages payable to the aggrieved party.

Where an invention is disclosed within a complete specification amended subsequent to the initial filing date, and where such amendment incorporates elements derived from technology previously developed by another party, the patent holder shall provide written notification to that other party detailing the specific contributions acknowledged. This notification must include a non-exclusive license grant permitting the utilization of those antecedent technologies for research purposes only, valid for the duration of the patent’s term. Failure to furnish this notice prior to commercial exploitation of the invention may render the patent liable to revocation under this Act. The Controller shall have the power to issue directions regarding compliance with these notification requirements and may impose penalties for non-compliance. Provided that, such license grant shall not extend to any activity infringing upon existing intellectual property rights held by third parties.

Where an application for a patent has been refused on the ground that the complete specification does not describe the invention claimed therein with sufficient clarity and completeness, and subsequently undergoes amendment pursuant to a direction issued under this Act, such amended specification shall be subject to further scrutiny. The Controller may require additional data or clarification regarding the impact of said amendments upon the novelty and inventive step of the invention as originally sought. Any party aggrieved by the decision relating to the acceptance or rejection of an application following a complete specification amended in this manner may appeal under the prescribed procedure, demonstrating that the amendment materially alters the scope of protection claimed and prejudices their existing rights.

Where an invention is patented following a complete specification amended pursuant to a request for further information under this Act, the patentee shall remain responsible for ensuring that the claims as finally granted accurately reflect the subject matter disclosed. Failure to do so may render the patent vulnerable to challenge on grounds of lack of enablement or clarity. Any licensee operating under a patent obtained through such an amended specification is entitled to enforce the terms of their license agreement, including the agreed royalties manner, against infringers without prejudice to any defenses available to them under this Act. The Controller shall not be bound by any prior representations made during examination and investigation proceedings relating to the amended specification. Further, remedies for infringement shall be pursued in accordance with established procedures as provided herein.

Where an application for a patent has been refused on grounds of lack of novelty or inventive step, and subsequently amended to overcome said objections, the complete specification amended shall be subject to rigorous scrutiny by the Controller. Any attempt to introduce matter not in the original disclosure through such amendments will render the patent liable to revocation under this Act. Furthermore, where the invention relates to a process involving a well-known trade mark used as an indicator of origin or quality, any infringement resulting from the patented process shall be deemed a violation attracting severe penalties and subject to immediate injunctions. The Controller may also impose compensatory damages for wilful misrepresentation during examination.

Where an invention disclosed in a complete specification is subject to a license granted by the patentee, such license may include provisions for assignment of rights relating to specific claims or aspects of the patented technology. The terms of any such assignment shall be documented within a supplementary agreement annexed to the original licensing contract and filed with the Controller. Further, where a complete specification amended pursuant to a request for re-examination incorporates modifications impacting the scope of protection, the patentee shall provide notice to all licensees detailing the revised claims. To facilitate equitable distribution of royalties arising from sublicensing activities undertaken by licensees, there shall constitute fund administered by the Department for Industrial Policy and Promotion, into which a percentage of such revenues will be deposited as determined by regulations framed under this Act.

For the purposes of this Act, a ‘clause invention’ shall be defined as an innovation which incorporates elements derived from two or more distinct prior art disclosures, wherein each element contributes to the claimed functionality but is not itself inventive when considered in isolation. A clause invention shall not be deemed non-obvious merely because it combines known features in an unexpected manner; rather, the synergistic effect of these combined elements must demonstrate a technical advance beyond the sum of their individual contributions. Provided that, where the combination results directly from combining subject matter disclosed in the same document, this provision shall not apply and such combination may be considered inventive as provided herein.

An application for registration of a design relating to an article shall be deemed invalid under this Act if it incorporates elements derived from a pre-existing invention, irrespective of whether such invention is currently protected by patent. The Controller may require the applicant to demonstrate that any incorporated element constitutes a novel and non-obvious modification of the original inventive concept, sufficient to warrant separate design protection. This requirement shall apply particularly where the application claims novelty based on aesthetic variations of a functionally defined article. For the purposes of determining such validity, the assessment of whether an element represents a genuine clause invention will consider its contribution to the overall character and appearance of the registered design.

Where an application for patents contains claims relating to a method or process, and it is demonstrated to the Controller that the claimed invention incorporates a novel clause invention which, if implemented, would result in the production of a substance already known to be used as a pharmaceutical ingredient, the patent may be granted subject to the inclusion of measures reasonably designed to prevent abuse of the exclusive rights conferred.
