Such measures shall include, but are not limited to, limitations on the scope of the claims and stipulations regarding licensing arrangements for third parties engaged in research or development related to that substance. The Controller may require the applicant to provide evidence demonstrating the non-infringing nature of the claimed process with respect to existing pharmaceutical formulations as provided herein. Failure to comply shall render the patent liable to revocation under this Act.

An application for a patent relating to a novel pharmaceutical composition shall be examined to determine whether the claimed invention constitutes an inventive step, subject to the provisions regarding obviousness. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish further particulars concerning the method of manufacture and clinical trials undertaken in respect of the composition, provided that such requirements are relevant to assessing non-obviousness. Where a prior publication discloses a similar compound with differing therapeutic application, the examiner shall consider whether the claimed use represents a sufficient inventive contribution. The determination of an inventive step requires assessment of the state of knowledge as it existed at the priority date and consideration of any related applications filed by the applicant. A finding that a *clause invention* lacks an inventive step may be appealed to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the decision.

An invention shall not be considered non-patentable under this Act solely on the ground that it involves an element previously disclosed in another patent application, provided that such disclosure does not render the claimed invention obvious to a person skilled in the art. The determination of whether a *clause invention* is inventive shall take into account the entire body of prior art as known at the date of filing and consider any combination of features from multiple sources. Further, an invention relating to a method of agricultural practice shall be eligible for patent protection only if it involves a technical process having an effect on the land or plant, subject to compliance with regulations issued by the Central Government concerning bio-safety protocols and environmental impact assessments as provided herein.

Where any person alleges that an invention does not constitute a clause invention as provided herein, and brings an action seeking a declaration to that effect, the burden shall lie upon them to demonstrate, with clear and convincing evidence, that the claimed invention lacks novelty or involves obviousness. Failure to satisfy this evidentiary standard will result in dismissal of the suit with costs awarded against the plaintiff. Furthermore, any party found to have maliciously instigated such an action without reasonable grounds for believing the invention invalid may be liable for damages as determined by the Court. The Controller shall issue guidelines regarding acceptable forms of evidence pertaining to inventive step assessments under this Act.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any patentee desiring to grant a license under this Act shall be required to submit a detailed memorandum to the Controller outlining the scope and terms thereof. Such memorandum must specify the territory covered by the license, the royalty rate payable, and the duration for which the license is granted. Where the patentee has assigned the patent rights to another party, that assignee shall possess all powers of licensing as if they were the original patentee, provided that such assignment was registered under this Act. The Controller may, after due consideration and public notice, approve or reject any proposed license agreement, taking into account whether the terms are manifestly unfair or restrictive concerning the exploitation of the clause invention within India. Any modification to a licensed clause invention requires prior consent from the Controller.

Where an objection is raised under this Act concerning the novelty of a claimed invention, the Controller may require the applicant to furnish evidence demonstrating that the alleged prior use did not involve exploitation of the invention as a clause invention. Such evidence shall be considered alongside any counter-submissions presented by the objector asserting that the prior use constituted substantial and demonstrable exploitation. The burden of proving non-exploitation rests upon the applicant, subject to the proviso that if the objector fails to adequately specify the nature and extent of said exploitation, the Controller may direct a hearing wherein both parties shall present arguments regarding the matter. Decisions made under this provision are appealable to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of notification.

An application for a patent may include visual recordings, including but not limited to photographic and videographic representations, demonstrating aspects of the invention’s operation or construction, provided that such recordings are supplementary to the written description and claims. The Controller shall consider these visual aids solely for clarity in understanding the nature of the claimed invention; they do not, however, form part of the patent itself unless explicitly incorporated within the textual description. For purposes of determining novelty under this Act, any publicly accessible visual recording depicting a device or process embodying a clause invention shall be treated as prior art, irrespective of whether it contains accompanying written material. The applicant bears the burden of demonstrating that such recordings do not anticipate the claimed invention.

For the purposes of this Act, an “invention convention” shall be deemed to have occurred when an applicant files an application for patent protection in India within twelve months of having initially filed an identical or substantially similar application for the same invention in a designated convention country. Such designation shall require that the originating application clearly identifies the inventor and specifies the subject matter claimed. An invention convention does not, however, confer any rights beyond those explicitly provided herein; nor does it preclude scrutiny under this Act regarding novelty or inventive step. The Controller may reject an invention convention application if certain conditions are met as specified elsewhere in this legislation.

An applicant seeking registration of an invention convention shall furnish with the application a declaration specifying the details of the prior applications made in respect of the subject matter of the invention. Such declaration must clearly state the countries where the initial application was filed, along with the dates thereof. The Controller may require further documentation substantiating these claims and verifying adherence to timelines stipulated under this Act concerning convention applications. Failure to provide accurate or complete information regarding prior filings will render the application liable for rejection. It is incumbent upon the applicant to maintain meticulous records pertaining to all related international patent applications, as verification of an invention convention is a prerequisite for progression through the examination process.

Where an aggrieved party alleges infringement of patent rights under this Act, such party shall be entitled to seek remedies including, but not limited to, permanent injunction restraining further acts of infringement. The Controller may, upon receiving evidence demonstrating wilful infringement, order the infringing party to pay damages equivalent to a percentage of the profits derived from the sale of the infringing product or process, as determined by the Controller’s assessment. In cases involving an invention convention, the burden shall lie on the defendant to prove that the initial application in the convention country was duly filed and contained sufficient detail regarding the claimed invention. Further, any claim for damages arising from infringement relating to a patent granted through an invention convention is subject to limitations as provided herein concerning prior use rights.

Where an objection is taken against a patent application under this Act on the ground that the claimed invention lacks novelty or involves an inventive step, the Controller may require the applicant to furnish evidence demonstrating the validity of the invention. Such evidence shall include, but not be limited to, documentary proof relating to prior publications, public demonstrations, or any other means by which the invention became available to the public before the date of filing of the patent application. In cases involving an *invention convention*, the Controller shall consider the dates of corresponding applications filed in convention countries when assessing novelty and inventive step. The applicant shall be afforded a reasonable opportunity to respond to such objections, presenting arguments and counter-evidence as deemed appropriate. Failure to adequately address the Controller’s concerns may result in rejection of the patent application or amendment of the claims as provided herein.

An invention shall be deemed non-obvious if, having regard to the state of the art as provided herein, it does not involve an element of ingenuity sufficient to warrant its being regarded as an advancement in the art. Subject to this, an application relating to an invention convention may proceed only if the applicant demonstrates that the initial filing date in the originating country was accurately recorded and verifiable through official documentation. Furthermore, where a prior publication or use exists which would render the claimed invention obvious, the Controller shall require conclusive evidence demonstrating that such publication or use did not reasonably inform any person skilled in the relevant art. Provided that this requirement is satisfied, the application may continue to examination.

Where an aggrieved party alleges infringement of patent rights relating to an invention convention, such party may institute proceedings before the relevant High Court seeking redress. The court shall consider whether the alleged infringing act falls within the scope of claims as defined in the granted patent. Failure to provide adequate notice prior to initiating legal action against a potential infringer will render any subsequent claim for damages unsustainable under this Act. Any person found guilty of wilful infringement, demonstrated through deliberate and knowing disregard of existing patents, shall be liable to pay compensation not exceeding ten times the proven damages suffered by the patentee. The court may also issue an injunction restraining further infringing activities as provided herein.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, an inventor may grant a license relating to any patentable invention or granted patent, either wholly or partially, to any person, including a body corporate, and such license shall be assignable. Where an invention convention has been filed in a convention country prior to the date of application for a patent in India, the licensee shall be bound by all terms and conditions applicable to the original invention convention. Any assignment or license granted under this Act shall require registration with the Controller, and failure to register such transaction within three months from its execution shall render it voidable at the option of any party affected thereby. The Controller may prescribe a fee for registering assignments and licenses, as deemed appropriate.

Where an objection is taken under this Act against a claim in respect of novelty or inventive step, the Controller may require the applicant to furnish such documentary evidence as he deems necessary to substantiate the claims made in the patent application. Such requirement shall be accompanied by a reasoned statement outlining the specific deficiencies identified and the information sought. The applicant shall have thirty days from the date of receipt of said requirement to comply; failure to do so will render the application liable for abandonment, subject to an appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days thereafter. In cases involving an invention convention, the burden of proving adherence to timelines stipulated under this Act rests entirely upon the applicant, and any discrepancy shall be construed strictly against them.

Where an inventor desires to utilize an invention convention secured under this Act through means other than direct manufacture or sale, they may execute a license agreement granting specified rights pertaining to such use. Such licenses shall be recorded with the Controller and are subject to annual fees as prescribed. The terms of any assignment of patent rights relating to the use invention must clearly delineate the scope of permitted activities, including but not limited to geographical limitations and fields of application. Further, where a license is granted under this Act, the licensee shall be obligated to provide periodic reports detailing the extent of commercialization undertaken, as provided herein. Any transfer or assignment made in contravention of these provisions may be deemed invalid by the Controller after due inquiry.

Where an objection is taken against the acceptance of an application for patent on the ground that the claimed invention lacks novelty or involves an inventive step, the applicant shall be afforded an opportunity to argue the merits of the case and present evidence rebutting said objection. Such argument may include demonstrating prior publication did not sufficiently disclose a complete ‘invention convention’ as understood under this Act. The Controller may require the applicant to amend the claims to overcome the objection, provided that such amendment does not alter the original invention disclosed. Any party aggrieved by an order of the Controller accepting or rejecting an application may appeal to the Appellate Board, subject to demonstrating prejudice arising from a misdirection of law concerning registration on the layout design register.

An applicant seeking registration of an invention convention shall furnish with the application a declaration specifying the details of any prior publication or use of the invention anywhere in the world. Such declaration must be complete and accurate, subject to penalties as provided herein for false statements. The Controller may require further clarification regarding the nature and extent of such prior disclosures. Failure to comply with these registration common regulations concerning disclosure may render the application liable for rejection under this Act. An applicant who has previously filed an identical invention convention in another jurisdiction must clearly state the date and location of that initial filing within the declaration.

Where an invention convention is claimed under this Act, the Controller shall issue a notice to the applicant requiring particulars as to the details of the prior application or applications relating to the said invention. Such notice may specify a period not exceeding sixty days within which the applicant must comply. Failure to provide the required information within the stipulated time shall be deemed abandonment of the application, subject to the provisions for revival under this Act. Further, where an infringing copy of any element disclosed in the patent specification is demonstrably utilized in subsequent applications claiming priority from the initial convention filing, the Controller may direct a review of the novelty and inventive step assessment undertaken previously. The applicant shall be afforded an opportunity to present arguments against such findings.

For the purposes of this Act, an “invention convention country” shall mean any country or territory specified in Schedule I; provided that the Central Government may, from time to time, by notification in the Official Gazette, add to, omit from, or substitute for names in Schedule I. An application made as a convention application shall be deemed to be filed on the date of its first filing in an invention convention country, subject to the provisions relating to priority dates under this Act. The term “convention application” applies only where the applicant demonstrates that an earlier corresponding application was filed within the prescribed period.

An applicant seeking registration of a patent under this Act shall furnish a declaration as to the true and full disclosure of the invention. This declaration must specify whether the application constitutes a convention application, and if so, identify the convention country where the initial filing occurred. The Controller may require further documentation substantiating the date of first filing in the identified convention country. Failure to accurately represent the status of an application as relating to an invention convention country shall render the applicant liable for penalties as provided herein. Furthermore, any alteration or misrepresentation concerning the priority claim based on a prior application in a convention country will be grounds for rejection of the patent application.

Where an invention is disclosed as being derived from an earlier application filed in an invention convention country, and it appears to the Controller that the applicant has failed to comply with the requirements regarding the priority claim under this Act, the Controller may issue a notice of objection. Such notice shall specify the particulars of the non-compliance and afford the applicant an opportunity of being heard. If, after such hearing, the Controller is satisfied that the failure constitutes a material deficiency in the application, he may reject the patent application entirely or require amendment to ensure full compliance with the provisions relating to convention applications. Any party aggrieved by an order made under this provision may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order.

An application for patent shall be deemed to include an inventive step if it involves more than the mere arrangement or combination of known elements and possesses novelty as provided herein. Where an applicant seeks protection based on a convention application, the date of priority shall be determined from the first filing date in the invention convention country. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish further particulars relating to the claimed invention, including details concerning its experimental results and technical specifications, if deemed necessary for assessment under this Act. Any request for information issued by the Controller must specify a reasonable timeframe for compliance; failure to respond within that period shall be considered as abandonment of the application. The determination of obviousness will consider existing knowledge accessible to a person skilled in the art at the time of the invention’s disclosure, irrespective of whether such knowledge was formally published or otherwise disseminated.

An invention shall be deemed non-obvious if, having regard to the state of the art as provided herein, it does not involve any element which would have been apparent to a person skilled in the art at the time of the filing date. Subject to this, an application for patent based on a convention application may be rejected if the invention was previously described in a publication or used publicly in an invention convention country prior to the priority date claimed; provided that such prior description or use does not render the invention obvious to a person skilled in the art. The Controller shall consider evidence presented by the applicant demonstrating that the aforementioned prior disclosure did not impact the novelty of the invention, and may require further documentation substantiating this claim before proceeding with examination.

Where an invention is claimed as derived from an earlier application filed in an invention convention country, and it is determined under this Act that such prior disclosure constitutes grounds for revocation of the patent, the Controller shall issue a notice to the patentee detailing the specific disclosures deemed anticipatory of the claimed invention. Failure by the patentee within sixty days of receiving said notice to demonstrate, through verifiable documentary evidence, that the disclosed information does not invalidate the patent’s novelty or inventive step, shall render them liable for penalties as prescribed under this Act. Furthermore, any party aggrieved by a patent granted based on such a convention application may petition the Controller seeking its revocation and be entitled to recover costs incurred in pursuing said action.

Where an objection is taken under this Act against a patent application claiming priority from an earlier application filed in an invention convention country, the applicant shall be afforded an opportunity to reply to such objection. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish further particulars or documentary evidence substantiating the claim of priority, and any dispute arising regarding the validity of said claim shall be determined by the Controller based on records available from the relevant intellectual property office in the convention country. Provided that, if the applicant fails to satisfy the Controller concerning the veracity of the priority claim within a period specified by the Controller, the application shall stand rejected. The decision of the Controller under this provision is subject to appeal before the Appellate Board.

Where an objection is raised under this Act concerning the patentability of an invention on the ground that it lacks novelty or involves an inventive step due to prior publication or use, the applicant shall be afforded an opportunity to demonstrate, through documentary evidence and expert testimony, that such publication or use did not occur in India, or was otherwise inconsequential. Provided that, if the objection relates to a convention application, the burden of establishing compliance with the twelve-month period from the first filing in an invention convention country rests solely upon the applicant. Furthermore, should it be demonstrated that a farmer utilized the patented process unknowingly and without commercial intent prior to the patent grant, the Controller may initiate proceedings to review the validity of the patent, subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

For the purposes of this Act, an “invention convention country” shall be deemed to include any nation which is party to an agreement or treaty providing for reciprocal arrangements concerning the recognition and enforcement of patents. An applicant making a convention application under this Act shall furnish a certified copy of the first patent application made in the invention convention country as evidence of priority date. The register respect goods relating to patented inventions shall clearly indicate whether the application originated as a convention application, and the date of such initial filing abroad. Provided that, any alteration or modification to the subject matter disclosed in the original foreign application may be scrutinized for compliance with Indian patentability standards.

Where an aggrieved party alleges infringement of patent rights granted under this Act, the remedies available shall be determined according to the principles established herein. Such aggrieved parties may seek injunctive relief preventing further acts of making, using or importing the patented invention without authorization. The Controller may, upon receiving evidence of wilful infringement, order damages to be paid by the infringer to the patentee, reflecting lost profits and reasonable royalty rates. This determination shall consider the extent of the infringing activity and its impact on the market share previously held by the patentee. Rules carry provisions for expedited hearings in cases involving urgent threats of irreparable harm arising from ongoing infringement. In matters concerning convention applications filed as an invention convention country application, the date of first filing abroad is crucial to establishing priority rights.

An invention shall be deemed non-obvious if, having regard to the state of the art as defined under this Act, it does not involve any element that would have rendered it obvious to a person skilled in the art; provided that the determination of whether an invention is obvious or not shall take into consideration technological advancements occurring after the date of filing of the patent application. Where an applicant seeks protection for an invention based on a convention application from an invention convention country, such application must adhere to all procedural requirements as prescribed herein. Furthermore, any registered design incorporated within the claimed invention shall be subject to independent examination and validation, ensuring it meets the novelty and originality criteria stipulated under the Designs Act.

A process respect patent, as used herein, means a new method for producing a substance or article, or for treating it to alter its characteristics, and includes processes carried out by fermentation or other biological means. For the purposes of determining novelty under this Act, a process shall be considered non-obvious if it does not involve an element of inventive step when compared to the prior art. The term "process" also encompasses any sequence of operations undertaken for achieving a desired result, provided that such sequence is novel and involves technical skill beyond what is readily apparent to a person skilled in the relevant field. Subject to this, a process patent shall be enforceable against those using or importing the process.

The Register shall maintain a publicly accessible record of all applications filed under this Act pertaining to processes, including biotechnological processes, and such record shall detail the claimed novelty, inventive step, and industrial applicability as asserted by the applicant. An application for a process respect patent may include claims directed to both the process itself and to compositions produced by or used in that process; however, where such composition is not novel independently of the process, it shall be considered inseparable from the process claim. The Register may require applicants to provide detailed schematics illustrating the steps involved in the claimed process, along with supporting data demonstrating its efficacy and reproducibility. Any challenge to a registered patent concerning the validity of the process shall be made within one year of publication of acceptance.

Where an infringement of a patent has occurred, the right to restrain such infringement shall vest in the registered proprietor and any person deriving title from him. Any party aggrieved by an act of patent infringement may institute suit in the competent civil court, seeking damages proportionate to the loss sustained by the plaintiff as a result of the infringement, subject to a ceiling determined by the Court considering factors including the willful nature of the infringing conduct. The Court may also award compensation for any measure of indirect loss suffered. Further, where a process respect patent is infringed, the proprietor shall be entitled to an injunction preventing further acts of infringement and requiring the infringer to account for profits derived from the use of the patented process.

Where an application for a patent relates to a process for producing a substance and that substance is used as an ingredient or intermediate in the manufacture of another substance, the determination of novelty and inventive step shall be undertaken with due consideration given to the nature of the process itself. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish particulars relating to the working of the process claimed, including details concerning any equipment utilized and the yield obtained under standard conditions. Any objection raised by a third party regarding the validity of a patent for a process respect patent shall be adjudicated according to the prescribed procedures, with emphasis on demonstrating prior use or public knowledge undermining inventive step. The applicant bears the onus of proving that the claimed process is capable of being performed by a person skilled in the art and produces the desired result consistently.

Any person who, without authorization from the patentee, uses, sells, offers to sell, distributes, or imports into India a patented invention shall be deemed to have infringed the patent and is liable for damages. Such damages shall be assessed at the discretion of the High Court, taking into account the reasonable royalty that would have been payable had the infringing party licensed the process respect patent from the patentee. Further, where infringement is proven, the court may grant an injunction restraining the infringer from continuing such acts, subject to considerations of public interest and proportionality. Repeated or willful infringements shall attract enhanced penalties, including imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years and fines up to one million rupees.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, the holder of a patent relating to an industrial process shall have the exclusive right to use, sell, and exploit said process within India. However, where such process involves a patented invention embodied in a machine or apparatus, the license to utilize the process may be granted separately from any rights pertaining to the underlying invention, provided that such separate licensing agreement explicitly defines the scope of permissible activities. Any assignment of a patent relating to an industrial process shall include all rights associated with said process, including but not limited to the right to grant licenses and sub-licenses under this Act. The Controller may, upon application by any interested party demonstrating substantial need, order compulsory licensing of a process respect patent where such refusal constitutes anti-competitive behaviour or impedes access to essential goods.

Where an application for a patent relates to a process respect patent for the manufacture of a substance and the invention claimed involves one or more steps relating to chemical reactions, the Controller may require the applicant to disclose the best method known to them for carrying out such reaction. Such disclosure shall be made in a prescribed form and shall include details regarding reagents employed, reaction conditions maintained, and yield achieved. Failure to provide this information as directed will render the application liable for rejection under this Act. The Director responsible for examining applications pertaining to chemical processes may, at his discretion, extend the time limit for compliance with such disclosure requirements by a period not exceeding three months, provided that reasons for extension are recorded in writing. Any subsequent request for further clarification shall be addressed promptly and completely.

A process respect patent shall not be granted where the claimed invention relates to a method of agriculture or horticulture. Register patents shall be permissible, however, if the applicant demonstrates that the process contributes significantly to improvements in yield, nutritional value, or disease resistance within such agricultural or horticultural practices. Further, any application for a patent claiming a process falling under this restriction must include detailed data substantiating these contributions, as verified by an accredited institution recognized under guidelines issued by the Controller. The Controller may require further testing and analysis at the applicant’s expense to confirm compliance with these requirements; provided that such tests are conducted within a reasonable timeframe stipulated by the Controller.

For the purposes of this Act, "invention" means a new and useful art, process, manufacture, or composition of matter, and includes improvements relating to an invention. An invention shall not include a mere discovery of scientific principle, nor life saving drugs that are solely based on traditional knowledge. The grant patent act may be applied for in respect of any process for producing a substance by chemical means, provided that the substance is new under this Act. Any application for a patent must disclose the matter which the invention is claimed to comprise and also show how it can be performed or used.

Application for registration of a biological entity shall be accompanied by a detailed report specifying the method of isolation and cultivation, including all relevant data pertaining to stability and genetic purity. The Controller may require submission of further documentation demonstrating reproducibility of results and absence of prior public disclosure concerning said entity. Upon satisfactory review, the grant patent act will proceed with examination as per established procedures. Any challenge to the validity of a registered biological entity must be filed within six months from the date of publication of acceptance. Further, the applicant shall provide an undertaking guaranteeing adherence to bio-safety protocols during commercial exploitation and ensuring equitable access to derived technologies, subject to conditions prescribed by regulations issued under this Act.

Where an aggrieved party alleges that a patent has been infringed, they shall institute proceedings before the relevant High Court, presenting evidence demonstrating substantial similarity between the patented invention and the alleged infringing activity. The court may grant interim injunctions restraining further acts of infringement pending final determination, provided that such restraint is demonstrably necessary to prevent irreparable harm to the patent holder. Compensation for past infringements shall be determined by the court, considering factors including lost profits, reasonable royalties, and demonstrable damage to reputation. Furthermore, where wilful infringement is established, punitive damages may be awarded up to three times the amount of compensation proven. The right to seek a grant patent act remains paramount in safeguarding innovation, subject to due process and equitable remedies for those claiming infringement.

An application for the grant of a patent shall be accompanied by an abstract of the invention and such documents as are necessary to enable a person skilled in the art to put the invention into practice. The Controller may, at any time during the examination of the application or proceedings before him, require the applicant to amend the claims or furnish further information relating to the invention. Where an objection is taken against a claim on grounds stipulated under this Act, the applicant shall be given an opportunity to argue against such objection and submit evidence in support of the claim. The grant patent act confers upon the Controller discretion to refuse the grant if he considers that the invention is not novel or does not involve sufficient inventive step. Any person aggrieved by any order passed by the Controller may appeal to the Appellate Board within a period specified herein.

The grant patent act shall apply to inventions relating to pharmaceutical compositions, provided that such composition contains a known substance applied in a novel manner. An application for a patent may be filed by any person claiming to be the inventor or assigningee of the invention; however, an applicant shall disclose the best method known to them for performing the claimed process or manufacturing the claimed product. Further, if the invention is not obvious to a person skilled in the art, considering the existing body of prior knowledge, it may proceed towards examination. The Controller General shall have power to require further clarification regarding the scope and claims of an application before proceeding under this Act.

The grant patent act relating to inventions concerning pharmaceutical compositions shall be subject to review upon challenge under this Act if it is demonstrated that the claimed invention lacks novelty, considering prior publications or publicly available substances. An appeal against such a determination may be filed within three months from the date of notification of the decision, before the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. The appellant shall bear the burden of proving, by clear and convincing evidence, that the initial finding was erroneous. Further, any party aggrieved by an order of the Tribunal concerning the validity of a patent may petition the Supreme Court on a point of law.

The Register of Patents shall maintain a record of all patents granted and related documentation, including particulars of the inventor, assignee, and claims as detailed in the patent specification. Any modification to the registered details concerning a patent, such as a change in ownership or address for correspondence, must be formally notified to the Controller and duly recorded within thirty days of the occurrence of the alteration. The Register shall be open to public inspection during normal business hours, subject to any restrictions imposed under this Act relating to trade secrets or confidential information. An application may be made to the Controller seeking rectification of entries in respect patent granted if they contain errors or omissions. Such applications must specify the nature of the error and provide supporting evidence.

Where infringement of a patent granted under this Act has occurred, the Controller may, subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board, issue an injunction restraining the defendant from further infringing the patented invention. The plaintiff shall be entitled to claim damages commensurate with the loss suffered by reason of such infringement, calculated on the basis of reasonable royalty or actual profits made by the infringer, whichever is higher. Provided that, in determining such damages, the Controller may take into account any measures taken by the patentee to prevent infringement and the extent to which the infringing activity was due to a lack of knowledge regarding the existence of the patent. The right to seek rectification of entries relating to respect patent granted shall not preclude remedies available under this Act for acts of infringement.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act relating to revocation of a patent, infringement proceedings, or counterclaim concerning a patent granted may appeal to the Appellate Intellectual Property Tribunal within sixty days from the date of such order. The Tribunal shall hear appeals expeditiously and may allow, dismiss, or modify the order appealed against. Failure to comply with the provisions regarding notice prior to initiating legal action relating to respect patent granted shall render any subsequent suit liable for dismissal. Where infringement is established, damages shall be assessed based on reasonable royalty, lost profits, and costs incurred in pursuing the remedy, subject to a statutory cap as determined by the Tribunal.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and the regulations framed thereunder, the holder of a patent granted shall have the exclusive right to exploit the invention for the term specified therein. Such exploitation may include making, using, selling, offering for sale, or importing the patented article or process. However, any person desiring to use the patented invention for purposes other than those expressly permitted by the patent holder may apply to the Controller for a license under this Act. The Controller shall consider such application and may grant a non-exclusive license on terms and conditions deemed just and equitable, provided that the applicant demonstrates compelling need and offers adequate compensation to the patentee. Assignment of rights pertaining to respect patent granted is permissible with prior written consent from the Controller, ensuring transparency regarding royalty obligations.

For the purposes of this Act, a “patent granted used” shall mean a patent that has been actively employed within India to manufacture, utilize, or commercialize the invention claimed therein. Such employment must be demonstrable and continuous for a period exceeding three years from the date of grant; provided that temporary cessation due to unforeseen circumstances, as determined by the Controller, shall not invalidate this status. An applicant seeking to assert rights relating to a patent granted used shall furnish evidence substantiating such use, including but not limited to sales records, production data, and licensing agreements, as may be required under this Act.

The Register of Patents shall maintain a record of all patents granted used within India, detailing the date of first commercial exploitation and the geographical areas where such utilization has occurred. An applicant seeking registration of a subsequent invention derived from a previously patented technology must provide evidence demonstrating that the earlier *patent granted used* has not been abandoned or revoked under this Act. The Controller may require submission of sales data and production records to verify compliance with these requirements, particularly concerning compulsory licenses issued as provided herein. Failure to disclose accurate information regarding the extent of patent utilization shall render the registration liable for cancellation. Any challenge to a registered patent must be accompanied by an affidavit attesting to the veracity of claims related to prior use.

A patent granted used in the manufacture of pharmaceuticals shall remain valid subject to compliance with stipulations regarding bioavailability. Where a post-grant opposition is filed alleging that the patented invention was anticipated by prior art, the Controller may require the patentee to submit data demonstrating bioequivalence between the patented pharmaceutical and an existing therapeutic agent. Such data must be generated according to Good Laboratory Practice guidelines as provided herein. Failure to provide satisfactory evidence within the timeframe specified shall render the patent liable for revocation under this Act. Furthermore, any compulsory license granted for the production of the patented pharmaceutical shall require payment of a royalty reflecting the reasonable net profit derived from sales, as determined by the Central Government.

Any person aggrieved by an order relating to infringement of a patent granted used may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order. The Appellate Board shall, after giving notice to all parties concerned, hear the appeal and make such orders as it deems fit, subject to just considerations and natural justice. Failure to comply with any injunction issued under this Act relating to a patent granted used shall constitute wilful disobedience and render the defaulter liable for damages, which may include compensation to the patentee for loss of profits, reasonable royalties, and costs incurred in enforcing the right. The Court may also impose a penalty not exceeding one thousand rupees for each day during which such disobedience continues.

A patent granted used for the manufacture of a pharmaceutical product shall be deemed to be infringed if, without authorization from the patent holder, an act involving the exploitation of the invention has been committed. Such acts include, but are not limited to, processes such as manufacturing, using, importing, or selling the patented product. The determination of whether an act constitutes infringement shall take into account the scope of protection conferred by the patent and any limitations imposed under this Act. In cases involving disputes regarding the interpretation of claims within a patent granted used, the Judicial Member may consider expert testimony to ascertain the technical meaning of such terms.

For the purposes of this Act, “invention” shall mean a new and useful art, process, manufacture, machine, apparatus, composition of matter, or improvement thereof, originally invented by the applicant and not previously known or publicly available. An invention shall be deemed to include any process for producing an article, substance or composite material; provided that such process is new and involves an inventive step. The term “inventive step” means a feature of an invention which does not appear obvious to a person skilled in the art. A method of agricultural practice shall not be considered an invention under this Act. To respect patent rights conferred herein, any unauthorized use or reproduction thereof constitutes infringement.

The Register of Designs shall maintain a record of all registered designs, including particulars relating to the proprietor, inventor, and the date of registration. An application for the registration of a design may be filed by any person claiming to be the owner of the design, provided that such claim is substantiated with appropriate documentation as prescribed herein. The Controller General may require the applicant to furnish further information or clarification regarding the novelty or originality of the design under this Act. Any interested party may challenge the validity of a registered design before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board, demonstrating grounds for revocation relating to lack of distinctiveness or prior use. To respect patent rights, any alteration made to a registered design post-registration shall be reported to the Register within three months.

Where an interested party alleges that another person has infringed a patent, they may institute proceedings before the relevant High Court, subject to the provisions regarding jurisdiction as provided herein. The court shall have power to grant such remedies, including injunctions restraining further acts of infringement and orders for the delivery up or destruction of infringing goods, as it deems just and equitable. Compensation for loss suffered by the patent holder due to the infringement shall be determined by the Court, taking into account factors such as the extent of the damage, the profits made by the infringer, and any measures taken to mitigate the harm. The court may also award costs to the prevailing party in the action. Any challenge to the validity of a patent may similarly be brought before the High Court, seeking a declaration that the patent is invalid or unenforceable. It is imperative that all parties respect patent rights diligently.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, an application for a patent shall contain a full description of the invention, including the manner in which it may be carried into effect, and must disclose the best method contemplated by the applicant for carrying out the invention. The invention claimed in the patent application shall be clear and distinct from the prior art as known to the public before the date of filing; otherwise, the application shall not meet the requirements for a patent. Any person seeking to respect patent rights relating to a process may apply for a patent only if that process is capable of industrial application. The applicant shall furnish such documents and particulars as are required under this Act.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and the regulations framed thereunder, the proprietor of a patent shall be entitled to grant exclusive licenses relating to the patented invention, either wholly or partially, and may assign such license to any person, firm or company. Such assignment shall require registration with the Controller and shall take effect only upon such registration. Where an invention is jointly owned, the right to grant licenses and make assignments of the patent shall be vested in all joint proprietors, acting by a majority decision; provided that dissenting proprietors may petition the Intellectual Property Appellate Board for redressal concerning the terms or conditions of any proposed license or assignment. The Controller may, upon application from any interested party, inquire into the reasonableness of royalty rates stipulated under such licenses and may issue directions accordingly to respect patent rights while ensuring equitable access.

Where an application for a patent has been refused under this Act solely on the ground that the invention lacks novelty due to prior publication, the applicant may appeal to the Appellate Board. Such appeal shall be predicated upon demonstrating that the said prior publication did not reasonably inform skilled persons in the art and therefore did not preclude respect patent protection. The Board may, after affording all parties an opportunity for hearing, substitute its decision for that of the Controller if it finds that the refusal was erroneous. Any party aggrieved by the order of the Appellate Board may further appeal to the Supreme Court on a question of law.

Application for registration of a certification trade mark shall be accompanied by a detailed specification outlining the characteristics so certified and the methods of production or description. The Registrar may, upon receiving such application and after due consideration of objections received under this Act, register a proposed certification trade mark if he is satisfied that it is distinctive in the specified goods or services. Any person claiming to respect patent rights relating to a process used in the manufacture of certified products must provide evidence demonstrating compliance with those rights during registration proceedings. The Registrar shall maintain a publicly accessible record detailing all registered certification trade marks and associated specifications, available for inspection as provided herein.

For the purposes of this Act, "biotechnological invention" means an invention involving a biological agent, including recombinant DNA, gene sequences, cell lines and genetically modified organisms, or utilizing such agents to produce or modify biochemical processes or products; provided that the mere discovery of an isolated gene or biological substance shall not be considered an invention. An application for a patent relating to a biotechnological invention shall disclose sufficient information to enable a person skilled in the art to perform the invention. The term "micro-organism" includes viruses, viroids, prions and bacteriophages. A patent act shall extend to inventions concerning any process or substance derived from biotechnology.

Registration of inventions under this Act shall require submission of a comprehensive technical disclosure detailing the novelty and non-obviousness of the claimed invention. The Controller General, upon receipt of such registration documentation, may direct an examination to ascertain compliance with prescribed standards for patentability. Further, applicants intending to secure exclusive rights relating to pharmaceutical compositions must provide evidence demonstrating efficacy data generated through clinical trials conducted in accordance with established protocols. A provisional registration shall be deemed valid for a period not exceeding twelve months, during which the applicant is obligated to file a complete application as provided herein. The patent act shall govern all aspects of this process and any deviation will render the registration voidable.

An application for a patent shall be accompanied by an abstract of the invention sufficient to indicate the subject matter and scope of the claim sought. The Controller may, at any time during the examination of the application or proceeding under this Act, require the applicant to amend the claims or provide further information relating to the invention. Such requirement shall specify the reasons for amendment or provision of additional details. Failure by the applicant to comply with such a requirement within the prescribed period may result in the rejection of the application. The patent act shall govern all aspects pertaining to the determination of novelty and inventive step, considering prior publications accessible to the public before the date of filing. Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order.

The application for a patent act shall contain a clear and concise description of the invention, specifying the matter claimed to be new and useful, and including the best method contemplated by the applicant for carrying out the invention. Such description must enable a person skilled in the art to make and use the invention without undue experimentation, provided that the disclosure is sufficient to satisfy the requirements of novelty and inventive step as defined under this Act. The Controller may require the applicant to amend the application if it does not meet these standards or if any part thereof appears to be unclear or ambiguous. Further, a patent shall not be granted for an invention which is frivolous or contrary to law, subject to compliance with prescribed procedural guidelines.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act relating to revocation of a patent, rectification of entries in the Register of Patents, or otherwise concerning enforcement of rights conferred by a patent shall have the right to appeal. Such appeal may be made to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. Failure to comply with prescribed procedures during an appeal will render it inadmissible. The Board shall hear appeals expeditiously and its decision shall be final, subject to further appeal to the High Court only on a point of law. Any party failing to abide by the orders of the Intellectual Property Appellate Board shall be liable for penalties as provided herein. A patent act shall not preclude civil remedies available under other laws.

The patent act shall provide that the assignor of a patent, or any interest therein, may, by instrument in writing and duly executed, license to any person, firm or company the right to make, use or sell the patented invention for specific territories or fields of use. Such licenses shall be deemed assignments unless expressly stated otherwise within the licensing agreement. Where an assignment or license is made without distinguishing between the whole or part of the patent, it shall be construed as an absolute assignment of the entire patent. The Controller may require proof satisfactory to him that any such assignment or license has been duly registered before recognizing its validity under this Act. Provided that a licensee may enforce the conditions of their license against the assignor and other licensees in accordance with principles of equity and good conscience, subject to limitations as provided herein.

The determination whether an invention infringes a patent shall be construed strictly against the patentee, particularly where the claims are broadly drafted and encompass a wide range of potential applications. An appeal under this Act concerning such a finding may only be entertained if it is demonstrated that the lower tribunal erred in its interpretation of the specification or failed to adequately consider prior art documentation presented by the alleged infringer. Further, any challenge to the validity of a patent based on lack of novelty shall require clear and convincing evidence establishing identical subject matter as previously disclosed; otherwise, the appeal will be dismissed summarily. The patent act shall not preclude equitable remedies where wilful infringement is proven, but such relief remains discretionary with the court.

Where an application for a patent act shall be deemed to be not fulfilling the requirements of novelty and inventive step, owing to prior publication or prior use, the Controller may, after giving notice to the applicant and affording him an opportunity of being heard, determine that such publication or use did not prejudice the rights of the applicant. An appeal lies from any order made by the Controller under this provision, and in determining whether a particular date claim shall be considered as constituting prior use, the Appellate Board shall take into account evidence demonstrating the extent and nature of exploitation of the invention at that time. The burden of proving such prejudice rests upon the party alleging it, subject to the provisions regarding presumptions relating to documentary evidence.

An application for a patent shall include particulars specifying the invention and shall be accompanied by a declaration by the applicant that he believes himself to be the true inventor. The Controller General may, upon receiving an application, require the submission of further documentation pertaining to the derivation of the inventive concept, including details regarding prior art searches conducted and any relevant technical reports generated during development. Such supplementary materials are deemed essential for facilitating a comprehensive assessment under this Act concerning the novelty and non-obviousness criteria relating to the article respect patent being sought. The applicant shall be afforded an opportunity to respond to any objections raised by the Controller General, subject to timelines prescribed in the regulations.

Where an infringement of a patent has occurred, the right to damages shall accrue to the proprietor of the article and extend to cover all losses directly attributable to the infringing activity. Such damages may include, but are not limited to, lost profits reasonably foreseeable, diminution in value of the patented article, and costs incurred in mitigating the effects of the infringement. The Controller may, upon application by the aggrieved party, issue an injunction restraining further acts of infringement, provided that it is demonstrated that irreparable harm would result without such relief. Any person found guilty of contributory infringement shall be liable to penalties as determined under this Act. Furthermore, a proprietor seeking remedies for breach of their article respect patent must demonstrate clear evidence of unauthorized use or exploitation of the invention.

An application for an article respect patent shall be accompanied by a declaration as to the true inventor or inventors. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish such further information and particulars relating to the invention, including working drawings or specimens, as he deems necessary for the purpose of examining the patentability of the invention. Where an objection is taken under this Act against the grant of a patent, the applicant shall be afforded an opportunity of being heard in person or by authorized representative. The Controller may, after giving notice to the objector and the applicant, proceed with the examination of the application. Any appeal from an order passed by the Controller shall lie to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of receipt of such order.

An application for an article respect patent shall be deemed to be lacking novelty if it discloses subject matter that has already been published in a publicly accessible manner, whether by written or oral description, by use, or otherwise. Provided that such lack of novelty shall not preclude the grant of a patent where the applicant can demonstrate, under this Act, that the disclosure was made inadvertently and without reasonable apprehension that it would anticipate the claimed invention. Furthermore, an article respect patent may be refused if the subject matter does not involve an inventive step, meaning that it is obvious to a person skilled in the art, considering the state of knowledge existing prior to the filing date. The Controller shall consider all relevant evidence presented by the applicant and any interested party concerning compliance with these requirements.

Any person who knowingly makes, uses, sells, distributes, or imports an article manufactured using a patented invention without authorization from the patent holder shall be guilty of an offence. Such offence will attract a penalty not exceeding three years imprisonment and a fine extending to one hundred thousand rupees, or both, as determined by the court. Repeated contravention of this provision may result in enhanced penalties, including forfeiture of any profits derived from the infringing activity. The Controller General is empowered to issue injunctions against parties found to be violating an article respect patent, preventing further acts of infringement and mandating remedial measures for damages incurred by the rightful owner.

An appeal against the revocation of an article respect patent shall lie to the Appellate Intellectual Property Tribunal within sixty days from the date of communication of the order of revocation. The Tribunal may, after giving notice to the appellant and the respondent, hear arguments and consider evidence not previously presented before the Controller, provided that such consideration is demonstrably relevant to a material fact not adequately addressed in the original proceedings. Any party aggrieved by an order of the Appellate Intellectual Property Tribunal may further appeal to the High Court within ninety days from the date of the Tribunal’s order; however, this right shall be subject to the condition that the appellant demonstrates substantial grounds for judicial review concerning errors of law apparent on the face of the record.

An article respect patent shall relate to an invention that is new and involves inventive step, and is capable of industrial application. For the purposes of determining novelty, a claim shall be compared with the prior publication documents irrespective of language. An established registry shall maintain records pertaining to applications for patents, including details of the applicant, inventor, claims asserted, and any objections raised under this Act. The Controller may require an amendment to a patent specification if it clarifies the invention or overcomes deficiencies identified during examination. Subject to appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board, decisions of the Controller are final.

Where an aggrieved party alleges infringement of a patent under this Act, they shall institute proceedings before the appropriate forum as provided herein. The claimant must demonstrate prima facie evidence of validity and ownership of the article respect patent being asserted. Failure to do so will result in dismissal of the claim without further hearing. In cases where contributory infringement is alleged, the party claiming such infringement bears the burden of proving knowledge and participation in the infringing act. Further, any entity collecting royalties on behalf of a patent holder shall remit fees collected as copyright society fee directly to the Controller General within three months of each financial year-end; default will attract penalties as determined by regulations framed under this Act.

For the purposes of this Act, the term “Patent Office” means the official body established under this Act to receive, examine, and process applications for patents, and shall include any branch offices or regional centers designated by the Central Government. The Patent Office is responsible for maintaining records pertaining to patent applications and granted patents, as well as providing public access to such information subject to regulations prescribed herein. Any communication required to be made under this Act with the Patent Office shall be deemed to have been duly made if addressed to the Controller or any officer authorized by him in this behalf. The Central Government may determine the procedures for appeals arising from decisions of the Patent Office.

Applications for registration of designs shall be made to the Controller in such form and manner as may be prescribed. Every application shall contain a full and clear representation of the design, either by means of drawings or photographs, accompanied by a statement defining the nature of the article in which the design is applied or proposed to be applied. The Patent Office shall maintain a register of designs, open for public inspection during office hours. Any person may inspect such register and obtain copies thereof, subject to payment of the prescribed fee. An application once filed shall not be altered without the written permission of the Controller. The Controller may require any further information or clarification deemed necessary for processing an application under this Act.

Where an applicant fails to comply with a direction issued by the Patent Office under this Act regarding the amendment or clarification of claims in a patent application, the Controller may, after giving the applicant reasonable opportunity of being heard, refuse the grant of the patent. Any person aggrieved by an order made by the Controller refusing a patent shall have the right to appeal against such order within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order. The Appellate Board may allow the appeal if it is satisfied that the refusal was not in accordance with the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder, and may direct the Patent Office to reconsider the application. Further, any costs incurred by an appellant shall be determined by the Appellate Board as just and equitable.

Applications filed under this Act shall be examined by the Patent Office in accordance with prescribed procedures. An examiner assigned to an application shall furnish a report to the Controller detailing observations regarding novelty, inventive step, and clarity of description as provided herein. The applicant shall have the opportunity to respond to any objections raised in the examiner’s report within a stipulated timeframe. Failure to submit a response may result in the rejection of the application. Where the examiner remains unconvinced by the applicant's arguments, the Controller may direct further examination or proceed with refusal. Any party aggrieved by an order of the Controller relating to the acceptance or rejection of a patent application may appeal to the Appellate Board. The Patent Office shall maintain records pertaining to all applications and granted patents in electronic form as deemed necessary.

An application for a patent shall include a specification describing the invention in sufficient detail to enable any person skilled in the art to make and use it, accompanied by claims clearly defining the scope of protection sought. The applicant must also furnish an abstract of the invention, not exceeding fifteen words, which accurately summarizes the technical subject matter disclosed. Upon receipt of an application, the Patent Office shall conduct a preliminary examination to ascertain compliance with these requirements under this Act. Failure to adhere to prescribed formalities regarding form and content may result in rejection by the Patent Office. The Controller may require amendments or clarifications if deemed necessary for proper understanding; such requests must be complied with within the timeframe specified.

Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Patent Office relating to the grant, revocation or sealing of a patent may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of that decision. Such an appeal shall only be entertained if the appellant has deposited with the Registry a sum equivalent to twenty-five percent of the prescribed fee for the appeal, and failure to do so will render the appeal void ab initio. The Patent Office is obliged to provide reasons in writing for any adverse determination; omission to comply constitutes grounds for judicial review under this Act. Further, wilful suppression of material facts during examination by the Patent Office shall attract a penalty not exceeding five thousand rupees, recoverable as arrears of land revenue.

Where a patentee desires to grant a license or assign the rights pertaining to a patent granted under this Act, such license or assignment shall be in writing and executed by the patentee or their authorized representative. The Patent Office shall maintain a register of all licenses and assignments recorded as provided herein. Any person seeking to acquire an interest in a patent through license or assignment may apply to the Patent Office for registration, furnishing details including consideration paid, territorial extent, and duration. Subject to payment of prescribed fees, the Patent Office shall record such licenses and assignments, providing notice thereof in the Official Gazette. Provided that any license granted prior to the commencement of this provision which is not registered shall be deemed invalid unless it has been subsequently registered within a period of six months from the date of its execution. The patentee shall retain ownership until full registration occurs.

The Controller of Patents, acting through the Patent Office, shall furnish to the applicant a statement of grounds of rejection under this Act. Any party aggrieved by any decision or order made by the Patent Office relating to the grant, revocation, or sealing of a patent may, within sixty days from the date of communication of such decision or order, prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board. Provided that the Appellant shall deposit with the Registry such fee as may be prescribed. The Appellate Board may, after giving notice to all parties concerned and affording them an opportunity of being heard, confirm, modify, or reverse the order appealed against. Any question of law arising for determination in connection with any appeal under this Act shall be determined by the High Court.

For the purposes of this Act, the term "registered goods" means articles or substances which have been entered in the register maintained by the Patent Office under this Act, indicating that a patent has been granted in respect thereof. The Controller shall maintain separate registers for different classes of goods as prescribed; applications for patents relating to pharmaceuticals shall be registered within a dedicated pharmaceutical register. Any alteration to the particulars of registered goods, including changes in composition or intended use, must be notified to the Patent Office and may require amendment of the relevant entry in the register. The public shall have access to inspect entries on the register respect goods during office hours as provided herein.

Applications filed under this Act relating to inventions pertaining to plant varieties or agricultural processes shall be examined by the Patent Office with particular regard to novelty and inventive step. The Registrar General Plant Varieties, acting in coordination with the Controller, shall provide technical expertise concerning compliance with provisions regarding essential derived characteristics and distinctiveness as they relate to such applications. Any objection raised under this Act concerning the eligibility of a plant variety for patent protection must be documented comprehensively within the application file maintained by the Patent Office. The applicant shall furnish all relevant data pertaining to field trials and genetic stability, subject to verification by the Registrar General Plant Varieties.

Where an application for a patent is refused by the Patent Office, the applicant may appeal to the Controller. Such appeal shall be filed within sixty days from the date of communication of the order of refusal. The appeal shall specify the grounds on which it is based and shall be accompanied by such fees as may be prescribed. The Controller shall give notice to any interested party who has raised an objection to the grant of patent, affording them an opportunity of being heard. The Controller’s decision on an appeal shall be final, subject to further appeal under this Act.

Provided that where a patent is granted and subsequently challenged in proceedings before a civil court seeking an order injunction restraining the applicant from exercising his patent rights, the Patent Office may intervene as a party to such proceedings at its discretion. The Controller may require production of documents or other evidence relevant to the determination of any question arising under this Act.

An application for a patent shall be filed with the Patent Office in the prescribed form and manner, accompanied by the requisite fee. Provided that an applicant who is not resident in India shall appoint as their authorized representative a legal practitioner person practicing in India, and furnish proof thereof to the office within thirty days of filing the initial application. The Patent Office may require further particulars or amendments to be made to the application if it appears deficient or ambiguous; such requirements shall be communicated in writing to the applicant. Failure to comply with these written directions within the stipulated period as provided herein will render the application liable for rejection, subject to an opportunity being afforded to the applicant to make a reasoned representation against such action.

For the purposes of this Act, an india patented invention includes any new and useful process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter, or any new and useful improvement thereof, which is claimed as an invention. An invention shall be deemed to be non-obvious if it does not involve such a departure from the existing knowledge as would have rendered it obvious to a person skilled in the art. Subject to the provisions relating to exceptions under this Act, a patent may be granted for an india patented invention which is novel, involves inventive step and is capable of industrial application. Provided that discoveries, scientific theories, or mathematical methods shall not be considered inventions within the meaning of this definition.

An application for registration as a registered proprietor of an india patented invention shall be accompanied by particulars specifying the priority date, if any, and the applicant’s claim to priority. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish such further information relating to the invention as he deems necessary for the purposes of examination under this Act. Where an india patented invention is jointly owned by two or more persons, the application shall be signed by all such joint owners or their authorized representatives. Subject to any directions issued by the Controller, the particulars required shall be submitted in the prescribed form and manner. Provided that where the applicant has previously filed an application relating to the same invention in a convention country, he shall disclose such prior filing under this Act.

Where an infringement of a patent has occurred, the right to seek relief lies with the patentee or their duly authorized agent. Subject to any order made under this Act, remedies for such infringement shall include injunctions restraining the infringing party from further acts of infringement and an account of profits derived from the use of the patented invention without authorization. The court may also award damages proportionate to the loss suffered by the patentee as a result of the infringement, or where appropriate, royalty rates reflecting the value of the india patented invention. Provided that in determining damages, the court shall consider any measures taken by the infringer to mitigate the harm caused. Any person aggrieved by an order made under this Act may appeal to the appellate authority within sixty days from the date of such order.

An application for grant of a patent for an india patented invention shall be made to the Controller in such form and manner as may be prescribed. The applicant shall furnish such particulars relating to the priority of invention, if any, as are required under this Act. Where the claimed invention includes matter which is not new or involves an inventive step, the application shall disclose the prior art known to the applicant at the time of filing. Upon receipt of the application, the Controller may direct that the applicant furnish a statement or explanation on any point arising out of the application. The Controller shall publish the application in such manner as he deems fit and invite representations from third parties. Any person may file an objection to the grant of patent under this Act within a period specified by the Controller.

An application for a patent, as provided herein, shall be deemed to disclose and describe the invention claimed therein clearly and completely unless it contains matter which does not contribute towards understanding of the invention. Where an applicant seeks patent protection for a process by which an article is manufactured, the specification must necessarily disclose the method of using the process for producing that article. Subject to compliance with these requirements, any person may apply for a patent relating to an india patented invention, provided that the invention relates to a product or process and is new and involves inventive step. The Controller General shall consider applications in accordance with prescribed guidelines regarding examination and grant of patents.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order. The Appellate Board shall, after giving notice to all concerned parties and affording them an opportunity of being heard, pass such orders as it deems fit, subject to the provisions herein. Failure to comply with a cease and desist order issued pursuant to this Act shall attract penalties not exceeding five lakhs rupees for each day of infringement. Further, any entity found to be knowingly importing or selling goods manufactured using a patented invention without authorization shall be liable for damages equivalent to three times the value of the infringing goods. The definition of india patented invention extends to processes as well as products.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any licensee granted under a patent may assign such license, either wholly or partially, to any person, provided that such assignment is made by instrument in writing and registered with the Controller. The assignee shall be subject to all the terms and conditions applicable to the original license agreement as recorded in the Register of Patents. Where an india patented invention has been assigned under this Act, notice of such assignment shall be given to the Controller within thirty days of the date of execution of the instrument effecting the assignment. Failure to provide such notice may render the assignor liable for a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees. The Controller may, upon application by any interested party, inquire into the terms and conditions of any license or assignment and determine whether they are prejudicial to public interest.
