Such response shall include particulars of any circumstances demonstrating that the layout design in question was created independently or derived from publicly available sources. Further, if the Registrar determines that the infringing activity involves the unauthorized transmission operation law relating to a layout design previously registered, they shall issue an interim order restraining such activity pending final determination. The applicant for registration may petition the Intellectual Property Disputes Tribunal against any decision of the Registrar concerning this matter within thirty days from the date of communication of said decision. Any appeal under this Act shall be made only on grounds of law and not otherwise.

Any person who, without authorization from the registered proprietor, commercially exploits a layout design by performing any transmission operation law relating thereto, shall be liable for damages. Such damages shall be determined based on the reasonable royalty that would have been payable had the use been authorized under this Act, subject to adjustments considering the extent of commercial exploitation and the resulting loss suffered by the proprietor. Further, where such unauthorized exploitation is proven to involve the reproduction of a substantial portion of the layout design, the infringing party may also be ordered to deliver up all infringing copies or materials for destruction. The Central Government may, through notification, prescribe guidelines for assessing damages in cases involving transmission operation law violations.

For the purpose of this Act, an “authorized user” means a person who has been granted a license to utilize a registered layout-design under the terms specified in the license agreement. The term "license agreement" shall include any contractual arrangement granting such rights, subject to conditions as provided herein. An established registry shall maintain a publicly accessible register of all licenses pertaining to registered layout-designs, including details of the licensor, licensee, and the scope of permitted use. This register shall be updated periodically, not less than once every six months, to reflect any modifications or terminations of existing license agreements. Access to this information is subject to applicable privacy regulations.

An application for registration of a layout-design shall include a representation of the integrated circuit in a form specified by the regulations. The Controller General may require the applicant to furnish further particulars concerning the layout-design, including details regarding its functionality and intended use. Upon receipt of an application, the established registry shall conduct a preliminary examination to ascertain compliance with the requirements under this Act. If the Controller General is satisfied that the layout-design is original and not contrary to public interest, he may proceed with registration. The applicant shall be notified of any objections received during the search period, provided that such objections must be substantiated by evidence demonstrating prior publication or similarity to an existing registered design.

Where a registered proprietor alleges that any person has contravened an exclusive right conferred under this Act, they may present a complaint to the Controller. The Controller shall afford the alleged infringer an opportunity of being heard and shall record his findings on all material questions of fact and law arising in the proceeding. Subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal, the Controller’s order shall be binding. Any registered layout-design shall be deemed infringed if a person has reproduced the layout-design for any purpose without authorization by the registered proprietor; provided that such reproduction does not amount to an act of infringement where it is substantially similar but differs in minor details. An established registry shall maintain records pertaining to all complaints received and orders passed, accessible upon request as determined under this Act.

Applications for registration of integrated circuit layout designs shall be made to the established registry in the prescribed form and accompanied by the requisite fee. The applicant shall furnish a true copy of the layout design as an electronic file conforming to standards specified by the Controller General. Upon receipt of an application, the established registry shall verify that it complies with all requirements under this Act and the regulations framed thereunder. If any deficiency is found, notice thereof shall be given to the applicant who shall have opportunity to rectify such deficiencies within a period not exceeding thirty days from the date of notification. The established registry may request further information or clarification from the applicant as deemed necessary for assessment. Any person aggrieved by an order passed by the established registry relating to registration may appeal to the designated appellate authority within sixty days of receipt of that order.

An application for registration of a layout-design shall accompany an affidavit verifying the originality of the design and confirming that no prior publication or unauthorized disclosure thereof has occurred. The Controller General may require such further documentation as is deemed necessary to ascertain compliance with these provisions, including detailed schematics and manufacturing processes. Upon receipt of an application, the established registry shall conduct a preliminary examination to determine if it meets the formal requirements under this Act. If any deficiency is identified, notice shall be served upon the applicant allowing for rectification within sixty days. Failure to rectify such deficiencies within the prescribed period will result in rejection of the application as provided herein.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act relating to rectification of a registered layout-design or refusal of registration may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. Such appeal shall be made within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order and shall be in such form as may be prescribed. Failure to comply with the provisions regarding timelines for filing appeals will render the appeal inadmissible, subject to any relaxation granted by the Tribunal due to sufficient cause shown. The established registry shall maintain a record of all rectification proceedings and appeals filed, accessible for inspection by authorized officers only. Any wilful suppression of material facts during registration or rectification proceedings shall be deemed an offence punishable with imprisonment and fine as provided herein.

Where a registered layout design owner desires to grant a license conferring any right or rights therein, such license agreement shall be recorded with the established registry. The application for recording shall include particulars of the licensor, licensee, and the scope of the licensed rights, clearly defining whether the license is exclusive or non-exclusive, and the duration thereof. Subject to compliance with regulations prescribed by the Central Government, any assignment of a registered layout design, or any interest therein, may also be recorded in like manner. Provided that no such recording shall prejudice any prior existing right or claim against the layout design owner. The established registry shall maintain a record of all licenses and assignments so recorded, accessible for public inspection as provided herein, upon payment of prescribed fees.

Where an application for registration is rejected under this Act, the applicant may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order of rejection. Such appeal shall only be entertained if the appellant deposits with the Tribunal such fee as may be prescribed. The Tribunal shall give notice to the Registrar and any other interested party, affording them an opportunity of being heard. The decision of the Tribunal shall be final, subject to further appeal under the relevant provisions concerning appeals from tribunals. It is provided that the established registry shall maintain a record of all appeals filed and their corresponding outcomes, accessible for public inspection as may be directed by the Central Government.

An established registry shall maintain a publicly accessible register detailing all registered semiconductor integrated circuit layout designs, including particulars of the applicant, the date of application, and any modifications to the design subsequently recorded. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the established registry relating to registration or rejection of a layout-design may appeal to the authority appellate board constituted under this Act. The appellate board shall have the power to entertain appeals arising from orders passed by the established registry concerning validity of registered designs, and its determination shall be final subject to provisions for judicial review as provided herein. Further, the established registry shall publish quarterly updates detailing applications received and registrations granted, ensuring transparency in the process.

An advertisement application registration shall be deemed to include the formal request submitted to the Controller for the purpose of securing protection under this Act for a layout-design. Such an application must contain particulars as specified herein, including but not limited to a representation of the integrated circuit and its designation. The applicant shall provide a statement affirming the originality of the layout-design and attesting that it does not infringe upon any prior rights. An advertisement application registration may be rejected if it fails to comply with these requirements or contains information deemed misleading as provided herein.

An advertisement application registration shall be deemed invalid if it contains any representation which is false or misleading concerning the layout design’s originality or its conformity with applicable technical standards. Any person aggrieved by a registered layout design may, subject to conditions as provided herein, file an objection within ninety days from the date of publication of the advertisement application in the Official Gazette. The Registrar shall serve notice on the applicant and the objector, affording them opportunities for argument and submission of evidence. Further, the applicant may submit counter-evidence within thirty days after service of the notice. If the layout design incorporates elements already registered under this Act, the registration may be revoked upon a finding of substantial similarity.

An advertisement application registration shall be deemed invalid if it is found, upon investigation under this Act, that the layout-design was copied from an existing work without due authorization. Any person aggrieved by a decision relating to the validity of such registration may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. The appellant shall be entitled to relief only if they demonstrate substantial prejudice arising directly from the erroneous determination. Furthermore, where infringement of layout-design rights is established following an advertisement application registration, the owner shall be empowered to seek injunctive relief and claim damages proportionate to the loss suffered, subject to limitations as provided herein regarding contributory infringement. The Registrar may require production of relevant documentation substantiating originality at any stage during proceedings.

An advertisement application registration shall be deemed invalid if it contains any representation which is false or misleading concerning the layout-design’s originality or its conformity with existing prior art. The applicant shall furnish such documentary evidence as the Controller may require to substantiate claims made in the advertisement application, including details of design generation processes and comparative analyses against publicly available designs. Failure to provide requested documentation within the stipulated timeframe prescribed herein will result in suspension of processing until compliance is achieved. Any interested party may file a counter-statement with the Registrar objecting to the registration, provided that such objection is filed within four months from the date of publication of the advertisement application. The Registrar shall serve a copy of the counter-statement on the applicant and afford them an opportunity for reply as provided herein.

An advertisement application registration shall be deemed invalid if the layout-design incorporated therein does not demonstrably exhibit originality, subject to the provisions regarding minor variations. The applicant shall furnish a detailed technical description accompanying the advertisement application, outlining the functionality and intended use of the integrated circuit layout-design. Further, the Registrar may require submission of additional documentation substantiating the claim of novelty, provided that such request is made within sixty days of receipt of the initial advertisement application. Any alteration to the layout-design subsequent to its initial advertisement shall necessitate a fresh advertisement application registration, as provided herein. The applicant must also declare compliance with all relevant export control regulations pertaining to the integrated circuit design.

Any applicant seeking advertisement application registration under this Act shall furnish a declaration verifying the originality of the layout-design and confirming that it does not infringe upon any existing right. Failure to provide such a declaration, or providing a false one, renders the applicant liable for penalties as provided herein, including fines up to five hundred thousand rupees and potential imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years. The Registrar may, subject to due process, reject an advertisement application registration if it contains information deemed misleading or inaccurate. Any party aggrieved by a decision regarding advertisement application registration may appeal to the relevant appellate authority within sixty days of receiving notification of such decision, provided that the prescribed fee is paid.

An advertisement application registration relating to a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design may be assigned by the applicant subject to the provisions herein. Such assignment shall require execution of a written instrument specifying the assignor and assignee, and detailing the specific rights being transferred, whether exclusive or non-exclusive. The Registrar may request further documentation substantiating the legal capacity of both parties involved in any such assignment. Where an application has been assigned, the assignee shall be deemed to possess all the rights and privileges which the applicant possessed prior to the assignment. Any subsequent assignments must also adhere to these requirements, ensuring a clear chain of title is maintained within the register. The Registrar may refuse registration of an assignment if it appears incomplete or otherwise not in compliance with this Act.

Any person aggrieved by a decision regarding the acceptance or rejection of an advertisement application registration for a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of communication of such decision. Provided that, where an objection is raised under this Act concerning prior publication or use, the appellant shall demonstrate reasonable grounds to believe that the alleged prior disclosure does not constitute substantial similarity to the layout-design claimed in the advertisement application registration. The Tribunal may, subject to just cause shown, entertain appeals filed after the expiry of the said period of sixty days. Further, any order made by the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal under this Act shall be final and binding, but is open to challenge before the Supreme Court on a point of law.

An advertisement application registration shall be deemed abandoned if the applicant fails to respond substantively to any communication from the Controller within ninety days of the date such communication is dispatched. Provided that, where a response is tendered but remains incomplete or deficient, the Controller may issue further notices requesting clarification or additional information, and the period for compliance with said subsequent notices shall not extend beyond sixty days from their respective dispatch dates. Any offer made in response to an advertisement relating to registration, which is unequivocally accepted by the applicant within thirty days of the date of such acceptance being advertised, shall be considered as a binding agreement between the parties; however, this advertised acceptance relates only to matters directly pertaining to the application’s processing and does not create any rights beyond those explicitly granted under this Act.

For the purposes of this Act, “transmissible use layout” means a layout-design in respect of which the right to make, sell, import or offer for sale integrated circuits incorporating that layout-design has been transferred by contract or otherwise, and where such transfer includes the right to grant further licences or assignments relating to the layout-design. A transmissible use layout shall be deemed to include any modification made to the original layout-design with the consent of the initial owner, provided that such modification does not alter the essential character thereof as defined under this Act. The scope of a transmissible use layout is subject to the terms and conditions stipulated in the transfer agreement.

An applicant seeking registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall, in the prescribed form, furnish particulars relating to the transmissible use layout embodied in the design. Such particulars must include a detailed description of the intended modes of reproduction, adaptation, and exploitation permissible under the terms of transfer. The Registrar may require further clarification or documentation demonstrating the scope and limitations of any such transmissible use layout, particularly concerning rights granted to third parties. Provided that the applicant affirms that the proposed transmissible use does not infringe upon existing registered layout-designs, the application shall proceed for examination as provided herein. Any alteration to a previously declared transmissible use layout requires notification to the Registrar and may necessitate further assessment.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, where any person makes an infringing copy of a registered integrated circuit layout design or engages in conduct relating to a transmissible use layout without authorisation from the registered proprietor, the registered proprietor shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief. Such injunction may restrain the infringing party from further acts of copying or exploitation and may require them to destroy all infringing materials within their control. Furthermore, the registered proprietor is empowered to claim damages equivalent to the reasonable royalty that would have been payable had a license for the transmissible use layout been granted, or in default thereof, an amount equal to the profits made by the infringer, whichever is greater. The Court may also award costs and such other relief as it deems just and equitable under this Act.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, a transmissible use layout shall be deemed to exist where an individual or entity is granted permission, either express or implied, to reproduce, adapt, or commercially exploit a registered integrated circuit layout-design. Such permission must be documented in writing and specify the scope, duration, and geographical limitations of the permitted activities. The Registrar may, upon receiving a complaint from any aggrieved party alleging unauthorized transmissible use, initiate an inquiry and issue notices to all relevant stakeholders, including the registrant and the alleged user. Any determination made by the Registrar regarding infringement of a transmissible use layout shall be subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Tribunal. Further, the applicant seeking registration may specify within their application limitations on any subsequent transmissible uses granted under this Act.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, a transmissible use layout shall be deemed to exist where an individual or entity obtains possession of a mask work and subsequently employs it in the manufacture of semiconductor integrated circuits. Such employment is permissible only if the transferor has explicitly granted permission for that specific purpose, documented in writing and accompanied by a detailed specification outlining the permitted scope of production quantities and circuit complexity. Further, any subsequent distribution or commercialization of integrated circuits manufactured under this transmissible use layout requires prior written consent from the original layout-design owner, detailing the intended market segment and geographical limitations. Failure to adhere to these conditions constitutes an infringement as provided herein, rendering the user liable for damages and injunctive relief.

Any individual, firm, company, or other body corporate who, without authorization from the registered owner, engages in the manufacture, reproduction, importation, sale, offer for sale, or distribution of any integrated circuit layout-design incorporating a transmissible use layout shall be deemed to have committed an infringement under this Act. Such infringement carries a penalty not exceeding three years imprisonment and a fine which may extend to ten lakhs of rupees, or both. Where the infringing activity is continued after conviction, a further fine not less than fifty thousand rupees for every day during which such continuation occurs, as provided herein, shall be imposed. The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, prescribe guidelines regarding assessment of damages incurred due to infringement.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any owner of an integrated circuit layout design may grant a transmissible use layout license conferring upon the licensee the right to perform acts which would otherwise constitute infringement of the layout-design. Such licenses shall be assignable in accordance with the principles of general law and may be granted for a term not exceeding five years, renewable by agreement between the licensor and licensee. Provided that where a transmissible use layout license is granted relating to a layout-design incorporated within a larger integrated circuit, the scope of such license shall be clearly defined, specifying the permitted acts and any restrictions on their performance. The owner granting such a license shall provide a written record detailing the terms and conditions thereof, accessible for inspection under this Act upon reasonable notice.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, nothing shall preclude an aggrieved party from initiating proceedings alleging unauthorized transmissible use of a layout design where such use demonstrably incorporates elements substantially similar to those protected by a registered layout. The determination of substantial similarity shall be undertaken considering the overall impression created upon the informed user and not merely isolated features. An appeal against any order made under this Act concerning infringement, including claims relating to transmissible use layouts, may be filed before the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of such order; provided that the Appellant must demonstrate a prima facie case of error apparent on the face of the record. The Tribunal shall afford both parties an opportunity for argument and submission of evidence.

An applicant seeking registration of a layout design shall furnish with the application, a detailed technical description elucidating the functionality and intended purpose of the integrated circuit. The Registrar may require further clarification or supplementary documentation deemed necessary for assessment under this Act. Where an application incorporates elements previously disclosed in publicly accessible publications, the applicant must provide evidence demonstrating substantial originality and inventive step beyond such prior disclosures. The layout design government shall be considered to have been infringed if any person without authorisation reproduces the registered layout-design for commercial purposes. Any alteration or adaptation of a registered layout design which substantially replicates its essential features constitutes infringement as provided herein.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, where any person infringes a registered layout design, the owner of the layout design shall be entitled to seek relief in respect of damages sustained by him as a consequence of the infringement. Such damages may include loss of profits, reasonable royalties which the infringer would have been willing to pay had he known of the existence of the right of the layout-design owner, and costs incurred in protecting the layout design government right. The Central Government may, acting reasonably and upon due consideration of all relevant factors, issue directions regarding the assessment of damages in cases of infringement. Provided that any action for damages shall be brought within three years from the date of first ascertained infringement; however, this limitation shall not preclude actions seeking injunctions or other equitable remedies as provided herein.

An application for registration of a layout design shall be accompanied by a prescribed fee, payable to the Controller. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish further particulars or submit revisions to the layout design drawings as deemed necessary to ensure clarity and compliance with the provisions herein. Where an objection is raised against a layout design under this Act, the applicant shall have the opportunity to file a written response within sixty days of the date of receipt of the notice of objection. The Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, establish guidelines for the assessment of originality in layout designs and specify criteria for determining whether a layout design is substantially similar to an earlier layout design. Any person aggrieved by any decision or order made by the Controller relating to the registration of a layout design as a protected layout design government property may appeal to the Intellectual Property Tribunal within sixty days from the date of communication of such decision or order.

Any person who, without authorization from the registered owner of a layout design, commercially exploits or imports for commercial purposes any infringing copy of that layout design shall be liable to pay damages equivalent to five times the cost of the infringing layout-design or the retail price thereof, whichever is higher. The Government may, upon receiving a complaint regarding such infringement, institute legal proceedings against the offending party in accordance with procedures as provided herein. Further, where an infringer fails to comply with an order issued under this Act directing them to cease commercial exploitation, they shall be subject to daily penalties not exceeding ten thousand rupees until compliance is achieved. The layout design government retains the right to pursue criminal prosecution for repeat offenders.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any licensee granted under a license agreement relating to a registered layout design may, with prior written consent from the owner of the layout design, assign or pledge such license, either in whole or in part, to any other person or entity. Such assignment shall be recorded with the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trademarks, and shall become effective upon registration thereof. The owner of the registered layout design shall retain the right to approve or deny any proposed assignment, provided that denial is not arbitrary or discriminatory. Further, where a license agreement contains restrictions on assignment, such restrictions shall remain binding unless expressly waived by the layout design government in writing. Any unauthorized assignment shall be deemed void and subject to penalties as may be prescribed under this Act.

An application for registration of a layout design shall be filed with the Controller in the prescribed form, accompanied by the requisite fee. The applicant shall furnish proof of ownership or right to apply, as determined satisfactory by the Controller. Where an objection is raised against the validity of a layout design under this Act, the concerned legal practitioner person representing the objector may submit written arguments and supporting documentation within sixty days from the date of receipt of notice of the objection. The Controller shall afford the applicant an opportunity for rebuttal and may conduct hearings as deemed necessary to ascertain the facts relevant to the objection. Any decision made by the Controller regarding the registration or rejection of a layout design government shall be communicated in writing to all parties involved, including the applicant and any objector. Appeals against such decisions lie with the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal.

For the purposes of this Act, "layout design providing" means the three-dimensional representation of an integrated circuit on a mask; it includes both the spatial arrangement and interconnections of elements comprising that layout. Such representation shall be considered as providing when it is fixed in a form perceptible by a person using ordinary skill in the art and capable of being reproduced or used to manufacture semiconductor chips. A layout design providing, irrespective of its complexity or sophistication, qualifies for protection under this Act if it embodies original features and is not merely dictated by technical function or processes; provided that such features are not themselves protected elsewhere under any other law.

An applicant seeking registration of a layout design shall furnish with the application, a detailed technical description outlining the functionality and intended purpose of the integrated circuit. The Registrar may require further clarification or supplementary documentation deemed necessary for assessing novelty and originality under this Act. Where an applicant has previously published the layout design prior to filing the application, such publication shall not preclude registration provided that the applicant demonstrates due diligence in safeguarding confidentiality before the disclosure. Any subsequent modification to a registered layout design which substantially alters its characteristics may necessitate a fresh application for registration as a new layout design. The right of layout design providing is conferred upon the registered proprietor for the duration specified herein.

Where a person, without authorisation from the registered proprietor, makes, for commercial purposes, an integrated circuit embodying a layout design that infringes any right conferred under this Act, the registered proprietor shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief restraining such infringing activity. Such injunction may extend to all acts relating to the manufacture, importation, distribution, sale or hire of the infringing integrated circuit. Furthermore, the registered proprietor is empowered to claim damages equivalent to the reasonable royalty that would have been payable had the infringer obtained a license for the layout design providing, or in default thereof, an amount equal to the profits made by the infringer as a result of such infringement. The Court may also order the delivery up to the registered proprietor of all infringing integrated circuits and materials used in their manufacture.

An aggrieved party seeking redress for infringement of a layout design shall file an interlocutory application with the Commercial Court having jurisdiction over the place where the alleged infringement occurred, detailing the nature and extent of the infringing activity. The application must be accompanied by an affidavit verifying the facts asserted therein and supported by documentary evidence demonstrating reasonable grounds to believe that the respondent is engaged in unauthorized reproduction or exploitation of the registered layout design providing. Subject to the provisions regarding interim orders under this Act, the Court may grant such temporary relief, including injunctions restraining further acts of infringement, as it deems just and equitable pending final determination of the matter. The applicant shall be responsible for maintaining the status quo until a substantive order is passed by the Court. Failure to comply with these procedural requirements may result in dismissal of the application without further notice.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, an authorisation for layout design providing shall be granted only if the applicant demonstrates exclusive right over the integrated circuit layout design in question. Such demonstration requires submission of detailed schematics conforming to the prescribed standards and a declaration affirming that the layout design does not incorporate any unregistered third-party intellectual property without express consent. The Controller may require further verification, including expert assessment, to ascertain originality and non-infringement. An applicant seeking authorisation for layout design providing shall also disclose all prior art relevant to the claimed invention, failing which the application is liable to be rejected. Furthermore, continued validity of the authorisation remains contingent upon periodic compliance audits as determined by the Controller.

Any person who, without authorization from the registered proprietor, makes, uses, imports, offers to sell or distributes any layout design which infringes the registered layout design shall be liable for damages. Such damages shall be determined by the adjudicating officer appointed under this Act and may include compensation not exceeding three times the actual losses suffered by the proprietor as a consequence of such infringement. Further, where an infringing act is committed with the intention to deceive or cause confusion in the market regarding the origin or ownership of the layout design providing, the adjudicating officer shall have the power to award punitive damages. The registered proprietor may also seek an injunction restraining further acts of infringement as provided herein.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, an owner of a registered layout design may grant a license conferring the right to exploit the layout design for any purpose, including but not limited to manufacture of semiconductor integrated circuits. Such license shall be in writing and may specify the territory within which the licensee is authorised to exercise the granted rights, as well as the duration of the license. The owner retains full ownership of the layout design providing and may assign such licenses or grant further sub-licenses subject to any conditions stipulated therein. Any assignment or sub-license must be registered with the Controller under this Act and shall not be effective until registration is complete. Failure to register an assignment will render it voidable at the option of the assignee. The owner is responsible for ensuring compliance by licensees with all applicable provisions as provided herein.

Where, upon review of an appeal under this Act, the Intellectual Property Tribunal finds that a claimant has demonstrated substantial similarity between a challenged layout design and a prior unregistered work, it shall direct the respondent to provide evidence demonstrating independent creation or permissible derivation. The Tribunal may further order an expert assessment to ascertain whether the alleged infringing features are dictated solely by technical function or represent original artistic expression within the layout design providing protection as provided herein. Subject to due process, if the respondent fails to satisfy the Tribunal that such similarity arises from functional necessity, the Tribunal shall grant interim relief pending final determination of the appeal and may award damages commensurate with lost profits attributable to the infringing use.

Where, upon review of an appeal under this Act, the Intellectual Property Tribunal finds that the alleged infringement of a layout design providing constitutes fair dealing for the purpose of research or study, it shall record its reasons for so finding. Such reasons must specifically address whether the reproduction, adaptation, or distribution of the layout-design was undertaken without any commercial advantage and solely for non-commercial purposes. The appellant may challenge this determination before the High Court within ninety days from the date of the Tribunal’s order, subject to provisions regarding costs as determined by the court. Further, the Tribunal shall provide a reasoned explanation if it upholds the respondent's claim that the challenged act falls outside the scope of permissible fair dealing.

Where an applicant submits documentation demonstrating diligent and continuous use of a layout-design in commerce prior to any public disclosure, and such use indicates a reasonable expectation of widespread adoption within the relevant industry sector, the Controller may, subject to due process, grant impliedly registration of that layout-design. This determination shall consider evidence of marketing materials, sales figures, and licensing agreements pertaining to the design. The applicant shall be deemed to have constructively registered the layout-design for a period not exceeding five years from the date of initial commercial use as determined by the Controller. Any challenge to this impliedly registration may be brought before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within ninety days of publication in the Official Gazette, provided that the challenger demonstrates demonstrable prejudice resulting from the grant.

Where an individual possesses exclusive control over the manufacture, import, or sale of integrated circuits incorporating a layout-design and demonstrates through substantial evidence that such control has been exercised consistently for a period exceeding three years, the Central Government may, upon application by such individual, grant impliedly registration of the layout-design. This determination shall be made without formal registration proceedings if it is established that the individual’s actions reasonably led others to believe the design was protected under this Act. Any party infringing upon rights arising from an impliedly registered layout-design shall be liable for damages as provided herein, calculated based on lost profits or unjust enrichment, whichever is greater. The Central Government may issue guidelines regarding the evidentiary standards required to establish exclusive control and reasonable belief, subject to judicial review.

Where an application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design is pending before the Registrar and no formal objection has been raised under this Act by any interested party within the prescribed period, the Registrar shall be deemed to have acknowledged receipt of the application and its initial assessment. Such acknowledgement does not constitute impliedly registration; it merely indicates that the application is undergoing standard procedural review. The applicant shall receive a digitally signed acknowledgment confirming this status. Further processing will proceed subject to compliance with all applicable regulations regarding layout-design protection, including those pertaining to originality and freedom from prior publication. Any subsequent communication from the Registrar concerning deficiencies or required clarifications shall be binding on the applicant, provided that the applicant has an opportunity to respond in writing within a stipulated timeframe as determined by the Registrar.

Where an applicant submits documentation demonstrating reasonable efforts toward securing formal registration under this Act but faces demonstrable impediments arising from circumstances beyond their control – including, but not limited to, protracted administrative delays exceeding twelve months following initial application submission and verifiable evidence of systemic processing errors – the Controller may, subject to due process and public notice, grant impliedly registration. Such impliedly registered layout-designs shall be afforded protection equivalent to that granted under this Act to formally registered designs, provided that the applicant continues to diligently pursue formal registration until such time as it is either achieved or definitively rejected. The controller may require periodic updates regarding progress toward formal registration and may revoke impliedly registration if compliance with these conditions ceases.

Any individual or entity utilizing a layout design in commerce without formal registration shall be deemed to have availed of impliedly registration under this Act, subject to demonstrating continuous and exclusive use consistent with established commercial practices. Such utilization constitutes an acknowledgement of potential infringement upon existing registered designs, and any subsequent reproduction, adaptation, or sale by another party will attract stringent penalties as provided herein. The adjudicating authority may impose a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand rupees for each instance of unauthorized exploitation, alongside compensatory damages reflecting lost profits and diminished market share. Repeated offenses shall result in escalating fines and potential injunctions barring further commercial application.

Where an owner of a layout-design has granted a license conferring rights to utilize the layout-design, and such license contains no express provision regarding assignment, the licensee shall be deemed to possess impliedly registration of the licensed elements for the duration and geographic scope specified in the licensing agreement. This deemed registration shall not prejudice any existing or subsequent registrations held by the owner under this Act. Provided that, where a layout-design has been assigned, the assignee’s rights relating to utilization shall supersede any prior impliedly registration granted to a licensee of the assignor. The owner may, subject to contractual obligations, revoke the license; however, such revocation shall not affect the validity of the impliedly registration for the remainder of its term unless expressly agreed upon in writing with the licensee.

Any individual or entity utilizing a layout design in commerce without formally registering it under this Act shall be deemed to have availed of impliedly registration, subject to verification by the Layout Design Registrar. Such utilization constitutes an infringement actionable at the instance of the rightful owner. Where the infringing party demonstrates demonstrable commercial gain attributable to the unregistered use, they shall be liable to pay damages equivalent to three times the value of profits earned, or rupees five hundred thousand, whichever is greater. Furthermore, repeat offenders found exploiting layout designs without registration may face prosecution and a prohibition from applying for registration under this Act for a period not exceeding two years, as determined by the Layout Design Registrar.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any person claiming title to a variety shall make an application for registration in such form as may be prescribed, specifying particulars including its name, pedigree, expression, and distinctiveness. The Authority constituted under this Act shall serve notice on the applicant requiring him to submit further information or clarification if deemed necessary. Objections to the grant of protection relating to varieties farmers rights may be filed by any interested person within a period not exceeding six months from the date of publication of the application. Such objections must state specifically the grounds upon which they are based and shall be accompanied by supporting documentation as determined by the Authority. The applicant shall have an opportunity to respond to such objections in writing, after which the Authority will consider all submissions before making its determination regarding registration. Decisions of the Authority are appealable to the Appellate Board.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any person holding a breeder’s right in a variety shall be entitled to grant non-exclusive licenses for propagation or other uses relating to farmers’ rights, provided that such licenses specify the terms and conditions governing royalty payments and duration. Assignment of breeder's rights, including all associated licensing agreements, may occur with the consent of the Controller and General Manager, who shall consider the impact on continued access for varieties farmers rights. Any licensee undertaking commercial exploitation of a protected variety under license shall be obligated to report annual production data to the relevant authority. Further, sub-licensing is permitted only with prior written authorization from the right holder, detailing the scope and geographical limitations. The Controller may, upon application by an aggrieved party demonstrating undue restriction or unfair pricing practices, review and modify licensing terms as provided herein.

The Authority established under this Act shall consist of an ex-officio President and such other members as the Central Government may deem necessary for the proper exercise of its functions. The chairperson shall be appointed by the Central Government from amongst individuals possessing substantial experience in agriculture, botany, or intellectual property law. Subject to provisions regarding qualifications, the chairperson shall preside over all meetings of the Authority and determine the agenda thereof. Decisions of the Authority shall be taken by a majority vote of the members present at any meeting, provided that the chairperson’s vote shall have a deciding influence in case of equality.

An application for registration of a plant variety shall include particulars relating to the denomination under which the variety is known, along with details regarding its distinctiveness, uniformity and stability as determined through trials conducted in accordance with guidelines issued by the Authority. The Registrar may require further information or clarification from the applicant concerning these aspects before proceeding with examination. Where an application relates to a variety derived from another variety, the applicant shall furnish evidence demonstrating that the derivation does not prejudice the rights of the breeder of the original variety. The Chairperson shall review any appeal against a decision of the Registrar refusing registration and may direct further investigation or trial if deemed necessary.

Where any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act relating to the revocation or modification of plant variety protection, or concerning infringement proceedings, appeals to the Appellate Board, the appeal shall be heard expeditiously and the Board shall provide a reasoned speaking order within ninety days from the date of receipt of the appeal. The Chairperson shall ensure that all hearings are conducted fairly and impartially, affording each party an opportunity to present their case and relevant evidence. Further, where the Appellate Board finds that infringement has occurred, it may grant such remedies as deemed appropriate, including injunctions preventing further infringing acts and orders for compensation reflecting lost profits or damages sustained by the plant variety rights holder. The Chairperson shall also oversee the implementation of any remedial measures directed by the Appellate Board.

The Authority shall establish a Grievance Redressal Sub-Committee for each agricultural zone within three months of its constitution under this Act. The composition of such Sub-Committees shall be determined by notification issued by the Authority and may include representatives from registered breeders, farmer organizations, and relevant government departments. Any aggrieved party seeking redress relating to decisions made by a Plant Variety Protection Committee shall first file a written representation with the Grievance Redressal Sub-Committee concerned. The chairperson shall oversee the functioning of all such Sub-Committees, ensuring adherence to procedural guidelines as provided herein. Decisions of the Sub-Committee shall be binding on the Authority subject to an appeal process detailed in Schedule B. The Authority may issue further directives regarding timelines and processes for filing appeals.

The Board shall, upon receiving an application for registration of a plant variety, conduct such inquiries as it deems necessary to ascertain compliance with the conditions stipulated under this Act. The Chairperson shall ensure that any technical data submitted by the applicant pertaining to distinctness, uniformity and stability is verified by independent experts appointed by the Authority. Provided that, if the Board determines that the applicant has failed to adequately demonstrate adherence to established protocols for conducting field trials, it may direct the applicant to undertake further testing at their own expense. Furthermore, the Chairperson shall cause a record of all proceedings undertaken during the examination process to be maintained and made available for public inspection subject to restrictions as provided herein.

Any person found to have knowingly made a false statement or suppressed material information in an application for registration of a plant variety shall be liable to pay a pecuniary penalty not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees, and may also face revocation of any granted protection under this Act. The Authority shall issue notices requiring compliance with orders relating to farmers’ rights, and failure to comply within the stipulated period shall attract a daily fine as determined by the chairperson. Further, where an infringement of plant variety protection is established, the chairperson shall order the infringer to pay damages equivalent to lost profits or unjust enrichment, whichever is higher. Repeated violations may result in criminal prosecution under relevant provisions.

The Authority shall grant licenses for the commercial use of Plant Varieties registered under this Act, subject to such terms and conditions as it deems fit, provided that any license granted shall clearly delineate the scope of permitted activities, including but not limited to propagation, distribution, and sale. Assignment of these licenses may occur with the prior written consent of the Authority, which shall be obtained through a formal application detailing the proposed assignee’s qualifications and intended use of the rights. The Chairperson shall review all applications for assignment and may require additional information or guarantees regarding compliance with farmers' rights provisions as provided herein. Further, any sub-licensing undertaken without express authorization from the Authority will constitute a breach of contract and render the license liable to revocation.

The authority shall, upon receiving an appeal against a decision regarding the grant or refusal of protection under this Act, afford both the appellant and the respondent a reasonable opportunity for being heard, subject to such procedural guidelines as may be formulated by the Central Government. The Chairperson may, at any stage of the appellate proceedings, direct the parties to submit further documentation or evidence relevant to the dispute. Provided that, if either party fails to comply with a direction issued under this sub-section within the time specified, the Chairperson shall have the power to proceed ex parte. Any order made by the Chairperson in disposing of an appeal may be challenged before the appellate tribunal as provided herein, but only on grounds of legal error or perversity.

The Board constituted under this Act shall maintain a register of applications for registration of plant varieties, and every application filed shall conform to Form ZM as prescribed by regulations framed hereunder. The Chairperson shall be responsible for ensuring that such registers are kept accurate and accessible to the public, subject to provisions regarding confidentiality relating to trade secrets. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Board concerning the acceptance or rejection of an application may file a petition before the Chairperson seeking review, provided that the grounds for such review are clearly articulated within the zm form petition. The Chairperson shall consider any such petition and pass appropriate orders as deemed just.

The Registering Authority shall maintain a publicly accessible register detailing all plant varieties granted protection under this Act, and such register shall include particulars relating to the breeder, the geographical location of initial cultivation, and any relevant research institutions involved in the development process. Applications for registration may be rejected if the proposed denomination is confusingly similar to an existing permitted register trade mark or another registered variety. The Chairperson shall review appeals against decisions concerning rejection under this provision within ninety days. Further, the Registering Authority shall provide a mechanism for stakeholders to submit objections to pending applications, and the Chairperson will adjudicate these objections according to procedures as provided herein.

Where any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act concerning the revocation or modification of a registration for a plant variety, or relating to compensation awarded due to infringement of breeder’s rights, appeals to the Appellate Board, the appeal shall be heard expeditiously and within six months from the date of the order. The Chairperson shall constitute a Bench of the Appellate Board to hear such appeals, ensuring representation from individuals with expertise in agricultural science and intellectual property law. Further, if the aggrieved party demonstrates demonstrable prejudice due to undue delay in the proceedings before the Appellate Board, they may petition the High Court for appropriate remedies, including claims for damages. The layout design registered in connection with a protected plant variety shall be afforded similar protection against unauthorized copying or use as provided herein.

The Biodiversity Management Board constituted under this Act shall prescribe its own procedures for conducting inquiries relating to traditional knowledge concerning plant genetic resources. The Chairperson of each Biodiversity Management Board shall prescribed chairperson by notification in the Official Gazette, and such appointment shall be made from amongst individuals possessing demonstrable experience in fields pertaining to agriculture, botany or ethnobotany. Subject to any rules made under this Act, the term of office for the prescribed chairperson shall ordinarily not exceed three years, and may be extended for a further period as determined by the State Government. Provided that a person shall not be eligible for appointment as prescribed chairperson if they are an employee of any commercial enterprise involved in biotechnology research.

Where any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act relating to the revocation or modification of plant breeder’s rights alleges that such order was made without due consideration of the impact on farmer’s privilege, they shall be entitled to appeal to the Appellate Board. The Appellate Board shall consider all relevant evidence presented and may direct the Authority to reconsider its decision. Any member of a farmers' collective demonstrably prejudiced by an infringement upon their right to save, reuse, exchange or sell farm-saved seed shall have standing to bring such an appeal. For the proper functioning of the Appellate Board, it shall prescribed chairperson who is a retired judge of a High Court and possesses demonstrable expertise in agricultural law. The Authority’s decision, as modified by the Appellate Board, shall be final.

Where an application for registration of a plant variety is received, the Board shall verify that the applicant has complied with all requirements pertaining to documentation and technical data as prescribed under this Act. Provided that, if the applicant fails to demonstrate adequate measures taken to prevent unintended presence of genetically modified organisms during propagation or multiplication, the application shall be deemed incomplete until such demonstration is provided. The Authority shall appoint a chairperson from amongst individuals possessing demonstrable experience in agricultural science or intellectual property law; the chairperson shall prescribed chairperson and shall hold office for a term as determined by the Central Government notification. Further, any appeal against an order of the Board concerning novelty criteria shall lie before the Appellate Tribunal.

Any person found to have knowingly made a false statement or representation in any application filed under this Act, or in any document submitted during proceedings before the Authority, shall be liable to pay a pecuniary penalty not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees, and may also face revocation of any granted protection. Further, where an infringement of farmers’ rights occurs due to misleading information provided by a protected plant variety holder, the Authority may order compensation payable directly to affected farmer communities as determined through assessment proceedings. The chairperson shall prescribed chairperson for the Appellate Board constituted under this Act; their qualifications and tenure shall be determined by notification issued by the Central Government.

The Board constituted under this Act for the purposes of hearing and determining appeals relating to decisions made by the Controller shall prescribe qualifications for membership. The Chairperson of such Board shall prescribed chairperson and shall be a person who is or has been a Judge of a High Court, or an eminent intellectual property lawyer with not less than fifteen years’ experience. Subject to this, the manner in which the members are selected shall be determined by regulations framed by the Central Government. Provided that at least one member shall possess demonstrable expertise in agricultural practices and plant breeding techniques as assessed under guidelines issued by the Controller.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, a court shall not grant in any suit for infringement referred to in section 65, relief beyond an injunction restraining the infringing activity and prohibiting further acts of infringement. Damages recoverable under this Act shall be assessed on the basis of reasonable costs incurred by the plaintiff as a consequence of the infringement, or where such costs cannot be ascertained, upon profits derived from the sale of the infringing plant material. The court may also order delivery up or destruction of the infringing material, provided that the defendant demonstrates good faith in their actions.
primary_entity: grant in any suit for infringement referred to in section 65

context: Where a person institutes a suit alleging infringement of plant variety rights as provided herein, the court shall be satisfied that the plaintiff has established ownership of the relevant protection certificate. The defendant may present evidence demonstrating prior use or cultivation of the alleged infringing material, subject to verification by the Plant Variety Authority. Upon finding of infringement, the court may grant in any suit for infringement referred to in section 65, a permanent or temporary injunction restraining further acts of infringement. Damages shall be assessed based on the reasonable demonstrable loss suffered by the plaintiff, taking into consideration the defendant’s profits attributable to the infringing activity. The court may also order delivery up or destruction of the infringing material, as it deems fit. Costs associated with the suit shall be determined according to established principles of equity and fairness.
primary_entity: grant in any suit for infringement referred to in section 65

context: Where infringement of plant variety rights has been established under this Act, a court shall grant in any suit for infringement referred to in section 65 such relief as it deems just and equitable. This may include an injunction restraining the infringing party from further propagation or sale of the protected variety, and compensation for losses suffered by the registered breeder. Provided that, where the infringement is deemed to be unintentional or due to a bona fide error, the court may impose a reduced penalty, subject to consideration of factors including the extent of commercial gain derived from the unauthorized activity. Further, any party found guilty of wilful infringement shall be liable for punitive damages not exceeding three times the value of the infringing material involved.
primary_entity: grant in any suit for infringement referred to in section 65

context: Where a plant variety is subject to a grant in any suit for infringement referred to in section 65, and where such infringement involves the unauthorized commercial use of propagating material derived from the protected variety, the proprietor shall be entitled to seek an assignment or license of rights pertaining to the infringing activity. Provided that, if the defendant demonstrates good faith reliance on a prior public disclosure made by the proprietor, the court may impose conditions upon any grant of relief, including but not limited to, a royalty-bearing license permitting continued production and sale for a period not exceeding three years. Further, where the infringement is attributable to an employee or agent acting within the scope of their employment, liability shall extend to the employer or principal, subject to provisions regarding contributory negligence as determined under this Act. The court may also order the infringer to provide full disclosure of distribution channels and sales records.
primary_entity: grant in any suit for infringement referred to in section 65

context: Where a person institutes a suit alleging infringement of plant variety rights as provided herein, the court shall afford due opportunity to the defendant to present its defence and counterclaims. The plaintiff is entitled to seek equitable remedies including, but not limited to, an injunction restraining further acts of alleged infringement, and may also claim damages proportionate to the loss suffered, subject to a cap determined by the presiding officer based on factors including the extent of commercial exploitation. Any order for delivery up or destruction of infringing material shall be accompanied by a reasoned justification recorded in the judgment. The defendant may appeal any grant in any suit for infringement referred to in section 65 to the appellate forum as prescribed under the relevant procedural law, within the stipulated period.
primary_entity: grant in any suit for infringement referred to in section 65

context: An applicant seeking a grant in any suit for infringement referred to in section 65 shall file an application with the Registrar detailing the nature and extent of the alleged infringement. The application must be accompanied by certified copies of the Plant Variety Registration certificate, relevant documentation establishing ownership of the breeder’s rights, and particulars of the infringing material or activity. Upon receipt of such application, the Registrar may direct the defendant to submit a written statement within thirty days specifying their response to the allegations. Failure to comply with this direction shall be deemed an admission of the charges. The Registrar is empowered to conduct preliminary inquiries as necessary to ascertain the veracity of the claims and may require further evidence from either party. Any order made by the Registrar concerning such inquiries is subject to review under appeal before a designated appellate authority, provided that the applicant registration remains valid during this process.
primary_entity: grant in any suit for infringement referred to in section 65

context: For the purposes of this Act, “international application” shall mean an application for a patentable invention filed in accordance with the Budapest Treaty on the International Recognition of Deposited Microorganisms, and where such an international application designates India, it shall be treated as if it were an application made under this Act. An applicant filing a request for grant of a patent based on an international application shall disclose all priority claims asserted in respect thereof. The Controller may require the furnishing of certified copies of documents relating to the international application and any subsequent proceedings concerning its examination or grant, provided that such requirement is reasonable and necessary for determining novelty and inventive step.

The Controller may, upon receipt of a request from an applicant who has filed a patent application in India and subsequently deposited biological material under this Act, register such deposit as part of the subject matter of the invention. Such registration shall be conclusive evidence of the date of deposition for the purposes of determining priority under this Act. An applicant seeking registration under this provision shall furnish to the Controller a certified copy of the international search report, if available, and details regarding the designated institution where the biological material is deposited. The Controller may require further information or clarification as deemed necessary before proceeding with the registration. This process is subject to compliance with the provisions of the Budapest Treaty on the International Recognition of the Deposits of Microorganisms for the Purposes of Patent Procedure, as adapted by Indian law.

Where, upon revocation of a patent under this Act, an applicant for restoration demonstrates that the decision was based solely on a misinterpretation of international treaty obligations concerning the filing date, as determined by a competent authority acting in accordance with the Budapest Treaty on the International Recognition of the Depositary Authority, the Controller may, subject to just terms and conditions, restore the patent. Such terms shall include compensation to any party who has demonstrably suffered loss due to the period of revocation. The applicant shall bear the burden of proving both the misinterpretation and the resulting demonstrable loss. Failure to provide adequate proof of such loss will preclude restoration. Further, where a patent is restored under these provisions, it shall be deemed to have continued in force as if it had never been revoked, provided that any compulsory licenses granted during the revocation period remain valid.

Applications for patents shall be filed in English or Hindi, and may also be filed in any other language as recognized by the Central Government. Where an application is filed in a language other than English or Hindi, it shall be accompanied by an authorized translation into either of those languages, certified under the seal of a person approved by the Controller. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish such further translations as he deems necessary for facilitating examination and processing of the patent application.

For applications seeking international protection under the Budapest Treaty on the International Recognition of the Deposited Sequences, the prescribed fees shall be remitted in accordance with the regulations framed by the Government from time to time. The Controller may, at any stage of the proceedings, require the applicant to furnish a declaration confirming compliance with the requirements of the Budapest Treaty and related guidelines. Failure to comply with these provisions may render the application liable for rejection as provided herein.

Where an applicant for a patent elects to utilize the provisions of the Budapest Treaty, such election shall be made in writing and filed with the Controller along with the complete specification. The application so filed must demonstrate compliance with all requirements pertaining to international applications as provided herein, including but not limited to the prescribed fees and formal specifications. Failure to adhere strictly to the procedural guidelines outlined for applicants availing of the Budapest Treaty may result in rejection of the patent application. Further, any subsequent amendment to the complete specification after the initial filing under this Act shall be subject to verification by the Controller as conforming to the international search report and written opinion, if applicable. The applicant shall provide a certified copy of the relevant international searching authority’s communication.

Any party failing to comply with the requirements for international applications filed under this Act, particularly those relating to the designation of States under the Budapest Treaty, shall be deemed to have committed a violation subject to penalties as provided herein. Such violations may include, but are not limited to, omissions in prescribed forms, incorrect translations, or failure to remit requisite fees within stipulated timelines. The Controller General shall issue notices requiring rectification of deficiencies; persistent non-compliance will result in the application being rejected and any associated filing fees forfeited to the government. Further, wilful attempts to circumvent the provisions regarding designated States under the Budapest Treaty may attract fines not exceeding five lakhs of rupees and imprisonment for a term up to three years.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any patentee may grant exclusive licences under the patent and such licence shall be irrevocable unless expressly stated otherwise in the terms of the agreement. Where a patent has been assigned or an exclusive licence granted, subsequent assignments or further grants of exclusive licences relating to the same invention shall be void, provided that the assignee or exclusive licensee provides written notice to any prospective assignees or licensees within thirty days of the initial assignment or grant. The right to assign a pending application for patent extension under this Act remains with the original applicant unless otherwise agreed upon in writing and registered with the Controller. Furthermore, an entity receiving a licence pursuant to the Budapest Treaty shall be deemed to hold such rights subject to any existing encumbrances on record.

Where an application for a patent is filed in India claiming priority from an application made outside India, and such foreign application is subject to the provisions of the Budapest Treaty on the International Registration of Industrial Designs, the Controller may require the applicant to furnish a certified copy of the said foreign application as evidence of the prior art. Failure to comply with this requirement shall not, however, automatically invalidate the Indian patent application, but the applicant remains obligated to provide the document within thirty days upon written notice from the Controller. Any party aggrieved by such a notice may appeal to the Appellate Board under this Act, demonstrating that the foreign application’s relevance is spurious or irrelevant to the inventive step claimed in the Indian application.

The Register shall maintain a record of all applications for registration under this Act, including particulars relating to international patent applications filed pursuant to the Budapest Treaty. Such applications shall be examined in accordance with the prescribed procedures, and where an invention is disclosed as being claimed in an international application, the Controller may require submission of certified copies of relevant documentation pertaining thereto. Any entity seeking to utilize or commercially exploit an invention protected by a registered patent shall provide reasonable compensation to any broadcasting organization which contributed significantly to the development or dissemination of knowledge relating to that invention; broadcast shall pay for such contributions as determined by the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. The Register shall be open to public inspection, subject to provisions safeguarding confidential information.

Where an application for a patent is filed in India claiming priority from an application filed outside India, the Controller may require the applicant to furnish a certified copy of the earlier application as evidence. Such certification shall be obtained under the procedures prescribed by the relevant national authority or, where applicable, pursuant to the Budapest Treaty on the International Recognition of the Deposits for Industrial Designs. The applicant shall provide this documentation within the time specified in the notice issued by the Controller; failure to do so may result in the application being deemed withdrawn. Any party aggrieved by a decision regarding the acceptance or rejection of such certified copies may appeal under this Act, subject to payment of the prescribed fee. Costs incurred in relation to these proceedings shall be determined by the Appellate Board and are liable costs unless the appellant demonstrates reasonable grounds for the appeal were absent.

Where an application for a patent is filed in India claiming priority from an application made outside India, and such foreign application is subject to the provisions of the Budapest Treaty, the Controller may require the applicant to furnish a certified copy of the prior application as evidence. Failure to comply with this requirement within the time specified by the Controller shall render the Indian application liable for rejection under this Act. Any person aggrieved by an order made under these regulations relating to the furnishing of documents or priority claims may appeal to the Appellate Board. The penalty for submitting a false certified copy, intended to mislead the Controller, is imprisonment and a fine as provided herein.

Where an applicant for registration of a trademark fails to comply with the requirements of notification issued under this Act regarding the submission of documentary evidence substantiating claim of use of the mark, the Controller may direct the applicant to submit such evidence within a specified period. Failure by the applicant to furnish the required documentation within that stipulated timeframe shall render the application liable for rejection. Furthermore, if any person knowingly makes a false statement or suppresses material information in connection with an application or proceeding under this Act, they shall be deemed guilty of an offence and subject to penalty thousand rupees, which may be imposed at the discretion of the Controller.

Where an application for registration of a geographical indication relates to agricultural products, foodstuffs, or other products of agriculture or manufacture, the Registrar may require the applicant to furnish evidence demonstrating that the quality, reputation, or characteristics of the goods are essentially attributable to the geographical origin indicated in the application. Such evidence shall include, but not be limited to, historical records, traditional practices, and expert testimonies establishing a direct link between the product's qualities and its place of origin. Any person found to have made a false statement in support of an application under this Act shall liable penalty which may extend to five thousand rupees for each such false statement.

Any proprietor who, without leave of the Controller, makes, collects, deals with, or disposes of any patented invention, or uses it for the purpose of production, supply, or exhibition, shall be deemed to have infringed the patent and may be subject to proceedings before the High Court. The aggrieved patentee may seek an injunction restraining such acts and further damages proportionate to the loss suffered by them as a consequence of the infringement. Where any person is found guilty of infringing a patent, they shall liable penalty not exceeding five per centum of the profits derived from the infringing activity, or in default of proving satisfactory accounts, a sum determined by the Court to be commensurate with the scale of operations. This provision applies irrespective of whether the infringement was intentional or negligent, subject to considerations of bona fide use as provided herein.

Where an examiner discovers that a patent has been granted in contravention of any provision of this Act, or any rule made thereunder, he shall forthwith report such discovery to the Controller. The Controller, upon receiving such report, may direct the Registrar to issue a notice to the patentee concerned, affording him an opportunity of being heard in the matter. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Controller under this provision may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of that decision. Failure on the part of any officer or authority to comply with directions issued by the Controller shall be deemed as contempt of the Controller and such person shall liable penalty which may extend to fifty thousand rupees for each instance of non-compliance. The Controller may, in his discretion, impose a further penalty not exceeding ten thousand rupees for every day during which the default continues.

Where an applicant for registration of a trademark utilizes a representation depicting the geographical origin of goods, subject to compliance with prescribed guidelines regarding accuracy and clarity, such depiction shall not constitute a bar to registration provided that the relevant authorities are satisfied that consumers are unlikely to be misled as to the true source or nature of those goods. Furthermore, if any proprietor of a registered trademark knowingly allows another person to use their mark in a manner which is likely to cause confusion amongst purchasers, or where such use constitutes an infringement under this Act, they shall liable penalty amounting to twice the value of the infringing goods sold, or five hundred thousand rupees, whichever is greater.
