The applicant shall provide such information regarding these prior arrangements as the Controller deems necessary for determining entitlement and preventing undue exploitation. Failure to disclose relevant licensing agreements may render the patent application liable to revocation under this Act.

Where a patent application is filed claiming priority from a foreign application, and an objection is raised by any interested party alleging that the claimed invention was anticipated or rendered obvious by prior publication occurring before the date of the said foreign application, the Controller shall provide the applicant with a reasonable opportunity to demonstrate the validity of the claim based on the priority document. Such demonstration shall be considered in light of the evidence presented and the arguments advanced by both parties. The decision of the Controller regarding novelty and inventive step, as determined under this Act, may be appealed before an appellate authority. It is provided that any appeal must specify the grounds upon which it is founded, and failure to do so will render the appeal inadmissible.

An applicant submitting a patent application relating to an invention involving a novel design shall ensure that such design is not identical or substantially similar to any design already registered under the Design Registry Registration Act. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish detailed specifications and working drawings demonstrating the novelty and inventive step of the claimed subject matter, alongside evidence confirming prior art searches conducted in accordance with prescribed guidelines. Further, a patent application shall be deemed invalid if it incorporates elements disclosed in a publicly available design registration without explicit authorization from the registered proprietor. The applicant must also provide an undertaking to disclose any conflicting prior registrations during examination proceedings as provided herein.

For the purposes of this Act, the date patent shall be deemed to be the date on which the application for a patent was first received by the Controller. Provided that where an application is filed with a priority claim under section 10, the date patent shall be the filing date of the earlier application as certified by the appropriate authority in the country where such earlier application was filed. Subject to any notification issued by the Central Government, this provision applies equally to applications for patents of addition and continuation applications. The Controller may require further documentation to verify the priority claim before establishing the date patent.

The Registering Authority shall record the date patent shall take effect from the date specified in the application for registration, provided that where a request for priority is filed under this Act, the date patent shall be deemed to be the earlier date of filing of the corresponding application in the designated country, subject to verification by the Controller. The applicant shall furnish all necessary documentation substantiating the claim of priority within the prescribed time limit as determined by regulations framed hereunder. Failure to provide such documentation may result in the rejection of the priority claim and a subsequent adjustment of the date patent. This determination is final and binding unless appealed before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board, subject to applicable timelines.

Where any person aggrieved by a decision made under this Act relating to the grant, revocation, or validity of a patent has suffered material loss or injury as a consequence thereof, such person may institute civil proceedings seeking compensation. The measure of damages shall be determined based on principles of fairness and equity, considering factors including lost profits, diminution in value, and reasonable expenses incurred in litigation. For the purposes of determining limitation periods for suits relating to infringement, the date patent shall be deemed the commencement point; however, this provision is subject to a proviso that no action may be brought under this Act concerning an alleged infringement occurring more than six years prior to the publication of notice of such suit in the Official Gazette. Further, any appeal from a decision made by the Controller regarding revocation proceedings must be filed within ninety days.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, the date patent shall be deemed to be the date on which the application for patent was first filed, both within India and outside India. Where a patent application includes claims relating to inventions disclosed in one or more earlier applications filed by the applicant or legal representative, the date patent for such invention shall be determined as of the date of filing of the earliest such application. The Controller may, upon review of documentary evidence submitted by the applicant, extend the date patent retrospectively where it is demonstrated that a substantial and unforeseen modification to the original disclosure occurred post-filing but was necessitated by regulatory requirements pertaining to public health safety. This extension shall not prejudice any rights accrued under this Act prior to such modified date patent. The record of the determined date patent shall be maintained in the prescribed manner, accessible for inspection as provided herein.

Subject to the provisions herein relating to priority claims and convention applications, the date patent shall be deemed to be the date on which the application for patent was first laid before a competent authority, whether in India or elsewhere. Provided that where an application is amended after the initial filing, such amendment shall not affect the original date patent unless the amending party demonstrates that the amendments are purely clarificatory and do not substantially alter the claimed invention. Furthermore, if an applicant has previously filed an identical application under this Act, the date patent for the subsequent application shall be determined by considering the earlier filing date, subject to a demonstration of genuine novelty and non-obviousness relative to the prior application. The Controller may require supporting documentation to verify such claims.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and any rules made thereunder, the date patent shall be deemed to be the date on which the application for patent was first laid before the relevant authority. Provided that where an application contains a claim referring back to an earlier disclosure not contained in the description, the date patent may be adjusted to reflect the publication date of such prior art, as determined by the Controller. Any party aggrieved by this adjustment shall have standing to petition the High Court for review within ninety days of notification under this Act. Failure to comply with this timeframe will preclude any subsequent challenge and render the adjusted date patent final and binding for all enforcement purposes. Penalties for attempting to circumvent this process are prescribed as a fine not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees, or imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years.

Subject to the provisions of this Act relating to inventions arising from undisclosed information, a patent shall be dated as of the date patent shall have been formally granted by the Controller General. Where the assignment of rights in a pending application for patent is registered under this Act, the date patent shall remain unchanged unless the assignee expressly elects to amend the priority claim date during the post-grant opposition period. Such election must be filed within three months of the grant and will be deemed conclusive regarding the effective date for all subsequent licensing agreements pertaining to that invention. Further, any license granted prior to registration of assignment shall continue in force as per its original terms, but the assignor retains no right to further exploit the patented invention beyond the scope defined therein. The Controller General may issue directions concerning the recording of such amendments and licenses.

Subject to the provisions of this Act relating to priority claims and convention applications, the date a patent shall be deemed to have been granted is that which appears on the sealed patent document issued by the Controller. However, where any objection has been raised under this Act against the grant of a patent, or where an appeal lies pending before the Appellate Board concerning the validity of such patent, the date patent shall remain provisional and subject to determination upon final resolution of the aforementioned objections or appeals. It is provided that any party aggrieved by a decision regarding the date patent may file an application for revision before the High Court within ninety days from the date of communication of said decision, notwithstanding any other provision under this Act relating to limitation periods.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and any rules made thereunder, a patent shall be dated as of the date on which the application for the grant of the patent was first filed, whether in India or outside India. Where such application has been filed in respect of a package comprising multiple inventions, the date patent shall pertain to the earliest priority date claimed for any element within that package. Any assignment or license granted prior to the date patent shall be deemed valid only if it explicitly acknowledges and is consistent with the invention’s scope as defined by the subsequently granted patent. Further, where a compulsory license is sought under this Act, the terms of such license, including royalty rates, may be adjusted to reflect the relative contribution of each element within the original package towards the patented technology. The Controller shall maintain a record of all assignments and licenses pertaining to patents relating to packages.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, the date patent shall be construed as the earlier of the date of filing of the application for patent or the date on which a corresponding application first came to be filed in any country outside India. Where an appeal lies before the Copyrights Appellate Board concerning the validity of a patent granted under this Act, the Board may, upon review, determine whether the claimed invention was anticipated by prior art not previously considered during the initial examination process. This determination shall be binding and conclusive, subject to further judicial review only on grounds of demonstrable procedural irregularity or error apparent on the face of the record. Any party aggrieved by such a decision may petition the Supreme Court within ninety days thereafter.

For the purposes of this Act, the “date patent shall” take effect is deemed to be the earlier of either the date on which the application for a patent was first filed in India, or the date on which the corresponding application, if any, was first filed in a convention country. Where an applicant is represented by a legal practitioner person, that representation shall not affect the determination of this date. The Controller may, subject to regulations framed under this Act, require further documentation to ascertain the precise date patent shall be assigned. This provision applies irrespective of whether the invention relates to a product or a process and without prejudice to any other provisions relating to priority claims as provided herein.

For the purposes of this Act, the “date application patent” means the calendar day upon which a formal request for examination is received by the Controller under this Act. Where an applicant has filed multiple applications relating to the same invention, the date application patent shall be determined based on the first such filing. The record of the date application patent shall be conclusive evidence regarding the priority of inventions and shall govern timelines pertaining to opposition proceedings as provided herein. Any alteration or correction to the recorded date application patent may only occur with leave of the Controller and subject to a demonstration of manifest error.

An application for a patent shall be deemed to have been filed on the day it is received by the Controller, and such date shall constitute the official date application patent for all purposes under this Act. Where an applicant has previously filed an identical or substantially similar application relating to the same invention in India, the date application patent shall be determined as the later of either the initial filing date or the date of the subsequent application received by the Controller. The Registrar may require applicants to furnish proof of prior filings made outside India; failure to comply with such a request may result in the provisional acceptance being withdrawn. It is provided that any alteration made to the patent application after the original date application patent shall not affect the validity of the patent granted, subject to review by the Controller.

For the purposes of determining priority under this Act, the date application patent is deemed to be the earlier of the date on which the application was first filed anywhere in the world, or the date on which the Indian application was formally received by the Controller. Where an applicant has previously filed an application relating to the same invention, and subsequently files a fresh application, the date application patent for the second application shall be determined based on the earlier filing date of the initial application, provided that the subsequent application claims priority from the first. The Controller may require such evidence as is necessary to establish this claim of priority. Any alteration made to an application after the date application patent will not affect its entitlement to priority unless expressly permitted by regulations framed under this Act. Further, any delay in processing due to administrative reasons shall not be taken into account when calculating periods prescribed herein relating to the date application patent.

For the purposes of determining priority under this Act, the date application patent is deemed to be the earlier of the date on which the application was first filed in India, or the date on which the corresponding application, if any, was first filed in a convention country. Provided that where an application for patent has been made within twelve months from the date of filing a corresponding application abroad, and the applicant fails to comply with the requirements of sub-section (2) of section 8, the application shall be deemed to have been filed on the later of those two dates. Subject to compliance with regulations regarding provisional applications, an applicant shall furnish such particulars as are prescribed relating to the invention claimed. The Controller may require further documentation demonstrating adherence to these stipulations before proceeding with examination.

An application for a patent shall be deemed to have been filed on the date it is received by the Controller, and such date shall constitute the ‘date application patent’ for all purposes under this Act. Any person aggrieved by a determination regarding the date application patent may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days of receiving notification of said determination. Failure to comply with this timeframe shall render the appeal inadmissible. The Controller shall be empowered to impose a penalty not exceeding one thousand rupees upon any party found to have knowingly misrepresented facts pertaining to the filing date, and such penalties shall be recoverable as arrears of land revenue. Further, wilful attempts to obstruct or mislead investigations into patent application dates will attract criminal prosecution under relevant provisions of the Indian Penal Code.

Subject to the provisions of this Act relating to priority and convention applications, any licensee under a patent granted pursuant to this Act may, with the written consent of the patentee, assign or otherwise transfer the benefit of such license to another party engaged in the manufacture, use, or sale of the patented invention within India. Provided that such assignment shall not operate to divest the original assignee of their rights unless expressly agreed upon in writing. The date application patent is deemed significant for determining the validity and enforceability of any such assignments, particularly concerning claims arising from pre-grant opposition proceedings. Further, where a license has been granted under this Act incorporating provisions regarding royalty payments, any subsequent assignment shall be subject to those same royalty stipulations unless modified by mutual agreement between the original assignee, patentee, and the new licensee. This provision applies equally to partial assignments of licenses relating to specific geographical territories.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, the determination of the date application patent is crucial for establishing priority rights and subsequent validity challenges. Where multiple applications relate to the same invention, the applicant seeking precedence shall bear the burden of demonstrating a clear and unequivocal claim to an earlier date application patent through documentary evidence acceptable to the Controller. An appeal against this finding may be made to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order; however, such appeal shall not suspend the operation of the order unless the Board is satisfied that the applicant has furnished sufficient security to protect the interests of any party likely to be affected by the decision. The Controller may require further affidavits or hearings as deemed necessary for a just resolution.

Where a patentee seeks to challenge the validity of a patent granted under this Act, the determination of the *date application patent* is paramount. The Controller may, upon receiving evidence demonstrating prior use or knowledge undermining novelty claims, direct that the patent be deemed invalid from its grant date if such prior activity predates the aforementioned filing date. Further, any party aggrieved by a decision regarding the validity assessment may appeal to the relevant appellate authority. It shall be the duty of the appellant to demonstrate, with irrefutable evidence, that the Controller erred in assessing the relevance of pre-grant disclosures. The patentee allow application for rectification only if they can prove such error prejudiced their interests and affected the scope of protection afforded.

Where an application for a patent relates to any invention already described or claimed in a prior document, the Controller may, subject to appeal under this Act, require the applicant to amend the specification so as to clearly define the scope of protection sought and distinguish it from that disclosed in the said prior document. The date application patent shall be construed strictly in accordance with the amended claims, notwithstanding any reference made within the original application to the name or names of inventors. Any party aggrieved by such a requirement may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days of communication of the order. It is provided that the Controller’s determination regarding the relevance of prior art and its impact on the date application patent shall be final, unless demonstrable prejudice arises from an error apparent on the face of the record.

For the purposes of establishing priority under this Act, the date application patent is deemed to be the date first mentioned in the records of the Patent Office. This determination applies irrespective of any subsequent amendments or additions made to the application during its examination process. Where an applicant has filed multiple applications relating to the same invention, the earliest date application patent shall prevail for determining rights and remedies. Pharmaceutical compositions are subject to these provisions; however, where a pharmaceutical product is claimed as a combination of known substances, the Controller may require further evidence demonstrating novelty and inventive step before establishing the relevant date application patent. The Registrar shall maintain a chronological record of all dates application patents filed, accessible for public inspection.

For the purposes of this Act, a “patent shall dated” means that the effective commencement of patent rights and obligations is determined by the filing date of the application. The date so established shall be recorded prominently within the register maintained under this Act, alongside relevant details pertaining to the invention’s subject matter. Where an applicant has previously filed an identical or substantially similar application in another jurisdiction, such prior filings may be considered during examination but shall not alter the patent shall dated as determined by Indian law. This determination is final and binding for all subsequent legal proceedings relating to the patent.

An application for a patent may be refused if it does not disclose or describe the invention clearly and completely enough for a person skilled in the art to put it into practice. Where a patent has been granted, the date thereof shall be deemed to be the date on which the patent was sealed by the Controller. The sealing of a patent constitutes conclusive evidence that the invention is patentable as provided herein. Any appeal against an order refusing a patent may be made within sixty days from the date of communication of the order to the applicant. Further, the Registrar shall maintain a record of all patents granted and their respective dates. Subject to any regulations framed under this Act, information pertaining to the sealing date is accessible by request to the Controller’s office. A patent shall dated as of the date on which the application for patent was filed, unless otherwise determined by the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

Any person aggrieved by a determination made under this Act relating to the validity of a patent may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such determination. The Appellate Board shall, after giving notice to all concerned parties and affording them an opportunity for being heard, make its award confirming, modifying or reversing the determination appealed against. Failure to comply with the prescribed procedures during appellate proceedings will render the appeal inadmissible. Where a patent is found to be invalid, any damages recoverable from infringement shall be reduced proportionately; furthermore, costs incurred by the aggrieved party in successfully challenging the patent’s validity may be awarded at the discretion of the Appellate Board. Every patent shall dated as of the date on which the application for patent was filed, subject to any post-grant opposition proceedings.

Subject to the provisions of this Act relating to compulsory licenses and government use, any licensee granted a license under a patent assigned pursuant to Section 139 may, with the written consent of the assignee, sub-license such rights on commercial terms. The Controller shall not grant approval for any assignment or sub-licensing agreement unless it is satisfied that the proposed sublicensee possesses the technical expertise and financial resources necessary to exploit the patented invention effectively. A patent shall dated as of the date on which the application for patent was filed, irrespective of subsequent amendments to the claims. Further, where a patent has been assigned, any action relating to infringement may be brought by either the assignee or the original patentee, subject to providing due notice to the other party. This provision applies even if the patent shall dated prior to the assignment taking effect.

An application for patent protection may include a complete specification detailing the invention; such specification is deemed to define the scope of the granted patent. A patent amendment specification refers to any modification made to this original complete specification under this Act, provided that such amendments are strictly confined to clarifying or correcting ambiguities within the initial disclosure and do not substantively alter the subject matter claimed. Any proposed patent amendment specification shall be accompanied by a statement explicitly outlining the rationale for the alteration and demonstrating its consistency with the originally filed invention as understood by a person skilled in the art.

An applicant seeking to amend a patent application after its publication may submit a request for amendment in Form X along with the prescribed fee. Such requests shall detail the specific alterations proposed to the original complete specification and drawings. The Controller shall consider any such amendment, provided that it does not substantially alter the nature of the invention claimed or extend the scope beyond what was originally disclosed. Any patent amendment specification must be accompanied by a declaration affirming its consistency with existing prior art. Further, the applicant shall furnish an undertaking guaranteeing the accuracy and completeness of all information presented in support of the requested modification. The Controller may require additional documentation to verify the proposed changes.

Where an applicant seeks to amend a patent specification after the publication of the application under this Act, such amendment shall be permissible only if it clarifies or explains matters disclosed in the original specification. The Controller may allow any such amendment provided that the amended specification still discloses the invention claimed and does not seek to introduce subject matter which was not originally present. Any party aggrieved by a decision allowing an amendment may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days of communication of the order, stating grounds for objection. Failure to comply with this appeals process shall preclude any further recourse under this Act. The Controller shall consider representations made by all interested parties before determining whether to grant or refuse permission for a patent amendment specification.

An applicant seeking to amend a patent specification after the publication of the application under this Act shall file with the Controller a request in writing setting forth the proposed amendments. Such request must clearly identify each alteration sought and provide justification for its necessity, demonstrating how it clarifies or supports the originally claimed invention. The Controller may require the applicant to submit a declaration affirming that the amended specification continues to disclose the subject matter of the original application as understood by a person skilled in the art at the priority date. Further, any patent amendment specification shall not introduce new matter which extends beyond the scope of the initial disclosure; such additions will be deemed invalid and may render the granted patent susceptible to revocation proceedings. The Controller’s decision regarding acceptance or rejection of an amendment is final, subject to appeal under procedures as provided herein.

An applicant seeking to amend a patent specification after the date of publication under this Act shall file a request in the prescribed form, accompanied by the requisite fee. Such request must clearly identify the specific portions of the original specification intended for alteration and provide a reasoned justification demonstrating how the proposed amendment maintains novelty and inventive step as provided herein. The Controller may allow such amendment only if satisfied that the changes do not substantially alter the scope of protection initially claimed and are consistent with the disclosure present in the prior art considered during examination. Further, any patent amendment specification shall be accompanied by an undertaking from the applicant confirming due diligence has been exercised to ensure compliance with all procedural requirements under this Act.

An applicant seeking to amend a patent specification after the date of publication under this Act shall file a request with the Controller specifying the nature of the proposed alteration. Such request must demonstrate that the amendment does not substantially alter the scope of protection claimed in the original application, and that the amended claims remain clear and concise. The Controller may allow or reject such request, providing reasons for the decision in writing. Any party aggrieved by the Controller’s order relating to a patent amendment specification may appeal under this Act to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. The appellate board shall consider whether the proposed amendment unfairly prejudices existing prior art disclosures and may remit the matter back to the Controller for further consideration.

An application for patent protection may include a complete specification detailing the invention; such specification is subject to amendment under this Act. A patent amendment specification shall relate only to matters disclosed in the original application and not introduce new matter or substantially alter the claimed invention. Where an applicant has previously filed a corresponding application for patent protection in another country, the amended specification must be consistent with any subsequent 73 convention application relating thereto. Any alteration made under this provision shall be clearly identified as an amendment and duly recorded within the official records of the Patent Office.

An applicant seeking to amend a patent specification after the date of publication under this Act shall file a request with the Controller in the prescribed form, accompanied by the requisite fee. Such request must clearly identify the specific portions of the specification intended for alteration and provide justification demonstrating the necessity for the amendment. The Controller may allow an amendment only if it is shown to be merely clarificatory or supplementary to the original disclosure, and does not substantially alter the scope of protection sought. Any proposed amendment affecting the claim language constitutes a modification of the patent’s claims and requires careful scrutiny. A request for amendment involving a specification shall not be granted if it introduces new matter that was not adequately described in the originally filed document. The Controller may direct an applicant to submit further information or arguments concerning any proposed specification amendment claim before rendering a decision.

An application for patent protection may include a specification detailing the invention; subject to this Act, the applicant shall have the right to seek an amendment of the said specification at any time before the grant of the patent. For the purposes of clarity, a specification amendment is defined as a modification or addition made to the original description of the invention within the application document. Such amendments are permissible only if they do not alter the nature of the claimed invention as originally disclosed and must be consistent with the disclosure contained in the complete specification initially filed. Any proposed specification amendment shall be accompanied by a reasoned justification demonstrating its compliance with these requirements.

An applicant seeking registration of a utility model may, prior to the grant of the certificate, submit a request for amendment of the specification detailing the functional characteristics and intended use of the invention. Such requests shall be accompanied by a reasoned statement justifying the proposed alterations and demonstrating their consistency with the original disclosure. The Controller General, after affording an opportunity for objection from any interested party, may allow or reject the requested amendment subject to the condition that it does not substantially alter the claimed novelty or inventive step as initially presented in the application. Any specification amendment introduced post-publication shall be deemed a material variation and require fresh examination under this Act.

An applicant seeking to amend the specification of an invention after the date of its first filing under this Act shall provide written justification demonstrating substantial new matter not previously disclosed or reasonably inferable from the original disclosure. Such amendment may only be permitted if it does not alter the nature of the claimed invention, and is demonstrably necessary for clarity or accuracy in defining the scope of protection sought. The Patent Office shall notify the applicant and any interested party of the proposed specification amendment, affording them a period of thirty days to submit objections. Any objection received shall be considered by the Controller, who may allow, reject, or modify the amendment. Failure to comply with these procedures will render the amended specification voidable at the instance of an aggrieved party seeking injunctive relief and damages.

An applicant seeking to amend a patent specification after the filing date shall submit a request in writing to the Controller, detailing the proposed modifications. Such requests must clearly identify the specific clauses or portions of the original specification affected by the amendment and provide justification for the changes sought, demonstrating their consistency with the disclosure initially presented. The Controller may require supporting documentation, including experimental data or prior art references, to assess the technical basis of the requested alteration. Any amendment shall be limited to matters of clarification, correction of typographical errors, or the addition of subject matter that does not broaden the scope of protection originally claimed; a significant specification amendment altering the inventive concept is prohibited. The Controller’s decision regarding the allowance or rejection of an amendment is final, subject to appeal under this Act.

An applicant seeking to amend a patent specification after the date of publication under this Act shall submit a request in writing to the Controller, detailing the proposed modifications. Such amendments must not alter the nature of the invention as originally disclosed; provided that minor clarifications or corrections relating to typographical errors or grammatical inaccuracies are permissible without requiring further examination. The Controller may allow an amendment if satisfied it does not substantially widen the scope of protection sought beyond the original disclosure and complies with prescribed forms. Any request for specification amendment must be accompanied by the requisite fee, as determined under this Act. Further, any such amendment shall be published for public inspection, affording third parties opportunity to object within a stipulated period.

An applicant seeking to amend a patent specification after the publication of the application under this Act shall file a request with the Controller specifying the nature of the proposed amendment. Such amendment shall be permissible only if it clarifies or explains matters already disclosed in the original specification and does not substantially alter the invention claimed therein. The Controller may allow or reject such request, providing reasons for the decision in writing. Any party aggrieved by an order rejecting a request for specification amendment may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days of receipt of that order. Failure to comply with this provision shall render the applicant liable to a penalty not exceeding one thousand rupees and further action under this Act.

Where an invention disclosed in a patent application relates to technology incorporated within a licensed field under a prior agreement, the Controller may permit a specification amendment if such amendment is deemed necessary to accurately reflect the scope of the licensee's rights. Provided that the proposed amendment does not broaden the claims beyond the originally filed disclosure and does not adversely affect any third party’s existing patent or application, the Controller shall consider the request. Any assignment of a patent, or an interest in a pending patent application, including rights arising from a specification amendment, must be executed in the prescribed form and duly registered under this Act. The assignor shall remain liable for ensuring compliance with all conditions precedent to grant, even where such conditions pertain to matters addressed by a subsequent specification amendment.

An applicant seeking to amend a patent specification after the first publication thereof shall file with the Controller a request setting forth the proposed amendments; provided that such request must demonstrate that the changes are necessitated by prior art becoming publicly available subsequent to the date of filing of the original application. The Controller may, upon review and affording an opportunity for objection from any interested party, allow or reject the amendment. Any rejection shall be accompanied by reasoned findings, which findings are subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. Further, where a proposed specification amendment introduces matter not disclosed in the original specification, it shall be deemed a new invention requiring separate filing and prosecution under this Act, notwithstanding any claim of dependency.

For the purposes of this Act, an *amendment complete specification* is defined as any modification to the detailed description of an invention contained within the complete specification originally filed or subsequently submitted under this Act. Such amendment shall only relate to clarification of the disclosure and may not alter the scope of protection sought for the invention. An amendment complete specification must be clearly identified as such, accompanied by a statement indicating the specific changes made relative to the prior version. The Controller may allow an amendment complete specification provided that it does not introduce any new matter which was not disclosed or reasonably derivable from the original disclosure and subject to compliance with prescribed procedural requirements.

Where an applicant seeks to introduce alterations to a patent application beyond those permissible under this Act, such request shall be deemed a substantive modification requiring formal consent. The Controller may permit minor clarifications or corrections within the original disclosure, provided that these adjustments do not broaden the scope of protection claimed nor contradict existing prior art. However, any proposed amendment constituting an alteration to the *amendment complete specification* itself, particularly concerning inventive step or novelty, shall be subject to a fresh examination process mirroring the initial assessment under this Act. Failure to satisfy the requirements for patentability following such re-examination will result in rejection of the application. The applicant retains the right to appeal any decision denying permission for amendment to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

Where an application for patent contains deficiencies in the disclosure relating to the matter disclosed, and such deficiency renders the specification not fulfilling the requirements of completeness under this Act, the Controller may require the applicant to furnish a further statement or drawing. Failure to comply with such requirement within the time specified shall render the application liable for rejection. Any amendment complete specification submitted pursuant to this process must be accompanied by an affidavit verifying its accuracy and conformity with the original disclosure. Knowingly submitting a false declaration in said affidavit constitutes an offence, punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and a fine. The Controller shall record any such conviction.

Where an applicant seeks to introduce alterations to a patent application beyond those permissible under this Act concerning matters of form or typographical error, such request shall be deemed a substantive amendment. The Controller may allow such alteration only if satisfied that the original disclosure, read in light of the proposed modification, would have clearly and unambiguously conveyed the invention to a person skilled in the art. Any challenge to the Controller’s decision regarding an amendment complete specification under this Act may be made through appeal before the Appellate Board, demonstrating prejudice resulting from the allowance or refusal thereof. The burden shall lie upon the appellant to establish that the alteration fundamentally alters the scope of protection sought and unfairly impacts existing rights.

An application for patent protection may include one or more claims defining the scope of the invention; such claims form an integral part of the patent. The term "claim specification" refers to the precise language used in these claims and their relationship to the detailed description provided within the complete specification. An amendment claim specification shall be permissible only if it clarifies, corrects, or explains matters already disclosed, subject to the condition that the amended claims do not broaden the scope of protection beyond what is supported by the original disclosure. Any alteration must maintain consistency between the claim specification and the accompanying written description as provided herein.

Where an applicant seeks to vary the matter disclosed in the original claim specification relating to a patent application, such variation shall only be permissible if it does not substantially alter the nature of the invention claimed. Any proposed amendment must be clearly and specifically supported by reference to the disclosure contained within the initial complete specification or prior published material as provided herein. The Controller may allow an amendment where he considers it necessary for securing proper and adequate definition of the subject matter which the applicant seeks to patent, but shall refuse such allowance if the amended claim would lack clarity or support. Further, any party aggrieved by a decision relating to an amendment claim specification may appeal under this Act to the Appellate Intellectual Property Tribunal within sixty days from the date of communication of that decision.

An applicant seeking to obtain a patent under this Act may submit an amendment claim specification relating to the invention disclosed in the complete specification previously filed. Such amendment shall not alter the nature of the invention claimed and must be consistent with the disclosure contained within the original application, subject to provisions regarding enablement. The Controller shall consider any proposed amendment claim specification only if it is made before the first examination report is issued or, where an extension of time for filing has been granted, before the expiration of that extended period. Any amendment sought after these timelines may be rejected at the discretion of the Controller. Provided that the applicant demonstrates a clear and justifiable reason for the delayed submission, the Controller may permit such amendments on payment of prescribed fees. The acceptance of any amendment claim specification shall be recorded in the patent register.

An applicant seeking to introduce an amendment claim specification in a patent application under this Act shall submit a written request detailing the proposed alteration. Such request must demonstrate that the amended claims remain consistent with the disclosure contained within the original complete specification and do not broaden the scope of protection beyond what was initially described. The Controller may, subject to compliance with these requirements, allow the amendment if satisfied that it does not substantially alter the inventive concept as originally presented. Provided that any such amendment claim specification shall be accompanied by a declaration affirming its fidelity to the prior disclosure. Further, where an amendment introduces new matter, the applicant must provide evidence demonstrating prior public knowledge of said matter at the date of filing.

Any applicant seeking to alter an existing claim specification within a patent application shall file a formal request with the Controller, detailing the proposed modifications and providing justification demonstrating their consistency with the original disclosure. Such requests are subject to rigorous examination; any amendment deemed to introduce new matter or substantially broaden the scope of protection beyond that originally described may be rejected outright. Failure to adequately substantiate an amendment claim specification can result in imposition of a monetary penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees, recoverable as civil debt. The Controller shall provide written reasons for any rejection, and appeal against such decision lies with the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. Repeated frivolous attempts at amendment will attract progressively higher penalties, potentially leading to application abandonment.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any patentee desiring to grant an exclusive license or assign the right to a patent in respect of an invention for which he has filed an application may execute a written instrument specifying the terms and conditions thereof. Such instrument shall clearly define the scope of the licensed rights or assigned interest, referencing specifically the amendment claim specification as it exists at the date of execution. The patentee shall file such instrument with the Controller within three months from the date of its execution; failure to do so may render the license or assignment voidable. Further provision is made that any subsequent amendment claim specification filed after the execution of a licensing agreement shall be deemed to modify the scope of the granted rights proportionally, unless otherwise explicitly agreed upon in writing by all parties involved.

Where an applicant seeks to introduce alterations to a patent application beyond those permissible under this Act relating to clerical errors or obvious matters, such proposed amendments shall constitute an amendment claim specification. The Controller may allow such amendment only if he is satisfied that the alteration does not substantially alter the nature of the invention as originally disclosed and that the amended claims remain clear and concise. Any party aggrieved by a decision of the Controller permitting or refusing an amendment claim specification may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order, demonstrating how the amendment fundamentally changes the scope of protection sought and prejudices their existing rights under this Act. The Board’s determination shall be final.

Where an applicant seeks to introduce an amendment claim specification in respect of a patent application already published under this Act, such amendment shall only be permissible if it clarifies the subject matter disclosed in the original specification and does not substantially alter the nature of the invention. Any attempt to broaden the scope of protection beyond that initially described will be deemed invalid and may render the granted patent liable for revocation proceedings. Furthermore, any party demonstrating prejudice arising from a late or unduly expansive amendment claim specification shall have standing to petition the Controller for appropriate remedies, including damages proportionate to the infringement suffered due to the extended exclusive rights afforded by the amended claim. The Controller shall impose penalties as provided herein upon finding such an infraction.

For the purposes of this Act, a “biotechnological invention” shall mean an invention which involves biological material obtained from living organisms or derived therefrom, including sequences or partial sequences of genes, genomic DNA, RNA, antisense oligonucleotides and peptides. An application to register patents shall include a clear and concise description of the biotechnological invention, specifying the source of the biological material used and detailing any modifications made thereto. The Controller may require further information regarding the stability and reproducibility of the biological element as part of the examination process. Provided that such disclosure does not compromise trade secrets, all relevant data must be submitted under this Act.

An applicant seeking to register patents shall furnish with the application a statement indicating the claimed priority, if any, based on an earlier publication or application for the same invention. The Controller General may require further documentation substantiating this claim and verifying its authenticity under this Act. Where an international preliminary examination is requested, the details of such request shall be recorded in the register. Any modification to the particulars relating to the inventor or assignee after registration must be notified to the patent office, and these alterations shall then be entered into the register as provided herein. The applicant’s declaration regarding the novelty and non-obviousness of the invention remains crucial for successful registration.

Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Controller relating to the grant, revocation, or infringement of a patent shall have the right to appeal to the Appellate Intellectual Property Tribunal. Such an appeal may be made within sixty days from the date of communication of the order and must specify the grounds upon which it is based. The Tribunal shall hear appeals expeditiously and may allow such remedies as are just and equitable, including but not limited to damages for past infringement or injunctions preventing future acts of infringement. It is provided that a patentee seeking relief under this Act relating to infringement shall demonstrate reasonable efforts were made to mitigate the harm caused by the infringing activity. The Tribunal’s decision shall be final, subject to further appeal to the Supreme Court on grounds involving questions of law only. To register patents shall be deemed an act requiring utmost good faith.

An applicant seeking to register patents shall furnish a complete specification detailing the invention, including its utility and manner of operation. This specification must disclose the best method contemplated by the applicant for carrying out the invention, provided that it is sufficient to enable a person skilled in the art to practice said invention without undue experimentation. Further, the application shall include claims clearly defining the scope of protection sought; these claims must be supported by the disclosure within the specification and not extend beyond what is described therein. Any alteration made to the claimed subject matter after the initial filing date will render the patent liable for invalidation under this Act. The Controller may require further clarification or amendments to ensure compliance with these requirements.

Any person aggrieved by a decision to register patents shall have the right to appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of communication of that decision. Failure to comply with prescribed procedures during application, or subsequent amendment processes, renders the patent vulnerable to challenge and revocation under this Act. Where infringement is established, the Controller may order injunctions restraining further acts of infringement, and shall determine compensation payable by the infringer to the patentee, taking into account lost profits and reasonable royalties. Repeated instances of wilful infringement shall attract enhanced penalties, as provided herein, including imprisonment for a term not less than six months and a fine extending up to ten lakhs rupees.

Any patentee desiring to grant a licence conferring rights to use or exploit a patented invention shall execute a written instrument specifying the scope of such licence, including but not limited to territorial limitations, field of use restrictions, and royalty rates. Such instruments must be registered with the Controller within three months of execution, subject to payment of prescribed fees. Failure to register a licence shall render it unenforceable against third parties claiming rights under that licence. The patentee may assign or pledge the patent, or any right pertaining thereto, to another person, provided that such assignment is also recorded in the Register and includes details of consideration paid, if any. Where an invention has been assigned, subsequent licences granted by the assignee shall be deemed valid, but the original patentee retains a right to audit royalty accounts annually for a period of five years following the initial assignment. The Controller may require further documentation to verify compliance with these provisions; and register patents shall remain subject to these stipulations.

An application to register patents shall contain a specification describing the invention clearly and completely for enabling any person skilled in the art to make and use it. The applicant must also furnish details regarding priority, if claiming under a prior application. Upon receipt of an application, the court registrar shall verify compliance with prescribed formalities relating to form and execution. Further, the registrar may require the applicant to submit clarifications or amendments deemed necessary for proper examination. Any deficiency in these particulars will be communicated to the applicant, who shall have opportunity to rectify them within the time specified under this Act. Failure to comply with such requirements will result in rejection of the application as provided herein.

Where a patentee desires to grant a license conferring specific rights relating to the invention for which he has applied to register patents shall file with the Controller a certified copy of the licensing agreement, detailing the scope and duration of the permitted use. Such agreements may include provisions for royalty payments, sub-licensing opportunities, or restrictions on field of use as deemed appropriate by the parties involved. The Controller may require further clarification regarding any ambiguous terms within the license. A basic application for a patent shall not preclude the patentee from subsequently assigning the entire interest in the invention to another party, provided that such assignment is duly registered under this Act. Any modification to an existing licensing agreement requires notification to the Controller and may be subject to review to ensure compliance with provisions herein.

Where an application for a patent is refused under this Act, the applicant shall have the right to appeal against such refusal to the Appellate Board. The Board shall consider any evidence submitted by the applicant demonstrating prima facie novelty and inventive step, notwithstanding any prior publication or use disclosed during examination. Any party aggrieved by an order of the Appellate Board may further appeal to the High Court within a period of ninety days from the date of communication of that order. It is provided that the register patents shall be deemed conclusive evidence of the facts stated therein unless proven otherwise through documented legal challenge, and any attempt to register shall brought before the Controller for initial assessment.

For the purposes of this Act, “invention” shall mean a new and useful art, process, manufacture, or composition of matter, and includes any improvement thereof. An application to register patents shall contain a specification describing the invention in sufficient detail to enable a person skilled in the art to make and use it; such specification shall also disclose the best mode contemplated by the applicant for carrying out the invention. The determination of whether an invention is novel or involves inventive step may be reviewed under appeal before the copyrights appellate board, subject to provisions regarding costs as provided herein.

For the purposes of this Act, a “biotechnological invention” shall mean an invention which involves biological material obtained from living organisms, including plants, animals, and microorganisms, or derivatives thereof, and utilizes biotechnology processes to produce goods, substances, or technologies. Patents shall entered in respect of biotechnological inventions subject to the condition that such inventions are novel, non-obvious, and useful. The term “biological material” includes genetic sequences, cell lines, antibodies, enzymes, and recombinant DNA molecules. Further, an invention relating to a process for producing biological material is patentable provided that the process itself is new and involves technical skill.

Applications for registration of plant varieties shall be accompanied by a detailed description of the variety, including its botanical name, origin, method of reproduction, and any distinctive features readily discernible by experts. Upon receipt of an application, the Plant Varieties Registry shall publish a notification inviting objections from interested parties within a period specified under this Act. Where no valid objection is received, or where such objections are withdrawn or dismissed, patents shall entered in the Register of Plant Varieties. The Registrar may require applicants to submit additional data relating to the stability and uniformity of the variety. Patents shall entered subject to the provisions regarding compulsory licensing as provided herein.

Applications for patents shall be examined by a Controller appointed under this Act, who may, after giving notice to the applicant and opportunity to be heard, reject any application if he finds that the invention is not novel or does not involve an inventive step. Where a patent has been granted, it shall entered in the Register of Patents maintained at the Patent Office, detailing the title of the invention, the name and address of the patentee, and the date of grant. The Controller may require amendments to be made to the specifications prior to entry if they are necessary for clarity or precision. Any person aggrieved by an order of the Controller under this Act may appeal to the Appellate Board within a period specified herein. Patents shall entered with such particulars as prescribed, subject to any modifications directed by the Controller and provided that the Register remains open to public inspection during normal business hours.

Where an application for a patent relates to a process for producing a substance controlled under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, it shall be referred to the Central Narcotics Control Board for assessment regarding its potential impact on public health and safety. Patents shall entered into the Register of Patents only after the Central Narcotics Control Board has submitted its report, provided that the Controller may proceed with examination if the applicant furnishes a bank guarantee deemed sufficient by the Controller towards any compensation which may be awarded under this Act. Any modification to the patented process following such referral must again be subject to review and approval as provided herein before patents shall entered. The Central Narcotics Control Board’s recommendations are advisory, but the Controller shall give due consideration thereto.

Any person aggrieved by a decision relating to the grant, revocation, or infringement of a patent shall have the right to appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. Such appeals must be filed within ninety days from the date of communication of the order appealed against and failure to do so will render the appeal inadmissible. Where an injunction is sought concerning a patent, the tribunal may require security to be furnished by the applicant, as provided herein, to compensate any party suffering loss due to the operation of the injunction. Patents shall entered in the Register of Patents upon payment of prescribed fees; however, failure to pay such fees within the stipulated timeframe will result in the patent being deemed abandoned and subject to forfeiture.

Where a patentee desires to grant a license conferring specific rights relating to their invention, they shall execute a written instrument detailing the scope of such license, including but not limited to territorial limitations, field of use restrictions, and royalty arrangements. Such instruments must be filed with the Controller within thirty days of execution; failure to do so renders the license unenforceable against third parties. The Controller may, upon application by any interested party, require further clarification regarding the terms of a license agreement. Patents shall entered in the Register detailing all assignments, transmissions, and licenses granted under this Act, along with the date of such actions and the names and addresses of the relevant parties involved. Any subsequent modification or revocation of a license must also be recorded as provided herein to maintain transparency and facilitate public access to patent information.

Where a patent is granted for an invention relating to a process for producing a substance defined by its chemical composition, the Controller may, upon application made by any person aggrieved, review the decision to grant said patent if it is demonstrated that the claimed subject matter lacks novelty or involves an obvious modification of existing knowledge. Such applications shall be accompanied by reasoned arguments and supporting documentation substantiating the grounds for challenge. The Patent Office shall provide a reasonable opportunity for both the applicant and the patentee to present their respective cases, including expert testimony. Patents shall entered in the register with notations reflecting any such review proceedings and their outcomes, subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

Where a patent has been granted for a novel variety of plant, any person aggrieved by a decision relating to infringement of that patent shall have the right to appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. Such an appeal may be made within sixty days from the date of communication of the order appealed against and shall be based on substantial grounds demonstrating error in law or fact. The tribunal shall consider evidence presented by both the patent holder and the aggrieved party, including expert testimony regarding the distinctiveness and stability of the new variety. Should the tribunal find infringement has occurred, it may grant such remedies as are deemed just and equitable, including injunctions preventing further exploitation of the patented invention and compensation for damages suffered. Patents shall entered in the Register of New Plant Varieties with details of the breeder’s rights.

For the purposes of this Act, “invention territory India” shall mean the territory comprising India and such other territories as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify; provided that an invention shall be deemed to be worked in invention territory India if it is manufactured or produced for sale within India, or used directly or indirectly in discharge of any function, activity or work carried on in India. The Central Government may, subject to conditions as provided herein, extend the application of this Act to any other country by notification in the Official Gazette; such extension shall be deemed to include that country within the meaning of invention territory India for the purposes of patentability and enforcement under this Act.

An application for a patent shall disclose the matter which the applicant considers to be his invention and also specify the class or classes to which it relates. The determination of novelty and inventive step, as provided herein, shall be assessed with reference to the state of the art in relation to the invention territory India. Where an applicant seeks protection for multiple inventions disclosed in a single application, each such invention must be clearly defined in the claims. Further, any request for amendment to the claims after the first examination shall be permissible only if such amendments do not alter the nature or scope of the original disclosure. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish further particulars or documents relating to the working of the invention within India.

Where an interested person considers that the grant of a patent is contrary to law, he may institute civil proceedings in the High Court, subject to the provisions regarding limitation as provided under this Act. The court shall have jurisdiction to determine whether the claimed invention infringes any prior publication or prior use, and if so, to restrain the patentee from exercising the rights conferred by the patent. Further, where a patent has been granted for an invention relating to a process that is not capable of being worked in India, the patent may be revoked under this Act upon application made by any interested person demonstrating such non-workability. The scope of the invention territory India shall extend to all areas within the geographical boundaries of India and its territorial waters. Any infringement occurring within this territory constitutes an actionable wrong, entitling the patentee to seek damages and injunctive relief.

An application for a patent shall be deemed to relate to an invention if it is not contrary to law and involves a process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter. The determination of whether an invention falls within this definition is subject to examination by the Controller, who may require further clarification regarding the nature and scope of the claimed invention. For the purposes of assessing patentability, the invention territory India extends exclusively to the territory of India, including its land territory, territorial waters, and airspace over it. Any prior use or publication relating to an invention occurring outside this defined geographical area shall not be considered in determining novelty or inventive step under this Act. The applicant shall furnish such documentary evidence as the Controller deems necessary to substantiate claims regarding the originality and non-obviousness of the invention within the specified territory.

An invention shall be deemed to include an improvement of an existing invention, provided that such improvement results in a substantial advance in the state of the art. For the purposes of determining patentability under this Act, the term "invention territory india" refers exclusively to the geographical area comprising the Union of India and its territorial waters. An application for a patent may be filed if the applicant is satisfied that the invention has not been previously disclosed to the public in any manner, whether by written or oral description, use, exhibition, or otherwise. Subject to compliance with prescribed formalities regarding documentation and claims, an inventor shall be entitled to a provisional patent right for a period of twelve months from the date of first filing, allowing time for assessment of commercial viability.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order, subject to payment of such fee as may be prescribed. The Appellate Board shall consider all relevant materials and hear any party who desires to be heard, and may pass such orders as it deems fit, including setting aside or modifying the original order. Failure to comply with a cease and desist order issued pursuant to an infringement proceeding constitutes a cognizable offence, punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and with a fine not less than fifty thousand rupees, recoverable as a pecuniary penalty under this Act. The invention territory India extends to the whole of India and any part thereof and includes overseas territories under the control of the Central Government.

Where the patentee of a patent granted under this Act desires to grant an exclusive license to work a patented invention within the invention territory india, such license may be assigned or surrendered subject to the provisions herein. The terms and conditions of any such assignment shall be recorded in the prescribed manner with the Controller, including details regarding royalty rates payable by the assignee to the licensor, which royalty rate shall not be less than two percent of net sales realized from the working of the invention. Provided that if the license is granted to a person resident outside india, the Central Government may require security to be furnished as deemed appropriate to safeguard national interests and ensure compulsory licensing provisions are adhered to. The patentee shall provide all necessary documentation relating to such assignments upon request by the Controller or any authorized officer.

Where an appeal lies under this Act against a decision of the Controller relating to the grant or revocation of a patent, the Appellate Board may, subject to such conditions as it deems fit, direct that the costs of the appeal be paid by any party thereto. It shall be open to the appellant to argue that the interpretation of “invention territory India” applied by the Controller was manifestly erroneous in law, particularly concerning the application of principles of territorial sovereignty and the impact of international treaties ratified by the Republic. The Board may, if satisfied that such an error occurred, remit the matter for reconsideration or determine the issue afresh. Provided that any order made under this provision shall not prejudice the rights of third parties who have bona fide acquired interests in reliance upon the Controller’s initial determination.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, and without prejudice to the rights of licensees, any patentee may grant exclusive licenses relating to the use or exploitation of an invention within the invention territory india, including but not limited to manufacturing, importing, selling, or offering for sale. Such license shall be in writing and clearly define the scope of the licensed right, the duration of the license, and the royalty payable by the licensee to the patentee. The denomination variety shall be considered when determining the extent of such exclusive rights where the invention relates to a plant variety protection. Assignment of patent rights may occur with the written consent of all parties holding licenses under the original patent, provided that such assignment includes provisions ensuring continued adherence to the terms and conditions of existing license agreements. Further, any transfer or assignment shall be registered as prescribed herein.

For the purposes of this Act, “invention territory India” shall mean the territory comprising the Union of India and its territorial waters. An application for patent shall be deemed to be made within the invention territory India if the applicant is domiciled or has a place of business within that territory. Where any person falsifies trade by representing as genuine an article produced otherwise than under authority, such action shall not preclude them from being held accountable under this Act regarding matters pertaining to patent validity or infringement. The Registrar may require proof of domicile or establishment of a place of business as provided herein.

An inventor desiring to secure protection for an invention under this Act shall, upon filing the application, specify the territorial extent within which such protection is sought; provided that where the applicant desires patent protection across multiple jurisdictions, a declaration affirming such intent may be included as an addendum to the formal application. The invention territory India shall encompass all areas within the geographical boundaries of the Union of India and its territories. Assignment of the patent rights arising from this application, whether by way of present or future interest, absolute or conditional, shall require registration with the Controller, subject to prescribed fees and forms. Failure to register such assignment renders it void against subsequent assignees.

Where an applicant for registration of a trademark utilizes a deceptive representation regarding the nature, quality, characteristics, geographical origin, or production process of goods or services, such application shall be deemed invalid under this Act. Any person found to have knowingly made false statements in support of a trademark application, or engaged in practices intended to mislead consumers concerning the source or composition of goods bearing a registered trademark, is liable for an offence. Such offender shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and also subject to penalty thousand rupees, recoverable as a fine.

Any Registrar, upon receiving an application for registration of a layout plan relating to land within a municipal corporation area, shall verify that the applicant has complied with all applicable regulations concerning environmental clearances and building bylaws. Failure to submit requisite documentation demonstrating such compliance, as provided herein, constitutes a deficiency in the application. The Registrar may require the applicant to rectify this deficiency within sixty days; otherwise, the application shall be deemed rejected. Any person who knowingly submits false or misleading information regarding compliance with these regulations is liable for penalty thousand rupees and may face further action under relevant municipal ordinances.

Where an objection is taken against the grant of a patent relating to a process by way of manufacture, and such objection alleges that the claimed invention does not involve an inventive step, the Controller shall afford the applicant and the objector an opportunity for cross-examination and oral argument. Any party aggrieved by any order passed under this Act may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. Provided that where a person is found to have made a false statement or suppressed material fact in relation to the application, they shall be liable to penalty thousand rupees for each such misstatement or suppression. The Appellate Board’s decision shall be final, subject to further appeal under the relevant appellate provisions.

Where an applicant for registration of a trademark knowingly presents false representations concerning the use of the mark within India, or regarding prior rights held by any other person, the Controller may, after affording due opportunity for cross-examination and rebuttal, determine that such representations are deemed falsify trade. The aggrieved party shall have the right to appeal this determination before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. Further, where a finding of false representation is upheld on appeal, the applicant shall be liable to penalty thousand rupees for each day during which the misleading information remained in the application record. This liability shall not preclude further action under other provisions of this Act relating to fraudulent conduct.

Where an international registration extending to India undergoes examination as provided herein, and the Controller finds that the application does not comply with the requirements of this Act, including but not limited to deficiencies in the description of the invention or claims, notice shall be given to the applicant specifying the grounds for non-compliance. The applicant may then amend the application within a period prescribed by the regulations. Failure to rectify such deficiencies within the stipulated time will result in the international registration being refused for India. Any person who knowingly makes a false statement in connection with an international registration referred, or attempts to mislead the Controller regarding compliance, shall be liable to penalty thousand rupees and may also face proceedings for professional misconduct.

Where an applicant for registration of a geographical indication fails to comply with the requirements regarding the prescribed form of application, including but not limited to the accurate representation of the territorial boundaries encompassed by the indication, or provides false information concerning the qualities, reputation, or other characteristics associated with the goods specified in the application, the Registrar may issue a notice requiring rectification within a period as determined by the Registrar. Should the applicant neglect to rectify the deficiencies within that stipulated timeframe, the application shall be deemed abandoned. Furthermore, any person who knowingly makes a false statement in connection with an application for registration or subsequent proceedings under this Act shall be liable to penalty thousand rupees and may also face prosecution under relevant provisions of the Indian Penal Code. The International Bureau shall be notified of such actions as provided herein.

The Register of Registered Designs shall maintain a record of all applications for registration pertaining to designs incorporating functional elements. An applicant seeking registration under this Act may, subject to fulfilling prescribed formalities, apply for the acquisition of exclusive rights relating to the design’s appearance and ornamental characteristics. Such application shall detail the specific features claimed as novel and original, accompanied by requisite drawings and specifications. The Controller General, upon examination, may grant registration provided that the design does not primarily serve a utilitarian purpose and is substantially different from existing prior art. Any person aggrieved by a decision relating to acquiring restrict of rights may appeal under this Act to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

Where a patent has been granted for an invention relating to a process for producing a substance controlled under this Act, the Controller may, subject to due process and after affording the patentee an opportunity of being heard, issue directions restricting the manufacture, sale, or importation of that substance by any person other than the patentee or persons authorized by the patentee. Such directions shall specify the conditions governing such restricted activities, including but not limited to limitations on quantity, duration, and intended use.
