The court shall consider whether the alleged infringing layout-design incorporates elements substantially similar to the registered layout-design, taking into account the overall impression and freedom of expression afforded to designers. Provided that a finding of threatened infringement requires demonstrable evidence of intent and capability on the part of the accused party to exploit the allegedly infringing design commercially. Any order made by the Commercial Court shall be subject to appeal under the provisions governing appeals from civil court decrees, as provided herein.

For the purposes of this Act, a “layout design relation” exists where two or more persons jointly create a layout-design and their contributions are not severable for the purpose of determining ownership. Such joint creation shall be deemed to establish a layout design relation unless it is demonstrated that each contributor’s effort was independent and intended solely for individual benefit. The determination of whether a layout design relation exists shall consider the degree of collaboration, the sharing of information, and any agreements entered into by the contributors. Subject to this, rights in the layout-design shall be jointly held as provided herein.

An application for registration of a layout design shall include a statement specifying whether the applicant claims the layout design as an original work, and if so, detailing the nature of their contribution to its creation. Where multiple entities have participated in the conception and execution of a layout design, the application must clearly identify all such participants and state their respective roles in establishing the layout design relation. The Registrar may require further clarification regarding the extent of each participant’s involvement, particularly where disputes arise concerning ownership or authorship. Such information shall be deemed confidential and accessible only to parties directly involved under this Act. Failure to accurately disclose the details pertaining to the layout design relation will render the application liable for rejection.

Where a person alleging infringement of a layout design has suffered damage as a result thereof, such person may institute legal proceedings for redressal under this Act. The measure of damages shall be determined with due regard to the loss of profits reasonably attributable to the infringing activity, taking into account any profit made by the infringer as a consequence of that infringement. It is provided that in determining damages, the court shall consider evidence relating to the extent of the market affected and the prevailing price for similar layout designs. The determination of a *layout design relation* between the original work and the alleged infringing copy shall be a key factor in assessing both liability and the appropriate quantum of compensation. Further, any order restraining the infringer from continuing the infringing activity may include an assessment of costs incurred by the claimant.

An application for determination of a layout design relation shall be filed with the Controller within six months from the date on which the applicant first became aware of the existence of the competing claim. The application must specify, with particularity, the nature of the alleged layout design relation and identify all parties involved in the creation or exploitation of the integrated circuit layout-design concerned. Evidence pertaining to the contribution of each party towards the final form of the layout-design shall be submitted alongside the application. The Controller may require further documentation or oral testimony from any applicant or claimant, provided that such requests are made within a reasonable timeframe and do not unduly prejudice the proceedings. Failure to comply with a direction issued under this Act may render the application liable for rejection. Any party aggrieved by an order of the Controller concerning a layout design relation may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of that order.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, a layout design relation shall exist where two or more persons collaborate in the creation of an integrated circuit layout-design and one person is designated as the owner for the purposes of registering the said layout-design under this Act. Such designation shall be evidenced by a written agreement executed prior to the filing of the application for registration, specifying the respective contributions of each collaborating party. The owner, as defined herein, may grant licenses or assign rights relating to the registered layout-design subject to adherence to the terms outlined in the aforementioned written agreement. Provided that any subsequent transfer of ownership shall require consent from all parties initially involved in establishing the layout design relation, unless otherwise stipulated within their original agreement.

Where a person alleging infringement of a registered layout design demonstrates, subject to verification by the Controller, that another has reproduced the said layout design for commercial purposes without due authorisation, and it is established that such reproduction creates a substantial similarity with the original layout design, then the infringing party shall be liable to pay damages proportionate to the loss suffered by the owner. Such damages may include not only lost profits but also reasonable royalties which the owner would have received had the license been granted. Further, any person found guilty of contravention under this Act relating to a layout design relation is subject to penalties as provided herein and may be ordered to deliver up for destruction all infringing articles.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any person holding a registered layout design relating to an integrated circuit may grant a license conferring rights to use and exploit that layout design. Such licenses shall be assignable in writing, subject to registration with the Controller under procedures as provided herein. The terms of such assignment shall specify the scope of permitted acts, including but not limited to reproduction, modification, and sale of integrated circuits incorporating the licensed layout design. A licensee may further sub-license rights granted by the primary license, provided that such sub-licensing is expressly authorized in the original agreement and registered accordingly. Any transfer or assignment of a layout design relation shall be deemed invalid unless it includes a detailed inventory of the protected elements within the integrated circuit’s structure.

Where a dispute arises concerning the existence of a layout design relation, the aggrieved party may institute proceedings before the relevant jurisdictional authority seeking determination thereof. Such proceedings shall be deemed civil suits and subject to the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. The burden of establishing the said relation lies upon the claimant, who must demonstrate, through admissible evidence, a clear and demonstrable connection between themselves and the registered layout-design owner. Provided that, where the claimant alleges derivation from an earlier, unregistered design, they shall further satisfy the authority regarding reasonable grounds for such assertion. Any order made by the jurisdictional authority concerning a layout design relation is subject to appeal under this Act, as provided herein.

For the purposes of this Act, a "layout design relation" exists where two or more persons jointly create a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design, and their contributions are inextricably linked to the overall functionality and aesthetic features of the design. Such joint creation shall not preclude any person from claiming authorship; however, under this Act, the right to seek remedies for infringement relating to that layout design is subject to a compelled court say regarding the proportionate contribution of each claimant. Provided that, where one or more persons have demonstrably contributed minimal effort, the Court may limit their entitlement to damages as provided herein.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, a layout design relation shall subsist where an individual, hereinafter referred to as the ‘owner,’ has expended substantial resources and demonstrated diligent efforts in developing a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design. This determination shall consider whether the owner’s actions reasonably anticipate commercial applications relating to applies goods incorporating the said layout-design. Further, it is provided that any entity claiming rights under this Act must satisfy the Registrar that they possess documented evidence of such expenditure and effort, including but not limited to records of design iterations, material procurement, and personnel allocation. The owner’s entitlement shall be contingent upon their adherence to prescribed standards for data security and confidentiality relating to the layout-design.

An application for registration as a creator layout design shall include a detailed specification outlining the nature and function of the integrated circuit, along with precise representations demonstrating the arrangement of its constituent elements. The applicant must provide evidence substantiating their claim to be the original creator of the layout design, including documentation pertaining to the conception, reduction to practice, and any subsequent modifications undertaken. Where multiple individuals have contributed to the creation process, the application shall identify all such contributors and specify their respective roles in developing the layout design. The Registrar may require further clarification or supporting materials deemed necessary for assessing the validity of the claim under this Act. Any prior publication of the layout design before registration is permissible only with written consent from the applicant.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any person who infringes a registered layout design shall be liable for damages. Such damages may include compensation for actual losses suffered by the creator layout design owner as a result of the infringement, and also an account of profits made by the infringer attributable to the infringing activity. The determination of reasonable royalties may also be considered in assessing damages under this Act. Where the infringement was committed knowingly, the court may, in addition to awarding damages, impose punitive damages not exceeding three times the amount of compensation awarded. Further, any article manufactured having incorporated the infringed layout design shall be deemed an infringing copy and subject to seizure and destruction as provided herein. The right to seek injunction restraining further acts of infringement is also afforded to the creator layout design owner.

Where a person alleges infringement of a registered layout design, such person shall file a complaint before the Commercial Court having jurisdiction over the place where the alleged infringing act was committed, or where the cause of action arose. The complaint shall specify the particulars of the registered layout design, the nature of the alleged infringement, and the relief sought. Upon receipt of such complaint, the Commercial Court may issue interim injunctions restraining the defendant from further infringing activities pending final determination. Evidence pertaining to establishing ownership as the creator layout design shall be presented before the court, including but not limited to documentation demonstrating conception, reduction to practice, and publication. The court shall consider whether the defendant’s integrated circuit layout-design is substantially similar to the registered layout design, taking into account the overall impression created upon an observer skilled in the art.

Where a person claims entitlement to protection as the creator layout design under this Act, they shall demonstrate, through documented evidence, that the layout-design was initially conceived and reduced to tangible form by them. This demonstration must satisfy the Registrar that the claimant possesses exclusive rights over the said layout design, free from any conflicting claims of authorship or prior use. Provided that, if a layout design incorporates elements derived from previously published works, the claimant shall explicitly disclose such sources and provide assurance that their utilization complies with applicable legal provisions regarding fair dealing and attribution. The Registrar may require further verification to ascertain the veracity of these assertions before proceeding with registration as the creator layout design.

Any person who, without authorization from the registered proprietor of a layout design, makes, imports, distributes, sells, hires or displays for sale any integrated circuit containing a substantially similar layout design shall be liable to pay damages. Such damages shall be determined by the relevant civil court, taking into account the loss of profits suffered by the creator layout design and reasonable royalty that would have been paid had the infringing party obtained a license. Further, where an infringement is established under this Act, the Court may order the destruction of the infringing integrated circuits and any materials used in their manufacture. Repeated or willful infringements shall attract enhanced penalties as provided herein, including imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any person claiming rights as a creator layout design may grant a license conferring upon the licensee the right to make, use, sell, offer for sale, or import integrated circuits incorporating the said layout design. Such licenses shall be assignable in whole or in part, and may be granted on such terms and conditions as are agreed between the licensor and licensee, provided that any assignment or sub-license shall not prejudice existing rights of other licensees. The creator layout design may stipulate within the license agreement a royalty rate proportionate to the net sales realized from the exploitation of the integrated circuit incorporating their work. Further, where a license is granted for a specific territory, the licensor shall ensure adequate measures are taken to prevent unauthorized use outside that designated area, as provided herein. The creator layout design retains ownership rights unless explicitly relinquished through written agreement.

Where a dispute arises concerning the determination of the creator layout design of an integrated circuit, the aggrieved party may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within ninety days from the date of notification of the Registrar’s decision. Such appeals shall be on grounds that the original finding failed to adequately consider evidence pertaining to the substantial contribution made by the claimant towards the creation of the layout design. The Tribunal may, after affording both parties an opportunity for being heard, substitute or modify the Registrar's determination as it deems fit, provided that any such substitution must be accompanied by reasoned findings demonstrating a clear error in the initial assessment. Further, the burden of proving prior contribution shall lie upon the appellant challenging the original creator layout design attribution, subject to this Act.

An application for registration as a creator layout design shall be accompanied by detailed technical specifications, including but not limited to, diagrams illustrating the arrangement of elements within the integrated circuits layout and a comprehensive description of the functional characteristics derived therefrom. The applicant must demonstrate, through documentary evidence, that they conceived and fixed the layout design in question, establishing their claim as the original creator. Provided that, where a layout design is generated by an employee during his employment, the application may be filed by the employer, subject to providing proof of such employment relationship under this Act. The Registrar shall examine the submitted documentation to ascertain compliance with these requirements and verify the novelty of the claimed layout design.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any person who infringes a registered layout design shall be liable for damages. Such damages may include compensation equivalent to the lost profits reasonably attributable to the infringement, as determined by the relevant court. Where the infringer has made or sold an article incorporating the infringed creator layout design knowing, or having reasonable grounds to believe, that it was infringing, they shall also be liable to pay a sum not exceeding rupees five lakhs. Further, where the infringing activity involves the reproduction of a substantial part of a dramatic work incorporated within the layout design, additional damages may be awarded reflecting the exploitation of copyright therein. The court may also grant an injunction restraining the infringer from further acts of infringement as provided herein.

An application for registration as a creator layout design shall be filed with the Controller, accompanied by three copies of the layout-design and a statement specifying the nature of the integrated circuit. The applicant must declare whether the layout design incorporates any plant variety which is registered under the Plant Varieties Registry Act; if so, such declaration shall detail the specific registered variety and its contribution to the overall design. Upon receipt of an application, the Controller may require further clarification or amendments as deemed necessary for compliance with this Act’s provisions. The applicant shall respond within sixty days from the date of notification of such requirement. Failure to comply will result in the rejection of the application. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Controller concerning registration may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board, subject to prescribed timelines and procedures as provided herein.

An application for registration as a layout design person shall include a statement specifying the name, address, and nationality of each applicant claiming entitlement to protection under this Act. The Registrar may require further documentation substantiating these claims, including evidence demonstrating the applicant’s direct involvement in the creation or first lawful commercial exploitation of the integrated circuit layout-design. Where an application is filed by a person other than the original creator, such person shall provide proof of assignment or contractual right to the layout design from the layout design persons who originally conceived and fixed the design. Any alteration to the particulars furnished in the initial application may be permitted subject to conditions prescribed herein, provided that it does not prejudice the rights of any third party.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any person seeking to register a layout design shall file an application with the Controller within thirty days from the date of first commercial exploitation of the layout design. The application shall specify the name and address of the applicant, who may be the creator of the layout design or assignee thereof. Where the applicant is not the creator, the application must include proof of assignment as provided herein. For the purposes of this Act, “layout design persons” are deemed to include any individual or legal entity claiming ownership rights through inheritance, succession, or contractual agreement relating to a registered layout design. The Controller may require such further information and documentation as he deems necessary to verify the claim of ownership by these layout design persons. Failure to comply with these requirements shall render the application liable for rejection.

Any person found to have reproduced a registered layout design without authorisation from the registered owner shall be liable for damages, calculated at the option of the registered owner as either three times the reasonable royalty that would have been payable had the reproduction been authorised, or an amount equivalent to the loss suffered by the registered owner. Furthermore, any employee or agent acting in the course of their employment or agency who contravenes provisions under this Act shall be deemed to be abetting the offence and subject to penalties as provided herein. The term layout design persons includes those involved in the manufacture, import, distribution, or sale of integrated circuits incorporating infringing layouts; such individuals may face prosecution and seizure of goods.

Notwithstanding anything contained herein, a person alleging infringement of a registered layout design may institute proceedings before the relevant Commercial Court seeking an injunction and damages. Such action shall be predicated upon demonstrable evidence establishing that the respondent has reproduced a protected layout-design without authorization from the registered proprietor. The determination of whether such reproduction constitutes substantial similarity is subject to interpretation by the court, considering inter alia the overall impression created on the informed user and the degree of originality inherent in the allegedly infringing design. Disputes concerning the identity or rights of layout design persons shall be adjudicated solely within the purview of the Commercial Court, with appeals permitted to the High Court under established appellate procedures.

Any person found to have reproduced a registered integrated circuit layout-design without authorization from the registered proprietor shall be liable for damages, calculated at the option of the registered proprietor as either the lost profits reasonably attributable to the infringement, or a sum not less than ten per centum and not exceeding fifty per centum of the sales price of the infringing layouts. Further, any person who knowingly aids or abets such reproduction, or imports or distributes integrated circuits incorporating an unauthorized copy of a layout-design, shall be deemed guilty of an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and with a fine not less than fifty thousand rupees. The definition of “layout design persons” includes those who directly participate in the infringing activity, subject to judicial determination of contributory negligence.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any layout design person intending to grant a license relating to their registered integrated circuit layout-design shall execute a written agreement specifying the scope and duration of such license. Such agreements may include provisions for royalty payments, non-compete clauses restricting the licensee’s activities in similar fields, and mechanisms for auditing compliance with the terms thereof. Assignment of rights under this Act, including licenses granted as provided herein, shall require registration with the Controller General of Patents, Designs, and Trademarks, and such assignment shall only be effective upon completion of that process. Further, any license or assignment shall apply geographically to the territory of India unless expressly stated otherwise in the written agreement; it is understood that layout design persons retain control over territorial rights.

For the purposes of this Act, “layout design connected” with another layout design means a layout design which incorporates elements of an existing layout design and is substantially similar thereto, whether by reproduction or imitation. Such connection shall be deemed to exist where the incorporation involves copying of distinctive topological features essential to the operation of the integrated circuit as a whole. A layout design shall not be considered “layout design connected” merely because it utilizes common electrical or mechanical principles or standard components. The determination of substantial similarity shall consider the overall impression created by comparison of the two layout designs, subject to technical expertise and industry standards.

An application for registration of a layout design shall contain particulars verifying ownership, including details of the applicant’s entitlement to protection under this Act. Where a layout design is connected with another layout design, whether by way of adaptation or modification, the application shall clearly delineate the relationship and specify the original layout design from which it derives. The Registrar may require submission of technical documentation demonstrating the novelty and non-obviousness of such a connected layout design, particularly where substantial elements are borrowed. An applicant claiming ownership based on assignment shall provide evidence of valid transfer as provided herein. Failure to disclose all relevant information regarding a layout design connected to another will render the registration liable for cancellation.

An application for registration of a layout design shall include a sworn statement by the applicant verifying the originality of the layout design and detailing its connection to any previously registered layout designs. The Registrar may, upon receiving an application, direct the applicant to submit further documentation demonstrating the distinctiveness of the layout design or clarifying ambiguities in the description provided. Where it is determined that a layout design is substantially similar to another existing layout design connected to a prior registration, the Registrar shall issue a notice to both applicants affording them an opportunity for rejoinder and counter-rejoinder. The applicant seeking registration shall be deemed to have knowledge of all previously registered layout designs accessible through the public register maintained by the Office. Failure to adequately address concerns raised in the Registrar’s notice may result in rejection of the application, subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal.

Any person who, without authorization from the registered proprietor, makes, imports, distributes, sells, hires or displays a layout design connected with any other layout design shall be deemed to have infringed upon the said registered layout design. Such infringement includes the reproduction of the protected elements of the layout design in another layout design, irrespective of alterations made thereto. The Court may, subject to appeal, impose a penalty not exceeding five times the cost of infringing activities or imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or both, as deemed appropriate. Further, damages shall be awarded to the registered proprietor to compensate for loss sustained due to the infringement, calculated based on prevailing market rates and demonstrable financial detriment.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any person holding a valid registration for a layout design may grant a license conferring rights relating to the use and reproduction of that layout design connected to another party. Such licenses shall be documented in writing and specify the scope of permitted activities, including but not limited to manufacture, import, and sale of integrated circuits incorporating the registered layout design. The licensor may stipulate conditions regarding quality control and reasonable assurance of non-infringement by the licensee. Assignment of rights under this Act concerning a layout design connected is permissible, provided that such assignment is executed in accordance with procedures prescribed herein and duly registered with the Controller General. Any subsequent transfer or sub-license shall be subject to similar registration requirements as provided herein.

Where a claim is made alleging infringement of a registered layout design, the aggrieved party shall institute proceedings before the relevant jurisdictional authority as provided herein. Such claim may assert that an unauthorized person has reproduced, imitated, or otherwise exploited a layout design connected to the registered work, and further alleges substantial similarity exists between the infringing layout design and the original, thereby creating confusion amongst consumers regarding the source of the goods or services associated with said designs. The respondent shall be afforded full opportunity to present evidence rebutting this assertion; however, the authority may consider expert testimony concerning the overall impression created by each layout design in determining whether infringement has occurred, subject to principles of natural justice and due process.

For the purposes of this Act, "layout design connected" shall mean a layout design which incorporates elements derived from another layout design, where such incorporation is not merely functional and results in an overall appearance distinctly different from the original layout design. The determination of whether a layout design is “layout design connected” shall consider the degree of similarity between the two designs, taking into account any modifications or additions made to the original. An application for a patent relating to a layout design connected may be granted subject to the standard application patent period as provided herein, and only if novelty and inventive step are established.

Where any dispute arises concerning the validity of registration of a layout-design under this Act, or regarding the appointment or powers of the chairperson vice chairperson of the Design Registry, an appeal shall lie to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. The appellant may seek review of decisions made by the design registry shall pertaining to objections raised during examination or relating to rectification proceedings. Provided that such appeals must be filed within ninety days from the date of communication of the order appealed against. Further, any party aggrieved by an interim order passed during appellate proceedings may apply for a stay of such order before the Tribunal. The chairperson vice chairperson may, at their discretion, require production of further documentation to substantiate claims made in appeal.

For the purposes of this Act, “layout-design infringement” includes any act of reproduction, adaptation, or commercial exploitation of a registered layout-design without authorization from the owner, subject to exceptions as provided herein relating to acts performed solely for private use or research. Where an infringing activity has been established and damages are awarded under this Act, the Court may order that property used in connection with such infringement be subjected to committed forfeiture directed towards compensating the registered proprietor for losses sustained. Such forfeiture shall include any equipment, materials, or documentation directly involved in the creation or distribution of infringing layout-designs.

Where any proprietor establishes that a registered layout-design has been reproduced in contravention of this Act, or where such reproduction constitutes a commercial act infringing upon their exclusive rights as provided herein, the adjudicating officer may order the seizure of all infringing articles and materials used in their manufacture. Further, subject to due process and opportunity for hearing, the proprietor shall be entitled to seek a court-directed forfeiture of any equipment, software, or documentation demonstrably employed in the unauthorized reproduction. Any person found guilty of such infringement shall also be liable to pay damages equivalent to a sum not exceeding ten times the actual loss suffered by the proprietor; provided that repeat offenders may face enhanced penalties and committed forfeiture directed towards assets derived from the infringing activity.

Any licensee granted rights under a registered layout-design pursuant to a contractual agreement may, subject to the terms of such agreement, assign or pledge said license to any third party with their prior written consent from the owner of the layout-design. Provided that, where an assignment or pledge is made, the assignee or pledgee shall be bound by all covenants and restrictions contained within the original licensing agreement. Further, if the licensee defaults in performance of obligations as stipulated under this Act concerning security measures protecting the layout-design, the registered owner may initiate proceedings for committed forfeiture directed towards any licenses granted to such defaulting party. Such forfeited licenses shall revert entirely to the ownership of the layout-design proprietor and become available for re-licensing according to prevailing terms.

An application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be deemed to have been improperly filed if it contains any information indicating a prior claim or share patent relating to the same design by another party, unless such prior claim is expressly acknowledged and consented to in writing by the claimant holding that right. Upon discovery of such improper filing, the Registering Officer may issue a notice requiring the applicant to rectify the application within thirty days. Failure to comply with this notice shall result in the committed forfeiture directed by the officer; all fees paid towards registration shall be remitted to Government funds. The layout-design remains subject to challenge under this Act pending final determination of any such forfeiture proceedings.

For the purposes of this Act, a “practitioner person” means an individual who habitually and for remuneration engages in the preparation, filing, prosecution, maintenance, or conduct of applications for registration of integrated circuit layout designs, or in advising clients concerning such matters; provided that such individual possesses qualifications prescribed by the Central Government, which may include, but is not limited to, a degree in law, electrical engineering, or computer science. A practitioner person shall be deemed to be acting on behalf of their client and subject to professional privilege as provided herein. Any entity employing a practitioner person shall ensure compliance with regulations regarding conflict of interest under this Act.

An application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be accompanied by a declaration verifying the identity of the applicant and confirming their entitlement to seek protection under this Act. Where the applicant is a body corporate, the declaration must be signed by a duly authorized officer thereof. In cases where an individual engages a legal practitioner or other agent to file the application on their behalf, such practitioner shall provide particulars of their professional qualifications and registration details in a prescribed form annexed to the application. A person claiming to be a practitioner person may also submit evidence demonstrating continuous engagement in providing intellectual property advisory services for at least three years preceding the date of application, as deemed necessary by the Registrar.

Any individual who infringes upon the layout-design rights vested under this Act shall be liable for damages, which include compensation for loss of profits reasonably foreseeable as a consequence of the infringement, subject to a ceiling determined by the High Court. Where an infringement involves the reproduction of a substantial part of the layout-design, the court may also award exemplary damages not exceeding three times the amount of compensation awarded. A legal practitioner representing a claimant in proceedings relating to infringement shall be entitled to costs as determined by the court. Further, any person found to have knowingly induced or assisted in an act of infringement is deemed jointly liable with the infringing party for all remedies available under this Act. The rights of a practitioner person may be enforced against any individual directly involved in the infringing activity.

An application for registration as a practitioner person shall be made to the Controller in Form A, accompanied by an affidavit verifying the particulars furnished therein and stating that the applicant possesses the requisite qualifications and experience as may be prescribed. The applicant must demonstrate continuous engagement in activities related to semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design for a minimum period of three years immediately preceding the date of application. Any person found to have made a false statement or suppressed material information in their application shall be liable to prosecution under this Act, and the registration shall stand nullified. Upon receipt of an application, the Controller may require further documentation or clarification as deemed necessary. The applicant shall be notified of any deficiencies within sixty days; failure to rectify these within thirty days will result in rejection of the application. A register of practitioner persons shall be maintained by the Controller and made available for public inspection.

A legal practitioner engaged by an owner of integrated circuit layout designs shall be deemed to hold such engagement subject to compliance with the stipulations outlined herein. Such practitioners must maintain records detailing all consultations undertaken concerning the protection and enforcement of layout-design rights, accessible for inspection upon reasonable notice from an authorized officer. A practitioner person providing advisory services relating to infringement proceedings shall file a declaration annually confirming adherence to professional standards as prescribed by the relevant Bar Council regulations. Further, any legal practitioner representing a claimant in respect of alleged infringement must disclose all prior engagements concerning the same or related integrated circuit layout designs, provided that such disclosure does not compromise client confidentiality under this Act.

Any individual engaging in the design, manufacture, import, or distribution of semiconductor integrated circuits layouts shall be deemed a practitioner person for the purposes of this Act. Where such a practitioner person is found to have reproduced a registered layout-design without authorization, they are liable to pay damages equivalent to a sum not exceeding five times the reasonable royalty that the owner was entitled to receive, or in default thereof, imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years. Further, any entity employing a practitioner person who contravenes the provisions of this Act shall be deemed vicariously responsible and subject to similar penalties as provided herein. The Central Government may, by notification, prescribe guidelines regarding professional conduct expected from practitioners.

A practitioner person engaged in the design, manufacture, or distribution of semiconductor integrated circuits may grant licenses to utilize a layout-design for commercial purposes subject to conditions stipulated in a written agreement executed prior to any such utilization. Such agreements shall clearly define the scope of permitted use, including but not limited to manufacturing processes and geographical territories. Assignment of rights under this Act relating to a registered layout-design is permissible only with the consent of the original registrant, provided that such consent may be withheld if it would substantially prejudice the interests of the registrant or any person deriving right from them. Any transfer of ownership or control affecting a licensee’s ability to exercise their granted license shall require prior notification and approval by the registrant, as provided herein. The terms governing sub-licensing are subject to similar restrictions and may be detailed within the initial licensing agreement.

Notwithstanding anything contained herein, an appeal against any order passed by the Registrar under this Act relating to the determination of validity of a registered semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall lie to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of such order. The Tribunal may, after giving notice to all parties concerned and affording them an opportunity of being heard, confirm, modify, or reverse the order appealed against. Any party aggrieved by any order passed by the Tribunal may further appeal to the Supreme Court on a question of law arising out of the decision of the Tribunal. For the purposes of this Act, a ‘practitioner person’ includes any advocate enrolled under the Advocates Act and any individual holding a degree in law from a recognized university.

Any individual engaged in the design, manufacture, import, or distribution of semiconductor integrated circuits layouts shall be deemed a practitioner person for the purposes of this Act. A practitioner person found to have infringed upon the layout-design rights of another shall be liable for damages equivalent to the reasonable royalty that such infringer would have been willing to pay for the right to use the layout design, or in cases where such willingness cannot be ascertained, an amount determined by the court having jurisdiction, not exceeding three times the value of profits made from the infringing activity. Further, the court may order the destruction of all infringing layouts and related materials held by the infringer. This remedy is subject to the condition that the infringement was committed knowingly or with reckless disregard for the layout-design right. The aggrieved party may also seek an injunction restraining the practitioner person from further acts of infringement as provided herein.

Any individual engaging in the design, manufacture, import, or distribution of semiconductor integrated circuits layouts shall be deemed a practitioner person under this Act. Any act of unauthorized copying, reproduction, or adaptation of a registered layout-design by such a practitioner person constitutes an infringement actionable at law. Where a registered user shall discover evidence of such infringement, they may initiate civil proceedings seeking injunctive relief and damages proportionate to the loss suffered. Failure to comply with prescribed security measures relating to confidential layout-design information will attract penalties as provided herein. Furthermore, any practitioner person found guilty of wilful inducement of infringement faces enhanced financial sanctions and potential criminal prosecution subject to judicial discretion.

For the purposes of this Act, a “design agent person” means any individual who, subject to such conditions as may be prescribed, is engaged by an owner of the integrated circuit layout design for the purpose of preparing, reproducing, or otherwise utilizing that layout design; provided that such engagement shall be in writing and clearly define the scope of authority granted to the design agent person. A design agent person shall not be deemed to include a mere occasional employee performing tasks incidental to the operation of an establishment engaged primarily in activities other than integrated circuit layout-design. Any alteration or modification made by a design agent person, without express authorization from the owner, shall be considered an unauthorized act under this Act.

An application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout design shall be deemed to be filed by a design agent person where such agent acts on behalf of the original owner unless evidence is presented demonstrating otherwise. The applicant must provide, along with the prescribed fee, a detailed technical description of the layout design, including its functionality and intended use, as well as certified copies of all relevant documentation pertaining to its creation. Further, it shall be the duty of the design agent person to verify that the original owner possesses the exclusive right to apply for registration under this Act. Provided that, if an application is found to have been filed through a design agent person without proper authorization from the original owner, such registration may be challenged and revoked as provided herein.

Where any infringement of design rights under this Act is established, the aggrieved party shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief restraining the infringing conduct, subject to the provisions regarding interim orders as provided herein. Damages recoverable shall be assessed based on the loss suffered by the proprietor of the layout-design, or a reasonable royalty if the infringer proves that they were unaware and had no reason to suspect that their actions constituted an infringement. A design agent person who knowingly participates in infringing activities may also be held liable for damages, jointly and severally with the primary infringer. Furthermore, the Court may order the delivery up or destruction of any articles made in contravention of these rights. The proprietor shall have the burden of proving both the existence of the layout-design right and the infringement thereof.

Where an application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design is filed by a design agent person acting on behalf of the applicant owner, such design agent shall be required to submit with the application a power of attorney or other document demonstrating express authority from the applicant owner to act as their representative under this Act. The Registrar may require further documentation establishing the identity and address for service of the design agent person, and verification of the authenticity of the authorization provided. Any communication regarding the application shall be deemed to have been properly served upon the design agent unless otherwise notified by the applicant owner. Provided that, if the design agent ceases to act on behalf of the applicant owner prior to registration, a written notice thereof must be submitted to the Registrar within thirty days; failing which, the application may be subject to rejection or other action as deemed appropriate by the Registrar.

A design agent person engaged by an owner of the intellectual property rights in a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be deemed to act on behalf of, and for the benefit of, that owner unless evidence is presented demonstrating otherwise. Such agents are obligated to adhere strictly to all confidentiality agreements executed between themselves and the owner concerning the layout-design. The performance of duties by a design agent person does not relieve the owner from responsibility under this Act relating to infringement or unauthorized reproduction. Further, any contract entered into by a design agent person pertaining to the layout-design shall be valid only if it explicitly states that the agent acts as such and identifies the principal for whom they are acting. The owner may terminate the engagement of a design agent person subject to providing thirty days’ written notice.

Any individual acting on behalf of an owner of a registered semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be deemed a design agent person for the purposes of this Act, subject to fulfilling the conditions prescribed under these regulations. Such a design agent person shall be held strictly liable for any infringement committed by them in the course of their duties, unless they demonstrate reasonable diligence to prevent such infringement. Failure to report suspected infringements to the owner, or deliberate acts facilitating unauthorized reproduction, shall attract penalties as provided herein. The owner may pursue civil remedies against both the infringing party and the design agent person jointly and severally. Any individual falsely representing themselves as a design agent person with intent to deceive is liable for prosecution under this Act.

Where a design agent person has been engaged by an owner of integrated circuit layout designs to perform services relating to the creation, modification, or commercialization of such designs, any assignment of rights arising from those services shall be subject to the provisions herein. The agreement between the owner and the design agent person may explicitly define the scope of assignable rights, including but not limited to reproduction, adaptation, and distribution. Provided that such agreement clearly identifies the specific layout-design works affected by the assignment, the owner retains the right to grant non-exclusive licenses under those assigned rights for a period not exceeding five years from the date of initial commercialization, subject to royalty payments to the design agent person as stipulated in the original engagement contract. Further, any subsequent assignments by the owner shall be disclosed to the design agent person and may require their consent if they impact pre-existing contractual obligations.

Where any act relating to the registration of a layout-design is performed by a design agent person, the liability for any errors or omissions committed in such performance shall be borne solely by the said design agent person, subject to the provisions regarding vicarious liability under this Act. An aggrieved party may appeal against any decision concerning the actions of a design agent person to the relevant Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of communication of that decision. Provided that, if the act was performed pursuant to express instructions received in writing from the applicant or registered proprietor, the responsibility for such errors shall be jointly borne by both parties unless it is demonstrated that the design agent person acted fraudulently or negligently beyond the scope of their mandate.

Where any infringement of design rights under this Act is established, the owner shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief restraining the infringing party from further acts of reproduction, adaptation, or commercial exploitation of the registered layout-design. Damages recoverable shall include compensation for loss resulting from the infringement, encompassing lost profits and reasonable royalties which the owner would have received had the infringement not occurred. The right to claim damages is subject to the condition that the owner has diligently prosecuted their application for registration and maintained the register references pertaining thereto. A design agent person acting on behalf of an owner shall be jointly liable with the owner for any wilful or negligent acts leading to such infringement, provided that the agent acted outside the scope of their authorized mandate.

Where any individual acting on behalf of an applicant for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout design is designated as a design agent person, such designation shall be recorded in the Register maintained under this Act. The application form submitted by the applicant shall clearly identify the name and address of each design agent person involved in the preparation or submission of the application. Any alteration to the designation of a design agent person after the initial filing requires prior written notification to the Controller, accompanied by an affidavit verifying the change. The Controller may request further documentation substantiating the authority granted to such design agent person to act on behalf of the applicant. Applications relating registered layout designs shall be processed according to established procedures as provided herein. Any communication pertaining to the application or registration shall be deemed validly served upon either the applicant or the designated design agent person, subject to any specific instructions given by the applicant in writing.

For the purposes of this Act, a "practitioner person registered" means an individual who is duly admitted to practice law under the Advocates Act, 1961, and who has applied for and been granted registration as a Layout-Design Agent in accordance with the prescribed procedures; provided that such registration shall be contingent upon verification by the Controller of satisfactory knowledge of semiconductor technology. A practitioner person registered may undertake activities relating to the preparation, filing, or prosecution of applications for layout-design protection, subject to adherence to ethical guidelines as determined under this Act and any relevant rules framed thereunder. The term does not include individuals engaged solely in administrative support roles.

An application for registration of a layout-design shall be accompanied by a declaration verifying the originality of the design and confirming that the applicant is either a legal practitioner, or a person registered in the prescribed manner as a layout-design agent, or a person in the sole and regular employment of the principal. The Registrar may require further documentation to establish the applicant’s entitlement under this Act, including proof of prior use or publication, provided that such requirements shall be reasonable and proportionate to the complexity of the design involved. A practitioner person registered as an agent shall adhere to a code of conduct prescribed by the Controller, failure to do so rendering them liable for disciplinary action and potential revocation of registration.

Where a practitioner person registered under this Act discovers an infringement of any right conferred by registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design, such practitioner may institute civil proceedings for redressal of damages sustained as a direct consequence of that infringement. The measure of damages shall be determined in accordance with principles of fairness and equity, taking into consideration the lost profits attributable to the infringing activity, reasonable royalty fees which would have been payable had a license been granted, and any other relevant factors deemed pertinent by the adjudicating authority. Provided that, where the infringement was committed wilfully or for fraudulent purposes, the court may award punitive damages not exceeding three times the amount of compensation otherwise determined. Subject to appeal to the appellate tribunal, orders regarding damages shall be binding on all parties involved in the proceedings.

A practitioner person registered under this Act shall be deemed to possess specialized knowledge relevant to the assessment of infringement claims pertaining to semiconductor integrated circuit layout designs. Any application for registration as a practitioner person must include detailed particulars regarding their qualifications, experience in intellectual property law, and any prior disciplinary actions taken against them by professional bodies. The Controller may require such applicant to appear before an examining officer at a time and place specified in the notice, and tender evidence substantiating the claims made in the application. Failure to comply with this requirement shall render the application liable for rejection. Furthermore, a practitioner person registered under this Act is obligated to maintain records of all consultations undertaken and make them available for inspection by the Controller upon request. This provision applies without prejudice to any confidentiality agreements entered into independently by the practitioner person.

A practitioner person registered under this Act shall be deemed to possess specialized knowledge relating to semiconductor integrated circuit layout-designs and their protection. Such registration is contingent upon demonstrating competence through an examination administered by the Controller and maintaining continuing professional development credits as prescribed, failing which the registration may be suspended. The applicant for registration must provide proof of relevant academic qualifications or equivalent practical experience, subject to verification by the Controller. A registered practitioner person shall adhere to a code of conduct outlining ethical obligations concerning confidentiality and fair representation of clients’ interests. Any deviation from this code, determined through inquiry initiated by the Controller, may result in disciplinary action including revocation of registration.

Any practitioner person registered under this Act who knowingly makes, for commercial purposes, an integrated circuit embodying any element substantially copied from a protected layout design shall be liable to pay damages equivalent to five times the cost of implementing the infringing layout design, or such higher amount as the Controller deems just and reasonable, subject to a maximum penalty not exceeding ten per cent of the infringer’s turnover in India for the preceding year. Furthermore, any person found guilty of contravention of provisions relating to reverse engineering without authorization shall be deemed to have committed an offence cognizable under this Act and may face imprisonment extending up to three years, or a fine which may extend to one million rupees, or both, as determined by the appropriate judicial forum.

A practitioner person registered under this Act may grant a non-exclusive license to utilize a registered integrated circuit layout design for the purpose of manufacturing semiconductor devices, subject to the terms and conditions stipulated in the written agreement executed between the licensor and licensee. Such agreements shall clearly define the scope of permitted use, including but not limited to geographical territory and field of application. Assignment of rights under this Act relating to a registered layout-design is permissible with prior notification to the Controller, who may require submission of documentation verifying due diligence regarding any existing licenses granted. Further, where a licensee sub-licenses the design, they shall ensure that the original licensor receives equitable consideration as provided herein and documented in the sub-licensing agreement. Any alteration made to the layout-design by the licensee requires prior consent from the registered owner.

Where any dispute arises concerning whether an individual qualifies as a practitioner person registered under this Act, the determination shall be made by the Controller based on evidence demonstrating continuous engagement in activities directly related to the creation, protection, or enforcement of layout-design rights. An appeal against such determination may be filed within sixty days from the date of notification of the order before the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. Provided that, if the appellant demonstrates exceptional circumstances preventing timely filing, the Tribunal may condone the delay. The Controller shall consider representations made by both parties and any expert testimony submitted, ensuring a fair opportunity for all involved to present their case. Decisions on appeals are final subject to further appeal to the High Court under established procedures.

Where a practitioner person registered under this Act alleges infringement of a registered semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design, they shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief restraining further acts of reproduction, adaptation, or commercial exploitation without authorization. Such injunction may include orders prohibiting the import, sale, or distribution of infringing products subject to demonstrating reasonable prospects of success in establishing infringement. The right to damages shall accrue to the registered owner, calculated as the greater of the actual loss suffered by them or a royalty determined based on prevailing industry rates for similar layout-designs. An application registration may be challenged within ninety days from its publication if it is shown that the design was substantially similar to an earlier unregistered layout-design. Provided that any such challenge fails, subsequent actions for infringement will not be barred.

Any practitioner person registered under this Act who knowingly makes or causes to be made any unauthorized copy of a registered integrated circuit layout design shall be liable for damages proportionate to the loss suffered by the owner of the layout-design, not exceeding an amount equivalent to ten times the cost of creating such layout-design. The rules carry provisions prescribing procedures for determining said damages and may specify factors considered in assessing reasonable royalties where applicable. Further, any person found guilty of contravention of this Act shall be subject to a penalty as determined by the Controller, which may include imprisonment for a term not less than six months but which may extend to three years, alongside a monetary fine.

A practitioner person registered under this Act may grant a license to utilize a protected integrated circuit layout design subject to the terms and conditions stipulated in a written agreement executed by both parties. Such licenses shall be assignable, either wholly or partially, provided that any such assignment is recorded with the Controller of Layout-Designs within thirty days of its execution; failure to do so renders the assignee liable for penalties as prescribed herein. Further, where a license granted includes rights relating to manufacture, the licensor shall retain the right to audit the licensee’s production records to ensure compliance with the licensed quantity and quality standards. A patent shall not be deemed to invalidate an existing layout design registration merely by virtue of similarity in functionality; however, any infringement proceedings arising from such patents will be adjudicated independently under relevant intellectual property laws.

For the purposes of this Act, a ‘practitioner’ means any individual who, by virtue of their education, training, or experience, is engaged in providing advice, representation, or assistance relating to semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design matters. This includes, but is not limited to, individuals holding qualifications recognized under the Advocates Act, 1961, engineers registered with a prescribed body, and patent agents duly authorized as provided herein. A person shall be deemed a practitioner even if they are employed by an organization offering such services, subject to them performing duties directly related to layout-design matters. Nothing in this definition shall extend to individuals providing purely clerical or administrative support.

An application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout design shall be deemed to be filed by a legal practitioner representing the applicant, provided that such practitioner is duly authorized in writing by the owner of the layout-design. The authorization must specify the particular layout-design being registered and remain on file with the Layout-Design Registry. Where an application is filed through a person other than the owner, documentation establishing ownership or right to apply shall be submitted alongside the application. Any alteration to details furnished in the initial application, including changes in representation by a legal practitioner, requires notification to the Registrar within thirty days of such change. Failure to adhere to this provision may result in rejection of the layout-design for registration as provided herein.

Where any infringement of layout-design rights has occurred, the owner shall be entitled to seek remedies under this Act including an injunction restraining further acts of infringement and recovery of damages sustained by reason thereof. Damages shall be assessed at such amount as may be determined by the competent court, taking into account the loss of profits suffered by the owner and any measure of reasonable royalties that would have been payable had the infringing conduct occurred under a license granted by the owner. A legal practitioner representing an aggrieved party in proceedings relating to infringement may recover their reasonable costs incurred in such representation, subject to just terms as determined by the court. Further, where an infringer has knowingly or wilfully engaged in acts of infringement, the court may award punitive damages not exceeding three times the amount of actual damages proven.

An application for registration as a practitioner may be made to the Controller in the form specified in Form D, accompanied by an affidavit verifying the particulars stated therein and stating that the applicant possesses the requisite qualifications and experience as determined under this Act. The prescribed fee shall be remitted along with the application. Upon receipt of such application, the Controller shall issue notice to the applicant directing him or her to appear before the Controller at a time and place specified in the notice for examination regarding his or her knowledge of semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design and related legal principles. Failure to attend the hearing without reasonable cause, as determined by the Controller, may result in rejection of the application. A practitioner found to be lacking in requisite qualifications is liable to have their registration suspended.

A legal practitioner engaged by an owner of integrated circuit layout designs for the purpose of preparing, filing, prosecuting, or maintaining applications relating to registration under this Act shall be deemed to be acting as an agent of the owner only insofar as such actions are directly connected with the aforementioned processes. Provided that, a practitioner’s compliance with clauses (a) and (b) of section 18 regarding confidentiality obligations remains absolute; any breach thereof will constitute a violation subject to penalties as provided herein. Furthermore, where a legal practitioner advises on matters pertaining to infringement or validity of registered layout designs, they must maintain detailed records of all consultations and correspondence for inspection by the Controller upon reasonable notice. The owner shall be responsible for ensuring that their practitioner adheres strictly to these stipulations.

Any individual engaging in the design, manufacture, import, or distribution of semiconductor integrated circuits layouts shall be deemed to be within the purview of this Act and subject to its provisions regarding infringement. Where an act of infringement is suspected, any aggrieved party may initiate proceedings before the relevant jurisdictional authority, presenting evidence demonstrating substantial similarity between the alleged infringing layout and the registered layout-design. Failure to comply with prescribed standards for quality control or accurate record keeping relating to semiconductor layouts shall be deemed a violation, punishable by fines not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees. A legal practitioner representing an aggrieved party may submit expert testimony regarding technical aspects of integrated circuit design, subject to verification under this Act.

A legal practitioner engaged by an owner of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be permitted to grant non-exclusive licenses relating to the design under this Act, provided that such license is executed in writing and specifies the scope of use, duration, and any associated royalties payable to the owner. Any assignment of rights in a layout-design undertaken by a practitioner on behalf of their client shall require prior written consent from the owner, unless explicitly authorized within a pre-existing contractual agreement. Further, where a legal practitioner acts as an agent for multiple owners concerning related integrated circuit designs, they must ensure that no conflict of interest arises which could prejudice the rights or interests of any such owner. The owner may, at their discretion, choose to retain exclusive control over licensing and assignment decisions despite engagement of a practitioner; this choice shall be documented in writing.

Where any question arises regarding whether an individual qualifies as a practitioner for the purposes of bringing an action under this Act, the determination shall be made by the relevant jurisdictional authority, subject to appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. An individual claiming status as a practitioner must demonstrate, through documented evidence and testimony, consistent engagement in advising or representing clients concerning matters relating to semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design rights. It is provided that mere possession of a law degree or engineering qualification shall not, by itself, establish such status; practical experience and demonstrable expertise are essential considerations. The authority may require the production of client contracts, correspondence, and other relevant materials in assessing eligibility, and any challenge to this determination may be appealed on grounds of procedural fairness or misinterpretation of the criteria as provided herein.

A legal practitioner engaged by an integrated circuit design house shall be deemed to hold confidential information pertaining to any layout design work undertaken for that house, subject to compliance with the non-disclosure agreements executed between the practitioner and their client. Such confidentiality obligations remain enforceable notwithstanding the termination of the employment or contractual relationship, provided that such termination does not arise from a breach by the design house itself. The term of patent protection granted under this Act shall not extend beyond twenty years from the date of filing the application; however, any information disclosed by a practitioner in good faith during proceedings related to validity challenges may be admissible as evidence. Further, a practitioner found to have wilfully violated these confidentiality provisions is liable for damages and injunctive relief as provided herein.

Any individual engaging in the design, manufacture, import, or distribution of semiconductor integrated circuits layouts shall maintain an entry register document detailing all practitioners employed by them, including their qualifications and areas of specialization. Failure to do so constitutes a violation under this Act and is subject to a penalty not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees for the first offence, and one million rupees for subsequent offences. Any person found to be employing a practitioner without proper registration or verification as recorded in the entry register document shall also be liable to pay a fine of two hundred fifty thousand rupees. The Registering Authority may conduct inspections at any time to ensure compliance with these provisions; obstruction of such inspection is punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than six months.

For the purposes of this Act, “layout-design” means the three dimensional representation of any integrated circuit embodied in a mask; provided that such representation is defined by the arrangement, however expressed, of active and passive components and interconnections on an integrated circuit, and does not include features solely for mechanical support or interconnection with external connectors. A person shall be deemed to have made an application for design apply registration when such application contains all particulars as may be prescribed; further, a layout-design is considered registered upon the grant of a certificate of registration by the Registrar, subject to any appeals under this Act.

An application for design apply registration shall be made to the Controller in the prescribed form and shall contain such particulars relating to the applicant, the layout-design, and its intended use as may be required by the regulations. The applicant shall furnish a representation of the layout-design, either in the form of drawings, photographs, or other visual media deemed appropriate by the Controller. Where an application relates to more than one layout-design, each design shall be treated separately for the purposes of examination and registration. Any person claiming right to apply for registration may do so subject to demonstrating a valid assignment or contractual agreement as provided herein. The Controller may require further documentation substantiating ownership claims before proceeding with the assessment of the application.

An application for design apply registration shall be made to the Controller in such form and manner as may be prescribed, containing particulars verifying ownership and detailing the features of the integrated circuit layout-design sought to be protected. The applicant shall furnish a sworn statement attesting to the originality of the layout-design and affirming that it does not infringe upon any prior rights. Upon receipt of an application, the Controller may require further clarification or modifications as deemed necessary for compliance with this Act.

The design apply registration process includes examination by the Controller to ascertain whether the layout-design is capable of registration under this Act, subject to provisions regarding novelty and distinctiveness. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Controller relating to an application may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of such decision. The Registrar shall maintain a register of registered layout-designs accessible for public inspection, as provided herein.

An application for design apply registration shall be accompanied by such particulars, drawings and other documents as the Controller may prescribe, demonstrating clearly the originality of the layout-design and its conformity with the requirements set out in Schedule A. The applicant shall furnish an affidavit verifying the correctness of the information contained therein, attesting to their exclusive right over the claimed design. Provided that, where a layout-design incorporates elements already disclosed publicly prior to the date of application, such disclosure shall not prejudice registration if it can be demonstrated that the overall arrangement and combination constitutes a novel contribution as provided herein. Any alteration made to the registered layout-design after its initial registration is subject to further review and approval by the Controller.

Any person who knowingly makes, uses, imports, or offers to sell any integrated circuit layout-design infringing a registered design shall be liable to pay damages equivalent to the loss suffered by the proprietor of the design, and may also be subject to a further penalty not exceeding five times the value of such infringing goods. The Central Government may, upon receiving a complaint from the proprietor of a registered design, issue an injunction restraining any person from engaging in acts that constitute infringement as provided herein. Failure to comply with such an injunction shall render the offender liable for contempt of court and subject to imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year. A design apply registration is deemed invalid if it does not meet the novelty requirements outlined under this Act.

Any person claiming right in a design applied for registration, or who is the absolute assignee of such right, may grant a license conferring upon the licensee the right to make, use, sell, offer for sale, or import any product incorporating the registered layout-design, subject to the terms and conditions stipulated therein. Such licenses shall be assignable, provided that notice of assignment is furnished in writing to the Controller within thirty days of the transfer. The proprietor of a design may also grant an exclusive license, restricting all other exploitation of the design during the term specified; however, such exclusivity shall not prejudice any prior rights or licenses granted under this Act. Further, any subsequent assignee of a layout-design registration shall be deemed to hold the right to grant further licenses consistent with the original design apply registration and as provided herein.

An application for design apply registration shall be deemed invalid if it is shown, upon appeal, that the layout-design was substantially similar to an earlier unregistered layout-design which had been publicly disclosed in India prior to the date of application, provided that the applicant demonstrates diligent efforts to ascertain the existence of such prior disclosure. The Appellate Intellectual Property Tribunal may allow a design apply registration where the similarity is demonstrably coincidental or arises from functional requirements inherent in the nature of the integrated circuit. Any party aggrieved by an order refusing registration under this Act may appeal to the Tribunal within sixty days, subject to payment of prescribed fees and furnishing security for costs as determined by the Tribunal.

An application for design apply registration shall be made in the prescribed form and shall contain such particulars relating to the applicant, the layout-design and its intended use as may be required by the regulations framed under this Act. The applicant shall furnish a representation of the layout-design, being either drawings or photographs, sufficient to enable an adjudicating officer to assess its originality and novelty. Where an application relates to more than one layout-design, each design shall be treated separately for the purposes of registration. Any person claiming right to apply for registration may do so subject to providing satisfactory evidence of such right as provided herein. The Registrar may require the applicant to submit further information or clarification concerning the layout-design and its features.

The central government may grant licenses to any person holding an extant Plant Variety Approval, enabling them to commercially utilize protected plant varieties for research purposes or for the development of new, derived varieties, subject to such terms and conditions as it deems fit. Any assignment of rights pertaining to a registered plant variety, including but not limited to the right to produce, sell, export, or import seeds, shall require prior approval from the central government, ensuring equitable benefit-sharing arrangements with any original breeder or contributor identified under this Act. Such approvals may be conditional upon adherence to specific labeling requirements and reporting obligations concerning the continued propagation of the variety. Furthermore, a licensee may sub-license rights relating to derived varieties only after obtaining written consent from the holder of the primary Plant Variety Approval and subsequent approval central government sanction.

An application for registration of a plant variety shall include detailed particulars regarding its genetic composition, expression phenotype, and method of propagation, as prescribed by the Regulations. Upon receipt of such an application, the Central Government shall initiate a process of technical examination, involving assessment against established criteria for novelty, distinctiveness, uniformity, and stability. The applicant shall be afforded an opportunity to present arguments and data in response to any objections raised during this evaluation.
