Further, where an application for cancellation registration is filed against a layout-design, any pending license agreements or assignments shall remain valid and enforceable until such cancellation becomes final and binding. The registered proprietor retains the right to revoke licenses or rescind assignments if they materially prejudice the validity of the underlying registration.

An application for the cancellation of registration of a layout-design may be presented to the Controller by any person claiming an interest adversely affected by the said registration. Such application shall specify the grounds upon which it is based, and shall include all relevant documents or other evidence relied on in support thereof; provided that the mere existence of prior use of a similar integrated circuit layout-design does not, of itself, constitute sufficient ground for cancellation under this Act. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish further particulars or evidence as deemed necessary. Upon receiving such an application, the Controller shall serve notice upon the registrant and afford them an opportunity to be heard, subject to the provisions regarding timelines as provided herein. Any order made by the Controller relating to cancellation registration is subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal.

An application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design incorporating a computer programme may be subject to an action for cancellation by any person alleging that the design does not satisfy the requirements of originality as provided herein. Such an action shall only be maintainable if the applicant has failed to demonstrate, through appropriate documentation and technical specifications, that the layout-design constitutes a novel work independent from pre-existing integrated circuits or computer programmes. The Registering Authority may require further evidence during proceedings relating to cancellation registration, including expert testimony regarding the inventive step involved in creating the design. Any order for cancellation shall be published in the Official Gazette, and the applicant shall have the right to appeal under this Act.

An application for the cancellation registration of a layout-design may be presented to the Controller by any person claiming an interest or being adversely affected by the registration. Such application shall state the grounds upon which it is based, and shall specify the facts made known to the applicant. The Controller shall give notice of the application to the registered proprietor, who shall be afforded a reasonable opportunity of being heard in his defense, subject to Common Regulations regarding procedural fairness. If, after considering all evidence presented, the Controller finds that any ground for cancellation exists under this Act, he may order the registration to be cancelled wholly or in part. The effect of such an order is that the layout-design ceases to be protected as a registered design from the date specified in the order.

For the purposes of this Act, “layout design appellate authority” means a body established by notification in the Official Gazette to hear and dispose of appeals arising from orders passed by the Registrar or other officers authorized under this Act. The layout design appellate authority shall consist of a Chairperson who is a retired Judge of a High Court or a person having experience in intellectual property law, and such other members as the Central Government may deem fit, subject to the provisions regarding qualifications and tenure as provided herein. Decisions of the layout design appellate authority shall be binding on all parties involved, and appeals from those decisions may be made to the relevant High Court within ninety days.

An application for registration of a layout design shall include a detailed description of the features defining the integrated circuit and its intended functionality, accompanied by requisite drawings conforming to standards prescribed by the Controller. The Registrar may require further clarification or modifications to ensure compliance with these requirements prior to acceptance of the application. Upon receipt of an objection from any interested party regarding the novelty or originality of the layout design as claimed in the application, a notice shall be served upon the applicant and the matter referred for determination under this Act. Any aggrieved person dissatisfied with a decision concerning registration, rejection, or revocation may appeal to the Layout Design Appellate Board. The appellate board’s order shall be binding and final subject to further appeals as provided herein.

Where a registered layout design is alleged to have been infringed, the owner may institute proceedings before the Layout Design Appellate Tribunal seeking remedies as provided herein. Such proceedings shall be commenced within three years from the date of the infringing act coming to the knowledge of the registrant. The Tribunal may grant such relief as it deems just and equitable, including but not limited to injunctions restraining further acts of infringement, damages proportionate to the loss suffered by the owner, and costs incidental to the litigation. Any party aggrieved by an order made under this Act by the Registrar relating to registration or any other matter may appeal to the Layout Design Appellate Tribunal. The appellate tribunal shall consider all relevant evidence presented before it and may affirm, reverse, or modify the order appealed from.

Where an appeal lies from any order passed by the Registrar relating to the registration or rejection of a layout design, or concerning infringement proceedings initiated under this Act, the aggrieved party shall have the right to prefer an appeal to the Layout Design Appellate Board. Such appeals must be filed within sixty days from the date of communication of the order appealed against. The Board may, after giving notice to all parties concerned and affording them opportunities for being heard, confirm, modify, or reverse the order appealed from, as it deems fit. Any party aggrieved by an order passed by the Appellate Board may further appeal to the High Court within a period of ninety days, subject to such penalties as are prescribed herein.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, the registered owner of a layout design may grant licenses conferring rights to use or reproduce the said design, either in whole or in part, for specific purposes or territories. Such licenses shall be documented in writing and may be assigned freely, provided that any assignment is notified to the Controller within thirty days of its execution. Where an application for a license involves a layout design subject to a prior registered layout design, consent from the original proprietor must be obtained unless such use falls under fair dealing provisions as defined herein. Any dispute arising concerning the validity or enforceability of a license agreement relating to a layout design shall be referred to a Layout Design Appellate Board for determination, and its decision shall be binding on all parties involved.

Where an appeal arises from an order passed by the Registrar refusing registration of a layout design, or revoking a registered layout design, the aggrieved party may prefer an appeal to the Layout Design Appellate Board. Such appeals shall be filed within sixty days from the date of communication of the order appealed against. The appellate board shall consider all relevant evidence presented by both the appellant and the respondent, including expert testimony pertaining to originality and freedom from prior publication as required under this Act. Decisions of the Layout Design Appellate Board are final subject to further appeal only on a point of law before the High Court. The Board may allow or dismiss an appeal, or make such other order as it deems just and equitable in the circumstances.

An appeal against an order passed by the Registrar refusing registration of a layout design may be made to the Layout Design Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order. The appellant shall, along with the memorandum of appeal, pay such fee as may be prescribed under this Act. Provided that if the Appellant demonstrates satisfactory cause for failing to comply with the time limit specified herein, the Tribunal may entertain the appeal. The Tribunal shall give notice to the Registrar and afford him an opportunity of being heard. Subject to compliance with all applicable regulations regarding procedural fairness, the tribunal’s decision on any such appeal is final. Any party aggrieved by an order of the Layout Design Appellate Tribunal may further appeal to a High Court.

An application for registration of a layout-design may be subject to cancellation by the Controller if it is found to lack novelty or originality as defined under this Act. Any person aggrieved by an order of the Controller refusing registration, or by any condition imposed on the registration, shall have the right to appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. The tribunal shall give notice to the applicant and the registered proprietor, respectively, before hearing any such appeal. Further, a registered layout-design may be subject to cancellation sub section if it is subsequently determined that it infringes upon an earlier, unregistered layout-design which was publicly available prior to the date of application for registration.

An application for an order concerning the rectification or cancellation of registration may be made by any person alleging that the registered layout-design does not satisfy the requirements of section 13. Such applications shall specify the grounds upon which it is based, and must include relevant documentary evidence supporting the claim. Where an order cancellation sub has been issued under this Act, the Central Government may, subject to just cause and after affording the registrant a reasonable opportunity for being heard, review such order. Any party aggrieved by any decision made under this provision may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal as provided herein.

An application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design may be cancelled by the Registrar if it is found that the applicant has failed to disclose material information relevant to the determination of originality, or if the layout-design incorporates elements copied from an unregistered layout-design in violation of principles of fair use. Such cancellation shall only occur after due notice is served upon the applicant and a reasonable opportunity afforded for them to present their objections. Any cancellation of the registration of a layout-design either in whole or in part under this Act, following such objection process, shall be subject to review by the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. The order cancellation sub will remain in effect until further direction from the Tribunal.

An application for an order cancellation relating to the registered layout-design pertaining to a microchip may be presented before the Controller by any person claiming interest in the design or alleging that the registration was obtained through fraud, misrepresentation, or substantial invalidity. The Controller shall serve notice upon the registrant of the layout-design and provide them with a reasonable opportunity to submit their response to the application, as provided herein. Upon consideration of the application and the registrant’s reply, if any, the Controller may direct the presentation of evidence by either party. Any order cancellation sub arising from such proceedings shall be subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days of its communication to the parties involved. The Controller shall record reasons for the decision in writing, which shall be made available to both the applicant and the registrant.

An application for an order cancellation relating to a registered integrated circuit layout-design may be filed with the Controller by any person claiming title or interest adversely affected by the registration. Such application shall specify, with particularity, the grounds upon which the cancellation is sought, demonstrating non-compliance with requirements under this Act pertaining to originality and freedom from prior publication. The Controller shall afford the registrant a reasonable opportunity for presenting its response and evidence in rebuttal of the claims made within the application. Any order cancellation sub granted by the Controller shall be subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal as provided herein, and such appeal must be filed within ninety days from the date of receipt of the order.

Where an order for infringement has been passed by the Controller and subsequently subjected to review resulting in a finding of error, the aggrieved party may apply to the Intellectual Property Tribunal for an order cancellation sub of the original determination. Such application shall be accompanied by a detailed statement outlining the grounds upon which the initial order is deemed flawed, supported by relevant evidence and legal arguments. The Tribunal may, after affording all parties a reasonable opportunity for hearing, confirm, vary or annul the Controller’s decision. Any party dissatisfied with an order cancellation sub made by the Intellectual Property Tribunal may appeal to the High Court within sixty days of such order, subject to imposition of costs as deemed appropriate by the court.

The registered proprietor of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design may, subject to the provisions herein relating to public interest and national security, grant exclusive licenses for the exploitation of their design, including rights to manufacture integrated circuits incorporating the design. Such licenses shall be assignable in whole or in part, provided that any assignment is recorded with the Controller of Layout-Designs within thirty days of its execution. Where a license granted under this Act contains provisions relating to sub-licensing, such provisions shall be binding on subsequent licensees and enforceable as if they were conditions precedent to the original grant. Any cancellation of the registration of a layout-design under this Act, specifically through an order cancellation sub arising from infringement proceedings, shall not affect existing licenses or assignments unless expressly stipulated within the terms of those agreements. The Controller may issue guidelines regarding the form and content of license agreements as provided herein.

An order for cancellation of registration pertaining to a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design may be passed by the Controller if it is established that the design was copied from an earlier unregistered layout-design, provided that the claimant demonstrating such copying satisfies the evidentiary burden as prescribed under this Act. The Controller shall afford the registered proprietor an opportunity of being heard and presenting counter-evidence before passing any order for cancellation. Any claims made regarding prior use or publication of a substantially similar layout-design shall be scrutinized with particular regard to demonstrable commercial exploitation and public accessibility. Further, such an order cancellation sub will only be valid if it is accompanied by a reasoned written judgment detailing the specific grounds upon which the determination was based.

Where an order for the rectification of a registered layout-design has been made by the Controller under this Act, and that order effects a *order cancellation sub* in respect of all or part of the design, any party aggrieved by such decision may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. The Tribunal shall give notice to the International Bureau as provided herein, affording it an opportunity to submit observations on the rectification order. Failure to comply with this requirement shall render the Tribunal’s subsequent determination voidable. Any penalty for non-compliance with directions issued by the Tribunal in respect of such notification shall be determined according to regulations framed under this Act. The aggrieved party must demonstrate demonstrable prejudice resulting from the rectification, subject to procedural fairness considerations.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, an owner of a registered integrated circuit layout-design may grant licenses conferring rights to utilize the design, including but not limited to reproduction, adaptation, and commercial exploitation. Such licenses shall be assignable in accordance with contractual agreements, provided that any assignment must be recorded with the Registrar within thirty days of execution. Further, where a license is granted for a term exceeding five years, the terms and conditions thereof shall be disclosed to the licensee in writing. Any cancellation of the registration of a layout-design under this Act, including an order cancellation sub arising from infringement proceedings, shall not prejudice existing licenses unless explicitly stated within the cancellation order itself. The registrar statement shall clearly indicate the effective date of such cancellations for all relevant parties.

An application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design may be cancelled by the Registrar if it is established that the applicant has presented false information or engaged in falsifying trade concerning the originality of the design. Such cancellation shall only occur after due opportunity has been afforded to the applicant under this Act, including the presentation of evidence and arguments. Any subsequent order cancellation sub regarding a layout-design registration may be appealed before the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal as provided herein. The tribunal’s decision shall be final subject to appeal to the Supreme Court on a point of law.

Where an infringement action is brought before a competent court and the defendant challenges the validity of the registered layout-design, the court may issue a register effect order. Such an order shall direct that for the purposes of determining liability in respect of the alleged infringement, the layout-design shall be treated as if it were not registered until the challenge to registration is resolved by the relevant authority. This determination shall be without prejudice to any other ground upon which the defendant may seek to avoid liability under this Act. The register effect order remains in force pending a final decision on the validity of the registration, subject to such conditions as the court deems appropriate.

Where an application for registration of a layout-design has been granted and subsequently challenged before the relevant authority, the applicant may seek interim protection through a register effect order. Such an order shall be issued by the Controller if it appears likely that the validity of the registered layout-design is disputed based on grounds relating to prior publication or lack of originality as provided herein. The register effect order will operate as if the registration were fully effective from the date of application, preventing exploitation of the design by any person other than the registrant during the pendency of the challenge. This protection shall remain in force until a final determination is made regarding the layout-design’s validity under this Act, subject to just terms and conditions imposed by the Controller.

Where an infringement of a registered layout-design has occurred, the owner may apply to the relevant civil court for a register effect order restraining the infringer from further acts of reproduction or exploitation. Such application shall be made within three years from the date of the first ascertained instance of infringement under this Act. The court may, upon being satisfied that substantial damage has been caused to the registered layout-design owner by the infringing activity, grant an order directing the infringing party to account for profits derived from the unauthorized use, even if those profits are not directly attributable to sales in India. Provided that, a register effect order shall only be granted where the court is convinced that monetary damages alone would not provide adequate relief. The court may also award costs and such other remedies as it deems just and equitable, subject to principles of natural justice.

Where an application for registration of a layout-design is opposed, the Controller may, subject to the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder, issue a temporary register effect order pending determination of the opposition. Such order shall remain in force for a period not exceeding ninety days from the date of its issuance, or until the disposal of the opposition, whichever occurs earlier. The Controller shall provide notice to all interested parties before issuing any such order, and may require them to submit written arguments within thirty days. Any party aggrieved by the temporary register effect order may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. The tribunal’s decision on an appeal under this Act shall be binding on the Controller. Further, the Controller may, at any time, revoke a temporary register effect order if satisfied that it was issued without due consideration of relevant facts.

Where an infringement of a registered layout design occurs, the Controller may, upon application by the registered proprietor and subject to compliance with prescribed procedures, issue a register effect order directing any person found to be exploiting the infringing layout design to cease such exploitation immediately. Such cessation shall include halting production, distribution, offer for sale, or importation of integrated circuits incorporating the infringing elements. The Controller shall provide all parties concerned with an opportunity to present their case and submit evidence before issuing this order; provided that the register effect order shall not prejudice any right of action available under other provisions of this Act relating to damages or injunctions. Further, compliance with a register effect order is mandatory for all relevant entities involved in the manufacture or supply chain.

Where an infringement of a registered layout-design occurs, the Controller may, subject to due process and upon application by the registrant, issue a register effect order directing any person found to be engaging in infringing activities to cease production, distribution, or importation of the infringing integrated circuit. Such order shall specify the precise layout-design infringed and detail the nature of the infringing acts. Failure to comply with a register effect order may result in penalties as provided herein, including fines not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees and imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years. The Controller shall provide an opportunity for any party affected by the proposed order to be heard before issuing it, ensuring fairness and adherence to principles of natural justice.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, the registered proprietor of a layout-design may grant licenses granting rights to use or exploit the design, including the right to manufacture integrated circuits incorporating the protected layout. Such licenses shall be assignable in accordance with standard commercial practice, provided that any assignment is recorded with the Controller of Layout-Designs within three months of its execution. Where a registered proprietor fails to comply with the terms of a license, and the licensee provides evidence thereof, the Controller may issue a register effect order suspending the proprietor’s exclusive rights for a period not exceeding one year. This suspension shall only apply to the specific infringing activity detailed in the complaint filed by the licensee. The Controller shall provide the registered proprietor an opportunity to be heard before issuing any such order.

Where an aggrieved party disputes the validity of a register effect order granted pursuant to this Act, they may appeal to the Intellectual Property Tribunal within ninety days from the date of service of notice of the order. Such appeal shall be on grounds that the layout-design in question does not meet the originality threshold as provided herein, or that the respondent did not possess the right to apply for registration. The Tribunal may, after affording both parties an opportunity for a hearing and consideration of all relevant evidence presented, affirm, reverse, or modify the register effect order. Any party dissatisfied with the decision of the Intellectual Property Tribunal may further appeal under the provisions governing appeals from orders of Tribunals.

The registered proprietor of a layout-design may grant exclusive licenses conferring the right to commercially exploit the design, subject to the terms and conditions stipulated in the license agreement. Such agreements shall be in writing and executed by both parties or their authorized representatives; failure to comply with this requirement renders the license voidable at the option of the non-executing party. Assignment of a layout-design registration, including rights arising from a register effect order, is permissible only through a registered instrument filed with the Layout-Design Registry. A legal practitioner duly enrolled under the Advocates Act may execute such assignments on behalf of their client, provided written authorization is furnished to the registry. Any subsequent transfer or sub-license shall be subject to similar registration requirements as the initial assignment and will not affect the validity of the original registered layout-design.

Where an aggrieved party disputes the validity of a registered layout design and seeks revocation through appeal before the Intellectual Property Tribunal, the Tribunal may, subject to due process and affording the registrant opportunity for hearing, issue a register effect order. Such an order shall temporarily suspend the legal protections afforded by registration pending final determination of the appeal. The applicant seeking such relief must demonstrate a reasonable likelihood of success in establishing invalidity based on prior publication or other grounds as provided herein. Layout design vested rights of the registrant remain unaffected during this interim period, and the Tribunal may impose conditions to safeguard against irreparable harm should the appeal ultimately fail.

An application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design may be subject to review and potential cancellation if the Controller receives a credible representation alleging non-compliance with the requirements outlined herein. Such representations must detail specific deficiencies in the claimed originality or substantial similarity to previously registered designs, supported by documented evidence submitted directly to the Controller’s office. The Controller shall provide the registrant an opportunity for rebuttal before proceeding; failure of the registrant to respond within sixty days constitutes a waiver of their right to contest the cancellation proceedings. Any subsequent order cancellation issued under this Act shall be published in the Official Gazette and on the designated online portal, detailing the grounds for revocation and the effective date thereof.

Where an aggrieved party believes that an order relating to the validity or enforceability of a registered layout-design has been passed erroneously, they may apply to the relevant intellectual property tribunal for its review. Such application shall be made within ninety days from the date of communication of the original order. The tribunal may, after affording all parties concerned an opportunity of being heard and considering evidence submitted, confirm, vary, or set aside the order in question. Notably, any *order cancellation* passed by a tribunal under this Act is subject to judicial review by the High Court. Provided that the tribunal shall not entertain any application if the aggrieved party failed to exercise due diligence in pursuing remedies available under this Act prior to seeking recourse through the tribunal.

An application for an order cancellation may be presented before the Controller by any person aggrieved by an order relating to the registration of a layout-design. Such application shall state specifically the grounds upon which it is based, and shall be accompanied by all relevant documents substantiating those grounds. The Controller shall serve notice on the registrant of the layout-design in question, affording them a reasonable opportunity to file a written response or appear for a hearing, as they may deem appropriate under this Act. Upon consideration of the application, the response submitted, and any evidence presented at a hearing, the Controller may direct that an inquiry be conducted by an Investigating Officer. The findings of the Investigating Officer shall be considered by the Controller in making a determination regarding the order cancellation. Any party aggrieved by the decision of the Controller may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal.

An order for cancellation of registration granted under this Act may be reviewed by the relevant Intellectual Property Division upon application made within ninety days from the date of service of notice of the order. Such an application shall specify grounds alleging material error apparent on the face of the record or demonstrable prejudice resulting from a failure to comply with prescribed procedural requirements during the original registration process. The Intellectual Property Division may, after affording all parties concerned a reasonable opportunity for being heard, confirm, vary, or set aside the order cancellation. Provided that any determination made by the Intellectual Property Division shall be final subject to appeal under this Act within sixty days of such determination.

Any party aggrieved by an order made under this Act relating to the infringement of a registered layout-design may appeal to the Intellectual Property Tribunal. Such appeal shall be filed within ninety days from the date of communication of the order, and the Tribunal may entertain the appeal only if the appellant demonstrates demonstrable prejudice arising directly from the impugned decision. Further, an order for damages or injunction granted by the Tribunal shall be subject to a review mechanism wherein the original adjudicating officer may petition for its cancellation upon establishing material errors of fact or law. Any such petition for order cancellation must be filed within sixty days and will trigger a de novo hearing before a different officer.

The registered proprietor of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design may grant an exclusive license conferring the right to manufacture integrated circuits incorporating the design, subject to conditions specified in the license agreement. Such licenses shall be assignable by the proprietor, provided that any assignment is recorded with the Controller of Layout-Designs within thirty days of its execution. Where a licensee subsequently seeks to transfer their rights under the license to a third party, such transfer requires prior written consent from the registered proprietor, which may not be withheld without reasonable cause demonstrated in writing. Any order cancellation of registration initiated by the Controller based on grounds of improper licensing practices or misrepresentation during assignment shall render all subsequent licenses and assignments derived therefrom void ab initio, with effect from the date of the original registration. The Controller shall publish notice of such an order cancellation in the Official Gazette.

An aggrieved party seeking review of an order granting interim relief against infringement may file an appeal before the Intellectual Property Tribunal within sixty days from the date of communication of that order. The Tribunal shall consider whether the original order was passed without due consideration of relevant evidence presented by all parties, or if it demonstrably failed to apply the principles of natural justice. Further, any party dissatisfied with a decision regarding costs incurred in relation to such appeal may petition the Tribunal for revision. Where the Intellectual Property Tribunal determines that an order cancellation was manifestly unjust or based on erroneous findings of fact, it shall have the power to set aside the original order and substitute its own.

An application for an order concerning the determination of royalties manner may be presented before the Controller, setting forth grounds demonstrating material prejudice arising from an error apparent on the face of the record. The Controller shall provide the applicant with a reasonable opportunity to be heard and to present evidence in support of their claim. Upon consideration of such submissions, the Controller may direct that a hearing be convened; provided that the respondent shall be notified of the proposed hearing and afforded a corresponding opportunity to respond. Any order cancellation granted by the Controller under this Act is subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. The applicant seeking order cancellation bears the burden of demonstrating, with requisite documentation, that the error substantially impacts the assessment or collection of royalties.

For the purposes of this Act, "board use layout" means a layout-design which is used solely for the purpose of manufacturing integrated circuits by an authorised person as defined under this Act. Such authorisation shall be granted subject to conditions specified therein and may include limitations on the number of integrated circuits manufactured using the board use layout. The term “authorised person” includes, but is not limited to, a person engaged in reverse engineering activities permitted under section 17, provided that such activity does not involve commercial exploitation beyond the scope allowed by this Act. Any modification or adaptation of a board use layout shall be deemed a new layout-design and subject to separate registration requirements as provided herein.

An applicant seeking registration of a layout-design shall, in the prescribed form, furnish particulars relating to the board use layout claimed to be original. Such particulars shall include detailed schematics, layer descriptions, and connectivity matrices demonstrating the unique arrangement of elements within the integrated circuit. The Registrar may require further documentation substantiating the novelty and inventive step of the layout-design, particularly concerning its functional aspects and manufacturing processes. Registration under this Act confers exclusive rights to exploit the registered board use layout, subject to any prior usage or publication as provided herein. Any person desiring to utilize a similar layout-design shall obtain consent from the registered proprietor, failing which they are liable for infringement proceedings.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, no person shall commercially exploit a board use layout without authorization from the owner of the layout-design. Any infringement of this nature shall constitute an actionable wrong, entitling the registered proprietor to seek injunctive relief and damages. The measure of damages awarded in such cases may include pre-award interest at a rate determined by the adjudicating officer, reflecting the commercial harm suffered due to the unauthorized exploitation. Furthermore, where the infringing party has made or sold integrated circuits incorporating the board use layout, they shall be liable to pay an account of profits derived from such acts, provided that such amount exceeds reasonable royalty payments which would have been payable under a license agreement. The adjudicating officer may also order the delivery up or destruction of infringing articles as deemed appropriate.

An application for permission to utilize a board use layout shall be made to the Controller in Form B, accompanied by a statement specifying the purpose for which such utilization is sought and the number of integrated circuits likely to be manufactured or imported utilizing the said layout. The applicant shall also furnish an affidavit verifying the accuracy of the information provided and declaring that the proposed utilization will not contravene any existing rights under this Act. Subject to the provisions herein, the Controller may grant permission upon being satisfied that the use is for non-commercial research purposes only, or constitutes a fair dealing as defined in section 47. The application shall be disposed of within ninety days from the date of its receipt; provided that the Controller may extend this period if further information or clarification is required from the applicant. Any party aggrieved by an order passed by the Controller may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, a person shall be deemed to have made unauthorized use of a registered board use layout if, without authorization from the owner of the design, he reproduces the layout-design or any part thereof in a physical form, and such reproduction is for the purpose of manufacturing integrated circuits. This determination shall not apply where the reproduced elements are wholly insignificant and do not substantially replicate the original artistic merit of the registered board use layout. Furthermore, it is provided that an employee acting within the scope of their employment may utilize a layout-design under these conditions without infringing upon the owner’s rights, subject to adherence to any contractual limitations agreed between employer and employee. Any commercial exploitation beyond such permitted uses shall be deemed unlawful as provided herein.

Any individual, firm, company or other body corporate who, without authorization from the registered proprietor, makes, for any purpose whatsoever, a board use layout which is substantially similar to the registered layout-design shall be liable to pay damages as determined by the Intellectual Property Enforcement Tribunal. Such damages shall not be less than five per cent of the cost of production of the integrated circuit incorporating the infringing layout or such higher amount as the Tribunal may deem just under this Act, taking into account the extent of the infringement and any loss suffered by the proprietor. Further, where an infringement is established, the Court may issue an injunction restraining the infringer from further making or selling integrated circuits utilizing the unauthorized board use layout, provided that the proprietor demonstrates continuing harm.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, the owner of a board use layout may grant licenses conferring the right to utilize, reproduce, or commercially exploit said layout for specific purposes. Such licenses shall be documented in writing and may be exclusive or non-exclusive as determined by the licensor. Assignment of rights pertaining to a board use layout is permissible, provided that such assignment includes all rights granted under this Act concerning the layout’s utilization and reproduction. Any transfer of ownership or licensing agreement relating to a board use layout shall require registration with the Controller General of Patents, Designs, and Trademarks, as prescribed herein. Failure to register an assignment may render it unenforceable against subsequent transferees. The licensor retains the right to terminate any license if the licensee engages in activities detrimental to the integrity of the registered layout design.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, nothing shall prevent a person from utilizing a board use layout for the purpose of analysing or assessing the originality of another’s layout design, provided that such utilization is solely for the aforementioned purposes and does not involve commercial reproduction or exploitation. Any party aggrieved by an order permitting such utilisation may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. The Tribunal shall consider whether the permitted use constitutes a fair dealing with the original layout design, taking into account the extent of similarity between the two designs and any potential prejudice to the rights holder. Decisions regarding permissible board use layouts are subject to judicial review under this Act.

An applicant seeking registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall, as part of the prescribed application process, submit detailed schematics illustrating the physical arrangement of elements constituting the board use layout. These schematics must clearly delineate all layers and interconnects within the design. Upon receipt of an application, the Controller may require the submission of additional documentation or clarifications deemed necessary to ascertain compliance with the provisions relating to originality and non-infringement under this Act. A relevant entry register shall be maintained by the Registrar, documenting each application received, including dates of filing, applicant details, and any correspondence pertaining thereto. The Controller shall provide a reasoned order for any rejection or modification proposed, which may be appealed before the Intellectual Property Tribunal as provided herein.

Any person who, without authorization from the registered owner, makes for sale or hire, or offers to make available for sale or hire, any integrated circuit embodying a layout design which infringes the registered layout design shall be liable to pay damages. Such damages shall be assessed by considering the loss suffered by the registered owner as a result of the infringing use, and may include reasonable royalty that the infringer would have been willing to pay. The Court may also grant an injunction restraining the person from further engaging in the unauthorized use layout design. Provided that, where the infringement is demonstrably minor and unintentional, the Court may determine a reduced amount for damages, subject to representations made by both parties regarding mitigation of harm. Further, any imported integrated circuits found to be infringing under this Act shall be liable for seizure and destruction.

Any person desiring to undertake the commercial use layout design of a protected integrated circuit layout design shall, prior to commencement of manufacture or sale, apply for permission from the Controller. Such application must specify the intended scale of production and the geographical area within which the use is proposed. The Controller may require submission of technical documentation demonstrating that the proposed use does not constitute an infringement of any existing registered layout designs under this Act. An applicant shall be deemed to have sufficient interest in the matter, provided that they demonstrate a clear commercial purpose for the intended use. Upon receipt of an application and after affording the relevant owner of the layout design an opportunity to file objections, the Controller may grant permission subject to such conditions as are deemed appropriate to safeguard the interests of the registered proprietor.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, no person shall commercially exploit a registered layout design without the prior written consent of the registered proprietor. Such consent may be granted upon such terms and conditions as the proprietor deems fit, including but not limited to limitations on geographical area, field of use, or duration of exploitation. Where consent is given for the use layout design, the licensee shall ensure that any integrated circuit manufactured pursuant to such license adheres strictly to the registered layout design specifications as filed with the Controller General. Any alteration to the registered layout design during manufacturing, without express written permission from the proprietor, constitutes a violation under this Act and renders the manufacturer liable for damages. The right to use layout design is deemed infringed if it involves reproduction or adaptation that substantially replicates the original design’s features.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, no person shall make, offer for sale, sell or import any product which infringes a registered layout design unless he has obtained prior permission from the owner of the layout design. An application for registration shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the drawing representing the integrated circuit layout-design and a statement specifying the nature of the technology used in its creation. The Registrar may, after giving all parties concerned an opportunity to be heard, refuse registration if he considers that the layout design does not involve a sufficient degree of skill or aesthetic appeal. Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act may appeal to the Intellectual Property Tribunal within sixty days from the date of such order. Registration shall confer upon the owner exclusive rights in relation to the use layout design.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, nothing shall prevent a registered user from engaging in the commercial use layout design for the purpose of manufacturing integrated circuits incorporating a protected layout-design, provided that such use is solely within the scope of the license granted under this Act. An application by a registered user seeking clarification regarding the permissible extent of their licensed use may be made to the Controller, who shall issue an order determining the boundaries of said usage. The Controller may require the applicant to submit detailed technical specifications demonstrating the nature and degree of integration involved in the manufacturing process. Any party aggrieved by such an order may appeal to the Intellectual Property Tribunal within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order. Further, a registered user shall be deemed to have complied with the terms of their license if they adhere to all quality control standards prescribed under this Act.

For the purposes of this Act, "use registered layout" with respect to an integrated circuit layout-design shall mean any act involving the reproduction, adaptation, or commercial exploitation of a registered layout. Such use includes, but is not limited to, the manufacture of integrated circuits based on the registered layout, the sale of such manufactured integrated circuits, and the importation of integrated circuits incorporating the registered layout. Nothing in this definition shall be construed as permitting reverse engineering undertaken solely for the purpose of identifying design features or functionality; provided that any subsequent use derived from such reverse engineering is subject to restrictions under this Act.

No person shall, without authorization from the registered proprietor, make, sell, import, or offer to sell any product which directly or indirectly infringes upon a registered layout. Such infringement includes the reproduction of the registered layout in whole or in part, or the use of the registered layout as a basis for another layout design. Where an infringement has occurred, the registered proprietor shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief restraining the infringing party from further acts of infringement and damages proportionate to the loss suffered by the registered proprietor. The amount of damages may include lost profits attributable to the sale of infringing products, or any reasonable royalty that the infringer would have paid had they obtained authorization for the use registered layout. This right shall be subject to a defense demonstrating fair dealing under this Act.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, the registered proprietor of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be entitled to grant licenses for the use registered layout design. Such license may be exclusive or non-exclusive, and may cover all or part of the rights conferred by registration, including but not limited to reproduction, adaptation, and commercial exploitation. Any assignment of ownership of a registered layout-design shall include any existing licenses granted under this Act relating thereto, unless otherwise expressly agreed in writing between the assignor and assignee. The terms and conditions of any license agreement shall be governed by contract law as provided herein; however, nothing in this provision shall preclude the Registrar from intervening where such agreements demonstrably impede access to essential technologies or unfairly restrict competition within the semiconductor industry.

Subject to appeal to the Intellectual Property Tribunal, no person shall be permitted to undertake commercial exploitation of a registered layout design without express written authorization from the registrant, provided that such authorization is accompanied by evidence of royalty agreements as may be prescribed. Any party alleging infringement of a registered layout design may institute civil proceedings in the District Court, demonstrating prima facie evidence of unauthorized use registered layout and substantial similarity between the infringing article and the original design. The defendant shall bear the burden of proving legitimate access to the protected design or establishing independent creation, failing which liability for damages and injunctive relief shall be imposed as determined by the court.

The Registrar shall, upon receiving an application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design, examine whether the layout-design incorporates inventive features beyond those dictated by commercially available technology. An applicant seeking registration must demonstrate that the design represents a unique configuration and arrangement of elements, distinguishing it from existing designs within the relevant field. The right to use registered layout shall be granted subject to the condition that the layout-design does not unduly restrict further innovation or constitute an invention far claimed beyond its functional purpose. Any challenge to the validity of registration may be brought before the Controller under this Act, asserting a lack of novelty or inventive step in the design’s features.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, no person shall manufacture for sale or import any integrated circuit embodying a registered layout design without prior authorization from the registrant. Such authorization may be granted upon application, provided that the applicant demonstrates legitimate commercial interest and adherence to quality control standards as prescribed by regulations framed under this Act. The use registered layout design shall not extend beyond the scope of the authorized purpose unless further consent is obtained in writing from the registrant. Where a geographical indication relates to an integrated circuit layout-design, any unauthorized use thereof may be deemed detrimental to the reputation and distinctiveness associated with that indication, attracting enhanced penalties as determined by the relevant adjudicating officer.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, a registered owner of a layout design shall be entitled to grant licenses for the use registered layout design, either wholly or partially, in exchange for royalty payments as mutually agreed upon. Such license may be exclusive or non-exclusive and shall be documented through a written agreement specifying the scope of permitted activities, duration, and territorial limitations. Assignment of rights relating to a use registered layout is permissible with the prior consent of the Controller, who may require disclosure of financial considerations involved. Where the layout design incorporates elements derived from plant varieties, the registered breeder of such variety shall be entitled to receive an equitable share of any royalties generated through licensing or assignment under this Act, as determined by the Controller based on a prescribed formula.

The right conferred by registration under this Act shall extend to the reproduction of the integrated circuit layout-design in any mode, including visual or graphical representations, provided that such reproduction is not for private use. The design shall extent to include acts which would otherwise constitute infringement but are undertaken solely for the purpose of research, experimental analysis, and reverse engineering relating directly to the functionality of the semiconductor device incorporating the registered layout-design, subject to a condition that any information derived from such acts is not commercially exploited without authorization. Further, this protection shall not apply where the design is substantially similar to an earlier unregistered design already in public use within India.

An application for registration of an integrated circuit layout design shall include particulars specifying the name and address of the applicant, whether the applicant is the first maker of the layout-design or has derived title thereto, and a statement indicating whether any prior publication or exploitation of the layout-design has occurred. Where the applicant claims derivation of title, the application must clearly identify the original registrant and provide documentary evidence substantiating such claim under this Act. The Registrar may require further documentation to verify the validity of the law registration referred to in the application, including assignments or licenses relating to the design.

An application for registration of a layout-design shall include particulars verifying ownership and detailing the technical specifications as prescribed under this Act. The Registrar may require the applicant to furnish further documentation substantiating claim to originality and demonstrating compliance with established standards relating to circuit functionality. Where an earlier identical or substantially similar layout-design has been previously registered, the application shall be deemed invalid unless it incorporates demonstrably novel elements. Any challenge to a registration based on prior art must be submitted within three months of publication for public inspection; failure to do so will preclude subsequent objections. The process of law registration referred herein is open to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

Any proprietor seeking to enforce rights under this Act relating to a registered layout-design shall provide evidence of such registration to any party against whom enforcement is sought. Failure to produce satisfactory proof of law registration referred will render the proprietor incapable of pursuing remedies for infringement, subject to an appeal to the relevant judicial authority. Where a claim of prior use or publication exists, the alleged infringer may present documentation demonstrating that the layout-design was publicly available before the date of application for registration. The burden of proving such prior use or publication shall rest upon the party asserting it. Remedies awarded under this Act, including injunctions and damages, are contingent upon establishing valid registration and adherence to procedural requirements as provided herein.

An application for registration of an integrated circuit layout design shall contain particulars specified in Form A and shall be accompanied by the prescribed fee. The Controller General may require the applicant to furnish such further information as he deems necessary for the purpose of examination under this Act. Upon receipt of an application, the Controller General shall issue a postal acknowledgement thereof and assign it an official reference number which shall be recorded in the Register of Applications. Where the application does not comply with the requirements of this Act or the regulations made thereunder, the Controller General shall communicate the defects to the applicant, allowing him a period of ninety days to rectify them. Failure to do so within that time will result in the rejection of the application. The applicant may appeal against such rejection as provided herein. Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act relating to law registration referred may prefer an appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

The owner of a registered layout-design shall be entitled to grant licenses conferring rights to utilize the design, subject to the terms and conditions stipulated in the license agreement. Such agreements may include provisions for royalty payments, duration of exclusivity, and permitted geographical territories. Assignment of ownership of a registered layout-design is permissible, provided that such assignment is executed in writing and duly stamped as per prevailing regulations. Any subsequent licensee shall be bound by the original registration’s terms unless explicit modifications are secured through further application under this Act. The Registrar may require submission of details regarding any license or assignment for public recordation to ensure transparency and facilitate verification of rights pertaining to law registration referred, safeguarding the interests of both licensors and licensees within the semiconductor industry.

Any individual or entity found to have commercially exploited a layout-design without prior registration, and subsequently sought law registration referred under this Act, shall be deemed to have acted in deliberate violation of established protocols. Such actions are subject to penalties as provided herein; specifically, fines not exceeding seventy-five thousand rupees may be imposed per instance of unauthorized production or distribution. Furthermore, the infringing party shall be liable to pay damages equivalent to a proportion of the profits derived from the entitled produce variety’s commercialization, determined by the Controller. Repeated offenses will attract enhanced penalties, including potential imprisonment for up to one year and forfeiture of any gains accrued through unlawful activity.

For the purposes of this Act, “fees surcharge” means any additional amount levied on prescribed fees relating to the registration of layout-designs, or for extensions of protection under this Act, and shall be determined by notification published in the Official Gazette. The Central Government may prescribe different rates of fees surcharge based on factors including, but not limited to, the complexity of the layout-design, the applicant’s status as a small enterprise, and the time taken for processing an application. Any fees surcharge collected shall be credited to the Fund established under this Act and utilized exclusively for promoting innovation in integrated circuit design.

Where a license is granted under this Act for the commercial exploitation of a registered layout-design, the licensee may elect to pay a periodic fees surcharge as an alternative to royalties stipulated within the licensing agreement. Such fees surcharge shall be determined by reference to the anticipated gross revenue derived from the licensed activities, subject to verification by the Controller General. The licensor shall provide detailed financial records for assessment purposes upon request. Assignment of layout-design rights, whether partial or complete, may only occur with the express written consent of all parties involved in any existing licensing arrangements; and where such assignment impacts ongoing fees surcharge obligations, a pro rata adjustment shall be calculated to ensure equitable distribution amongst licensors and licensees as provided herein. Failure to remit the agreed fees surcharge within the prescribed timeframe will constitute a breach of contract and may trigger remedies available under general contractual law.

Where any applicant for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design fails to remit the prescribed fees within thirty days from the date of demand, the Registrar may, subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal, impose a surcharge not exceeding twenty-five percent of the unpaid amount. Such surcharge shall be recoverable as an arrear due from the Government and shall accrue to the Consolidated Fund of India. An aggrieved applicant desiring to challenge the imposition of such fees surcharge must file an application for revision within sixty days of receipt of notification thereof; failing which, the order shall be deemed final. The Registrar shall provide reasons in writing for any decision to impose a surcharge, and these reasons shall accompany the notification sent to the applicant.

The term “audiovisual work” with respect to copyright shall include cinematograph films, excluding any works solely comprising literary or musical elements, and further encompasses compilations of such films integrated with accompanying sound recordings. For the purposes of this Act, an audiovisual work is deemed to be authored by the producer thereof. The registrar copyrights shall maintain a public register containing particulars of all registered audiovisual works, including details of ownership and duration of copyright protection as claimed in the application. Any alteration to these particulars may only be effected with the prior written consent of the Central Government, subject to such conditions as it may deem appropriate.

The application for registration of copyright, as provided herein, shall be in such form as may be prescribed by the regulations framed under this Act. Every applicant shall furnish with their application three certified copies of the work to which the claim relates, unless the work is an audio-visual recording, in which case two copies are sufficient. The Registrar copyrights shall examine each application to ascertain whether it complies with all requirements specified under this Act and the rules made thereunder. If any deficiency is noted, the applicant shall be notified accordingly and given a reasonable opportunity to rectify such deficiencies. Upon satisfactory examination, the Registrar copyrights shall proceed with registration in accordance with established procedures.

Applications for registration of copyright shall be made to the registrar copyrights in such form and containing such information as may be prescribed. Every application so filed shall include certified copies of the work, or where the work is unpublished, an extract thereof sufficient for identification; provided that in the case of musical works, a transcription or notation conforming to the accepted standard practice shall suffice. The registrar copyrights may require the applicant to furnish further particulars regarding ownership and creation of the work if deemed necessary for verification under this Act. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the registrar copyrights relating to the acceptance or rejection of an application may appeal to such authority as is prescribed, within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. The registrar copyrights shall maintain a register of all copyright registrations and related documents.

The application for registration of copyright, submitted in accordance with the prescribed form and accompanied by the requisite fee, shall be examined by the receiving officer to verify compliance with the provisions relating to eligibility under this Act. Provided that any deficiency identified during examination may be brought to the attention of the applicant, who shall have a period of thirty days from the date of notification to rectify such deficiencies or submit further documentation as deemed necessary. The registrar copyrights shall, upon satisfactory completion of the verification process and determination of copyright subsistence, proceed with the registration of the work in the public record. Any objection raised by any person against the proposed registration must be filed within sixty days of publication of the acknowledgement.

The registrar copyrights shall, upon receiving an application for registration of copyright, examine whether the work is original and satisfies the requirements as provided herein. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the registrar denying registration may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of communication of such decision. Failure to comply with this time limit shall render the appeal inadmissible. The registrar copyrights shall maintain a record of all applications received, works registered, and appeals filed, accessible for public inspection subject to reasonable restrictions as determined by the Central Government. Any unauthorized access or dissemination of these records will be penalized with imprisonment extending to two years, or fine, or both, under this Act.

The owner of copyright in any work, whether registered or not, may grant an exclusive license authorizing the doing of specified acts relating to that work, subject to such terms and conditions as are agreed upon between the licensor and licensee; provided that such license shall clearly define the scope of the permitted acts, including but not limited to reproduction, distribution, public performance, and adaptation. The registrar copyrights shall maintain a publicly accessible register of all assignments and licenses granted under this Act, detailing the parties involved, the work subject to the assignment or license, and the duration thereof. Any subsequent assignee or licensee may record their interest in the Copyright Office for evidentiary purposes. Failure to accurately reflect the terms of an agreement within the recorded document shall render such recording voidable at the instance of any aggrieved party.

The application for registration of copyright, if accompanied by any document appearing to contradict information provided therein or raising doubt as to the applicant’s entitlement, may be rejected by the Registrar of Copyrights after affording the applicant an opportunity of being heard, subject to principles of natural justice. Any party aggrieved by such rejection shall have the right to appeal against the order within sixty days from the date of communication thereof to the Controller, who may entertain the appeal if satisfied that the rejection was manifestly unjust or based on an erroneous interpretation of the provisions under this Act. The Registrar copyrights shall record the reasons for any such rejection in writing and make them available for inspection by the applicant upon request.

Any person aggrieved by any order made under this Act relating to the registration of copyright, or concerning the refusal to register marks indications customary to a trade or business, may appeal to the High Court within sixty days from the date of such order. Failure to comply with the prescribed procedures for submitting applications and associated documentation shall render the application liable for rejection without further notice. The Registrar Copyrights shall have the power to issue summonses and administer oaths in relation to any inquiry undertaken pursuant to this Act, and wilful disobedience of a summons or false evidence given before the Registrar may attract penalties as determined by the Central Government. Repeated violations concerning the accuracy of information provided during copyright registration proceedings will result in revocation of said registration.

Where any registered user, having lawfully obtained a copy of a computer program protected under this Act, alleges that the copyright owner has unreasonably withheld license to modify or distribute such program in furtherance of interoperability with other systems, he may file an appeal before the Controller. Such appeal shall specify the grounds for alleging unreasonableness, including but not limited to demonstrable prejudice resulting from the withholding and evidence of attempts made to negotiate a reasonable license. The Registrar Copyrights shall, upon receiving such appeal, issue notice to the copyright owner affording him opportunity to be heard. Any order passed by the Controller may be appealed to the appellate forum as provided herein, subject to a prescribed fee.

The registrar copyrights shall, upon receipt of an application for registration of copyright, examine whether the work is original and satisfies the requirements of this Act. The examination shall include verification of ownership details as provided in the application. Further, the registrar shall ascertain if any Right Management Information pertaining to the work has been altered or removed without authorization. Any such alteration or removal discovered during the examination process may be grounds for rejection under this Act, subject to due consideration of representations made by the applicant. The registrar’s determination regarding originality is final, provided that an appeal lies as provided herein.

The registrar copyrights shall, upon receipt of an application for registration of literary or artistic works, examine whether the work is original and satisfies the requirements as provided herein. Applications relating to musical compositions shall be assessed with particular regard to the originality of both the lyrics and the underlying music. The applicant shall furnish details regarding the first publication, if any, of the work, including the place and date thereof. Where a work incorporates elements derived from traditional cultural expressions or folklore, the registrar copyrights shall require evidence demonstrating due diligence in ascertaining community consent where applicable. Registration shall apply geographically to works originating within the territory of India, subject to provisions concerning international conventions.

For the purposes of this Act, an india patentee shall be deemed to include any person or body corporate who is registered as the grantee of a patent under this Act and who, subject to the provisions herein, possesses the exclusive right to make, use, exercise, sell, offer for sale, and import the patented invention within India. Where a patent has been assigned, the assignee shall be considered an india patentee with respect to the rights transferred as provided in the assignment document. Any subsequent transfer of such patent or any part thereof shall not alter the status of the original assignee unless explicitly stated otherwise in the instrument of transfer. The term "patent" refers only to patents granted under this Act.

An application for registration as an india patentee shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the grant certificate issued under the corresponding law of the foreign country, demonstrating prior filing of the invention. The Controller may require further documentation substantiating the claim of priority and authenticity of the grant certificate, including declarations from authorized signatories of the foreign registry. Such requirements are subject to prevailing international agreements concerning patent cooperation. An applicant claiming entitlement as an india patentee must also provide a concise statement outlining the nature and extent of their rights derived from the foreign patent. The Controller shall verify these particulars against publicly available records before proceeding with examination under this Act, provided that any discrepancies may be rectified through supplementary affidavits.

Where an interested person considers that a patent has been granted in contravention of this Act or the rules made thereunder, he may petition to the Controller requesting revocation of the patent. Such petition shall specify the grounds upon which it is based and shall be accompanied by such documentation as the Controller deems necessary to substantiate the claims made therein. The Controller may, after giving notice to the india patentee and affording him an opportunity of being heard, determine whether the patent has indeed been granted in violation of any provision. If the Controller finds that the patent was improperly granted, he shall order its revocation, subject to providing just compensation to the india patentee as determined by the Controller. Any party aggrieved by an order made under this Act may appeal to the Appellate Board within a period of sixty days from the date of such order.

Where an application for patent is presented by way of assignment or concession, the Controller shall require proof satisfactory to him that the applicant has been duly authorized to make the application. Such proof may include a certified copy of the instrument effecting the assignment or concession and such other documents as the Controller deems necessary to establish the validity of the transfer. The Registrar may, at any time, call upon an assignee or concessionaire to furnish further evidence relating to the authorization, subject to providing reasonable notice. Failure to comply with such request shall render the application liable for rejection. For the purposes of this Act, a person acquiring rights by way of assignment or concession shall be deemed to be an india patentee from the date specified in the instrument of transfer, provided that the Controller is satisfied with the authenticity and completeness of the documentation submitted.

Where an application for a patent is presented by an assignee, it shall be established that the transfer of right was effected with the consent of the original applicant and in compliance with regulations prescribed under this Act. The Controller may require evidence demonstrating such consent prior to proceeding with examination of the patent application. Further, if the invention relates to a process for producing a substance defined by its chemical composition, any claim relating to that substance shall be deemed invalid unless it is shown that the process described is essential for the working of the claimed invention. A person claiming to be an india patentee must satisfy the Controller regarding their entitlement to the rights sought and provide documentation substantiating ownership or legal assignment.

Any person seeking revocation of a patent shall apply to the Controller in the prescribed form and manner, demonstrating reasonable grounds to believe that the patented invention does not meet the criteria for patentability as provided herein. The Controller may, after affording the india patentee an opportunity of being heard, grant or refuse such revocation if satisfied that the invention was not novel or obvious at the time of the application’s filing date. Further, any party aggrieved by an order passed under this Act relating to revocation may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within a period of sixty days from the date of communication of the order. Failure to comply with procedural requirements during such proceedings shall render the appeal inadmissible and subject the appellant to penalties as determined by the Board.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, an india patentee shall be entitled to grant exclusive rights comprising the privilege of making, using, selling, offering for sale, and importing the patented invention in India. Such rights may be assigned or licensed by the india patentee to any person, either wholly or partially, and such assignment or license shall be recorded in the Patents Office as provided herein. Where an assignment includes a power of revocation, the instrument creating such power shall specify the conditions under which it may be exercised. Any licensee acquiring rights under a license granted by the india patentee shall be bound by the terms of the license agreement; however, any modification to the scope of the patented invention through sub-licensing requires prior written consent from the original india patentee. The Controller may require disclosure of licensing agreements for examination concerning anti-competitive practices.

Where an appeal is preferred under this Act against the decision or order of the Controller refusing the grant of a patent, the Appellate Board may, subject to such conditions as it deems fit, direct the Controller to rehear the matter. Such direction shall be given only if the Board considers that the refusal was manifestly unjust or based on an erroneous interpretation of the law relating to patentability, novelty, or inventive step. The determination of whether a person qualifies as an india patentee for the purposes of claiming priority under this Act shall be subject to judicial review by the Appellate Board upon appeal from any decision of the Controller regarding said qualification. Provided that such appeals must demonstrate prejudice resulting directly from the Controller's order and may be dismissed if deemed frivolous or vexatious.

Where an objection is raised under this Act against the grant of a patent, and such objection challenges the status of the applicant as a true india patentee, the Controller shall provide both the objector and the applicant with an opportunity to present evidence and arguments in support of their respective positions. The determination of whether an individual or entity qualifies as a india patentee is subject to judicial review, provided that the aggrieved party demonstrates demonstrable prejudice arising from any error apparent on the face of the record. Further, if the invention relates to technology originating outside India, the Controller may request clarification and supporting documentation from the International Bureau regarding prior art disclosures relevant to assessing novelty and inventive step.

An application for registration as an india patentee shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the grant certificate issued by the relevant authority in the country of origin, demonstrating prior filing of the invention. The Controller may require further documentation substantiating the claim to priority under this Act, including declarations from co-applicants or assignees. Any person aggrieved by an order passed by the Controller relating to the registration of a patentee’s rights may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of such order. The Appellate Board shall consider all relevant evidence and arguments presented before it. Subject to provisions regarding costs, the decision of the Appellate Board shall be binding on both parties.

A certificate issued under this Act, when purporting to be signed by an authorized officer and bearing the official seal of the Trade Marks Registry, shall be prima facie evidence of the facts stated therein, subject to the provisions for rectification as provided herein.
