The Controller’s decision regarding a patent found to be obtained through fraudulent means is final, though appeal lies only on grounds of legal error and not factual dispute. It is expressly stated that this provision applies even where a section withdrawn has previously been relied upon in support of the patent's validity.

An application for patent may be refused if the Controller considers that the invention is not novel or involves an obvious step. The applicant shall have the right to file a written response addressing the grounds of refusal communicated by the Controller within sixty days from the date of communication. Such response shall include arguments and evidence supporting the claim of novelty or non-obviousness, as applicable. Where the application has been previously rejected under this Act and subsequently amended, the Controller may require further clarification regarding the impact of such amendments on the original claims. The power to grant or refuse a patent remains with the Controller, subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. Notably, an invention which was once considered patentable but is now deemed to lack novelty due to prior publication shall be treated as having been *section withdrawn* and its examination suspended accordingly.

An invention shall not be patentable if, at the time of filing the application, it is determined that the claimed subject matter constitutes a method for agricultural purposes and such method was previously described in published literature accessible within India; provided that, where the applicant demonstrates diligent effort to locate prior art during the prosecution process, and provides evidence satisfactory to the Controller regarding novelty arising from specific implementation details not disclosed in said literature, the application may proceed. Furthermore, an invention relating to a pharmaceutical substance shall be deemed non-patentable if it is established that the substance was known as a traditional knowledge practice for over fifty years preceding the date of filing; however, this provision shall not apply where the applicant can prove substantial inventive step beyond the documented use. Any application found to fall under these conditions may be subject to immediate *section withdrawn* and subsequent rejection.

Any person aggrieved by any order made under this Act may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order; provided that the Board may, if it considers reasonable to do so, entertain an appeal lodged after the expiry of the said period if satisfactory explanation is furnished for the delay. Failure to comply with a direction issued by the Controller regarding the destruction or delivery of infringing goods or materials shall be deemed a contempt of the Controller and subject to penalties as provided herein. Further, any party found to have wilfully concealed information during proceedings relating to revocation of a patent may face additional fines and be barred from applying for patents under this Act; particularly where such concealment relates to a section withdrawn due to lack of novelty.

Where the proprietor of a patent desires to grant a license for the use of the patented invention, such license may be assigned or surrendered wholly or in part, subject to the conditions as provided herein. Any assignment shall include all rights and powers conferred upon the proprietor under this Act, unless a lesser interest is expressly specified within the instrument of assignment. The assignee shall possess all privileges previously held by the assignor relating to the patent, including the right to sue for infringement. Further, where a license has been granted, the licensee may sub-license such rights with the prior written consent of the proprietor, provided that such sub-licensing does not contravene any terms stipulated in the original licensing agreement. It is explicitly stated that a section withdrawn from this Act shall be deemed to have no effect on existing licenses or assignments relating thereto.

Where any patent is granted and subsequently the patentee fails to comply with a notice issued by the Controller requiring him to furnish proof of working or production relating to the patented invention, the Controller may, after giving opportunity for hearing to the patentee, issue an order declaring the patent to be withdrawn. Such declaration shall not prejudice the right of the patentee to challenge the correctness of the order under appeal before the Appellate Board within a period of sixty days from the date of receipt of the notice of the order. The Controller shall consider any representations made by the patentee in response to such an appeal and may, if satisfied that there were sufficient grounds for non-compliance, set aside or modify the order declaring the section withdrawn.

For the purposes of this Act, "published expiry period" means the time interval commencing from the date on which a patent is initially advertised in the Patent Journal as provided herein, and terminating sixty months thereafter. This period shall be deemed conclusive for determining rights under this Act relating to compulsory licensing or revocation proceedings. Where an extension of the patent term has been granted under this Act, the published expiry period shall be recalculated from the date of such extended term’s initial advertisement. Any challenge to the accuracy of the publication date is subject to appeal before the Controller and must be brought within three months of the relevant publication.

An applicant seeking registration of a utility model shall furnish with the application details pertaining to any prior publication relating to the invention. Such publications, whether in India or abroad, will be assessed for their impact on novelty and inventive step. Where an earlier publication discloses all elements essential to the claimed invention, the application may be rejected under this Act. However, if the disclosure was made incidentally during the course of an authorized exhibition or demonstration, a grace period shall apply. This grace period allows for consideration of the utility model’s patentability even after the published expiry period of such incidental disclosures, provided that the applicant demonstrates diligent efforts to secure protection following the public display.

Where a patent is granted and subsequently revoked by the Controller under this Act, any party aggrieved by such revocation may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. The Appellate Board shall consider whether the grounds for revocation were adequately substantiated and whether due process was followed in the original determination. Further, where a patent has been granted, the right to exploit the patented invention shall remain subject to the published expiry period as determined under this Act; any infringement occurring after that date may be pursued through civil remedies available under general law. Provided that, if an appeal is pending before the Appellate Board concerning the revocation of a patent, enforcement actions relating to alleged infringement shall be stayed until the final order of the Appellate Board is delivered.

Where an invention is disclosed in a publication prior to the date of filing of a patent application claiming priority from a foreign application, and such disclosure would otherwise invalidate the patent under this Act, the Controller may grant a patent if he is satisfied that the published information does not disclose the complete inventive concept. The period during which the patent can be granted despite such prior publication shall be determined by reference to the *published expiry period* as defined in Schedule B, and shall not exceed thirty-six months from the date of first publication. An applicant seeking a patent under these circumstances shall file Form X with the Controller, detailing the nature of the published disclosure and demonstrating its insufficiency to preclude inventive step. The Controller may require further evidence or argument concerning the impact of the prior publication before making a determination. Any appeal against a decision made under this provision shall be heard by the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

Where an invention relates to a process for producing a substance intended for use as food or medicine, and such process is claimed in the patent application, the publication of the grant of the patent shall be deferred until six months from the date of filing. Provided that, if the applicant provides satisfactory evidence demonstrating prior public knowledge of the process, the Controller may waive this deferment. Further, upon expiry of a period of five years from the date of first granting of the patent, any person may apply to the Controller for revocation on grounds including non-obviousness or lack of utility. The published expiry period relating to such patents shall be deemed conclusive evidence of the invention's public availability and accessibility for subsequent innovation, subject to judicial review as provided herein.

Any person aggrieved by an order relating to revocation of a patent, or any other action taken under this Act which adversely affects their interests, may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order. The Appellate Board shall consider all relevant evidence and arguments presented before it and may affirm, modify, or reverse the original decision. Failure to comply with prescribed procedures during a patent revocation proceeding will render any subsequent appeal inadmissible. Further, where a patent has expired due to the passage of its published expiry period, no action for infringement can be maintained; however, remedies relating to unfair practices occurring prior to that date may still be pursued as provided herein.

Where a patent has expired under this Act, and the patentee has granted a non-exclusive license in respect of the invention claimed therein prior to such expiration, any subsequent assignment of the patent shall be deemed to include assignment of all rights pertaining to that license. Provided that, where an invention is subject to a compulsory license granted as provided herein, the assignee under this Act may, with the consent of the original patentee and the licensee, further assign the right to exploit the patented invention for a period not exceeding the published expiry period of the original patent. Such subsequent assignment shall be recorded with the Controller and shall be binding on all parties claiming through the original patentee or any prior assignee. The Controller may require proof of consent as stipulated above before registering such an assignment, subject to regulations framed under this Act.

Where an invention is subject to a patent granted under this Act and concerns a process for producing a substance intended for use, or produced in, the food industry, the published expiry period shall be calculated from the date of first commercial exploitation of that substance. Provided that, if the patentee fails to provide satisfactory evidence demonstrating such commercial exploitation within six months of an appeal against a pre-grant opposition under this Act being dismissed by the Appellate Board, the Controller may, subject to due process and affording the patentee an opportunity for hearing, deem the invention not commercially exploited and recalculate the published expiry period accordingly. Any party aggrieved by such a determination may further appeal to the High Court within ninety days of notification of the order.

Where a patent is granted for an invention incorporating a novel layout-design, the publication of such grant shall not preclude subsequent challenges relating to the validity of the patent based on prior published matter. An objection may be raised within six months from the date of publication under this Act, asserting that the claimed invention was already disclosed in a publicly accessible document predating the patent’s filing date. Provided that the challenger demonstrates with reasonable certainty the existence and content of such prior disclosure, the Controller shall issue an order directing the patentee to submit a counter-statement within three months. Failure to satisfactorily rebut this challenge may result in the patent being declared invalid, notwithstanding the published expiry period already having commenced.

Where a patent is granted and subsequently subjected to a request for pre-grant opposition under this Act, the publication of such patent shall remain subject to a revised published expiry period. This revised period commences from the date the decision on the opposition is communicated to the parties involved, or where an appeal against that decision has been filed, from the final disposal of such appeal. The Controller may, upon application by any interested party and after affording due opportunity for hearing, extend this revised published expiry period if it is demonstrated that exceptional circumstances exist which preclude timely compliance with procedural requirements. A practitioner person representing a patentee shall be responsible for ensuring adherence to these timelines and shall file necessary documentation as provided herein. Failure to comply may render the patent liable for revocation under this Act.

An application for patent shall be deemed to be published upon its entry into the Publication Application Section, subject to compliance with regulations as provided herein. The Controller may direct that an application not be entered into the Publication Application Section if it contains matter which is contrary to law or morality; however, such direction shall only be given after due opportunity has been afforded to the applicant for representation and revision of the offending material. Further, publication shall be withheld where the applicant requests confidentiality under this Act and provides a duly executed request form along with requisite fees, provided that such withholding may not exceed thirty-six months from the date of filing. Any person aggrieved by a decision regarding entry into or non-entry into the Publication Application Section may appeal to an appellate authority as prescribed.

Where a patent is granted and subsequently revoked under this Act, any party aggrieved by such revocation may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order of revocation. The Appellate Board shall have the power to entertain such appeals and dispose of them in accordance with the procedures prescribed herein. Further, where a patent has been published, its validity remains subject to challenge under this Act irrespective of any subsequent modification or amendment to the claims as originally filed. Upon expiry of the term for which the patent was granted, it shall published expiry be declared by the Controller and notice thereof published in the Official Gazette. Any person intending to exploit the invention after such declaration may do so freely, subject to remedies available under this Act for any infringement occurring prior to the date of publication of the said expiry.

Where a patent is granted for an invention relating to a pharmaceutical substance, the Controller may, upon application by any person interested, direct that particulars of such patent be published in the Official Gazette indicating that the patent shall published expiry occurs six months from the date of grant. Such direction shall only be given if the applicant demonstrates reasonable grounds to believe that the invention is essential for addressing a public health emergency as defined under regulations framed by the Central Government. The Controller shall provide an opportunity for the patentee to make representations before issuing such a direction, and any order made under this provision is subject to appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of its publication. Failure to comply with procedural requirements during the application process may render the direction invalid.

Where a patent is granted for an invention relating to a pharmaceutical substance, the Controller may, subject to compliance with regulations prescribed by the Central Government, direct that particulars of such patent be published in the Official Gazette at intervals not exceeding six months from the date of grant. Such publication shall include details pertaining to the claimed therapeutic use and dosage regime as specified within the patent specification. Further, where a compulsory license has been granted under this Act, the period for which said patent remains in force shall be determined by the Controller. Upon expiry of the term stipulated therein, or upon revocation of the compulsory license, the patent shall published expiry notification, disseminated through the Official Gazette and other media as deemed appropriate by the Central Government.

Where a patent is granted for an invention relating to a pharmaceutical substance, the Controller may direct that particulars of such patent be withheld from publication for a period not exceeding six months from the date of grant. Any person aggrieved by such direction may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days of receipt of notice thereof. Upon expiry of the directed period, or upon revocation of the order by the Appellate Board, the patent shall published expiry and become accessible in the public domain. Failure to comply with this provision, including unauthorized dissemination prior to publication, constitutes an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, and with a fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, any patentee desiring to grant a license in respect of the invention for which patent protection is granted may execute an assignment or enter into a licensing agreement with any person, firm, or company, specifying the terms and conditions governing such license. Where a patent has been assigned or licensed, the assignee or licensee shall be entitled to exercise all rights and privileges pertaining to the patent as if they were the original patentee, provided that the terms of the assignment or license are clearly defined in writing. Upon *shall published expiry* of the term for which protection is granted under this Act, any such assignment or licensing agreement shall automatically terminate, and the invention shall become available for use without restriction. The Controller may, upon application by an interested party, determine the validity of a disputed assignment or license agreement as provided herein.

Where a patent is granted for an invention relating to a process for producing a substance claimed in the patent, application for compulsory license may be made at any time within six months from the date on which the patent shall published expiry. Provided that such application must demonstrate that the reasonable requirements of the Indian market have not been satisfied. The Controller may allow or reject the application subject to conditions as deemed appropriate, and any party aggrieved by an order under this Act may appeal to the Appellate Board within a period of sixty days from the date of communication of the order; however, the Appellate Board shall consider only questions of law arising out of the decision of the Controller.

Where an invention relates to a process for producing a substance intended for use as food or medicine, the application for patent may include details regarding the manufacturing procedure. Upon receipt of such an application, the Registrar shall powers to require further clarification concerning the scope and methodology described therein. The particulars of any granted patent relating to such processes shall published expiry after a period of six months from the date of grant, provided that this publication requirement does not preclude the applicant’s right to request extended confidentiality under provisions pertaining to national security. Any challenge to the validity of a patent granted under these circumstances may be initiated within one year following the date of its public disclosure as stipulated herein.

Where a patent is granted and subsequently subjected to compulsory licensing under this Act, the term of such patent shall published expiry upon the determination of the said license. Provided that any party aggrieved by an order granting a compulsory license may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. Further, where an application for patent has been filed in a convention country and subsequently becomes the subject of a 73 convention application in India, the rights granted under this Act shall be construed as not infringing upon any prior publication or use occurring before the date of filing in India, subject to provisions regarding pre-grant opposition. Any person violating the terms of a compulsory license may be liable for damages and injunctions as provided herein.

Upon grant of a patent, the Controller General shall direct that particulars of the invention, including the title and name of the applicant, are entered into the Register of Patents. Such entry shall be deemed publication for all purposes under this Act. Where an application is refused or subsequently revoked, any information disclosed in relation to the invention prior to its *shall published expiry* remains subject to confidentiality obligations as provided herein. Any party aggrieved by a decision concerning the publication of patent details may seek redress through appropriate proceedings before a civil court registry established for intellectual property disputes. The Controller General shall maintain records pertaining to all publications and related correspondence, accessible upon request to authorized personnel only. Further, any alteration or amendment to published particulars requires prior approval from the Controller General and subsequent notification via public notice.

Where a patent is granted and subsequently challenged on grounds of prior publication, the Controller may direct that such patent shall published expiry occur six months from the date of the order. Any party aggrieved by this determination may appeal under this Act within thirty days of notification. Failure to comply with any conditions imposed during the challenge period, including but not limited to providing requisite documentation pertaining to the ii india document demonstrating inventive step, will render the appellant liable for a penalty not exceeding five thousand rupees. Further, wilful obstruction of proceedings or submission of false evidence shall be deemed cognizable offences and subject to prosecution under relevant penal codes as provided herein.

Where the Controller considers that the invention disclosed in an application for patents is not novel or involves an inventive step but possesses commercial value due to prior use or publication, he may grant a license to work the patented invention under this Act. Such license shall be granted subject to such terms and conditions as determined by the Controller, including provisions regarding royalty payments and duration of exclusivity. The applicant for the patent shall have the right to assign any rights arising from an application section 35 order to another party, provided that such assignment is recorded with the Patents Office. Any subsequent licensee may further assign their interest in the license, again subject to registration. Failure to comply with the terms of a license granted under this Act may result in its revocation and potential penalties as prescribed herein.

For the purposes of this Act, “published expiry” with reference to a patent shall mean the date upon which an official notification detailing the lapse of protection is disseminated in the Official Gazette. This publication occurs automatically following the expiration of the term specified under this Act and shall be deemed conclusive evidence of such expiry for all legal proceedings. Provided that, where an application for extension of patent term has been filed and remains pending, the published expiry date shall be deferred until a determination regarding said extension is made. Any challenge to the validity of the patent after the published expiry date may only be entertained under provisions relating to post-grant opposition.

An application for registration of a botanical invention may be refused if the description of the plant variety fails to adequately disclose the essential characteristics necessary for its identification. Subject to this, where an applicant seeks to register a process for producing a pharmaceutical substance, details regarding the manufacturing procedure shall be furnished in sufficient detail to enable a person skilled in the art to reproduce the said substance. Furthermore, any publication disclosing information pertaining to a patent application prior to its grant constitutes a disclosure and may affect the novelty assessment under this Act. The date of such published expiry is deemed critical for determining priority rights, provided that the applicant can demonstrate diligent efforts to secure the invention’s protection.

Where a patent has expired by virtue of the effluxion of time as provided herein, any person aggrieved by reason of an infringement of the patent during its term may institute proceedings for damages against the patentee. Such proceedings shall be subject to the limitation period of three years from the date the cause of action arose. The measure of damages recoverable shall reflect the reasonable royalty that would have been payable had the patentee lawfully licensed the invention, or the patentee’s profits attributable to the infringement, whichever is the greater amount. Provided that, in determining such profits, due account shall be taken of any expenditure incurred by the patentee which directly relates to the exploitation of the patented invention. The right to claim damages relating to published expiry shall not extend to actions predicated on matters arising after the date of publication.

Where an invention is deemed to have become publicly known prior to the date of filing of a patent application, the Controller may, upon receipt of evidence demonstrating such publication, issue a notice to the applicant. This notice shall detail the particulars of the published matter and invite the applicant to submit its response within a period not exceeding sixty days from the date of the notice. The Controller shall consider any submissions made by the applicant and may afford an opportunity for interested parties to present their views regarding the impact of the publication on patentability. If, following such consideration, the Controller is satisfied that the invention has been disclosed in a manner constituting *published expiry*, the application may be rejected or amended as deemed appropriate. The decision of the Controller shall be final subject to appeal under this Act.

Where a patent is granted for an invention relating to a pharmaceutical substance, the Controller may, upon application by any interested party and subject to compliance with regulations prescribed herein, declare a date of published expiry prior to the expiration of the term specified under this Act. Such declaration shall only be made if it is demonstrated that the substance has been manufactured and marketed in India for a continuous period exceeding five years from the grant of the patent, and that sufficient information regarding its composition and method of manufacture has been publicly disseminated. Provided that any challenge to the validity of the patent may still be brought under this Act notwithstanding such declaration of published expiry, and subject to procedural requirements as provided herein.

Any patent granted under this Act shall cease to have effect upon the date of its published expiry, as determined by notification in the Official Gazette. Such publication shall occur following a reasoned determination that the invention’s commercial exploitation is demonstrably and substantially complete, considering factors including market penetration and sales volume. Failure to comply with prescribed reporting requirements regarding post-grant commercial activity may trigger an expedited review leading to earlier published expiry. Any party aggrieved by a decision concerning published expiry may institute proceedings before the Controller within ninety days of such notification, seeking judicial review. The Controller shall impose penalties, including fines not exceeding one million rupees, for wilful misrepresentation relating to commercial exploitation data used in determining published expiry.

Where a patent has reached its published expiry date and the Controller has duly notified such expiry in the Patent Journal, any person possessing an interest in the patent, including but not limited to the original patentee or their assignees, may grant non-exclusive licenses relating to the invention disclosed in the patent. Such licenses shall be documented by a deed of assignment registered with the Patents Office and are subject to prevailing market rates as determined by the Controller. The patentee shall provide reasonable notice to all licensees prior to any subsequent assignment of the patent or any portion thereof, provided that such notice does not impede the enforcement of existing rights under this Act. Further, where an invention is jointly patented, consent from all joint patentees shall be required for any license granted after published expiry, as provided herein.

Where a patent is granted and subsequently subject to a challenge regarding its novelty or inventive step, the Controller may, upon receiving evidence demonstrating prior publication that anticipates the claimed invention, issue an order directing the provisional publication of the patent’s expiry date. Such publication shall be deemed conclusive for all purposes under this Act unless within sixty days from the date of such publication, the patentee files a notice of objection disputing the validity of the determination and requesting a review by the Appellate Board. The Controller may require further documentation to substantiate the claim of published expiry. Provided that any decision rendered by the Appellate Board shall be final, subject only to appeal to the High Court on grounds limited to jurisdictional error or violation of principles of natural justice.

Where a patent is granted and subsequently subject to a request for rectification concerning entries in the Register of Patents, the Controller may, upon review of the application and supporting documentation, order amendments reflecting accurate details pertaining to the invention’s claimed priority date or inventor. Such an amendment shall only be permissible if it does not substantively alter the scope of protection afforded by the patent as originally granted. Furthermore, where a patent's term is nearing its natural expiry, publication regarding the anticipated published expiry date shall occur at least six months prior to that event, and such notification must adhere strictly to the prescribed format under this Act. Any appeal against an order relating to rectification register appellate proceedings will be governed by regulations as provided herein.

Where a patent relating to a computer programme is granted and subsequently subject to a request for early publication, such request may be entertained only if accompanied by an affidavit affirming that no prior public disclosure of the invention occurred before the date of filing. Failure to comply with this requirement shall render the requesting party liable for costs incurred by the Controller in investigating potential anticipatory disclosures. Any challenge to the validity of the patent based on alleged prior publication must specifically detail the nature and extent of said publication, and demonstrate its impact on novelty or inventive step. The determination of whether a disclosure constitutes ‘published expiry’ requires consideration of all available evidence; an appeal against such determination lies to the Appellate Intellectual Property Tribunal.

For the purposes of this Act, a later publication application is defined as an application for patent which relates to an invention disclosed in a document laid open to public inspection prior to the date of filing of said application, provided that such disclosure did not anticipate or render obvious the claimed invention. An applicant shall be deemed to have knowledge of any matter contained in a document laid open to public inspection as from the date when the document was first made available to the public. The existence of a later publication application shall not, by itself, invalidate an earlier patent grant, subject to provisions relating to novelty and inventive step under this Act.

An applicant who has previously filed an application for a patent relating to the same invention may, subject to the provisions herein, file a subsequent application disclosing information contained in a prior publication. Such later publication application shall be deemed to have been laid open for public inspection from the date of its initial filing, notwithstanding any earlier disclosure through published material. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish evidence demonstrating the existence and content of the aforementioned publication, along with proof of the applicant's diligent efforts to secure a patent based on that prior art. Further, the acceptance of a later publication application is conditional upon satisfying all other requirements under this Act relating to novelty and inventive step.

Where an applicant for a patent, having previously filed an application relating to the same invention in any country outside India, subsequently files a publication application in India, such later publication application shall be deemed to lack novelty unless it is proven that the prior disclosure was made under conditions of confidentiality and with no intention to seek protection in India. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish evidence demonstrating the date of the earlier application and its status. Failure to comply with this requirement within the time prescribed will result in the publication application being deemed abandoned. Any person aggrieved by a decision regarding novelty under this provision may appeal to the Appellate Board, subject to payment of the prescribed fee. The burden of proving lack of confidentiality rests upon the applicant filing the later publication application.

Where an applicant for a patent elects to publish a later publication application, such election shall be made in writing and filed with the Controller along with the prescribed fee. The Controller may require further documentation substantiating the claim of novelty arising after the initial filing date, including but not limited to affidavits from the inventor or supporting third parties. Subject to compliance with these requirements, the Controller shall acknowledge receipt of the election and specify a provisional publication date. Any objection raised by a third party regarding the validity of the later publication application based on prior art predating the original filing date may be addressed through standard opposition proceedings under this Act. The applicant shall be afforded an opportunity to respond to such objections in writing, supported by evidence. Provided that the Controller is satisfied with the response and any supplementary documentation submitted, the application may proceed towards grant as per established procedures.

An applicant who has previously filed an application for a patent relating to the same invention may, subject to compliance with these provisions, file a later publication application. Such subsequent application shall disclose in its specification that a prior application exists and provide the date of filing and application number of said earlier application. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish evidence demonstrating that the earlier application has not resulted in the grant of a patent or is pending examination. Further, if the earlier application contains matter which would invalidate the later publication application under this Act, the Controller shall notify the applicant and provide an opportunity for amendment. A later publication application filed without adhering to these conditions shall be deemed invalid.

Where an applicant for patent protection files a later publication application relating to matter already disclosed in a previously filed patent application, and such disclosure was not publicly available prior to the date of filing of the subsequent application, the Controller may require the applicant to provide evidence demonstrating independent creation of the invention. Failure to satisfy this requirement shall render the later publication application liable for rejection. Any party aggrieved by a decision under this provision may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of such order. The penalty for knowingly submitting false information in support of a later publication application is imprisonment and a fine, as provided herein.

Where an invention is disclosed in a later publication application filed subsequent to the initial filing date of a related patent application, and where such later publication application contains subject matter not previously described within the earlier application, the applicant shall be obligated to provide written notification to all assignees and licensees of record pertaining to the original patent application. This notification must detail the scope of the additional disclosures contained in the later publication application and their potential impact on existing licensing agreements. Assignees may, subject to contractual obligations, grant non-exclusive licenses incorporating these newly disclosed elements. Provided that any such assignment or license is executed within six months from the date of notification, it shall be deemed valid under this Act. Failure to provide timely notification will render the assignee liable for damages incurred by licensees due to unforeseen expansion of patent scope.

Where an applicant for a patent files a later publication application relating to a previously filed but unpublished application, such later application shall be deemed to relate back to the date of the earlier application for the purposes of novelty and inventive step. However, if it is alleged that the information disclosed in the later publication application was not adequately described or claimed within the original application, the Controller may require the applicant to demonstrate substantial equivalence between the two applications. An appeal against such a determination by the Controller lies to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board under this Act, provided that the appellant demonstrates prejudice resulting from the Controller’s decision and establishes a reasonable basis for believing that the earlier application adequately disclosed the subject matter of the later publication application.

An applicant for a patent who has previously filed an application disclosing substantially the same invention outside India shall, upon filing a later publication application in India, disclose all such prior applications and their dates of filing. Such disclosure shall be made in a prescribed form annexed to the later publication application and verified by affidavit. Failure to comply with this requirement renders the later publication application liable for rejection under this Act. Where an earlier application discloses use of a reference trade mark in relation to the invention, details of such use must also be included within the aforementioned disclosure. The Controller may require further documentation substantiating these disclosures, provided that any delay caused by such requests shall not prejudice the applicant’s right to priority as otherwise established under this Act.

Where an applicant for patent protection elects to pursue a later publication application following initial provisional filing, such election shall not absolve them from strict adherence to all procedural requirements as provided herein. Failure to accurately reflect the original disclosure in any subsequent translation work undertaken for public dissemination of the publication shall constitute wilful misrepresentation and render the applicant liable for penalties under this Act. Any party demonstrating demonstrable prejudice due to inaccuracies arising from a publication work translation may petition the Controller for injunctive relief and damages, subject to satisfying the Court that such prejudice directly impacts their ability to exploit the invention. The Controller may impose fines not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees where non-compliance is established.

Where an applicant elects for a later publication application concerning an invention previously disclosed elsewhere, such election shall remain valid only if the Controller is satisfied that the disclosure did not prejudice the interests of any person. The applicant bears the burden of demonstrating this satisfaction. Should any party object to the granting of a patent based on a later publication application, alleging prior public knowledge detrimental to novelty or inventive step, an adjudicating officer period of ninety days shall be afforded for investigation and submission of counter-evidence. Decisions regarding prejudice under this Act are appealable to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of order, subject to prescribed fees and procedural requirements as provided herein.

For the purposes of this Act, a "later publication application" means an application for patent relating to an invention which is disclosed in a document laid open to public inspection, whether by way of printed publication or otherwise, prior to the date of filing of the said application; provided that such disclosure did not contain sufficient particulars as to enable the invention to be performed. An applicant shall be deemed to have knowledge of any matter contained in a later publication application if it is readily available and accessible under this Act. The existence of a geographical indication applied for, but not registered, does not preclude consideration of a later publication application.

For the purposes of this Act, an "applicant patent claimant" is defined as a natural or juridical person who files an application for a grant of a patent and asserts ownership or right to the invention claimed therein. Such assertion shall be deemed conclusive subject to challenge under provisions relating to pre-grant opposition. An applicant patent claimant may assign their rights in the invention, provided that such assignment complies with the requirements as provided herein regarding notification to the Controller General. Where multiple applicants jointly file an application, each applicant shall be considered an applicant patent claimant with respect to the entire claimed invention unless otherwise specified within the application itself.

An applicant patent claimant shall, upon filing the formal request for registration of an invention, furnish a declaration verifying the authenticity of the particulars furnished relating to the claimed inventive step. This declaration must explicitly state whether the invention is already known or utilized within India, and if so, provide comprehensive details regarding such prior use. The Controller General may, subject to due process, require further documentation substantiating any claims made in this declaration. Failure to comply with these requirements shall render the application liable for rejection under this Act. Further, an applicant patent claimant who knowingly provides false information relating to prior usage is deemed guilty of an offence and shall be punishable accordingly as provided herein.

Where an applicant patent claimant institutes proceedings for infringement of a patent, the Controller may, upon being satisfied that there is reasonable ground to believe that the patent was obtained through material misrepresentation or suppression of fact during the examination process, issue an order restraining the claimant from exercising the patent rights. Such restraint shall remain in effect pending final determination by the relevant judicial forum regarding the validity of the patent. The Controller may also direct the applicant patent claimant to provide such evidence as is deemed necessary to substantiate the allegations of misrepresentation or suppression. Failure to comply with this direction may result in the proceedings being summarily dismissed. Further, any party aggrieved by an order issued under this Act may appeal to the appellate authority within a period of sixty days from the date of such order.

Where an applicant patent claimant seeks to amend the description of the invention disclosed in a patent application subsequent to its publication under this Act, such amendment shall be permissible only if it clarifies matters relating to the claimed invention. The Controller may require the applicant to submit a declaration affirming that the amended description remains consistent with the original disclosure and does not introduce any new matter. Further, an examiner assessing the patentability of the invention following such amendment shall consider whether the clarification unduly broadens the scope of protection sought or prejudices the interests of third parties who have relied upon the originally published specification. The applicant shall be afforded a reasonable opportunity to respond to any objections raised by the examiner concerning the amended description. Any decision regarding the permissibility of an amendment is subject to appeal under this Act, as provided herein.

Where an applicant patent claimant seeks to amend the description of the invention disclosed in a patent application subsequent to its publication under this Act, such amendment shall be permissible only if it does not alter the essence of the claimed invention. The Controller may require the applicant to submit a declaration affirming that the proposed amendments remain consistent with the original disclosure and do not introduce new matter beyond the scope of the initial specification. Provided that any such amendment is accompanied by the prescribed fee, and subject to satisfying the Controller that the amended claims are clear and concise, the Controller shall consider allowing the modification. The applicant shall be responsible for ensuring compliance with all procedural requirements as provided herein regarding amendments.

Where an applicant patent claimant institutes proceedings for infringement of a patent, it shall be incumbent upon them to demonstrate, with reasonable certainty, that the alleged infringing activity falls within the scope of the claims as originally granted or subsequently amended. Failure to do so will render the claim untenable and subject the claimant to costs incurred by the defendant in defending against such frivolous action. Any party demonstrating wilful infringement may petition the relevant authority for enhanced damages, not exceeding three times the actual damages awarded. The Controller shall have power to issue injunctions restraining further acts of infringement, provided that due consideration is given to the public interest and any potential impact on essential services.

Where an applicant patent claimant, being a juridical person, desires to grant a license or assign the rights pertaining to a pending patent application, such authorization shall be executed by a duly authorized officer possessing express power of attorney ratified by the governing body of said juridical person. The instrument of assignment or licensing agreement must clearly identify the applicant patent claimant and the assignee or licensee respectively, along with a comprehensive description of the intellectual property rights being transferred or permitted. Further, any such license granted under this Act shall specify the field of exploitation and the duration thereof, subject to limitations as may be prescribed by regulations framed hereunder. Provided that, prior consent from the Controller General is required for assignments involving transfer of ownership outside the territory of India, demonstrating compliance with foreign exchange regulations.

Where an objection is raised against the grant of patent concerning novelty or inventive step, the Controller shall provide the applicant patent claimant with a reasoned statement detailing the grounds for such objection. The claimant may then submit a written response addressing each point raised, accompanied by evidence supporting their position and demonstrating the validity of the claimed invention as provided herein. Failure to respond within the stipulated period shall be deemed an abandonment of the claim. Any party aggrieved by the Controller’s decision following consideration of the claimant's response may appeal under this Act to the Appellate Board, presenting arguments and documentary proof substantiating their contention that the patent should not have been granted or modified.

Where an applicant patent claimant institutes proceedings for infringement of a patent, it shall be presumed that the patented invention was indeed novel and non-obvious at the date of filing, unless the respondent demonstrates, by clear and convincing evidence presented before the relevant judicial forum, otherwise. The respondent may challenge this presumption by presenting documented proof pertaining to prior publication or public knowledge concerning the denomination variety sub of the claimed invention. Failure to adequately substantiate such a challenge shall result in imposition of costs against the respondent, as determined by the presiding officer. Any party aggrieved by an order made under this Act may appeal to the appellate authority within sixty days from the date of communication of that order; and any failure to comply with provisions relating to payment of fees shall render the appeal void.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, an applicant patent claimant may grant a license or assign their rights relating to a patented invention, including rights pertaining to a breeder registered variety incorporated within that invention, to any person, firm, or company, either wholly or partially. Such licenses shall be in writing and may specify the field of exploitation, duration, and royalties payable. The applicant patent claimant shall disclose all material terms and conditions of any assignment made under this Act to the Controller, who shall maintain a record thereof. Further provision is made for the revocation of such assignments if it is determined that the terms are manifestly unfair or prejudicial to public interest, as provided herein. Any transferor of rights shall remain liable for breaches of contract relating to the licensed technology until the expiry of the license period.

An application for registration of a claim applicant patent shall be accompanied by a declaration, signed by the claimant, attesting to their entitlement and specifying the nature of their interest in the invention. The Controller may require further documentation substantiating this claimed interest, including assignments or contractual agreements relating to the underlying intellectual property. Where the original inventor is not the applicant for the patent, the claim applicant shall provide evidence demonstrating a valid transfer of rights under this Act. Such evidence must be satisfactory to the Controller and may include deeds of assignment duly executed. The Registrar shall maintain a register of all registered claim applicants, accessible for public inspection subject to prescribed fees and confidentiality provisions as provided herein.

Where an objection is taken against a claim applicant patent during examination, relating to novelty or inventive step, the Controller shall provide written reasons for such objection. The claimant may then file a counterstatement within sixty days from the date of communication of the objection, presenting arguments and evidence rebutting the grounds raised. Failure to submit a timely counterstatement shall be deemed an abandonment of the claim applicant patent application. Further, if the Controller finds, after considering the counterstatement and any rejoinder filed by the examiner, that the objection remains valid, the claimant shall be entitled to request an oral hearing. The alphabetical index classification assigned to the invention at the time of filing shall be considered during this process. Any order passed following such a hearing is final subject to appeal under this Act.

For the purposes of this Act, a “patent claimant person” shall be deemed to include any individual who is recorded as the inventor in the patent application or subsequently assigned rights pertaining thereto, subject to verification by the Controller. Such designation may be altered only with the written consent of all initially named inventors and upon notification to the Registrar. A patent claimant person retains standing under this Act until such time as their interest has been formally relinquished through a duly executed instrument registered with the Patents Office. Any individual claiming status as a patent claimant person shall provide satisfactory evidence substantiating their claim, as provided herein.

For the purpose of this Act, a patent claimant person shall be deemed to have fulfilled the requirements for registration where the prescribed Form 1 is submitted electronically through the designated portal, accompanied by all requisite supporting documentation as specified in Schedule A. The Controller General may, subject to due process and after affording an opportunity for hearing, reject the application if it appears that the information provided regarding the patent claimant person’s identity or address is false or misleading. Further, any alteration of details pertaining to a patent claimant person subsequent to initial registration shall be effected only through a formal amendment request filed in the prescribed format and acknowledged electronically by the office. Provided that such amendments do not substantially alter the nature of the invention claimed.

Where a patent claimant person alleges infringement of their patent, they may institute proceedings for remedy before the appropriate commercial court, subject to the provisions regarding jurisdiction as provided herein. The court shall have power to grant such relief as it deems just and equitable, including but not limited to injunctions restraining further acts of infringement, damages proportionate to the loss suffered by the claimant person, and costs incurred in bringing the action. Provided that, where the alleged infringing act was committed unknowingly and without intent to infringe, the court may reduce the amount of damages awarded. Further, a patent claimant person shall be entitled to seek discovery from the defendant relating to their manufacturing processes and sales records, as deemed necessary by the court to ascertain the extent of infringement. The right to appeal any judgment rendered under this Act is preserved.

Where an application for patent includes a reference to any prior published document, whether Indian or foreign, disclosing particulars of the invention, the Controller may require the applicant to furnish a certified true copy of such document. The applicant shall comply with this requirement within the time specified by the Controller; failure to do so shall render the application liable for rejection under this Act. For the purposes of determining entitlement to be a patent claimant person, the date of publication of any prior published document shall be deemed relevant. Any objection raised concerning the validity of the claimed invention based on such prior publication may be addressed during the examination process as provided herein. The Controller shall provide an opportunity for both the applicant and any interested party to present arguments and evidence relating to the novelty and inventive step of the invention.

A patent claimant person shall, upon filing a provisional application, furnish an affidavit verifying the originality of the invention and confirming that no prior publication or public use disclosing the subject matter exists anywhere in the world. The Controller may require further documentation substantiating this claim, including but not limited to records of internal research, experimental data, and correspondence relating to the inventive concept. Provided that a patent claimant person has previously assigned rights to another party, such assignment shall be disclosed within thirty days of the application’s publication; failure to do so renders the assignee ineligible for claiming priority under this Act. Any alteration in ownership subsequent to the initial filing must also be reported as provided herein and subject to Controller approval.

Any patent claimant person who, having knowledge of an infringement of a patent granted under this Act, fails to report such infringement to the Controller within thirty days of becoming aware thereof, shall be liable to pay a pecuniary penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees for each instance of non-reporting. The Controller may, subject to due process and affording opportunity for hearing, issue notices requiring disclosure of information relating to infringing activities. Further, any person found to have wilfully concealed information regarding patent infringement, or made false statements in connection with reporting obligations as provided herein, shall be deemed guilty of an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or both. Recovery of penalties and enforcement of such orders shall be subject to the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any patent claimant person desiring to grant a license or assign their rights relating to a patented invention shall execute a written instrument specifying the scope of such license or assignment, including but not limited to the field of use, territory, and duration. Such instruments must be registered with the Controller within three months of execution; failure to register shall render the license or assignment voidable at the option of any subsequent assignee or licensee. The patent claimant person may stipulate conditions relating to quality control or working of the patented invention as part of such a license agreement. Provided that, where an assignment is made without registration, the assignor retains standing to enforce the terms of the agreement against the assignee under this Act until the Controller confirms the validity of the unregistered transfer.

Where an objection is raised against the designation of a patent claimant person appearing on the record of a patent application, such objection shall be deemed to relate to the veracity and propriety of that designation. The Controller may, upon receiving such an objection, issue notice to all parties concerned, including the applicant and the individual whose designation is challenged, affording them a reasonable opportunity for argument and submission of evidence. Any party aggrieved by the Controller’s decision on this matter may appeal under this Act to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. Provided that the Appellate Board shall consider only questions of law arising out of the interpretation or application of provisions as provided herein, and not matters of fact already determined by the Controller.

Where a patent claimant person, being an individual, desires to assign or license rights pertaining to a patented invention incorporating an integrated circuits layout, such assignment or license shall be executed in writing and attested by at least two witnesses. The instrument of assignment or license must clearly identify the patent specification number and title of the invention concerned, as well as the specific territory within which the rights are being transferred. Further, any licensee granted rights under this Act may sub-license those rights subject to prior written consent from the patent claimant person, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld. An assignment or license executed outside India shall be admissible as evidence if duly legalized as provided herein. The Registrar may require submission of a certified copy of the assignment or license for record purposes.

Where an objection is raised against the designation of a patent claimant person appearing on a patent application, such objection shall be deemed to relate to the veracity and entitlement asserted by that individual. The Controller may, upon receiving such objection, issue notice to both the applicant and the challenged patent claimant person, affording each party a reasonable opportunity for argument and presentation of evidence. Any decision regarding the validity of the designation is subject to appeal before an appellate authority as provided herein. Furthermore, where the disputed patent claimant person seeks to establish their claim through registered certification demonstrating prior inventive activity, the burden shall lie upon them to provide satisfactory proof of authenticity and relevance under this Act.

Where an appeal arises from an order passed by the Controller refusing the grant of patent, or revoking a patent, the appellant, being a patent claimant person aggrieved by such order, may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board. The appeal shall be filed within sixty days from the date of communication of the order to the appellant. Provided that the Board may, if it considers fit, extend this period for reasons to be recorded in writing. Notice of hearing shall be served upon all parties concerned under this Act at least thirty days before the appointed date of hearing. The Appellate Board shall give notice to any other person who appears to the Board to have a right to be heard. Any party may, with the leave of the Board, file additional documents or evidence after the close of pleadings.

For the purposes of this Act, an “applicant patent person” is defined as any individual or legal entity who files for a grant of exclusive rights relating to an invention. An applicant patent person shall be deemed to include not only the original filer but also any subsequent assignee or representative authorized under this Act to act on their behalf in proceedings related to the patent application. Where multiple individuals are jointly seeking protection, each such individual shall constitute an applicant patent person with equal standing. The rights and obligations of an applicant patent person are subject to the provisions relating to inventorship as provided herein.

Where an applicant patent person, being a body corporate, fails to comply with the requirements of this Act relating to the disclosure of particulars concerning beneficial ownership, the Controller may, after affording it an opportunity for hearing, direct that the application be deemed abandoned. Any party aggrieved by such direction may appeal against the same before the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. Further, if a person claiming through the applicant patent person demonstrates to the satisfaction of the Controller that the failure to disclose was due to circumstances beyond their reasonable control and without intent to mislead, the Controller may permit rectification of the record or grant such other relief as it deems fit, subject to payment of prescribed fees. This power shall not prejudice any civil action which a party aggrieved may initiate under this Act.

Where an application for a patent contains particulars relating to more than one invention, the Controller may require the applicant to restrict the claim to one or more inventions so as to comply with the provisions of this Act. Such requirement shall be served on the applicant within six months from the date of filing of the application or where a request for examination has been made, within six months from the date of such request. The applicant may, subject to any directions given by the Controller, amend the claims to restrict them accordingly and shall comply with this obligation within three months from the date of service of the requirement. Failure to do so shall render the application liable to be refused. For the purposes of determining entitlement to a patent, an *applicant patent person* shall be deemed to be the true inventor unless the applicant proves otherwise. The Controller may require evidence demonstrating such proof as provided herein.

Where an applicant for a patent seeks to assign their interest in the invention, such assignment shall be evidenced by a formal instrument executed in accordance with prescribed procedures and duly registered with the Controller. The instrument must clearly identify both the assigning party and the assignee, specifying the precise rights being transferred under this Act relating to the patent application. Further, if the applicant is not the sole inventor, the consent of each inventor shall be obtained in writing and attached as an annexure to the assignment document. Any person claiming title through such assignment must demonstrate that they fulfilled all conditions precedent for valid assignment, including timely payment of prescribed fees. The Controller may require further documentation establishing the identity of the applicant patent person and their entitlement to assign the invention.

Where an applicant patent person fails to comply with a notice issued under this Act requiring disclosure of information relating to foreign applications for the invention, or provides false or misleading information in response thereto, the Controller may, after affording him an opportunity of being heard, impose a pecuniary penalty not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees. Such penalty shall be recoverable as if it were an arrear of land revenue. Further, any person found to have knowingly made a false statement or representation in connection with an application for patent, or in proceedings before the Controller, is liable to imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and a fine. The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, vary the amount of the penalty as provided herein.

Where an applicant patent person, being a body corporate, seeks to assign or license rights pertaining to a pending patent application, such assignment or license shall be executed by a duly authorized officer of that body corporate and accompanied by a certified copy of the resolution authorizing such authorization. The Controller may require further evidence demonstrating the validity of this authorization if deemed necessary for ensuring transparency under this Act. Any subsequent modification or revocation of an earlier assignment or license agreement relating to the patent application must also be formally notified to the Controller within thirty days, along with supporting documentation establishing the change in ownership or rights. Provided that, where the applicant patent person is a partnership firm, the assignment shall be executed by all partners or their duly authorized representatives acting on behalf of the firm.

Where an objection is raised against the acceptance of a patent application on the grounds that the claimed invention was not conceived by the applicant patent person, or that the applicant lacks standing to pursue the patent, the Controller shall provide written notice to all parties asserting such objection. Such notice shall detail the specific basis for the challenge and afford each party fifteen working days from the date of notification within which to submit a detailed response, supported by documentary evidence and expert testimony where applicable. The applicant may then file a rejoinder addressing these submissions. Following consideration of all materials presented, the Controller’s decision regarding the validity of the objection shall be final, subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board under this Act.

Where an application for patent contains particulars indicating that another person was the true inventor, and the applicant desires to proceed with the application notwithstanding such indication, the applicant shall file a declaration affirming their belief regarding the inventive contribution of the named individual. This declaration must be accompanied by evidence demonstrating due diligence in ascertaining the facts presented. The Controller may, subject to an appeal under this Act, require further clarification or additional documentation from the applicant patent person concerning the circumstances application advertised prior to the filing date. Any aggrieved party claiming rights as a true inventor may challenge the validity of such declaration before the Controller and seek redressal through appropriate appellate mechanisms, provided that the challenge is made within the prescribed timeframe.

For the purposes of this Act, an “applicant patent person” is defined as a natural or juridical person who makes an application for a grant of patent and includes any individual or entity claiming inventorship rights relating to the subject matter of such application. An applicant patent person shall be deemed to have knowledge of prior art relevant to the claimed invention from the date of filing, subject to provisions regarding grace periods as provided herein. The registrar may, upon receiving information indicating a potential conflict of interest concerning an applicant patent person's inventorship or entitlement, initiate inquiries and request further documentation for verification.

Where an application for a patent includes or contains subject matter which appears to be, or may reasonably be regarded as, infringing existing registered layouts, the Controller shall issue a communication to the applicant patent person indicating such appearance and requiring the applicant to file within three months of the date of said communication a written representation either admitting the infringement and proposing modifications to the invention described in the application, or denying the infringement and providing reasoned arguments supported by documentary evidence demonstrating non-infringement. The Controller may, subject to due process, consider any such denial and associated documentation before proceeding with examination under this Act. Failure of the applicant patent person to respond within the stipulated time shall be deemed a withdrawal of the application. Any modification proposed pursuant to an admission of infringement shall require further scrutiny as to novelty and inventive step.

Where an applicant for a patent, being a body corporate, fails to comply with the requirements of regulation 6 regarding notification of changes in ownership or control, the Controller may, after affording the applicant an opportunity to be heard, direct that the said applicant shall nominate another person to act as the designated *applicant patent person* for all purposes under this Act. Such nomination must be made within a period not exceeding thirty days from the date of the aforementioned direction. Failure to comply with such direction will render the application liable to be deemed abandoned. The Controller may, at any time, revoke the designation of a nominated person and require another appointment if it appears that the designated person is unable or unwilling to fulfill their obligations relating to patent rights.

For the purposes of this Act, the “patent filed date” in relation to any application for patent shall be deemed to be the date on which the application was first received by the Controller. Where an application is filed electronically, the patent filed date shall be the time and date recorded automatically by the electronic filing system as provided herein. This date shall be conclusive evidence of when the invention was formally brought before the office, subject to any demonstrable error in recording. The patent filed date determines priority under this Act and influences the period for which a patent may remain in force, as determined elsewhere within these provisions.

For the purposes of maintaining a clear record of intellectual property rights under this Act, all applications for patents filed with the Controller shall be assigned a sequential registration number. The patent filed date is deemed to be the date upon which the complete application, including all requisite forms and fees, is received by the office of the Controller. Where an applicant has previously filed a related application, as determined by the Controller, the patent filed date for the subsequent application may be adjusted to reflect the earlier filing, subject to conditions prescribed in the regulations. The register shall accurately reflect each patent’s assigned registration number and its corresponding patent filed date, ensuring transparency and facilitating efficient searches by interested parties. Any alteration of this information requires formal notification and approval from the Controller.

Where a person aggrieved by any order made under this Act relating to the grant, revocation or sealing of a patent has suffered loss or damage as a consequence thereof, that person may petition the High Court for redress. Such petition shall be maintainable only if it is presented within ninety days from the date of communication of the order concerned. The relief sought in such petition shall be limited to compensation commensurate with the demonstrable financial detriment incurred, excluding claims for exemplary or punitive damages. It is provided that in determining the amount of compensation, due consideration shall be given to the patent filed date and any intervening period during which the aggrieved party reasonably relied upon the validity of the patent. Further, the Court may order costs against either party as it deems just.

An application for a patent shall be deemed to have been filed on the date it is received by the Controller, provided that where such application is delivered through post, it shall be deemed to have been filed on the date on which it is actually received. For the purposes of determining priority under this Act, the filing date shall be conclusive evidence unless proven otherwise to the satisfaction of the Controller. Where an applicant has previously filed an application relating to the same invention in a country outside India, the Indian application may incorporate such earlier filing date subject to compliance with prescribed formalities and conditions as provided herein. The Controller may require submission of certified copies of prior applications for verification. Any request for amendment to the patent specification after the *patent filed date* shall be considered only if it does not substantially alter the scope of protection sought, and is accompanied by the requisite fee.

An application for a patent shall be deemed to have been filed on the date it is received by the Controller, provided that if such application is delivered through post, it shall be deemed to have been filed on the date indicated on the postal stamp affixed thereto. Where an applicant has previously filed an application relating to the same invention under this Act, the patent filing date shall be determined as the earlier of either the date of the first application or the date of the subsequent application, subject to compliance with all applicable regulations regarding grace periods and provisional applications. The Controller may require submission of further documentation to verify the claimed patent filed date if inconsistencies arise during examination. Failure to provide such documentation within the prescribed timeframe shall render the application liable for rejection.

Any person aggrieved by a determination made under this Act relating to the validity of a patent, including but not limited to claims concerning the priority date or the patent filed date, may institute proceedings before the relevant intellectual property tribunal. Such proceedings shall be initiated within six months from the date of communication of the order sought to be challenged. Failure to comply with this time limit shall permanently bar any subsequent legal recourse against the determination. The tribunal may, upon application and subject to a demonstration of wilful infringement or substantial financial prejudice, award compensatory damages not exceeding three times the proven loss suffered by the aggrieved party. Costs associated with these proceedings will be determined as provided herein.

Subject to the provisions of this Act relating to priority, any assignment or license granted subsequent to the patent filed date shall require registration with the Controller. Such registration shall be deemed conclusive evidence of the validity of the transfer for all purposes under this Act and against third parties. Where an application for registration of an assignment is accompanied by a certified copy of the original patent document, including the recorded patent filed date, the Controller may expedite the processing thereof. Failure to register an assignment or license prior to its enforcement shall render it voidable at the option of the patentee. The patentee may grant exclusive licenses under this Act, provided that such licenses do not impair the security of India or prejudice the public interest; and any subsequent transfer of such exclusive license requires similar registration as detailed herein.

Where a dispute arises concerning the priority between two or more applications for patents filed on the same day, the Controller may, after affording both applicants an opportunity to be heard, determine the order of filing based upon documentary evidence establishing the precise time of submission at the patent office. It shall be presumed that the application received first was indeed filed earlier unless proven otherwise by the applicant claiming a later date. The determination made under this Act is final and binding, subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. For the purpose of ascertaining the patent filed date in such disputes, electronic records maintained by the office shall be considered primary evidence.

Where a person aggrieved by any order made under this Act concerning the grant, revocation or sealing of a patent has suffered loss or damage as a direct consequence thereof, that person may institute proceedings seeking compensation.
