Decisions regarding permissible patents amendments are subject to judicial review under established principles, provided that a reasoned order is issued detailing the grounds for decision.

Applications for registration of inventions shall include a detailed trade description of the patented product or process, specifying its composition, method of manufacture, and intended use. The Controller General may require further clarification regarding this trade description if deemed necessary to ascertain the scope of protection sought. Amendments to registered patents, relating to the claimed invention's characteristics or application, must be filed with the patent office in a prescribed form, accompanied by an updated trade description reflecting any modifications. Such amendments shall not alter the fundamental nature of the patented subject matter as originally disclosed and are subject to examination under this Act. Any applicant seeking to effect such patents amendments shall provide evidence demonstrating consistency between the amended claims and the original disclosure.

Where an application for registration of a patent is refused under this Act, the applicant shall have the right to appeal to the Controller. Such appeal may be made within sixty days from the date of communication of the order of refusal and shall state specifically the grounds upon which it is based. The Controller shall consider such appeal expeditiously and issue an order either confirming or reversing the original decision. Any party aggrieved by an order passed by the Controller under this Act, including decisions relating to a register references act concerning patent validity or infringement, may further appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. Costs associated with any appeal shall be determined as provided herein, subject to the discretion of the appellate body. Failure to comply with procedural requirements during appeals may result in their dismissal.

Where an application for registration of a utility model is filed under this Act, the Controller shall maintain a comprehensive register detailing all such applications. This register shall include, but not be limited to, the name and address of the applicant, the title of the invention, the date of filing, and any subsequent amendments or modifications as approved by the Controller. A *register references act* is enacted to ensure clarity regarding access to this information; specifically, all parties seeking to ascertain the status of an application shall be entitled to inspect the relevant entries in the register during normal business hours. Provided that a certified copy of any entry may be obtained upon payment of prescribed fees. The Controller may, at his discretion, provide electronic access to portions of the register subject to security protocols as determined by regulations framed under this Act.

Where a patent application incorporates by reference material external to the specification, including but not limited to prior art publications, technical drawings, or data sheets, the Controller shall scrutinize such incorporation for compliance with the requirements under this Act. Failure to adequately describe and support the incorporated material within the patent specification shall render the patent liable for revocation. Any party demonstrating that a claim is anticipated or obvious due to inadequately referenced external material may petition the relevant authority for an inquiry into the validity of the patent, subject to applicable costs and penalties as provided herein. The register references act applies equally to digital and physical documentation incorporated within patent applications; deliberate obfuscation regarding such references will attract severe financial sanctions.

Where a patentee elects to utilize a third-party intermediary for managing aspects of their registered invention’s commercial exploitation, including but not limited to manufacturing, distribution, or offering for sale, such intermediary shall be deemed to hold a license granted under this Act. This license is assignable subject to the prior consent of the Controller and any conditions stipulated therein relating to quality control and adherence to prescribed standards. Any subsequent assignment of rights by the intermediary shall require notification to the patentee within thirty days, allowing for objection based on demonstrable prejudice to the original invention’s integrity. The register references act pertaining to such licensed operations will explicitly detail the scope of permitted activities and any royalty obligations payable to the patentee. Failure to comply with these conditions may render the license voidable at the Controller's discretion.

Where an application for registration of a trademark is refused under this Act on the grounds that it conflicts with a prior mark already registered in respect of identical or similar goods services according, the applicant shall have the right to appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. Such appeal may be predicated upon demonstrating either that the similarity between the marks is not substantial enough to cause confusion amongst consumers, or that the earlier registration was improperly granted due to procedural irregularities affecting its validity. The Board shall consider any evidence submitted by both the appellant and the Registrar pertaining to consumer perception and market analysis. A decision of the Board regarding a register references act determination shall be final, subject to further appeal to the High Court on grounds of law alone.

Upon application by the assignee of a patent, or a pending patent application, the Controller may direct that the record of title relating to such patent or application be amended to reflect the transfer of rights. Such application shall specify the details of the assignor and assignee, along with supporting documentation establishing the validity of the assignment as provided herein. The Controller shall publish notice of the proposed amendment in the Patent Journal. Any person aggrieved by the proposed amendment may, within sixty days from the date of such publication, file an objection with the Controller, stating the grounds for their opposition. The Controller shall consider any objections received and may require further evidence or clarification from either the applicant or the objector. Following due consideration, the Controller’s decision regarding the register references act concerning the assignment transmission rights shall be final.

For the purposes of this Act, a “register reference” shall mean an indication within the official records maintained under this Act identifying a specific entry pertaining to an invention. Such register references may include alphanumeric codes, sequential identifiers, or other systematic designations as prescribed by the Controller General. A register reference shall be considered conclusive evidence of the existence and particulars of the corresponding entry, subject to any order made by the Intellectual Property Appellate Board upon appeal. The term "register reference" does not extend to informal notations or unofficial records maintained outside the central database system; only entries formally recorded as provided herein constitute a valid register reference.

Where an application for registration of a utility model is filed, the Controller shall maintain a comprehensive register detailing all such applications. This register shall include, but not be limited to, the applicant’s name and address, the title of the invention, the date of filing, and any subsequent amendments or modifications made under this Act. The register references pertaining to abandoned applications shall remain accessible for a period of ten years from the date of abandonment, subject to regulations prescribed by the Government. Further, all assignments and transmissions of utility model rights shall be recorded as distinct entries within the register, creating clear and unambiguous register references for ownership determination. Any party may inspect the relevant portions of this register upon payment of the prescribed fee.

Where an application for registration of a patent is refused under this Act, the applicant shall have the right to appeal to the Appellate Board. Such appeal may be made within sixty days from the date of communication of the order of refusal and shall state specifically the grounds upon which the applicant relies in challenging the decision. The Board shall afford the applicant and any other party interested an opportunity to present their respective cases, including oral arguments, and shall record its findings on each issue raised during the appeal proceedings.

The register references maintained by the Controller are deemed conclusive evidence of the status of patent applications and granted patents subject to any fraud or misrepresentation proven before the Board. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Appellate Board may further petition the Supreme Court under this Act, provided that such petition is filed within ninety days from the date of the order appealed from.

Where the Controller deems it necessary for efficient management of patent applications and granted patents, the records pertaining to such matters may be maintained wholly or partly through digital means. In such cases, any reference under this Act to a document forming part of the register shall include electronic representations thereof stored in accordance with prescribed standards. The public shall have access to these electronically represented documents subject to regulations issued by the Controller regarding security and confidentiality. Furthermore, all entries made within the register, whether physical or digital, shall be considered official records for the purposes of legal proceedings. Any request for inspection of patent application details or granted patents must specify the precise reference numbers required; failure to provide adequate reference information may result in denial of access until clarification is received. The Controller shall publish guidelines regarding acceptable formats for submitting register references.

Where an application for registration of a patent is refused under this Act, the Controller shall maintain a separate register of rejected applications. This register shall contain detailed records pertaining to each such application, including but not limited to the date of filing, applicant’s name and address, subject matter of the invention, reasons for rejection as determined by the Controller, and any subsequent correspondence or procedural actions undertaken. Access to this register of rejected applications shall be conditional upon a written request submitted by an interested party demonstrating a legitimate need for such access, provided that confidential commercial information contained therein shall be protected according to regulations prescribed under this Act. Any alteration to entries in the register references must be authenticated with signatures and dates indicating the responsible officer.

Where any alteration is made to the official register relating to the grant, renewal, lapse, or revocation of a patent, such alteration shall be recorded conspicuously therein, and a corresponding entry made in the index maintained under this Act. Any person aggrieved by an erroneous or unauthorized alteration to the register or its associated indices may file a complaint with the Controller within ninety days of becoming aware of the error. Failure to do so shall preclude them from seeking rectification through legal recourse. The Controller may, after affording the patentee and any other interested party an opportunity for being heard, order such corrections as are deemed necessary. Any person found guilty of making false entries or tampering with register references shall be liable to a fine extending to ten thousand rupees, and imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months.

Where a patentee elects to maintain a digital repository containing comprehensive details pertaining to registered inventions, including but not limited to process variations, material substitutions, and application refinements, such repository shall be considered an official extension of the public register. Any assignment or licensing agreement relating to a patent shall explicitly detail whether the assignor or licensee assumes responsibility for maintaining accurate and up-to-date records within this digital repository. Failure to provide complete and verifiable details regarding any modifications made post-registration may render subsequent enforcement actions subject to review under this Act. The Controller shall maintain a publicly accessible index of all registered repositories, facilitating ease of access for interested parties seeking information related to specific patent register references. This obligation applies equally to corporate entities and individual inventors alike, provided that the digital repository adheres to prescribed data security protocols as determined by the government.

Where an application for registration of a patent is refused under this Act, the Controller shall provide written reasons for such refusal. Any person aggrieved by the decision of the Controller refusing registration may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order. The Appellate Board shall consider any evidence submitted by the appellant and the Controller in relation to the novelty or inventive step of the invention, as well as any arguments pertaining to the clarity and sufficiency of the specification. Furthermore, a challenge to the accuracy of register references contained within the patent application documentation is permissible during such an appeal, subject to demonstrating material prejudice arising from inaccuracies.

For the purposes of this Act, "register references" are defined as notations within the official records maintained by the Controller General relating to applications for patents, granted patents, and related procedural actions. Such references shall include, but not be limited to, identifiers assigned to applicants, inventors, patent numbers, priority dates, filing dates, examination reports, and any amendments or objections recorded under this Act. Where an international application designating India has been processed in accordance with the Budapest Treaty, register references pertaining to such applications shall incorporate information as received from the International Bureau, subject to verification by the Controller General.

Where an application for registration of a breeder registered variety is refused, the applicant may appeal to the Controller within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. The Controller shall consider any objections raised by third parties regarding the distinctiveness or uniformity of the claimed variety and may require further evidence as deemed necessary under this Act. Any person aggrieved by an entry in the register references pertaining to a breeder registered variety, including but not limited to claims of infringement or unauthorized use, shall have the right to file a complaint with the Controller within ninety days from the date such entry became public. The Controller shall investigate such complaints and may order rectification of the register if it finds the entry to be erroneous or misleading, subject to due process and opportunity for all parties to present their case.

For the purposes of this Act, a “form reference act” is defined as an action taken by the Controller or any officer authorized by him under this Act, relating to the acceptance, processing, examination, sealing, advertisement, opposition, or grant of a patent application, and such action shall be recorded in a prescribed form. Where such record is maintained wholly or partly through digital means, reference to the original record as provided herein shall include references to any electronic document or data storage medium containing identical information. The Controller may prescribe the manner in which these records are stored and accessed, subject to ensuring their integrity and accessibility for inspection as per rules framed under this Act.

Where an application for registration of a design relates to a pattern which is primarily dictated by technical function or process, the Controller may require the applicant to furnish evidence demonstrating that such pattern constitutes an aesthetic choice distinct from the functional requirements. For the purpose of determining novelty under this Act, any published description or illustration relating to the design shall be deemed to constitute prior publication. Where a design incorporates elements derived from existing works, a form reference act shall apply; namely, the applicant must provide detailed documentation identifying each source element and demonstrating substantial modification sufficient to establish originality as provided herein. Failure to comply with this requirement may result in rejection of the application.

Where an invention incorporates a design as an integral element thereof, and such design is claimed in a patent application, the Controller may, upon receiving objection from a person alleging prior use or publication of that design, direct the applicant to amend the claims to exclude matter disclosed in the design. Such direction shall be accompanied by a reasoned order detailing the basis for the finding of prior use or publication. The applicant shall have the right to appeal such order under this Act within sixty days. Failure to comply with an amendment directed as per this provision shall render the patent application liable for rejection on grounds of lack of novelty or obviousness, provided that the design element does not constitute a mere form reference act impacting the inventive step. Any person aggrieved by a decision relating to a claim amendment may seek redress through appropriate legal proceedings.

Where an application for registration of a utility model incorporates by reference matter disclosed in a prior publication, the Controller shall require the applicant to furnish certified copies of such publications. Such requirement applies irrespective of whether the incorporated material constitutes an essential element of the claimed invention or relates solely to background information. The applicant shall be afforded a period of ninety days from the date of notification under this Act to comply with this furnishing obligation; failure to do so will render the application liable for rejection. A form reference act, as defined herein, occurs when such incorporated material is not readily accessible through standard library or public domain resources. In instances involving a form reference act, the Controller may direct the applicant to provide an affidavit attesting to the authenticity and completeness of the submitted copies.

Where an application for patent is filed relating to a process by which a substance is produced, the invention disclosed shall be taken to include the composition of matter obtained directly from that process. Provided that, if such a process involves a form reference act wherein the claimed invention relates solely to the method of producing said substance and does not encompass the substance itself, the controller may require the applicant to demonstrate with reasonable certainty that the resulting substance possesses properties substantially different from those previously known or described in prior art. Furthermore, subject to compliance with regulations pertaining to industrial scale production, such a requirement shall be waived if the process is novel and involves an inventive step beyond mere manipulation of existing chemical reactions.

Where a patent is granted incorporating matter disclosed in a prior publication, whether such publication occurred before or after the date of filing of the patent application, and it is established that the invention was not kept confidential as required under this Act, the Controller may, upon complaint by any interested party, direct revocation of the patent. Such direction shall be issued only if it is demonstrated that the prior publication substantially anticipates the claimed invention and constitutes a form reference act impacting novelty. Any person aggrieved by such an order may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of receipt of notice thereof; failure to comply with this provision will render the appeal inadmissible, subject to penalties as provided herein.

Where a patentee elects to utilize a standardized biological sequence as an element within their patented invention, and such sequence is explicitly referenced by its accession number assigned under a recognized international database, the patentee shall be obligated to grant a non-exclusive license for research purposes relating solely to that specific form reference act. This licensing obligation extends to institutions engaged in academic or governmental research, provided that the terms of the license are determined through arbitration as provided herein. The patentee may stipulate reasonable royalties and conditions regarding publication of findings derived from such licensed use. Further, assignment of rights pertaining to this limited license shall be permissible subject to prior notification to the Controller, who may review for compliance with public interest considerations. Any subsequent commercial exploitation based on these research findings remains solely within the purview of the licensee’s own intellectual property protections.

Where an application for patent includes matter derived from a previously published source, whether such publication constitutes prior art shall be determined considering the date of its availability to the public. This determination shall be made irrespective of whether the applicant was aware of said publication at the time of filing. An appeal against any finding that a reference to a published work operates as a form reference act may be made to the Appellate Intellectual Property Tribunal, subject to demonstrating reasonable grounds for believing the tribunal’s initial decision was erroneous in law or fact. The Controller shall provide detailed reasoning justifying any assessment regarding the relevance and impact of such external material on patentability, which reasoning is open to challenge under this Act.

Where an application for registration of a design relates to a pattern which is primarily dictated by technical function or process, the Controller may require the applicant to furnish evidence demonstrating that such pattern constitutes an aesthetic feature independent of its functional characteristics. Such evidence shall include detailed schematics and specifications outlining the manufacturing methodology employed, alongside comparative analyses against functionally equivalent designs lacking distinctive ornamentation. The requirement for form reference act applies equally whether the design is embodied in a three-dimensional article or presented as a two-dimensional motif. Furthermore, if the applicant seeks protection within a Contracting State that has adopted differing standards regarding functional exemptions, the Controller shall consider those standards when assessing compliance under this Act.

Where an application for patent includes subject matter disclosed in a prior publication, whether in printed or electronic form, the controller shall assess novelty under this Act considering such publication as constituting prior art. Provided that, if the applicant demonstrates, through documentary evidence accepted by the controller, that the said publication was made without the consent or knowledge of the applicant and contained information not publicly available before the date of filing of the patent application, the assessment may proceed disregarding the publication. For civil court purposes relating to infringement claims arising from patents granted under these conditions, the burden of proving lack of knowledge on the part of the applicant shall rest upon the claimant. A form reference act is deemed to have occurred when such a prior publication directly informs a claim element.

For the purposes of this Act, “form references act” means the process by which information pertaining to an invention’s subject matter is conveyed through depictions, schematics, drawings, models, or other representational media included within a patent application. Such representations shall be considered integral components for understanding the scope and construction of the claimed invention as provided herein. Where such form references incorporate elements derived from prior art publications, the applicant shall provide detailed annotations identifying these sources and demonstrating their adaptation to the inventive concept. The Controller may require further clarification regarding any ambiguity arising from a form reference act during examination under this Act.

Where an application for registration of a design incorporates elements derived from existing published works, including architectural plans, technical drawings, or photographic representations, such incorporation shall not invalidate the registration provided that the applicant demonstrates a substantial and original transformation of those referenced materials. The Controller may require submission of detailed documentation outlining the sources of form references acted upon in the creation of the design, along with an explanation of the inventive steps undertaken to achieve originality. Failure to provide satisfactory evidence as directed by the Controller shall render the application liable for rejection under this Act. Any challenge to a registered design based on alleged improper use of form references must be filed within six months from the date of publication of the registration.

Where a patent has been granted based on information derived from an earlier publication, whether in printed or electronic form, and such publication discloses the invention as claimed, the patentee shall be liable to pay damages to any person who, prior to the date of application for the patent, relied upon that published information in good faith and acted accordingly. This liability extends to instances where the applicant knowingly incorporated elements from said publication into their claim construction; a form references act is deemed to have occurred when such reliance and action are demonstrably linked. The Controller may, after due inquiry and subject to principles of natural justice, determine the quantum of damages payable, considering factors including but not limited to the extent of commercial exploitation enabled by the patent and the demonstrable loss suffered by the reliant party. Any appeal against this determination shall lie before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

Where an application for patent includes drawings depicting objects or processes, such drawings shall be construed as representations intended solely to illustrate aspects of the invention claimed. The Controller may, at any stage of examination, direct the applicant to provide further clarification regarding any element depicted within said drawings, provided that such direction is accompanied by a reasoned explanation outlining the ambiguity necessitating additional detail. Any reference made under this Act to “the drawing” shall encompass all sheets submitted as part of the application’s technical documentation, irrespective of their sequential order or labeling. The interpretation of claims referencing specific features shown in the drawings shall be governed by principles of form references act, ensuring consistency between textual descriptions and visual representations. Failure to comply with a direction under this provision may result in rejection of the patent application.

Where an application for patent includes drawings depicting functional elements through schematic representations, such representations shall be considered as constituting form references acts under this Act. Such depictions must clearly delineate the operational relationship between components without disclosing inventive steps beyond those explicitly claimed within the specification. The Controller may require applicants demonstrating reliance on form references acts to submit supplementary documentation detailing the underlying principles of operation if clarity is deemed insufficient. Provided that, such requirement shall not impede the grant of a patent where the functional elements are readily ascertainable by persons skilled in the art and do not obscure the essential features of the invention as described herein.

Where a patent application incorporates by reference drawings, diagrams, charts, or other visual representations included as appendices or supplementary materials, such incorporated elements shall be deemed part of the specification for the purposes of novelty assessment and inventive step determination. Any challenge alleging lack of clarity or enablement based on these form references act shall require demonstration that the referenced material is essential to understanding the invention claimed. Failure to provide access to the complete and unaltered version of any referenced document during examination or opposition proceedings will render the patent liable to revocation, subject to a penalty not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees. The Controller may issue directions for ensuring compliance with this provision regarding form references act.

Where a patentee elects to utilize a standardized graphical representation, commonly referred to as a ‘form reference act,’ for depicting aspects of their invention within the patent documentation, such representations shall be considered integral components of the disclosed subject matter. The right to reproduce and distribute these form references acts is governed by this Act and may be assigned or licensed under terms agreed upon between the patentee and any third party. Provided that such assignment or license explicitly acknowledges the originating inventor’s intellectual property rights, it shall not prejudice the validity of the underlying patent. Any subsequent modification or adaptation of a form reference act requires express consent from the original patentee unless such alteration is demonstrably necessary for interoperability with existing technologies as determined by the Controller. The patentee retains ownership of all copyright associated with their created form references acts.

Where an invention incorporates elements derived from prior publications or publicly accessible designs, the question of novelty and inventive step shall be determined with particular regard to what is disclosed therein. Any party alleging a lack of novelty or inventive step under this Act may submit evidence demonstrating that the claimed invention was anticipated by such form references act. The Controller, upon receiving such submission, shall afford the patent applicant an opportunity to rebut the allegations and present counter-evidence establishing the distinctiveness of their contribution. Decisions regarding the impact of prior publications are subject to appeal to the Appellate Board, whose determination shall be final, provided that the appellant demonstrates a substantial prejudice arising from any error apparent on the record.

Where an application for registration of a utility model incorporates by reference material external to the description and claims, the Controller shall determine whether such incorporated material constitutes essential elements for understanding the invention as claimed. The applicant shall be required to furnish certified copies of all documents referenced within the application, and these shall be treated as part of the public record pertaining to the utility model. Failure to provide such documentation within the prescribed time may result in rejection of the application under this Act. A trade mark proprietor claiming rights based on a form references act relating to an incorporated design element must demonstrate that the reference was clear and reasonably discoverable by a person skilled in the art at the date of filing. The Controller may, upon receiving objections from any interested party, require further clarification regarding the scope and relevance of referenced material.

Where a patent application incorporates by reference material not explicitly disclosed therein, such incorporation shall be construed strictly according to the principles of form references act. The applicant shall demonstrate that the incorporated material is essential to understanding and implementing the invention claimed, and that the description adequately conveys the same to a person skilled in the art. Failure to satisfy these conditions renders the referenced material unavailable for consideration during examination or opposition proceedings. Assignment of patent rights, including those pertaining to inventions incorporating external references, shall be governed by the provisions relating to assignment transmission registered under this Act. Any transfer must clearly identify the patented invention and its associated incorporated materials.

Where a patent has been granted based on a design registered under the Designs Act, 2000, and subsequent evidence demonstrates that the invention incorporates elements derived from prior published works, the Controller may, subject to due process, initiate proceedings for revocation. Such proceedings shall be predicated upon demonstrable infringement of form references act principles, establishing an undue reliance on pre-existing designs in the claimed inventive step. Any party aggrieved by a decision under this Act relating to such revocation may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. Failure to comply with orders issued concerning the cessation of manufacture or importation following a successful revocation shall attract penalties as provided herein, including substantial monetary fines and potential imprisonment for repeat offenders.

Where a patentee, prior to grant or publication under this Act, has entered into an agreement for the assignment or licensing of rights pertaining to the invention, such agreement shall be deemed valid notwithstanding any provision regarding form references act relating to the manner of execution. Provided that the assignor or licensor demonstrates, through documentary evidence, that they possessed the right to grant the said assignment or license at the priority date meaning, which is defined as the date on which the application for patent was first filed in India or in a convention country. Further, any subsequent transfer of such assignment or license shall be subject to registration under this Act and shall not prejudice the rights of third parties who have bona fide acquired interests prior to the registration of such subsequent transfer. The Controller may require further affidavits confirming the chain of title for clarity.

Where rectification of the patent register is sought on the grounds of error, misrepresentation, or fraud, an aggrieved party shall be entitled to apply to the Controller for such amendment as may be just and equitable. The application must specify the nature of the alleged error and provide supporting evidence demonstrating its impact upon the rights conferred by the patent. Failure to adequately substantiate the claims within the application will render it liable to dismissal. Particulars comprising register relating to any invention shall be deemed open to inspection, subject to reasonable restrictions as provided herein to protect confidentiality. Any person dissatisfied with the Controller’s decision may appeal under this Act to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. The Board's order shall be final, save for further appeals permitted by law.

The Controller may, at any time, require the patentee to furnish such further particulars relating to an invention as he deems necessary for maintaining the accuracy and completeness of the register. Such particulars shall include, but are not limited to, details regarding manufacturing processes, commercial exploitation, and any modifications made to the originally claimed subject matter. The Controller shall provide a reasonable opportunity to the patentee to comply with such requirement, affording them at least thirty days from the date of notification. Failure to furnish the required particulars within the stipulated period may result in the imposition of a monetary penalty as determined by the Controller. All information submitted under this provision shall be treated as confidential and accessible only to authorized personnel subject to provisions regarding data protection. The particulars comprising register are considered public documents, available for inspection upon application and payment of prescribed fees.

Any person who knowingly furnishes false particulars for inclusion in the register, or who obstructs an officer authorised under this Act in the performance of his duties relating to the maintenance of the register, shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees and may also be subject to imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months. The Controller, upon receiving credible information regarding such false particulars or obstruction, may initiate suo moto proceedings against the offending party. Failure to comply with directions issued by the Controller in connection with rectification of erroneous entries within the prescribed timeframe shall attract daily penalties as determined under this Act. Furthermore, any deliberate misrepresentation affecting the rights of other patent holders will render the perpetrator liable for damages recoverable through civil action. The particulars comprising register are deemed sacrosanct and subject to rigorous verification procedures.

For the purposes of this Act, a “reference act entry” means an inscription recorded by the Controller of Patents upon receipt of a request for rectification relating to a patent granted under this Act. Such request may concern matters including but not limited to alleged errors in the specification, claims, or drawings as originally filed; alterations necessitated by judicial pronouncements concerning the scope of protection afforded by the patent; and modifications required to ensure consistency with international obligations undertaken by the Union of India. The Controller shall maintain a separate register for reference act entries, accessible for public inspection subject to such conditions as may be prescribed.

The Register of Registered Designs maintained under this Act shall contain, for each registered design, a detailed entry specifying the name and address of the proprietor, the title of the design, the date of registration, and a concise description of the features of ornamental character. Such entries are deemed conclusive evidence of the particulars therein stated subject to any fraud or misrepresentation proven before an appropriate authority. Where a reference act entry is made relating to a design incorporating elements derived from prior published works, the Register shall record details pertaining to such source material including its publication date and location. The Controller may, upon application by an interested party, require rectification of any inaccurate information contained within a reference act entry provided that sufficient evidence supporting the claim is presented.

Where an aggrieved party alleges that a patent has been infringed, they may institute proceedings before the relevant High Court, subject to the provisions herein regarding jurisdiction. The court shall afford the patentee an opportunity to present evidence demonstrating validity and ownership of the patent right. Should the court find infringement established, it may grant such remedies as are just and equitable, including permanent injunctions restraining further acts of infringement and orders for accounts of profits derived from the infringing activity. Furthermore, in cases involving wilful infringement, the court shall be empowered to award damages exceeding reasonable compensation, taking into consideration the patentee’s losses and the infringer's gain. A reference act entry concerning prior art disclosures will not preclude remedies if the disclosure was made with fraudulent intent or constitutes a deliberate attempt to circumvent the patent system.

Where an application for registration of a geographical indication is opposed under this Act, the Registrar shall maintain a record of all documents filed by the applicant and the opponent relating to the opposition. Such record shall include, but not be limited to, written submissions, expert reports, and any evidence adduced during hearings. For the purpose of facilitating access to these proceedings and ensuring transparency, the Registrar may publish summaries of the grounds of opposition and responses thereto on the official website maintained by the Controller General. Any party aggrieved by an order made under this Act concerning a geographical indication registration may seek redressal through appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. The record pertaining to each reference act entry shall be deemed public information, subject to restrictions imposed in accordance with applicable data protection legislation and as provided herein.

Where an application for patent is made relating to a process by which a substance is manufactured, the Controller may require the applicant to disclose the best method known to them at the time of making the application for carrying out the invention. Such disclosure shall include details pertaining to raw materials utilized and any ancillary processes integral to the manufacturing procedure. Further, if the invention involves an improvement upon a previously existing process, the applicant shall provide a detailed reference act entry outlining the prior art considered during development. This reference act entry must explicitly identify publications or other publicly available information relied upon in formulating the claimed improvements, subject to the provisions regarding trade secrets as provided herein.

Where an application for rectification of a patent is presented alleging that a reference act entry relating to a prior use publication contains inaccurate information concerning the date of such publication, the Controller shall serve notice on the patentee and the person who made the reference act entry. The respondent may file a counter-statement within the time specified in the notice. Failure by either party to comply with the provisions of the notice shall render them liable for costs incurred by the other party under this Act. Any order altering the date recorded in a reference act entry is subject to appeal to the Appellate Board, and such appeal must be filed within sixty days from the date of the order. The Controller may impose a penalty for wilful misrepresentation made during rectification proceedings.

Where a patentee elects to utilize a compulsory license under this Act for the manufacture and importation of pharmaceuticals primarily intended for export, such license shall be assignable subject to prior approval from the Controller. The assignment may include the transfer of all rights pertaining to the licensed process or product, or a portion thereof, to another entity engaged in pharmaceutical production or research. Any proposed assignee must demonstrate sufficient technical capability and financial stability to ensure compliance with quality standards as prescribed by relevant regulatory authorities. Furthermore, any reference act entry relating to such an assignment shall explicitly detail the original patentee’s continued obligations regarding royalty payments derived from the assigned rights, apportioned appropriately between the assignor and assignee. The Controller may require periodic audits to verify adherence to these stipulations.

Where an application for patent is refused under this Act based on novelty considerations arising from prior publication, the Controller shall provide a detailed written statement outlining the specific publications relied upon and the precise manner in which they undermine the claimed invention. The applicant may then submit a counter-statement disputing the findings of the Controller, accompanied by evidence demonstrating either that the cited publications do not disclose the subject matter of the claim or that the publication was obtained through unauthorized disclosure. Upon receipt of such a counter-statement, the Controller shall consider it and may afford the patentee an opportunity for oral hearing. Any decision made following this process shall be recorded as a reference act entry, accessible for public inspection and subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

Where an application for patent relating to a process by which a substance is produced is opposed under this Act on the ground that the claimed invention does not involve an inventive step, the Controller may, after affording the applicant and opponent an opportunity of being heard, direct that the reference act entry pertaining to the said process be examined by a Board constituted as per sub-regulation (1) of regulation 6. Such examination shall specifically consider whether the cited prior art discloses all elements necessary for carrying out the claimed invention, or whether such disclosure would render the claim obvious to a person skilled in the art. The applicant may appeal against any direction made under this provision, subject to demonstrating prejudice arising from the Board’s involvement and without affecting the validity of any mark registered in relation to the substance produced by the process.

Where an application for registration of a layout design incorporates elements previously disclosed in a published work, a reference act entry shall be made against the record of the registered layout design. This entry will detail the nature and extent of the prior disclosure, including bibliographic information pertaining to the original publication. The Controller may require submission of certified copies of such publications as evidence for inclusion within the reference act entry. Such entries are public documents accessible for inspection at the civil court registry designated by the government, subject to applicable fees and regulations. Any person aggrieved by an inaccurate or incomplete reference act entry may petition the Controller for rectification, providing supporting documentation.

For the purposes of determining patent validity under this Act, an invention shall be considered obvious if, prior to the date of filing of the patent application, a person skilled in the art could have derived the claimed invention from existing knowledge using only straightforward and predictable combinations. This determination shall take into account the totality of the circumstances, including the nature of the problem addressed and the level of ingenuity involved in arriving at the solution. The assessment of whether such derivation was obvious requires consideration of the time elapsed between the publication of relevant prior art and the filing date; a reasonable period shall be deemed to vary according to technological field.

Where an infringement action is brought before a competent court, and the defendant alleges that the patent in question lacks novelty or involves an obvious invention, the patentee shall be entitled to present evidence demonstrating the inventive step. Should the court find, upon review of such evidence, that the alleged lack of novelty or obviousness substantially impacts the scope of the claims as initially granted, it may order a rectification of the patent. This rectification shall clarify the legitimate subject matter protected by the patent. Further, if the defendant demonstrates through credible testimony and documentary proof that attempts to secure a voluntary license from the patentee were made on reasonable terms and conditions, yet remained unsuccessful within a reasonable period, the court may consider this factor in determining damages for infringement. The assessment of what constitutes a reasonable period shall be guided by principles of fairness and equity.

Where an infringement action is brought before a competent court, and it is demonstrated to the satisfaction of the court that the alleged infringer has knowingly exploited a patent without authorization, the court shall order damages equivalent to a percentage of the profits derived by the infringer from such exploitation. This percentage shall be determined based on factors including but not limited to the extent of the infringement, the willfulness thereof, and any attempts made by the infringer to mitigate harm following notification of the infringement. Further, where an attempt to negotiate a license has occurred, failure to reach agreement within a reasonable period shall be considered as evidence of unwillingness to engage in good faith, impacting the assessment of damages. The court may also order the destruction of infringing goods or materials.

Where an invention relating to pharmaceuticals is patented under this Act, the Central Government may, subject to conditions specified therein, require the patentee to grant a license to any interested party willing to manufacture and sell the pharmaceutical product within India. Such requirement shall be predicated upon a determination that the patented invention is not available to the public at affordable prices or in sufficient quantities. The terms of such compulsory license, including royalty payments to the patent holder, shall be determined by the Controller, taking into account factors such as the nature of the invention and the extent of exploitation thereof. A reasonable period shall be allowed for the patentee to comply with a licensing requirement before enforcement actions may be initiated. Provided that any assignment or sub-license granted subsequent to the initial patent grant shall remain subject to these provisions.

Where an application for compulsory license is made, the Controller shall inquire into whether the patentee has been approached by the applicant regarding a license and if so, under what terms. The applicant shall demonstrate that negotiations were undertaken in good faith with the intention of securing access to the patented invention. Further, it shall be established that the proposed royalty or other consideration offered by the applicant did not meet the criteria for patentee reasonable terms as determined by prevailing industry standards and market conditions. The Controller may require both parties to submit detailed financial analyses substantiating their positions regarding appropriate compensation. Subject to this, the application will proceed under this Act.

Where an interested party seeks to challenge the validity of a patent granted under this Act, and demonstrates that the patented invention has not been worked on the territory of India, the Controller may require the patentee to satisfy the Controller as to why compulsory licensing should not be imposed. Such determination shall take into account whether the patentee has made reasonable efforts to work the invention within India, including attempts to assign or license the patent rights. The Controller shall also consider if the patentee has offered the invention for sale at reasonable prices and in sufficient quantities to meet the demands of the market. In assessing whether the patentee has offered the invention on *patentee reasonable terms*, the Controller may examine any licensing agreements entered into by the patentee, or lack thereof.

Where an application for compulsory license is made under this Act, the Controller shall determine whether the patentee has offered a license to the applicant on reasonable terms. For the purpose of such determination, the Controller may consider factors including but not limited to the extent to which the invention addresses unmet needs, the nature and scope of the patentee’s exploitation of the invention within India, and any discriminatory practices employed by the patentee in offering licenses. The term "patentee reasonable terms" shall be interpreted as encompassing a fair balance between the interests of the patentee in receiving adequate compensation for their intellectual property rights and the broader public interest in access to essential technologies. Subject to this, the Controller may direct the patentee to negotiate with the applicant within a specified timeframe, failing which, the Controller may impose terms deemed just and equitable.

Where an interested party seeks to import goods which are the subject matter of a patent, and alleges that the patentee has refused to grant a license for such goods under terms deemed reasonable, they may apply to the Controller for relief. The application shall specify the nature of the patented invention, the proposed importation quantity, and details of attempts made to secure a license from the patentee. Should the Controller find that the patentee has demonstrably failed to offer a license on patentee reasonable terms, or has engaged in practices designed to frustrate such negotiations, they may grant permission for the importation subject to conditions regarding royalty payments to be determined by the Controller. Failure to comply with these conditions shall render the importer liable for penalties as provided herein.

Where the controller is satisfied, upon application made by any person aggrieved, that the patentee has imposed unreasonable terms and conditions relating to the grant of a license under this Act, the controller may direct the patentee to negotiate with such applicant within a specified period. Such negotiation shall be conducted in good faith and with a view towards arriving at mutually acceptable terms. The determination of what constitutes ‘patentee reasonable terms’ shall take into account prevailing market conditions, the extent of research and development undertaken by the patentee, and any prior use or knowledge relating to the invention within India. Provided that nothing herein shall prevent a patentee from seeking compensation commensurate with the value derived from the exploitation of the patented invention. The controller may also direct mediation as a means of resolving disputes concerning licensing terms.

Where an application for compulsory license is made under this Act, the Controller shall inquire into whether the patentee has offered a license to the applicant on patentee reasonable terms and conditions. For the purposes of determining such reasonableness, consideration shall be given to the nature of the invention, the extent of exploitation of the patent, and any impediments to working the patented invention in India. A specification patent shall clearly disclose the best method known to the applicant for performing the invention as claimed, and failure to do so may prejudice the assessment of reasonable terms. The Controller may also consider whether the patentee has engaged in anti-competitive practices that have hindered access to the patented technology.

A patentee granting a licence shall define the terms and conditions governing such grant with precision, including but not limited to the scope of exclusivity conferred, the field of use permitted, and any royalty obligations imposed upon the licensee. Such terms may stipulate limitations on manufacture, sale, or importation as provided herein. The patentee is obligated to ensure that the licence agreement clearly delineates the rights transferred and responsibilities undertaken by both parties; ambiguity in these *licence patent terms* shall be construed against the licensor. Further, any assignment of a patent subject to an existing license requires consent from the original licensee unless otherwise agreed upon in writing.

The Registering Authority shall maintain a comprehensive record of all patent licence agreements entered into concerning inventions protected under this Act. Every such agreement, prior to its implementation, must be submitted for registration within thirty days from the date of execution. The prescribed fee for registration shall be remitted at the time of submission. Registration confers upon the licensee certain rights as provided herein, including the right to enforce the terms and conditions stipulated in the licence patent terms against any infringement by the patentee or third parties. Failure to register a licence agreement does not invalidate it but renders the licensee unable to pursue legal remedies relating to its enforcement under this Act; however, the patentee remains bound by the unregistered agreement.

Where a patentee grants a licence under this Act, the terms and conditions of such licence shall be determined solely between the parties unless those terms are deemed unreasonable or exploitative by the Controller. Any licensee aggrieved by the imposition of unduly restrictive conditions within a licence patent terms may petition the Controller for redressal, demonstrating that the imposed limitations substantially impede the exploitation of the patented invention in India. The Controller may, after affording the patentee an opportunity to be heard, modify such conditions to ensure fairness and promote innovation. Failure by a patentee to comply with the agreed terms or any modification ordered by the Controller shall constitute a breach of contract, rendering them liable for damages as determined by a competent civil court. Further, the Controller may issue directions relating to royalty payments and other financial obligations arising from the licence agreement.

Where a patentee grants a licence relating to an invention for which a patent has been granted under this Act, the terms of such licence shall be governed by the provisions herein. The Controller may, upon receiving a complaint from any aggrieved party alleging unfair or restrictive conditions within a licence patent terms agreement, initiate inquiries and direct the parties involved to submit relevant documentation pertaining to the grant, operation, and termination of the licence. Such directions shall include but not be limited to copies of the licence agreement itself, correspondence relating to its negotiation, and records demonstrating compliance with any stipulated performance metrics. The Controller may also require the patentee or licensee to provide evidence substantiating claims regarding royalty rates or other financial considerations as part of the licensing arrangement. Failure to comply with these directions shall render a party liable to penalties as provided herein.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, a patentee shall have the exclusive right to exploit the patented invention throughout India, but such right shall be granted upon adherence to stipulated terms within the licence agreement. Any licensee operating under a patent license shall comply with all conditions expressly stated in the grant documentation regarding royalty payments, duration of exploitation, and territorial limitations. Further, the patentee may stipulate, as a condition precedent to granting a further sub-licence, that the sublicensee maintains quality control standards equivalent to those employed by the primary licensee, ensuring consistent product specifications. Failure to comply with any term specified within the licence patent terms shall render the license voidable at the discretion of the patentee.

Where a patentee grants a licence relating to an invention and fails to comply with the terms stipulated therein concerning royalty payments or duration of exclusivity, the Controller shall, upon receiving a complaint from any aggrieved party, issue notice to the patentee. The notice shall specify the alleged breach and provide opportunity for response within sixty days. Failure by the patentee to satisfactorily address the concerns raised in the notice may result in revocation of the licence patent terms as determined under this Act. Any person unlawfully exploiting an invention pursuant to a revoked licence shall be liable to pay damages equivalent to three times the present royalty, alongside prosecution for offences cognizable under the Indian Penal Code.

Where a patentee grants a licence under this Act, the terms and conditions of such licence shall be determined solely at the discretion of the parties unless those terms are subsequently challenged before an appropriate judicial forum. Any dispute arising from the interpretation or enforcement of a licence patent terms may be referred to arbitration as agreed upon by both the licensor and licensee; provided that either party may elect to pursue litigation in a court of competent jurisdiction notwithstanding such agreement. The decision of any arbitral tribunal shall be final, subject to appeal on grounds limited to legal error demonstrable during the proceedings. Further, the Central Government may intervene in any such dispute if it deems the terms unduly restrictive or prejudicial to public interest.

The Registering Authority shall, upon receipt of an application for registration of a patent licence agreement, verify compliance with the prescribed format and requisite fees. Such agreements must clearly delineate the scope of rights granted, including territorial limitations and field of use, as specified within the terms of the underlying patent. The applicant shall provide evidence of assignment or consent from all co-patent holders where applicable. Further, any condition imposed relating to certification trade marks used in conjunction with the patented product must be explicitly stated and deemed reasonable under this Act. Failure to adequately define these licence patent terms may result in rejection of registration. An appeal against such a decision lies before the Controller.

Where a patentee grants a licence under this Act, the terms and conditions of such licence shall be binding on both the licensor and licensee, subject to any agreement explicitly stated therein. Any dispute arising concerning the interpretation or enforcement of these licence patent terms may be referred to arbitration as provided herein, with the arbitral tribunal having jurisdiction to award specific performance and damages for breach. The Controller shall established registry for maintaining records pertaining to all licences granted, including details of royalty rates, exclusivity periods, and any sub-licensing arrangements. Failure by a licensee to adhere to the agreed terms may result in revocation of the licence, subject to due process and an opportunity for the licensee to be heard. Further, the patentee shall provide reasonable access to the registry records upon request from interested parties demonstrating a legitimate need.

Where a patentee grants a licence relating to an invention concerning crop sciences, the terms of such licence shall be subject to review under this Act if a complaint is received from any aggrieved party alleging unfair or restrictive practices. Any person demonstrating substantial prejudice arising from unreasonable licence patent terms may petition the Controller for redressal. The Controller may, after affording the patentee an opportunity of being heard, impose penalties including monetary fines not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees and direct modification of the offending clauses. Failure to comply with such directions shall render the licensee liable to further penalties as provided herein and may result in revocation of the licence.

For the purposes of this Act, “export patented pharmaceutical” means the direct shipment from India of a pharmaceutical product that is protected by an active patent under this Act, or corresponding foreign laws, intended for sale outside of India. Such export shall be deemed to include transshipment through another territory, provided that the ultimate destination remains outside Indian jurisdiction. The term "pharmaceutical product" includes any medicinal substance or combination thereof, whether in finished dosage form or bulk drug, manufactured and packaged according to Good Manufacturing Practices as prescribed under this Act. Any application for a compulsory license relating to an export patented pharmaceutical shall be subject to conditions regarding affordability and accessibility in the importing nation.

Where a patentee desires to grant a license or assign the right to manufacture and export patented pharmaceutical products, such license or assignment shall be subject to approval by the Controller. The application for approval under this Act must specify the territory covered by the proposed license or assignment, including details of the intended recipient and their manufacturing capabilities. Provided that any licensee or assignee may subsequently apply to transfer the granted rights, subject to similar review and determination as the initial application. The Controller may impose conditions on such licenses and assignments, ensuring equitable access to essential medicines and preventing anti-competitive practices. Further, where a license is non-exclusive, the patentee shall provide justification demonstrating that the export volume will not prejudice domestic availability of the patented pharmaceutical.

Where an objection is raised under this Act against the grant of a patent concerning a pharmaceutical product, alleging that its manufacture or use would involve infringement of prior art relating to such product’s composition, the Controller may direct the applicant to furnish within a period not exceeding six months, documentary evidence demonstrating freedom to operate in respect of said export patented pharmaceutical. Such direction shall be without prejudice to the applicant's right to appeal under this Act. The determination of whether sufficient evidence has been furnished shall date filing and be conclusive for all purposes, subject to demonstrable fraud or misrepresentation by the applicant. Any party aggrieved by such a determination may prefer an appeal within sixty days from the date of communication thereof.

The Registering Authority, upon receiving an application under this Act pertaining to a compulsory licence exported for a patented invention relating to pharmaceuticals, shall require the applicant to furnish detailed particulars regarding the intended recipient nation and the volume of product destined for export. Such information must include verifiable data demonstrating unmet public health needs within the importing country justifying the issuance of the compulsory licence. The Controller may request further documentation substantiating the non-availability of patented products at a reasonable price or in sufficient quantities within the importing territory. Provided that, any application deemed deficient in these particulars shall be returned to the applicant for rectification and resubmission, subject to prescribed timelines as provided herein.

Where a patentee fails to work a patented invention within the territory of India, or if the patented invention is not readily available to the public at a reasonable price, the Central Government may, subject to conditions as provided herein, grant a compulsory licence exported. Such a compulsory licence shall permit any person to make, use and sell the patented invention solely for export purposes. The application for such a compulsory licence shall be made to the Controller, who shall give notice of the application to the patentee and provide an opportunity for them to present their objections. The Central Government may impose conditions limiting the quantity or type of exported product, provided that these limitations are demonstrably necessary to address the initial concerns regarding non-working or unaffordable access within India. Any person exercising a compulsory licence exported shall be liable for damages to the patentee as determined by the Controller.

Where a patentee fails demonstrably to satisfy the reasonable demands of the Indian market for a patented invention, or where such invention is not made available at a price that is affordable to the public, the Central Government may, after due inquiry and subject to conditions as provided herein, grant a compulsory licence exported. Any entity granted a compulsory licence exported shall be liable to pay royalties to the patentee equivalent to no less than ten percent of the aggregate sales revenue derived from such export, remitted quarterly to a designated government account. Failure to remit these royalties promptly shall constitute an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and a fine not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees; repeated offences will attract enhanced penalties. The Central Government reserves the right to revoke any compulsory licence exported granted under this Act if conditions are violated.

For the purposes of this Act, an “importation patented pharmaceutical” is defined as a pharmaceutical product which is protected by a patent under this Act and which has been imported into India, whether directly or indirectly, from outside India. Such importation shall be deemed to constitute exploitation of the invention for the purposes of determining infringement. Provided that where the importation patented pharmaceutical is intended solely for use in clinical trials conducted with the approval of the Drugs Controller General of India, it shall not be considered as commercial exploitation unless offered for sale within India. As provided herein, any person importing such a product shall comply with all applicable regulations concerning drug registration and import licenses.

The Registering Authority, upon receipt of an application for registration concerning an importation patented pharmaceutical, shall verify that the applicant possesses a valid patent granted under this Act relating to the said pharmaceutical product in the originating jurisdiction. Such verification shall include examination of documentation establishing the date of grant and the term of validity of the foreign patent. The application may be rejected if the Registering Authority finds that the imported pharmaceutical is not identical to the substance disclosed in the foreign patent, or if the applicant fails to demonstrate sufficient control over the importation process as provided herein. Further, registration shall be conditional upon adherence to all relevant regulations pertaining to drug safety and efficacy established by the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization.

Where an importation patented pharmaceutical is found, subject to due process, to infringe a patent valid under this Act, the Customs Officer shall detain such goods pending determination by the Controller. The aggrieved party, being either the patent holder or the importer, may apply to the Controller for a prompt hearing and decision regarding the validity of the infringement claim. Should the Controller determine that an importation patented pharmaceutical does indeed constitute an infringing product, the importer shall be liable to pay damages equivalent to a reasonable royalty, as determined by the Controller, plus costs incurred in the investigation. Further, the Customs Officer may order the seizure and destruction of the infringing goods, provided that such action is taken after affording the importer a reasonable opportunity to present their case. The Controller’s decision under this provision shall be final subject to appeal before the relevant appellate authority.

Where an importation patented pharmaceutical is seized by a Customs Officer at any port or airport, the officer shall immediately notify the Controller of Patents. The Controller may, upon receipt of such notification and after providing reasonable opportunity for hearing to the patentee concerned, issue an order directing the release of the goods pending determination of their status under this Act. Such order shall be accompanied by a direction requiring the importer to furnish security satisfactory to the Central Government, covering any costs or damages that may arise if it is subsequently determined that the importation constitutes an infringement of the patent. The Central Government may, after due consideration of the Controller’s recommendations and representations from interested parties, determine whether the imported pharmaceutical infringes the relevant patent rights as provided herein. Any determination shall be binding on all concerned subject to appeal under the prescribed procedure.

Where an importation patented pharmaceutical is found, subject to the provisions relating to compulsory licensing, to infringe a patent in force under this Act, the Customs Officer at the port of entry shall seize such goods. Any person aggrieved by seizure may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of the order of seizure. Failure to comply with an order issued by the Appellate Board regarding the release or forfeiture of imported patented pharmaceutical products constitutes a cognizable offence and is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and with a fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees. The Central Government may, as provided herein, issue directions relating to the disposal of seized goods.

Where a patent has been granted for an importation patented pharmaceutical, the patentee shall have the right to assign or license such patent, either wholly or partially, to any person, firm, or company, subject to the conditions as provided herein. Any assignment or license shall be in writing and executed by the patentee or their authorized representative, and a certified copy thereof shall be filed with the Patents Office for registration. The Controller may require disclosure of royalty rates and other financial considerations pertaining to such assignments or licenses, particularly where the importation patented pharmaceutical is intended for use within India. Provided that any license granted permitting manufacture within India shall specify the terms governing quality control and adherence to relevant pharmacopoeial standards. Further, the patentee shall ensure that sub-licensees comply with all applicable regulations under this Act relating to drug pricing and availability.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, an importation patented pharmaceutical shall be deemed to infringe a patent if it is knowingly imported into India with the intention to market or distribute it within the territory of India, without the authorization of the patentee. The determination of such intent shall be based on all relevant circumstances surrounding the importation, including but not limited to commercial agreements and marketing strategies employed by the importer. Any party aggrieved by a decision regarding infringement relating to an importation patented pharmaceutical may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order; provided that the appellate board may, at its discretion, entertain appeals filed after the expiry of such period if satisfactory reasons for the delay are furnished.

Where an importation patented pharmaceutical is found, subject to the provisions regarding process patents under this Act, to infringe a specification patent already granted in India, the importer shall be deemed guilty of an offence. Such offence carries a penalty not exceeding two thousand rupees for each infringing unit imported and a further fine determined at the discretion of the Court. Repeated offences may result in imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months. The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, prescribe measures to prevent circumvention of this provision relating to importation patented pharmaceuticals. Any person aggrieved by an order made under these provisions may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, a patentee may grant licences relating to their invention, including licences permitting the manufacture, use, or sale of the patented product outside India. Such licences may be exclusive or non-exclusive, assignable or unassignable, as determined by the terms stipulated in the licence agreement. Where a patentee seeks to export goods manufactured under a compulsory license granted under this Act, they shall provide detailed documentation to the Controller outlining the intended destination country and quantity of exported products. The Controller may require further information deemed necessary to ascertain compliance with relevant international trade regulations. Any assignment of rights relating to a licence export patented invention shall be recorded in the prescribed manner, conferring upon the assignee all rights and obligations previously held by the assignor.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, a compulsory license export may be granted where the reasonable requirements of the importing country have not been satisfied. For the purposes of this section, “reasonable requirements” includes consideration of the quantity needed, affordability, and accessibility of the patented product within that importing nation. An application for a compulsory licence export shall include detailed information regarding the specific circumstances justifying such authorization, including evidence demonstrating the inadequacy of voluntary licenses or other means to meet the importing country's needs. The Central Government may prescribe conditions relating to pricing, technology transfer, and public health considerations as deemed necessary under this Act.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, an application may be made to the Controller by any person seeking authorization for a compulsory licence export of a patented invention. Such application shall specify the patented product, the intended exporting nation, and the quantity proposed for export, demonstrating reasonable attempts to secure a voluntary license from the patentee. The Controller shall consider whether the patented invention addresses an unmet need in the importing country and if the patentee has not granted a voluntary licence within a reasonable period. A notification of such application shall be served upon the patentee, who may submit objections. The Controller’s decision regarding the compulsory licence export shall be recorded and published as provided herein.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, a compulsory license may be granted for the purpose of enabling import or export of a patented invention relating to pharmaceuticals or agricultural implements, where such import or export is deemed necessary by the Central Government to address a national emergency or other circumstance of exceptional import.
