Failure to remit such fees may result in the application being deemed abandoned or any proceedings stayed until full payment is received. Where an applicant seeks to grant a licence relating to the trade mark applied for, evidence of the proposed licensing agreement shall be submitted alongside proof that the act fee paid pertaining to the initial application remains current and valid. The Registrar may require updated documentation demonstrating continued compliance with these provisions at any stage during examination or registration proceedings, provided that such requests are made within a reasonable timeframe.

For the purposes of this Act, "trade mark" means a mark capable of being represented graphically and which is used or proposed to be used, directly or indirectly, in connection with goods or services to identify and distinguish those goods or services of one undertaking from those of others and shall include a service mark; provided that such marks are not merely descriptive of the characteristics of the goods or services. The right conferred by registration protection trade marks shall extend to the territory of India and any other territory in which the trade mark is used, or has been previously used, subject to limitations as may be prescribed under this Act.

For the purposes of this Act, “issuing notice sub” shall mean the process by which the Registrar transmits a communication to a registered trade mark proprietor concerning a proposed rectification or alteration of their registration. Such notice shall be issued in writing and contain particulars of the application for rectification, including details of the applicant and the grounds relied upon. The Registrar may, subject to any procedural requirements as provided herein, serve such notice by post to the address specified in the register or electronically if permitted under regulations framed by the Trade Marks Board. Failure to comply with these provisions shall not invalidate subsequent proceedings before the India Registrar.

For the purposes of this Act, a “registration proprietor” means the person entered in the Register of Designs as the registered owner of a design, and such person shall be deemed the exclusive legal owner of that design throughout India, subject to any rights or licenses granted under this Act. The registration proprietor may enforce against all others any civil remedy available under law relating to the infringement of the design. Where a design is registered by an agent on behalf of another party, that other party shall be considered the registration proprietor provided that such agency is disclosed in the application for registration as required herein.

An application for registration of a design may be filed by any person claiming to be the creator or owner of the design, or by a registered proprietor seeking to extend the term of protection. Where an application is filed by a person other than the original creator, such applicant shall provide evidence satisfactory to the Controller establishing their right to apply under this Act, including assignment documents duly executed and notarized. The registration proprietor shall be entitled to exclusive rights relating to the design as specified herein, preventing unauthorized reproduction or use thereof for commercial purposes. Any alteration to a registered design requires notification to the Controller and may necessitate further examination before any amended registration is granted. The Controller may require additional information from the applicant concerning the novelty of the design.

Where any person considers that the registration of a design has been wrongly granted, or that any act restricted by this Act has been wrongfully done in relation to a registered design, such person may prefer an appeal to the High Court within sixty days from the date on which such decision was communicated to him. The High Court shall have the same jurisdiction and authority as it would possess in respect of original suits relating to matters of like nature under this Act. Any order made by the High Court affirming, reversing or modifying a decision may be enforced by that Court in manner similar to decrees. Further, where an infringement of design rights occurs, the registration proprietor shall be entitled to seek remedies including injunctions and damages as provided herein, subject to limitations on recoverable sums determined according to prevailing legal principles. The right to sue for such relief accrues only to the registered proprietor or their duly authorized agents.

An application for rectification of a registered design may be presented to the Controller by any person aggrieved, subject to payment of the prescribed fee. Such application shall state specifically the grounds on which it is founded and shall be accompanied by copies of all relevant documents substantiating the claim. The Controller may entertain such an application only if the applicant demonstrates standing as a person demonstrably prejudiced by the registration. Where the application seeks to challenge the validity of the design, the Controller shall serve notice upon the *registration proprietor* and afford them an opportunity for response within the time specified under this Act. Any party aggrieved by an order made by the Controller may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order. The Appellate Board’s decision shall be final and binding, provided that it does not contravene any provision of law.

Where an application for registration of a design is granted, the person to whom the certificate of registration is issued shall be deemed to be the registration proprietor thereof and shall have exclusive right to exploit the registered design in accordance with the provisions herein. The registration proprietor may assign the entire design or any part thereof, along with the benefit of the registration, to another party subject to compliance with prescribed formalities and payment of requisite fees as determined by the government. Any alteration made to the registered design without prior notification and approval from the Controller shall render the registration proprietor liable for penalties under this Act. Furthermore, the registration proprietor is obligated to renew the registration periodically, failing which it shall be deemed lapsed.

Any person who, without the consent of the registration proprietor, applies any process for the manufacture or use of an article in which a registered design is incorporated, or offers to sell such articles, or does otherwise infringe upon the exclusive right of the registration proprietor to exploit the design, shall be deemed to have committed an offence under this Act. Such infringement includes the importation or distribution within India of any article made or imported by him containing a copy of the registered design. The Controller may, on receiving a complaint from the registration proprietor, issue orders restraining such infringing activities and direct the seizure and destruction of goods embodying the design. Penalties for first offences shall include fines not exceeding fifty thousand rupees; subsequent offences will attract penalties up to one hundred thousand rupees and imprisonment extending to six months.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and the regulations framed thereunder, a registration proprietor may grant licenses relating to the registered design, specifying the scope of such license including but not limited to the territory within which the licensee may exploit the design. Such licenses shall be assignable in accordance with the procedures prescribed herein, provided that any assignment or sub-license granted without the prior written consent of the Controller shall be deemed void. The registration proprietor shall provide a copy of the license agreement to the Controller upon request and maintain records pertaining to all assignments and sub-licenses for a period of not less than five years from the date of such transaction. Further, any person acquiring an interest in the design through assignment or otherwise shall be subject to the same obligations as the original registration proprietor under this Act.

Where a person aggrieved by an order passed by the Registrar refusing registration or revoking registration under this Act appeals to the Appellate Board, the appeal shall lie within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order. The Appellate Board may, after giving notice to all parties concerned and affording them an opportunity of being heard, confirm, modify, or reverse the order appealed against, subject to just considerations. Any party dissatisfied with the decision of the Appellate Board may further appeal to the High Court within a period of ninety days from the date of that decision. The registration proprietor shall be deemed to hold title to the design only upon successful completion of the registration process and payment of prescribed fees; any challenge to this title is subject to judicial review as provided herein.

An application for registration of a design may be filed by any person claiming to be the owner of the design or by any manufacturer authorized by the claimant. Where an application is presented by a person other than the true and first inventor, he shall provide satisfactory evidence to substantiate his claim under this Act. The Controller shall, upon receiving such an application, initiate proceedings prosecution in accordance with the prescribed procedures. Upon successful completion of these proceedings and satisfaction that the design is registrable, the registration proprietor shall be entered into the Register of Designs. Any person aggrieved by a decision relating to the acceptance or rejection of an application may appeal to the relevant appellate authority as provided herein.

Where a design is registered, the person by whom the design is so registered shall be deemed to be the registration proprietor thereof and shall have the exclusive right to use or apply the design. Any other person infringing such right may be restrained by injunction as provided herein. The registration proprietor shall be entitled to recover damages from any party who has infringed their design rights, calculated on the basis of lost sales and profits attributable to the infringement. Further, where an unregistered design is deceptively similar to a registered design, creating confusion amongst consumers regarding trade mark identity, the Controller may order the infringer to pay compensation reflecting such misleading presentation. The registration proprietor shall be responsible for maintaining the validity of their registration through timely renewal fees.

An application for registration of a design shall be accompanied by such information and drawings as the Registrar may prescribe, detailing the aesthetic characteristics of the design and its intended use. Where an applicant has previously filed an identical or substantially similar design, the Controller may require submission of further documentation demonstrating distinctiveness under this Act. The registration proprietor is deemed to hold exclusive rights relating to the registered design for the duration specified herein, preventing unauthorized reproduction, adaptation, or exploitation thereof. Any person aggrieved by a decision regarding an application registration may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of such decision. The Registrar shall maintain a register of designs, accessible for public inspection subject to prescribed fees and conditions. Further, the Controller may, upon receiving credible evidence, initiate inquiries into potential infringements of registered design rights.

Where a design is registered under this Act, the person whose name appears as the applicant in the Register of Designs shall be deemed to be the registration proprietor thereof. The registration proprietor shall be entitled to exercise all rights and privileges pertaining to the design, subject to any conditions stipulated during the application process or subsequent amendments. An alleged offence relating to infringement of a registered design may be investigated by an officer authorized under this Act, who shall record statements from relevant parties and seize materials deemed pertinent to the inquiry. The registration proprietor shall provide such assistance as reasonably requested by the investigating officer in relation to any investigation undertaken. Failure to comply with reasonable requests for information or access constitutes an impediment to the due administration of justice.

An application for rectification register may be made by any person aggrieved by an entry in the Designs Register, or by a refusal to rectify such entry. Such application shall specify the particulars of the entry sought to be rectified and the grounds on which it is claimed that the entry is erroneous or should be amended. The applicant shall furnish evidence supporting the claim for rectification, as provided herein. Rectification register proceedings are subject to natural justice, ensuring both parties an opportunity to present their case. Any decision regarding rectification register shall be recorded in writing and communicated to all affected parties.

An application for rectification register may be filed by any person aggrieved by an entry appearing in the Designs Register, subject to compliance with the prescribed forms and fees. Such applications shall specify the particulars of the entry sought to be rectified and state the grounds on which such rectification is claimed, including instances where the design lacks novelty or originality as defined under this Act. The Controller may entertain any application for rectification register if satisfied that it involves a substantial question relating to the registrability of a design. Notice of the application shall be served upon the registered proprietor in the prescribed manner, allowing them an opportunity to file their response within a stipulated period. Any order made by the Controller concerning the rectification register is appealable before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

An aggrieved party seeking rectification register concerning a registered design may institute proceedings before the Controller, subject to payment of the prescribed fee. The application for rectification must specify the particulars of the entry in the register sought to be rectified and the grounds upon which such rectification is claimed, including evidence substantiating the claim. Failure to adequately demonstrate prima facie validity or novelty as per this Act shall render the application liable to dismissal without further hearing. The Controller may, after affording a reasonable opportunity for all interested parties to present their case and cross-examine witnesses, order rectification of the register if satisfied that the entry is erroneous or contrary to established law. Any party aggrieved by an order made under this provision may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days.

An application for rectification of register may be made by any person aggrieved by an entry or omission in the Designs Register. Such application shall be in Form D and accompanied by a statement specifying the grounds upon which the applicant relies, supported by all relevant documents and evidence. The application must be presented to the Controller within six months from the date of the publication of the design in the Designs Journal, subject to an extension granted by the Controller for reasons deemed sufficient.

The Controller shall serve notice of the application on the registered proprietor, affording them a reasonable opportunity to file a counter-statement. Proceedings relating to rectification shall be conducted as nearly as may be in accordance with the procedure followed in suits before ordinary courts of law. The Controller’s decision regarding the rectification register is final and binding, provided that an appeal lies to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order.

Any person aggrieved by an entry in the Designs Register, or by a refusal to enter a design, may apply to the Controller for rectification of register. Such application shall specify the grounds upon which it is based and shall be accompanied by such fees as may be prescribed. The Controller shall give notice of the application to the concerned party and afford them an opportunity of being heard, subject to just cause shown. Failure to comply with a direction issued under this Act concerning rectification proceedings constitutes an offence punishable with imprisonment or fine, or both. Any order made by the Controller regarding rectification register is final, provided that an appeal lies to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order.

Where a registered proprietor of a design seeks to assign or license the right to apply for rectification register entries, such assignment or license shall specify clearly the scope of the rights transferred, including whether it extends to specific designs listed in the register or encompasses all designs registered under the proprietor’s name. Any subsequent transfer of that assigned right, relating to an application for rectification register, requires prior written consent from the original registered proprietor, unless otherwise stipulated within the initial assignment agreement. The Controller may, subject to due process and providing opportunity for hearing, grant a rectification register entry based on an application filed by a licensee acting under such authority, provided that the license explicitly authorizes this action and the underlying design remains valid as per provisions of this Act. Failure to disclose relevant details in any assignment or license concerning rectification register applications shall render it voidable at the discretion of the Controller.

An application for rectification of the register shall be deemed inadmissible if it is not accompanied by an affidavit verifying the truthfulness of the statements made therein and specifying the grounds upon which the applicant relies; provided that the Controller may, subject to just cause shown, entertain such an application notwithstanding this omission. Any party aggrieved by an order passed under this Act relating to rectification register may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. The Appellate Board shall consider any evidence submitted by either party and may direct the Controller to rehear the matter or substitute its own decision, subject to principles of natural justice.

An application for rectification register may be filed by any person claiming an interest in a registered design, or by the proprietor of a design that is substantially similar to a design already on record. Such applications shall specify the particulars of the entry sought to be rectified and the grounds upon which it is claimed that the entry is erroneous or otherwise requires amendment. Where the application relates to a package incorporating a registered design, the applicant must clearly delineate the elements constituting the design as applied to said package in the rectification request. The Controller may require further information or clarification regarding the proposed rectification. Provided that the application complies with all requirements under this Act and the rules made thereunder, it shall be processed according to established procedures.

Any person aggrieved by an entry in the Designs Register, or by a failure to make an entry, may apply to the Controller for rectification of register. Such application shall specify the grounds upon which it is based and shall be accompanied by such fees as may be prescribed. The Controller shall afford the applicant and any other interested party an opportunity of being heard under this Act. Where the rectification sought involves a matter relating to priority established under the Budapest Treaty, the Controller shall consider evidence pertaining to international design applications and registrations. Failure to comply with procedural requirements regarding service of notice or representation may result in dismissal of the application. The Controller’s order concerning rectification register is final subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

An application for rectification register concerning a registered design may be filed by any person claiming an interest, subject to compliance with prescribed forms and fees. Such applications must specify the particulars of the entry sought to be rectified and state the grounds upon which such rectification is claimed, including demonstrable errors or misrepresentations in the original registration. The Controller shall, upon receipt of an application, initiate a procedure investigation into the matter, affording the registered proprietor an opportunity to submit their response within sixty days. Any evidence presented must adhere strictly to evidentiary standards as provided herein and be relevant to the claim for rectification. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in rejection of the application or further procedural delays.

Any person aggrieved by an entry in the Designs Register, or by a failure to enter particulars relating to a design, may apply to the Controller for rectification of register. Such application shall specify the grounds upon which it is based and shall be accompanied by such fees as prescribed under this Act. The Controller may, after giving notice to all interested parties and affording them an opportunity of being heard, order rectification as claimed or otherwise dispose of the matter in conformity with principles of natural justice. Failure to comply with any direction issued by the Controller concerning rectification register proceedings constitutes a punishable offence, attracting penalties as determined under this Act. The layout design government may intervene in such matters where public interest is concerned.

For the purposes of this Act, "prejudicial security india" with regard to a design shall mean information pertaining to the aesthetic characteristics or functional features of a design that, if disclosed, would reasonably be expected to compromise national defense capabilities, critical infrastructure protection, or essential government services. Any officer receiving an application for registration may require the applicant to submit a declaration affirming that the design does not incorporate elements constituting prejudicial security india. The Registrar shall have the power to withhold publication of any such information and may refer concerns regarding potential prejudicial security india to the designated authority as provided herein.

An applicant seeking registration of a design shall furnish with the application particulars detailing the manufacturing process employed in its creation, including materials utilized and anticipated production costs. The Registrar may, upon receiving credible intelligence suggesting that the proposed design’s registration poses a demonstrable threat to national security or economic stability, initiate an inquiry into the matter. Such inquiries are without prejudice to any other proceedings under this Act. If, following such inquiry, it is determined that the design's dissemination would constitute a prejudicial security india risk, the Registrar shall refuse registration and provide written reasons for said refusal. The applicant may appeal against this decision before the relevant appellate authority as provided herein.

Where an application for registration of a design is deemed likely to compromise national interests, the Controller shall have power to require the applicant to furnish security. Such security shall be determined at the discretion of the Controller, but cannot exceed two times the prescribed fee for registration. The amount so secured may be forfeited if the applicant subsequently fails to comply with any direction issued under this Act concerning the design’s publication or modification, or if information provided during examination is found to be false and materially affects the assessment of novelty. Any security furnished shall be deemed prejudicial security india if it relates directly or indirectly to designs incorporating elements derived from sources accessible within foreign jurisdictions posing a threat to India's strategic autonomy. The Controller may demand further assurances as he deems necessary.

Where an application for registration of a design is deemed likely to affect national interests, the Designs Registrar shall refer the matter to the Secretary, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, for assessment. The Secretary may, after consultation with such authorities as they deem appropriate, recommend whether or not a prejudicial security india exists concerning the proposed design. Such recommendation shall be binding on the Designs Registrar in respect of proceeding further with the application. If the Registrar is satisfied that the registration of the design would compromise the operational capabilities or strategic assets of India, the application may be rejected outright. Any party aggrieved by such rejection may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. The Board’s decision shall be final and binding.

Where an application for registration of a design is pending, and information comes to the attention of the Controller indicating that the applicant’s activities relating to the proposed design pose a demonstrable threat to national economic stability or constitute a prejudicial security india, the Controller may require the applicant to furnish a bond or other security deemed appropriate. Such security shall be in an amount determined by the Controller, taking into consideration the potential impact on affected industries and the cost of monitoring compliance. The applicant shall provide documentation substantiating their financial standing and operational procedures within thirty days of notification. Failure to comply with this requirement may result in suspension of processing of the application until such time as satisfactory evidence is submitted, subject to a written appeal to the Controller.

Any person found to be engaging in activities that undermine the integrity of registered designs or applications pending examination shall be subject to penalties as provided herein. Such activities include, but are not limited to, the deliberate dissemination of false information intended to mislead examiners or the public regarding the novelty or originality of a design. Furthermore, any financial instrument or transaction used to facilitate such deceptive practices may be deemed to constitute prejudicial security india and shall be immediately frozen pending investigation by the designated authority. The Central Government may issue directives compelling individuals possessing knowledge of such activities to disclose relevant information, subject to due process protections as guaranteed under the Constitution. Repeat offenders face enhanced penalties including imprisonment and forfeiture of assets.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, the proprietor of a registered design shall be entitled to grant licenses granting rights to exploit the design commercially, specifying the territory within which such exploitation is permitted. Any license granted under this Act may be exclusive or non-exclusive, as determined by the grantor, and shall clearly define the scope of permissible activities, including but not limited to manufacture, sale, import, and use. Furthermore, a proprietor may assign their entire design registration, or any rights pertaining thereto, to another party through a written instrument duly executed. Such assignment shall be recorded with the Controller of Designs. The Central Government may, in circumstances deemed prejudicial security india, direct that a license be granted on terms and conditions determined by it, ensuring continued access to essential designs for national purposes.

Where an objection is raised against the grant of design protection on grounds of national security, the Controller shall afford the applicant an opportunity for a hearing, subject to the proviso that the proceedings may be conducted in camera if deemed necessary by the Controller. Any determination made under this Act concerning prejudicial security india shall be accompanied by reasoned findings, detailing the specific threat assessment and the nexus between the design’s features and the identified risk. The applicant aggrieved by such a determination may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days of receipt of the order. The Board's decision shall be final, provided that it is not challengeable under any other law for the time being in force.

An applicant for design registration shall furnish with the application a declaration verifying the novelty and originality of the design claimed. Where an application contains features that are deemed prejudicial security india, the Registrar may require the applicant to submit further documentation substantiating the non-infringing nature of the design. Such documentation must be submitted within thirty days from the date of notification under this Act. Failure to comply with this requirement shall render the application liable for rejection. The application date shall be considered as the date on which the complete application, including all required declarations and supporting documents, is received by the Registrar. Any subsequent amendment affecting the design’s claimed novelty must be accompanied by an updated declaration.

Where an application for registration of a design is deemed to pose a potential threat to national economic interests or constitutes a prejudicial security india, the Designs Office shall immediately notify the relevant investigative agency as defined under the National Security Act. The applicant shall then be afforded a period of thirty days from the date of such notification within which to submit representations demonstrating that the design does not present the claimed risk. Failure to adequately address concerns raised by the investigative agency may result in suspension of processing, and ultimately rejection of the application. Further, any registered design subsequently determined to constitute a prejudicial security india is subject to compulsory licensing for public use, as provided herein. The patent office shall maintain strict confidentiality regarding all information pertaining to such investigations.

An application for registration of a design shall be deemed abandoned if the Controller is satisfied that the applicant has engaged in activities demonstrably undermining national economic stability or posing a threat to public order. Such determination shall be made after affording the applicant an opportunity for a hearing and presentation of evidence, as provided herein. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish security, not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees, to ensure compliance with any undertaking given during such proceedings. This security may be forfeited if the applicant fails to comply with directions issued by the Controller or provides false information. Where an application is abandoned due to prejudicial security india concerns, the design shall remain unregistrable for a period of ten years from the date of abandonment. Further, applications filed under the Madrid Protocol relating to designs deemed detrimental to India’s interests are subject to this provision and may be rejected outright.

Where an application for registration of a design is deemed likely to affect national interests, the Controller shall require the applicant to furnish security, the amount thereof being determined based on factors including the potential commercial impact and scope of the design’s claims. Such security shall be considered prejudicial security india if it is found that its forfeiture would compromise the sovereignty or integrity of India, or disrupt relations with a foreign state. The Controller may, at any time, demand further security from an applicant already providing such assurance, subject to due process and opportunity for hearing. Failure to comply with this requirement regarding the provision of adequate security shall render the application liable for rejection under this Act.

The proprietor of a registered design shall be entitled to grant licenses conferring rights to utilize the protected design for commercial purposes, subject to conditions stipulated within the license agreement. Such licenses may be exclusive or non-exclusive, and the terms thereof shall be binding on both licensor and licensee as provided herein. Assignment of design registration is permissible with prior written consent from the Controller, and any such assignment must disclose full details of the assignor and assignee. Further, where a licensed use demonstrably involves used falsifying trade by creating confusion amongst consumers regarding the origin or characteristics of goods, the Controller may review the license terms and impose remedial conditions to safeguard public interest. The Central Government may order temporary suspension of design rights if the proprietor’s conduct is deemed prejudicial security india, pending investigation into allegations of misuse impacting national economic stability.

The Registrar shall exercise all powers necessary for the discharge of his functions under this Act, including but not limited to, receiving applications for registration of geographical indications, conducting examinations as to distinctiveness and suitability for registration, and affording opportunities for interested parties to submit objections. The Registrar may request information from any person or authority relevant to the determination of an application’s merits. Any decision made by the Registrar concerning the acceptance or rejection of an application, or regarding rectification proceedings, shall be subject to appeal under this Act. The functions registrar act includes maintaining a register of registered geographical indications and ensuring compliance with provisions relating to use and enforcement.

Applications for registration of a geographical indication shall be made to the Registrar in the prescribed form and accompanied by the requisite fee. The applicant shall furnish evidence demonstrating that the quality, reputation or other characteristic of the goods originates from the specified geographical origin. Upon receipt of an application, the Registrar may direct the applicant to submit further particulars or clarifications deemed necessary for assessment under this Act. The functions registrar act includes publication of the application in the Geographical Indications Journal and inviting objections from interested parties within a stipulated period. Any opposition received shall be considered by the Registrar after providing the applicant with an opportunity to file its response, following principles of natural justice as provided herein.

Any proprietor seeking rectification of a registered geographical indication alleging that entry is erroneous or obtained through misrepresentation shall file an application before the Registrar. The Registrar may, after giving notice to all interested parties and affording them an opportunity of being heard, direct amendment or cancellation of the register as provided herein. An appeal from any order made by the Registrar under this Act lies to the Appellate Board. Where a geographical indication is used in contravention of this Act, the proprietor of the registration may institute suit for damages recoverable subject to such limitations as are prescribed. The functions registrar act includes the power to issue interim injunctions restraining such use pending final determination of the matter before the court or the Appellate Board.

An application for registration of a geographical indication shall contain particulars relating to the name of the agricultural product or good concerned, the territory from which it originates, the qualities, reputation or other characteristics directly attributable to its origin, and the producers, dealers or traders involved in ensuring its authenticity. The Registrar may require the applicant to furnish further information deemed necessary for assessing compliance with the provisions under this Act. Should the Registrar find that the proposed geographical indication is descriptive of the product’s common name or qualities, or if it conflicts with existing trademarks, registration shall be refused. The functions registrar act in examining applications and determining eligibility are subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

The initial registration of a geographical indication, as provided herein, remains valid for a term not exceeding thirty years from the date of its original grant. Renewal of this registration may be sought by the registered proprietor prior to the expiry of the said period, subject to payment of prescribed fees and demonstration that continued use of the indication is occurring within the defined geographical area. Failure to demonstrate such ongoing usage shall constitute grounds for refusal of renewal. Upon expiration registration, any person who, without authorisation, applies the protected geographical indication to identical goods or uses it in a manner likely to cause confusion may be subject to civil action and damages as determined by an appropriate forum. The registered proprietor retains standing to enforce these rights during the period of validity and for three years thereafter.

The initial registration of a geographical indication, as provided herein, shall remain valid for a term not exceeding thirty years from the date of its original grant. An application for renewal may be submitted to the Registrar within one year preceding the expiration registration date. Such an application must include any necessary alterations to the particulars of the registered proprietor or the area of production defining the geographical indication. The Registrar, after affording due opportunity for hearing to all interested parties, may approve or reject the renewal application. If approved, the registration shall continue for a further period of thirty years from the date of expiration registration. Any objection to a renewal application must be filed within two months of its publication in the Geographical Indications Journal. Failure to comply with these procedural requirements may render the renewal invalid under this Act.

The owner of a registered geographical indication may, subject to any conditions specified therein, grant exclusive licenses relating to the use of the indication for specific goods or services. Such licenses shall be assignable by the licensor, provided that prior written consent of the registering proprietor is obtained from the licensee. Upon the expiration registration of a geographical indication, any license granted prior thereto shall continue in force for a period not exceeding five years from the date of such expiration, unless earlier terminated by mutual agreement between the licensor and licensee or by order of the Geographical Indications Registry. Further, an assignment of a license under this Act requires notification to be filed with the Registry within thirty days of its execution; failure to do so shall render the assignment void. The registering proprietor may revoke any license granted if the licensee acts in contradiction to the conditions specified therein.

The registration of a Geographical Indication, once granted under this Act, shall remain valid for a term not exceeding thirty years. Renewal may be sought prior to the expiration registration date, subject to payment of prescribed fees and demonstration that continued protection remains necessary to prevent misuse or unfair competition. Failure to file renewal applications within the stipulated timeframe will result in automatic lapse of rights. Any person utilizing a registered Geographical Indication without authorization after such lapse shall be liable for damages, including compensation for loss of reputation associated with trade mark relations, and may face prosecution under relevant penal provisions as provided herein. Repeated or willful infringements shall attract enhanced penalties and potential injunctions.

For the purposes of this Act, an “unregistered geographical indication” means a geographical indication which is not registered under this Act and includes any indication that misrepresents the true origin of goods, even if such indication does not conform to the established standards for production or quality characteristic of the genuine article. An unregistered geographical indication shall be deemed to create unfair competition when it exploits the reputation, goodwill, or other characteristics associated with a registered geographical indication relating to identical or similar goods. Any use of an unregistered geographical indication in commerce shall be subject to review under this Act if such use is likely to cause confusion among consumers regarding the origin of the goods.

An application for registration of a geographical indication may be filed by any association of persons, cooperative society, producer company, or other organization engaged in production, processing, and marketing of goods originating from that territory, or by an individual authorized by such producers. The Registrar shall refuse registration if the proposed geographical indication is deemed to be descriptive of characteristics of the goods, qualities, reputation, or other attributes associated with them, or if it comprises surnames or pseudonyms without authorization. Further, registration shall not be granted for any *unregistered geographical* indication which would be likely to cause confusion amongst consumers regarding the origin of the goods. The applicant must demonstrate exclusive rights over the use of the proposed indication within the defined geographical area as provided herein.

Any proprietor of a registered geographical indication may institute civil proceedings for relief from acts constituting detrimental use, including but not limited to the application of signs likely to cause confusion with the registered geographical indication, or misrepresentation concerning the origin of goods. Where an unregistered geographical indication is used in commerce in relation to goods identical with those for which the registration is sought, and such use constitutes a likelihood of deception as to the origin of such goods, any interested party may apply to the relevant court for an injunction restraining further use. The remedies available under this Act shall include damages sustained by the proprietor due to the detrimental use, taking into account the commercial value of the registered indication. Provided that, nothing herein shall prevent a person from lawfully using a geographical name which does not falsely suggest an association with the registered indication.

An application for registration of a geographical indication may be filed with the Registrar by any association of persons, cooperative society, producer company, or individual authorized by such associations or societies representing the interests of the producers of the goods concerned. The applicant shall furnish particulars demonstrating that the said indication is primarily associated with a definite geographical locality and enjoys reputation due to unique qualities originating from that location. Where an objection is raised against registration on the ground that the proposed geographical indication is descriptive of the goods, the applicant may submit counter-arguments and evidence establishing distinctiveness acquired through long usage. The Registrar shall consider such objections and submissions before proceeding with examination. Protection under this Act extends only to registered geographical indications; no protection is afforded to an *unregistered geographical* indication. Any person aggrieved by an order of the Registrar may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of receipt of that order.

Any collective body seeking registration of a geographical indication relating to agricultural products, foodstuffs, wine, spirits, beverages, or spices shall submit an application demonstrating exclusive quality, reputation, or other characteristic of the goods attributable essentially to the origin of such goods within the defined geographical area. The application must include a map clearly delineating the boundaries of the geographical area and a detailed description of the production method employed, conforming strictly to traditional practices as documented by the relevant agricultural authority. Registration shall be refused if the proposed name conflicts with an existing trademark or is deemed deceptive regarding the true origin of the goods; furthermore, protection under this Act does not extend to use by any producer located outside the specified geographical area unless authorized by the registered proprietor and compliant with conditions prescribed herein. An unregistered geographical indication may still be subject to action for unfair competition.

Any individual or enterprise utilizing a name susceptible to be mistaken for a registered Geographical Indication, or employing an identical or deceptively similar mark in connection with goods for which the indication is registered, shall be liable for damages proportionate to the loss suffered by the registered proprietor. The Central Government may, upon receiving a complaint from any interested party, direct the seizure and destruction of goods bearing such unauthorized use, subject to due process as provided herein. Further, where an unregistered geographical indication is used in a manner contrary to honest practices in industrial or commercial matters, leading to confusion amongst consumers regarding the origin of goods, the aggrieved proprietor may seek injunctive relief from the relevant High Court. Penalties for contravention shall include fines up to five lakhs rupees and imprisonment extending to three years.

Any proprietor of a registered geographical indication may grant exclusive licenses conferring the right to use the indication in relation to specific goods or services, subject to such terms and conditions as are agreed upon in writing between the proprietor and the licensee. Such licenses shall be assignable by the licensee, provided that any assignment is approved by the Registrar and notification thereof is published in the Official Gazette. Where a geographical indication is deemed an unregistered geographical indication due to non-renewal of registration, no license granted prior to such lapse shall become invalid solely on account of the indication’s status; however, subsequent assignments may require further review under this Act. The proprietor retains ultimate control over the quality and reputation associated with the geographical indication, and any licensee shall adhere strictly to standards prescribed by the Registrar for maintaining that integrity.

Any proprietor seeking registration of a geographical indication may apply to the Registrar, but such application shall be rejected if the proposed indication is deemed descriptive of characteristics or quality attributable to the territory of origin and not primarily indicative of its geographical origin; however, this rejection may be appealed before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. The Board shall consider whether the applicant has demonstrated distinctiveness through established use exceeding five years prior to the date of application, provided that evidence presented fails to adequately distinguish the indication from generic terms commonly employed in trade. Furthermore, an aggrieved party demonstrating demonstrable consumer confusion arising from the use of an unregistered geographical indication may petition the Registrar for injunctive relief, subject to a counter-claim asserting bona fide usage and lack of deceptive intent.

Any proprietor of a registered geographical indication relating to agricultural products, foodstuffs, wine, spirit distillates, cereals, spices, or other such products originating from a specific territory within India may grant licenses permitting the use of their protected name and symbols subject to conditions as provided herein. Such licenses shall be in writing and clearly define the scope of permitted activities, including but not limited to production, processing, packaging, sale, and export. Assignment of these rights, including any pending license agreements, requires prior approval from a member appointed bench established under this Act for the purpose of ensuring continued adherence to quality standards associated with the geographical indication. Further, any licensee may sub-license their rights only with express consent of the proprietor, and such sub-licensing shall be subject to similar scrutiny by the aforementioned bench regarding potential impact on the reputation of the unregistered geographical indication.

An application for registration of a geographical indication may be filed by any association of persons, cooperative society, producer company, or other organization engaged in production and processing of goods, or by collectives, provided that such applicant is authorized to use the indication concerning the good for which it seeks registration. The Registrar shall, upon receiving an application, issue a public notice inviting objections from interested parties within three months. Any objection received shall be considered during the examination process, and the applicant shall have opportunity to respond as provided herein. Where the geographical indication is deemed distinctive by virtue of its prior use or reputation, but remains an unregistered geographical indication, the Registrar may proceed with registration subject to fulfilling all other requirements under this Act, including a design registry exercise to assess potential confusion.

Where any goods are seized pursuant to a warrant issued under this Act, and subsequently a judgment is rendered against the registered proprietor for infringement of a geographical indication as provided herein, the Court shall have the power to order, subject to due process and affording opportunity for representation, the court directed forfeiture of such seized goods. Such forfeiture shall vest absolute ownership in the Registering Proprietor or their nominee, to be disposed of according to regulations framed by the Government. Provided that any perishable goods so forfeited may be sold at public auction with proceeds distributed as determined by the Court, and further provided that the costs associated with seizure, storage, and disposal are recoverable from the infringer.

An application for registration of a geographical indication shall include particulars as to the quality and characteristics of the goods, their reputation, and any prior use thereof. Where it is found that the registered proprietor has engaged in activities contrary to the interests of the consumers or producers concerned with the geographical indication, or has otherwise acted in bad faith undermining its distinctiveness, the Registrar may initiate proceedings for revocation of registration. Upon such revocation, or where a court finds evidence of fraudulent misrepresentation relating to the origin of goods bearing the registered geographical indication, the court directed forfeiture to the Central Government shall apply to all goods bearing the mark and any materials used in their production.

Where any proprietor institutes legal proceedings against a person alleging infringement of a geographical indication registered under this Act, and such proceedings result in a judgment finding the alleged infringer guilty of infringing use, the Court shall have the power, subject to appeal, to order the forfeiture to the registered proprietor of goods bearing the false or deceptively similar indicator that were manufactured, imported, sold, offered for sale, or distributed by the infringer. This forfeiture shall extend to all materials and implements used in the production or application of such infringing marks or indications. Provided that, where the infringement was committed unknowingly and without malicious intent, the Court may, at its discretion, impose a lesser penalty, including but not limited to monetary compensation to the registered proprietor. The court directed forfeiture will be deemed equitable relief against unfair trade practices.

Where any proprietor institutes proceedings alleging an infringement of a geographical indication registered under this Act and fails to diligently pursue such proceedings for a continuous period exceeding twelve months, the Central Registry shall issue notice to the proprietor affording thirty days for compliance. Should the proprietor fail to demonstrate satisfactory progress in the litigation within the stipulated timeframe, or cease the legal action altogether, the Registrar may apply to the District Court requesting an order of court directed forfeiture of the registered geographical indication. Such application must detail the reasons for non-compliance and evidence of lack of diligence. The court shall consider representations from both the Central Registry and the proprietor before issuing any such order. Any goods bearing the mark subject to a forfeiture order shall be deemed infringing under this Act, irrespective of prior usage.

Where any proprietor institutes legal proceedings against a person alleging infringement of a geographical indication registered under this Act and fails to substantiate such allegation before the relevant judicial authority, the Court shall have the power to order, as part of its judgment, court directed forfeiture of assets acquired or utilized by the complainant in connection with the aforementioned litigation. Such forfeiture shall be limited to those assets demonstrably employed for pursuing the unsuccessful claim, including but not limited to legal fees and associated expenses. Provided that, where the Court finds evidence of a bonafide belief in the existence of infringement, it may exercise discretion regarding the extent of such forfeiture, subject to ensuring fairness and proportionality between the frivolous nature of the allegation and the potential impact on the complainant’s livelihood.

The proprietor of a registered geographical indication shall be entitled to grant exclusive licenses conferring specific rights relating to the use of the indication on goods conforming to the standards as provided herein. Such licenses may be assigned freely subject to the terms and conditions stipulated in the license agreement, including provisions for royalty payments and quality control measures ensuring adherence to the established norms of the geographical indication. Where a proprietor fails to prevent the use of the registered geographical indication by an unauthorized party, or where such misuse demonstrably damages the reputation or distinctiveness of the goods, the court may order forfeiture to the Government of any assets derived directly from the infringing activities, including but not limited to profits and inventory. This power of court directed forfeiture shall be exercised judiciously, considering the proportionality between the infringement and the penalty imposed.

Where any proprietor institutes proceedings alleging an infringement of a geographical indication registered under this Act and fails to substantiate such allegation before the relevant judicial authority, the court may, subject to appeal, order the provisional seizure of goods bearing imitated indications. Provided that the proprietor demonstrates reasonable grounds for believing that continued use of the infringing mark is likely to cause dilution or damage to the distinctiveness of the registered geographical indication. Further, where a final determination establishes such infringement and finds the proprietor’s claim unfounded, the court directed forfeiture shall apply to all goods seized under this order, along with any materials used in their production, vesting them in favour of the State Government for disposal as deemed fit.

For the purposes of this Act, “Darjeeling Tea” means tea produced exclusively in specified geographical areas comprising the Darjeeling district and parts of the Jalpaiguri and Kooka districts of West Bengal, as notified by the Register; such notification shall specify the precise boundaries of the area. The term "Darjeeling Tea" includes only that tea which conforms to standards of quality, flavour, aroma and characteristics prescribed under this Act. Any use of the indication “Darjeeling Tea” in relation to any goods other than tea produced within the notified geographical areas or not conforming to such standards shall be deemed an infringement as provided herein. The Register may, from time to time, revise the geographical limits defining "Darjeeling Tea" subject to section 21 Indian.

An application for registration as a geographical indication shall be accompanied by an affidavit verifying the correctness of the particulars furnished therein and confirming that the applicant is the exclusive proprietor of the proposed geographical indication, subject to any customary rights or concessions granted under this Act. The Registrar may require the applicant to provide further documentation substantiating the claim of exclusivity, including records demonstrating continuous use and reputation associated with the goods in relation to the specified territory. Any material misstatement or omission in the affidavit provided shall render the application liable for rejection, and where such falsification is demonstrably intended to mislead the Registrar regarding the applicant’s entitlement, it may constitute used falsifying trade, attracting penalties as determined under relevant penal provisions. The Registrar shall maintain a record of all affidavits submitted and may request clarifications from applicants at any stage during processing.

For the purposes of this Act, a “design registered proprietor” means the person whose name is entered in the Register as the proprietor of a registered layout-design and includes any successor in title to such proprietor. The design registered proprietor shall be entitled to exercise all rights pertaining to the registered layout-design, subject to any license granted under this Act or any other agreement lawfully made. Any assignment or transmission of interest in a registered layout-design shall require notification to the Registrar within thirty days, as provided herein. A person claiming to be a design registered proprietor must demonstrate valid title documentation upon request by the Registrar.

An application for registration of a layout-design may be filed by any person claiming to be the first inventor of the design, or by any other person entitled under this Act to make an application. Where a layout-design has been previously published outside India, the applicant shall disclose all particulars of such prior publication as provided herein. The Registrar shall, upon receipt of an application, issue a notification requiring objections to be filed within three months from the date of such notification. Any person may file an objection under this Act, subject to payment of the prescribed fee. Upon determination of any objections, if satisfied that the applicant is the design registered proprietor and that the layout-design is original and not infringing existing rights, registration shall be granted.

Subject to any modifications as may be directed by the Controller, where an infringement of layout-design rights occurs, the design registered proprietor shall be entitled to seek remedies including, but not limited to, permanent and interlocutory injunctions restraining further acts of infringement. Damages recoverable under this Act shall be assessed based on the loss suffered by the design registered proprietor as a consequence of the infringing activity, or where such calculation is not feasible, upon the profits made by the infringer. The Controller may order the delivery up or destruction of infringing copies and materials used in connection with their manufacture. Provided that, any person claiming to be aggrieved by an order under this Act may appeal to the Appellate Board within a period of sixty days from the date of such order. Further, the design registered proprietor shall have the right to claim compensation for loss of reputation arising directly from the infringement.

An application for rectification of a registered layout-design may be presented to the Controller by any person aggrieved by an order made under this Act or by any entry in the Register. Where the applicant is a design registered proprietor, the application shall specify the particulars of the registration and the grounds upon which it is sought that the Register be rectified. The Controller shall serve notice on the respondent, being the current registered proprietor or other party whose interest is affected, affording them an opportunity to submit their response within the prescribed time. Any person may appear before the Controller at any hearing and adduce evidence in support of or opposing the application. The Controller’s decision regarding rectification shall be final subject to appeal under this Act. Costs relating to such proceedings shall be determined as provided herein, taking into account the complexity of the matter and the conduct of the parties.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, an application for rectification of a registered layout-design may be presented by any person aggrieved, including the design registered proprietor, alleging facts that would entitle that person to seek such rectification. Such application shall specify the particulars of the registration and the grounds on which it is sought. The design registered proprietor shall furnish evidence demonstrating continued compliance with conditions stipulated during initial registration, particularly concerning ongoing security measures implemented to protect against unauthorized copying or use of the layout-design. Failure to provide satisfactory evidence as provided herein may result in rejection of the rectification application or imposition of penalties, as determined by the Registrar.

Any person who knowingly imports, manufactures, distributes, displays for sale, or offers for sale any layout-design infringing the rights of the design registered proprietor shall be liable to pay damages equivalent to ten times the number of infringed integrated circuits. Such liability may be enforced by way of civil suit in the District Court having jurisdiction over the territory where the infringement occurred. Further, under this Act, a design registered proprietor aggrieved by an act of infringement may apply for an injunction restraining the infringing party from continuing such acts. The court shall consider evidence presented demonstrating actual or threatened loss to the design registered proprietor as a consequence of the infringement and may award costs reflective of that harm.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, a design registered proprietor may grant licenses relating to the layout-design for which registration has been obtained, specifying the scope and duration of such license. Any such license shall be in writing and may include conditions restricting the licensee’s activities concerning reproduction, exploitation, or importation related to the layout-design. The design registered proprietor shall retain ownership of the copyright subsisting in any mask works created by the licensee under the terms of the license, provided that the agreement explicitly states this intention. Assignment of a layout-design, including all rights pertaining thereto, may be effected through a written instrument executed by the design registered proprietor and delivered to the Registrar for record. Such assignment shall vest in the assignee all rights and privileges previously held by the assignor under this Act.

Where an appeal is brought under this Act against any decision of the Controller relating to rectification of a registered layout-design, the Appellate Board may, subject to such inquiry as it deems necessary, confirm, reverse, or modify the order appealed from. The appellant shall be deemed to have sufficient interest if they are the design registered proprietor, or a person claiming through them by way of assignment or license. Provided that any party aggrieved by an interim order made by the Controller may appeal directly to the Appellate Board within sixty days of such order. Further, the Appellate Board shall not entertain any appeal unless the appellant has deposited with it such sum as may be prescribed; and the decision of the Appellate Board shall be final.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any person who infringes a registered layout-design shall be liable for damages proven to have been caused thereby. The design registered proprietor may institute legal proceedings against such infringer within three years from the date of the infringement. Where an infringing act has occurred through the transmission of a layout-design or information in relation thereto, without authorization from the design registered proprietor, liability shall extend to all parties involved in that transmission, including those who knowingly facilitated it. The Court may grant an injunction restraining further acts of infringement and order the destruction of infringing layouts or articles incorporating such designs. Further, the design registered proprietor is entitled to claim compensation for loss of profits resulting from the infringement, as determined by the Court, considering factors like market share and retail price.

An application for rectification of a registered layout-design may be made by any person claiming through an interest acquired under this Act, including a design registered proprietor. Such applications shall be filed with the Registrar within six months from the date of registration or from the date on which the grounds for rectification became known to the applicant, whichever is later. Where an application relates to alleged infringement, the Registrar may require the applicant to furnish security for costs as deemed appropriate. A member of a partnership claiming such interest shall be bound by the terms of the partnership deed and shall act through its duly authorized representative in all proceedings under this Act. The Registrar shall serve notice on the design registered proprietor and any other interested party, affording them an opportunity to submit their objections or counter-claims as provided herein.

Where an application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design is pending before the Registrar, any person claiming to have a relationship proposed registered with respect to the design shall be afforded reasonable opportunity to present evidence demonstrating their interest in the outcome of the proceedings. Such evidence must pertain directly to the validity or enforceability of any contractual arrangement underlying that relationship. The Registrar may, at his discretion, require such persons to furnish security for costs incurred by other parties as a consequence of their intervention. Further, where the design registered proprietor disputes the existence or nature of the proposed relationship, the Registrar shall conduct an inquiry and determine the matter according to principles of natural justice, ensuring fairness to all concerned parties under this Act.

Any person who knowingly imports, manufactures, distributes, or directly or indirectly deals with any layout-design infringing the exclusive right of the design registered proprietor shall be liable to pay damages equivalent to ten times the number of infringed integrated circuits. Such liability accrues irrespective of whether commercial gain was realized by the infringer. An application date shall not preclude a claim for relief where evidence demonstrates wilful infringement occurring subsequent to publication but prior to registration. Further, any party aggrieved may apply to the relevant court for an injunction restraining such infringing activity; failure to comply with such an order renders the offender subject to penalties as provided herein and potential seizure of all infringing materials.

For the purposes of this Act, a “design affidavit registered” signifies the formal declaration made under oath by an applicant seeking registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design. This affidavit shall detail, with particularity, the identity of the creator or creators of the layout-design and confirm their entitlement to apply for registration as provided herein. The design affidavit registered must also explicitly state whether the applicant is the sole proprietor or a joint proprietor of the layout-design. Failure to accurately disclose information within the design affidavit registered may render the application liable to rejection, subject to appeal before an appropriate appellate authority.

An applicant seeking registration of a layout-design may submit a design affidavit along with the formal application as provided herein. The design affidavit shall contain a verification by the claimant affirming that to the best of their knowledge and belief, no identical or substantially similar layout-design is currently registered under this Act or has been published in any manner prior to the date of application. Failure to disclose such existing registrations or publications may render the registration liable for cancellation. The Registrar shall scrutinize the design affidavit and may require further clarification or supporting documentation from the applicant. A *design affidavit registered* constitutes prima facie evidence of the originality claim, subject to challenge under established legal procedures.

Where any person alleging infringement of a design affidavit registered under this Act seeks redressal, they may institute proceedings before the Commercial Courts as constituted under applicable legislation. Such proceedings shall be limited to claims arising directly from acts contravening the exclusive rights conferred by the registration of the design layout-design. The claimant must demonstrate that the infringing act occurred after the date of publication of the design affidavit registered and that said infringement substantially copies the protected elements of the registered layout-design. Provided that, a finding of prior use or independent creation shall constitute a complete defense against any claim of infringement. Further, damages awarded under this Act shall not exceed three times the actual loss suffered by the claimant, subject to considerations of proportionality as determined by the Commercial Court.

An applicant seeking registration of a design affidavit registered relating to a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall submit Form D along with the requisite fee as prescribed. The application must contain a true and complete representation of the layout-design, including all relevant technical specifications and supporting documentation demonstrating originality. Upon receipt of an application, the Registrar may direct the applicant to rectify any deficiencies or provide further clarification deemed necessary for assessment under this Act. Failure to comply with such directions within the stipulated period shall render the application liable for rejection. The Registrar shall publish a notice of the application in the Official Gazette and on the website maintained by the Office. Objections, if any, may be filed within two months from the date of publication as provided herein. The applicant shall have an opportunity to respond to such objections before the Registrar proceeds with examination.

An applicant seeking registration of a design affidavit registered under this Act shall furnish with the application a declaration verifying the accuracy and completeness of the information contained therein, conforming to Form D as prescribed. The Registrar may require further documentation substantiating the originality of the layout-design, including details regarding prior publication or disclosure, provided that such requirement is limited to instances where reasonable doubt concerning the design’s novelty arises. Failure to comply with this provision shall render the application liable for rejection. Any alteration made to a registered design affidavit after its initial registration requires notification to the Registrar within thirty days and may necessitate re-examination under this Act. The applicant remains responsible for ensuring continued compliance with these stipulations throughout the duration of the registered design’s protection.

Any person found to have made a false statement material to the determination of validity within a design affidavit registered under this Act shall be liable for a penalty not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees and may also face proceedings for misrepresentation. The Registrar shall, upon receiving credible information regarding such falsity, issue notice to the registrant affording them an opportunity of being heard; failure to satisfactorily rebut the allegations will result in automatic revocation of the registration. Furthermore, any individual who knowingly assists in the preparation or submission of a fraudulent design affidavit is also subject to similar penalties and may be deemed complicit in obstructing the fair administration of justice as provided herein.

The holder of a design affidavit registered under this Act may grant a license conferring specific rights relating to the use, reproduction, and exploitation of the layout-design. Such licenses shall be documented in writing and may be exclusive or non-exclusive as determined by the licensor. Any assignment of ownership or a substantial portion of the rights associated with a design affidavit registered herein requires prior notification to the Registrar, detailing the terms of transfer and identifying all parties involved. The assignee shall be deemed subject to any existing licenses granted under the original registration, provided that the terms of such licenses do not conflict with the assignment agreement. Further, the Registrar may require an undertaking from the assignee ensuring continued compliance with obligations as provided herein relating to security measures protecting the layout-design.

Where any person aggrieved by an order refusing registration of a design affidavit registered under this Act, or revoking a design affidavit registered, may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. Such appeal shall be made within sixty days from the date of communication of the order to the appellant and shall state specifically the grounds on which the order is sought to be challenged. The Tribunal may, after giving notice to all parties concerned and affording them an opportunity of being heard, confirm, modify, or reverse the order appealed against. Provided that the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal shall not entertain any appeal under this Act unless the appellant has deposited with it such fees as may be prescribed.

An applicant seeking registration of a design affidavit registered relating to a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall furnish with the application a declaration verifying the originality of the design and affirming that it does not infringe upon any prior registered designs. The Registrar may require such further documentation as is deemed necessary to ascertain compliance with the provisions under this Act, including details pertaining to the indication certification trade marks employed in relation to the integrated circuit layout-design. Any alteration to the design subsequent to the date of the design affidavit shall be disclosed within the application and assessed for its impact on originality. Failure to disclose such alterations may render the registration liable to cancellation. The Registrar is empowered to reject an application if it finds that the design lacks sufficient novelty or contains elements already incorporated in a previously registered layout-design.

Any person found to have knowingly made a false statement in a design affidavit registered under this Act shall be liable for a penalty of not less than fifty thousand rupees but which may extend to two hundred and fifty thousand rupees. Furthermore, such person shall also be subject to proceedings for recovery of costs incurred by the Controller in rectifying the erroneous registration or investigating allegations of falsity. The Registrar may, upon receiving credible information regarding discrepancies between the registered design and actual goods, initiate an inquiry into the veracity of the design affidavit. Where it is established that the layout-design incorporates elements infringing on existing intellectual property rights relating to j) “goods”, the Controller shall have power to order cancellation of the registration and impose additional penalties as provided herein.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any India patentee holding a design affidavit registered relating to a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design may grant a license for the exploitation of such registered design to any person, either within India or abroad. Such licenses shall be assignable in accordance with standard commercial practice and may include rights pertaining to reproduction, modification, and adaptation of the layout-design, as agreed upon between the patentee and licensee. The terms of any assignment or license granted under this Act must be documented in writing and submitted to the Registrar for record within thirty days of execution; failure to do so shall render such assignment or license unenforceable against third parties. Further, a design affidavit registered may be assigned by operation of law as if it were movable property, provided that all subsequent assignees adhere to the original terms stipulated within the initial licensing agreement.

Where an applicant seeks registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design and has entered into a relationship proposed as a registered license with another party, the application for registration shall disclose fully the terms of that relationship. The Registrar may require further particulars concerning such a relationship proposed registered if deemed necessary to ascertain compliance with this Act. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Registrar relating to the acceptance or rejection of an application based on the existence of a relationship proposed registered may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.
