It shall be the duty of the applicant to ensure that the terms of the relationship proposed registered do not contravene any provisions under this Act, particularly those concerning fair competition and public interest. Failure to disclose such a relationship or providing false information relating thereto shall render the application liable for rejection.

Where an application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design is filed disclosing a relationship proposed as a registered licensee, the Registrar may require submission of a detailed memorandum outlining the terms governing such arrangement. This memorandum shall be deemed part of the public record upon registration and its contents are subject to challenge under this Act. Any party aggrieved by the disclosed terms or their impact on existing rights may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days of publication, demonstrating prejudice arising directly from the relationship proposed registered. The Board’s determination regarding the validity of the challenged aspects shall be final, provided that it does not affect the underlying layout-design registration itself.

Where an applicant seeks registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design and demonstrates a pre-existing relationship proposed registered with another person, that other person may apply to the Registrar for recognition as a co-owner of specified rights in the design. Such application shall detail the nature of the relationship and provide evidence substantiating its existence prior to the initial application date. The applicant’s entitlement to registration is subject to the Registrar's satisfaction regarding the validity of this proposed registered relationship, including verification that it does not prejudice existing or subsequent claims under this Act. Further, where a co-owner utilizes an authorised use mark in connection with the layout-design, they shall be liable for any infringement arising from misuse of said mark, provided that such usage is expressly permitted within the agreement establishing the relationship proposed registered.

Registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be deemed to have been granted improperly, and consequently, provided cancelling registration, if it is established that the layout-design incorporates elements substantially derived from a previously registered layout-design without due authorization. For the purposes of this Act, “substantially derived” means that an examination of the allegedly infringing layout-design reveals a clear and demonstrable copying of key structural or functional features, such that the original inventive concept is replicated. The Registrar may require evidence demonstrating both the prior registration and the degree of similarity to ascertain whether provided cancelling registration applies under this Act.

Registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be deemed to have been granted in error, and consequently, provided cancelling registration may occur, if it is established that the layout-design was substantially similar to an already registered design under this Act. The determination of substantial similarity shall consider the overall impression created by the designs, irrespective of minor variations. An application for cancellation must specify the grounds upon which it is based and identify the prior registered design. The Registrar may require further evidence supporting the claim of substantial similarity before proceeding with a hearing concerning the validity of the design registry registration.

Registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be deemed to be invalid if, following its grant, it is established that the layout-design incorporates substantial elements derived from an earlier unregistered layout-design. The Registrar may initiate proceedings for cancelling registration registered under this Act where evidence demonstrates such unauthorized appropriation. An application for cancellation may also be filed by any interested person, subject to demonstrating a direct and demonstrable prejudice resulting from the infringing incorporation. For the purposes of determining substantial similarity, consideration shall be given to both the overall impression created by the layout-design and the replication of key functional elements as provided herein.

The registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall remain valid for a period of ten years from the date of its initial registration, subject to renewal as provided herein. An application for renewal may be filed within one year preceding the expiry of the said period. However, the registration registered under this Act may be cancelled by the Controller if it is established that the layout-design was not originally valid or infringed upon existing rights prior to the date of application. Such cancellation may also occur if the applicant fails to pay the prescribed renewal fees within the stipulated timeframe, or demonstrates a lack of diligent prosecution of the registration. The Controller shall provide an opportunity for the registrant to be heard before issuing any order for cancelling registration registered.

Where, following registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design, it comes to the notice of the Controller that any representation made in the application for registration was materially false, the Controller shall issue a notification directing the registered proprietor to show cause why the registration should not be cancelled. Such direction shall specify the grounds upon which the cancellation is sought and provide a reasonable opportunity for the proprietor to submit their response. If, after considering the response, or if no response is received within the stipulated time, the Controller finds that the representation was indeed false and prejudicial to the interests of other persons, the registration may be cancelled as provided herein. The effect of cancelling registration registered shall be that the layout-design ceases to enjoy protection under this Act from the date of cancellation.

An application for the cancellation of a registration, whether absolute or conditional, shall be made to the Controller in the prescribed form and accompanied by the requisite fee. The grounds for such an application include demonstrable misrepresentation during the original registration process concerning the originality of the layout-design, or where it is proven that the registered layout-design incorporates substantial elements copied from a prior unregistered design. Further, a cancellation may be sought if the registered proprietor has ceased to carry on business or has become insolvent. The Controller shall provide the registered proprietor with an opportunity to be heard and present evidence in their defense. Following due consideration of all submissions, the Controller may order the registration to be cancelled, subject to providing reasons for such decision in writing. It is provided that a registration already granted cannot be unilaterally altered; cancelling registration registered requires adherence to this procedure.

The registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be deemed to be vulnerable to cancellation proceedings where it is established, through evidence presented before the Controller, that the applicant knowingly misrepresented facts pertaining to prior publication or availability of the design. Such misrepresentation must be material to the assessment of novelty and originality as required under this Act. Furthermore, registration may be cancelled if it becomes apparent that the layout-design incorporates elements substantially derived from an unregistered work, and the applicant failed to acknowledge such derivation in the application. The Controller shall issue a notice to the registered proprietor prior to any order for cancelling registration registered, affording them an opportunity to submit their response and counter evidence.

Where a registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design has been granted, such registration shall remain valid subject to the provisions herein. However, the Registrar may, acting upon an application made in the prescribed form by any interested party, initiate proceedings for cancelling registration registered if it is established that the assignor had not obtained prior consent from the original registrant before assigning rights pertaining to the layout-design. Further, a licensee of a registered layout-design shall be deemed an interested party for the purpose of such application. The Registrar may also entertain applications seeking cancellation where evidence demonstrates a material alteration of the layout-design post-registration without proper notification and consent as provided herein. Any person aggrieved by an order cancelling registration registered may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within a period of sixty days from the date of communication of the order.

Registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be deemed to be invalid, and consequently subject to cancellation, if it is established that the registered layout-design incorporates elements substantially derived from an earlier unregistered layout-design or design. The Registrar may initiate proceedings for cancelling registration registered where evidence demonstrates such derivation, provided that the applicant demonstrating prior creation furnishes documentation satisfying the requirements as prescribed herein. Furthermore, a registered layout-design relating to services specified alphabetically within Schedule A may be cancelled if it is found that the description of those services was inaccurate or misleading at the time of application. Any party aggrieved by a proposed cancellation order may submit objections in writing detailing grounds for dissent and supporting documentation.

Registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be deemed to be voidable if, following its grant, it becomes evident that the trade description furnished during the application process was false or misleading in a material respect. The Registrar may, sua sponte or upon receiving a complaint from an aggrieved party, initiate proceedings for cancelling registration registered under this Act. Such cancellation shall only occur after providing the registrant with a reasonable opportunity to be heard and present counter-evidence. Failure by the registrant to demonstrate the veracity of the original trade description will constitute conclusive proof warranting revocation. Any person suffering loss or damage as a direct consequence of such misleading information may pursue remedies available under this Act, including claims for compensation.

The registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall remain valid subject to its assignment or licensing under conditions as provided herein. Any registered proprietor desiring to grant a license conferring rights in respect of the layout-design may, through an instrument executed in the prescribed form and manner, assign such rights wholly or partially, irrevocably or revocably, to another party. Provided that where a registration is subsequently cancelled, any existing licenses granted prior to the cancellation shall remain enforceable for a period not exceeding three years from the date of the order cancelling registration registered, unless a case proceeding is initiated by the former proprietor seeking their termination. The Registrar may, upon receiving notification of such assignment or licensing agreement, record the details in the Register and issue certificates accordingly. Further, any alteration to the terms of an existing license requires prior approval from the Registrar.

A registration of a layout-design shall be deemed to have been cancelled by operation of law if, following an application made in the prescribed form and supported by affidavit, it is determined that the applicant has established, to the satisfaction of the Registrar, that the original registered proprietor failed to respond to a notice served under this Act regarding objections to the registration. For the purposes of determining whether a layout-design registration constitutes a cancelled registrar layout, the date of service of such notice shall be considered conclusive evidence for establishing non-response. Any subsequent application relating to the same layout-design is barred where a cancelled registrar layout exists.

An application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be deemed to have been abandoned if, after the publication of the acceptance thereof under this Act, the applicant fails to comply with the requirements of sub-section (3) within the prescribed time. Where a registered layout-design is subsequently found to infringe upon prior art or has been obtained through fraudulent means, the Registrar may initiate proceedings for its cancellation. In such instances, a cancelled registrar layout shall remain open to challenge by any aggrieved party before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within a period of ninety days from the date of publication of the order of cancellation. The applicant in such challenges must demonstrate substantial prejudice resulting directly from the cancellation.

Where a registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design has been granted, the Registrar shall have the power to initiate proceedings for its cancellation if it comes to their notice that the registered proprietor has failed to comply with any condition stipulated during the registration process relating to the manufacture or importation of integrated circuits incorporating the layout-design. Such failure constitutes grounds for cancellation under this Act. The applicant seeking cancellation must provide evidence demonstrating the non-compliance, and the Registrar may issue a notice to the registered proprietor allowing them an opportunity to be heard. If, following such hearing, the Registrar finds that the condition has not been met, they may order the registration cancelled; a *cancelled registrar layout* shall then be deemed void ab initio. Any person aggrieved by this decision may appeal under provisions as provided herein.

An application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be deemed to have been abandoned if, following an invitation under this Act requiring the applicant to submit specific details regarding the fabrication process, the applicant fails to respond within the prescribed time limit. Furthermore, where a registered layout-design is subsequently found to be substantially similar to a prior unregistrable design, or where it has been determined that the registration was obtained through fraudulent misrepresentation, the Registrar may initiate proceedings for cancellation. In such instances, the cancelled registrar layout shall remain accessible for public inspection as provided herein, with appropriate notations indicating its status and the reasons for cancellation. Any party aggrieved by a decision of the Registrar concerning the cancellation of a registered layout-design may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order.

Where a registrar layout has been declared invalid under this Act, subsequent applications for registration relating to the same integrated circuit shall be considered only if the applicant demonstrates that the prior declaration of invalidity did not stem from an inherent deficiency in the underlying design principles. The Registrar may require submission of expert testimony substantiating such demonstration and assessing the novelty of the new application relative to the previously rejected layout. Further, any party aggrieved by a decision concerning a cancelled registrar layout is entitled to appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days of notification of the order. Provided that this right of appeal shall not revive the registration; it merely allows for judicial review as provided herein.

Where the Registrar, following a reasoned order published as per the prescribed procedure, determines that a registered layout-design has been obtained through fraudulent means or involves an infringement of prior rights, the registrar layout shall stand cancelled. Any person aggrieved by such cancellation may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of publication of the Registrar’s order. Failure to comply with this timeframe shall render the appeal inadmissible. The tribunal may, after affording opportunity for hearing to all concerned parties, confirm, vary or annul the cancellation order. Where a cancelled registrar layout involves ongoing commercial exploitation, penalties as provided herein shall be levied against those continuing such activity.

The Registrar shall, upon receiving an application from a third party demonstrating substantial investment made in reliance on a purportedly valid semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design registration, investigate whether such registration has been properly maintained. Where it is determined that the registered proprietor failed to adhere to prescribed maintenance protocols, or otherwise engaged in conduct detrimental to the interests of those relying on the public register, the Registrar may initiate proceedings for cancellation of the said registration. Should the cancellation be confirmed, any existing licenses granted by the original registrant relating to the layout-design shall remain valid and enforceable against third parties, subject to the terms thereof. Furthermore, assignment of rights under such licenses will not be affected by the cancelled registrar layout status, provided that the assignee was a bona fide purchaser for value at the time of grant.

Where a registrar has, pursuant to an order of the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal, revoked a registration for a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design and subsequently reinstated it, that reinstatement shall not revive any rights or remedies accrued prior to the date of revocation. Any party aggrieved by such reinstatement may appeal to the High Court within ninety days from the date of communication of the Tribunal’s order. The appellate court may entertain an appeal only if the appellant demonstrates demonstrable prejudice arising directly from the initial cancellation and subsequent reinstatement, subject to the registrar's determination that the cancelled registrar layout was validly registered initially. Provided that a certificate issued by the Registrar confirming the validity of the registration shall be prima facie evidence thereof in any legal proceeding.

Where a registrar layout has been, at any time, declared invalid through judicial determination, such declaration shall constitute conclusive evidence for purposes of enforcement actions under this Act. Any party aggrieved by an order cancelling a registrar layout may appeal to the relevant High Court within ninety days from the date of that order; provided that the claim shall date back to the original filing of the layout-design application and any subsequent proceedings relating to its validity are deemed continuous therefrom. Failure to comply with prescribed timelines for appeals will render such appeals inadmissible. The court may, upon finding merit in an appeal, reinstate a cancelled registrar layout subject to conditions as it deems fit, and impose penalties on parties found to have acted in bad faith during the cancellation process.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, a license granted under section 26 shall continue in force unless revoked by the Registrar or terminated as per its terms. Where a layout-design registration has been cancelled by the Registrar, any assignment of rights relating to that design, whether executed prior to or subsequent to the cancellation, shall be deemed null and void; however, this provision shall not prejudice existing contractual obligations arising from such assignments. The Registrar may, upon application by an interested party demonstrating substantial reliance on a purportedly valid license linked to a cancelled registrar layout, order interim enforcement of the license pending determination of its validity. Furthermore, if a trade mark identical or deceptively similar to elements within the layout-design is also registered, this shall not automatically invalidate the licensing agreement but may be considered during disputes concerning infringement under this Act.

A registration for a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be deemed to have been cancelled if, following an inquiry as provided herein, the Registrar finds that the registered layout-design was obtained through fraud or misrepresentation. For the purposes of this Act, a “cancelled registrar layout” refers specifically to such a layout-design whose registration has ceased to have effect under these provisions. The notice applicant shall be afforded a reasonable opportunity to present evidence and arguments against the proposed cancellation. Further, any person aggrieved by an order of the Registrar cancelling a layout may appeal to the relevant appellate authority within a prescribed time period, subject to conditions as provided herein.

An application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design relating to a novel formulation process used in the manufacture of pharmaceutical compounds shall be deemed invalid if it is established that the applicant has failed to maintain accurate records pertaining to the design’s creation and modification, as required under this Act. Furthermore, where the Registrar reasonably believes that a registered layout-design incorporates elements substantially derived from an unregistered prior art design, or that representations made during the registration process were materially false, the registrar may initiate proceedings for cancellation. A cancelled registrar layout shall remain so until such time as any appeal against the order of cancellation is disposed of by the relevant appellate authority.

An application for the registration of copyright shall be made in writing in such form as may be prescribed, and shall be presented to the Registrar of Copyrights having jurisdiction over the work’s place of origin. The application must identify the applicant, the work being claimed, and the particulars of the copyright sought to be registered. Where the application relates to a cinematograph film, it shall include a statement regarding all rights comprised in the copyright subsisting therein. Subject to such conditions as may be prescribed, an incomplete application may be amended within one month from the date of its initial submission; provided that no material alteration affecting the identity or ownership of the work is permitted after scrutiny begins. Any false representation in an application shall render it liable for rejection under this Act.

Every application for the registration of a work under this Act shall be made in writing in the prescribed form and shall be accompanied by the requisite fee as specified in Schedule III. The applicant shall furnish all details relating to authorship, ownership, publication, and other particulars relevant to the determination of copyright subsisting in the work. Where an application is for the registration of a cinematograph film, proof of necessary censorship certification from the Central Board of Film Certification shall be submitted along with the application. An incomplete application may, at the discretion of the Registrar, be returned to the applicant requesting clarification or additional information; however, no such request shall extend the statutory processing time beyond ninety days. Subject to verification and satisfaction that all requirements are met as provided herein, the Registrar shall enter the particulars of the work in the Register of Copyrights and issue a certificate of registration. Any false representation made within an application will be subject to penalties under this Act.

Any person intending to register a work under this Act shall submit an application to the Registrar of Copyrights in the prescribed form, accompanied by the requisite fee and a copy of the work for which registration is sought. The application shall clearly identify the applicant as proprietor of the copyright, or state the basis of their right to make the application including details of any assignment or license subsisting on the work. Should an application be found deficient in any material particular, the Registrar may require the applicant to remedy such deficiency within a period not exceeding thirty days from the date of such requirement; failure to do so shall render the application liable to rejection. A false statement in an application constitutes grounds for revocation of registration as provided herein and may subject the applicant to penalties under this Act. The Registrar, upon satisfactory verification of the application and compliance with all procedural requirements, shall enter the particulars of the copyright in the Register of Copyrights and issue a certificate of registration.

Any person claiming to be an applicant for registration of copyright shall submit an application in the prescribed form to the Registrar of Copyrights, accompanied by the requisite fee as specified in Schedule I. The application shall contain a statement regarding the work’s origin, including details of authorship and date of creation, and shall clearly identify the specific portions of the work for which protection is sought. Where the applicant is not the author of the work, evidence establishing valid assignment or legal transfer of rights from the author must be furnished with the application. 

Subject to verification by the Registrar, an acknowledgement of receipt of the application shall be issued to the applicant within a period of thirty days. Should deficiencies exist in the application, the Registrar may require rectification within sixty days; failure to comply may result in rejection of the application as provided herein. An incomplete application will not be processed further until all required information is submitted and verified.

Any person intending to register a work under this Act shall submit an application in the prescribed form to the Registrar of Copyrights, accompanied by the requisite fee and a copy of the work for which registration is sought. The application must clearly identify the author, publisher, and claimant of copyright, along with details regarding the nature of the right claimed—whether it pertains to literary, dramatic, musical or artistic works, cinematograph films, or sound recordings. Subject to verification by the Registrar, an incomplete application shall be returned to the applicant with a notice specifying the deficiencies. Provided that if the Registrar is satisfied that the application substantially complies with the requirements as provided herein, they may require rectification within thirty days from the date of such notice. Failure to comply with this requirement may result in rejection of the application and loss of priority date for copyright claim. Any false representation made in an application shall be punishable under relevant provisions of law.

Any person desiring to register a work under this Act shall submit an application in the prescribed form to the Registrar of Copyrights, accompanied by the requisite fee and a copy of the work claiming copyright. The application shall clearly state the title of the work, the author’s name and address, and the particulars relating to publication, if any. Where the applicant is not the author, proof of assignment or legal entitlement to make the application shall be furnished subject to verification by the Registrar. Failure to provide complete and accurate information in the application may render it liable for rejection, and a false declaration therein shall attract penalties including imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. The Registrar may require further evidence or clarification regarding any aspect of the application as deemed necessary before proceeding with registration.

Any person desiring to secure copyright in a work shall submit an application to the Registrar of Copyrights in the prescribed form, accompanied by the requisite fee and all particulars relating to such work. The application for copyright shall clearly state the nature of the right sought to be secured—whether it pertains to literary, dramatic, musical or artistic works—and shall identify the author and owner thereof. An applicant may simultaneously apply for more than one class of rights in respect of a single work, provided that separate fees are paid for each such application. Subject to verification by the Registrar, an assignment of copyright must be recorded with the Copyright Office; failure to do so will render any subsequent claim based on said assignment unenforceable against third parties unaware of its existence. The registrar may require further evidence or clarification regarding the validity of the application and shall communicate any deficiencies to the applicant for rectification within a specified timeframe as provided herein.

Any person claiming ownership of copyright in a work shall submit an application to the Registrar of Copyrights, demonstrating substantial connection with India, unless otherwise provided herein. The application shall be accompanied by the prescribed fee and particulars as to the author, publisher, and nature of the work. Where an application is made for registration of a cinematograph film, proof of necessary censorship certification from the Central Board of Film Certification shall also be furnished. Should the Registrar raise objections regarding the validity or completeness of the application, notice thereof shall be served upon the applicant, affording them thirty days to rectify deficiencies or submit representations. Any aggrieved party may file an appeal before the High Court against any order refusing registration, provided that such appeal is instituted within ninety days from the date of the refusal and demonstrates a prima facie case for interference with the Registrar’s discretion. Failure to comply with these provisions shall render the application liable to rejection.

Any person intending to make an application for registration of copyright shall submit such application in the prescribed form along with the requisite fee to the designated authority within thirty days from the date of publication of the work. The application shall clearly and accurately identify the author and the producer, if different, and detail the nature of rights claimed. Subject to verification that the applicant is indeed the owner or duly authorized agent of the copyright holder, and provided that no valid objection is raised under this Act within a period of sixty days from the date of advertisement of the application, registration shall be effected. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in rejection of the application; however, such rejection shall not prejudice the right of ownership itself but only the benefit of statutory presumptions arising from registration. Any false statement made in an application will attract penalties as provided herein.

Any person intending to secure copyright in an original literary, dramatic, musical or artistic work shall submit an application to the India Registrar, accompanied by the prescribed fee and all particulars required under rule 8. The application must clearly identify the author and claimant of copyright, and specify the nature of the right sought to be protected. Failure to provide complete and accurate information in the application may render it liable to rejection, and any work subsequently found to have been registered on the basis of such deficient application shall not be afforded protection under this Act. Any person knowingly making a false statement in an application shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine, or with both; provided that the India Registrar may, subject to payment of a penalty, allow amendment of any material error discovered within thirty days of registration.

Any person claiming ownership of copyright shall submit an application to the Registrar of Copyrights in the prescribed form, accompanied by the requisite fee, demonstrating a prima facie case for authorship or derivation. Should the Registrar raise objections regarding the validity of such application, notice thereof shall be served upon the applicant, affording them thirty days to remedy the deficiencies or file a statement of grounds for disputing the objection. Failure to comply with this notice may result in rejection of the application; however, any aggrieved party may appeal said decision to the High Court having jurisdiction, subject to payment of an appellate fee as prescribed. The procedure for such appeals shall conform to the rules established by that court and evidence presented must substantiate a reasonable likelihood of successful copyright registration. Any claim made fraudulently within this application process will be considered a cognizable offense under this Act.

A trade mark consists of a mark capable of being represented graphically including words, letters, numerals, figures, symbols, graphic representations, shapes of goods, their packaging and combination of colours, and may distinguish the goods or services of one person from those of others. A collective trade mark is owned by an association which, as such, uses the mark to identify the goods or services of its members; and a certified trade mark is acquired by persons who, when using it in relation to goods or services for which it is used, certify that these goods or services are in accordance with specified standards. Registration of a trade mark under this Act shall confer upon the proprietor thereof exclusive right to use the trade mark in relation to the goods or services for which it is registered.

A person desiring to register a trade mark shall apply for registration in writing in such form and manner as may be prescribed. The application shall include a representation of the trade mark, particulars relating to the applicant including name, address and nationality, and a list of goods or services for which the trade mark is intended to be used. An affidavit stating user of the trade mark prior to the date of application, or an intention to use it, shall accompany the application as provided herein. 

Where a series of trade marks are similar but not identical, a single application may cover multiple variations subject to payment of additional fees. The Registrar may require evidence substantiating distinctiveness and prohibiting deceptive similarity with existing registered trade marks or pending applications for registration under this Act. A collective mark denoting membership in an association may also be similarly registered.

Any person claiming to be the proprietor of a trade mark used or proposed to be used may apply to the Registrar for registration thereof, subject to the provisions of this Act. An application for registration shall not be refused on the ground that the trade mark is descriptive of the character or quality of the goods or services if it has acquired distinctiveness through use. The Registrar may require evidence of such distinctive character before allowing the application to proceed. Where a trade mark consists wholly of a surname, or a geographical name, registration shall not be granted unless it is shown that the said mark distinguishes the applicant’s goods or services in the relevant market. A registered trade mark shall confer upon the proprietor exclusive rights to use the mark in relation to the goods or services for which it is registered and to obtain relief in respect of infringement thereof as provided herein. Any person aggrieved by a refusal to register a trade mark may, within such period as may be prescribed, appeal to the High Court.

Any person claiming to be the proprietor of a trade mark used or proposed to be used may apply to the Registrar of Trade Marks in the prescribed manner for the registration of the trade mark. The application shall include a statement as to the goods, services and description of goods relating to which the registration is sought. An applicant seeking registration of a trade mark incorporating any geographical indication shall submit a certificate from the concerned authority confirming that the applicant is authorized to use such geographical indication in relation to those goods or services. Subject to such conditions as may be prescribed, where a trade mark consists of a well-known mark which is not registered in India for those goods or services, but is registered in one or more other countries, the Registrar may require evidence of its use in those countries. Provided that the Registrar shall consider any opposition filed against the application and determine whether the proposed trade mark is capable of distinguishing the goods or services of one person from those of another, as provided herein. The Registrar may, after examination, accept or refuse the application.

Any person desiring to register a trade mark shall submit an application in the prescribed form to the Trade Marks Registry accompanied by the requisite fee, subject to verification that the proposed trade mark does not conflict with any existing registered trade mark or pending applications therefor. An applicant may claim priority under this Act if they have previously filed an application for registration of the same trade mark in a convention country and such application was filed within six months prior to the Indian application. The Registry shall examine the application and, where it conforms to all requirements as provided herein, shall advertise it in the Trade Marks Journal. Opposition to the registration of a trade mark may be filed by any person alleging that its use would be detrimental to their interests or likely to cause confusion among consumers; such opposition shall be adjudicated according to established procedures. Registration of a trade mark confers upon the owner the exclusive right to use the same in relation to the goods or services for which it is registered, subject to continued renewal and payment of prescribed fees.

Any person who applies a trade mark deceptively similar to a registered trade mark, whether in connection with identical or dissimilar goods as provided herein, shall be deemed to have committed an act of unfair trade practice and shall be liable for damages. A proprietor of a registered trade mark may institute civil proceedings for infringement before any District Court competent to hear such matters; however, prior notice of intention to sue is mandatory unless circumstances render it impractical. Any counterfeit goods bearing a falsely applied trade mark seized under this Act shall be subject to order of destruction by a Magistrate First Class or higher. Failure to comply with an order for destruction shall attract a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees and imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, subject to the discretion of the court. The Registrar may, upon sufficient cause shown, direct rectification of the Register of Trade Marks if fraudulent application is proven.

Any person desiring to assign a trade mark, or any right in a trade mark, shall execute a written instrument of assignment embodying all the necessary terms and conditions including but not limited to the specific mark assigned, consideration paid, territory of application, and duration of the assignment. Such an instrument may also provide for covenants restricting the use of the trade mark by the assignor following the completion of the transfer, subject to such limitations as are reasonable and do not unduly restrain trade. A license to use a registered trade mark shall be construed as a partial assignment of right, and any agreement pertaining thereto must clearly delineate the scope of permitted usage, including class of goods or services, geographical area, and duration. Failure to fully disclose all material terms in an instrument of assignment or licensing may render it unenforceable under this Act. The Registrar shall maintain a public register of assignments and licenses as provided herein.

Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Registrar refusing to register a trade mark, or requiring an amendment of any entry in the Register, may file an appeal to the High Court within three months from the date of such decision; provided that such appeal shall not be entertained unless the appellant satisfies the court that they have suffered substantial loss or injury as a direct result of the Registrar’s action. The aggrieved party must demonstrate prior use of a deceptively similar mark, establishing likelihood of confusion amongst consumers, and further prove that the refusal to register impacts their commercial interests. Where an appeal concerns a claim of passing off based on unregistered trade marks, evidence of goodwill and misrepresentation shall be paramount. Should the High Court uphold the Registrar’s decision, no further appeal shall lie except where questions of law are involved, subject to the discretion of the appellate court.

Any person claiming to be the proprietor of a trade mark used or proposed to be used upon particular goods may apply to the Trade Marks Registry in the prescribed manner for registration of the said trade mark. The application shall contain a representation of the trade mark, particulars relating to the goods and services to which it relates, and details of the applicant including their address for service. Upon receipt of an application appearing to be duly completed, the Registrar shall examine it and may require amendments or further information as deemed necessary. Subject to satisfaction of all requirements as provided herein, and following publication of the trade mark in the Trade Marks Journal for purposes of opposition, the Registrar may register the trade mark if no valid grounds for refusal exist. Registration shall confer upon the proprietor exclusive right to use the trade mark in relation to those goods or services, subject to limitations outlined within this Act. An applicant registration will be maintained on the Register and is open to public inspection.

A trade mark shall be registrable under this Act if it is distinctive and not descriptive of the character or quality of the goods for which registration is sought, and does not conflict with any earlier trade marks existing on the Register. An application for registration must clearly identify the goods intended to be covered by the mark, categorized according to the international classification of goods and services as adopted from time to time. Registration shall confer upon the proprietor exclusive rights to use the trade mark in relation to those specified goods. However, such rights are subject to honest local practice and do not extend to prevent bona fide use of descriptive terms necessary for designating the character or quality of the goods. Provided that a registered trade mark may be revoked if it remains unused for a continuous period of five years and there is no intention to resume its use. Any person aggrieved by the registration of a trade mark, alleging bad faith or lack of distinctive character, may file an opposition within the prescribed time limit.

Any person claiming ownership of a trade mark used in connection with agricultural produce, including uniquely identified plant varieties registered under the Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Act, 2001, shall apply for registration as provided herein. Failure to register such a trade mark within three years from the date of first use in commerce shall render it vulnerable to opposition based on prior art or confusing similarity with existing marks. Any person who falsely applies a registered trade mark, or a deceptively similar mark, to goods relating to protected plant varieties, intending to deceive purchasers as to origin or quality, commits an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. The court trying such offence may also order the seizure and destruction of falsely marked goods. Any aggrieved party may initiate proceedings for rectification of the register where misrepresentation exists regarding the plant variety associated with the trade mark.

Any person desiring to assign or otherwise transfer their rights in a registered trade mark shall submit an application for such assignment or transfer to the Trade Marks Registry in the prescribed form, accompanied by the requisite fee. The application shall clearly identify the trade mark, the parties involved in the transaction, and the nature of the rights being transferred, whether partial or complete. Subject to verification by the Registry that the proposed assignee is legally competent to hold a trade mark, and provided that no objection is sustained under this Act relating to the assignment itself, the Trade Marks Registry shall register the transfer of ownership. A license, whether exclusive or non-exclusive, may also be recorded with the Registry upon submission of a written agreement outlining the terms and conditions governing its use. Failure to record any such assignment or license shall not invalidate it but may affect its enforceability against third parties unaware of the transaction. The Registrar reserves the right to require further evidence as deemed necessary for proper adjudication.

A trade mark, as defined under this Act, shall mean a mark capable of being represented graphically including words, letters and numerals or by conventional symbols, the combination of colours or any combination thereof, used or proposed to be used in relation to goods to indicate a connection between the goods and some person having the right to use the mark. The India Registrar may maintain a Register of Trade Marks wherein applications for registration shall be recorded subject to verification of distinctiveness and compliance with procedural requirements as provided herein. A registered trade mark shall confer upon the proprietor exclusive rights to use the mark in relation to the goods specified, and subject to limitations prescribed by this Act, to obtain relief against infringement. Any person aggrieved may apply to the India Registrar for rectification of the register.

The Registrar appointed under this Act shall maintain a Register of Copyrights in such form as may be prescribed, and all entries made therein shall be subject to verification by such means as the Registrar deems fit. Any person intending to claim copyright in a work shall submit an application to the Registrar accompanied by the requisite fee and particulars of the work. The Registrar may, after examining the application and being satisfied that it conforms to the requirements of this Act, register the copyright and issue a certificate of registration. Provided that failure to obtain registration shall not prejudice any rights accruing to the applicant as provided herein, but such registration shall be prima facie evidence of facts stated therein. All records maintained by the Registrar shall be open to inspection by interested parties subject to payment of prescribed fees and compliance with conditions specified by the Registrar.

The Registrar, exercising functions as provided herein, shall maintain a Register of Copyrights in such form as may be prescribed. Any person claiming to be the owner of copyright, or intending to become so, may apply to the Registrar for registration of their work, subject to payment of the applicable fee. Upon receipt of an application and satisfactory verification of particulars, the Registrar shall enter the details in the Register and issue a Certificate of Registration. The certificate shall constitute prima facie evidence of ownership unless and until duly challenged through legal proceedings. Any alteration or amendment to the registered particulars requires notification to, and subsequent entry by, the Registrar. Failure to maintain accurate records with the Registrar may be considered during disputes regarding copyright entitlement, though registration is not mandatory for claiming copyright under this Act. The Registrar may require additional evidence if doubt arises concerning the validity of a claim.

The Registrar, upon receiving an application for registration of copyright, shall examine it to ascertain whether it conforms to the requirements of this Act and the rules made thereunder. If the Registrar is satisfied that such requirements are met, they may register the work and issue a certificate of registration. However, registration shall not be refused solely on the ground that the applicant has failed to disclose any prior publication of the work, provided that full particulars of such prior publication are furnished at the time of application or within thirty days thereafter. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Registrar refusing registration may, within sixty days from the date of such refusal, prefer an appeal to the High Court having jurisdiction. The Registrar shall maintain a Register of Copyrights open for inspection subject to payment of prescribed fees and any person may obtain certified copies of entries therein as provided herein. Failure of the Registrar to perform duties mandated under this Act will constitute grounds for administrative review.

The Registrar, appointed by the Central Government, shall maintain a Register of Copyrights in such form as may be prescribed. Any person intending to claim copyright in a work shall submit an application to the Registrar, accompanied by the requisite fee and a copy of the work claiming protection, subject to provisions relating to dramatic, musical or literary works where excerpts only may suffice for initial registration purposes. The Registrar may require the applicant to furnish further information or clarification as deemed necessary to ascertain the validity of the claim. Upon satisfactory verification and confirmation that the submitted work meets the criteria stipulated under this Act, the Registrar shall enter the particulars in the Register and issue a Certificate of Registration. Any objection to an entry in the Register shall be filed with the Registrar within thirty days of public notice thereof, after which the Registrar’s decision shall be final, subject to appeal to such appellate authority as may be designated by the Central Government. The Registrar possesses the power to inspect records and conduct inquiries relevant to copyright ownership.

The Registrar, exercising functions as provided herein, shall maintain a Register of Copyrights in such form as may be prescribed by rules made under this Act. Any person intending to claim copyright in a work shall submit an application to the Registrar accompanied by the requisite fee and particulars regarding authorship and ownership. The Registrar may require the applicant to furnish further information or clarification subject to reasonable timelines established through public notification. Upon satisfactory verification of the submitted materials, and confirmation that the work meets the criteria for copyright protection under this Act, the Registrar shall enter the details in the Register and issue a Certificate of Registration. Provided that failure to register a work shall not prejudice its eligibility for copyright; however, registration constitutes prima facie evidence of facts stated therein. The Registrar may, with just cause, rectify any errors or omissions discovered in the Register following due process and opportunity for hearing. All records maintained by the Registrar are open to inspection as prescribed under rules made by the Central Government.

The Registrar, upon receiving an application for registration of copyright as provided herein, may require such further information or evidence from the applicant as deemed necessary to satisfy themselves regarding the particulars furnished in the said application. Any person who knowingly furnishes false information or suppresses material facts in any application made to the Registrar shall be punishable with imprisonment not exceeding three years, or a fine, or both. Should the Registrar refuse registration, a reasoned order detailing the grounds for such refusal must be communicated to the applicant within sixty days of the decision. Appeals against the decisions of the Registrar may be preferred to the High Court having jurisdiction; however, no appeal shall lie if the refusal is based on a determination that the work lacks sufficient originality or does not fall within the scope of works protectable under this Act. Failure to comply with any lawful direction issued by the Registrar constitutes an offence punishable with fine.

The assignment of copyright, and any subsequent transfer thereof, shall vest in the assignee subject to the provisions contained herein. Any person desiring to record an assignment with the Registrar shall submit an application in the prescribed form accompanied by the requisite fee. The Registrar may, prior to registration, require further evidence or clarification regarding the validity or scope of the purported assignment. Where a copyright is assigned for a term, and that term expires, the assignee shall promptly notify the Registrar of such expiration, failing which continued recordation may be deemed an offence under this Act. 

Provided that, where an assignment involves multiple copyrights, a consolidated application detailing each work’s particulars must accompany the submission. The Registrar shall maintain a public register of assignments and licenses, accessible for inspection subject to reasonable conditions. Any dispute regarding ownership arising from registration with the Registrar shall be adjudicated by the competent court having jurisdiction over copyright matters as provided herein.

The Registrar, upon receiving an application for copyright registration accompanied by the prescribed fee as provided herein, shall examine it to ascertain whether it fulfils all requirements stipulated within this Act and associated rules. Should the Registrar deem the application deficient, notice of such deficiency shall be issued to the applicant, affording a period of thirty days to remedy the same; failure to do so may result in rejection of the application without further recourse, unless extended by the Registrar for sufficient cause shown. Any person aggrieved by the decision of the Registrar regarding refusal of registration or any other matter pertaining to copyright ownership may prefer an appeal to the High Court within sixty days from the date of communication of such decision. Such appeals shall be heard expeditiously and subject to the procedural norms established by that court, with a right granted for representation by legal counsel before it. The Registrar’s records shall remain open for inspection during office hours under reasonable conditions prescribed.

The Registrar, exercising functions as provided herein, shall maintain a comprehensive register of copyrights, ensuring accurate recording of all applications and subsequent amendments thereto. Any person aggrieved by any act or omission of the Registrar may submit a reasoned representation seeking review; however, such representations must be lodged within thirty days of the relevant action. The Controller, acting in aid of the Registrar, is empowered to conduct inquiries into the veracity of claims made within said representations. Failure to comply with duly issued directives from either the Registrar or the Controller shall attract a penalty not exceeding five thousand rupees. Knowingly providing false information to the Registrar constitutes an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. All fees collected by the Registrar shall be credited to the Consolidated Fund of India.

The Registrar appointed under this Act shall maintain a Register of Copyrights in such form as may be prescribed, and all entries made therein shall be subject to verification and confirmation by the Registrar. Any person aggrieved by any decision of the Registrar relating to registration or refusal of registration may, within thirty days from the date of such decision, prefer an appeal to the High Court. Provided that the Registrar may, with prior notice to the copyright owner, initiate proceedings for revocation of a registered copyright if credible evidence suggests misrepresentation in the original application or non-compliance with statutory requirements as provided herein. The Registrar shall have the power to require any person to attend before them and produce documents relevant to any matter under consideration. All records maintained by the Registrar shall be open to inspection subject to reasonable fees.

The Registrar, exercising the powers conferred by this Act, may require an applicant seeking registration of a dramatic work to furnish a clear statement regarding the authorship of the underlying literary work upon which such dramatic work is based, subject to the provisions contained herein. Any application not accompanied by said statement shall be deemed incomplete and liable for rejection without further notice. The Registrar shall maintain a register of all registered dramatic works, detailing the title, author, publisher, and date of first publication where applicable. Should any dispute arise concerning ownership or originality, the Registrar may request additional evidence from the applicant or require them to appear before an examining officer for clarification. Provided that the Registrar’s decision on matters of registration shall be without prejudice to any legal proceedings relating to copyright infringement which may subsequently be initiated. All fees associated with applications processed by the Registrar are non-refundable except as explicitly provided under these rules.

Registration of a work under this Act shall be optional, and no right to copyright shall accrue solely by virtue of such registration. An application for registration may be made by the author of a work, or his duly authorized agent, and shall be in such form as may be prescribed. The Register of Copyrights shall maintain a register containing particulars of all works registered under this Act, which register shall be open to inspection subject to payment of the prescribed fee. Provided that information relating to the identity of the author, if explicitly requested to remain confidential at the time of registration, shall not be disclosed except upon production of an order from a court of competent jurisdiction or as otherwise provided herein. Any person aggrieved by the refusal of registration may appeal to the High Court.

Any person claiming ownership of copyright in any work shall maintain a Register of Copyrights with the Registrar of Copyrights established under this Act. The application for registration shall be made in the prescribed form and accompanied by the requisite fee, subject to rules framed regarding acceptable evidence of authorship and publication. Upon satisfactory verification of the particulars furnished and confirmation that the work is not already registered or subject to any existing dispute, the Registrar may enter the details in the Register of Copyrights and issue a Certificate of Registration. Provided that registration shall not be refused merely on account of minor defects which do not affect the veracity of the claim. The register maintained under this Act shall be open for inspection by any person interested therein upon payment of the prescribed fee, subject to reasonable restrictions as may be necessary to protect confidential information. Failure to maintain accurate records or provide truthful details in support of a registration application may attract penalties as provided herein.

Any person claiming to be the author of a literary, dramatic, musical or artistic work, or the producer of a cinematograph film or sound recording, may make an application for registration of copyright subsisting in such work as provided herein. The Registrar shall, upon receipt of an application duly accompanied by the prescribed fee and particulars, examine it and, if satisfied that the applicant is the author or producer, register the copyright in the Register of Copyrights. Registration constitutes *prima facie* evidence of ownership and subsistence of copyright; however, such registration shall not be conclusive proof as to validity of the right. A certificate of registration may be issued under seal, and a copy thereof shall be furnished to the applicant. Subject to the provisions of this Act, any person aggrieved by a refusal of registration may appeal to the High Court within thirty days from the date of such refusal. Failure to register does not prejudice any rights or remedies otherwise available to the copyright holder; however, in any legal proceeding concerning ownership, registration shall be a significant factor considered by the court.

Any person claiming to be the author of a work, or deriving title from such author, may make an application for registration of copyright in such work as provided herein. The application shall be made in writing, in such form and accompanied by such fee as may be prescribed, and shall contain such particulars as are necessary for identification of the work, including its title and details of authorship. Upon receipt of a complete application, the Copyright Office shall examine it to ensure conformity with the requirements of this Act. If satisfied that the application is duly completed and contains no discrepancies, the Registrar of Copyrights shall register the copyright in the Register of Copyrights and issue a certificate of registration to the applicant. Registration shall be conclusive evidence of entry but not proof of validity of copyright; however, absent compelling reasons to the contrary, such registration shall be considered prima facie evidence of facts stated therein. Subject to rules made under this Act, any alteration or amendment to particulars registered may be effected upon application and payment of prescribed fees.

Any person claiming ownership of copyright shall, subject to the provisions of this Act, apply for registration with the Registrar of Copyrights in the prescribed manner. The application for registration shall be accompanied by the requisite fee as specified in Schedule I and include particulars relating to authorship, publication, and other details necessary to establish a prima facie case for copyright. Registration is not compulsory; however, it creates a rebuttable presumption of valid copyright ownership and date of creation, facilitating legal proceedings. Provided that failure to register does not invalidate the copyright itself, but may affect evidentiary weight in disputes concerning infringement or assignment. The Registrar may require further evidence or clarification before granting registration, and shall maintain a public Register of Copyrights accessible for inspection as provided herein. Any alteration to particulars registered shall be duly notified to the Registrar within thirty days of such change occurring.

Any person claiming to be the author of a work, or deriving title from such author, may apply for registration of copyright as provided herein. The application shall be made in writing to the Registrar of Copyrights and shall be accompanied by the prescribed fee and requisite particulars including details regarding authorship and publication. Failure to complete registration shall not invalidate the existence of copyright but shall prejudice any claim to relief in suits for infringement or other legal proceedings under this Act. Provided that, if a work is registered with demonstrable falsity concerning ownership or originality, the Registrar may initiate inquiries and impose a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees. Any person who knowingly makes a false statement in an application for registration shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. The Registrar may, subject to such conditions as deemed fit, restore a lapsed registration if sufficient cause is shown.

Any person desiring to assign or license, whether exclusively or non-exclusively, the copyright in a work, or any right therein as provided herein, shall submit an application for registration of such assignment or licence to the designated Registrar of Copyrights. The application shall be accompanied by certified copies of the instrument of assignment or licensing agreement and shall clearly delineate the scope of rights transferred, including territorial limitations and duration. Registration of an assignment or license is not compulsory but serves as prima facie evidence of its validity in any legal proceeding. Failure to register such transfer does not invalidate it, however, a registered assignee or licensee shall be entitled to certain benefits regarding proof of ownership and enforcement of rights. Subject to the provisions contained within this Act, the Registrar may require additional information or clarification from the applicant before granting registration. The Registrar shall maintain a public index of all registered assignments and licenses for inspection as prescribed.

Any person claiming ownership of copyright may apply for registration with the Registrar of Copyrights, submitting an affidavit detailing the work’s creation and authorship. The application shall be subject to verification by the Registrar, who may require further evidence or clarification regarding originality and subsistence of copyright. Should the Registrar refuse registration, a reasoned order stating grounds for rejection will be issued, affording the applicant thirty days to file an appeal before the High Court having jurisdiction. An appeal lodged beyond this period shall not be entertained unless sufficient cause is demonstrated. Furthermore, any aggrieved party disputing a validly registered copyright may initiate proceedings seeking rectification of the register or revocation of registration, provided that such dispute does not pertain to questions of artistic merit but solely to matters of ownership and validity as per provisions herein. The Registrar’s decision on rectification requests shall be final, subject only to appeal to the Supreme Court.

Any person intending to claim copyright in a work shall apply for registration with the Registrar of Copyrights in the prescribed manner, furnishing all necessary particulars and depositing the required fee. Registration is not compulsory but serves as prima facie evidence of authorship and ownership as provided herein. Any party opposing such registration shall file a notice of opposition within thirty days of the publication of the application, stating the grounds for objection with supporting documentation. Failure to substantiate claims made in an opposition may render the objector liable to pay damages and costs to the applicant. The Registrar, upon considering all evidence presented, may accept or reject the application; a rejected applicant may appeal this decision to the High Court having jurisdiction. Any false statement made during the registration process shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

Any person desiring to commercially exploit a copyrighted work, including through licensing arrangements or assignment of rights, shall apply for registration as provided herein. The application for such registration shall be made to the designated Registrar of Copyrights in the prescribed form and accompanied by the requisite fee. Upon satisfactory verification of the particulars furnished and subject to fulfillment of all statutory requirements, the Registrar shall enter the details of the copyright ownership and licensing terms in the Register of Copyrights. 

A registered proprietor may also seek to register trade marks associated with the copyrighted work to further protect its brand identity and prevent unauthorized merchandising. Any subsequent assignment or transfer of rights arising from a license granted under this Act must be duly recorded with the Registrar, failing which such transfers shall be deemed invalid against third parties acting in good faith. The Register maintained under these provisions shall be prima facie evidence of ownership and licensing status.

Any person intending to claim copyright in a literary, dramatic, musical or artistic work shall apply for registration as provided herein, submitting such particulars and delivering such copies of the work as may be prescribed. The Register of Copyrights shall, upon examination of the application and satisfaction that the work is eligible for copyright, enter the particulars in the Register and issue a certificate of registration. Registration constitutes prima facie evidence of valid copyright ownership and subsisting rights therein, subject to rectification proceedings where fraud or error is established. However, failure to register does not prejudice the right to claim copyright; it merely affects enforceability against infringers. Where a work has been registered and a dispute arises concerning its exploitation, an application may be made for compulsory licensing if the owner of copyright fails to adequately utilize such rights within a period specified by notification, provided that reasonable notice is given and fair remuneration determined. All registrations shall remain in force until cancelled or revoked as per the provisions of this Act.

A geographical indication identifies goods originating from a specific geographical area where a quality, reputation or other characteristic of such good is essentially attributable to its place of origin. Such indication serves to distinguish the goods of one region from those of another and may function as a signpost of quality for consumers. A registered geographical indication shall be protectable under this Act, subject to fulfilling conditions regarding specificity of origin and linkage to qualities or reputation. Where a product possesses both a geographical indication and a trade name, the latter shall not prejudice the protection afforded to the former, provided that such trade name does not mislead consumers as to the true origin of the goods. The Registrar may, upon application, refuse registration if the proposed geographical indication is generic in nature.

Any person claiming a geographical indication for goods originating from a specific region in India may apply for registration under this Act, submitting an application to the Geographical Indications Registry in the prescribed manner. The application shall clearly identify the goods, their source, and define the area of origin constituting the geographical indication. A statement detailing how the specified qualities or reputation of the goods are linked to that geographical area must accompany the application. Where a producers’ organization is established for promoting and protecting the geographical indication, it may apply on behalf of its members subject to demonstrating adequate representation and control over quality standards. The Registry shall examine the application to ascertain if the claimed geographical indication meets the criteria as provided herein, including verification of origin rules and potential conflicts with existing registered indications or trademarks. Registration shall confer exclusive rights to use the geographical indication in relation to those goods.

Any person who, being the proprietor of a registered geographical indication, discovers the unauthorized use of such geographical indication by any other person, may institute civil proceedings for injunction and damages before a District Court having jurisdiction over the place where the offending goods are sold or manufactured. The plaintiff shall, prior to institution of such suit, provide reasonable notice in writing to the defendant of the claim, indicating the nature of the unauthorized use and demanding cessation thereof; provided that no such notice shall be necessary if the plaintiff demonstrates imminent irreparable harm resulting from continued infringement. 

A registered geographical indication vests a right *in rem* against all potential infringers, subject to limitations as provided herein regarding permissible usage for bona fide prior users established before the registration date. The court may, at its discretion and considering the nature of the unauthorized use, award exemplary damages not exceeding three times the actual damages suffered by the proprietor, alongside reasonable costs of litigation. Any order granting relief shall clearly define the geographical territory to which such protection extends.

A register maintained by the Controller of Geographical Indications shall, subject to such conditions as may be prescribed, contain particulars of all registered geographical indications and applications for registration pending before him. Any person considering himself aggrieved by any decision of the Controller regarding the refusal of a geographical indication or its modification, may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board within three months from the date of the order appealed against. The Appellate Board shall, after giving the applicant and the Controller a reasonable opportunity of being heard, pass such orders as it deems fit, confirming, modifying or reversing the decision of the Controller. A geographical indication shall not be registered if it is likely to cause confusion with an existing trade mark under the Trade Marks Act, 1999, or if it contains scandalous or deceptive matter. Provided that a geographical indication which, though resembling a trade mark, identifies the region of origin and possesses distinctive character may be permitted registration subject to such conditions as the Controller deems necessary to avoid consumer deception. The Controller may require evidence establishing a clear link between the goods and their geographical origin before granting registration.

A geographical indication denoting the origin of goods, and possessing qualities or a reputation attributable to that place of origin, shall be registrable under this Act subject to compliance with all provisions herein. An applicant seeking registration must demonstrate a demonstrable link between the specified goods and the geographical area concerned, evidenced by traditional knowledge or production methods unique to that region. The register maintained as provided herein shall contain particulars of the geographical indication including its description, the territory it represents, and the list of producers associated with it. Any alteration affecting the essential characteristics of the geographical indication, or a substantial change in the specification of goods, requires prior notification to the Registry and may be subject to review. A registered proprietor shall exercise due diligence in maintaining quality control and preventing misuse or unauthorized use of the geographical indication, failing which remedies as prescribed herein may apply. The term of registration is renewable for successive periods of ten years.

Any person who, with intent to deceive the public, falsely applies a geographical indication in relation to goods not originating from the territory associated with such indication shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than six months but which may extend to three years and with fine not less than fifty thousand rupees but which may extend to two lakh rupees. Where any consignment of goods bearing a false geographical indication is imported into India, the Customs authorities may seize such goods as provided herein. The registered proprietor of a geographical indication, or anyone authorised by them, may institute civil proceedings for infringement under this Act. Any act constituting an offence under this Act shall be cognizable and non-bailable, subject to investigation by a police officer not below the rank of Inspector. A collective body representing producers of goods associated with a geographical indication may also pursue remedies available as provided herein.

Any person being an applicant for the registration of a geographical indication, desiring to grant licenses to others for use of said geographical indication in relation to goods conforming to the standards prescribed herein, shall submit an application to the Registry detailing the terms and conditions proposed for such licensing arrangements. The Registrar may, subject to verification that the proposed terms do not unduly restrict production or harm the reputation of the geographical indication, approve the license format. Assignment of any right in a registered geographical indication shall be effective only upon registration of the assignment with the Registry and payment of the prescribed fee; provided that no such assignment shall prejudice existing licenses granted prior to the date of assignment unless expressly agreed to by both parties. The holder of a geographical indication may, as provided herein, enter into contracts for its exclusive exploitation in specific territories or for particular goods within the scope of the registered specification. Any dispute regarding licensing or assignment shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the designated court.

Any person aggrieved by the refusal of the Registrar to register a geographical indication, or by any decision of the Board regarding the rectification, revocation, or assignment of registration of such an indication, may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board. Such appeal shall be filed within three months from the date of the order appealed against, subject to extension granted by the Appellate Board for sufficient cause shown. The grounds for appeal shall be limited to errors apparent on the record and questions of law; factual disputes shall not form the basis of any such appeal. Furthermore, an application for rectification may be instituted before the Registrar if it appears that a registered geographical indication has ceased to be a geographical indication or is falsely represented as being associated with goods not originating from the specified region. The Appellate Board’s decision shall be final and binding, save for appeals to the Supreme Court on questions of law of general public importance.

Any transfer of right, title and interest in a registered geographical indication shall be subject to the provisions of this Act and require prior written consent from all producers who are legitimately engaged in the activity giving rise to the said geographical indication.
