The petition shall clearly articulate the grounds for the allegation, identifying the specific layout-design right claimed to be infringed and detailing the nature of the infringing act. Supporting evidence, including but not limited to, comparative analyses of the layout-design and the alleged infringing article, shall accompany the petition. 

The Board may, subject to verification of the petition’s veracity and completeness, direct the alleged infringer to file a response within a period not exceeding thirty days. Failure to respond within the stipulated timeframe may result in ex parte proceedings. A petitioner seeking interim relief, such as an injunction restraining the manufacture or sale of the infringing article, shall demonstrate a prima facie case and the potential for irreparable harm. The Board, as provided herein, retains the discretion to award costs to the prevailing party. Any misrepresentation in the zm form petition shall be subject to penalties as deemed fit.

Any person intending to initiate a dispute regarding the validity of a registered layout-design, or alleging infringement thereof, shall submit a zm form petition to the appropriate authority designated for the purpose, and such petition shall be accompanied by a non-refundable fee as prescribed in Schedule III. The petition shall clearly and concisely state the grounds upon which the dispute is founded, identifying with particularity the registered layout-design in question and the alleged acts of infringement. Supporting documentation, including but not limited to, technical drawings, samples of the integrated circuit, and evidence of commercial exploitation, may be submitted to substantiate the claims made within the petition. 

Provided that, a petition lacking the requisite fee or failing to adequately specify the grounds for dispute may be rejected by the authority. The authority, upon receipt of a complete zm form petition, shall, subject to the provisions contained herein, notify the respondent and afford them an opportunity to submit a reply within thirty days. Failure to respond within the stipulated timeframe may result in ex parte proceedings.

Any person desiring registration of a layout-design shall submit a zm form petition to the Controller, accompanied by the prescribed fee and all necessary documentation as provided herein. The petition shall clearly and accurately delineate the layout-design for which protection is sought, including a detailed description of its topological features and the semiconductor integrated circuit in which it is incorporated. Supporting documentation shall include a clear and unambiguous depiction of each layer constituting the layout-design, demonstrating its original character. 

Provided that, if the applicant is claiming priority based on an earlier application filed in a convention country, a certified copy of such application, along with a verified English translation if necessary, must be submitted with the zm form petition. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in the rejection of the petition, subject to a reasonable opportunity to rectify the deficiencies. The Controller may, at their discretion, request additional information or clarification to ensure full compliance with this Act.

Any person alleging infringement of a registered layout-design, prior to initiating proceedings before any court, shall submit a zm form petition to the Controller of Patents and Designs, detailing with particularity the nature of the alleged infringement and identifying the registered layout-design relied upon. The Controller, upon receipt of such petition and subject to verification of the registration status, may, if satisfied that a prima facie case exists, issue a cease and desist notice to the alleged infringer. Failure to submit a zm form petition as provided herein shall render any subsequent legal action initiated by the complainant inadmissible. Any person found to have knowingly made false representations in a zm form petition shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with a fine, or with both. The Controller’s decision regarding the prima facie case is subject to appeal before the High Court. Repeated failure to comply with the requirements of this Act may result in suspension of rights to register further layout-designs.

Any person desiring to obtain a license under this Act, or to assign rights in a registered layout-design, shall submit a zm form petition to the appropriate authority, duly completed and verified in the manner prescribed. The petition shall clearly identify the layout-design in question, including its registration number and the name and address of the registered proprietor. Furthermore, it shall state the specific terms and conditions sought in the license, or details of the proposed assignment, including the consideration offered and the scope of rights being transferred. 

Subject to verification of the petition’s completeness and accuracy, the authority may, if satisfied, proceed to notify the registered proprietor and invite their response. Any assignment of rights shall be void unless recorded with the authority, and a request for such recordation must be accompanied by a written consent from the registered proprietor. Provided that, the authority may, in exceptional circumstances, direct assignment even without explicit consent, if it deems such action necessary to prevent undue hardship or promote public interest, following a reasoned order.

Any person aggrieved by an order of the Registrar refusing to register a layout-design, or imposing conditions on registration, or revoking registration, may file a petition with the Appellate Board. Such petition shall be filed within ninety days from the date of the order appealed against, and shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the order and a statement of the grounds on which the appeal is based. The Appellate Board may, if satisfied that sufficient cause exists, extend this period, but not beyond an additional thirty days. The prescribed fee for filing the zm form petition shall be remitted as detailed in Schedule IV. Furthermore, any party opposing the registration may, subject to the provisions of this Act, submit a counter-statement to the Appellate Board within thirty days of receiving notice of the petition. The Appellate Board shall, after considering the petition, any counter-statement, and all relevant evidence, pass an order affirming, modifying, or reversing the order of the Registrar. A decision of the Appellate Board shall be final and binding, subject to writ jurisdiction by the High Court.

Any person desiring to initiate a dispute regarding the validity of a registered layout-design, or alleging infringement thereof, shall present a zm form petition to the Registrar. The petition shall be in triplicate and accompanied by a statement of facts supporting the claim, alongside certified copies of any relevant documentation demonstrating proprietary rights or evidence of alleged infringement. The Registrar, upon receipt of such petition, shall assign a unique reference number and acknowledge receipt to the petitioner within fourteen days. Subject to verification of jurisdictional competence and adherence to procedural requirements as provided herein, the Registrar may direct the alleged infringer to file a reply within thirty days of service of notice. The register title registrar maintains a public record of all petitions received and associated correspondence, accessible for inspection during office hours, subject to reasonable restrictions. Provided that, the Registrar may, at any stage, require the petitioner to amend the petition if it is found to be deficient in form or substance, and failure to comply within the stipulated timeframe may result in its rejection.

Any person desiring to initiate a dispute regarding the validity of a registered layout-design, or alleging infringement thereof, shall submit a zm form petition to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board, duly completed in all respects as prescribed by rules made under this Act. The petition shall clearly identify the registered layout-design in question, the alleged infringer, and the specific grounds upon which the dispute is based, supported by verifiable technical documentation. Should the petition lack sufficient detail or fail to meet the procedural requirements, the Board may, at its discretion, request further clarification or reject the petition outright. It is further provided that any amendment to the petition, affecting the scope of the claim or the identity of the parties, requires prior approval of the Board. The Parliament may, by notification in the Official Gazette, prescribe additional forms or modify existing ones to facilitate efficient adjudication of disputes arising under this Act, ensuring consistent application of the prescribed procedures. Compliance with these provisions is mandatory for the valid commencement of any legal proceedings.

Every petition for the registration of a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design shall contain particulars affirming exclusive rights, and shall be filed with the Controller in the manner as provided herein. The petition particulars contained within any such filing must include a statement of ownership, clearly identifying the applicant as the proprietor of the layout-design, or demonstrating sufficient cause for claiming rights derived from the proprietor. A detailed description of the layout-design, including its topological characteristics and intended application, is also mandatory. Should the applicant not be the sole creator, a declaration outlining the contributions of each individual involved, alongside evidence of assignment of rights, shall accompany the petition. Furthermore, representation of the layout-design, in the form of a mask or other suitable depiction, must be submitted, subject to the Controller’s requirements regarding format and scale. Any claim of priority based on an earlier application shall be explicitly stated, along with supporting documentation. Failure to furnish complete and accurate petition particulars may result in rejection of the application.

Any person desiring to initiate proceedings for infringement of a layout-design right, as provided herein, shall present a petition to the designated Intellectual Property Appellate Board, setting forth particulars of the alleged infringement with sufficient specificity to enable a reasoned adjudication. Such petition particulars contained shall include a clear and concise description of the layout-design right claimed, identifying the semiconductor integrated circuit in which it is embodied, and demonstrating the commercial exploitation of said layout-design within the territory of India. The petitioner shall also furnish details of the alleged infringer, the nature of the infringing act, and the relief sought, including but not limited to an injunction restraining further infringement and a claim for damages. Provided that, the petition shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the registration certificate for the layout-design, unless an exception applies under this Act relating to derived layout-designs. Failure to comply with these requirements may render the petition inadmissible, subject to the discretion of the Appellate Board. The Board may, at any stage, require further information or clarification from either party to ensure a fair and just determination of the matter.

Any person desiring to register a layout-design shall present a petition to the Controller in the prescribed form, accompanied by the requisite fee as specified in the Schedule. The petition particulars contained therein shall include a statement of ownership, identifying the applicant as the creator or assignee of the layout-design, and a clear and accurate depiction of the layout-design, including all layers constituting the same. Should the applicant be an assignee, verifiable evidence of title, such as a duly executed assignment deed, must accompany the petition. 

Furthermore, the petition shall state the extent of protection sought, limited to the specific layout-design depicted and not extending to the underlying semiconductor integrated circuit. A declaration affirming the originality of the layout-design and that it has not been previously published or exploited anywhere in the world is mandatory. The Controller may, subject to such terms and conditions as may be deemed fit, require the applicant to furnish additional information or documents to satisfy themselves as to the validity of the petition and the accuracy of the representations made therein. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in the rejection of the petition.

Any petition for the rectification of the register of layout-designs shall be presented to the Controller in the prescribed form and shall be accompanied by a statement of the grounds on which the rectification is sought. The petition particulars contained therein must clearly identify the layout-design in question, specifying the article in which it is incorporated, and demonstrating sufficient interest by the petitioner. Subject to such conditions as may be prescribed, a petitioner who is not the proprietor of the layout-design may present a petition for rectification based on grounds of prior art, provided that such prior art was publicly known or available before the filing date of the layout-design. Where a petition alleges fraudulent misrepresentation, supporting evidence demonstrating such misrepresentation shall be furnished with the petition. The Controller may, at any stage, require the petitioner to furnish further evidence or clarification, and failure to comply with such a requirement may lead to the rejection of the petition. All petitions shall be subject to a prescribed fee.

Any person alleging infringement of a registered layout-design right shall, prior to the institution of proceedings before a competent court, furnish to the Controller a detailed petition particulars contained therein specifying with precision the nature of the infringement, the layout-design right asserted, and the grounds upon which relief is claimed. Failure to submit complete petition particulars, as determined by the Controller, shall render the application inadmissible and may attract a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees. The Controller, subject to verification of the petition particulars, may initiate an inquiry and, if satisfied of prima facie infringement, direct the alleged infringer to cease all activities contributing to such infringement. Any continued violation of such direction, despite due notice, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years, or with a fine, or with both. Provided that, the Controller may, in cases of demonstrable hardship, extend the time for submission of petition particulars by a period not exceeding thirty days.

Any person aggrieved by an order of the Registrar refusing to register a layout-design, or by an order revoking the registration of a layout-design, may file a petition with the Appellate Board seeking redressal, subject to the provisions contained herein. The petition particulars contained within such filing shall clearly delineate the grounds of objection to the Registrar’s decision, specifying with precision the alleged errors in fact or law. Furthermore, the petitioner shall demonstrate a substantial question of law requiring consideration by the Appellate Board. Should the Appellate Board determine that no such question exists, it may dismiss the petition summarily, with costs as it deems fit. An applicant seeking restoration of a revoked registration shall, in addition to the aforementioned requirements, provide evidence of due diligence exercised to correct the deficiencies that led to the initial revocation, and shall satisfy the Board that the continued registration serves the public interest. All petitions must be accompanied by certified copies of the impugned order and any relevant supporting documentation.

Any person desiring registration of a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design shall submit a petition to the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trademarks in the prescribed form, accompanied by the requisite fee as specified in the Schedule. The petition particulars contained therein must clearly and accurately delineate the scope of the layout-design for which protection is sought, including a detailed description of each layer constituting the layout. A representation, preferably in electronic format conforming to established standards, shall also be furnished. Where the applicant is not the originator of the layout-design, evidence establishing the right to make the application, such as an assignment or license, shall be submitted. The registered proprietor proposed in the petition shall be identified with complete address details and, in the case of a legal entity, proof of incorporation. Subject to verification and satisfaction of the Controller, a certificate of registration may be issued. Any misrepresentation in the petition shall render the registration liable to revocation as provided herein.

Any person desiring to initiate a dispute regarding the validity of a registered layout-design shall present a petition to the appropriate authority in the prescribed form, detailing with specificity the grounds upon which the challenge is based. The petition particulars contained therein must clearly identify the registered layout-design, the petitioner, and the respondent, alongside a statement of material facts supporting the claim of invalidity. Such petition shall be accompanied by all relevant documentation, including but not limited to, prior art demonstrating lack of novelty or originality, and evidence of any misrepresentation made during the registration process. 

Where the dispute concerns the unauthorized use or reproduction of a registered layout-design, and involves a claim of mark use relating to a product incorporating said layout-design, the petition shall also specify the nature and extent of such use, and the alleged damage suffered by the petitioner. The authority may, subject to such terms and conditions as it deems fit, require the respondent to furnish samples of the allegedly infringing product for examination. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in dismissal of the petition.

Any person alleging infringement of a registered layout-design right shall, prior to the institution of proceedings before any court, submit a petition particulars contained to the appropriate authority, detailing with precision the nature of the alleged infringement, the quantum of damages claimed, and the identity of the alleged infringer, supported by demonstrably reliable technical documentation. Failure to furnish complete and accurate petition particulars contained shall render the initiating party liable to a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees. Where the alleged infringement arises from a dispute subject to an agreement means madrid, the authority may, at its discretion, refer the matter to arbitration under the relevant international treaty, provided that the parties consent to such referral. Any false representation in the petition, intended to mislead the authority, constitutes an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. The authority may, subject to such terms and conditions as it deems fit, require the petitioner to deposit a security for costs.

The petition particulars, required for initiating proceedings under this Act, shall comprehensively detail the alleged infringement, specifying with precision the registered layout-design which is claimed to be violated. Such petition shall further include a clear and concise description of the infringing act, identifying the alleged infringer and the extent of the unlawful reproduction, use, or commercial exploitation. Where a claim for damages is made, the petition particulars must state the basis for calculating such damages, referencing relevant production costs or lost profits, subject to verification as provided herein. Any request for interim injunction shall be accompanied by a statement of justification demonstrating irreparable harm. The applicant shall also disclose any prior art known to them that may bear upon the validity of the registered layout-design, and a declaration affirming the truthfulness of the contents of the petition.

Every petition for the registration of a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design shall contain particulars as prescribed under this Act, and failure to furnish such particulars may render the petition incomplete and liable to rejection. The petition particulars shall include a statement of ownership, identifying the applicant as the creator or lawful assignee of the layout-design, and a clear and concise description of the layout-design, sufficient to enable a person skilled in the art to reproduce the same. A representation or drawing of the layout-design, conforming to the standards as may be notified, shall also be furnished. Where the applicant is not the sole creator, a statement detailing the contributions of each creator and their respective rights shall be included. Subject to verification, the applicant may also submit priority claims based on earlier filings in other jurisdictions, provided that supporting documentation is attached. Any amendment to the petition particulars shall be submitted in writing and be subject to the same scrutiny as the original filing.

Any person desiring to initiate proceedings for infringement of a layout-design right, or seeking rectification of the register, shall present a petition to the appropriate High Court. The petition particulars shall clearly and concisely state the grounds upon which the claim is based, identifying the registered layout-design and the alleged act of infringement with sufficient specificity to enable reasonable investigation. A petitioner may also seek an injunction restraining the defendant from continuing the infringing act, and a decree for damages sustained as a consequence thereof, subject to demonstrating actual loss or reasonable apprehension of loss. 

Where the petition concerns a claim of prior art invalidating a registered layout-design, the particulars must include a detailed description of the prior art, accompanied by supporting evidence establishing its existence before the date of registration. The Court may, at its discretion, require the petitioner to furnish security for costs, particularly if the claim appears frivolous or vexatious. Any misrepresentation in the petition particulars may render the petitioner liable for appropriate penalties as provided herein.

Every petition for the rectification of a registered layout-design shall conform substantially to the requirements as prescribed, and shall be presented to the appropriate authority in the manner directed. The petition particulars shall include a clear and concise statement of the grounds on which rectification is sought, specifying with precision the alleged defects in the registration. Any petition alleging anticipation by prior art shall contain a detailed description of such prior art, accompanied by supporting evidence demonstrating its availability to the public before the filing date of the layout-design. 

Where the petition concerns a claim of lack of novelty, the petitioner shall demonstrate that the layout-design lacks originality, and is not substantially different from any existing layout-design or combination of existing layout-designs. Provided that, a petition may also seek amendment of the registered layout-design, subject to the conditions that such amendment does not extend beyond the scope of the original disclosure, and does not introduce matter which, if the layout-design had been so amended, would have prevented its registration. The authority may, at its discretion, require the petitioner to furnish additional information or evidence as deemed necessary for the proper adjudication of the matter.

Every petition for the rectification of a registered layout-design shall contain particulars as prescribed, and failure to comply with these requirements may render the petition inadmissible. The petition particulars shall include a clear statement of the layout-design sought to be rectified, specifying the alleged defects or inaccuracies therein. A detailed description of the prior art, if any, relied upon to demonstrate the lack of originality of the registered layout-design, must accompany the petition. 

Any petition alleging infringement shall also state the nature of the alleged infringement, identifying the infringing article or act with sufficient precision. The petitioner shall demonstrate a prima facie case of commercial exploitation of the layout-design without authorization, and shall specify the relief sought, including but not limited to, an injunction and damages. Provided that, the petitioner shall furnish an affidavit verifying the truth of the statements contained within the petition particulars, subject to the provisions of this Act regarding false statements.

Any person alleging infringement of a layout-design right, and desiring to initiate proceedings for recovery of damages or an injunction, shall present a petition to the High Court having jurisdiction. Such petition particulars shall include a detailed description of the layout-design alleged to be infringed, identifying the specific elements copied or derived from the petitioner’s registered layout-design. Failure to adequately specify such elements may render the petition inadmissible. The petitioner shall also furnish a statement of the value of the infringed layout-design, calculated according to the provisions of this Act, and a reasonable estimate of damages sought. Provided that, the Court may, subject to verification, direct the respondent to disclose all information relating to production, sale, and inventory of the infringing article. Any false representation in the petition particulars, knowingly made, shall attract a penalty not exceeding five lakh rupees, and may be considered grounds for dismissal of the petition. The Court may, at its discretion, impose costs upon the petitioner for frivolous or vexatious proceedings.

Any person desiring to obtain an assignment of a registered layout-design right shall submit a petition to the appropriate authority, detailing the particulars of the proposed assignment and the consideration offered therefor. Such petition shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the registration certificate and a no-objection statement from the registered proprietor, unless the assignment is by operation of law. The petition particulars shall include the names and addresses of both the assignor and the assignee, a clear description of the layout-design being assigned, and the territorial scope of the assignment. 

Where the assignment involves a partial transfer of rights, the petition shall delineate with precision the specific rights being transferred, and those retained by the assignor. The authority may, subject to verification of the submitted documents and satisfaction of applicable fees as provided herein, record the assignment in the register of layout-designs. Failure to provide complete and accurate petition particulars may result in rejection of the application or delay in processing. Any dispute regarding the validity of the assignment shall be subject to the provisions of this Act.

Any person alleging infringement of a layout-design right, prior to initiating proceedings before the appropriate High Court, shall file a petition with the Controller of Patents, detailing the particulars of the alleged infringement and the relief sought. Such petition particulars shall include a clear and concise description of the layout-design right claimed, identifying the semiconductor integrated circuit in question and specifying the date of its first commercial exploitation. The petitioner must also demonstrate a prima facie case of substantial similarity between the protected layout-design and the allegedly infringing layout-design, supported by technical drawings or photographic evidence. 

Provided that, if the alleged infringer is a foreign national, service of notice of the petition shall be effected in accordance with the provisions relating to international service of process. The Controller, upon receiving the petition, may, subject to such terms and conditions as may be prescribed, direct the alleged infringer to furnish a statement of account regarding articles incorporating the allegedly infringing layout-design. Any appeal against the Controller’s decision on the petition particulars shall lie before the High Court.

Every petition for the registration of a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design shall be presented in triplicate to the Controller, accompanied by a statement detailing the particulars of the layout-design, including its creator, date of creation, and a clear and complete technical description sufficient to enable a person skilled in the art to reproduce the layout-design. The statement shall further specify the class of layout-design and any relevant prior art known to the applicant. All drawings and documentation submitted as part of the petition particulars must conform to the standards prescribed by the Controller. 

Upon receipt of a petition, the Controller shall enter the details in the register and assign a unique registration number. Should the petition be found incomplete or deficient in any respect, the Controller may, subject to these rules, require the applicant to amend or supplement it within a specified period. Failure to comply may result in the rejection of the petition as provided herein.

Any person claiming ownership of a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design shall submit a petition particulars to the appropriate authority, detailing the nature of the layout-design, the date of creation, and the applicant’s right to the layout-design. The petition shall further specify the extent of geographical protection sought and any prior publication or commercial exploitation of the layout-design. Where the applicant seeks certification trade benefits relating to the layout-design, evidence of substantial investment in research and development, and demonstrable market presence, shall accompany the petition. Failure to provide complete and accurate petition particulars may render the application liable to rejection. Any aggrieved party may, subject to such conditions as may be prescribed, file a counter-petition disputing the applicant’s claim. The authority, upon receiving a petition, may require further evidence or clarification from either party, and shall conduct a thorough examination to determine the validity of the claim, as provided herein. Any order made regarding the petition shall be communicated to all parties in writing.

Any person desiring to register a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design shall present a petition to the Controller of Patents, Designs and Trademarks in the prescribed form, accompanied by the requisite fee as detailed in Schedule I. The petition particulars shall include a statement of ownership, identifying the applicant as the proprietor of the layout-design, and a clear declaration regarding the originality of the design. A detailed description of the layout-design, including supporting documentation such as topological data and visual representations, must also be furnished. 

Where the layout-design incorporates an invention convention, being a novel combination of existing layout-designs or features, the applicant shall specifically delineate such convention within the petition, demonstrating its inventive step and industrial applicability. Failure to adequately disclose any prior art relevant to the claimed invention convention may render the petition incomplete. The Controller may, subject to the provisions herein, require the applicant to amend the petition or furnish additional information to ensure its completeness and accuracy. All submissions shall be subject to verification as per the established procedures.

Any person desiring to initiate proceedings relating to the infringement of a layout-design right shall submit a petition particulars to the appropriate authority, detailing with specificity the alleged infringement and the layout-design right claimed. The petition particulars shall include a clear and unambiguous representation of the layout-design, demonstrating its originality and the date of its first commercial exploitation. Subject to verification, the authority may require supplementary evidence to substantiate the claims made within the petition particulars. Where the petitioner seeks representation through a copyright society duly registered under the relevant provisions of this Act, authorization for such representation must accompany the petition particulars. Failure to comply with these requirements may render the petition inadmissible, and the authority shall not be bound to proceed with its consideration. Provided that, the authority may, at its discretion, request clarification or additional information even after acceptance of the petition particulars, to ensure a comprehensive understanding of the matter.

Any person desiring to obtain a license under this Act, or seeking assignment of rights in a registered layout-design, shall submit a petition particulars to the appropriate authority, detailing the scope of the proposed license or assignment, including the territory, duration, and field of use. The petition shall clearly identify the registered layout-design in question, referencing the application number and registration date. All petitions for assignment must specify the consideration offered for the transfer of rights, and demonstrate that the proposed assignee possesses the technical capacity to exploit the layout-design commercially. An appeal fee accompanied, as prescribed by rules made under this Act, shall be submitted with the petition, and failure to do so may render the petition inadmissible. The authority may, subject to such terms and conditions as it deems fit, grant the license or approve the assignment, provided that the applicant demonstrates a legitimate interest and the proposed arrangement does not unduly restrict competition. Any modification to the petition particulars requires prior written consent of the authority.

Any person aggrieved by an order of the Semiconductor Layout-Design Registry rejecting an application for registration, or imposing conditions deemed unfavorable, may, subject to the provisions herein, form petition to the High Court. Such petition shall be filed within ninety days from the date of the order appealed against, and shall clearly state the grounds upon which the order is contested, supported by verifiable evidence. The Registry, upon receipt of notice of such petition, shall forthwith transmit all relevant documents and records pertaining to the application to the High Court. Provided that, the High Court may, at its discretion, require the petitioner to demonstrate prima facie grounds for appeal before proceeding with a full hearing. Furthermore, any opposing party shall be entitled to file a counter-affidavit within thirty days of receiving notice of the petition, outlining their defense. The High Court’s decision on the matter shall be final and binding, subject to any further appeal permissible under the general provisions of law.

Any person aggrieved by an order of the Registrar refusing to grant a layout-design right, or imposing limitations thereon, may, within ninety days of such order, form petition to the Appellate Board seeking redressal. Such petition shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the impugned order and a statement of the grounds on which the order is sought to be set aside or modified. The Appellate Board may, if satisfied that sufficient cause exists, extend the period for filing the petition, provided that the delay is not attributable to deliberate inaction on the part of the petitioner. Where the dispute concerns a clause invention forming a substantial part of the claimed layout-design, the petitioner shall clearly demonstrate the inventive step involved and its non-obviousness to a person skilled in the art, as provided herein. Failure to comply with these requirements may render the petition inadmissible, subject to the discretion of the Appellate Board. The Board shall consider all evidence presented and may, after hearing both parties, confirm, reverse, or modify the Registrar’s order.

The expression “commercial exploitation” with reference to a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design, shall include any act involving the reproduction, distribution, communication to the public, or importation of the layout-design, or of a semiconductor integrated circuit embodying such layout-design, as provided herein. However, such commercial exploitation shall not extend to acts done solely for the purpose of private study, research, or educational purposes, subject to the provisions of this Act. Further, acts involving reverse engineering, to examine, analyze or study the functionality of the layout-design, shall not constitute commercial exploitation, provided that such reverse engineering is solely for the purpose of interoperability or repair. The determination of whether an act falls within the ambit of section 53 zn shall be made considering the totality of circumstances and the intent of the actor.

Any person claiming ownership of a layout-design, intending to avail protections as provided herein, shall submit an application for registration to the designated Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Registry. The application shall be accompanied by a detailed layout topography, demonstrating the three-dimensional configuration of the semiconductor integrated circuit. Such layout topography must adhere to the prescribed format and include all layers constituting the integrated circuit. A statement of ownership, clearly identifying the applicant and detailing the extent of rights claimed, is also mandatory. 

Furthermore, any information relating to commercial exploitation of the layout-design, including licensing agreements or assignments, shall be disclosed. The Registry may, subject to verification of the submitted materials and satisfaction of all requirements, grant a certificate of registration. The certificate shall contain particulars relating to section 53 zn, specifically the date of filing, the applicant’s name, and a unique registration number assigned to the layout-design. Failure to maintain accurate records of commercial exploitation may impact the validity of the registration.

Any person alleging infringement of a layout-design right, as established under this Act, shall be entitled to commence legal proceedings in the appropriate District Court, notwithstanding any other law for the time being in force. The plaintiff, in such proceedings, shall, subject to the provisions herein, be entitled to seek an injunction restraining the defendant from the acts constituting the infringement. Furthermore, the plaintiff may also claim damages for the loss suffered due to such infringement, assessed in accordance with the actual loss or reasonable royalty, whichever is higher. A defendant, however, may avail of defenses as provided herein, including proof of independent development or that the act complained of does not constitute infringement. Where a layout-design right is found to have been improperly asserted, the Court may award costs to the defendant. The determination of damages, and the grant of injunctions, shall be governed by principles of equity and fairness, and shall consider the extent of commercial prejudice suffered by the plaintiff due to the alleged acts falling within the scope of section 53 zn, relating to the limitation period for initiating such proceedings.

Any person alleging infringement of a layout-design right, as provided herein, may institute civil proceedings in the District Court having jurisdiction over the place where the alleged infringement occurred, subject to the provisions of this Act. The plaintiff shall, within thirty days of knowledge of the infringement, serve a notice of such intention upon the alleged infringer, detailing the specific layout-design right claimed and the nature of the infringement. Failure to serve such notice shall be a bar to the institution of civil proceedings, unless the Court, upon sufficient cause shown, permits such institution. 

The defendant may, within thirty days of receipt of the notice, file a counter-claim asserting invalidity of the layout-design right or seeking a declaration of non-infringement. Where a party seeks to rely upon section 53 zn, establishing prior art, such evidence shall be submitted to the Court along with the pleadings and shall be subject to verification. The Court may, at its discretion, grant interim injunctions to prevent further infringement pending the final determination of the suit. Costs shall follow the event, unless the Court deems otherwise.

Any person alleging infringement of a registered layout-design, prior to initiating proceedings before any court, shall furnish to the alleged infringer a notice of such infringement, specifying the particulars of the layout-design infringed and the nature of the infringement claimed, subject to the provisions contained herein. The notice shall be accompanied by a clear and concise statement of the relief sought, and shall offer the alleged infringer a period of thirty days from the date of receipt to remedy the infringement through cessation of manufacture, sale, or distribution of the infringing article. Provided that, if the alleged infringer demonstrates, to the satisfaction of the complainant, that the layout-design is not valid or that the complainant’s claim is frivolous, no further action shall be required. Compliance with this requirement constitutes section 53 zn, and failure to adhere to these stipulations may render any subsequent legal action inadmissible. Any settlement reached shall be documented and remain confidential unless disclosure is mandated by law.

Any person who, with intent to deceive, represents a layout-design which is not an original layout-design as provided herein, or who falsely states that a layout-design is his own, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than six months, but which may extend to three years, and with a fine not less than fifty thousand rupees, but which may extend to five lakh rupees. Where an offence under this Act involves commercial scale reproduction, distribution, or sale of integrated circuits embodying such falsely represented layout-design, the term of imprisonment may extend to five years and the fine may extend to ten lakh rupees. The Controller, upon receiving credible information of such an offence, may initiate an inquiry and, subject to the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, direct a police officer to investigate. Furthermore, any evidence obtained during such investigation shall be admissible in any proceedings under this Act, and the Controller’s findings shall be considered persuasive by any court of competent jurisdiction concerning section 53 zn.

Any person possessing a layout-design right, subject to the provisions of this Act, may grant licenses to any other person for the use of such layout-design, whether such license is sole, exclusive, or non-exclusive, and may determine the terms and conditions of such license, including royalty payments and duration. An assignment of a layout-design right shall be effective upon a written instrument signed by the assignor and the assignee, and such assignment shall be subject to registration with the appropriate authority as provided herein. Where a license or assignment is made jointly by multiple right holders, the instrument evidencing such transaction shall clearly delineate the respective shares and interests of each party. 

Furthermore, any agreement relating to section 53 zn, concerning the commercial exploitation of a layout-design, must be in writing and specify the scope of permitted use, including the geographical territory and field of application. Failure to comply with these requirements may render the agreement unenforceable, and the rights of the layout-design owner shall remain protected under this Act. Any dispute arising from such license or assignment shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the competent court.

Any person aggrieved by an order of the Controller refusing to register a layout-design, or by an order revoking the registration of a layout-design, or by any decision concerning the grant or refusal of a license, may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board. Such appeal shall be filed within ninety days from the date of the order appealed against, subject to the Appellate Board allowing an extension of time for sufficient cause. The Controller, upon receiving notice of an appeal filed under this Act, shall forthwith transmit to the Appellate Board all papers and documents relating to the case. The Appellate Board, while hearing an appeal concerning section 53 zn, relating to the determination of relative rights where layout-designs are substantially similar, may direct the parties to produce evidence of commercial exploitation and independent development, if deemed necessary for a just determination. Provided that the Appellate Board’s decision shall be final and binding, save for any recourse available by way of writ petition to the High Court.

Any person desiring registration of a layout-design shall submit an application to the Controller in the prescribed form, accompanied by the requisite fee, and satisfying such conditions as may be specified in the regulations. An india application shall demonstrate sufficient detail of the layout-design, including a top-level cell view and all layers comprising the complete layout, and shall be accompanied by a statement of originality. Where a layout-design is claimed to be a derivative work, the applicant shall furnish a clear and concise statement detailing the original layout-design from which it is derived, along with evidence of authorization. The Controller may, subject to such terms and conditions as deemed appropriate, require the applicant to submit additional information or samples to verify the accuracy and completeness of the application. Compliance with these requirements is essential for the successful processing of the application and determination of registrability under this Act, and failure to do so may result in rejection of the application as provided herein, specifically concerning section 53 zn.

Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Controller refusing to register a layout-design, or by any order made by the Controller relating to the rectification of the register of layout-designs, may, within ninety days from the date of such decision or order, prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board established under this Act. Such appeal shall be in the prescribed form and shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the decision or order appealed against, and a statement of the grounds on which the appeal is based. The Controller shall, where a request for a visual recording of the layout-design was made during the initial application, forward such recording as part of the appeal record to the Appellate Board. Provided that the Appellate Board may, subject to such conditions as it deems fit, extend the time for filing an appeal if it is satisfied that sufficient cause existed for the delay. A decision of the Appellate Board shall be final and binding, except where a substantial question of law arises, in which case an appeal may lie to the Supreme Court. The Appellate Board shall, when considering any appeal concerning section 53 zn, give due consideration to the commercial implications of the layout-design in question.

An applicant patent, for the purposes of this Act, signifies a complete application, duly filed in the prescribed manner, claiming an invention as defined herein and satisfying all requirements relating to provisional or complete specification, drawings, and statement of utility, where applicable. The applicant shall be deemed a ‘person’ as defined under the General Clauses Act, 1897, and may include a legal entity. Subject to the provisions contained herein, an applicant patent shall be examined by the Controller of Patents, who may require the applicant to amend the claims or specification to conform to the requirements of this Act. Provided that, failure to comply with a requirement for amendment within the stipulated timeframe may result in the abandonment of the applicant patent.

An applicant patent shall be deemed to have been duly filed when the application, conforming to the requirements as provided herein, is accompanied by a complete specification and necessary drawings, if any, and the prescribed fee has been paid to the Controller. Should the applicant claim priority from one or more prior applications made in a convention country, a certified copy of the priority document, duly translated if necessary, shall be furnished within the prescribed period. The Controller may, subject to such conditions as may be deemed fit, extend the period for furnishing the priority document. Any omission or irregularity in the application shall not render it invalid, provided that the applicant rectifies the same within a period specified by the Controller. An applicant may request amendment of the specification, but such amendment shall not extend beyond the scope of the original disclosure. Failure to comply with these provisions may result in the application being deemed abandoned.

Any person claiming to be the applicant patent for an invention, and desiring to obtain a patent, shall submit an application as provided herein, accompanied by a declaration of ownership and inventorship. Should a co-applicant dispute the declared inventorship, they may petition the Controller for a hearing to determine proportionate entitlement to the patent. The Controller, upon reasonable cause being shown, shall direct an inquiry into the matter and may, subject to the findings, adjust the applicant patent accordingly. 

Where an applicant fails to diligently pursue the application, and does not respond to official communications within the prescribed timeframe, any other person demonstrating substantial interest and a prior right to the invention may apply to be substituted as the applicant. Provided that, the original applicant shall have thirty days to remedy the deficiency before substitution is granted. Any aggrieved party may appeal decisions regarding applicant patent to the Appellate Board, subject to payment of the requisite fee.

An applicant patent shall be deemed to have been duly filed when the application, conforming to the requirements as provided herein, is accompanied by the prescribed fee and a declaration of inventorship. The Controller may, subject to such conditions as may be deemed necessary, permit the amendment of an applicant patent specification, provided that such amendment does not extend the scope of the invention beyond what is reasonably supported by the original disclosure. Where an applicant seeks priority based on a corresponding application filed in a convention country, evidence of such filing, duly certified, shall be submitted within the prescribed period. Failure to comply with these requirements may render the applicant patent vulnerable to revocation. Any person alleging to be a rightful inventor, and disputing the claim of the applicant, may file a representation with the Controller, detailing the grounds of such dispute and supporting evidence. The Controller shall, after due consideration, determine the rightful inventor and adjust the applicant patent accordingly.

An applicant patent shall be deemed provisional subject to the fulfillment of conditions as provided herein. Any person desiring to obtain a patent shall submit an application in the prescribed form to the Controller of Patents, accompanied by a provisional specification. The provisional specification must describe the invention sufficiently to enable a person skilled in the art to carry it into effect, but need not include all the details necessary for complete construction. Provided that, the applicant patent shall, within twelve months from the date of filing the provisional specification, file a complete specification; otherwise the provisional specification shall be treated as abandoned. Failure to comply with this requirement regarding the complete specification shall render the applicant patent ineligible for consideration under this Act. Any subsequent amendment to the complete specification, affecting the scope of the invention, may be subject to review by the Controller.

Any person claiming to be the applicant patent for an invention shall furnish to the Controller a declaration of proprietorship as provided herein, stating that they are the true and first inventor of the invention sought to be patented. Failure to submit such a declaration, or submission of a materially false declaration, shall be deemed an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. The Controller may, subject to such conditions as may be deemed fit, allow an applicant to amend the declaration within a period of one month from the date of its submission. Any amendment made fraudulently, with intent to deceive, shall attract the penalties outlined herein. A provisional specification filed without a corresponding complete specification within the prescribed period shall be considered abandoned, and the applicant patent shall have no further recourse under this Act.

Any applicant patent, subject to the provisions of this Act, may assign, or grant a license to work the patented invention, either wholly or partially, and for any term, to any person. Such assignment or license shall be in writing and shall be registered with the Controller of Patents as provided herein, failing which it shall be void. The Controller, upon registration of an assignment or license, shall record the particulars thereof in the register of patents. Where an applicant patent has made an assignment of the patent, the assignee shall be entitled to all the rights and remedies as if he were the original applicant. Provided that, the assignee shall give notice of the assignment to the Controller within the prescribed period. Any license granted under this Act shall be non-exclusive unless otherwise specified in the agreement and registered accordingly. The terms and conditions of any such license may be subject to review by the Controller to ensure compliance with the principles of public interest and reasonable royalty.

An applicant patent, if contested under this Act, shall be subject to a notice of opposition filed by any person alleging prior art or lack of inventive step, provided that such notice is served within four months from the date of publication of the application. The Controller, upon receipt of a valid opposition, shall communicate it to the applicant, who may file a counter-statement within three months. Failure to submit a counter-statement may result in the applicant patent being deemed withdrawn. Where the Controller, after examining the evidence presented by both parties, is satisfied that the applicant patent does not meet the requirements of novelty or involves an obvious variation of existing knowledge, it may reject the application. Any aggrieved party may appeal such rejection to the Appellate Board established for the purposes of this Act, subject to the payment of prescribed fees and adherence to the procedural timelines as provided herein. The Appellate Board’s decision shall be final and binding, unless a substantial question of law is involved, warranting review by a higher court.

Any person aggrieved by an order of the Controller refusing an applicant patent, or requiring the applicant to amend the claims, may file an appeal to the Appellate Board. Such appeal shall be filed within a period of sixty days from the date of the order of the Controller, subject to the Chairperson extending this period for a further period not exceeding thirty days if sufficient cause is shown. The Appellate Board, upon receiving an appeal, may direct the Controller to furnish within a specified period, a statement of the case and the documents relating thereto. If the Appellate Board considers that the invention claimed is not patentable under this Act, it may dismiss the appeal. Provided that, prior to dismissal, the Board shall provide the applicant an opportunity to be heard and present evidence supporting the patentability of the invention. Any decision of the Appellate Board shall be final and binding, save for rights of appeal to the Supreme Court as provided by law.

An applicant patent for an invention relating to a pharmaceutical formulation shall, upon satisfying the Controller of Patents with regard to novelty and non-obviousness as provided herein, be subject to a detailed examination concerning its therapeutic efficacy and potential side effects. The Controller may require submission of clinical trial data demonstrating safety and effectiveness. Where a subsequent applicant patent claims a modification of an existing formulation, it shall be deemed deceptively similar if the modification does not result in a significant and demonstrable improvement in therapeutic outcome or a reduction in adverse effects. Provided that, such determination of deceptive similarity shall consider the established pharmacological principles and expert testimony. Any application found to be deceptively similar to a previously granted patent shall be refused, and the applicant shall bear the costs associated with the examination of said application. The Controller shall maintain a register of all granted applicant patents accessible to the public.

Any applicant patent filed under this Act shall be subject to a diligent pursuit of patent rights, and failure to do so may render the patent vulnerable to revocation as provided herein. An applicant may, however, request a period of extension for responding to any examination report, subject to demonstrating justifiable cause and payment of the prescribed fee. Where an applicant patent originates from an international application designating India, the applicant shall, within the prescribed timeframe, furnish a translation of the international application and any supporting documents if not already in an official language. Should the applicant fail to comply with these requirements, the application shall be deemed withdrawn. Any aggrieved person may file a representation against the grant of a patent, alleging lack of diligent pursuit or non-compliance with the provisions relating to international applications, and the Controller shall, after due inquiry, pass an appropriate order. The Controller’s decision shall be subject to appeal.

An applicant patent, when filed as provided herein, shall be accompanied by a statement detailing the extent of foreign applications relating to the same invention. Such statement shall disclose the country or countries in which applications have been filed, the dates of those filings, and their current status. Where a patent means patent as defined under this Act, the applicant shall also furnish a declaration confirming that the information provided is true and correct to the best of their knowledge and belief. Failure to comply with this requirement may render the applicant patent liable to be refused, subject to a reasonable opportunity being given to remedy the deficiency. The Controller may, however, waive this requirement in exceptional circumstances, particularly where the applicant demonstrates justifiable cause for non-compliance. Any amendment to the statement shall be promptly communicated to the Controller and shall be subject to verification. The Controller shall maintain a register of such statements for public inspection.

Any person desiring to obtain a patent shall submit an application in the prescribed form to the Controller of Patents, accompanied by a provisional or complete specification and the necessary fee as provided herein. The specification shall fully and particularly describe the invention, and shall disclose the best method known to the applicant for carrying out the invention. A patent application relating to a process shall clearly define the process and the apparatus, if any, used therein. Where an invention involves a new and useful composition of matter, the application shall include the chemical structure and properties of said composition. 

Subject to the provisions of this Act, a patent may be granted for any invention which is new, involves an inventive step, and is capable of industrial application. The grant of a patent shall confer upon the patentee the exclusive right to make, use, sell, and import the invention in India for a period of twenty years from the date of filing the application.

Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Controller of Patents, refusing to grant a patent or revoking a patent, may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board established under this Act, subject to the provisions contained herein. Such appeal shall be filed within a period of ninety days from the date of the order appealed against, and shall be accompanied by the prescribed fee. The Appellate Board may, while considering such appeal, require the appellant to furnish further evidence or documents, and may, after hearing the parties concerned, confirm, modify, or reverse the decision of the Controller. Where a patent is revoked, the patentee shall be entitled to reasonable compensation for any loss suffered, determined by the Appellate Board, taking into account the unexpired term of the patent and the extent of commercial exploitation. A licensee of a patent, whose license is terminated unfairly, shall have recourse to a civil court for damages, provided that the terms of the license agreement do not preclude such action. The grant of a patent does not confer any right to manufacture, use, or sell the invention in cases where such acts would infringe another valid patent.

Any person desiring to obtain a patent shall submit an application in the prescribed form to the Controller of Patents, accompanied by a provisional or complete specification and the requisite fee as provided herein. The specification shall fully and particularly describe the invention and the manner in which it is to be performed, and shall disclose the best method of performing it known to the applicant. Where a complete specification is not filed with the application, a provisional specification may be filed, and a complete specification shall be filed within twelve months from the date of filing the provisional specification. 

A patent granted under this Act shall confer upon the patentee the exclusive right to make, use, exercise, sell or distribute the invention in India, subject to the provisions of this Act. However, such exclusive right shall not extend to inventions relating to atomic energy or processes specifically prohibited by law. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Controller may, within a period of one month from the date of the order, prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board.

Any person who infringes a patent granted under this Act shall be liable to pay damages to the patentee, assessed in accordance with the principles as laid down in this Act, and may also be subject to an injunction restraining further infringement. Where a defendant proves that the patent is invalid, the Court may order the patentee to pay costs incurred by the defendant in defending the action. Any act of anticipation, as demonstrated through prior public use or publication, shall constitute grounds for revocation of a patent, and the patentee shall forfeit all rights therein. A person abetting the infringement, or procuring the infringement, shall be deemed to be jointly and severally liable with the principal infringer. The High Court shall have exclusive jurisdiction to hear and determine all disputes relating to patents, subject to appeals to the Supreme Court as provided herein. Failure to comply with an injunction issued under this Act shall be punishable with imprisonment.

Any person alleging infringement of a patent, as provided herein, shall furnish to the High Court a detailed statement of the grounds upon which such allegation is based, including a point-by-point comparison of the patented invention with the allegedly infringing activity. The Court may, subject to such terms as it deems fit, direct the alleged infringer to produce for inspection all relevant documents and materials pertaining to the disputed activity. An appeal from any order refusing inspection shall lie to a Division Bench of the same High Court. Where a patentee seeks an injunction restraining the manufacture, use, sale or import of an invention, the Court shall consider the potential public benefit accruing from the continued availability of the allegedly infringing product, particularly in cases relating to pharmaceutical patents. A counter-claim asserting invalidity of the patent may be filed by the defendant, and shall be adjudicated upon prior to any determination of infringement, unless the Court determines that such adjudication would unduly delay proceedings. Any decision regarding the scope of the patent shall be based on a purposive construction of the claims, giving due weight to the specification.

Any person applying for a patent shall submit with their application a certified statement regarding the origin of any biological material utilized in the invention, demonstrating lawful acquisition and adherence to applicable access and benefit-sharing regulations. Failure to provide such certification may render the patent application subject to rejection, as provided herein. A patent for an invention incorporating a registered certification trade mark shall not be granted unless the applicant demonstrates current and valid registration of said trade mark with the relevant authority, and proves that the mark is legitimately used in connection with the goods or services to which the patent pertains. The Controller of Patents may, subject to established procedures, require evidence of such registration and usage. Any patent granted under this Act is conditional upon continued compliance with these provisions regarding biological origin and trade mark validity. Non-compliance may result in revocation of the patent.

A Technical Member of the Trade Marks Registry shall be a person possessing a degree in engineering or technology, or holding a diploma in engineering or technology from a recognised institution, and having not less than ten years of experience in the field of trade marks or related intellectual property matters. The Controller of Trade Marks may, subject to the approval of the Central Government, appoint such number of Technical Members as may be necessary to efficiently discharge the functions under this Act. A Technical Member shall assist the Controller in matters requiring technical expertise, including the examination of applications for registration and the adjudication of disputes relating to the technical aspects of trade marks. Provided that, no person shall be appointed as a Technical Member who is not a citizen of India. The term of office for a Technical Member shall be five years from the date of appointment, or until attaining the age of sixty-two years, whichever is earlier.

A person proposed for appointment as a Technical Member of the Trade Marks Registry shall possess a postgraduate degree in science or engineering from a recognized university, or be a person holding a degree in law with a postgraduate diploma in intellectual property rights from a recognized institution. The Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks may, if satisfied that a candidate does not possess the aforementioned qualifications but has demonstrable experience in the field of trade marks, including practical knowledge of examination and registration procedures, consider such a person for appointment, provided that such experience shall not be less than ten years. Any appointment of a Technical Member shall be subject to a rigorous screening process conducted by a committee constituted by the Central Government, ensuring adherence to principles of transparency and merit. The Controller shall maintain a panel of eligible candidates for future vacancies, updated annually. A Technical Member shall exercise jurisdiction as provided herein, and their decisions are subject to review by the Appellate Board.

A Technical Member of the Trade Marks Registry, possessing the requisite qualifications as prescribed, shall conduct a hearing where an application for registration is opposed under this Act, and shall submit a reasoned opinion to the Registrar of Trade Marks regarding the merits of the opposition. The Registrar, considering the opinion of the Technical Member and any further evidence presented, may either dismiss the opposition, direct the registration of the trade mark, or require modifications to the application subject to the consent of the applicant. Any party aggrieved by the decision of the Registrar may, within a period of ninety days, file an appeal with the High Court. Provided that, a Technical Member may, with the approval of the Registrar, also be assigned to examine applications for registration, and to determine whether a mark meets the criteria for distinctiveness as provided herein, ensuring adherence to established precedents and international conventions. The decision of a Technical Member on matters of distinctiveness shall be binding unless successfully appealed.

A person proposed for appointment as a Technical Member of the Trade Marks Registry shall possess a postgraduate degree in science or engineering from a recognized university, or be a person holding a degree in law with a postgraduate diploma in intellectual property rights from a recognized institution. The Central Government may, if it deems fit, relax this requirement in exceptional circumstances, subject to the condition that such a person possesses not less than ten years of experience in a relevant technical field or in the practice of intellectual property law. All appointments to the cadre of Technical Members shall be made through a transparent and competitive selection process conducted by a duly constituted Search-cum-Selection Committee. Any person appointed as a Technical Member shall be entitled to such salary, allowances, and other benefits as may be prescribed. A Technical Member shall exercise jurisdiction over matters requiring specialized technical knowledge, as determined by the Registrar of Trade Marks, and shall participate in hearings and adjudications as provided herein. The decision of the Technical Member shall be subject to review by the Controller of Trade Marks.

A person appointed as a Technical Member of the Trade Marks Registry shall possess a postgraduate degree in science or engineering from a recognized university, or be a person holding a degree in law with a postgraduate diploma in intellectual property rights. Such a Technical Member shall exercise jurisdiction over applications involving scientific or technical aspects of trade marks, including but not limited to chemical, pharmaceutical, and engineering goods. The Controller of Trade Marks may, subject to the provisions of this Act, assign specific cases to a Technical Member for examination and decision. Provided that, any decision rendered by a Technical Member shall be subject to review by the Controller, and an appeal may be preferred to the Appellate Board as provided herein. A Technical Member shall maintain strict confidentiality regarding all information accessed during the course of their duties and shall be bound by the code of conduct prescribed by the Central Government. Failure to comply with these provisions may result in disciplinary action.

Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Registrar relating to the qualifications or removal of a Technical Member shall have the right to prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board, subject to the provisions of this Act. The Appellate Board may, if satisfied that reasonable cause exists, direct the Registrar to reinstate a removed Technical Member or to reconsider the initial determination regarding qualifications. Failure to comply with an order of the Appellate Board regarding reinstatement or reconsideration shall attract a penalty not exceeding five lakh rupees. Any Technical Member found to have wilfully misrepresented qualifications or engaged in corrupt practices shall be liable for immediate removal and a fine of not less than two lakh rupees. All fines collected under this provision shall be credited to the Consolidated Fund of India and may be utilized for the training of additional Technical Members, as provided herein. A Technical Member shall possess a degree in engineering or technology.

A Technical Member appointed under this Act shall hold office for a period of five years from the date of assumption of charge or until attaining the age of sixty-two years, whichever is earlier, and may be considered for reappointment subject to such terms and conditions as the Central Government may deem fit. Any assignment or transfer of rights in a registered trade mark, including a license, shall be subject to the prior approval of the Registrar, and such approval may be granted upon satisfactory evidence of a bona fide transaction and the preservation of the essential character of the mark. Where a Technical Member is absent or incapable of performing the duties of their office, the Central Government may appoint a qualified officer to act as Technical Member. All fees and charges associated with the assignment or licensing of trade marks shall be payable to the Trade Marks Registry and shall be utilized for the purposes as provided herein. Any dispute regarding the validity of an assignment or license may be referred to the Registrar for adjudication.

Any decision of the Registrar regarding the qualifications of a Technical Member shall be subject to appeal to the Appellate Board, provided that such appeal shall be filed within ninety days from the date of the order appealed against. The Appellate Board may, after giving the aggrieved party an opportunity of being heard, confirm, modify or reverse the decision of the Registrar. A person aggrieved by any decision of the Appellate Board relating to a Technical Member may, within sixty days of such decision, apply to the High Court for review on grounds of legal error apparent on the face of the record. The qualifications of a Technical Member shall include a degree in engineering or technology, with not less than ten years of experience in the relevant field, and demonstrated knowledge of trade mark law as provided herein. Any dispute regarding the interpretation of ‘relevant field’ shall be adjudicated by the Appellate Board, whose decision shall be final and binding.

A Technical Member of the Trade Marks Registry shall be a person possessing a degree in engineering or technology, or holding a diploma in engineering or technology from a recognised institution, and having not less than ten years of experience in the field of trade marks or related intellectual property matters. The Registrar shall, in consultation with the Central Government, determine the specific qualifications and experience required for a Technical Member, and may establish a panel of eligible candidates for appointment. Subject to the provisions of this Act, a Technical Member shall exercise such powers and perform such duties as are conferred or imposed upon him by or under this Act, and shall be responsible for the technical examination of trade mark applications and related proceedings. Provided that, the decision of a Technical Member shall be subject to review by the Registrar where deemed necessary.

A person proposed for appointment as a Technical Member of the Trade Marks Registry shall possess a postgraduate degree in science or engineering from a recognized university, or be a person holding a degree in law with a post-graduate diploma in Intellectual Property Rights. The Central Government may, if deemed necessary, constitute a committee to assess the suitability of a candidate based on experience in the relevant technical field and familiarity with trade mark practices. Any decision regarding the appointment of a Technical Member shall be subject to a review process, and objections raised during such review, particularly those mirroring the principles established in the authority registrar case pertaining to procedural fairness, shall be duly considered. The Registrar of Trade Marks, in consultation with the committee, may recommend a panel of eligible candidates to the Central Government for final selection, provided that the qualifications and experience of each candidate are fully documented and verifiable as provided herein.

Any person claiming to be the proprietor of a trade mark used in India may apply for registration of such trade mark under this Act, subject to the provisions herein. The application shall be in the prescribed form and shall include a representation of the trade mark and a statement of the goods or services for which registration is sought. Upon receipt of the application, the Trade Marks Registry shall examine it to ascertain whether it meets the requirements of this Act and the rules made thereunder. If the application is found to be in order, the trade mark shall be advertised in the Trade Marks Journal. Any person may, within the prescribed period, file a notice of opposition to the registration of the trade mark. Following resolution of any opposition, and satisfaction of all requirements, the trade mark shall be registered and a certificate of registration issued, conferring upon the proprietor the exclusive right to use the registered trade marks in relation to the goods or services specified in the certificate. A registered trade mark shall remain valid for ten years from the date of registration, renewable for further periods of ten years.

Any person claiming to be the owner of a registered trade mark and alleging an infringement thereof may, subject to the provisions of this Act, institute a suit for recovery of damages or an injunction, or both, in a District Court having jurisdiction over the place where the infringement occurs. The proprietor of a registered trade mark shall, notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, have the right to institute civil proceedings for infringement of such trade mark. Where a plaintiff, being the proprietor of a registered trade mark, succeeds in an infringement suit, the Court may grant an account of profits and also award damages not exceeding rupees two lakh for each such infringement. 

Provided that, in cases where the infringement is shown to be a result of a deliberate and willful act on the part of the defendant, the Court may also award enhanced damages, not exceeding rupees five lakh per infringement.
