Any order made under this Act relating to registered trade marks shall be enforceable by the same Court as if it were a decree in a suit in that Court.

Any assignment of a registered trade mark shall be subject to the provisions of this Act and shall be effected by an instrument in writing signed by the assignor and assignee, or their duly authorized agents. The instrument shall clearly identify the registered trade marks assigned, including the registration number and class, and shall specify any limitations or conditions attached to the assignment, such as territorial restrictions or field of use. Where the assignment encompasses goodwill, it shall be deemed to include the right to sue for any infringement of the registered trade marks assigned, subject to the terms of the assignment agreement. 

A licensee of a registered trade mark may, with the consent of the proprietor, assign their license rights to a third party, provided that such assignment does not contravene any terms stipulated in the original license agreement. The Trade Marks Registry shall maintain a record of all registered assignments and licenses, accessible for public inspection as provided herein. Failure to register an assignment or license shall not invalidate it, but may affect its enforceability against third parties.

Any person claiming to be the owner of a registered trade mark and alleging an infringement thereof may, subject to the provisions of this Act, institute a suit for rectification, revocation, or for an injunction, in the District Court having jurisdiction over the place where the infringement occurs. The defendant in any such suit may, by counter-claim, seek rectification or revocation of the plaintiff’s registered trade mark, or may allege that the use of the trade mark by the plaintiff is likely to deceive or cause confusion. An appeal from any decree or order of a District Court in a suit concerning registered trade marks shall lie to the High Court, provided that a further appeal to the Supreme Court may be made only if a substantial question of law is involved. Where a trade mark is registered in multiple classes, a finding of non-use in respect of one class shall not necessarily invalidate the registration in other classes, unless specifically proven as provided herein.

Any person intending to oppose the registration of a trade mark shall file a notice of opposition in the prescribed form with the Trade Marks Registry within the stipulated period from the date of advertisement of the application for registration. Such notice shall clearly state the grounds on which the opposition is based, referencing the relevant provisions of this Act and any prior rights claimed. The applicant for registration of the trade mark shall be served with a copy of the notice of opposition, and shall be entitled to file a counter-statement, addressing the grounds raised by the notice opposition applicant. Failure to file a counter-statement within the prescribed time may result in the trade mark being refused registration. The Registrar, having considered the notice of opposition and counter-statement, if any, shall hear both parties and determine whether the contested registered trade marks should proceed to registration or be refused.

An unregistered trade mark shall be protectable under this Act, notwithstanding the absence of formal registration, provided that the mark has been consistently used in relation to specific goods or services and has acquired distinctiveness in the relevant local market. Such distinctiveness shall be evidenced by demonstrable use, public recognition, and association of the mark with the proprietor. A proprietor of an unregistered trade mark may seek remedies for passing off, subject to establishing goodwill and the likelihood of deception or confusion amongst consumers. However, the scope of protection afforded to an unregistered trade mark shall be limited to the geographical area where such use and recognition have been established, and shall not extend to goods or services unrelated to those for which the mark has gained reputation.

A person regularly using a mark as a trade mark, even if not registered under this Act, shall be entitled to certain protections, subject to the provisions herein. Such an unregistered trade mark shall be protectable against any subsequent adoption or use of an identical or deceptively similar mark by another person, provided that the prior user can demonstrate continuous and bona fide use of the mark in relation to specific goods or services. The scope of protection afforded to an unregistered trade mark shall be limited to the geographical area in which the mark has been actively used and to the specific goods or services for which it has acquired local reputation. Any aggrieved person claiming rights in an unregistered trade mark may apply to the appropriate court for an injunction restraining the subsequent user, and may also seek damages for any loss suffered as a direct result of the infringement, subject to establishing goodwill.

Any person who adopts an unregistered trade mark in relation to goods or services and establishes a substantial reputation therein, shall be entitled to certain protections as provided herein. Such a person may seek an injunction from a competent court restraining any other person from using a deceptively similar mark, provided that the plaintiff demonstrates a likelihood of confusion amongst consumers. The court, in considering such applications, shall have regard to the extent of the plaintiff’s reputation, the degree of similarity between the marks, and the nature of the goods or services involved. A proprietor of a registered trade mark, however, shall have priority over a user of an unregistered trade mark, subject to a finding of non-use by the registered proprietor. Remedies under this Act extend to damages for loss suffered and an account of profits made by the infringing party, assessed according to the principles of equity. Any claim relating to an unregistered trade mark shall be subject to the limitations period prescribed for actions concerning passing off.

A person who has continuously and uninterruptedly used an unregistered trade mark in relation to particular goods or services for a period of not less than five years, and who intends to continue such use, may apply to the Registrar for registration of the trade mark as if it were a registered trade mark under this Act. Such application shall be accompanied by a statement detailing the date of first use of the mark, the duration of use, and a representation of how the mark is used in commerce. The Registrar may, subject to such conditions as may be deemed fit, require the applicant to furnish evidence of such use, including but not limited to invoices, advertisements, and other relevant documentation. Where a dispute arises regarding the ownership or use of an unregistered trade mark, the aggrieved party may initiate proceedings for passing off, seeking injunctive relief and damages. The Registrar shall not register an unregistered trade mark if it is likely to deceive the public or cause confusion with an existing registered trade mark, or is descriptive of the goods or services concerned.

Any person who adopts an unregistered trade mark in relation to goods or services and demonstrates continuous and substantial use of such mark for a period not less than five years, shall be entitled to certain protections as provided herein. Such entitlement, however, is subject to the condition that the use of the unregistered trade mark does not conflict with any existing registered trade mark, nor shall it be deceptive or likely to cause confusion amongst consumers. A claimant seeking protection for an unregistered trade mark shall furnish evidence of actual use, including details of sales, advertising, and geographical reach of the mark’s application. Where a dispute arises concerning an unregistered trade mark, the onus of proving prior continuous use shall lie upon the claimant. Remedies available to the user of an unregistered trade mark shall be limited to injunctions preventing further infringement, and shall not include claims for damages unless fraudulent intent is established.

Any person who uses in the course of trade, a mark which is identical with or deceptively similar to a mark used by another, and which is an unregistered trade mark, shall be subject to a penalty not exceeding five lakh rupees. Provided that, the court may, subject to the circumstances of the case, impose a lower penalty, but not less than fifty thousand rupees. Where a continuing offence involving the use of an unregistered trade mark is established, the court may order an injunction restraining the offender from further use of the mark, and may also order the destruction or obliteration of all materials bearing such mark. Any goods found to be infringing, and in the possession of the offender, shall be deemed forfeited to the Government, and may be disposed of in a manner as prescribed. An appeal against any order made under this Act shall lie to the High Court.

Any person claiming rights in an unregistered trade mark used in India may, subject to the provisions of this Act, apply to the Registrar for the assignment or licensing of such rights to a designated entity. The application shall detail the scope of the mark, the class of goods or services to which it pertains, and the proposed terms of assignment or license, including royalty rates and duration. Where the unregistered trade mark has acquired goodwill, such goodwill shall be considered an asset capable of assignment, and the instrument of assignment shall be in writing and registered with the Trade Marks Registry. A license granted under this Act shall be non-exclusive unless expressly stated to be exclusive, and may be subject to conditions regarding quality control and territory. Failure to comply with the terms of a registered assignment or license may, as provided herein, constitute grounds for revocation of the instrument. The Registrar may, at their discretion, require evidence of genuine use of the unregistered trade mark prior to approving any assignment or license.

Any person claiming rights in an unregistered trade mark, and alleging that another person is using a deceptively similar mark, may apply to the High Court for an injunction restraining such use, subject to proof of prior use and goodwill attached thereto. However, such injunction shall not be granted unless the applicant demonstrates a continuous and uninterrupted use of the unregistered trade mark for a period of not less than five years immediately preceding the date of the application. Any order granting such injunction may also direct an account of profits derived by the defendant from the unlawful use of the mark, provided that the plaintiff establishes a clear nexus between the defendant’s use and the profits claimed. An appeal from any order of the High Court in this regard shall lie to the Supreme Court, subject to the provisions of this Act and any other relevant law. The Court may, at its discretion, require the applicant to furnish security for costs.

Any person making use of an unregistered trade mark in the course of trade shall be subject to such conditions as may be prescribed. A Contracting Party, desiring to avail remedies under this Act in respect of an unregistered trade mark, shall demonstrate continuous and demonstrable use of said mark for a period not less than two years immediately preceding the date of any complaint or assertion of right. Provided that, such use shall be bona fide and not merely for the purpose of reserving rights or circumventing the provisions of this Act. Where a complaint is lodged alleging infringement of an unregistered trade mark, the burden of proving continuous use and bona fide intention shall lie upon the complainant. Failure to satisfy these conditions shall render the complaint inadmissible and may attract penalties as provided herein. No injunction shall be granted unless the court is satisfied that irreparable harm would otherwise result.

The Chairperson shall be a person of eminence from the field of semiconductor technology, or law, or possessing a combination of both, and appointed by the Central Government. The Chairperson shall exercise such powers as are necessary to ensure the effective administration of this Act, including the constitution of Benches for the hearing of applications and appeals. A Vice-Chairperson may be appointed to assist the Chairperson and shall, in the absence of the Chairperson, perform their functions. The term of office for the Chairperson, and any Vice-Chairperson appointed, shall not exceed five years, subject to the possibility of reappointment. All orders passed by the Chairperson shall be final and binding, except as provided herein for appeal to a higher court.

The Semiconductor Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Authority shall maintain a Register of Registered Layout-Designs in which all particulars of registered layout-designs shall be recorded. Any person desiring to register a layout-design shall submit an application to the Authority in the prescribed form, accompanied by the requisite fee and a detailed layout of the circuit. The application shall be subject to verification by the Authority to ensure compliance with the provisions of this Act. The Chairperson of the Authority may, if satisfied that the application meets all requirements, direct the registration of the layout-design and cause the particulars to be entered in the Register. Provided that, if the Chairperson requires further information or clarification, the applicant shall be given an opportunity to submit the same within a period of thirty days. The register shall be open for inspection by any person on payment of the prescribed fee, subject to such conditions as the Chairperson may deem fit. Any amendment to the registered layout-design shall be recorded in the Register upon application and verification as provided herein.

The Chairperson shall exercise ultimate authority in the determination of disputes relating to the infringement of layout-designs and shall ensure expeditious resolution of proceedings, subject to the provisions contained herein. Any party aggrieved by a decision of a Technical Officer may, within a period of sixty days from the date of such decision, appeal to the Chairperson, providing reasonable grounds for such appeal and submitting all relevant evidence. The Chairperson may, if satisfied that a prima facie case exists, direct a re-examination of the matter or constitute a Special Committee for further investigation. Should the Chairperson find evidence of wilful misrepresentation or fraudulent activity by any party, they may impose enhanced damages, not exceeding three times the actual damages proven. Furthermore, the Chairperson possesses the power to issue interim injunctions to prevent ongoing infringement, provided that sufficient security, as determined by the Chairperson, is furnished by the applicant. All decisions of the Chairperson shall be final and binding, save for recourse to the High Court on grounds of legal error.

The Chairperson shall be a person of eminence in the field of semiconductor technology or law, appointed by the Central Government, and shall hold office for a term of five years or until attaining the age of sixty-five years, whichever is earlier. The Central Government may, if it deems fit, grant an extension of tenure to the Chairperson for a further period not exceeding two years. All administrative matters concerning the functioning of the Layout-Design Registry shall be overseen by the Chairperson, who shall exercise such powers as are necessary to ensure the efficient discharge of its duties. 

Any vacancy arising in the office of the Chairperson shall be filled by the Central Government in like manner as the first appointment, and any person appointed to fill a vacancy shall hold office only for the remaining portion of the term of their predecessor. The remuneration and other terms and conditions of service of the Chairperson shall be as prescribed by the Central Government, subject to public funds being duly appropriated. The Chairperson may, with the prior approval of the Central Government, constitute a Standing Committee to assist in the technical examination of applications.

The Chairperson shall be a person of eminence from the field of semiconductor technology or intellectual property law, appointed by the Central Government, and shall hold office for a term of five years or until attaining the age of sixty-five years, whichever is earlier. Any vacancy arising in the office of the Chairperson shall be filled by a similar process, and the appointed person shall be eligible for the remainder of the term. The Chairperson may delegate administrative powers to an officer of the organization, subject to oversight and final responsibility remaining with the Chairperson. All decisions of the Chairperson regarding the acceptance of applications, grant of registrations, and imposition of penalties shall be reasoned and recorded in writing. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Chairperson may, as provided herein, seek a review before a designated committee, provided that such request is submitted within sixty days of the decision’s communication. The Chairperson shall ensure compliance with all procedural requirements under this Act.

The Chairperson appointed under this Act shall exercise ultimate authority in determining matters relating to the registration and enforcement of layout-designs, and any decision of the Chairperson shall be binding except as provided herein. Any person aggrieved by an order of the Chairperson may, subject to payment of a prescribed fee, file an appeal to the High Court. Failure to comply with an order issued by the Chairperson, or obstructing the Chairperson in the lawful performance of their duties, shall constitute an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with a fine, or with both. Provided that, the Chairperson may, in cases of minor procedural irregularities, issue directives for rectification rather than initiate punitive action. All records and documents pertaining to proceedings before the Chairperson shall be maintained confidentially and access thereto shall be restricted to authorized personnel only. Any unauthorized disclosure shall attract penalties as prescribed.

The registered proprietor of a layout-design may, subject to the provisions of this Act, assign the right, title and interest therein, either wholly or partially, and either generally or subject to specific limitations, by an instrument in writing. Any assignment of a layout-design shall be subject to such terms and conditions as may be agreed upon between the assignor and the assignee, and such instrument shall clearly define the scope of the assignment, including territorial limitations, if any. The Chairperson may, upon application by either party, adjudicate disputes arising from the interpretation of assignment agreements, ensuring equitable consideration of the rights of both parties. Where an assignment is made as security for a loan or other financial obligation, the assignee’s rights shall be limited to recovery of the outstanding amount, and the layout-design shall revert to the original proprietor upon full settlement. The Chairperson shall maintain a register of all assignments recorded under this Act, accessible to the public subject to payment of the prescribed fee. Any transfer of rights without proper recording shall be deemed invalid.

Any aggrieved person may prefer an appeal to the Chairperson against any decision or order passed by a Licensing Authority or an Inspector, provided that such appeal shall be filed within a period of forty-five days from the date of the impugned decision or order. The Chairperson, upon receipt of such appeal, shall, if satisfied that sufficient cause exists, admit the appeal and shall notify the respondent, requiring them to submit their response within thirty days. Should the Chairperson deem the appeal frivolous or vexatious, they may dismiss it with a reasoned order and a cost not exceeding five thousand rupees, payable to the Appellant. Any party dissatisfied with the decision of the Chairperson may apply to the High Court for review, subject to the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. The Chairperson shall maintain a register of all appeals received and their respective statuses, open for inspection during office hours.

The Chairperson shall exercise ultimate authority in matters pertaining to the registration and rectification of semiconductor layout-designs as provided herein, and shall ensure adherence to principles of natural justice in all proceedings. Any decision of the Chairperson regarding the acceptance or rejection of an application for registration may be subject to review by a designated officer, provided that such review shall not exceed thirty days from the date of the Chairperson’s initial order. In cases involving disputes concerning the similarity of a proposed layout-design to an existing registered layout-design, or where allegations of trade mark similarity are raised in relation to the commercial exploitation of a layout-design, the Chairperson may appoint a technical expert to provide an independent assessment. The remuneration of such an expert shall be borne by the applicant, or apportioned between the parties as the Chairperson deems just. The Chairperson shall maintain a register of all registered layout-designs and shall make such register accessible to the public subject to reasonable restrictions. Any appeal against a decision of the Chairperson shall be made to the High Court having territorial jurisdiction.

The Chairperson shall be a person of eminence in the field of semiconductor integrated circuits, or a person possessing expertise in law, engineering, or management, and appointed by the Central Government. The Chairperson shall exercise such powers as are necessary to ensure the effective administration of this Act, including the constitution of Benches and the regulation of proceedings. Any person appointed as Chairperson shall be eligible for a monthly remuneration, the amount of which shall be determined by the Central Government. An applicant seeking registration of a layout-design shall remit the prescribed registry fee, the schedule of which shall be determined by notification in the Official Gazette, and such fee shall be a condition precedent to the processing of the application by the Registry. The Chairperson may, subject to the provisions of this Act, delegate any of their powers to an officer of the Registry.

The registered proprietor of a layout-design shall, subject to the provisions of this Act, have the exclusive right to reproduce, exploit, and import the layout-design. This exclusive right extends to any act which would constitute an infringement of such rights, including the commercial exploitation of the layout-design in any manner. A person deriving title from, or legally assigned from, the registered proprietor shall be deemed to possess the same rights as the original proprietor, provided that such derivation or assignment is duly recorded with the Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Registry. However, the rights of the registered proprietor are subject to limitations as prescribed herein, particularly concerning layouts-design created for specific purposes or under contracts containing stipulations regarding usage. Any unauthorized act impacting the registered proprietor layout shall be actionable under this Act.

The registered proprietor of any layout-design shall have the exclusive right to reproduce, exploit, and commercially benefit from such layout-design, subject to the provisions contained herein. Any person desiring to commercially exploit a registered layout-design, other than the registered proprietor, may apply to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board for a compulsory license, provided that reasonable notice is given to the registered proprietor and adequate remuneration is offered. The application for a compulsory license shall detail the scope of exploitation sought and demonstrate that the applicant has made sufficient efforts to obtain a voluntary license from the registered proprietor. Where a registered proprietor layout-design is not commercially worked within a period of three years from the date of registration, a rebuttable presumption of abandonment arises, and any interested party may petition for revocation of the registration, subject to due process as prescribed. The rights of the registered proprietor shall subsist for a period of ten years from the date of filing, or until the layout-design ceases to be commercially viable, whichever is earlier.

The registered proprietor of any layout-design shall have the exclusive right to reproduce, exploit, and import the layout-design, subject to the provisions contained herein. Any act infringing upon the rights of the registered proprietor layout shall be actionable, and the aggrieved party may institute a suit in the appropriate District Court for the recovery of damages. Where a person, despite knowledge of the registration, continues to exploit the layout-design without authorization, an order of permanent injunction may be granted against such person. The court, while determining damages, shall have regard to the actual losses suffered by the registered proprietor, as well as the profits unjustly earned by the infringer. A registered proprietor may, as provided herein, also seek an account of profits and delivery up of infringing articles. However, such remedies shall not be available if the alleged infringement occurred prior to the registration of the layout-design, or where the act constitutes a fair use as defined under this Act.

The registered proprietor of a layout-design shall have the exclusive right to exploit the layout-design in India, and to receive any profits accruing from such exploitation, subject to the provisions contained herein. Any person desiring to commercially exploit a registered layout-design must obtain a license from the registered proprietor, and such license may be granted on mutually agreed terms and conditions, including royalty payments and duration of use. Where a registered proprietor fails to respond to a request for a license within a period of six months from the date of such request, any interested party may apply to the appropriate authority for compulsory licensing. 

A registered proprietor layout shall be deemed to be commercially exploited where it is used for the manufacture of any semiconductor integrated circuit, or where any semiconductor integrated circuit embodying the layout-design is imported into India. The rights conferred by registration under this Act are personal to the registered proprietor and are not transferable except by way of assignment or testamentary succession, and any such assignment shall be subject to registration with the appropriate authority.

The registered proprietor of a layout-design shall have the exclusive right to reproduce, exploit, and import the layout-design in India. However, such exclusive right shall be subject to the conditions that commercial exploitation commences within two years from the date of registration, or the right shall lapse as provided herein. A registered proprietor may assign, transfer, or license the rights relating to a registered layout-design, and any such assignment or transfer shall be in writing and duly recorded with the appropriate authority. Where a layout-design is exploited by a person other than the registered proprietor without authorization, a civil action may be instituted for infringement. Provided that, a registered user of a layout-design, having obtained the necessary license, may continue to exploit the layout-design even after the expiry of the registration period, subject to the terms of the license agreement. Any dispute regarding the validity of the registered proprietor layout shall be adjudicated in accordance with the established procedures.

Any person dealing in goods incorporating an infringing layout-design shall be liable to pay actual damages or statutory damages, whichever is greater, as determined by the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. The registered proprietor layout, if commercially exploited without authorization, shall constitute infringement actionable under this Act, and the proprietor may seek an injunction restraining such exploitation. Provided that, the registered proprietor shall not be entitled to damages for acts committed prior to the date of registration of the layout-design, unless such acts were committed with knowledge of the pending application for registration. Any person abetting the infringement, or dealing with goods known to be infringing, shall be deemed a party to the infringement and subject to the same liabilities. Failure to comply with an injunction issued under this Act shall be punishable with imprisonment not exceeding three years, or a fine, or both.

The registered proprietor of any layout-design shall have the exclusive right to exploit the layout-design in any manner, including reproduction, modification, or commercial exploitation, subject to the provisions contained herein. Any assignment of the registered proprietor’s rights in a layout-design shall be in writing and registered with the Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Registry to be effective against third parties. A license, whether sole or non-exclusive, granted by the registered proprietor shall similarly be documented in writing and registered as provided herein, detailing the scope of permitted exploitation and any applicable royalty or consideration. Where a layout-design is jointly held by multiple registered proprietors, each shall have an equal right to grant licenses, unless otherwise agreed in a written agreement amongst them. Failure to register an assignment or license does not invalidate the transfer of rights between the parties, but may affect its enforceability against subsequent purchasers or licensees acting in good faith. The registered proprietor layout remains subject to the limitations on rights as stipulated elsewhere in this Act.

The registered proprietor of a layout-design, aggrieved by any alleged infringement occurring after the registration date, may institute a civil suit in the District Court having jurisdiction over the place where the infringing activity is alleged to have taken place, subject to demonstrating substantial similarity between the registered layout-design and the alleged infringing article. However, a defendant in such a suit may, as a matter of defence, demonstrate that the alleged infringement constitutes a fair use as provided herein, specifically relating to research or educational purposes, and shall provide full details of such use to the Court. Any appeal from the decree of the District Court shall lie to the High Court, provided that such appeal is filed within ninety days from the date of the decree. The High Court, upon review, may confirm, modify, or reverse the decision of the District Court concerning the rights of the registered proprietor layout and the validity of the asserted infringement.

The Registrar may, as provided herein, require any person claiming to be the applicant or proprietor of a layout-design to furnish a declaration verifying the particulars entered in the application and stating that to the best of their knowledge, the layout-design does not violate any existing layout-design right. Subject to the provisions contained herein, the Registrar shall, upon receipt of an application for registration, examine it and may require such amendments as are necessary to ensure compliance with the requirements of this Act. The manner issuing notice of any deficiency in the application or of any objection raised during examination shall be by registered post with acknowledgement due, or by such other electronic means as the Central Government may, by notification in the Gazette, specify. Provided that, any notice issued electronically shall also be sent by ordinary post as a precautionary measure. The applicant shall have a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of such notice to respond.

The applicant seeking registration of a layout-design shall, upon determination of the requisite particulars, submit a request for registration to the Registrar in the prescribed form and accompanied by the appropriate fee as provided herein. Should the Registrar deem the request incomplete or deficient in any manner, a notice shall be issued to the applicant specifying the deficiencies and requiring rectification within a period not exceeding thirty days from the date of such notice. Failure to comply with the requirements of said notice may result in the rejection of the application. The Registrar may, subject to the provisions contained herein, extend the said period for rectification if sufficient cause is demonstrated by the applicant. Any person aggrieved by a decision regarding the issuance or non-issuance of such notice may, within sixty days, file a petition for review before the designated authority. The manner issuing notice shall be by registered post with acknowledgement due, or by electronic means where the applicant has so opted and provided a valid electronic address.

Any person alleging infringement of a layout-design right, prior to initiating proceedings before a competent court, shall issue a written notice to the alleged infringer, clearly identifying the layout-design right claimed, and specifying the nature of the infringement. The manner issuing notice shall require detailing the specific elements of the registered layout-design that are being infringed, accompanied by reasonably sufficient evidence to support the claim. Provided that, if the alleged infringer is reasonably identifiable only through publicly available information, service of notice by registered post shall be deemed sufficient compliance. 

A defendant, upon receipt of such notice, may, subject to the provisions contained herein, request further particulars relating to the alleged infringement within thirty days from the date of the notice. Failure to provide such particulars may, at the discretion of the court, be considered in determining the merits of the case. The registrar may, by notification in the Official Gazette, prescribe the form and content of the notice to ensure clarity and prevent frivolous claims.

The registered proprietor, upon reasonable belief of infringement of a layout-design right, may issue a written notice to the alleged infringer, detailing the nature of the infringement and demanding cessation of the unlawful activity. Such notice shall specifically identify the registered layout-design, the manner in which it is being infringed, and the relief sought by the proprietor, including but not limited to, an injunction restraining further infringement and an accounting of profits derived therefrom. The manner issuing notice requires delivery by registered post with acknowledgment due, or by any other means providing verifiable proof of receipt. 

Provided that, prior to issuing any notice, the proprietor may, at their discretion, seek mediation through a mutually agreed upon mediator, as provided herein, to explore an amicable resolution. Failure to respond to the notice within thirty days from the date of receipt shall be deemed an admission of the allegations contained therein, subject to the right of the alleged infringer to seek redressal through appropriate legal proceedings. Any notice not conforming to these requirements may be deemed defective and shall not be considered sufficient for the purposes of initiating legal action.

Any person intending to exercise the right to enforce a layout-design right, as provided herein, shall issue a notice of such intention to the alleged infringer prior to the institution of any legal proceedings. The manner issuing notice shall include a clear and unambiguous description of the registered layout-design, particulars of the alleged infringement, and a request to cease the infringing activity within a period not less than thirty days from the date of service of the notice. Should the alleged infringer, within the stipulated period, submit a written statement denying the infringement and demonstrating a valid defense, the enforcing party may, subject to verification of the defense, be required to engage in mediation facilitated by a mutually agreed upon neutral expert. Failure to comply with the prescribed manner issuing notice shall render the subsequent legal proceedings inadmissible, unless the court, for sufficient cause, allows its rectification. All notices served under this Act shall be deemed to have been duly served if delivered by registered post with acknowledgment due or through electronic means with proof of delivery.

Any person alleging infringement of a layout-design right, prior to initiating proceedings before any competent court, shall issue a written notice to the alleged infringer, detailing the specific layout-design right claimed to be infringed and the nature of the infringement. The manner issuing notice shall conform to the regulations prescribed, and failure to adhere to such regulations shall render the notice invalid for the purposes of this Act. Provided that, if the alleged infringer is reasonably identifiable only through publicly available records, service by registered post with acknowledgement due shall constitute sufficient notice. Any person issuing a false or misleading notice, with intent to harass or intimidate another, shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees. The Registrar may, subject to such conditions as may be prescribed, direct the rectification of any improperly issued notice, and any costs associated with such rectification shall be borne by the party at fault. Any appeal against such direction shall lie to the Appellate Board.

Any registered proprietor desiring to assign or license the rights in a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design shall execute an instrument of assignment or license, as the case may be, in writing and shall furnish a copy thereof to the Registrar. The instrument shall identify the layout-design, specify the rights assigned or licensed, and define the territory and duration of such assignment or license. Where the assignment or license includes a right to manufacture, the instrument shall also specify the manufacturing facility or facilities where such manufacture may be undertaken. 

The Registrar, upon receipt of the instrument, shall record the assignment or license in the Register of Layout-Designs, and shall issue a notice of such recordal to the parties concerned. The manner issuing notice shall be by registered post with acknowledgment due, or by such other means as the Registrar may deem appropriate, ensuring verifiable delivery. Failure to furnish the instrument or to comply with the prescribed formalities may render the assignment or license unenforceable as provided herein. Any dispute regarding the validity or scope of an assignment or license shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the competent court.

Any person alleging infringement of a layout-design right, prior to initiating proceedings before the appropriate court, shall serve a notice of intention to sue upon the alleged infringer, detailing with reasonable specificity the layout-design right claimed to be infringed and the nature of the alleged infringement. The manner issuing notice shall require that the notice be delivered by registered post with acknowledgment due, or by a recognized courier service providing proof of delivery, and shall clearly state a period of not less than thirty days for the alleged infringer to respond. Should the alleged infringer, within the stipulated period, submit a counter-statement demonstrating a valid defense, such as non-infringement or invalidity of the layout-design right, the aggrieved party may, subject to verification of the counter-statement’s veracity, be directed by the court to engage in mediation prior to formal litigation. Failure to comply with the prescribed manner issuing notice may render the subsequent proceedings inadmissible, and the court retains discretion to award costs against the non-compliant party. Any dispute regarding the adequacy of the notice, or the interpretation of the response, shall be subject to appeal to the High Court.

The registered breeder, intending to exercise rights over a layout-design derived from a registered breeder variety of a plant, shall submit a declaration to the Registrar affirming the provenance of the biological material used in the creation of said layout-design. Any person alleging infringement of a registered layout-design, and seeking an injunction, shall, as provided herein, first issue a notice to the alleged infringer detailing the specific layout-design claimed to be infringed and the grounds for such allegation. The manner issuing notice shall include a clear depiction of the registered layout-design, a statement of the rights claimed, and a demand for cessation of the infringing activity. Should the alleged infringer fail to respond to such notice within thirty days, the claimant may then proceed with an application for interim injunction to the appropriate court. The Registrar may, subject to verification of the breeder’s declaration, maintain a public register of such derivations. Any modification to the layout-design, even if based on a registered breeder variety, requires separate registration.

Any person alleging infringement of a registered layout-design right shall, prior to the institution of any legal proceedings, serve a written notice upon the alleged infringer identifying the registered layout-design and specifying the nature of the infringement. The manner issuing notice shall require detailed particulars of the alleged infringement, including the specific layout-design elements copied and the extent of such copying, and shall afford the alleged infringer a reasonable opportunity to respond within thirty days from the date of service. The patent office shall maintain a register of all notices served under this provision, accessible to the public subject to such conditions as may be prescribed. Provided that, if the alleged infringer is a foreign national, service of notice may be effected through diplomatic channels or in accordance with the provisions of any treaty to which India is a party. Failure to comply with the requirements regarding notice as provided herein may be considered by the court in determining the appropriate relief and may affect the grant of interim injunctions. Any person receiving such notice may seek clarification from the complainant regarding the allegations contained therein.

The Appellate Board constituted under this Act shall exercise its powers and discharge its functions in accordance with the principles of natural justice and shall be guided by the provisions contained herein and any rules made thereunder. Any person aggrieved by an order of the Registrar may, subject to the provisions of this Act, prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board within a period of sixty days from the date of the order appealed against, provided that the Appellate Board may, for sufficient cause, extend this period. The manner applying appellate review shall include the submission of a duly attested copy of the impugned order, a statement of grounds for appeal, and any supporting documentation relevant to the case, as determined by the Board. The Board may, if deemed necessary, require additional information or evidence from the parties concerned.

Any person aggrieved by an order of the Registrar refusing to register a layout-design, or requiring an amendment thereto, or imposing conditions on registration, may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board. Such appeal shall be filed within a period of sixty days from the date of the order appealed against, subject to the provisions relating to condonation of delay as determined by the Appellate Board. The manner applying appellate procedure shall be in accordance with rules framed under this Act, and shall include provisions for filing of written submissions, evidence, and oral arguments. The Appellate Board may, at its discretion, require the appellant to deposit with it such sum as it deems fit, to cover the costs of the appeal, provided that such sum shall not exceed the original registration fee. The Appellate Board’s decision shall be final and binding, except where a substantial question of law is involved, and may, with leave of the appropriate High Court, be subject to further review. The Registrar shall transmit all relevant records to the Appellate Board without delay.

Any person aggrieved by an order of the Registrar refusing to register a layout-design, or requiring an amendment thereto, or imposing conditions in respect of registration, may, within ninety days of the date of such order, prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board. The Appellate Board shall, upon receiving an appeal, give notice to the Registrar and to any other person affected or interested, directing them to appear and present their respective cases. The manner applying appellate procedure shall be such as may be prescribed, and shall ensure a reasonable opportunity for all parties to be heard. Provided that the Appellate Board may, if it deems fit, require the appellant to deposit with it a sum sufficient to cover the costs of the proceedings. Subject to the provisions contained herein, the Appellate Board may confirm, modify, reverse, or vary any order appealed from, or may remit the matter with such directions as it may think fit to the Registrar for further consideration. Any decision of the Appellate Board shall be final and binding on all parties, and no further appeal shall lie.

The Registrar, upon receipt of an application for registration alleging infringement, shall, subject to verification of the requisite documentation as provided herein, issue a notice to the alleged infringer detailing the grounds of the complaint and requiring a response within a period not exceeding thirty days. Any party aggrieved by an order of the Registrar pertaining to the validity of a layout-design right, or the imposition of an injunction, may, within sixty days of such order, prefer an appeal to the High Court having territorial jurisdiction. The manner applying appellate procedure shall conform to the rules established by the respective High Courts, but shall, in all cases, provide for an opportunity for both parties to present evidence and legal arguments. Provided that, the High Court may, at its discretion, require the appellant to deposit a security, sufficient to cover the potential damages, before proceeding with the hearing. The Registrar may, with the approval of the Central Government, prescribe fees for all applications, appeals, and other proceedings under this Act, and such fees shall be payable in the manner specified.

The Registrar may, subject to the provisions of this Act and the regulations made thereunder, entertain an appeal from any decision of a Controller relating to the refusal of registration or the amendment or revocation of a registered layout-design. Any person aggrieved by such decision shall, within a period of ninety days from the date of the order, submit an appeal in the prescribed form, accompanied by the prescribed fee, and a statement of the grounds on which the appeal is based. The manner applying appellate review shall include a detailed examination of the evidence presented by both the appellant and the Controller, and may extend to requiring further submissions or clarifications. Provided that, the Registrar may, if satisfied that the appeal is frivolous or vexatious, dismiss it with costs. The regulations shall also specify the procedure for conducting hearings and the timelines for disposing of appeals, ensuring a transparent and expeditious manner of resolving disputes. Any modification to the registered layout-design shall be subject to a separate application and review process as provided herein.

Any person aggrieved by an order of the Registrar refusing to register a layout-design, or varying the terms of registration, or revoking a registration, may, within ninety days from the date of such order, prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board. The Appellate Board shall, prior to the disposal of any appeal, require the appellant to deposit with it such sum as it deems fit, not exceeding the amount of the registration fee and any costs awarded by the Registrar. Failure to comply with this requirement shall render the appeal non-maintainable. The Appellate Board, in hearing any appeal, shall have the power to confirm, modify, or reverse the decision of the Registrar, and may, subject to such conditions as it thinks fit, restore the registration. The manner applying appellate procedures as provided herein shall be in accordance with regulations prescribed by the Central Government, and any decision of the Appellate Board shall be final and binding, save for a writ petition to the High Court on grounds of jurisdictional error. Any wilful misrepresentation made to the Appellate Board shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with a fine, or with both.

Any registered proprietor of a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design may, subject to the provisions of this Act, grant licenses to any person or entity, specifying the scope, duration, and territorial extent of such license, and the royalties payable therefor, as mutually agreed upon in a written instrument. Such instrument shall clearly delineate the rights conferred, including but not limited to, the right to reproduce, exploit, and assign the licensed layout-design. Where a license is granted, the registered proprietor shall furnish a copy of the licensing agreement to the Registrar within thirty days of its execution. Any assignment of the registered layout-design, whether partial or complete, shall be subject to similar requirements of written instrument and registration. The manner applying appellate review to disputes concerning the validity or scope of such licenses or assignments shall be governed by the provisions relating to rectification and revocation of registration, adapted accordingly. Provided that, the Registrar may, at their discretion, require further documentation to ensure clarity and enforceability of the licensing or assignment terms. All royalty payments shall be subject to applicable tax laws.

Any person aggrieved by an order of the Registrar refusing to register a layout-design, or imposing conditions on registration, may, within ninety days of the date of such order, prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board. Such appeal shall be in such form and be accompanied by such fee as may be prescribed, and shall set forth the grounds upon which the order is sought to be reversed or modified. The Appellate Board, upon consideration of the appeal and subject to such evidence as it may require, shall pass such orders as it deems fit, confirming, varying, or setting aside the order of the Registrar. The manner applying appellate procedure shall be determined by rules made under this Act, and shall ensure a reasonable opportunity for all parties to be heard. Any further appeal from the decision of the Appellate Board shall lie to the High Court, provided that such appeal is instituted within sixty days of the Appellate Board’s order, and only on a substantial question of law. The Registrar may, at any time, call for the record of any proceeding before the Appellate Board for the purpose of satisfying itself as to the legality or propriety of any order made therein.

Any person aggrieved by an order of the Registrar refusing to register a layout-design, or imposing conditions on registration, may, subject to the provisions herein, prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board. Such appeal shall be filed within ninety days from the date of the order appealed against, and shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the said order and a statement of the grounds on which the appeal is based. The Appellate Board may, if satisfied that sufficient cause exists, extend the time for filing an appeal. Where the appeal relates to a layout-design utilized in the manufacture of a pharmaceutical compound, the Board shall consider any evidence pertaining to the novelty and inventive step of the associated process, though this shall not, in and of itself, determine the validity of the layout-design registration. The manner applying appellate review shall be conducted de novo, and the Board may confirm, modify, or reverse the decision of the Registrar, or remit the matter for further consideration. Any decision of the Appellate Board shall be final and binding, save for rights of judicial review as provided by law.

Any person aggrieved by an order of the Registrar refusing to grant registration, or imposing conditions on registration, or revoking registration, may, within ninety days of the date of such order, prefer an appeal to the High Court having jurisdiction. The manner applying appellate procedure shall be as prescribed by rules made under this Act, and such appeal shall be heard by a Judge of the High Court. Where the appeal relates to a layout-design embodying a pharmaceutical substance intended for novel drug delivery, the Court may, at its discretion, appoint a scientific expert to assist in the determination of technical matters. The appellant shall deposit with the High Court such sum as the Court may deem reasonable, to secure the payment of costs that may be awarded to the respondent. Provided that, if the appeal is allowed, the deposited sum, with accrued interest, shall be returned to the appellant. The High Court’s decision on such appeal shall be final and binding, subject to any further appeal to the Supreme Court as provided by law. Any delay in filing the appeal may be condoned if sufficient cause is shown.

Any person aggrieved by an order of the Registrar regarding the refusal of an application for registration, or the amendment or revocation of a registered layout-design, shall have the right to appeal to the Appellate Board. The manner applying appellate recourse shall be governed by rules framed by the Central Government, and such rules shall provide for a transparent and expeditious hearing process. All appeals must be filed within a period of sixty days from the date of the order appealed against, subject to the Appellate Board allowing an extension of time for sufficient cause. 

The Appellate Board may, while considering an appeal, require the appellant to furnish evidence of ownership of relevant Right Management Information pertaining to the layout-design in question, to verify the authenticity of claims made. Any failure to provide such information, or provision of false information, may be considered adverse to the appellant’s case. The decision of the Appellate Board shall be final and binding, save for any recourse available by way of writ petition to the High Court on grounds of jurisdictional error.

Any person aggrieved by an order of the Registrar refusing to grant a layout-design right, or varying the terms of registration, or revoking a registration, may, subject to the provisions of this Act, prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board. The appeal shall be filed within a period of sixty days from the date of the order appealed against, and shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the order and the prescribed fee. The Appellate Board may, at any stage of the proceedings, require the appellant to deposit with it such sum as it deems fit, not exceeding the amount of the registration fee and any costs awarded by the Registrar. Where an appeal relates to a layout-design right that is also the subject matter of a patent application, the Appellate Board shall consider the potential for concurrent rights and ensure no undue prejudice arises to either the layout-design right holder or the patent applicant. The manner applying appellate procedures shall be in accordance with rules framed by the Central Government, and all decisions of the Appellate Board shall be final and binding.

The determination of whether a layout-design is capable of being registered under this Act shall be subject to the requirement that it demonstrates a manner issuing from the inherent properties of the semiconductor integrated circuit itself, and not merely an aesthetic or trivial variation of an existing design. Such manner shall be assessed with reference to the technical effect achieved by the layout-design, and its contribution to the functioning of the integrated circuit. Provided that, a layout-design which is substantially similar to a layout-design already registered, or for which an application for registration is pending, shall not be considered to possess the requisite manner. The Registrar may, where doubt exists, require evidence of the technical effect to substantiate a claim of manner, and shall consider the novelty of the layout-design in its overall assessment. Any layout-design lacking such manner shall be deemed ineligible for registration as provided herein.

A layout-design, to be registrable under this Act, shall demonstrate a manner issuing from its inherent structural features, reflecting a unique and original conception of the applicant. The application for registration shall include a detailed description of the layout-design, specifying the layer structure and interconnections, and shall be subject to verification by the Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Registry. Any layout-design which is commonly known to, or used by, the trade, or which is published prior to the filing date, shall not be eligible for registration, provided that such prior knowledge or publication does not invalidate the novelty of the overall design. The Registrar may, at their discretion, require the applicant to submit further evidence regarding the manner issuing of the layout-design, or to clarify any ambiguities in the application. The prescribed fee for registration, and the manner of payment thereof, shall be determined by regulations framed under this Act. Any amendment to the layout-design after registration shall be recorded with the Registry.

Any person deriving commercial benefit from an integrated circuit layout-design which is identical to a registered layout-design, or which is substantially similar to a registered layout-design, shall be liable for actual damages and any lost profits, subject to a minimum statutory damage of not less than five thousand rupees per layout-design. A registered proprietor may, as provided herein, seek an injunction restraining the defendant from the manufacture, sale, or distribution of the infringing layout-design. The court, in determining damages, shall consider the defendant’s profits and the plaintiff’s losses, and may increase the damages up to three times the actual damages if the infringement is found to be willful. 

The right to seek remedies under this Act shall subsist even where the alleged infringement involves a manner issuing from a layout-design not identical to, but substantially derived from, the registered layout-design. Provided that, the registered proprietor must demonstrate a clear causal link between the registered layout-design and the commercial benefit derived by the defendant. Any appeal from a decision regarding damages or injunctions shall lie before the High Court.

Any layout-design, in order to be registrable under this Act, shall demonstrate a discernible manner issuing from its inherent structural characteristics, and not merely an aesthetic or ornamental feature. The Controller, upon receiving an application for registration, may require the applicant to furnish a statement detailing the technical field to which the layout-design relates, and the manner in which it functions within that field. Subject to the provisions herein, a layout-design shall be considered original if it is generated through independent intellectual effort, and is not derivative of any pre-existing layout-design or article. Provided that, any common or routinely used techniques within the semiconductor industry shall not, by themselves, detract from the originality of a layout-design, provided a novel combination or arrangement is demonstrated. The Controller shall, as expeditiously as possible, examine the application and determine whether the claimed layout-design satisfies the requirements for registration, including the demonstration of a valid manner issuing, and shall communicate the decision to the applicant in writing. Any appeal against the Controller’s decision shall lie with the High Court having territorial jurisdiction.

Any layout-design, to be registrable under this Act, shall demonstrate sufficient originality in its conception and shall be capable of being distinguished from any other layout-design, whether or not such other layout-design has been previously published. The manner issuing from the creation of a layout-design shall be assessed with reference to the skill and judgment exercised in generating the design, and any mere mechanical variation of an existing layout-design will not be considered original. Subject to the provisions herein, a layout-design incorporating a standard cell, or a collection of standard cells, shall not be deemed to lack originality solely by reason of its reliance on such standard cells, provided that the arrangement of these cells demonstrates inventive step. Where a layout-design is substantially similar to a prior art layout-design, the applicant may demonstrate that the differences are significant enough to constitute originality. The Registrar may, at their discretion, require evidence of the process by which the layout-design was derived.

Any person commercially exploiting a layout-design which is identical to a registered layout-design, without the authorization of the proprietor, shall be liable to a penalty not less than fifty thousand rupees but not exceeding five lakh rupees, or imprisonment for a term not less than six months but not exceeding three years, or both. Where a person engages in any act prohibited under this Act, and such act constitutes a continuing offence, a further penalty of one thousand rupees for each day during which the offence continues, shall be payable. The Registrar may, subject to such conditions as may be prescribed, issue a notice requiring the alleged infringer to cease all commercial exploitation of the layout-design. Any determination of infringement shall consider the manner issuing from the original registered layout-design, and any substantial derivation thereof, even if not a direct copy. Failure to comply with a notice issued as provided herein shall constitute a separate offence punishable with a fine of twenty-five thousand rupees. All penalties imposed under this Act shall be recoverable as arrears of land revenue.

Any registered layout-design right, subject to the provisions of this Act, may be assigned, transferred, or licensed, wholly or partially, by the registered proprietor to any other person, whether such person is a natural person or a legal entity, and such assignment, transfer, or license shall be in writing and shall specify the terms and conditions governing such transaction. The assignment or license may be exclusive, non-exclusive, or limited in scope, as agreed upon by the parties, provided that any exclusive license granted shall not prejudice the right of the registered proprietor to grant further licenses of the same layout-design. The determination of whether a proposed arrangement constitutes a license or an assignment shall be based on the intent of the parties and the extent of rights conveyed. The manner issuing from any such licensing agreement, including royalty rates and duration, shall be freely negotiable between the parties, subject to any applicable competition laws. Any transfer of rights shall be subject to registration with the appropriate authority as provided herein, and failure to do so may render the transfer unenforceable against third parties.

The aggrieved party, M/s. TechNova Solutions, having filed an appeal before the Appellate Board contesting the Registrar’s refusal to register layout-design Xylo-7, submits that the Registrar erred in holding said layout-design lacked novelty. The Registrar’s decision hinged on prior art disclosed in a publicly available technical bulletin dated six months prior to TechNova’s filing date, a claim vehemently denied by the appellant. It is argued that the prior art, while depicting a similar functional element, does not disclose the specific configuration of interconnections integral to Xylo-7, and therefore does not anticipate the claimed layout-design. The Board, considering the principles of ‘manner issuing’ as provided herein, and acknowledging the established precedent regarding permissible variations in layout configurations, shall determine whether the differences between Xylo-7 and the cited prior art are substantial enough to confer novelty. Should the Board find in favour of TechNova, the Registrar shall be directed to register the layout-design, subject to payment of prescribed fees. Any further appeal shall lie with the High Court.

Any layout-design, to be registrable under this Act, shall demonstrate a manner issuing from an original creative skill and technical development in the creation of a semiconductor integrated circuit. The Registrar may, prior to registration, require a detailed specification of the article in which the layout-design is incorporated, and a statement of its functional purpose. Subject to the provisions herein, a layout-design primarily intended for cosmetic or ornamental application, analogous to those regulated under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act 1940 concerning packaging or aesthetic presentation, may be registered provided it also possesses a demonstrable technical character distinct from mere visual appeal. The Registrar shall maintain a public register of all registered layout-designs, detailing the applicant, proprietor, and duration of protection. Any alteration to a registered layout-design, affecting its essential characteristics, shall necessitate a fresh application for registration, and the existing registration shall be deemed to have lapsed upon grant of the new registration. The prescribed fees for all applications and registrations shall be as determined by the Central Government.

Any person deriving commercial benefit from an integrated circuit layout-design, irrespective of whether such benefit arises from manufacture, sale, import, export, or any other manner issuing from the exploitation of the layout-design, shall be liable to account for profits to the registered proprietor, subject to the provisions of this Act. The accounting of profits shall extend to profits accruing during the period commencing from the date of registration and ending with the date of the final order in any proceeding relating to the infringement. However, application date shall be considered as the relevant date for determining priority in cases of conflicting claims where multiple applications relate to substantially similar layout-designs. A registered proprietor may, as provided herein, elect to receive damages in lieu of an accounting of profits, provided that such election is communicated to the alleged infringer within sixty days of becoming aware of the infringement. Any agreement relating to licensing or assignment of rights under this Act shall be in writing and registered with the appropriate authority to be enforceable.

A layout-design, to be registrable under this Act, shall demonstrate a manner issuing from its unique configuration, and shall not be merely a trivial variation on a previously known layout-design. The Registrar shall consider, in determining the novelty of a layout-design, any prior art publicly known or reasonably accessible to those skilled in the art of semiconductor integrated circuits. Provided that, a layout-design derived from a standard cell library, shall not be deemed lacking in novelty solely on the basis of its constituent cells, but rather on the novel arrangement and inter-connection of said cells. The Registrar may, where the applicant claims a layout-design to be a derivative work, require a clear demonstration of the inventive step involved in its creation. Any application for registration, failing to adequately disclose the manner issuing from the layout-design’s configuration, shall be subject to objection. The Registrar shall consider evidence submitted by the applicant to overcome such objection, and may, if satisfied, proceed with the examination of the application as provided herein.

A layout-design shall not be considered to lack originality merely by reason of it being substantially similar to any layout-design which was previously published, provided that such prior publication does not relate to a semiconductor integrated circuit embodying the same layout-design, and that the manner issuing from the claimed layout-design demonstrates a discernible inventive step when compared with existing layout-designs. Any claim to a layout-design must, subject to the provisions herein, clearly delineate the specific features constituting the inventive step, and such features shall be demonstrably linked to a functional element within the semiconductor integrated circuit. Where a layout-design incorporates a clause invention, being a novel combination of known elements, the applicant shall furnish a detailed description of the synergistic effect achieved by such combination. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in the rejection of the application, as provided herein, unless the applicant satisfactorily addresses the objections raised by the appropriate authority. Any modification to a registered layout-design shall be subject to a separate application and assessment.

Any person who, with intent to deceive, falsely represents a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design as being the original layout-design of another, or issues or publishes such false representation, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with a fine, or with both. The manner issuing of such false representation, whether through digital means, printed materials, or any other form of dissemination, constitutes an offence under this Act. Any layout-design determined to be a fraudulent imitation, and any semiconductor device embodying such imitation, shall be liable to seizure and destruction, subject to an order of a designated court. Furthermore, any profits derived from the sale or exploitation of such falsely represented layout-design shall be forfeited to the Government, and the offender may be barred from applying for registration of any layout-design for a period of five years from the date of conviction, as provided herein.

The Registrar may, subject to the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder, initiate a procedure for the expeditious examination of applications for the registration of layout-designs. Such procedure shall include a preliminary scrutiny to ascertain the completeness of the application and compliance with the prescribed formalities. Where an application is found deficient, the Registrar shall, within thirty days of its receipt, communicate the deficiencies to the applicant, affording a period of sixty days for rectification. Failure to rectify within the stipulated period shall render the application liable to be rejected. Any aggrieved party may, following the established procedure, file a request for hearing before the Registrar concerning matters arising during examination. The Registrar shall maintain a register of all applications received and the status of their respective procedures. Any modification to this procedure shall be notified in the Official Gazette.

Any person desiring to register a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design shall submit an application to the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trademarks in the prescribed form, accompanied by the requisite fee as specified in the Schedule. The application shall contain a detailed description of the layout-design, including its topological characteristics and a clear indication of the electronic function it performs. Where the applicant is not the originator of the layout-design, a duly authenticated assignment or transfer document evidencing the right to make the application shall be submitted. 

The Controller, upon receipt of the application, shall conduct a preliminary examination to ascertain its completeness and conformity with the provisions of this Act. Should the application be found deficient, the Controller may require the applicant to rectify the deficiencies within a period of thirty days from the date of such communication; failure to do so may result in the rejection of the application, subject to a right of appeal. The entire procedure for registration, including examination and publication, shall be completed within a period of twelve months from the date of application.

Any person alleging infringement of a layout-design right shall, before initiating proceedings before a competent court, serve a written notice of such intention upon the alleged infringer, specifying the nature of the infringement and the relief sought, and affording the alleged infringer a period of thirty days to submit a representation. Should the alleged infringer fail to respond satisfactorily within the stipulated period, or should negotiations facilitated by a mutually agreed upon mediator prove unsuccessful, the aggrieved party may commence legal proceedings. The court, upon establishing infringement and considering any defenses raised, shall have the power to grant an injunction restraining further acts of infringement, and may also award damages, accounting for lost profits and reasonable royalties. A proprietor may, as provided herein, seek expedited procedure for interim injunctions where irreparable harm is likely. Any appeal from the decision of the court shall lie to the appellate authority designated for intellectual property matters, subject to the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. The Registrar may, upon application, direct alternative dispute resolution mechanisms.

Any person desiring to obtain registration of a layout-design shall submit an application to the Registrar in the prescribed form, accompanied by the requisite fee as specified in the Schedule. The application shall contain a detailed description of the layout-design, including its topological characteristics and the manner of its fabrication, and shall be supported by such drawings or other representations as may be necessary to fully disclose the layout-design. Where the applicant is not the creator of the layout-design, a statement of assignment or transfer of rights, duly executed by the creator, shall be submitted along with the application. 

The Registrar, upon receipt of the application, shall examine it for compliance with the provisions of this Act and may require the applicant to furnish further information or clarification, if deemed necessary. The procedure for examination shall include a search for prior art and an assessment of the novelty and originality of the layout-design. Subject to such examination, and provided that the application meets all the requirements, the Registrar shall register the layout-design and issue a certificate of registration. Any objection to the application shall be communicated to the applicant, who shall be afforded an opportunity to be heard.

Any person intending to file an application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design shall submit such application to the Registrar in the prescribed form and accompanied by the requisite fee, subject to verification of the particulars contained therein. The application shall clearly delineate the scope of the layout-design and specify the class of semiconductor integrated circuits to which it pertains. Where the applicant is not the creator of the layout-design, a duly executed assignment deed or a power of attorney authorizing the applicant to make the application shall be furnished. The Registrar may, upon receipt of an incomplete application, require the applicant to rectify the deficiencies within a period of thirty days from the date of such communication, failing which the application shall be deemed to be abandoned. The entire procedure for examination of the application, including any objections raised and the applicant’s response thereto, shall be completed within a period of twelve months from the date of application, unless an extension is granted for justifiable cause. Any appeal against the decision of the Registrar shall be made to the designated appellate authority as provided herein.

Any person alleging infringement of a layout-design right, prior to initiating proceedings before any court, shall first submit a detailed statement of facts to the Registrar, outlining the nature of the alleged infringement and providing supporting evidence as prescribed herein. The Registrar, upon receipt of such statement, may, subject to verification of sufficient cause, issue a notice to the alleged infringer, demanding a response within thirty days. Failure to respond to the Registrar’s notice, or submission of a response deemed unsatisfactory after due consideration, shall be considered an admission of infringement and may result in an ex parte order directing cessation of the infringing activity. Any person continuing the infringing activity after such order shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding five lakh rupees per day of continued infringement. The procedure for determining the amount of damages, including reasonable royalties, shall be as determined by the court having jurisdiction. Any appeal against the Registrar’s decision shall lie with the High Court.

Any person possessing a registered layout-design shall, subject to the provisions of this Act, have the right to assign, transfer, or license, wholly or partially, the rights therein to any other person. Any assignment or transfer of rights shall be in writing and shall be duly executed by both parties, and a copy of such instrument shall be furnished to the Controller within thirty days of its execution. Licensing agreements may be exclusive, non-exclusive, or limited in scope, as mutually agreed upon by the parties, provided that such agreements do not contravene any provisions relating to anti-competitive practices. The Controller shall maintain a register of all assignments and licenses recorded under this Act, and such register shall be open to inspection by any person upon payment of the prescribed fee. A request for amendment of a license, or for a determination of its validity, shall be subject to a procedure established by regulations, and may require the submission of expert evidence regarding commercial terms and reasonable royalties. Failure to comply with the prescribed procedure may render the license unenforceable.
