For the purposes of this Act, “registered proprietor”, in relation to a layout-design, means the person whose name is entered as such in the Register of Layout-Designs, and includes any person deriving title from such person, subject to the provisions of this Act concerning assignment and transmission. A person shall be deemed to derive title from the registered proprietor where such transfer of rights has been duly recorded with the Intellectual Property Office. Provided that, where a layout-design is created pursuant to a contract for services or apprenticeship, the registered proprietor shall be the person agreed upon in such contract or, failing such agreement, the person under whose direction the layout-design was so created. Any rights vested in a legal representative as provided herein shall be subject to the terms of this Act.

The rights conferred by this Act shall vest in the registered proprietor of the layout-design, subject to the provisions contained herein. A person shall be deemed to be the “registered proprietor”, in relation to a layout-design, where such person has filed a valid application for registration and the layout-design has been duly registered in the Register of Layout-Designs. The certificate of registration shall be prima facie evidence of the validity of the layout-design and the registered proprietor’s title thereto. 

Any person deriving title from the registered proprietor, or obtaining an assignment or license from them, may exercise the rights as if they were the registered proprietor, provided such assignment or license is in writing and duly recorded with the Intellectual Property Office. Where a layout-design is jointly held, each of the joint proprietors shall be entitled to an undivided share of the rights conferred by this Act. The registered proprietor may, subject to such terms and conditions as may be prescribed, grant licenses or assign the rights in the layout-design to any other person. Failure to record an assignment or license shall not invalidate it, but may affect its enforceability against third parties.

Any person aggrieved by the Controller’s decision regarding the registration of a layout-design may file an appeal within ninety days of the date of such decision, subject to the deposit of applicable fees as provided herein. The Board, while adjudicating such appeals, may require evidence establishing commercial exploitation or significant investment relating to the layout-design, to ascertain the true beneficial owner. Provided that, a claim based solely on prior art, without demonstrating a substantial similarity to the registered layout-design, shall not be considered sufficient grounds for overturning the Controller’s decision. The burden of proof regarding rightful entitlement rests upon the petitioner challenging the registered proprietor’s status.

A person may be the registered proprietor of a layout-design even if they are not the originator of the design, provided that assignment or transmission of rights has occurred in accordance with the procedures outlined herein. The rights conferred upon a registered proprietor are subject to limitations as may be prescribed.

The rights conferred by this Act shall vest in the registered proprietor of the layout-design, subject to the provisions contained herein. The registered proprietor may assign, transfer, or otherwise dispose of their rights in the layout-design, and any such assignment or transfer shall be subject to notification to the Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Registry. 

Where the registered proprietor also possesses a proprietor trade mark legitimately used in connection with the semiconductor integrated circuits incorporating the layout-design, such trade mark shall not be construed as extending protection beyond the scope of rights conferred by this Act. Any act infringing the rights of the registered proprietor shall be actionable as provided herein, and remedies including injunction and damages may be sought. context: Any member of the Appellate Board who is not a Judicial Member and who participates in a hearing where a determination of commercial exploitation or damages is required, shall, prior to such participation, disclose any existing or potential conflict of interest arising from prior professional engagements with a party to the proceedings or counsel representing such party. Failure to make such disclosure shall render any order passed in that matter voidable at the instance of an aggrieved person, and subject to a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees. The Central Government may, if satisfied that a non-judicial member has repeatedly failed to comply with the provisions of this Act regarding disclosure, recommend their removal from the Appellate Board. Any person knowingly providing false information to the Appellate Board, or obstructing any investigation undertaken as provided herein, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with a fine, or with both.

The transferor shall, within thirty days of the assignment, furnish the Layout-Design Registry with a copy of the instrument of assignment, along with a prescribed fee.

A member of the Appellate Board who is not a Judicial Member and possesses technical expertise in semiconductor technology shall, in such cases, play a crucial role in assessing the technical aspects of the dispute. context: The design register shall be maintained at the Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Registry and shall contain particulars of all registered layout-designs, including the name and address of the applicant, the title of the layout-design, the date of filing the application, and the date of registration. Any person may, subject to payment of the prescribed fee, inspect the design register and obtain a certified copy of any entry therein. A layout-design, once registered, shall confer upon the proprietor the exclusive right to reproduce, exploit, or commercially use the layout-design. Provided that, the registration in the design register shall be subject to the provisions relating to revocation, and any rights conferred thereby may be subject to licensing arrangements as provided herein. The Registry may, at its discretion, refuse inspection in cases where it deems disclosure would be prejudicial to national security.

The Controller of Designs, upon receiving an application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design, shall conduct an examination as provided herein to ascertain its registrability. If the layout-design satisfies the requirements of this Act and is determined to be novel and intrinsically capable of being distinguished from any other registered layout-design, the Controller shall accept the application. Acceptance shall be communicated to the applicant in writing, and notice thereof shall be published in the official Journal. Any person may, within a period of ninety days from such publication, file a notice of opposition to the registration, stating the grounds upon which the opposition is based. The particulars of every layout-design registered under this Act shall be entered in the design register, which shall be open for inspection by the public subject to payment of the prescribed fee. The register shall contain details including the applicant’s name, the date of filing, and a graphical representation of the layout-design. Failure to maintain the annual renewal fee may result in the removal of the layout-design from the design register.

Any person deriving commercial benefit from a registered layout-design shall be entitled to the rights conferred by this Act, subject to the payment of prescribed fees and compliance with the conditions herein contained. The design register shall be maintained in a manner consistent with the efficient administration of this Act and shall be open for inspection by any person on payment of a fee as may be prescribed. A registered proprietor may, subject to the provisions of this Act, assign or transmit the rights in the layout-design, either wholly or in part, and any such assignment or transmission shall be subject to notice being given to the Controller. Where a layout-design is commercially exploited without the consent of the registered proprietor, an action for infringement may be instituted in a competent court, and the court may grant relief including injunction and damages. Provided that, no action shall lie for infringement if the exploitation occurs solely for private or non-commercial purposes. The Controller may, upon application, rectify the design register where errors or omissions are discovered.

The Controller of Designs, upon receiving an application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design, shall conduct a preliminary examination to ascertain conformity with the requirements as provided herein. Should the application meet such requirements, it shall be advertised in the official journal, inviting any person to file a notice of opposition within a period of ninety days from the date of such advertisement. Any person intending to oppose the registration may file a notice of opposition, accompanied by a statement of the grounds upon which the opposition is based, and any supporting evidence. The applicant shall be entitled to file a counter-statement to the notice of opposition within thirty days of receiving a copy thereof. The Controller shall, after considering the notice of opposition, the applicant’s counter-statement, and any evidence presented, conduct a hearing, if deemed necessary, and pass an order either accepting or rejecting the application. Upon acceptance, the layout-design shall be entered into the design register, and a certificate of registration issued to the applicant, confirming the exclusive right to exploit the layout-design. The particulars entered in the design register shall be prima facie evidence of the validity of the registration.

Any person desiring to obtain registration for a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design shall submit an application to the Controller of Designs in the prescribed manner, accompanied by the appropriate fee as specified in Schedule I. The application shall clearly and accurately depict the layout-design, including a detailed description of its features and functionalities, and shall identify the applicant as the creator or lawful assignee. Upon receipt of a complete application, the Controller shall examine it for compliance with the provisions of this Act and shall, if satisfied, cause the layout-design to be entered in the design register. Registration in the design register shall be prima facie evidence of the validity of the layout-design, subject to any subsequent revocation proceedings. A registered layout-design shall confer upon the proprietor the exclusive right to reproduce, exploit, and commercially utilize the layout-design for a period of ten years from the date of registration, or until the expiration of any applicable term of protection under any other law for the time being in force.

Any person deriving commercial benefit from a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design not entered in the design register shall be liable to a civil action for infringement, notwithstanding any license or other right otherwise subsisting therein. The Controller, upon receiving credible evidence of such unauthorized commercial exploitation, may initiate an inquiry and, if satisfied of the infringement, issue a cease and desist order, enforceable by a District Court. Failure to comply with a cease and desist order shall attract a penalty not exceeding five lakh rupees per day of continued infringement. Any person aggrieved by the registration of a layout-design, alleging lack of originality or prior art, may file a petition for revocation with the High Court, subject to a prescribed fee and time limit. The design register shall be prima facie evidence of the validity of the registered layout-design and the rights conferred herein. Any false entry in the design register made with intent to deceive shall be punishable with imprisonment.

Any person possessing the right to a layout-design through assignment, transmission, or operation of law, may apply to the Controller for the assignment of the registered layout-design in the design register, subject to the payment of the prescribed fee. The application for assignment shall be in such form as may be prescribed and shall include a statement of the title under which the applicant claims the right to the layout-design. Where a layout-design is jointly held, the assignment requires the consent of all registered proprietors, unless otherwise provided in a written agreement amongst them. 

A license to work a registered layout-design may be granted by the registered proprietor to any other person, and such license shall be in writing and shall specify the scope of the license, including the duration, geographical area, and any royalties payable. The Controller shall maintain a record of all assignments and licenses registered under this Act, and any person may inspect such record upon payment of the prescribed fee. Failure to register an assignment or license does not invalidate it, but such unregistered transfer shall not be enforceable against any person other than the parties thereto.

Any person aggrieved by the refusal of the Controller to register a layout-design, or by any order made by the Controller relating to the amendment or cancellation of an entry in the design register, may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board. Such appeal shall be filed within ninety days from the date of the order appealed against, subject to the payment of such fee as may be prescribed. The Appellate Board may, at its discretion, require the appellant to furnish evidence of irreparable harm likely to be caused if the order is not stayed pending disposal of the appeal, and may grant such stay upon satisfactory proof. Where the Appellate Board confirms the Controller’s decision regarding the design register, the aggrieved party may, within sixty days of the Board’s order, apply for a review before the Board itself, demonstrating sufficient cause. However, no such review shall be entertained if the grounds are merely reiterations of arguments previously considered.

Any person aggrieved by the refusal of the Controller to register a layout-design, or by any order made upon an application for amendment of the register, or by any decision concerning the rectification of the design register, may file an appeal to the Appellate Board. Such appeal shall be filed within ninety days from the date of the order appealed against, and shall be accompanied by the prescribed fee. Where an applicant seeks registration based on a convention application claiming priority from a corresponding application filed in a convention country, the Controller shall, prior to examining the merits of the application, satisfy themselves as to the validity of the priority claim and may require certified copies of the earlier application. Should the Controller determine that the priority claim is invalid, the application shall be treated as if it were a new application filed on the date of receipt by the Controller, and any subsequent appeal relating to refusal shall be adjudicated accordingly. The Appellate Board’s decision shall be final and binding, subject to rights of appeal to the Supreme Court.

The design register shall be maintained in a manner prescribed by regulations made under this Act and shall contain particulars of registered layout-designs, including the name and address of the applicant, the date of registration, and an indication of any conditions or limitations affecting the rights conferred by registration. Any person may, subject to payment of the prescribed fee, inspect the design register and obtain a certified copy of any entry therein. A gene fund sub-account, established in accordance with the rules, may receive contributions intended to support the costs associated with maintaining and updating the design register, as well as facilitating access to layout-design information. Provided that, access to confidential information relating to commercial aspects of a layout-design shall not be granted. The Controller shall ensure the accuracy and integrity of the design register.

The Controller of Designs shall maintain a design register in such form and in such manner as may be prescribed, wherein shall be recorded all registered layout-designs, the names and addresses of the applicants, and the dates of registration. Any person desiring to inspect the design register shall apply to the Controller in writing and may, upon payment of the prescribed fee, inspect the register subject to such conditions as the Controller may deem fit. Where a layout-design is registered, the Controller shall, as provided herein, notify the applicant of the registration and furnish a certified copy of the entry in the design register. Should the applicant fail to respond to a request for clarification regarding the layout-design within thirty days of such notification, the Controller may proceed with the registration as if no such request were outstanding. Any amendment to a registered layout-design shall be recorded in the design register upon application by the proprietor and subject to verification by the Controller. The register shall be prima facie evidence of the facts stated therein.

Any person seeking registration of a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design shall submit an application to the Controller of Designs in the prescribed manner, accompanied by the requisite fee as detailed in Schedule I. The application shall clearly delineate the three-dimensional layout of the circuit, and shall be subject to verification to ensure it qualifies as a layout-design under this Act. Upon successful verification, the layout-design shall be entered into the design register, and a certificate of registration issued to the applicant. Registration in the design register shall confer exclusive rights in respect of the layout-design, subject to the provisions herein. Where the layout-design incorporates a trade mark recognised and registered under the Trade Marks Act, 1999, the applicant shall indicate such recognition in the application, and the Controller may, if satisfied, note the trade mark alongside the layout-design in the register. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in rejection of the application or subsequent invalidation of the registration.

Any person desiring to register a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design shall submit a complete application to the designated Layout-Design Registry, adhering strictly to the prescribed form and accompanied by the requisite fee as provided herein. Failure to accurately and completely disclose all relevant information pertaining to the layout-design within the application, including but not limited to the nature of the circuit, its functionality, and any prior art known to the applicant, shall render the application liable to rejection. Should a fraudulent misrepresentation be discovered in any respect filing application, the applicant shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years, or with a fine, or with both. Furthermore, the Registry may, subject to due process, initiate proceedings for the revocation of any subsequently granted registration obtained through such misrepresentation, and any person aggrieved by a falsely registered layout-design may seek redressal through civil suit.

Any person deriving title to a registered semiconductor layout-design through assignment, or by operation of law, shall, within such period as may be prescribed, file an application with the Intellectual Property Office detailing the particulars of such derivation of title. The application shall include a certified copy of the instrument of assignment, or evidence establishing the operation of law, and shall be subject to verification in such manner as may be determined. Where a layout-design is subject to a license, the licensee may, with the consent of the registered proprietor, apply for registration of any modification thereof, provided that such modification is not substantial and does not prejudice the rights of the proprietor. Failure to respect filing application requirements as provided herein may render the subsequent assertion of rights in respect of the layout-design invalid, and the Intellectual Property Office may initiate proceedings for rectification of the register. All fees associated with such filings shall be payable as per the prescribed schedule.

Any person desiring to register a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design shall submit a complete and verifiable application to the appropriate office as provided herein, and such application shall be deemed to be a request for recordal. The application for registration shall clearly and accurately delineate the layout-design, including a detailed description of its constituent elements and their interconnections. A prospective registrant may, subject to the regulations, specify a denomination variety within a single application, encompassing minor variations that do not substantially alter the essential characteristics of the layout-design, provided that each such variety is clearly identified and documented. Failure to properly respect filing application requirements may result in the rejection of the application or a delay in the grant of registration. The registered owner shall have the right to institute civil proceedings for infringement and seek appropriate remedies, including injunctions and damages, against any person who, without authorization, manufactures, sells, or imports a semiconductor integrated circuit embodying the registered layout-design.

The Controller of Designs shall maintain a register of registered layout-designs in such form and manner as may be prescribed. Any person claiming to be the proprietor of a layout-design may apply for registration under this Act, submitting requisite documentation and the prescribed fee. The application shall clearly delineate the matters relating to the registered layout-design, including its topological characteristics and the semiconductor integrated circuit in which it is embodied. Upon satisfactory examination and confirmation of originality, the Controller shall register the layout-design and issue a certificate of registration. Registration shall confer exclusive rights on the proprietor, subject to the provisions herein. A registered layout-design shall be valid for a period of ten years from the date of filing, or until it enters the public domain, whichever is earlier. The register shall be open for inspection by any person interested in matters relating registered layout-designs, subject to payment of a prescribed fee. Any alteration to a registered layout-design requires notification to the Controller and may be subject to further scrutiny.

Any person being the proprietor of a registered layout-design shall have the right to assign, transfer or otherwise dispose of the same, whether or not coupled with or subject to any condition, restriction or limitation, as provided herein. Such assignment or transfer shall be subject to the recording of the transfer with the Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Registry, and until so recorded, the original proprietor shall continue to be deemed the proprietor for all purposes under this Act. A license, whether exclusive or non-exclusive, may be granted in respect of a registered layout-design, and any such license shall be in writing and shall specify the duration, scope, and territorial limits of the license. Matters relating registered layout-designs, including the terms of any assignment or license, shall be governed by the provisions of this Act and any associated regulations. The proprietor may, subject to the terms of any existing license, grant further licenses in respect of the same layout-design. Failure to comply with the recording requirements shall not invalidate the assignment or license but may affect its enforceability against third parties.

Any person being the proprietor of a registered layout-design shall have the right to assign, or otherwise transfer, all or any of the rights vested in such layout-design, subject to the terms and conditions as may be mutually agreed upon between the parties to such assignment or transfer. Where a registered layout-design is assigned or otherwise transferred, the transferee shall, as provided herein, notify the Controller of such assignment or transfer within such period and in such manner as may be prescribed. Matters relating registered layout-designs, including the licensing of rights therein, shall be governed by the principles of equitable assignment and may include provisions relating to royalty payments, territorial scope, and duration of the license. The use of any marks means trade associated with a layout-design, in the course of licensing or assignment, shall be subject to applicable trademark laws. Failure to comply with the notification requirements outlined herein may render the assignment or transfer unenforceable against third parties.

The form issuing authority, constituted as provided herein, shall maintain a register of layout-designs and shall issue certified copies of entries therein to any person requesting such copies, subject to payment of the prescribed fee. Any request for a certified copy shall be made in writing and shall clearly identify the layout-design in question, including the registration number, if known. The form issuing authority may, if it deems necessary, require the applicant to provide further information to facilitate the identification of the layout-design. Provided that, the authority shall not unreasonably delay or refuse to issue a certified copy, and any refusal shall be accompanied by a statement of reasons. The register maintained shall be open to inspection by the public during office hours, subject to such conditions as may be prescribed. Any person obtaining a certified copy shall treat the information contained therein as confidential.

The Controller of Designs shall, upon receipt of a complete application for registration and verification of the prescribed fee, issue a form issuing acknowledging the application number and date of filing to the applicant, and a further communication shall be dispatched confirming the acceptance or rejection of the layout-design within a period of three months from the date of such receipt, subject to the provisions concerning expedited examination as provided herein. Any request for amendment to the layout-design, after the form issuing, shall be accompanied by a further fee and may be considered at the discretion of the Controller, provided that such amendment does not materially alter the original layout-design. Where the Controller requires further information or clarification, the applicant shall respond within one month from the date of such request, failing which the application may be deemed withdrawn. The Controller shall maintain a digital register of all applications and issued forms.

Any person deriving commercial benefit from a layout-design registered under this Act shall be entitled to an injunction against any act constituting an infringement of their exclusive right, subject to the provisions contained herein. The injunction may extend to restraining the sale, import, or distribution of integrated circuits embodying the infringing layout-design. A registered proprietor may, at any time within a period of three years from the date of knowledge of the infringement, institute civil proceedings for the recovery of damages sustained by reason of the infringement. The court, while determining damages, shall have regard to the actual losses suffered by the registered proprietor, as well as the profits unjustly earned by the infringer. 

The form issuing a license under this Act shall be in writing and shall specify the scope of the license, the royalty payable, and the term of the license. Any dispute regarding the terms of such a license may be referred to arbitration, as agreed upon by the parties, or to the High Court having jurisdiction. Failure to comply with the terms of a registered license shall constitute a breach of contract, giving rise to remedies available under general contract law.

The Controller of Designs shall, upon receipt of a complete application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design, conduct a preliminary examination to ascertain that the application meets the procedural requirements as provided herein. Should the application be found deficient in any material particular, the Controller shall issue a form issuing, specifying the defects and requiring rectification within a period not exceeding thirty days from the date of such issuance. Failure to rectify the defects within the stipulated timeframe shall render the application liable to be treated as abandoned. The Controller may, subject to the payment of a prescribed fee, extend the said period for rectification, provided that a reasonable cause is demonstrated by the applicant. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Controller regarding the issuance of a form issuing may, within sixty days, file an appeal to the Appellate Board. The Appellate Board shall consider such appeals in accordance with the procedures outlined in this Act and may confirm, modify, or reverse the decision of the Controller. All forms issued under this Act shall be deemed to be official communications and shall be served by registered post.

The Registrar shall, upon a determination of completeness and compliance with the prescribed requirements for an application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design, issue a form issuing acknowledging receipt and initiating the examination process. Such form shall clearly state the application number, the date of filing, and the name and address of the applicant. Provided that, if the application is found to be deficient in any material particular, the Registrar may, within thirty days of receipt, issue a communication detailing the deficiencies and requiring rectification within a specified timeframe. Failure to rectify such deficiencies within the stipulated period shall be construed as abandonment of the application, subject to a right of appeal to the Appellate Board as provided herein. Any form issuing related to transfer of rights shall also include details of the transferor and transferee, and evidence of valid consideration, where applicable. The Registrar may maintain a digital record of all forms issued under this Act.

Any person alleging infringement of a registered layout-design shall, prior to the institution of any legal proceedings, serve a notice of such intention upon the alleged infringer, detailing the specific layout-design infringed and the nature of the infringement. The form issuing such notice shall be prescribed by regulations made by the Central Government and must include a clear and unambiguous depiction of the registered layout-design, along with particulars of its registration. Failure to serve a notice in the prescribed form, or to accurately represent the registered layout-design therein, shall be deemed a procedural irregularity and may, subject to the discretion of the court, result in dismissal of the subsequent legal action. Provided that, if the alleged infringer demonstrates willful concealment or deliberate destruction of evidence related to the infringement, this requirement may be waived. Any person found to have knowingly issued a false or misleading form shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees.

Any person possessing a registered layout-design shall, subject to the provisions of this Act, have the right to assign, transfer, or otherwise dispose of the same, whether or not coupled with any other property. An assignment of a registered layout-design shall be in writing and signed by the assignor or duly authorized agent. The form issuing for such assignment shall clearly state the particulars of the layout-design, including the registration number, the date of registration, and the name and address of the assignee. 

Where a layout-design is jointly held, no joint owner shall assign their share without the consent of all other joint owners, and any such assignment not complying with this requirement shall be void. A licensee of a registered layout-design may, with the prior written consent of the registered proprietor, further assign or license their interest in the layout-design, provided that such sub-license or assignment is subject to the terms and conditions of the original license. Failure to comply with these provisions relating to form issuing may render the assignment unenforceable.

Any person aggrieved by an order of the Controller refusing to issue a form issuing certificate, or varying the terms of such a certificate, may, within ninety days from the date of such order, file an appeal to the High Court. Such appeal shall be filed in the manner prescribed and shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the order appealed against, together with the prescribed fee. The High Court, upon consideration of the appeal and subject to such evidence as it may require, shall either confirm, modify, or reverse the decision of the Controller. Provided that no appeal shall lie against an order relating to the rectification of the register unless such order affects the validity of a registered layout-design. Further, the High Court may, at any stage of the proceedings, require the appellant to deposit with the Court a sum sufficient to cover the costs of the respondent, and may, in case of default, dismiss the appeal. Any decision of the High Court under this Act shall be final and binding.

Any person who has filed an application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design shall, upon satisfaction of the conditions as provided herein, be issued a form issuing confirming the particulars of the layout-design as entered in the design register layout. The Controller may, subject to such terms and conditions as may be prescribed, require the applicant to amend the layout-design to ensure compliance with the requirements of this Act. Where a layout-design is registered, the registered owner shall be entitled to the exclusive right to make, use, sell, offer for sale, distribute, and import the layout-design. Any person who infringes this right shall be liable to pay damages to the registered owner, assessed in accordance with the principles of equity and justice. Provided that, the registered owner may also seek an injunction restraining the infringer from further acts of infringement. A request for rectification of the register may be made by any person aggrieved by an incorrect entry, subject to a prescribed fee and procedure.

The Controller of Designs shall, upon receipt of a complete application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design, conduct a preliminary examination to ascertain conformity with the requirements as provided herein. Should the application meet such requirements, the Controller shall issue a form issuing notice of acceptance to the applicant, specifying the date of filing and a provisional registration number. A request for patent addition shall be permissible, provided that such addition does not substantially alter the scope of the original layout-design and is supported by clear and concise documentation detailing the modifications. Any objection raised by the Controller regarding the patent addition shall be communicated to the applicant in writing, affording a period of thirty days for response. Failure to respond within the stipulated timeframe may result in the rejection of the request. The Controller may, subject to the payment of the prescribed fee, grant a certificate of registration once satisfied that all requirements have been duly met and the layout-design is registrable under this Act.

The Controller of Designs shall, upon satisfactory verification of the application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design, issue a form issuing acknowledging the receipt and completeness of the documentation, provided that the applicant has complied with all procedural requirements as detailed in the prescribed rules. Any deficiency in the application shall be communicated to the applicant within thirty days, affording an opportunity for rectification. Where an applicant seeks protection for a layout-design already registered in a convention country through the Madrid Protocol International, a statement of priority and certified copy of the foreign application shall accompany the initial filing. The Controller may, subject to the provisions of this Act, require additional information or clarification regarding the novelty and originality of the layout-design. Failure to respond to such requests within the stipulated timeframe may result in the rejection of the application, unless reasonable cause is demonstrated. All forms issued under this Act shall be deemed public record.

Any person desiring to commercially exploit a registered semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design, or to assign or otherwise transfer rights therein, shall furnish a form issuing notice to the Semiconductor Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Registry. Such notice shall include details of the proposed exploitation, assignment, or transfer, including the identity of all parties concerned and the geographical scope of the arrangement. The Registry shall maintain a publicly accessible record of all such form issuing notices, subject to payment of the prescribed fee. Where the exploitation involves goods bearing a recognized geographical indication, the Registry may, in consultation with the Geographical Indications Registry, verify the authenticity of the indication and its relevance to the layout-design. Failure to comply with the requirements of this provision shall render any subsequent assignment or transfer voidable at the option of the original proprietor, provided that such failure is brought to the notice of the Registry within one year of the exploitation, assignment, or transfer. The Registry may, upon reasonable cause, request additional information to clarify any ambiguity in the form issuing notice.

The registrar shall maintain a register of layout-designs in such form and manner as may be prescribed. Any person claiming to be the proprietor of a layout-design may submit an application for registration to the registrar, accompanied by the prescribed fee and a detailed layout topography. The application shall include the name and address of the applicant, a clear and complete description of the layout-design, and supporting documentation demonstrating its originality. Subject to verification of the application and confirmation that the layout-design meets the requirements as provided herein, the registrar shall register the layout-design and assign a registration number. A registered layout-design shall be valid for a period of ten years from the date of registration, unless cancelled or surrendered. The registrar registration sub-system shall be updated with all relevant details of the layout-design, including the proprietor’s name and any subsequent assignments or licenses.

The registrar shall maintain a register of semiconductor integrated circuits layout-designs, and all applications for registration shall be made in the prescribed manner to the registrar. Any person claiming to be the proprietor of a layout-design may apply for registration, subject to the payment of the applicable fee as provided herein. The application shall include a detailed description of the layout-design, including supporting documentation demonstrating its originality. Upon receipt of a complete application, the registrar shall examine it for compliance with the requirements of this Act. Where the registrar is satisfied that the application meets all criteria, the layout-design shall be registered and an official certificate of registration issued. The registrar registration sub shall be open for public inspection, subject to reasonable restrictions to protect confidential information. Any objection to the registration may be filed with the registrar within the prescribed period.

Any person deriving commercial benefit from an unregistered layout-design, and who knows or has reasonable grounds to know that such layout-design is eligible for registration, shall be liable to account for profits to the registered proprietor, subject to the provisions of this Act. The registrar registration sub-process, when completed in accordance with the prescribed manner, shall create a public record of the layout-design, establishing a clear right in rem. A proprietor may, notwithstanding any other remedy available, apply to the High Court for an injunction restraining any act constituting an infringement of their rights, and may also claim damages for such infringement. Provided that no injunction shall be granted unless the plaintiff satisfies the Court that irreparable harm will be suffered if the injunction is not granted. Any appeal from an order of the High Court relating to such injunction shall lie to the Supreme Court. The registrar shall maintain a record of all appeals and related judgements.

The registrar, upon receipt of an application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design, shall examine the application to ascertain whether it meets the requirements as provided herein. Such examination shall include verification of the applicant’s right to make the application, confirmation of the completeness of the application form, and a preliminary assessment of the novelty and originality of the layout-design. If the registrar is satisfied that the application is in order, a notice of acceptance shall be issued to the applicant, and the layout-design shall be registered subject to payment of the prescribed fee. Any person aggrieved by the registrar’s decision regarding the acceptance or rejection of an application may, within a period of thirty days from the date of such decision, file a petition for review before the registrar. The registrar registration sub-system shall maintain a public register of all registered layout-designs, accessible for inspection during office hours. Provided that, the registrar may, at their discretion, refuse access to confidential information submitted by the applicant.

Any person who falsifies documents presented to the registrar for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design shall be punishable with imprisonment not exceeding three years, or with a fine, or with both. The registrar registration sub-process, if found to be compromised by such falsification, will render any resulting registration null and void ab initio, and subject the applicant to immediate disqualification from future applications for a period of five years. Furthermore, any expert witness knowingly providing false testimony in support of a fraudulent registration claim, as determined by a competent court, shall be liable for a penalty equivalent to the projected commercial value of the falsely registered layout-design, subject to a minimum fine of five lakh rupees. The registrar may, with prior approval of the Central Government, initiate investigations into suspected fraudulent practices and impose interim injunctions to prevent further damage. Any appeal against decisions of the registrar shall lie with the High Court.

Any person possessing a registered layout-design shall have the right to grant licenses to others for the commercial exploitation of such layout-design, subject to the terms and conditions as may be mutually agreed upon between the owner and the licensee. An assignment of any right to a registered layout-design shall be effective only upon registration of the assignment with the registrar, and notice of such assignment shall be furnished to the registrar in the prescribed manner. The registrar registration sub-section mandates a publicly accessible record of all valid assignments, ensuring transparency and preventing disputes regarding ownership. Where a license or assignment is made for a definite period, the registrar shall note the duration within the register. Failure to register an assignment does not invalidate it, but renders it unenforceable against any subsequent bona fide assignee who has duly registered their assignment. The owner of a layout-design may, as provided herein, revoke a license granted for cause, following a procedure established by regulations.

Any person aggrieved by an order of the registrar refusing registration of a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design, or revoking a registration, may file an appeal to the Appellate Board within ninety days from the date of such order. The appeal shall be in such form and be accompanied by such fee as may be prescribed, and shall state the grounds upon which it is based. The Appellate Board may, after giving the respondent an opportunity of being heard, confirm, modify, or reverse the order appealed from, or may remit the case back to the registrar with directions for fresh consideration. Should the registrar’s decision concern a claim of prior art, evidence submitted in support of the layout-design’s originality shall be subject to rigorous examination. Furthermore, a failure by the registrar to issue a reasoned order for refusal or revocation shall render the decision vulnerable to appeal, and the Appellate Board may direct the registrar to provide such reasoning. The registrar registration sub-process is subject to judicial review.

Any person who, with intent to deceive, falsely represents a registered semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design as being their own, or applies such layout-design to any article for the purposes of sale or distribution, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with a fine, or with both. The registrar registration sub-process, if found to have been compromised through fraudulent means in relation to an application for registration involving a layout-design used in the manufacture of a pharmaceutical drug, will trigger an immediate review of all associated registrations. Provided that, the Central Government may, subject to sufficient evidence of systemic abuse, direct the registrar to initiate a special audit of all pending applications. Failure to comply with a directive issued under this Act shall attract a daily penalty of ten thousand rupees until compliance is achieved. Any evidence obtained during such an audit shall be admissible in any subsequent legal proceedings.

Any person being the proprietor of a registered layout-design shall have the right to assign, or otherwise transfer, all or any of the rights vested in such layout-design to any other person, subject to the terms and conditions that may be agreed upon between the parties and recorded with the registrar registration sub. An assignment or transfer of rights shall not be valid unless it is in writing and duly executed by both the assignor and the assignee. Where a registered layout-design is subject to a licensing agreement, the licensee may, with the consent of the proprietor, further assign or license their interest therein, provided that such sub-licensing does not contravene any terms specified in the original license. Any act constituting an infringement of a registered layout-design, or any unauthorized assignment or transfer, shall be actionable under this Act, and the aggrieved party may institute a suit infringement registered before a competent court for appropriate relief, including injunction and damages. The registrar shall maintain a record of all registered assignments and licenses.

Any person deriving commercial benefit from an integrated circuit layout-design shall be entitled to register the same under this Act, provided that such layout-design is original and not previously disclosed to the public, whether in India or elsewhere. The application for registration relating registered layout-design shall be made in the prescribed form and shall be accompanied by the necessary fee as specified in the Schedule. Upon satisfactory verification of the application and confirmation that the layout-design meets the criteria as provided herein, the Controller shall register the layout-design and issue a certificate of registration to the applicant. The register of layout-designs maintained under this Act shall be open for inspection subject to such conditions and payment of fees as may be prescribed. Any assignment or transfer of rights relating registered layout-design shall be subject to the provisions of this Act and must be duly recorded with the Controller. Failure to comply with these requirements may invalidate the registration.

Any person who, without the permission of the registered proprietor, commercially exploits a registered layout-design, or performs any act that constitutes an infringement as provided herein, shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding five lakh rupees for each such infringement. Where the infringement involves repeated offences, the penalty may extend to ten lakh rupees. Any layout-design falsely representing a registered layout-design, or a substantial part thereof, as its own, shall be deemed to be an infringement relating registered to the original layout-design. The court, while determining the amount of damages, shall have due regard to the actual loss suffered by the registered proprietor, and may also consider the profits unlawfully gained by the infringer. Evidence of the sale or distribution of articles bearing the infringing layout-design shall be admissible as prima facie evidence of infringement. Any order of injunction granted under this Act may include an order for delivery up or destruction of infringing articles.

Any person alleging infringement of a registered layout-design shall, prior to initiating proceedings before a competent court, furnish the alleged infringer with a notice of such infringement, detailing the specific layout-design relating registered to the claim and the nature of the alleged act of infringement. Should the alleged infringer, within thirty days of receipt of such notice, submit a statement demonstrating a valid defense, including but not limited to prior art or independent development, the aggrieved party may apply to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board for a determination of the validity of the defense. The Board shall, after affording both parties an opportunity to be heard, issue a reasoned order either upholding or rejecting the defense, and such order shall be binding on the parties subject to further appeal to the High Court. Failure to comply with the notice requirement as provided herein shall render the infringement claim inadmissible, unless the court is satisfied that exceptional circumstances existed justifying such non-compliance.

Any person who commercially exploits a registered layout-design without the authorization of the registered proprietor, or causes another to do so, shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding five lakh rupees for each such infringement, and the goods infringing the layout-design shall be subject to seizure and destruction as determined by a designated officer. Where a producer, despite due diligence, was unaware of the infringement and can prove reasonable grounds for believing the layout-design was not relating registered, the penalty may be reduced at the discretion of the court. However, repeated offenses, or exploitation with intent to deceive, shall attract enhanced penalties up to ten lakh rupees and may also constitute grounds for criminal prosecution. Any appeal against an order imposing a penalty shall be made to the High Court within ninety days of the order’s issuance, subject to the payment of prescribed fees. The burden of proof regarding lawful exploitation rests with the alleged infringer.

Any person alleging infringement of a registered layout-design shall, prior to initiating proceedings before any court, furnish the alleged infringer with a notice of such infringement, detailing the specific layout-design relating registered to the complaint and the nature of the alleged acts of infringement. Provided that, such notice shall be served at least thirty days prior to the commencement of any legal proceedings. Where the alleged infringer, in response to such notice, submits that the layout-design is not novel or is already the subject of an article patented, the aggrieved party may apply to the Appellate Board for a preliminary determination of the validity of the registration. The Appellate Board shall, subject to the provisions of this Act, conduct an expedited hearing and issue its determination within ninety days of the application. Any party aggrieved by the determination of the Appellate Board may prefer an appeal to the High Court. Failure to comply with the notice requirement as provided herein shall be considered a procedural irregularity, curable by the court, but may impact costs awarded.

A layout-design, once registered under this Act, shall be considered a ‘relating registered’ property, conferring upon the registered owner the exclusive right to reproduce, exploit, and commercially benefit from the layout-design. The term ‘relating registered’ extends to any derivative layout-design substantially based upon the original registered layout-design, irrespective of minor modifications not impacting its essential characteristics. To foster innovation and provide financial support for the development of novel semiconductor technologies, a gene fund may be established by the Central Government, utilizing a portion of the registration fees collected under this Act. Contributions to the gene fund shall be allocated towards research and development grants, prioritizing projects focused on indigenous layout-design creation and commercialization, subject to guidelines prescribed by the appropriate authority. Any transfer of rights in a relating registered layout-design shall be documented and filed with the Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Registry.

The proprietor of a trade mark shall, for the purposes of this Act, mean the person or entity registered as the owner of said trade mark and vested with the exclusive right to its use in respect of specified goods or services. Such proprietorship may be held by an individual, a company, a partnership, or other legal entity capable of owning property. A registered trade mark confers upon the proprietor the right to prevent unauthorized use of an identical or deceptively similar mark by another, subject to any limitations or conditions as provided herein. Transfer of the proprietor trade mark shall be effected through assignment, and notice of such assignment must be filed with the Trade Marks Registry. The rights of the proprietor are enforceable through civil remedies, including injunctions and damages, as prescribed under this Act.

The proprietor of a registered trade mark shall, subject to the provisions of this Act, have the right to sue for infringement of the mark in a court of competent jurisdiction. Any assignment of the trade mark, or an interest therein, shall be subject to the registrar’s approval and recorded as provided herein, and notice of such assignment shall be furnished to the Trade Marks Registry within the prescribed period. Where a trade mark is registered in the name of a person who is not the actual proprietor, a disclaimer may be filed with the Registry, outlining the true proprietor’s interest. Failure to accurately reflect the proprietor trade mark during registration or subsequent transfer may render the registration liable to revocation upon application to the Trade Marks Registry. The registered proprietor shall also be entitled to renew the registration of the trade mark for successive periods of ten years, subject to payment of the prescribed renewal fee.

The registered proprietor of a trade mark shall have the right to sue for infringement of the trade mark in any court of competent jurisdiction, notwithstanding any other law for the time being in force. Any suit for infringement shall be subject to such conditions and limitations as may be prescribed, and shall be maintainable only upon proof of actual use of the proprietor trade mark in relation to the goods or services for which it is registered. Where a proprietor proves likelihood of confusion, and the defendant is a competitor engaged in the sale of identical or similar goods or services, an injunction may be granted restraining the defendant from further use of the offending mark. A proprietor may also seek damages for loss suffered as a direct result of the infringement, or an account of profits made by the defendant through the unlawful use of the trade mark, provided that such account shall be subject to verification by the court. Remedies under this Act are cumulative and not alternative.

The proprietor of a trade mark registered under this Act shall have the right to maintain an action for infringement of such trade mark, notwithstanding any other right of action the proprietor may have independently of this Act. Where a registered trade mark is used by a person other than the registered proprietor, and such use constitutes an infringement as provided herein, the proprietor may, at his option, seek an injunction restraining such use. Any contract restraining the use of a trade mark shall be void, except where such restraint is reasonably necessary to protect the goodwill of the proprietor. A registered proprietor may, subject to the provisions of this Act, assign the trade mark and the goodwill of the business carried on under the trade mark in part or whole. Assignment of a trade mark shall be subject to the conditions specified in the register and any applicable rules. Provided that, assignment of a trade mark shall not affect any existing rights or liabilities. The registrar may, upon application, record the assignment of a proprietor trade mark.

Any person who, not being the registered proprietor of a trade mark, uses in the course of trade, or advertises for the purpose of trade, any colour, device, word, name or other designation which is identical with or deceptively similar to a registered proprietor trade mark, shall be liable to a suit for infringement as provided herein. However, honest trade usage, or the adoption of a descriptive term, shall not, subject to proof of likelihood of confusion, constitute infringement. Where a collective mark is registered, use by an authorized member shall not be considered an infringement, provided that such use conforms to the regulations governing the collective mark. Any goods found to bear an infringing mark may be seized and destroyed, and the offender shall be punishable with imprisonment not exceeding three years, or with fine, or with both. The Court may, at its discretion, also award damages to the proprietor of the trade mark.

Any assignment of the right to a proprietor trade mark, or any interest therein, shall be subject to the provisions of this Act regarding the registration of assignments. A license, whether oral or written, may be granted by the proprietor of a trade mark to another party, permitting the use of the trade mark under specified terms and conditions. Such license shall not affect the ownership of the trade mark itself, and the proprietor retains all rights not expressly granted to the licensee. Where a trade mark is assigned with the goodwill of a business, the assignee shall be deemed to be the proprietor of the trade mark, subject to any limitations as provided herein. Any assignment or license not duly recorded with the Trade Marks Registry may not be enforceable against third parties. The proprietor shall furnish the Registry with particulars of every assignment or license within the prescribed period, failing which a penalty may be levied. A registered user, deriving title under a license, shall have the same rights and remedies as the proprietor against any infringement not authorized by the license.

Any person claiming to be the proprietor of a trade mark, whether registered or unregistered, may apply to the High Court for an injunction restraining any person from using a deceptively similar mark, subject to the provisions herein. An application for such injunction shall be accompanied by a statement of use demonstrating bona fide adoption and continuous use of the proprietor trade mark for a period not less than three years prior to the date of the application. However, the Court may, at its discretion, grant an interim injunction pending a full hearing, provided that sufficient cause is shown and adequate security is furnished. Any order made under this Act shall be appealable to the Division Bench of the High Court, and further to the Supreme Court, subject to the usual terms and conditions. The burden of proving non-use or abandonment of the proprietor trade mark shall lie on the defendant.

Any person claiming to be interested in the registration of a geographical indication for goods, being a natural person, firm, association, or body corporate, shall present an application in the prescribed form to the Geographical Indications Registry. The application shall identify the goods in respect of which the registration is sought, and shall clearly define the geographical area within India to which the goods relate, demonstrating a specific quality, reputation, or other characteristics attributable to that geographical origin. A statement detailing the rules governing the use of the geographical indication by producers of the goods shall also be included, and must be consistent with customary practices. Provided that, where the geographical indication also constitutes a trademark, evidence of such prior trademark registration, or a no-objection certificate from the trademark holder, shall accompany the application. The Registrar may, subject to such conditions as may be deemed necessary, require further information or evidence to substantiate the claim regarding the goods geographical indication.

Any registered proprietor of a geographical indication for goods shall have the right to assign, transfer or otherwise dispose of the registration, or any right therein, subject to the conditions as may be prescribed. Any assignment or transfer of a geographical indication shall be subject to prior notification to the Geographical Indications Registry, and shall be effective only upon registration of the transfer with the Registry. Where a geographical indication is assigned, the assignee shall be entitled to all the rights and remedies available to the original proprietor, as provided herein. A license to use a registered geographical indication may be granted by the registered proprietor to any person, subject to such terms and conditions as may be mutually agreed upon and recorded with the Registry. The Registrar may, upon application, revoke a license if it is established that the licensee has failed to adhere to the quality standards associated with the geographical indication, thereby impacting the reputation of the goods geographical indication.

Any person claiming to be the proprietor of a geographical indication, and alleging infringement of such geographical indication as a goods geographical indication, may apply to the Registrar for an order restraining the defendant from manufacturing or selling goods with a false or deceptive indication of origin. The application shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the registration certificate and a detailed statement of the alleged infringement, including particulars of the goods, the manner of infringement, and the likely damage suffered. Provided that, where the defendant claims that the indication is not false or deceptive, but merely a descriptive term, the burden of proving otherwise shall lie upon the applicant. Any order made under this Act shall be subject to appeal to the Appellate Board, and the Board may, after hearing both parties, confirm, modify, or set aside the order of the Registrar. The Appellate Board’s decision shall be final and binding, save for any recourse available under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

A work shall be considered to be published when copies thereof are made available to the public, whether by sale, distribution, public exhibition, or otherwise. For the purposes of this Act, the publish translation of a work, whether literary, dramatic, musical or artistic, requires the prior authorization of the copyright holder, except as otherwise provided herein. However, a translation may be published without such authorization if it is intended solely for internal study or research, and is not disseminated further. Subject to the provisions relating to fair dealing, any unauthorized publish translation constitutes an infringement of copyright and is actionable under this Act. Provided that, the translation accurately reflects the original work and does not introduce any substantial alterations or distortions.

Any author intending to publish a translation of a work, whether literary, dramatic, musical or artistic, shall register such intended publication with the Registrar of Copyrights prior to dissemination to the public. The application for registration of a proposed publish translation shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the original work, a complete and accurate translation thereof, and a declaration affirming the originality of the translation and the applicant’s right to undertake it. Where the original work is subject to existing copyright, the applicant shall demonstrate, subject to verification, that a no-objection certificate has been obtained from the copyright holder or that sufficient time has elapsed as provided herein for independent creation of the translation. Failure to register a publish translation, where registration is required, may render the translation vulnerable to claims of infringement, and shall preclude the applicant from availing certain remedies under this Act. The Registrar may, at their discretion, require additional information or clarification to ensure compliance with these provisions.

Any person intending to publish a translation of a copyrighted work shall, prior to such publication, furnish notice in writing to the copyright holder, specifying the intent to do so and the terms proposed for remuneration. Should the copyright holder, within sixty days of receipt of such notice, decline to grant a license or propose terms deemed unreasonable by the intending publisher, the latter may apply to the High Court for determination of fair and equitable remuneration. The Court, upon hearing both parties, shall determine the royalty payable for the publish translation, considering the nature of the work, the extent of the translation, and prevailing market rates. Provided that, if the copyright holder fails to respond to the notice within the stipulated timeframe, it shall be deemed that they have no objection to the proposed terms. Any dispute regarding the quality of the publish translation, alleging misrepresentation or distortion of the original work, shall be subject to the remedies available under this Act.

Any person desiring to publish a translation of a work in which copyright subsists shall, prior to such publication, submit a notice of intention to the Registrar of Copyrights, detailing the nature of the work, the proposed language of translation, and the intended method of dissemination. Such notice shall be accompanied by a royalty deposit equivalent to five percent of the anticipated retail price of the translated work, held in escrow pending determination of rightful ownership and applicable licensing fees. Where a translation is published without prior notice and royalty deposit, as provided herein, the publisher may be subject to innocently punishable imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years, or a fine, or both. However, such penalty shall not apply if the publisher demonstrates a reasonable belief, supported by documented evidence, that the original work is in the public domain or that valid licensing arrangements are already in place. Assignment of rights to publish translation may be executed only with the express written consent of the copyright holder, and all such assignments shall be registered with the Registrar.

An invention far claimed, for the purposes of determining inventive step under this Act, shall be assessed against the person skilled in the art, being a person possessing ordinary skill in the relevant field, and having access to all prior public knowledge, including knowledge commonly available to such a person. The assessment shall not consider knowledge acquired through confidential experimentation unless such experimentation was publicly known or readily deducible from publicly available information. Provided that, a mere variation of a known art, lacking substantial novelty or demonstrating obviousness to the person skilled in the art, shall not constitute an invention far claimed. Subject to the provisions herein, the burden of demonstrating an inventive step rests with the applicant. Any challenge to the inventive step may be raised during examination or opposition proceedings as provided herein.

Any person claiming an invention far claimed under this Act shall furnish a detailed statement of the matter constituting the invention for which protection is sought, demonstrating a clear and concise disclosure of the best mode contemplated by the inventor for carrying out the invention. The statement shall be accompanied by one or more claims defining the scope of the invention, and each claim shall be supported by matter in the description. Where an invention comprises a process, the description shall clearly explain the steps involved and the parameters necessary for its successful implementation. Provided that, if the invention relates to a microorganism, a deposit of the microorganism with a recognised depository institution shall be considered sufficient disclosure, subject to the provisions herein. Failure to adequately define the invention far claimed, or to provide sufficient supporting detail, may render the application liable to be refused. The Controller may require the applicant to amend the claims to accurately reflect the invention disclosed.

Any person aggrieved by a decision of a District Court relating to the revocation of a patent, or by a decision refusing an application for revocation, may prefer an appeal to the High Court, subject to such terms and conditions as may be prescribed. Where an invention is found to be far claimed, meaning the claims extend beyond the matter for which protection is legitimately sought considering the disclosure in the complete specification, the patentee shall be liable to pay damages to any person who has suffered loss as a result of the erroneous grant. Such damages shall be assessed based on reasonable royalty rates and lost profits demonstrably attributable to the overreach of the patent. Provided that, the Court may, in its discretion, reduce the damages if the patentee proves they acted in good faith and with reasonable diligence in defining the scope of their invention. Any action for infringement based on a patent subsequently found to contain an invention far claimed, shall be stayed pending final determination of damages.

A patent application shall be deemed to contain an invention far claimed where the claims, considered in light of the description and any drawings accompanying the application, extend beyond the matter originally disclosed or reasonably derivable therefrom, and do not satisfy the requirements of novelty and inventive step as provided herein. The Controller may, subject to a reasoned order, require the applicant to amend the claims to accurately reflect the scope of the invention as originally conceived. Should the applicant fail to comply with such requirement, or should the amended claims still demonstrate an invention far claimed, the application may be refused. However, an applicant may demonstrate that a person skilled in the art would have considered the extended claim obvious, thereby mitigating the finding of an invention far claimed. Any evidence presented in support of such demonstration shall be subject to verification by the Controller, and may be considered alongside expert testimony as deemed necessary. A claim extending to a mere aggregation of known elements shall not be considered inventive.

Any person claiming an invention far claimed under this Act shall furnish a detailed statement of the matter constituting the invention for which protection is sought, demonstrating a clear and unambiguous scope of the claimed subject matter. Such a statement shall be accompanied by a reasoned argument establishing that the claimed invention extends beyond the existing state of the art, and does not merely represent a trivial or obvious modification thereof. Where an invention relates to a process, the applicant shall disclose the best mode contemplated by him for carrying out the invention, subject to the proviso that such disclosure does not prejudice national security. Failure to adequately define the invention far claimed, or to substantiate the novelty and inventive step as provided herein, may result in the rejection of the application, or the subsequent revocation of any patent granted. The Controller may require further clarification or supporting evidence to satisfy these requirements.

Any person who knowingly and wilfully asserts a patent claim extending beyond the scope of the invention far claimed in a complete specification, as provided herein, shall be deemed to have committed an act of unfair competition. Such assertion, if proven before a competent authority, may result in a penalty not exceeding five lakh rupees per instance of false claim. Furthermore, any profits unjustly gained through the exploitation of the invention far claimed, exceeding the legitimate bounds of the patented subject matter, shall be recoverable by the aggrieved party, subject to a limitation period of three years from the date of such exploitation. The Controller may, upon receiving credible evidence of such practice, initiate an inquiry and impose a fine equivalent to twice the unjustly gained profits, or imprisonment not exceeding one year, or both. Any attempt to mislead the public regarding the true extent of the patented invention shall also be treated as a violation under this Act.

Any assignment of the right, title, and interest in a patent, whether perfected before or after the grant of the patent, shall be in writing and shall specify the invention far claimed, and shall be executed by or on behalf of both the assignor and the assignee. Where an assignment is made subject to a condition, the assignee may, subject to the terms of the assignment, enforce the patent against third parties. The Controller shall, upon application by either the assignor or the assignee and after giving notice to the other party, record the assignment in the Register of Patents. A license granted under this Act, whether exclusive or non-exclusive, shall be construed as an assignment of rights limited to the scope of the license. Provided that, no assignment of a patent shall be valid unless it is accompanied by a statement of the consideration paid or to be paid for the assignment, and such statement shall be recorded with the Controller. Failure to comply with these provisions may render the assignment unenforceable.

Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Controller refusing to amend a patent, or determining the scope of a claim, may file an appeal to the Appellate Board within a period not exceeding ninety days from the date of the order appealed against, subject to such conditions as may be prescribed. The Appellate Board shall, after giving the applicant and the Controller an opportunity of being heard, confirm, modify, vary or reverse the decision of the Controller. Where the Appellate Board finds that the invention far claimed extends beyond the matter originally disclosed in the specification, it may direct that the patent be amended accordingly, provided that such amendment does not introduce matter foreign to the invention. Furthermore, any claim so amended shall be subject to further examination as provided herein, and the Board may, if satisfied that the amendment substantially alters the invention, require a fresh examination fee to be paid. Failure to comply with the timelines established by the Board may result in dismissal of the appeal.

Any person alleging that an invention far claimed in a patent registered under this Act has been worked without his authorization, may institute a suit for recovery of damages, subject to the provisions contained herein. The suit shall be filed in the District Court having jurisdiction over the place where the infringing act occurred, or where the defendant resides or carries on business. Upon satisfactory proof of infringement registered and resultant damage, the Court may grant an injunction restraining the defendant from further infringement, and award damages not exceeding such sum as it deems reasonable. Provided that, where the defendant proves that the patented invention was not novel or involved an obvious step, or was not duly patented, the Court shall dismiss the suit. Any sum recovered by way of damages shall be distributed amongst the aggrieved parties in proportion to their respective interests. The patentee may, instead of damages, seek an account of profits made by the defendant through the infringing act.

A patent application shall be deemed to involve an invention far claimed where the scope of the claims extends beyond the matter originally disclosed in the complete specification, or lacks support therein, and a person skilled in the relevant art would not, with reasonable effort, be able to derive the full scope of the invention from the specification as filed. However, the Controller may, subject to such conditions as he may deem fit, allow an amendment to the claims to rectify such a deficiency, provided that the amendment does not introduce matter beyond the scope of the original disclosure. Any attempt to broaden the claims to encompass a zb trade mark, not inherently connected to the inventive step, shall be considered an extension beyond the originally disclosed invention and will be subject to rejection. The Controller shall, prior to any such decision, issue a reasoned order outlining the deficiencies and affording the applicant an opportunity to be heard. Failure to adequately address the concerns raised in the order may result in the application being refused.

Any person who knowingly and wilfully asserts a claim to an invention far claimed in a complete specification filed under this Act, and thereby induces another person to undertake an act which would otherwise constitute an infringement of a valid patent, shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding five lakh rupees. The Registrar shall consider all evidence presented regarding the scope of the original claim and the extent to which the asserted claim deviates therefrom, and shall issue a reasoned order detailing the basis for any imposed penalty.
