Where an application is accompanied by a form issuing from an unauthorized source, or is materially deficient in information required as provided herein, the Controller may, notwithstanding any prior notice, reject the application without further consideration. Any appeal against such rejection shall be subject to the payment of a surcharge equivalent to twice the original examination fee. Provided that, if the applicant demonstrates reasonable cause for the initial non-compliance, the Controller may, at their discretion, grant a period of sixty days to rectify the deficiency, subject to payment of a late filing fee. Repeated failure to adhere to the prescribed manner, even after such rectification, will render the application void. All penalties collected under this Act shall be credited to the Consolidated Fund of India.

Any assignment of a patent, or an interest therein, shall be made in writing and shall be executed by or on behalf of the assignor and the assignee, and subject to the provisions of this Act, may be assigned to any person, firm or company. Where an assignment is made to a Bench of persons jointly, the Bench shall be deemed to be a single entity for the purposes of holding and exercising the rights in the patent, and any act done by any member of the Bench, duly authorised, shall bind the Bench as a whole. The application for registration of an assignment shall be in the prescribed manner and shall include the particulars of the assignment, including the date of execution and the consideration paid. Failure to register an assignment shall not invalidate it, but such assignment shall not be enforceable against any person other than the parties thereto or their legal representatives, until so registered. Any dispute regarding the validity of an assignment or the interpretation of the terms thereof, shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the appropriate court.

A patent application shall be deemed to be complete only upon fulfillment of all requirements as provided herein, including the submission of a detailed specification, claims defining the scope of the invention, and any necessary drawings. The Controller of Patents may, subject to such conditions as may be deemed necessary, require an applicant to amend the specification or claims to ensure clarity and compliance with this Act. To register patents, an applicant must demonstrate novelty and non-obviousness of the invention, substantiated by prior art searches. Where an invention is a process, the specification shall clearly define the process with sufficient detail to enable a person skilled in the art to carry it out. Any assignment of a patent shall be in writing and registered with the Patent Office to be effective against third parties.

Any person desiring to register patents for any invention shall submit an application to the Controller of Patents in the prescribed manner, accompanied by a complete specification and necessary drawings, if any, detailing the invention sufficiently for a person skilled in the art to carry it into effect. The application shall also include a statement regarding the corresponding foreign applications, if any, for the same invention, and shall claim the priority date as per the established international convention. A request for examination of the application shall be filed within thirty-six months from the date of filing, subject to payment of the examination fee. Where an invention relates to a biological application, a deposit of the biological material in a recognized depository shall be a prerequisite to registration, provided that such deposit complies with the internationally accepted guidelines. The Controller may, after examination, grant the patent if the invention satisfies the criteria as provided herein.

Any person desiring to register patents for any invention shall submit an application to the Controller of Patents in the prescribed manner, accompanied by a full and clear description of the invention and its operation. The Controller, upon examination and subject to the provisions of this Act, may register the patent if satisfied that the invention is novel, non-obvious, and capable of industrial application. A patentee shall have the exclusive right to prevent others from making, using, selling, or importing the patented invention without their consent, provided that such right shall be subject to licensing terms as determined by the Central Government in the interest of public welfare. Any person aggrieved by a refusal to register a patent, or by any act infringing their registered patent, may apply to the High Court for redressal, and the Court shall have jurisdiction to grant such injunctions or damages as it deems fit. The register of patents maintained by the Controller shall be open to inspection by the public subject to payment of the prescribed fee.

Any person desiring to register patents under this Act shall submit an application to the Controller of Patents in the prescribed manner, accompanied by a provisional or complete specification, and a declaration of inventorship as provided herein. The application shall contain details sufficient to identify the invention and demonstrate its utility, and shall be subject to verification by the Controller. Where a complete specification is not initially filed, a provisional specification may be submitted, requiring a complete specification to follow within a period not exceeding twelve months from the date of the provisional application, failing which the provisional application shall be deemed to be abandoned. 

An applicant may, at the time of filing the application, indicate a priority date, if claiming priority from a convention country, subject to the provisions of the relevant international conventions. The Controller shall, upon examination, determine whether the application meets the requirements of this Act and, if satisfied, shall proceed to register patents accordingly, issuing a patent grant in due course.

Any person desiring to register patents for any invention shall submit an application to the Controller of Patents in the prescribed manner, accompanied by a detailed specification and necessary drawings, if applicable. The application shall disclose the invention in a clear and complete manner sufficient to enable a person skilled in the art to carry it into effect. An applicant may, subject to the provisions of this Act, claim priority from a corresponding application filed in a convention country within twelve months from the date of such application. Where an applicant seeks to register a patent based on a provisional specification, a complete specification shall be filed within twelve months from the date of the provisional specification, failing which the provisional specification shall be deemed to be abandoned. All applications received shall be subject to examination as provided herein, and the Controller may require the applicant to amend the specification or drawings to comply with the requirements of this Act before a patent is granted.

Any person failing to register patents for inventions meeting the criteria as provided herein, within twelve months from the date of the first communication to the public, shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees. Where an application for registration is found to be lacking in essential particulars, the Controller may, subject to the payment of a surcharge of ten thousand rupees, allow a period of one month for rectification. Any false representation made during the process to register patents, including but not limited to claims of novelty or inventive step, shall constitute an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years or with fine, or with both. The Controller may, at any time, initiate an audit of registered patents to ensure compliance with the provisions of this Act. All fees collected pursuant to the registration of patents shall be credited to the Consolidated Fund of India.

Any person desiring to register patents for an invention, being a citizen of or having a domicile in India, or being a citizen of a convention country, shall submit an application to the Controller of Patents in the prescribed manner, accompanied by the requisite fee as provided herein. Assignment of the right to a patent, or an interest therein, shall be evidenced by an instrument in writing, duly executed by the assignor and assignee, and such instrument shall be subject to verification by the Controller. Where a patent is jointly held, any joint patentee may, subject to the provisions contained herein, assign their share of the patent without the consent of the other joint patentees, unless otherwise agreed in writing. A license of a patent, whether exclusive or non-exclusive, shall be in writing and shall specify the terms and conditions of such license, including the duration, scope, and territory. The Controller shall maintain a register of all assignments and licenses of patents, and such register shall be open to inspection by any person upon payment of the prescribed fee. Failure to register an assignment or license shall not invalidate the same, but may affect its enforceability.

Any person desiring to register patents for any invention shall submit an application to the Controller of Patents in the prescribed manner, accompanied by a detailed specification and necessary drawings, if any, demonstrating the inventive step and industrial applicability of the invention. The Controller, upon examination and subject to fulfilling the requirements as provided herein, may grant a patent. However, if it is established that the patent unjustly targets a process legitimately developed by another party, and that continued enforcement would cause irreparable harm, a court of competent jurisdiction may issue an erasure order injunction, directing the patent holder to cease all activities related to the infringing patent and to expunge the relevant claims from the register of patents. Any appeal against such an erasure order injunction shall lie before the Appellate Board. The Controller shall maintain a public register of all patents granted and applications received, accessible for inspection during office hours. Failure to comply with the provisions of this Act may result in the revocation of a granted patent.

Any person desiring to register patents for an invention shall submit an application to the Controller of Patents in the prescribed manner, accompanied by a detailed specification and any necessary drawings. The application shall clearly identify the inventor or inventors and shall include a statement as to their entitlement to claim the invention. Where the applicant is not the sole inventor, a duly executed assignment or authorization from all co-inventors shall be furnished. 

An application for registration shall be examined to ascertain its compliance with the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder. Should the Controller require further information or clarification, the applicant shall respond within a period of sixty days from the date of such request. Furthermore, the application shall not proceed if the claimed invention incorporates a trade mark identity that infringes upon existing registered trade marks, unless adequate justification and consent are provided. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in the rejection of the application.

A denomination variety submitted for registration shall conform to the requirements of this Act and the rules made thereunder, and shall be designated by a denomination which enables ready identification. The applicant shall, at the time of application, furnish a clear and concise description of the proposed variety, including its genealogy, physiological characteristics, and, where applicable, its resistance to biotic and abiotic stresses. Subject to verification by the Plant Variety Protection Authority, a variety exhibiting substantially derived characteristics from an existing registered variety may be considered for registration, provided that the breeder of the existing variety has been duly acknowledged and appropriate benefit sharing arrangements are established as provided herein. Any denomination found to be misleading or likely to cause confusion with existing varieties shall be rejected, and the applicant may be required to propose an alternative. The Authority may, at its discretion, request additional information or evidence to ascertain the distinctiveness, uniformity, and stability of the proposed denomination variety.

The Registrar, upon receipt of an application for registration of a new plant variety, shall conduct a preliminary examination to ascertain compliance with the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder. A variety shall be considered a ‘denomination variety sub’ if it demonstrably possesses characteristics that distinguish it from any other variety whose existence is a matter of common knowledge, or is commercially available, subject to a period of six years from the date of commercialization. Any person claiming breeder’s rights in a denomination variety sub may, following notification by the Registrar of a potentially conflicting variety, submit evidence of prior creation or independent discovery. 

Provided that, if the evidence is deemed insufficient, the Registrar may, after affording the applicant an opportunity of being heard, reject the application. The Registrar may also require a comparative field trial to definitively establish distinctiveness, uniformity, and stability, the cost of which shall be borne by the applicant. All applications and supporting documentation shall be maintained as confidential records, accessible only as provided herein or upon order of a competent court.

A denomination variety sub shall be deemed to be essentially derived if it is not substantially different from the parent variety in terms of characteristics relevant to the plant’s utility and is clearly demonstrable through objective, scientific methods. Compliance with the provisions relating to essentially derived varieties is subject to the establishment of a clear lineage tracing back to the initial variety, as recorded with the Plant Variety Protection Authority. Where a breeder develops or commercially exploits an essentially derived variety without the authorization of the breeder of the parent variety, such activity shall constitute an infringement under this Act. Provided that, a farmer exercising the right to save, sell, share or distribute seeds of a protected variety, and who subsequently develops a variety meeting the criteria of an essentially derived variety, may do so without prior authorization, subject to the payment of royalties as determined by the Authority. Any dispute regarding the determination of ‘essentially derived’ status may be referred to the Plant Variety Protection Appellate Tribunal for adjudication.

Any person who sells, offers for sale, or distributes a variety protected under this Act, shall conspicuously and legibly display the designated denomination variety sub as registered, on all relevant packaging and planting material. Failure to comply with this provision shall constitute an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with a fine which may extend to five lakh rupees, or with both. Provided that, if the offence is committed by a company, every person who, at the time the offence was committed, was in charge of, and responsible for the conduct of the business of the company, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable for the punishment as aforesaid. The Registrar may, subject to such conditions as may be prescribed, authorize a competent authority to inspect premises and seize any material in violation of this provision, and any costs incurred in such seizure shall be recoverable from the offender. Any variety falsely marked with a denomination shall be deemed to be an infringement.

Any person being the breeder of a new denomination variety sub, or his successor, may apply for registration of the said variety in accordance with the provisions of this Act. The application shall be in such form as may be prescribed and shall be accompanied by such fee as may be determined by regulations made under this Act. Where a breeder assigns or transfers the right in a variety to another person, the assignee or transferee shall, within ninety days of such assignment or transfer, notify the Authority in writing of the transfer and furnish such documents as may be required. 

Subject to the provisions contained herein, a license to use or propagate a registered variety may be granted by the breeder to any other person, and such license shall be subject to mutually agreed terms and conditions. The Authority may, in cases where a breeder fails to exploit a registered variety, grant compulsory licenses to interested parties, provided that reasonable compensation is paid to the breeder. Any dispute relating to the terms of a license or the validity of an assignment shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the designated court.

Any person aggrieved by the refusal of the Registrar to register a denomination variety sub, or by any decision concerning the scope of the breeder’s or farmer’s rights relating to such variety, may file an appeal before the Appellate Board. Such appeal shall be presented within ninety days from the date of the order appealed against, accompanied by a certified copy of the order and a statement of the grounds on which the appeal is based. The Appellate Board may, at any stage of the proceedings, require the appellant to deposit a sum sufficient to cover the costs of the respondent, and may dismiss the appeal if such deposit is not made within the time specified. Provided that, where the appeal relates to a claim of essentially derived variety, the Board shall consider evidence of phenotypic and genotypic characteristics demonstrating substantial derivation. The Appellate Board’s decision shall be final and binding, subject to the right of appeal to the Supreme Court as provided herein. Any delay in filing an appeal may be condoned if sufficient cause is shown.

Any person desirous of obtaining a breeder’s or farmer’s right in a new denomination variety shall submit an application to the Plant Variety Protection Authority in the prescribed manner, accompanied by the requisite fee. The application shall clearly delineate the characteristics of the said variety, demonstrating its distinctiveness, uniformity, and stability, and shall include a sample of the propagating material. The Authority, upon examination, may require the applicant to furnish further information or evidence as deemed necessary. Where the application pertains to a denomination variety sub, the applicant shall also provide evidence of the variety’s origin and the identity of the breeder. The Chairperson, or an officer duly authorized, may conduct inspections and field trials to verify the claims made in the application. Rights granted under this Act shall be subject to the provisions relating to licensing and assignment, ensuring fair access and benefit sharing, and may be transferred by way of inheritance or testamentary succession. Any assignment of breeder’s rights shall be registered with the Authority to be effective against third parties.

A denomination variety shall be considered a distinctly identifiable plant variety, subject to the provisions contained herein, and shall be eligible for registration under this Act, provided that such variety demonstrates substantial novelty, distinctiveness, uniformity, and stability in its characteristics. The applicant seeking registration of a denomination variety may submit evidence of its genetic purity and phenotypic stability, as demonstrated through field trials conducted in accordance with guidelines established by the Plant Varieties Protection Authority. A variety derived from a denomination variety, and possessing substantially similar characteristics, may be considered an essentially derived variety, subject to a determination of dependency and retention of the essential characteristics of the parent denomination variety. The Authority may, however, refuse registration if the denomination variety lacks sufficient distinctiveness from commonly known varieties.

A denomination variety, for the purposes of registration under this Act, shall be deemed to be a new variety if it satisfies the criteria of distinctiveness, uniformity, and stability as determined by the Plant Variety Protection Authority. The applicant seeking registration of a denomination variety may submit evidence of its characteristics, including morphological, physiological, and molecular markers, to substantiate its novelty. Provided that, a denomination variety derived from an essentially derived variety, as defined herein, shall not be eligible for registration unless the breeder of the original variety consents in writing. The Authority may, subject to such terms and conditions as it deems fit, permit the use of a denomination variety for research purposes. Any person alleging infringement of a registered denomination variety shall have recourse to the remedies provided under this Act, including injunction and damages. The register of denomination varieties maintained by the Authority shall be open for inspection during office hours.

A breeder who has developed a new denomination variety shall be entitled to registration, subject to the provisions of this Act, if such variety conforms to the essential characteristics as prescribed and is duly registered with the Plant Variety Protection Authority. Any farmer who has bred or developed a new denomination variety, or a descendant thereof, may, as provided herein, apply for registration, notwithstanding any rights accruing to the initial breeder, provided that such farmer can demonstrate substantial contribution to the development of the said variety. Where a registered variety is found to be essentially derived from an existing variety, the breeder of the existing variety shall have the right to equitable compensation from the breeder of the essentially derived variety. The Authority may, upon application and subject to verification, grant a license to a registered breeder to utilize a protected denomination variety for research purposes, and any commercialization arising from such research shall be subject to a royalty agreement negotiated between the parties. Any dispute regarding the entitlement to benefit sharing or compensation shall be adjudicated by the designated tribunal.

A denomination variety, for the purposes of registration under this Act, shall demonstrate substantial novelty, distinctiveness, uniformity, and stability in accordance with the prescribed guidelines. Any applicant seeking registration of a denomination variety must submit a detailed description of the variety’s characteristics, including its genealogy, physiological traits, and performance data, as evidenced by field trials conducted over a period not less than three successive generations. Provided that, where the denomination variety is a hybrid or a clone, the requirement of three generations may be waived subject to the competent authority being satisfied with the demonstrated stability of the variety. The variety shall be designated by a denomination that is clearly distinguishable from all other registered varieties, and the proposed denomination must not mislead or cause confusion. Any transfer of rights relating to a denomination variety shall be subject to notification to the Plant Variety Protection Authority and compliance with the conditions stipulated herein. Failure to comply with these provisions may result in the revocation of registration.

Any person being the breeder of, or having a right to exploit a new denomination variety, may apply for registration of the said variety to the Plant Variety Protection Authority in the prescribed manner, subject to payment of the requisite fee as provided herein. The application shall include a detailed description of the denomination variety, demonstrating its distinctiveness, uniformity and stability, and shall be accompanied by the results of such trials as are necessary to establish these characteristics. A licensee of a breeder may, with the breeder’s written consent, apply for the assignment of the breeder’s rights, provided that such assignment does not prejudice the breeder’s right to receive royalties or other consideration. Where a denomination variety is jointly bred, the application for registration may be made by any or all of the breeders, and the rights conferred by registration shall be jointly held unless otherwise agreed in writing. Any transfer of rights relating to a denomination variety shall be subject to the provisions of this Act and shall be registered with the Plant Variety Protection Authority.

A denomination variety shall be considered essentially derived if it is not substantially derived from the initial variety but retains the principal characteristics thereof, subject to the provisions herein. The breeder of the initial variety shall be deemed to have the right to exploit the essentially derived variety, or to authorize another person to do so, in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Provided that, where the essentially derived variety is itself a denomination variety, the holder of the breeder’s right in the essentially derived variety may exploit it, subject to a reasonable royalty payable to the breeder of the initial variety. Security india relates to the maintenance of a publicly accessible database of all registered plant varieties, ensuring transparency and facilitating benefit sharing as provided herein, and this database shall be updated annually. Any dispute regarding derivation shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the Plant Variety Protection Authority.

The term “Patent Cooperation Treaty” shall mean the agreement concluded at Washington on the nineteenth day of June, nineteen seventy, as amended and modified by any subsequent Assembly of the Contracting States, and any regulations made thereunder. A national phase application, as provided herein, constitutes the entry of an international application into the national phase before the Indian Patent Office, subject to the provisions of this Act and the regulations made thereunder. The applicant shall furnish a translation of the international application, if not originally filed in an official language of India, and shall comply with all requirements relating to fees and other formalities. Failure to do so may result in the application being deemed withdrawn. The Controller of Patents may, notwithstanding anything contained herein, require additional information or documentation to facilitate examination.

Any application for a patent, claiming priority from a national filing date, may, subject to the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder, designate India as a designated or elected State for the purposes of the Patent Cooperation Treaty. An applicant intending to avail benefits under the Patent Cooperation Treaty shall file an international application in the prescribed form with the International Bureau of the World Intellectual Property Organization, and shall comply with all requirements stipulated therein. The Controller of Patents shall, upon receipt of the international search report and the written opinion of the International Searching Authority, conduct a further examination as provided herein, to determine the patentability of the invention. Where the international application proceeds to the national phase before this office, the applicant shall furnish a translation of the international application, if not originally filed in an accepted language. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in the application being deemed withdrawn.

Any applicant filing a complete specification under this Act, intending to seek protection in Convention countries or under the Patent Cooperation Treaty, shall, within the prescribed period, furnish a declaration of priority as provided herein, stating the country of first filing and the date of such filing. Failure to submit such a declaration, or a declaration containing materially false information, may be considered grounds for rejection of the application, subject to a reasonable opportunity to rectify the deficiency. Where an international application has been filed under the Patent Cooperation Treaty, the applicant may, upon receiving the international preliminary examination report, request the Controller to proceed with national phase examination. The Controller, upon such request and payment of the prescribed fees, shall examine the application as if it were a complete application filed directly under this Act. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Controller relating to a Patent Cooperation Treaty application, including refusal of national phase entry, may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board, in accordance with the established procedures.

Any application for a patent, claiming priority from a national filing date, may, subject to the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder, be converted into an international application under the Patent Cooperation Treaty, provided that such conversion is effected within the prescribed period as stipulated by the Treaty. The Controller of Patents shall, upon receipt of a request for such conversion accompanied by the necessary fee, examine the application to ensure compliance with the requirements of both this Act and the Patent Cooperation Treaty. Where an applicant seeks to designate India as an elected State or designated Office within the framework of the Patent Cooperation Treaty, such designation shall be deemed valid subject to the payment of the requisite fees and fulfillment of all procedural requirements as prescribed. The international searching authority’s report and the international preliminary examination report, if any, shall be considered during the examination of the corresponding national phase application filed under this Act. Any objection relating to the international search report or preliminary examination report shall be addressed in accordance with the established procedures for examination of patent applications.

Any application for a patent claiming priority from a national filing date under the Patent Cooperation Treaty shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the priority document, duly translated into English or Hindi if the original document is not in either of those languages. The applicant shall, within the prescribed period, furnish the patent office with a demand for international preliminary examination, indicating compliance with all requirements of the designated International Searching Authority and the International Preliminary Examining Authority. Provided that failure to submit the demand within the stipulated timeframe may result in the application being deemed withdrawn, subject to the applicant demonstrating sufficient cause for the delay. An applicant intending to proceed with national phase entry, as provided herein, shall file the required translation and fee within thirty months from the priority date. Compliance with the provisions of the Patent Cooperation Treaty, including the payment of international fees, is a condition precedent to the grant of a patent based on an international application.

Any Indian national or resident, intending to seek protection for an invention in a designated contracting state under the Patent Cooperation Treaty, shall file an international application in the prescribed manner with this Office, subject to the provisions of this Act and the regulations framed thereunder. Failure to comply with the requirements relating to the form, content, or timelines for such international applications shall render the application liable to be rejected, and the applicant may be subject to a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees. Where an applicant knowingly provides false or misleading information in connection with an application filed under the Patent Cooperation Treaty, they shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. The Controller of Patents may, however, waive penalties in cases of demonstrable hardship, provided that sufficient cause is shown. Any appeal against a decision of the Controller regarding such penalties shall lie before the High Court.

Any application for a patent, claiming priority from a national filing date but designating India as a country for which protection is sought under the Patent Cooperation Treaty, shall be processed in accordance with the regulations prescribed herein and the provisions of the said Treaty. An applicant intending to assign or license any right, title, interest or obligation arising from such an international application, including any priority claim, shall furnish a written instrument of assignment or license to the Controller, subject to verification of its authenticity and enforceability. Where the assignment or license relates to a pending application under the Patent Cooperation Treaty, the Controller may, at the request of the assignee or licensee, record the transfer of rights in the international register maintained for that purpose. Provided that, such recordal shall not prejudice the rights of any third party validly claiming from the original applicant. Any dispute concerning the validity of such assignment or license shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the High Court having local jurisdiction.

Any application claiming priority from a national filing date under the Patent Cooperation Treaty shall be subject to the provisions of this Act relating to priority dates, provided that the applicant furnishes a certified copy of the priority document within the prescribed period as stipulated by the International Bureau of the World Intellectual Property Organization. Should a dispute arise regarding the authenticity or validity of such a certified copy, the Controller of Patents may, after affording the applicant an opportunity of being heard, require additional evidence or seek clarification from the designating office. An appeal from any decision of the Controller concerning the acceptance or rejection of priority claims under the Patent Cooperation Treaty shall lie before the Appellate Board, subject to payment of the prescribed fee and compliance with procedural requirements as herein provided. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in the dismissal of the appeal. The Controller shall maintain a register of all applications claiming PCT priority.

The Patent Cooperation Treaty, hereinafter referred to as the PCT, is a multilateral treaty concluded under the auspices of the World Intellectual Property Organization, providing a unified procedure for filing patent applications simultaneously in numerous countries. An applicant seeking protection in multiple designated states may file a single international application, which undergoes a preliminary examination and international search. Subject to fulfilling requirements as provided herein, a designated office shall, upon request and payment of requisite fees, grant a national or regional patent based on the international application. Registration of the international application with the receiving office is a condition precedent to commencing the PCT process. The international bureau maintains the central database for all applications filed under the treaty, facilitating access and transparency. Any person may access this database, subject to prescribed regulations.

Any application claiming priority from a national filing date under the Patent Cooperation Treaty shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the priority document, duly translated into English if the original document is not in English, and shall meet the requirements as to form and content as prescribed in the International Bureau regulations. The Controller of Patents may, subject to such terms and conditions as may be prescribed, accept a later filed priority document if sufficient cause is shown, provided that a penalty fee is submitted. Any person claiming rights based on a certification trade mark registered in a convention country, and seeking a patent in India, shall disclose such registration details within the application. Failure to provide accurate information regarding the priority claim or certification trade mark may render the application liable to be rejected as provided herein. All documents submitted shall be deemed official records.

Any applicant seeking a patent for an invention derived from biological material accessed from a biodiversity-rich country shall, as provided herein, demonstrate compliance with relevant access and benefit-sharing regulations of that country. Where such material originates from indigenous knowledge or traditional practices, the applicant shall furnish evidence of prior informed consent obtained from the concerned communities, and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the commercialization of the invention. An international application filed under the Patent Cooperation Treaty shall be subject to a search report assessing the novelty and inventive step of the claimed invention, with particular regard to prior art reflecting such indigenous knowledge. The Controller of Patents may, subject to established procedures, require the applicant to disclose the origin of the biological material and the terms of access. Failure to comply with these provisions shall render the patent voidable, and may attract remedies including revocation of the patent and claims for damages, as determined by a competent authority. Any funds received through benefit-sharing arrangements relating to such inventions shall be contributed to a designated sources gene fund for conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity.

Any application seeking a patent, where the applicant intends to rely upon a priority claim based on a first application filed under the Patent Cooperation Treaty, shall adhere to the timelines prescribed within this Act for furnishing the necessary priority documents. Failure to submit a certified copy of the priority document, translated into the language of the proceeding if necessary, within the stipulated sixteen months from the priority date, shall result in the abandonment of the claim. For registration claims purposes, a declaration of authenticity and a statement confirming the applicant’s right to claim priority based on the international application are mandatory. Provided that, the Controller of Patents may, subject to justifiable cause, extend the time for submission by a maximum of three months, attracting a prescribed penalty. All applications referencing the Patent Cooperation Treaty must clearly indicate the international application number and filing date. Compliance with these provisions is essential for maintaining the validity of any resulting patent.

A provisional specification may be filed with an application for a patent, subject to the conditions as provided herein, and shall describe the invention to a reasonably skilled person in the relevant art. The provisional specification does not require any claims, but must fully and particularly describe the invention and its method of manufacture, and the scope of the invention must be clear. A complete specification, satisfying all requirements under this Act, shall be filed within twelve months from the date of filing of the provisional specification; provided that, an extension of this period may be granted by the Controller, not exceeding three months, upon a request made before the expiry of the initial twelve-month period and subject to payment of the prescribed fee. Failure to file a complete specification within the stipulated or extended period shall result in the application being deemed withdrawn.

A provisional specification, filed under this Act, shall be treated as a document establishing an early filing date for an invention, subject to the subsequent filing of a complete specification as provided herein. The provisional specification need not conform to the formal requirements prescribed for a complete specification, but must adequately describe the invention to allow a person skilled in the art to understand its nature. An applicant desiring to claim priority based on an earlier application in a convention country may, within the prescribed period, file a complete specification claiming priority, referencing the provisional specification as the basis for the claim. Failure to file a complete specification within twelve months from the filing of the provisional specification will result in the application being deemed abandoned, unless an extension of time is granted by the Controller of Patents, and any such extension shall be subject to applicable fees and conditions. The complete specification shall fully and particularly describe the invention, including the best method known to the applicant for carrying out the invention.

A person desiring to obtain a patent shall, subject to the provisions of this Act, file an application with the Controller of Patents, and such application may be accompanied by a provisional specification. The provisional specification shall describe the invention to the best of the applicant’s knowledge and shall not exceed the prescribed length, serving as a basis for a complete specification to be filed later. Any communication regarding the provisional specification, including any request for examination, shall be addressed to the Controller. Should a complete specification not be filed within twelve months from the date of filing the provisional specification, the application shall be deemed withdrawn, unless an extension of time is granted by the Controller upon demonstrating sufficient cause. A request for extension shall be accompanied by the prescribed fee. The applicant retains the right to amend the complete specification, provided that such amendment does not introduce matter extending beyond the scope of the provisional specification. Failure to adhere to these requirements may result in a loss of priority.

A provisional specification, submitted under this Act, shall be treated as a document establishing an early filing date for an invention, subject to the subsequent filing of a complete specification as provided herein. The provisional specification need not contain claims, but must adequately describe the invention to allow a person skilled in the relevant art to understand its nature. An applicant may, at the time of filing the complete specification, amend the provisional specification to correct any obvious errors or omissions, provided that such amendment does not introduce matter extending beyond the content initially disclosed. Where a complete specification is filed claiming priority from a provisional specification, the Controller shall examine whether the complete specification adequately supports the claims made and is based upon the disclosure contained within the provisional specification. Failure to demonstrate such support may result in objections being raised during the examination process. The provisional specification shall be maintained confidentially until the complete specification is filed or until fifteen months have elapsed from the date of filing, whichever occurs first.

A provisional specification submitted under this Act shall be treated as a document establishing an early filing date for an invention, subject to the subsequent filing of a complete specification as provided herein. The provisional specification must describe the invention with sufficient detail to allow a person skilled in the relevant art to understand the concept and its potential application. Any disclosure within the provisional specification relating to a best mode contemplated by the inventor shall not be a condition for validity, but must be consistent with the overall description. A request for examination, accompanied by the complete specification, shall be filed within the time prescribed, failing which the provisional application shall lapse. Where a complete specification is filed claiming priority from a provisional specification, the complete specification must adequately support the claims made and disclose all information material to the invention as it existed on the date of filing of the provisional specification.

Any person claiming to be the inventor of an invention may present a provisional specification at the Patent Office, subject to the payment of the prescribed fee, and such provisional specification shall relate to the invention and shall be filed with a declaration stating that a complete specification will be filed within twelve months. Failure to file a complete specification satisfying the requirements as provided herein within the stipulated period shall render the provisional specification void, and the application shall be deemed to be withdrawn without prejudice to any penalty applicable under this Act. Should the complete specification differ substantially from the provisional specification in terms of the claimed invention, the Controller may, after notice to the applicant, require amendment or consider the application abandoned. Any false representation in the declaration accompanying the provisional specification shall be punishable with imprisonment and a fine, as determined by the Controller.

Any assignment of the right to apply for a patent based upon a provisional specification shall be executed in writing and shall clearly identify the provisional specification to which it relates, including the application number and date of filing. A licensee acquiring rights under such an assignment shall be subject to the same terms and conditions as the assignor, unless otherwise agreed in writing and recorded with the appropriate office. Where a provisional specification discloses an invention which is subsequently found to lack novelty or involve an obvious step, any assignment made prior to the determination of such lack of novelty or obviousness shall not be invalidated, provided that the assignee was not a party to the initial concealment of material facts. The assignee may, subject to the provisions of this Act, proceed with filing a complete specification based on the provisional specification, or may elect to terminate the assignment and seek a refund of any consideration paid. Failure to file a complete specification within the prescribed period following a valid assignment shall, however, render the assignment null and void.

A provisional specification, filed under this Act, shall not confer any right to a patent unless it is followed by a complete specification fulfilling the requirements as provided herein. Should a dispute arise concerning the enablement of the invention disclosed in a provisional specification, the Controller may, subject to a reasoned application by any interested party, require the applicant to demonstrate a prima facie case of sufficient disclosure to a person skilled in the art. An appeal from any decision of the Controller regarding such demonstration shall lie to the Appellate Board, provided that the appellant deposits the prescribed fee and furnishes security for the payment of costs. Furthermore, any amendment to the provisional specification after filing, intending to broaden the scope of the invention, may be rejected unless the applicant demonstrates that such amendment was reasonably and directly supported by the original disclosure. Failure to comply with these provisions shall render the application liable to be refused.

A provisional specification may be filed with an application for a patent, subject to the conditions as provided herein, and shall serve as a basis for claiming priority in a complete specification to be filed subsequently. The provisional specification need not conform to the formal requirements of a complete specification, but must adequately describe the invention. Registration shall be effected only upon the filing of a complete specification claiming the benefit of the provisional specification. Where a complete specification is not filed within twelve months from the date of filing the provisional specification, the application shall be deemed withdrawn, unless an extension of time is granted by the Controller of Patents. Any amendment to the provisional specification shall be permitted only before the filing of the complete specification, and such amendment shall not extend beyond the scope of the original disclosure.

An application for a patent, not being a convention application or an application filed under the Patent Cooperation Treaty designating India, may be initially filed with an accompanied provisional specification, serving as a basis for a later complete specification. The accompanied provisional specification shall, at a minimum, disclose the concept of the invention in a manner sufficient to reasonably convey to a person skilled in the art the nature of the invention. A complete specification, detailing the invention fully and clearly, shall be filed within twelve months from the date of filing of the application containing the accompanied provisional specification. Failure to file the complete specification within the stipulated period, subject to the provisions for extension as provided herein, shall result in the application being deemed abandoned. The controller may, however, require amendments to either specification to ensure clarity and compliance with this Act.

Any application for a patent claiming priority from a previously filed application in a convention country, or under the Patent Cooperation Treaty designating India, shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the priority document, duly translated into English if necessary, as provided herein. Where an application is accompanied by an accompanied provisional specification, the applicant shall file a complete specification, satisfying the requirements of this Act, within a period of twelve months from the date of filing the provisional specification. Failure to submit the complete specification within the stipulated timeframe shall result in the provisional application being deemed withdrawn, subject to the Controller’s discretion to allow a further period not exceeding three months upon sufficient cause shown. The complete specification shall fully and particularly describe the invention, and shall be accompanied by any drawings necessary for its understanding. Any amendment to the complete specification shall be subject to the provisions of this Act regarding amendments.

Any person filing an application for a patent shall, where such application is accompanied by an accompanied provisional specification, ensure that a complete specification satisfying the requirements of this Act is filed within a period of twelve months from the date of filing of the said application. Failure to file the complete specification within the stipulated timeframe shall result in the application being deemed abandoned as provided herein. However, the Controller may, subject to justifiable cause being demonstrated by the applicant and upon payment of a prescribed fee, allow an extension of this period not exceeding three months. Should the complete specification reveal a lack of inventive step compared to the matter disclosed in the accompanied provisional specification, the patent application may be subject to revocation proceedings initiated by any person aggrieved. The rights to a patent shall vest with the applicant upon grant, and any infringement of such patent shall be actionable under this Act.

Where an application for a patent is accompanied by an accompanied provisional specification as provided herein, the applicant shall ensure that such provisional specification describes the invention in a manner sufficiently clear to enable a person skilled in the relevant art to understand the scope and nature of the invention. The Controller may, subject to such conditions as may be deemed necessary, extend the time for filing the complete specification if sufficient cause is shown, not exceeding a period of three months. However, any extension granted shall not exceed a total of fifteen months from the date of filing the provisional specification. 

A request for extension, accompanied by the prescribed fee, shall be filed before the expiry of the initial twelve-month period. Failure to file a complete specification within the stipulated time, or the extended time if granted, shall result in the application being deemed withdrawn, unless the Controller, considering the circumstances, directs otherwise. The Controller’s decision regarding withdrawal shall be final and binding.

Any application for a patent claiming an invention which is not a complete invention at the time of filing shall be accompanied by an accompanied provisional specification describing the invention and its underlying principles. The provisional specification shall be in Form 2 and shall disclose the invention sufficiently for a person skilled in the art to understand its scope and potential application. An applicant intending to rely upon a priority date associated with a foreign application shall ensure that the accompanied provisional specification adequately supports that claimed priority. Failure to file a complete specification referencing and building upon the accompanied provisional specification within twelve months of the provisional filing date will result in the application being treated as withdrawn, subject to the Controller’s discretion to allow a further period not exceeding three months upon demonstrating reasonable cause. The complete specification must fully and particularly describe the invention, including any best method known to the applicant for carrying it out, as provided herein.

Any person filing an application for a patent, accompanied by an accompanied provisional specification, shall ensure that such specification describes the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for a person skilled in the art to carry it into effect. Failure to do so shall render the provisional specification invalid, and the application subject to immediate rejection as provided herein. Where a complete specification is subsequently filed claiming matter extending beyond that disclosed in the accompanied provisional specification, such matter shall be considered novel only from the date of filing of the complete specification. Any false representation regarding the scope of the invention in the accompanied provisional specification, made with intent to deceive, may attract a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees. The Controller shall have the power to impose such penalty, and any appeal against such imposition lies with the Appellate Board, subject to the conditions prescribed.

Any assignment of the right to an accompanied provisional specification, or of a patent obtained pursuant thereto, shall be in writing and shall specify the terms and conditions governing such assignment, including but not limited to the territory, duration, and scope of the assigned rights. An assignee of such a right may, subject to the provisions of this Act, further assign the same to another person. Where an accompanied provisional specification relates to a patentable subject matter but lacks clarity regarding the inventive step, the Controller may, prior to acceptance, require the applicant to amend the specification to adequately demonstrate such step. Failure to comply with this requirement within a period of sixty days from the date of such requirement shall render the application liable to be refused. Any licensing agreement pertaining to rights derived from an accompanied provisional specification shall be registered with the appropriate authority as provided herein, and failure to do so may invalidate the license.

Where an application for a patent is accompanied by an accompanied provisional specification, the Controller shall, subject to the provisions herein, examine said specification for compliance with the requirements of this Act regarding disclosure and clarity of the invention. Should an objection arise concerning the enablement of the invention as disclosed in the provisional specification, the applicant may, within a period not exceeding three months from the date of the objection, file a reasoned argument demonstrating sufficient disclosure for a person skilled in the art to carry out the invention. Failure to submit such argument, or submission of an argument deemed insufficient by the Controller, shall constitute grounds for refusal of the patent application, unless the applicant successfully appeals to the Appellate Board. Any appeal lodged shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the Controller’s objection and the applicant’s initial response, and the Board’s decision shall be final, subject to the remedies available under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

Where an application for a patent, not being a convention application or an application filed under the Patent Cooperation Treaty designating India, is accompanied by an accompanied provisional specification, the applicant shall file a complete specification in the manner as provided herein, satisfying all requirements for a complete and clear disclosure of the invention. Should the complete specification not be filed within twelve months from the date of filing the provisional specification, the application shall be deemed to be abandoned, unless an extension of time is granted by the Controller of Patents, subject to justifiable cause. In the event of a user party proceeding initiated concerning the claimed invention, the Controller may, at their discretion, require further evidence relating to the accompanied provisional specification to ascertain the scope and validity of the initial disclosure. Any incomplete specification filed shall not be considered for grant of patent.

A business india application, seeking registration of a trade mark under this Act, shall be presented to the Trade Marks Registry in the manner as prescribed. Such application shall include a representation of the trade mark, a list of goods or services to which it relates, and the applicant’s description of business. Where the applicant claims colour as a feature of the trade mark, a clear statement to that effect, along with a colour chart or reference, shall accompany the application. The application may be made electronically, subject to the regulations framed by the Central Government. An affidavit confirming ownership and lawful use of the mark, or a bona fide intention to use it, may be required as part of the examination process, provided that failure to submit such affidavit shall not *ipso facto* invalidate the application but may result in delays.

Any applicant seeking registration of a trade mark incorporating the designation “Business India” shall submit a statement detailing the specific goods or services for which the mark is intended to be used, and shall demonstrate bona fide intention to use the mark in relation to those goods or services. An application for a business india application shall be subject to a heightened standard of scrutiny, particularly where the goods or services relate to financial services, investment advisory, or business consultancy. The Registrar may, at his discretion, require evidence of prior use or a clear and detailed business plan outlining the intended commercial exploitation of the mark. Provided that, a mere intention to adopt the mark is insufficient; the applicant must also demonstrate that the use of the mark will not be deceptive or misleading to the public, nor will it infringe upon any existing registered trade marks or cause undue prejudice to any prior rights holder, as provided herein. Failure to satisfy these requirements may result in the rejection of the application.

Any person aggrieved by the refusal of a business india application, or by any condition imposed in relation to the registration of a trade mark, may file a written appeal to the Appellate Board within a period of ninety days from the date of the order appealed against, subject to the payment of such fee as may be prescribed. The Appellate Board shall, after giving the applicant and the Registrar an opportunity of being heard, and after considering the evidence adduced before it, pass such order as it deems fit, confirming, modifying, or reversing the decision of the Registrar. Where an appeal relates to a matter involving a geographical indication, the Appellate Board shall consist of not less than one member possessing expertise in that area. A party dissatisfied with the decision of the Appellate Board may, with the leave of the High Court, prefer an appeal to the High Court, provided that such appeal shall be filed within sixty days of the Appellate Board’s order. The High Court’s decision shall be final and binding, subject to any further appeal permissible under the law.

Any person intending to apply for registration of a trade mark incorporating a representation of the words “Business India” or any deceptively similar variation thereof, shall, prior to the filing of an application under this Act, submit a declaration affirming diligent use of the mark in relation to financial, investment, or business consultancy services. The Registrar may, subject to verification of the declaration and supporting evidence of such use, proceed to examine the application according to the usual procedure. However, an application for a business india application shall be subject to enhanced scrutiny regarding potential conflict with existing registered trade marks in Class 36, and related classes, concerning financial services. Provided that, if the applicant demonstrates a period of continuous use exceeding five years prior to the application date, and provides audited statements confirming substantial revenue generated through the use of the mark, the Registrar shall expedite the examination process. Failure to comply with the requirements as provided herein may result in the rejection of the application. The Registrar reserves the right to request further information or clarification from the applicant at any stage of the process.

Any application for registration of a trade mark incorporating the words “Business India” or substantially similar variations thereof, shall be subject to enhanced scrutiny as provided herein. The Registrar may, prior to acceptance of such a business india application, require the applicant to submit evidence demonstrating lawful use and distinctiveness, beyond the standard requirements under this Act. Failure to provide satisfactory evidence within a period of sixty days from the date of such request shall be deemed grounds for rejection of the application. Any person found to have knowingly submitted a false or misleading business india application shall be liable to a fine not exceeding five lakh rupees. Furthermore, the Registrar may, in cases of repeated or egregious violations, issue a cease and desist order prohibiting the applicant from submitting further applications for a period of two years. All decisions regarding such applications shall be subject to appeal to the Appellate Board.

Any person being the proprietor of a registered trade mark, desiring to grant a license to another party for the use of said mark in relation to specified goods or services, shall execute an instrument of licensing in writing, detailing the scope of permitted use, geographical territory, and duration of the license. Where a business india application is made seeking assignment of the trade mark, the transferor shall, subject to the provisions of this Act, clearly delineate all existing licenses granted prior to the proposed assignment, including particulars of the licensees, royalty rates, and any conditions attached thereto. The assignee shall be deemed to be bound by the terms of such pre-existing licenses unless expressly agreed otherwise in writing by all parties concerned. Assignment of a trade mark incorporating a license shall not automatically terminate said license; however, the assignee may, with reasonable cause, seek modification or termination of any license as provided herein, subject to dispute resolution mechanisms established under this Act. Failure to disclose existing licenses in a business india application may render the assignment invalid.

Any aggrieved party may file an appeal with the Appellate Board concerning the refusal of a business india application, provided that such appeal is presented within ninety days of the refusal communicated by the Trade Marks Registry. The grounds for appeal shall be limited to errors apparent from the record, and shall not extend to a re-evaluation of evidence already considered by the Registrar. Furthermore, a cross-appeal may be filed by the Registrar, contesting the appellant’s assertions regarding the distinctiveness of the mark or the validity of the refusal. Should the Appellate Board determine that the refusal was justified, it may impose costs on the appellant, subject to a maximum amount as prescribed. A stay of the Registrar’s decision pending appeal may be granted, contingent upon the appellant furnishing security, as determined by the Board, to cover potential damages. Any party dissatisfied with the decision of the Appellate Board may seek recourse through a writ petition before the High Court.

Any aggrieved party may file an application for rectification of the register concerning a business india application, alleging that the trade mark registered is likely to cause confusion or is deceptively similar to a pre-existing mark. Such application shall be accompanied by a statement of grounds and supporting evidence, as provided herein. The Registrar, upon receiving such application, shall serve a notice to the registered proprietor, affording them an opportunity to file a counter-statement. Should the Registrar deem the application well-founded, they may direct rectification of the register. An appeal against the Registrar’s decision shall lie before the Appellate Board, and the proceedings before the Appellate Board may be heard by a chairperson judicial member, appointed in accordance with the rules. The Appellate Board’s decision shall be final and binding, subject to any recourse available under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. Failure to exhaust this remedy may preclude further legal action.

A “business india situate” shall mean a business undertaking that maintains a verifiable and continuous commercial presence within the territorial jurisdiction of India, evidenced by registration with the appropriate governmental authorities and demonstrable economic activity. Such presence shall be distinct from a mere branch office or agent of a foreign entity, and shall require a locally appointed representative authorized to act on behalf of the business. Where a business india situate utilizes a trade mark, proof of such local establishment and ongoing operation, including but not limited to tax filings and documented transactions, may be required as part of any proceedings under this Act. The Registrar may, subject to verification, accept such evidence as sufficient demonstration of legitimate business activity.

Any person desiring to register a trade mark incorporating or relating to the expression “business india situate” shall, in addition to the usual requirements under this Act, furnish a declaration detailing the geographical limitations of such use. The Registrar may, subject to verification of such declaration, proceed with the examination of the application. Provided that, if the applicant claims use of “business india situate” beyond the territory of India, evidence of lawful use and registration, or equivalent protection, in those territories shall be submitted. An application for registration of a trade mark containing “business india situate” shall be advertised in the Trade Marks Journal, specifically highlighting the declared geographical scope of use. The Registrar may, if satisfied that the use is bona fide and does not mislead the public, register the trade mark. However, registration shall not confer exclusive rights to the expression “business india situate” in territories where the applicant has not demonstrated lawful use as provided herein.

Any person aggrieved by a non-use of a registered trade mark relating to ‘business india situate’ may apply to the Registrar for a declaration of its removal from the register, provided that such application shall not be entertained unless at least five years have elapsed since the registration of the trade mark. The Registrar, upon being satisfied that the trade mark has remained unused for a continuous period of five years and there is no reasonable cause for such non-use, shall order its removal. However, a certificate of registration of a trade mark shall be prima facie evidence of the exclusive right to use the trade mark subject to the provisions of this Act. Any assignment of rights in a ‘business india situate’ trade mark shall be subject to verification by the Registrar to ensure legitimate transfer and prevent fraudulent practices. A registered proprietor may, as provided herein, seek an injunction against any unauthorized use of their trade mark, and claim damages for any loss suffered due to such infringement. The court may, in determining damages, consider the profits made by the infringer.

Any person aggrieved by an assertion of rights in a registered trade mark relating to the expression “business india situate” may, subject to the provisions of this Act, apply to the Appellate Board for rectification of the register. Such application shall be made in the manner prescribed and shall clearly demonstrate that the use of the mark by the complainant is likely to cause confusion, or is deceptive, or is likely to injure the reputation of the applicant. The Appellate Board may, if satisfied that the grounds for rectification exist, order rectification of the register accordingly, and may also grant such other relief as it deems fit. 

Provided that, no rectification shall be ordered unless the applicant has first given notice of the application to the proprietor of the trade mark, and the proprietor has been afforded an opportunity to be heard. Where a claim of “business india situate” is made in relation to geographical indication, the application shall also include evidence of origin and a statement of user consistent with established practices. The Appellate Board shall consider any relevant evidence submitted by either party in determining the matter.

Any application for registration of a trade mark incorporating a geographical indication shall be subject to verification of the standards of the goods concerned, as provided herein, to ensure authenticity and quality consistent with established practices for that business india situate. The Registrar may, prior to acceptance of such application, require evidence of origin and a detailed scheme for quality control maintained by the applicant or a recognized association representing producers of the goods. Where a trade mark is registered for goods originating from a specific geographical area, any subsequent transfer of ownership or assignment of rights shall necessitate prior intimation to the Registrar, detailing the new proprietor’s commitment to upholding the established quality control standards. Failure to maintain these standards, or a material alteration to the production process affecting the goods’ characteristics, may render the registration liable to revocation under this Act. A registered proprietor shall also submit annual compliance reports detailing adherence to the quality control scheme.

Any person who, in the course of trade, uses a mark that falsely suggests a connection with any business situate in India, or any goods associated with such business, shall be deemed to have committed an act of unfair trade practice as provided herein. Where a plaintiff demonstrates that a defendant’s use of a mark creates confusion or deception amongst consumers regarding the origin of goods or services, and that said defendant knew or ought reasonably to have known of the business india situate, a permanent injunction may be granted. Any violation of an injunction issued under this Act shall be punishable with imprisonment not exceeding three years, or with fine, or with both. The Registrar may, subject to such terms and conditions as may be prescribed, order the removal of any deceptive mark or packaging. Any goods found to be in violation may be seized and destroyed at the expense of the owner.

Any assignment of a registered trade mark relating to goods or services falling within the class of ‘business india situate’ shall be subject to the prior written consent of the Central Government, where such mark is deemed by the said Government to be of importance to the industrial or economic welfare of India. Such consent may be granted subject to conditions ensuring the continued beneficial use of the mark within Indian territory. Where a license is granted concerning a trade mark incorporating ‘business india situate’, the licensor shall furnish the Registrar with details of the licensee, the scope of the license, and the duration thereof. Failure to do so may render the license voidable at the option of the Central Government. An assignment or license not complying with the provisions of this Act shall be deemed unlawful and unenforceable, and the proprietor may be subject to penalties as provided herein. The Registrar shall maintain a public register of all assignments and licenses relating to marks of national importance.

Any aggrieved party may, subject to the provisions of this Act, file a rectification petition before the Appellate Board alleging that the trade mark ‘Business India Situate’, registered in Class 35 concerning advertising and business management services, was improperly accepted or should not have been registered. The Registrar, having received a counter-statement from the registered proprietor, shall transmit the petition and such statement to the Appellate Board for adjudication. Provided that, where the rectification petition is based on a claim of prior use of a similar mark, evidence of such use, including dates and extent of use, shall be submitted with the petition. The Appellate Board may, if satisfied that the mark ‘Business India Situate’ lacks distinctiveness or is deceptively similar to an earlier mark, order its rectification or removal from the register. Any decision of the Appellate Board shall be final and binding, subject to appeal to the Supreme Court as provided herein. The registered proprietor may, within one month of the Appellate Board’s order, apply for a stay of execution pending appeal.

Any aggrieved party may, subject to the provisions of this Act, file a rectification petition before the Appellate Board concerning the register of trade marks, specifically where a mark registered indicates a ‘business india situate’ outside of India, and the applicant alleges that such indication is false or misleading. The Appellate Board shall, after notice to the proprietor of the trade mark and opportunity of being heard, determine the matter and may, if satisfied of the falsity or misleading nature of the indication, order its removal or amendment. Furthermore, if a registered trade mark incorporates a claim to novelty based on a corresponding patented invention, and that patent is subsequently revoked or held invalid, the Board may, upon petition by an interested party, consider this as grounds for rectification, potentially leading to the removal of the trade mark registration. Decisions of the Appellate Board shall be final and binding, though an appeal to the High Court may be permissible on points of law.

A “business india situate” shall denote a commercial enterprise established and operating within the territorial jurisdiction of India, possessing a verifiable place of business and engaged in lawful trade. For the purposes of registration as a trade mark, evidence of such business india situate, including but not limited to, incorporation documents, business licenses, and proof of commercial activity, shall be submitted with the application. Where goods originate from a specific geographical area within India and possess qualities or reputation attributable to that origin, a geographical indication authorised under the provisions of this Act may be registered as part of the trade mark, subject to demonstrating a clear link between the goods, their origin, and the established geographical indication. The Registrar may require additional documentation to verify the authenticity of any claimed geographical indication.

A trade mark application, once accepted, shall proceed to registration subject to the provisions contained herein. Where an applicant, having duly filed an application and satisfied all requirements as to form and substance, claims a date of adoption or first use earlier than the date of application, such claimed date may, at the discretion of the Registrar, be considered as the relevant date for the purposes of establishing priority. However, should sufficient evidence demonstrating such earlier use not be furnished within a period of one year from the Registrar’s request, the registration shall be deemed to have occurred on the date of the application itself. This deemed date registration will be recorded in the Register of Trade Marks. Any subsequent challenge to the validity of this deemed date shall be subject to the established procedures for rectification of the Register, and the onus of proof regarding actual prior use remains with the applicant.

A trade mark application, accepted under this Act, shall, subject to the provisions herein, proceed to registration upon fulfillment of prescribed formalities and payment of the requisite registration fee. Where an application for registration contains a reference to a prior trade mark application, or a claim of prior use, and such reference or claim is duly recorded, the date of such prior application or recorded use, as the case may be, shall be deemed to be the date of registration for the purposes of establishing priority amongst conflicting trade marks. Provided that, if the Registrar, upon examination, finds the reference or claim to be false or misleading, the benefit of the deemed date registration shall not accrue to the applicant. Any person aggrieved by a decision refusing the benefit of a deemed date registration may, within one month from the date of such decision, prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board, subject to payment of the prescribed fee and compliance with procedural requirements as stipulated. The Appellate Board’s decision shall be final and binding.

A trade mark application, accepted under this Act, shall be deemed to have been registered as of the date of application, provided that all requisite statutory fees have been duly paid and deposited with the Trade Marks Registry. However, this deemed date registration shall not confer any rights against a prior user of an identical or deceptively similar trade mark, established before the date of application, unless such prior user has failed to file a counter-statement within the prescribed time limit.
