An applicant seeking registration of goods produced limits india must furnish a declaration detailing the origin and manufacturing process, alongside a representation of the goods’ packaging as ordinarily presented to the consumer. A qualified legal practitioner may, on behalf of an applicant, submit the necessary documentation and attest to the veracity of the declarations made. The Registrar shall, subject to verification of the submitted information and payment of the prescribed fee, issue a certificate of registration. Registration shall be valid for a period of ten years from the date of application, renewable upon payment of a renewal fee and compliance with any updated requirements as stipulated by the Central Government. Failure to comply with these provisions may result in the cancellation of registration.

A reference geographical indication, for the purposes of this Act, signifies a geographical indication which, though not directly registered under this Act, is recognized and protected in its country of origin through legislation affording comparable protection. Such recognition shall be evidenced by official documentation from the competent authority in that country, establishing the geographical indication as legally protected therein. Where a foreign country does not possess legislation equivalent to this Act, the Registrar may, subject to satisfying themselves of the genuine and consistent use of the geographical indication and its association with a specific region, consider such indication as a reference geographical indication. Provided that the applicant demonstrates a reciprocal arrangement, or lack thereof, concerning the protection of Indian geographical indications within that foreign country, as determined by the Central Government.

Any application for the registration of a geographical indication shall be made in the prescribed manner to the Geographical Indications Registry. The application shall include a statement of case containing an accurate and complete description of the goods for which the geographical indication is sought, and the area of origin in India to which the goods are linked. A clear and unambiguous reference geographical indication, denoting the specific geographical area and quality or reputation of the goods, must be prominently displayed within the application. Where a producer group or association exists, evidence of its constitution and authority to represent the producers shall accompany the application. The Registry may, subject to such conditions as it deems fit, require further evidence relating to the origin, quality, or reputation of the goods. Provided that, the Registry shall not reject an application without affording the applicant an opportunity to be heard. Any registered geographical indication shall be subject to renewal as provided herein.

Any person dealing in goods bearing a registered geographical indication, and alleging that another person is infringing their rights, may apply to the Registrar for an order of injunction restraining the alleged infringer from dealing in such goods. Such application shall be accompanied by a statement of facts and evidence supporting the claim of infringement, and shall be subject to verification on oath or affirmation. The Registrar, upon being satisfied of the prima facie case and potential irreparable harm, may issue an interim injunction pending disposal of the proceedings. A registered proprietor of a geographical indication may, as provided herein, also seek damages for loss suffered due to the infringement. Where a geographical indication is used in relation to goods not originating from the specified geographical area, it shall constitute a misrepresentation likely to deceive or cause confusion. Any reference geographical indication, when used, must accurately reflect the origin and characteristics associated with that region, and any deviation shall be actionable under this Act. The court may, at its discretion, award costs to the prevailing party.

Any person desiring to obtain registration of a geographical indication shall apply to the Controller of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks in the prescribed manner, and shall furnish with such application a statement of case. The application shall include a clear and precise definition of the goods to which the geographical indication relates, specifying the qualities, reputation or other characteristics in respect of which the goods are associated with a particular geographical area. Where a geographical indication is a reference geographical indication, meaning one already registered for goods originating from a different territory, the applicant shall demonstrate substantial connection and a clear consumer perception linking the goods to the Indian territory sought to be protected. The Controller may, subject to such conditions as may be deemed necessary, require evidence of prior use or a rule of practice establishing a legitimate link. Provided that, the Controller shall not reject an application solely on the basis of a prior registration elsewhere without due consideration of the specific circumstances and potential for consumer confusion as provided herein. Any false representation regarding the origin of goods bearing a registered geographical indication shall be actionable under this Act.

A geographical indication shall be considered a reference geographical indication for the purposes of this Act, provided that the applicant demonstrates continuous use of the indication in the territory to which it relates for a period not less than five years immediately preceding the date of application. The Registrar may, subject to verification of such continuous use through documented evidence of trade, require additional proof of origin and quality characteristics unique to the geographical area. Any association of producers or artisans claiming a reference geographical indication shall maintain a register of authorized users, accessible for inspection as provided herein. Failure to maintain such a register, or to demonstrate genuine connection to the geographical area, shall render the indication ineligible for registration. A reference geographical indication, once registered, confers upon the registered proprietor the exclusive right to use the indication in relation to the goods in respect of which it is registered.

Any person who falsely represents a geographical indication as a reference geographical indication, or who uses a geographical indication not duly registered under this Act, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than six months but which may extend to three years and with fine not less than fifty thousand rupees but which may extend to two lakh rupees. Where the offence involves the sale of goods bearing such falsely represented or unregistered geographical indication, all such goods shall be liable to seizure and destruction, subject to the order of a designated court. The registered proprietor of a geographical indication, or any association representing such proprietor, may initiate proceedings for recovery of damages sustained due to the unlawful use. Any evidence obtained through search and seizure conducted under the provisions of this Act shall be admissible in any legal proceeding, provided that the procedure established by law has been duly followed. A second or subsequent offence shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than one year.

Any person being the registered proprietor of a geographical indication, or a licensee authorized by such proprietor, may, subject to the provisions of this Act, assign or transfer the said geographical indication, or any right therein, to any other person. An assignment or transfer of a geographical indication shall be subject to such terms and conditions as may be agreed upon between the parties, and shall be in writing and registered with the Geographical Indications Registry. The Registrar shall, upon receipt of an application for registration of an assignment or transfer, examine the application and, if satisfied that it is in order, register the assignment or transfer. A reference geographical indication, being one officially approved and listed in the Register, shall be assignable as any other registered property, but the assignment shall not prejudice existing rights of producers within the specified geographical area. The assignee shall, within six months of the assignment, notify the Registrar and demonstrate continued adherence to the production standards associated with the geographical indication. Failure to do so may result in revocation of the registration.

Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Registrar refusing to register a geographical indication, or varying the register of geographical indications, may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board within three months of the date of the order appealed against, subject to the payment of such fee as may be prescribed. The Appellate Board shall, after giving the applicant and the Registrar an opportunity of being heard, pass such orders as it deems fit, confirming, modifying or reversing the decision appealed against. Where a registered geographical indication is alleged to be falsely applied to goods, any interested party may apply to the Appellate Board for rectification of the register, and the Board shall, following due process and consideration of evidence, determine whether the continued registration of the geographical indication is justified. A ‘reference geographical indication’ shall mean a geographical indication which, though not directly registered under this Act, is recognized in a country outside India and to which goods originating from that country are linked, and may be considered by the Board in assessing the distinctiveness of a proposed geographical indication. Provided that such reference shall not create any right or obligation under this Act.

Any person dealing in goods bearing a reference geographical indication, and claiming entitlement thereto, shall maintain a register of all consignments dispatched, detailing the quantity, destination, and date of dispatch, and make such register available for inspection by an officer authorized under this Act. The controller may, upon reasonable suspicion of misrepresentation or unauthorized use of a registered geographical indication, direct any such person to produce the register and all related documentation within thirty days. Failure to comply with such direction shall constitute an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. Furthermore, goods found to be in violation of the provisions of this Act, and bearing a falsely applied reference geographical indication, shall be liable to seizure and destruction, subject to the controller’s order. Any controller acting maliciously or without due process shall be liable to disciplinary action.

Any assignment of a registered geographical indication, or a license to use a registered geographical indication, shall be subject to such conditions as may be prescribed, and shall be in writing and registered with the Registrar within thirty days of its execution. The Registrar may, upon application made by the assignee or licensee, record the assignment or license in the Register of Geographical Indications. A reference geographical indication, being a specific indication identifying goods originating from a particular geographical area, may be assigned independently of the goodwill of the business carrying on the trade in those goods, provided that such assignment does not mislead the public as to the origin of the goods. Where a conviction for an offence involving the fraudulent use of a registered geographical indication results in a forfeiture directed conviction, any associated license or assignment shall automatically stand void, and the Registrar shall record such voidance. The registered proprietor may, subject to the terms of any existing assignment or license, revoke any license granted under this Act if the licensee fails to adhere to quality standards.

A reference geographical indication, for the purposes of determining a conflict under this Act, shall extend to include not only the registered geographical indication itself but also any colourable variation thereof likely to cause confusion or deception amongst the public, or to unfairly compete with the proprietor of the registered geographical indication. Such determination of colourable variation shall be made according to the principles governing comparative advertising and unfair trade practices as understood in the ordinary course of civil procedure. Provided that, a mere similarity in appearance or sound shall not, by itself, constitute a colourable variation, unless accompanied by evidence of actual confusion or intent to deceive. Any party alleging infringement based on a reference geographical indication may initiate proceedings before the competent court, subject to the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908.

Any person claiming to be aggrieved by the misrepresentation of a reference geographical indication, or the false application thereof, shall be entitled to institute a civil suit in the District Court having jurisdiction over the place where the misrepresentation occurred. The suit may seek an injunction restraining the defendant from using the falsely represented geographical indication, or from engaging in any activity that constitutes unfair competition. The Court, upon being satisfied of the misrepresentation and the resulting damage to the reputation of the registered geographical indication, may also award damages to the claimant, assessed in accordance with the principles of restitution and deterrence. Furthermore, any goods bearing a false trade description relating to the geographical origin, and intended to deceive the public into believing they possess the qualities associated with the genuine reference geographical indication, shall be deemed counterfeit goods as provided herein. The registered proprietor may, subject to the rules, apply for the removal of such goods from the market and their destruction.

Any person who falsifies genuine geographical indications, or falsely represents goods as originating from a geographical area when they do not, shall be subject to the penalties as provided herein. Such falsification includes, but is not limited to, alteration, addition, or effacement of a registered geographical indication, or the use of a deceptively similar indication likely to cause confusion. Where a registered proprietor of a geographical indication demonstrates actual or potential damage resulting from such falsification, they may apply to the appropriate court for an injunction restraining the offender. The court, subject to verification of the claim, shall issue an order for immediate cessation of the infringing activity and may also order the destruction or forfeiture of goods bearing the falsified geographical indication. Any individual abetting or conspiring to commit such an offence shall be liable jointly and severally with the principal offender, and shall be punishable with imprisonment not exceeding three years, or with fine, or with both.

Any person desiring to obtain a license to use a registered geographical indication, or to assign rights therein, shall submit an application in the prescribed form to the Registrar, accompanied by the requisite fee. The application for assignment shall clearly demonstrate that the proposed assignee is genuinely engaged in the production or processing of goods associated with the geographical indication and possesses the requisite expertise. A transfer of ownership, or a license granted, shall be subject to a reasonable royalty determined by mutual agreement between the assignor and assignee, or, failing such agreement, by the Registrar, considering prevailing market rates and production costs. Any act which falsifies genuine geographical indications, including the misrepresentation of origin or quality, shall constitute a breach of the licensing agreement and render the license voidable at the option of the registered proprietor. The Registrar may, upon sufficient cause shown, revoke a license if the licensee is found to be in violation of these provisions, or if the quality of goods bearing the geographical indication deteriorates significantly.

Any person who falsifies genuine geographical indications, as provided herein, shall be liable to a penalty not less than fifty thousand rupees and which may extend to two lakh rupees, and to imprisonment for a term not less than six months and which may extend to three years, or with both. The falsification includes, but is not limited to, alteration, addition, or effacement of a registered geographical indication in relation to goods. Any application for an injunction restraining such falsification may be made to the District Court having jurisdiction over the place where the offence occurred, or to the High Court. The Court, upon being satisfied of the prima facie case, may grant an interim injunction pending the final disposal of the proceedings, subject to such terms and conditions as it deems fit. Repeated offences shall attract enhanced penalties and may result in the revocation of registration.

Any company registered under the Companies Act, 2013 and desiring to utilize a registered geographical indication for goods falling within the specified class shall obtain a license from the registered proprietor, subject to such terms and conditions as may be mutually agreed upon. Where a registered proprietor falsifies genuine geographical indications associated with their goods, either through misrepresentation of origin or quality, or by applying the indication to goods not originating from the defined geographical area, they shall be liable to a penalty as prescribed under this Act. Assignment of a license shall be permitted only with the prior written consent of the geographical indication’s proprietor, and any transfer without such consent shall be considered void. The proprietor may, however, revoke a license if the licensee consistently fails to adhere to quality standards or engages in activities detrimental to the reputation of the geographical indication, provided that reasonable notice and opportunity for rectification are given. Any dispute regarding licensing or assignment shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the appropriate court.

Any person desiring to obtain a license to use a registered geographical indication, or to assign any right in such geographical indication, shall submit an application in the prescribed form to the Registrar, accompanied by the requisite fee. The application for assignment shall clearly demonstrate that the proposed assignee is a producer of goods to which the geographical indication relates and is located within the defined geographical area. Any transfer or assignment of rights without prior registration of the assignment with the Registrar shall be void *ab initio*. A registered proprietor may, subject to the terms and conditions as may be prescribed, grant licenses to other persons for the use of the geographical indication. However, any act that constitutes the falsify geographical indication, including the application of a false or deceptively similar indication to goods not originating from the specified region, shall be a ground for revocation of the license and subject to penalties as provided herein. The Registrar may, upon sufficient cause shown, refuse to register an assignment if it is deemed detrimental to the reputation or quality of the geographical indication.

For the purposes of determining the authenticity and origin of goods, a ‘registration referred fact’ shall constitute conclusive evidence of a geographical indication’s association with a specific region, subject to proof of continued adherence to quality standards as prescribed in the register. This fact, once established through registration under this Act, may be rebutted only upon demonstrable evidence of fraud in the procurement of registration or a material alteration in the characteristics of the goods or the geographical region itself. Any representation, whether direct or indirect, implying registration when no such registration exists, shall be deemed a misrepresentation and actionable as provided herein. The register maintained under this Act shall be prima facie evidence of all facts stated therein, including the ‘registration referred fact’.

Any application for the registration of a geographical indication shall be examined by the Registrar, and such examination shall be conducted as expeditiously as possible, subject to the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder. The Registrar may, before refusing an application, require the applicant to furnish further information or evidence, or to limit the scope of the geographical indication sought to be registered. Where a geographical indication is registered, the register shall contain the particulars of the goods in respect of which the geographical indication is registered, the area of origin, and the name and address of the applicant. A registration referred fact establishing the link between the goods and their geographical origin is a prerequisite for the grant of protection as provided herein. The Registrar shall maintain a register of all registered geographical indications, which shall be open to inspection by the public, subject to payment of the prescribed fee. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Registrar may, within a period of ninety days from the date of such decision, prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board.

Any person aggrieved by a refusal of the Registrar to register a geographical indication, or by any alteration of the register relating to a geographical indication in which he has an interest, may, within a period of ninety days from the date of the order of the Registrar, prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board. The Appellate Board shall, after giving the applicant and the Registrar an opportunity of being heard, pass such order as it deems fit, confirming, modifying or reversing the decision of the Registrar. A registration referred fact established in the register shall be conclusive evidence of the validity of the registration, subject to a successful appeal or rectification proceeding. Where a registered geographical indication is falsely represented in connection with goods, the aggrieved party may institute civil proceedings for injunction, damages, or both. The court, while granting relief, may also order the destruction or forfeiture of goods bearing such false representation, and may require the defendant to account for profits derived from the wrongful use.

Any application for registration of a geographical indication shall be examined by the Registrar as provided herein, and such examination shall be completed within a period of eighteen months from the date of the application, subject to the applicant fulfilling all requirements regarding documentation and fees. Where the Registrar is satisfied that the application meets the criteria for registration, a notice of acceptance shall be published in the Journal. Any person may, within a period of four months from such publication, file a notice of opposition to the registration, detailing the grounds upon which the application is contested. The Registrar shall consider any opposition filed and may, after giving the applicant an opportunity to be heard, either reject the application or direct that the geographical indication be registered. A registration referred fact, once established and recorded in the Register, shall be prima facie evidence of the validity of the right to the geographical indication. However, such registration may be subject to revocation on grounds of non-use or misleading representation, as detailed in this Act. The Register maintained under this Act shall be open to inspection by any member of the public, subject to payment of the prescribed fee.

Any application for registration of a geographical indication shall be subject to a rigorous examination as to its compliance with the provisions of this Act and associated rules. The Registrar may, prior to accepting an application, require the applicant to furnish additional evidence establishing a prima facie case for the uniqueness of the goods in relation to the specified geographical area. A registered geographical indication constitutes conclusive evidence, unless proven otherwise, of the origin of goods bearing that indication and shall be recorded in the Register maintained under this Act. However, registration referred fact alone does not confer an absolute right; continued use of the geographical indication in commerce, demonstrating a direct link to the geographical origin, is essential for maintaining the validity of the registration. Failure to demonstrate such continued use may render the registration liable to revocation, subject to the procedures outlined herein. The Registrar may, at any time, initiate a review of registered geographical indications to ensure ongoing compliance with the established criteria.

Any person who, for the purpose of trade, manufacture or business, falsely applies a registered geographical indication to goods not originating from the specified geographical area, or falsely represents goods as possessing qualities attributable to such geographical indication, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than six months, but which may extend to three years, and with a fine not less than fifty thousand rupees, but which may extend to two lakh rupees. The Registrar may, subject to such conditions as may be prescribed, direct the removal of the falsely applied geographical indication from the goods or packaging. Any evidence of intent to deceive, or repeated offences, shall be considered an aggravating factor in determining the penalty. A registration referred fact, established in the Register of Geographical Indications, shall be conclusive evidence of the origin and qualities associated with the goods. The court may, in addition to the above penalties, order the destruction of goods bearing the false geographical indication.

Any person aggrieved by the refusal of the Registrar to register a geographical indication, or by any modification made by the Registrar in the particulars of a registered geographical indication, may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board. Such appeal shall be filed within three months from the date of the order of the Registrar, and shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the said order and a statement of the grounds on which the appeal is based. The Appellate Board may, if satisfied that the grounds for appeal are substantial, admit the appeal and direct the Registrar to furnish all relevant documents and information pertaining to the case. A registration referred fact established before the Registrar, and not successfully rebutted, shall be considered prima facie evidence of the validity of the geographical indication. However, the Appellate Board retains the power to review such established facts and may, subject to due process and evidence presented, overturn the Registrar’s initial determination. The decision of the Appellate Board shall be final and binding.

Any dispute regarding the registration referred fact concerning a geographical indication shall be adjudicated by the Appellate Board established under this Act, provided that such dispute arises after a reasoned order is passed by the Registrar refusing registration or revoking a registration. An applicant aggrieved by the Registrar’s decision may, within a period of ninety days from the date of the said order, file an appeal to the Appellate Board, furnishing such evidence as may be required to substantiate their claim. The Appellate Board, while considering appeals relating to a registered geographical indication, shall have the power to call for evidence and examine witnesses, and may, subject to rules made under this Act, confirm, modify, or reverse the decision of the Registrar. Failure to file an appeal within the stipulated time shall not preclude a party from seeking judicial review under the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. The decision of the Appellate Board shall be final and binding, except where a substantial question of law is involved.

Any registered user who, in the course of applying for registration or in any document submitted to the Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Registry, makes a false representation concerning a material particular, shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees. The Registrar may, following due process and affording the registered user an opportunity to be heard, initiate an inquiry into any allegation of misrepresentation. Should the inquiry establish that a registered user misrepresented facts relating to their entitlement to register a layout-design, or concerning the originality of the layout-design itself, the Registrar shall issue a notice outlining the proposed cancellation of the registration. 

Provided that, the registered user may submit a reasoned response to the notice within thirty days from the date of its receipt. Failure to respond, or a response deemed unsatisfactory by the Registrar, shall result in the cancellation of the registration and a prohibition against future applications for a period of two years. Any person aggrieved by such cancellation may appeal to the High Court, subject to the provisions of this Act.

Any registered user who, through a statement or representation made during the registration process or subsequently to the Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Registry, knowingly misleads or provides false information regarding their identity, principal place of business, or the extent of their commercial exploitation of a registered layout-design, shall be deemed to have misrepresented themselves as provided herein. Such misrepresentation shall constitute a breach of the obligations incumbent upon a registered user under this Act. The Registrar may, following due notice to the registered user and consideration of any evidence submitted, impose a monetary penalty not exceeding five lakh rupees for each instance of such misrepresentation. Furthermore, the Registrar may suspend the registration of the concerned user for a period not exceeding one year, subject to the severity and frequency of the false statements. Repeated instances of a registered user misrepresented may lead to permanent cancellation of registration.

Any registered user who, in the course of seeking or maintaining a license or assignment of rights in a registered layout-design, knowingly misrepresents a material fact relating to their commercial standing, technical capacity, or intended use of the layout-design, shall be deemed to have violated the principles of good faith as established under this Act. Such misrepresentation shall constitute grounds for immediate suspension of all licensing privileges and may, subject to an inquiry conducted by the Controller of Designs, result in permanent revocation of registered user status. Furthermore, any contract or agreement entered into based upon such misrepresented information may be declared void ab initio at the discretion of a competent court. A party aggrieved by such misrepresentation may seek equitable remedies, including but not limited to, recovery of damages and specific performance, provided that a claim is filed within two years of discovery of the misrepresentation. The Controller may also impose a monetary penalty not exceeding five lakh rupees for each instance of a registered user misrepresented.

The aggrieved party, M/s. Stellar Circuits, has filed an appeal before this Authority alleging that the respondent, Mr. Rohan Verma, a registered user of layout-design registration number 4789/HYD/2023, has engaged in misrepresentation regarding the commercial exploitation of the said layout-design, as provided herein. Specifically, the appellant contends that Mr. Verma, despite claiming to manufacture integrated circuits solely for domestic consumption, has demonstrably exported a significant quantity to overseas markets without proper accounting or remittance of royalties due to the registered proprietor, NovaTech Semiconductors. The Authority notes that the initial registration was granted subject to the condition of strict adherence to the declared scope of commercialization. Evidence submitted indicates a deliberate omission of export sales figures in quarterly reports, constituting a clear case of a registered user misrepresented. Should the appeal be upheld, the Authority may, in addition to imposing financial penalties, recommend cancellation of Mr. Verma’s registered user status and initiate proceedings for recovery of outstanding royalties.

A person shall be considered a registered user registered under this Act upon successful application to the Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Registry and payment of the prescribed fee, subject to verification of particulars furnished and confirmation of eligibility as per the regulations. The Registry shall maintain a register of registered users, detailing the name, address, and scope of authorized use relating to registered layout-designs. A registered user may, with the consent of the registered proprietor, exercise the rights as provided herein concerning the exploitation of a layout-design, limited to the specified terms of such consent. Any transfer of rights or change in particulars of a registered user shall be notified to the Registry in the manner prescribed, failing which the registration may be subject to revocation. The proprietor retains the right to revoke registration of a user upon reasonable cause.

A registered user registered under this Act shall maintain a register of all licenses granted by him, detailing the terms and conditions of each license, including the scope of permitted use, duration, and royalty payable, and such register shall be open to inspection by the Controller upon reasonable notice. Any registered user who fails to comply with the requirements of maintaining such a register shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding five thousand rupees per day for the period of such failure, subject to a maximum penalty of one lakh rupees. The Controller may, however, extend the time for compliance with these requirements if sufficient cause is demonstrated. A person aggrieved by any action of a registered user relating to a license may submit a complaint to the Controller, who shall, following an inquiry conducted as provided herein, issue directions for rectification of the matter. Provided that, no such direction shall prejudice any rights accrued to a third party prior to the issuance of said direction. The Controller’s decision on any complaint shall be final and binding, unless appealed to the High Court.

A registered user registered under this Act shall maintain a record of all commercial exploitation of the registered layout-design, including the quantity manufactured, the consideration received, and the identities of all licensees. Subject to the provisions herein, the Controller may, upon reasonable cause and after notice, inspect such records to verify compliance with the terms of registration and any licensing agreements. Any registered user failing to maintain accurate records or obstructing such inspection shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees. Provided that, a registered user may, with the prior written consent of the registered proprietor, assign their rights to exploit the layout-design to a third party, but such assignment shall be subject to the same conditions and limitations as apply to the original registration. The Controller shall maintain a public register of all registered users, detailing the scope of their authorized exploitation.

Any registered user registered under this Act, who, with intent to deceive, represents a layout-design as their own which was not originally created by them, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than six months, but which may extend to three years, and with a fine not less than fifty thousand rupees, but which may extend to five lakh rupees. Furthermore, any person who, being a registered user, fails to maintain accurate records of all transactions relating to the commercial exploitation of a registered layout-design, subject to reasonable notice from the Controller, shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding ten thousand rupees for each such failure. Provided that, the Controller may, in exceptional circumstances and with reasoned order, extend the period for maintaining such records. Any appeal against an order imposing such penalty shall lie before the designated court within thirty days of the order’s issuance.

A person shall be considered a registered user registered under this Act upon successful completion of the application process and issuance of a certificate of registration by the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trademarks, or an officer duly authorized by them. The register of registered users shall be maintained in the prescribed manner and be open to inspection subject to payment of the prescribed fee. A registered user may, subject to the terms of any agreement with the registered proprietor, exercise the rights conferred by this Act in respect of the registered layout-design. Where goods incorporating a registered layout-design are imported into India, the provisions of the Customs Act 1962, relating to the prevention of infringement of intellectual property rights, shall apply mutatis mutandis, and the authorized officer may seize such goods if reasonable suspicion of infringement exists.

The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, constitute a Registration Office for the purpose of receiving applications for registration of semiconductor integrated circuits layout-designs and maintaining a register thereof as provided herein. Every application for registration shall be accompanied by a layout-design drawing, a detailed description of the layout-design, and the prescribed fee. The Controller of the Registration Office shall, upon examination, satisfy themselves that the layout-design is novel and intrinsically capable of being realized. A function judicial member, possessing qualifications in law and experience in intellectual property matters, shall be appointed to assist the Controller in determining novelty and to adjudicate on any objections raised during the examination process. Subject to the provisions relating to priority, the Controller shall register the layout-design and enter the particulars in the register, and a certificate of registration shall be issued to the applicant. Any person aggrieved by the decision of the Controller may file an appeal.

The aggrieved party may, subject to the provisions of this Act, institute a suit for infringement before a District Court having jurisdiction over the place where the act of infringement has occurred or where the defendant resides or carries on business. Any person defending against a claim of infringement may, as provided herein, file a counter-claim seeking a declaration of non-infringement or invalidity of the registered layout-design. The Court shall, following due process and consideration of evidence, determine the quantum of damages, which shall not be less than such amount as may be prescribed, and may also grant an injunction restraining the defendant from further acts of infringement. A function judicial member, appointed by the Central Government, shall assist the Court in matters requiring legal interpretation and procedural guidance related to layout-design rights. The Court may, at its discretion, appoint an expert assessor to evaluate the technical aspects of the alleged infringement and provide an independent opinion. Costs associated with such assessment shall be borne by the losing party.

Any person alleging infringement of a registered layout-design right shall, prior to initiating proceedings before the High Court, furnish to the Controller a statement detailing the nature of the infringement and the relief sought, as provided herein. The Controller, upon receipt of such statement, may, if satisfied that a prima facie case exists, direct the alleged infringer to furnish a statement of their defense within thirty days. Failure to comply with such direction shall be deemed an obstruction of justice and subject to a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees. A function judicial member, appointed by the Central Government, shall preside over any hearing conducted by the Controller relating to such statements and shall have the power to summon witnesses and documents. Any knowingly false statement made to the Controller shall attract a fine of up to one lakh rupees, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years, or both. The Controller’s decision on prima facie assessment shall be final and binding.

The registered proprietor of a layout-design, or a person deriving title from such proprietor, may, subject to the provisions of this Act, assign or license the rights in the layout-design, either wholly or partially, and either generally or subject to limitations, to any other person. Any assignment or license shall be in writing and shall specify the territory in which the rights are assigned or licensed, and the duration of the assignment or license, and shall be subject to such terms and conditions as may be mutually agreed upon by the parties. Where a dispute arises concerning the validity or scope of any such assignment or license, the aggrieved party may apply to the appropriate High Court. A function judicial member, appointed by the Central Government, shall be present on any Bench hearing such disputes, and shall contribute to the legal determination of the matter. The registrar shall maintain a public register of all registered assignments and licenses, accessible for inspection during office hours. Failure to register an assignment or license does not invalidate it, but may affect its enforceability against a bona fide purchaser without notice.

Any person aggrieved by an order of the Layout-Design Registry concerning the validity of a layout-design right, or the refusal of an application for registration, may file an appeal to the Appellate Board established under this Act. The Appellate Board shall, prior to commencing adjudication of any appeal, ascertain whether the appellant has deposited the prescribed fee and furnished such evidence as may be required to substantiate the grounds of the appeal. A crucial function judicial member of the Appellate Board shall be appointed from amongst persons who are, or have been, judges of a High Court, or are qualified to be so appointed, and shall preside over any bench hearing appeals relating to the interpretation of legal principles. Provided that, in cases involving complex technical issues, the Board may constitute a special bench with enhanced technical expertise, subject to the approval of the Chairperson. The decision of the Appellate Board shall be final and binding, save for any recourse permissible under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

The Central Government may, for the purposes of efficient adjudication of disputes relating to layout-design rights, constitute a Judicial Member Selection Committee consisting of a retired Judge of the Supreme Court, the Controller of Patents, and a nominee of the Department of Electronics and Information Technology. Any person appointed as a function judicial member shall possess a postgraduate degree in law from a recognized university and a minimum of ten years of experience as a practicing advocate or a judicial officer. Provided that the Central Government may, if it deems necessary, give preference to candidates with demonstrated expertise in intellectual property law, particularly concerning semiconductor technology. Furthermore, consideration shall be given to applicants familiar with the principles governing registered geographical indication, recognizing the increasing convergence of technological and traditional knowledge protection. All appointments shall be subject to such terms and conditions as the Central Government may specify. The Committee’s recommendations shall be binding.

The Central Government shall, with a view to ensuring efficient adjudication of disputes relating to semiconductor integrated circuits layout-designs, constitute a Layout-Design Registry and appoint a Controller of Designs who shall be the Registrar of Layout-Designs under this Act. Any person claiming to be the proprietor of a layout-design may apply for registration in the manner as prescribed, submitting requisite documentation and the applicable fee. The application shall be examined by the Controller, who may require further information or amendments, subject to the provisions herein. A functions judicial member, possessing legal qualifications and experience in intellectual property matters, shall be appointed to assist the Controller in assessing the validity of claims and determining the originality of the layout-design. Provided that, the Controller may, in cases involving complex technical issues, seek the advice of a technical expert before making a final decision on the registration of a layout-design. Registration, if granted, shall confer exclusive rights on the proprietor for a period of ten years from the date of filing.

The Central Government may, for the purposes of hearings involving complex technical issues relating to semiconductor integrated circuits layout-designs, designate a judicial member technical, possessing not less than ten years of experience in adjudicating intellectual property disputes and a demonstrated understanding of semiconductor technology. Such a judicial member technical shall, when appointed to a Bench, have the power to direct the scope of technical evidence presented and to formulate specific questions for expert witnesses, subject to the approval of the Chairperson of the Appellate Board. The presence of a judicial member technical on a Bench shall be mandatory where the dispute concerns the originality or inventive step of a layout-design, or where the validity of a registration is challenged on technical grounds, as provided herein. Any decision rendered by a Bench including a judicial member technical may be reviewed by a larger Bench if a party demonstrates material prejudice arising from a misinterpretation of technical evidence.

The Controller shall, upon receipt of an application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design, conduct a preliminary examination to ascertain that the application meets the procedural requirements as provided herein. Should the application satisfy these requirements, the Controller shall cause a notification to be published in the Journal, inviting any person to represent against the registration of the layout-design. Any person intending to oppose the registration shall file a notice of opposition with the Controller within a period of ninety days from the date of such notification. The Controller shall, after considering the representations, if any, and subject to such inquiry as may be deemed necessary, determine whether the layout-design is registrable. A crucial aspect of this determination shall involve assessment by a judicial member technical, possessing expertise in both legal principles and semiconductor technology, to ensure compliance with the novelty and originality criteria. The Controller’s decision shall be final and binding, unless appealed to the Appellate Board.

Any person alleging infringement of a registered layout-design right shall be entitled to commence legal proceedings in the appropriate District Court, subject to the provisions of this Act regarding prior notice to the alleged infringer. The Court, upon being satisfied of a prima facie case of infringement, may grant a temporary injunction restraining the defendant from the manufacture, sale, or distribution of the integrated circuit embodying the infringing layout-design. A key determination in such proceedings shall be made by a judicial member technical, possessing expertise in both law and semiconductor technology, who shall advise the Court on the technical aspects of the case and the validity of the plaintiff’s claims. Where the alleged infringement involves a complex layout-design, the Court may appoint an assessor with specialized knowledge to assist the judicial member technical. Remedies available to the aggrieved party, as provided herein, include an injunction, damages, and an account of profits, calculated in accordance with established legal principles. The Court may also order the delivery up or destruction of infringing articles.

The Central Government shall, when constituting the Appellate Board, ensure adequate representation of persons possessing expertise in semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design and related fields. A qualified judicial member technical shall be appointed to each Bench hearing appeals concerning the validity of registered layout-designs, and such member shall possess at least ten years of experience as a District Judge or equivalent in the judicial service. Provided that, the Central Government may, by notification, specify alternative qualifications for a judicial member technical, subject to demonstrable competence in interpreting technical evidence. The Technical Member of any Bench shall, in all cases involving complex technical issues, provide a reasoned opinion to the Bench prior to any decision being rendered. Any decision of the Appellate Board shall be accompanied by a summary of the Technical Member’s opinion, as a matter of record. Subject to the provisions of this Act, the Appellate Board may, at any stage of proceedings, require an expert opinion from a person not otherwise a member of the Board, should the need arise for specialized knowledge.

The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, constitute a Technical Evaluation Committee for the purpose of assisting the Controller of Patents and Designs in determining the validity of any claim relating to a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design registration. Any person applying for registration shall submit a detailed technical datasheet conforming to the standards prescribed by the Controller, and failure to do so may result in rejection of the application. The Controller shall, prior to registration, ensure that the layout-design does not incorporate any prior art, and shall maintain a register of such prior art for public inspection. A judicial member technical, possessing a degree in law and demonstrated expertise in semiconductor technology, shall always be present during the evaluation of complex cases involving alleged infringement or invalidity. Subject to the provisions herein, the Committee’s recommendations shall be advisory, and the final decision rests with the Controller. Any appeal against the Controller’s decision shall lie before the Appellate Board.

Any person alleging infringement of a registered layout-design right shall, prior to initiating proceedings before a competent court, furnish to the alleged infringer a notice of such infringement, detailing the specific layout-design right claimed and the nature of the alleged infringement, and affording a period of sixty days for rectification. Failure to comply with this provision shall render the initiating party liable to costs, and may be considered by the court in assessing damages. The court, while adjudicating disputes involving layout-design rights, may appoint one or more independent experts to provide technical assistance, and the opinion of such experts shall be admissible as evidence. A judicial member technical, possessing expertise in semiconductor integrated circuits, shall invariably be included in any Bench hearing appeals related to the validity of a registered layout-design. Any person found to be knowingly making false representations regarding the ownership of a layout-design, as provided herein, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years, or with a fine, or with both.

Any registered layout-design right, being property, may be assigned, transferred, or licensed, wholly or partially, by the registered proprietor to any other person, subject to such terms and conditions as may be mutually agreed upon between the parties and recorded with the Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Registry. A license granted under this Act shall be construed as a contract between the licensor and the licensee, and shall be subject to the provisions of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, insofar as applicable. Where a layout-design is assigned or licensed, the Registry shall record the particulars of such assignment or license within the prescribed period. 

The determination of reasonable royalty for any such license shall, where the parties fail to agree, be adjudicated by a judicial member technical, possessing expertise in both law and semiconductor technology, appointed by the Central Government. Such adjudication shall consider prevailing industry standards and comparable licensing agreements, and shall be final and binding on all parties concerned. Any dispute arising from the interpretation or enforcement of a license agreement shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the competent court.

Any aggrieved person may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board against any order or decision of the Registrar, provided that such appeal is filed within sixty days from the date of the order or decision appealed against. The Appellate Board, upon receipt of an appeal, shall first ascertain whether the appellant possesses sufficient locus standi and that the subject matter of the appeal falls within the purview of this Act. Where the appeal concerns a complex technical issue relating to the semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design, the Appellate Board shall necessarily constitute a Bench including a judicial member technical, possessing expertise in the relevant field, to ensure a technically sound adjudication. The decision of the Appellate Board shall be final and binding, subject to any remedies available under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, where questions of law are involved and require further judicial consideration. Failure to comply with procedural requirements may render the appeal inadmissible.

Any person claiming infringement of a registered layout-design right shall, prior to initiating proceedings before any court, furnish to the alleged infringer a notice of such claim, detailing the specific layout-design alleged to be infringed and the manner of such infringement. Where the alleged infringer, upon receipt of such notice, applies for a patent relating to the same layout-design, the applicant patent shall be subject to a stay of all infringement proceedings until the grant or rejection of said patent. The determination of technical aspects of any dispute relating to the validity of a registration or alleged infringement shall, as provided herein, require the opinion of a judicial member technical, possessing expertise in semiconductor integrated circuits. Such judicial member technical shall be appointed by the Central Government and shall submit a report to the court, which report shall be considered persuasive evidence. Failure to provide the requisite notice or a reasonable opportunity to respond shall be a bar to maintaining any action under this Act.

The determination of a dispute concerning the validity of a layout-design right, or any allegation of infringement thereof, shall require the presence of a judicial member with demonstrated technical expertise in the field of semiconductor integrated circuits. Such a judicial member technical shall be appointed from amongst persons possessing a degree in engineering or technology, with not less than five years’ experience in the design, manufacture, or practice relating to semiconductor integrated circuits, or holding a law degree with equivalent specialized knowledge. Provided that, if the layout-design right is claimed to relate to an invention far claimed, the Bench adjudicating the matter may also include an assessor possessing specialized knowledge of the relevant technological field, at the discretion of the presiding officer. Any evidence presented relating to the novelty or originality of the layout-design shall be subject to rigorous scrutiny, as provided herein, to ensure compliance with the criteria for registration under this Act. Failure to adhere to these provisions may render the proceedings invalid.

Any registered layout-design right may be assigned, transferred, or licensed, wholly or partially, by the registered owner to any other person, and such assignment, transfer, or license shall be subject to such terms and conditions as may be mutually agreed upon between the parties, provided that any such agreement shall be in writing and registered with the appropriate authority as prescribed. Where a judicial member technical is appointed to assess the validity of an assignment, the Central Government may, if satisfied that the assignee or licensee is not genuinely utilising the layout-design, revoke the assignment or license. Furthermore, a person falsifies trade secrets relating to a registered layout-design if they knowingly represent an unoriginal layout-design as one protected under this Act, or if they utilize confidential information obtained during a licensing negotiation for improper purposes. Any license granted under this Act shall be non-exclusive unless otherwise expressly stated in the agreement. The registered owner retains the right to exploit the layout-design independently, even after granting licenses to third parties.

The Authority Appellate Board is hereby established for the purpose of hearing and deciding appeals from the orders of the Semiconductor Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Authority. The Board shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. A retired Judge of a High Court shall be appointed as the Chairperson of the Authority Appellate Board, and the term of such appointment shall be for a period of five years or until attaining the age of seventy years, whichever is earlier. Technical Members, possessing expertise in semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design, may be appointed to assist the Chairperson, and their qualifications shall be such as may be prescribed. Any person aggrieved by an order of the Authority may, subject to the provisions of this Act, prefer an appeal to the Authority Appellate Board within a period of sixty days from the date of the order.

The authority appellate board established under this Act shall entertain appeals from any decision of the Registrar relating to the refusal of registration, revocation of registration, or any other matter arising under this Act, subject to the provisions herein. Any person aggrieved by such a decision of the Registrar may file an appeal to the authority appellate board within a period of ninety days from the date of the order appealed against, accompanied by the prescribed fee. The authority appellate board may, at its discretion, extend this period for a further period not exceeding thirty days, provided that sufficient cause is shown. All appeals shall be filed in the manner as prescribed and shall contain a statement of the grounds on which the appeal is based. The authority appellate board shall, after examining the appeal and any evidence submitted, pass an order confirming, modifying, or reversing the decision of the Registrar, and such order shall be final and binding. The Registrar shall furnish all relevant documents and information to the authority appellate board as and when requested.

The authority appellate board established under this Act shall have the exclusive jurisdiction to hear and determine appeals from the orders of the Registrar relating to the refusal of registration, revocation of registration, or any other matter concerning the rights of a proprietor of a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design. Any person aggrieved by an order of the Registrar may prefer an appeal to the authority appellate board within a period of ninety days from the date of the order, subject to the payment of such fees as may be prescribed. The authority appellate board may, at its discretion, require the appellant to furnish evidence or documents to substantiate the grounds of appeal. Provided that, the authority appellate board shall not entertain any appeal unless the appellant demonstrates prima facie a substantial question of law or fact requiring determination. The decision of the authority appellate board shall be final and binding, subject to the provisions for judicial review as may be available under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. The Registrar shall furnish all relevant records to the authority appellate board for the purpose of hearing and determining the appeal.

The Authority Appellate Board shall be the final forum for hearing appeals from the decisions of the Semiconductor Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Registry. Any person aggrieved by an order concerning the registration of a layout-design, or the refusal thereof, may prefer an appeal to the Authority Appellate Board, subject to the provisions of this Act. Such appeal shall be filed within ninety days from the date of the order appealed against, and shall be accompanied by the prescribed fee. The Authority Appellate Board may, at any stage of the proceedings, require the appellant to deposit with such officer as it thinks fit, a sum equivalent to the amount in dispute, provided that such sum shall be refunded to the appellant if the appeal is allowed. The Board shall have the power to summon witnesses, issue commissions for examination of witnesses, and to require the production of documents, as it deems necessary for the just determination of the appeal. Decisions of the Authority Appellate Board shall be final and binding, except where a question of law of general public importance arises, in which case an appeal may lie to the Supreme Court.

The authority appellate board constituted under this Act shall exercise jurisdiction over all appeals arising from the decisions of the Semiconductor Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Registry. Any person aggrieved by an order of the Registry concerning the registration of a layout-design, or the refusal thereof, may prefer an appeal to the authority appellate board, subject to the payment of such fees as may be prescribed. An appeal shall be filed within a period of sixty days from the date of the order appealed against, and shall be accompanied by a statement of the grounds on which it is based. The authority appellate board may, at its discretion, require the appellant to furnish further information or evidence, and shall afford the respondent an opportunity to present their case. Provided that the authority appellate board may, if satisfied that the appeal is frivolous or vexatious, dismiss it with costs. All decisions of the authority appellate board shall be final and binding, save for any recourse permissible under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

The authority appellate board constituted under this Act shall have the power to impose penalties for any contravention of the provisions relating to the registration of layout-designs, and for acts infringing registered layout-designs, including but not limited to monetary fines not exceeding five lakh rupees for each such infringement. Any person aggrieved by an order of the Registrar refusing registration, or imposing conditions on registration, may prefer an appeal to the authority appellate board within sixty days of the date of such order. Provided that the authority appellate board may, if satisfied that sufficient cause existed for the delay, entertain an appeal filed beyond the stipulated period. Failure to comply with an order of the authority appellate board, or obstruction of its proceedings, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with a fine, or with both. All penalties collected under this Act shall be credited to the Consolidated Fund of India.

The registered proprietor of a layout-design may, subject to the terms of any contract to the contrary, assign the right, title and interest in the layout-design, or any right therein, to any other person, and such assignment shall be in writing and shall be subject to such conditions, if any, as may be agreed upon between the parties. Any license granted under this Act, whether exclusive or non-exclusive, shall be in writing and shall specify the duration, scope, and territorial limits of the license, as well as the royalty or other consideration payable. Where a dispute arises concerning the validity of an assignment or the terms of a license, or any alleged infringement thereof, the aggrieved party may apply to the authority appellate board for redressal. The authority appellate board shall have the power to examine the evidence, hear the parties, and pass such orders as it deems fit, including orders for specific performance, injunction, or damages, subject to the provisions contained herein. Any decision of the authority appellate board shall be final and binding on all parties, unless appealed to the High Court.

Any person aggrieved by an order of the Registrar relating to the registration of a semiconductor layout-design, or the rectification thereof, may prefer an appeal to the authority appellate board. Such appeal shall be filed within ninety days from the date of the order appealed against, subject to the payment of such fee as may be prescribed. The appellate board shall, after giving the parties an opportunity of being heard, either confirm, modify, or reverse the decision of the Registrar. Provided that the appellate board may, if it deems necessary, require additional evidence to be furnished by either party. Any decision of the appellate board shall be final and binding, except where a substantial question of law is involved, in which case an appeal may lie to the Supreme Court. The Registrar shall transmit all relevant records to the authority appellate board expeditiously upon receipt of notice of appeal. Failure to do so may be considered a willful disregard of the provisions of this Act.

The Authority Appellate Board established under this Act shall have the power to hear and decide appeals from any order passed by the Controller of Designs, including those relating to the refusal of registration or the revocation thereof. Any person aggrieved by such an order may, within a period of sixty days from the date of the order, file an appeal to the Authority Appellate Board in the prescribed manner and accompanied by the prescribed fee. The register maintained by the Controller, detailing all registered layout-designs, shall be open for inspection by any person during office hours, subject to such conditions as may be prescribed. Provided that the Authority Appellate Board may, at any stage of the proceedings, require the appellant to deposit with it a sum sufficient to cover the costs of the appeal. Failure to comply with this requirement may result in the dismissal of the appeal. The decisions of the Authority Appellate Board shall be final and binding, subject to any remedies available under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

The Authority Appellate Board established under this Act shall be the final forum for hearing appeals from the decisions of the Registrar. Any person aggrieved by an order of the Registrar concerning the registration of a semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design, or the refusal thereof, may prefer an appeal to the Board. Such appeal shall be filed within a period of sixty days from the date of the order appealed against, subject to extension granted by the Board for sufficient cause. The Board may, at any stage of the proceedings, require the appellant to deposit such fees as may be prescribed. 

A board means appellate and, accordingly, the Authority Appellate Board shall have the power to confirm, modify, or reverse the decision of the Registrar, and may also direct such further action as it deems appropriate. The Board shall, before passing any order, provide an opportunity of being heard to the parties to the appeal. All decisions of the Authority Appellate Board shall be final and binding, and no further appeal shall lie to any court.

Any person desiring to commercially exploit a registered layout-design, or to assign or otherwise transfer rights therein, shall submit a statement of proposed registered assignment to the authority appellate board for its review and record. The statement shall clearly identify the parties involved, detail the scope of the assignment including territorial limitations, and specify any associated royalty or licensing terms. The authority appellate board may, subject to such conditions as it deems necessary to safeguard the interests of the original creator and ensure continued innovation, approve the proposed assignment. Approval shall be recorded in the register proposed registered layouts-designs maintained by the authority. Where the assignment involves a license, the terms of the license, including duration and field of use, shall be explicitly stated. Failure to obtain approval from the authority appellate board prior to any commercial exploitation, assignment or transfer may render such acts void and subject the offender to penalties as provided herein. The authority appellate board’s decision shall be final and binding, subject to judicial review.

The Consist Judicial Member shall be a person of eminence with at least ten years of experience as a Judge of a High Court, or a legal professional possessing equivalent qualifications and expertise in intellectual property law. The Central Government shall appoint the Consist Judicial Member from a panel of names recommended by a Search Committee constituted as provided herein. The Search Committee shall comprise the Secretary to the Government in the Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion, a nominee of the Chief Justice of India, and an eminent technologist with expertise in semiconductor integrated circuits layout-design. A person shall be disqualified for appointment as a Consist Judicial Member if they have any financial or other interest which may conflict with their duties. The term of office for the Consist Judicial Member shall be five years, or until attaining the age of seventy years, whichever is earlier.

The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, constitute a Consist Judicial Member for the purposes of hearing appeals under this Act, provided that such Member shall be a person of proven integrity and possess at least ten years of experience as a Judge of a High Court or in the legal profession. The selection of the Consist Judicial Member shall be made from a panel of names recommended by a Search-cum-Selection Committee constituted for this purpose, and the terms and conditions of appointment shall be as prescribed. Any vacancy arising amongst the Consist Judicial Members shall be filled in the manner as herein provided. 

The Consist Judicial Member, while adjudicating matters pertaining to layout-design rights, shall be assisted by a Technical Member possessing specialized knowledge in the field of semiconductor integrated circuits. Subject to the provisions contained herein, the quorum for any sitting of the Consist Judicial Member shall be two, including at least one Judicial Member. Decisions shall be made by majority vote, and in the event of a tie, the Judicial Member shall have a casting vote.

The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, constitute a Consist Judicial Member to preside over hearings relating to the revocation of a registered layout-design right where a petition alleging improper obtaining of such right has been filed as provided herein. Any person intending to file such a petition shall deposit with the designated authority a sum equivalent to five percent of the prescribed fee for registration of the layout-design, subject to refund upon satisfactory resolution of the matter. The Consist Judicial Member shall, within ninety days of the petition’s filing, determine if prima facie grounds exist for revocation, and shall issue notice to the registered proprietor accordingly. Failure to comply with the procedural requirements outlined in this Act shall render the petition inadmissible. The decision of the Consist Judicial Member shall be final and binding, unless appealed to the appropriate court. Any evidence submitted must be duly authenticated and presented in a manner consistent with the rules of procedure.

The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, establish a Consist Judicial Member to hear and determine appeals arising from decisions of the Registrar. Any person aggrieved by an order of the Registrar refusing to register a layout-design, or imposing conditions on registration, may file an appeal to the Consist Judicial Member within ninety days of the date of such order. Failure to file such appeal within the stipulated period shall preclude the aggrieved party from pursuing further remedies as provided herein. The Consist Judicial Member, upon establishing prima facie evidence of irreparable harm, may grant interim injunctions restraining the infringement of a registered layout-design, and any violation of such injunction shall be punishable with imprisonment not exceeding three years, or a fine, or both. All decisions of the Consist Judicial Member shall be final and binding, subject to writ jurisdiction of the High Court. Any false representation made before the Consist Judicial Member shall constitute an offence punishable with a fine up to five lakh rupees.

The registered proprietor of a layout-design may, subject to the provisions of this Act, grant licenses to any person to use the layout-design for any purpose, and such license may be assigned, with or without conditions, to any other person. Any assignment of a license shall be in writing and shall specify the scope of the license, the duration, the territory, and the royalty or other consideration payable. Where a license is granted exclusively, the registered proprietor shall not grant any further licenses in respect of the same layout-design for the same purpose. The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, establish a Layout-Design Registry for the purpose of maintaining a register of layout-designs and for facilitating the grant of licenses and assignments. The Registry shall consist of a Controller of Layout-Designs and such other officers and staff as may be necessary. Any dispute arising out of a license or assignment shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the Controller, and the Controller shall appoint a consist judicial member to adjudicate such disputes, ensuring a fair and impartial resolution.

The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, constitute a Consist Judicial Member to preside over hearings relating to disputes concerning the validity of semiconductor integrated circuits layout-designs, as provided herein. Such a Member shall be a person of proven integrity and possess at least ten years of experience as a Judge of a High Court or equivalent judicial authority. The Consist Judicial Member, when considering applications for interim injunction subject to final determination of rights, shall prioritize evidence demonstrating irreparable harm to the applicant, and the balance of convenience favoring immediate preservation of the layout-design. Any order granting such injunction shall be accompanied by a reasoned statement outlining the grounds for its issuance. Provided that, the Consist Judicial Member may, at any stage, direct the parties to submit expert opinions to aid in the assessment of technical complexities. All decisions of the Consist Judicial Member shall be communicated in writing and shall be subject to review by the appropriate appellate authority, as established under this Act.

The Central Government shall constitute a Consist Judicial Member within ninety days of the notification of this Act, possessing qualifications equivalent to those of a Judge of a High Court, and with not less than ten years of experience in intellectual property law or related fields. Any person intending to seek registration of a semiconductor layout-design shall first file an application with the designated Intellectual Property Office, accompanied by the prescribed fee and a detailed description of the layout-design, including supporting documentation as provided herein. The application shall be subject to verification by the Office to ensure compliance with all regulatory requirements. Provided that, the Consist Judicial Member may, at any stage of the examination process, request additional information or clarification from the applicant. All decisions regarding the acceptance or rejection of a filing application shall be communicated to the applicant in writing, with a clear statement of reasons.

The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, constitute a Consist Judicial Member to hear and decide appeals arising from decisions of the Registrar. The Registrar shall decide upon the maintainability of any appeal filed under this Act, and may dismiss frivolous or vexatious appeals with a reasoned order communicated to the appellant. Any person aggrieved by such dismissal may, within thirty days of the order, apply to the Consist Judicial Member for review. Failure to comply with the procedural requirements for filing an appeal, as provided herein, shall render the appeal inadmissible and subject the appellant to a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees. Repeated instances of filing frivolous appeals may result in a bar from future proceedings under this Act, determined at the discretion of the Consist Judicial Member. All penalties collected under this provision shall be credited to the Consolidated Fund of India.

The Licensing Authority, constituted under this Act, shall examine any application for the grant of a license to commercially exploit a registered layout-design, ensuring adherence to the principles of fair and reasonable terms. A consist judicial member of the Licensing Authority, possessing not less than ten years’ experience in intellectual property law, shall preside over all hearings relating to licensing disputes and determine the royalty rates, subject to the provisions concerning national policy. Any registered user seeking to obtain a license for a layout-design incorporated into an article manufactured for the purpose of repair or replacement shall submit a detailed justification outlining the necessity of such use. Provided that, the applicant demonstrates a genuine need and offers reasonable compensation to the proprietor, the Licensing Authority may grant a compulsory license. All licensing agreements shall be documented in writing and filed with the Licensing Authority within thirty days of execution, and failure to do so may result in penalties as provided herein. The proprietor retains the right to assign the license, subject to prior notification to the Licensing Authority.
